children.text: BhG 1
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 1

children.text:
atha arjuna-viṣāda-yogo nāma
prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now [begins] the chapter called '<s>Arjuna-Viṣāda-Yoga</s>' (The Yoga of <s>Arjuna</s>'s Despondency), the first chapter.

children.text: bhagavat-śaṅkarācārya-kṛta-bhāṣyam
children.translated_text: The commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>

children.text: upodghāṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>)

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>

children.text: nārāyaṇaḥ paro 'vyaktād aṇḍam avyakta-sambhavam |
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is beyond the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>); the cosmic egg arose from the Unmanifest;

children.text: aṇḍasyāntas tv ime lokāḥ sapta-dvīpā ca medinī ||
children.translated_text: within the egg are these worlds and the earth with its seven continents.

children.text:
sa bhagavān sṛṣṭvedaṃ jagat | tasya ca sthitiṃ cikīrṣuḥ marīḍyādīn agre sṛṣṭvā prajāpatīn pravṛtti-lakṣaṇaṃ dharmaṃ grāhayāmāsa vedoktam | tato 'nyān ca sanaka-sanandanādīn utpādya nivṛtti-lakṣaṇaṃ dharmaṃ jñāna-vairāgya-lakṣaṇaṃ grāhayāmāsa | dvividho hi vedokto dharmaḥ pravṛtti-lakṣaṇo nivṛtti-lakṣaṇaś ca | jagataḥ sthiti-kāraṇam | prāṇināṃ sākṣād abhyudaya-niḥśreyasa-hetur yaḥ sa dharmo brāhmaṇādyair varṇibhir āśramibhiś ca śreyo 'rthibhir anuṣṭhīyamānaḥ | dīrgheṇa kālena anuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ kāmodbhavād dhīyamāna-viveka-jñāna-hetukena adharmeṇa abhibhūyamāne dharme, pravardhamāne ca adharme, jagataḥ sthitiṃ paripipālayiṣuḥ sa ādi-kartā nārāyaṇākhyo viṣṇur bhaumasya brahmaṇo brāhmaṇatvasya cābhirakṣaṇārthaṃ
devakyāṃ vasudevād aṃśena kṛṣṇaḥ kila sambabhūva | brāhmaṇatvasya hi rakṣaṇena rakṣitaḥ syād vaidiko dharmaḥ tad-adhīnatvād varṇāśrama-bhedānām |
children.translated_text:
That Blessed Lord, having created this world, and desiring its preservation, first created <s>Marīci</s> and the other <s>Prajāpatis</s> (lords of creation) and taught them the <s>dharma</s> of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) as declared in the <s>Vedas</s>. Then He produced others — <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, and the rest — and taught them the <s>dharma</s> of withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>), characterized by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). For the <s>dharma</s> declared in the <s>Vedas</s> is twofold: that characterized by activity and that characterized by withdrawal. It is the cause of the world's preservation. That <s>dharma</s> which is directly the cause of worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) for living beings — when practiced by the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) beginning with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and by the <s>āśramins</s> (those in the stages of life) who desire welfare. Over a long period, when <s>dharma</s> was being overpowered by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) — caused by the diminishing of discriminative knowledge due to desires arising in the practitioners — and when <s>adharma</s> was increasing, the primordial creator called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, desiring to protect the preservation of the world and for the sake of protecting the earthly <s>Brahman</s> (the Vedic tradition) and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood,
was born as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> from <s>Devakī</s> through <s>Vasudeva</s>, with a portion [of His being]. For by protecting <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood, the Vedic <s>dharma</s> would be protected, since the distinctions of <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> depend upon it.

children.text: sa ca bhagavān jñānaiśvarya-śakti-bala-vīrya-tejobhiḥ sadā sampannas triguṇātmikāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ svāṃ māyāṃ mūla-prakṛtiṃ vaśīkṛtya, ajo 'vyayo bhūtānām īśvaro nitya-śuddha-buddha-mukta-svabhāvo 'pi san, sva-māyayā dehavān iva jāta iva ca lokānugrahaṃ kurvan lakṣyate | sva-prayojanābhāve 'pi bhūtānujighṛkṣayā vaidikaṃ hi dharma-dvayam arjunāya śoka-moha-mahodadhau nimagnāya upadideśa guṇādhikair hi gṛhīto 'nuṣṭhīyamānaś ca dharmaḥ pracayaṃ gamiṣyatīti | taṃ dharmaṃ bhagavatā yathopadiṣṭaṃ veda-vyāsaḥ sarvajño bhagavān gītākhyaiḥ saptabhiḥ śloka-śatair upanibabandha |
children.translated_text: And that Blessed Lord, ever endowed with knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, valor, and splendor, having brought under control His own <s>Māyā</s> — the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s> (Nature), which is of the nature of the three <s>guṇas</s> and belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s> — though unborn, imperishable, the Lord of beings, and by nature eternally pure, awakened, and free, is seen, through His own <s>Māyā</s>, as if embodied, as if born, conferring grace upon the world. Even though having no personal purpose, out of compassion for beings, He taught the twofold Vedic <s>dharma</s> to <s>Arjuna</s>, who was sunk in the great ocean of grief and delusion — for <s>dharma</s>, when adopted and practiced by those of superior qualities, will flourish. That <s>dharma</s>, as taught by the Blessed Lord, was compiled by the omniscient, blessed <s>Veda-Vyāsa</s> in seven hundred verses called the <s>Gītā</s>.

children.text: tad idaṃ gītā-śāstraṃ samasta-vedārtha-sāra-saṅgraha-bhūtaṃ durvijñayārthaṃ tad-arthāviṣkaraṇāya anekair vivṛta-pada-padārtha-vākya-vākyārtha-nyāyam api atyanta-viruddhānekārthatvena laukikair gṛhyamāṇam upalabhyāhaṃ vivekato 'rtha-nirdhāraṇārthaṃ saṃkṣepato vivaraṇaṃ kariṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: This <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>, being a compendium of the essence of the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s>, is difficult to understand. Though its words, word-meanings, sentences, sentence-meanings, and logical reasoning have been explained by many [commentators], perceiving that it is being grasped by ordinary people as having many mutually contradictory meanings, I shall compose a brief commentary for the purpose of determining its meaning through discrimination.

children.text: tasya asya gītā-śāstrasya saṃkṣepataḥ prayojanaṃ paraṃ niḥśreyasaṃ sa-hetukasya saṃsārasya atyantoparama-lakṣaṇam | tac ca sarva-karma-sannyāsa-pūrvakād ātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā-rūpād dharmād bhavati | tathā imam eva gītārtha-dharmam uddiśya bhagavataivoktam | sa hi dharmaḥ suparyāpto brahmaṇaḥ pada-vedane [Mbh 14.16.12] ity anugītāsu | tatraiva coktaṃ - naiva dharmī na cādharmī na caiva hi śubhāśubhī [Mbh 14.19.7], yaḥ syād ekāyane līnas tūṣṇīṃ kiṃcid acintayan [Mbh 14.19.1], jñānaṃ saṃnyāsa-lakṣaṇam [Mbh 14.43.26] iti ca | ihāpi cānte uktam arjunāya - sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja [Gītā 18.66] iti |
children.translated_text: The purpose of this <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>, in brief, is the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), characterized by the complete cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) together with its cause. And that comes from the <s>dharma</s> consisting of steadfast devotion to Self-knowledge (<s>ātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>), preceded by the renunciation of all actions. And with reference to this very <s>dharma</s> that is the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s>, the Blessed Lord Himself stated: 'For that <s>dharma</s> is fully sufficient for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>' [<s>Mbh</s> 14.16.12] — in the <s>Anugītā</s>. And therein too it is stated: 'Neither righteous nor unrighteous, nor of good and evil [nature]' [<s>Mbh</s> 14.19.7], 'One who is absorbed in the single path, silent, not thinking of anything' [<s>Mbh</s> 14.19.1], and 'Knowledge is characterized by renunciation' [<s>Mbh</s> 14.43.26]. And here too, at the end, it is stated to <s>Arjuna</s>: 'Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s>, take refuge in Me alone' [<s>Gītā</s> 18.66].

children.text: abhyudayārtho 'pi yaḥ pravṛtti-lakṣaṇo dharmo varṇān āśramāṃś coddiśya vihitaḥ sa devādi-sthāna-prāpti-hetur api san, īśvarārpaṇa-buddhyānuṣṭhīyamānaḥ sattva-śuddhaye bhavati phalābhisandhi-varjitaḥ | śuddha-sattvasya ca jñāna-niṣṭhāyogyatā-prāpti-dvāreṇa jñānotpatti-hetutvena ca niḥśreyasa-hetutvam api pratipadyate | tathā cemam evārtham abhisandhāya vakṣyati brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi [Gītā 5.10], yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātma-śuddhaye [Gītā 5.11] iti |
children.translated_text: Even the <s>dharma</s> of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), which is for the purpose of worldly prosperity and is enjoined with reference to <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s> — though it is the cause of attaining the stations of gods etc. — when practiced with the attitude of offering to the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), without attachment to results, it leads to the purification of <s>sattva</s> (inner being). And for one whose <s>sattva</s> is purified, it also attains the status of being a cause of the supreme good — through being the cause of the arising of knowledge, by way of attaining fitness for steadfast devotion to knowledge. And intending this very meaning, he will say: 'Offering actions to <s>Brahman</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.10], and 'Yogins perform action, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.11].

children.text: imaṃ dviprakāraṃ dharmaṃ niḥśreyasa-prayojanam | paramārtha-tattvaṃ ca vāsudevākhyaṃ para-brahmābhidheya-bhūtaṃ viśeṣataḥ abhivyañjayad viśiṣṭa-prayojana-sambandhābhidheyavad gītā-śāstram | yatas tad-artha-vijñānena samasta-puruṣārtha-siddhiḥ | ataḥ tad-vivaraṇe yatnaḥ kriyate mayā ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>, which specially reveals this twofold <s>dharma</s> having the supreme good as its purpose, as well as the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha-tattva</s>) known as <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> which is the referent — possessing a distinguished purpose, connection, and subject — since by the knowledge of its meaning, the accomplishment of all human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>) is achieved, therefore effort is made by me in its commentary.

children.text: BhG 1
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 1

children.text: dharma-kṣetre kuru-kṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
children.translated_text: On the field of <s>Dharma</s>, on the field of the <s>Kurus</s>, assembled together, desiring to fight —

children.text: māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata saṃjaya ||BhG_1.1||
children.translated_text: my [sons] and the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> — what did they do, O <s>Saṃjaya</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 1.1 //

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjaya</s> said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanas tadā |
children.translated_text: Having seen the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> arrayed in formation, <s>Duryodhana</s> then,

children.text: ācāryam upasaṃgamya rājā vacanam abravīt ||BhG_1.2||
children.translated_text: approaching the teacher (<s>Droṇa</s>), the king spoke these words: // <s>BhG</s> 1.2 //

children.text: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍu-putrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
children.translated_text: 'Behold, O teacher, this great army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: vyūḍhāṃ drupada-putreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||BhG_1.3||
children.translated_text: arrayed by the son of <s>Drupada</s>, your wise disciple. // <s>BhG</s> 1.3 //

children.text: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjuna-samā yudhi |
children.translated_text: Here are heroes, mighty archers, equal in battle to <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> —

children.text: yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ ||BhG_1.4||
children.translated_text: <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and <s>Drupada</s>, the great chariot-warrior; // <s>BhG</s> 1.4 //

children.text: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśirājaś ca vīryavān |
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and the valiant king of <s>Kāśī</s>;

children.text: purujit kuntibhojaś ca śaibyaś ca nara-puṃgavaḥ ||BhG_1.5||
children.translated_text: <s>Purujit</s>, <s>Kuntibhoja</s>, and <s>Śaibya</s>, the bull among men; // <s>BhG</s> 1.5 //

children.text: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān |
children.translated_text: the valiant <s>Yudhāmanyu</s> and the mighty <s>Uttamaujas</s>;

children.text: saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahā-rathāḥ ||BhG_1.6||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Subhadrā</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s> — all indeed great chariot-warriors. // <s>BhG</s> 1.6 //

children.text: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama |
children.translated_text: But know those who are distinguished among us, O best of the twice-born —

children.text: nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te ||BhG_1.7||
children.translated_text: the leaders of my army; I name them to you for your information: // <s>BhG</s> 1.7 //

children.text: bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiṃjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Your good self, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and <s>Kṛpa</s>, the ever-victorious in battle;

children.text: aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattir jayadrathaḥ ||BhG_1.8||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, <s>Vikarṇa</s>, and <s>Saumadatti</s> (<s>Bhūriśravas</s>), [and] <s>Jayadratha</s>; // <s>BhG</s> 1.8 //

children.text: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā mad-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: and many other heroes who have risked their lives for my sake,

children.text: nānā-śastra-praharaṇāḥ sarve yuddha-viśāradāḥ ||BhG_1.9||
children.translated_text: armed with various weapons — all skilled in warfare. // <s>BhG</s> 1.9 //

children.text: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
children.translated_text: Unlimited is that army of ours, protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s>;

children.text: paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam ||BhG_1.10||
children.translated_text: while limited is this army of theirs, protected by <s>Bhīma</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 1.10 //

children.text: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathā-bhāgam avasthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Stationed at your respective positions in all the strategic points,

children.text: bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||BhG_1.11||
children.translated_text: all of you must protect <s>Bhīṣma</s> in particular!' // <s>BhG</s> 1.11 //

children.text: tasya saṃjanayan harṣaṃ kuru-vṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Generating joy in him, the grandsire, the eldest of the <s>Kuru</s> [clan],

children.text: siṃha-nādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān ||BhG_1.12||
children.translated_text: roaring a lion's roar loudly, blew his conch, the valiant one. // <s>BhG</s> 1.12 //

children.text: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānaka-gomukhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then conches and kettledrums, tabors, drums, and cow-horns

children.text: sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat ||BhG_1.13||
children.translated_text: were sounded all at once — that tumultuous sound arose. // <s>BhG</s> 1.13 //

children.text: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau |
children.translated_text: Then, seated in a great chariot yoked with white horses,

children.text: mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||BhG_1.14||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) blew their divine conches. // <s>BhG</s> 1.14 //

children.text: pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) [blew] <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) [blew] <s>Devadatta</s>;

children.text: pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahā-śaṅkhaṃ bhīma-karmā vṛkodaraḥ ||BhG_1.15||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> of terrible deeds blew the great conch <s>Pauṇḍra</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 1.15 //

children.text: ananta-vijayaṃ rājā kuntī-putro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
children.translated_text: King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of <s>Kuntī</s>, [blew] <s>Anantavijaya</s>;

children.text: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣa-maṇipuṣpakau ||BhG_1.16||
children.translated_text: <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> [blew] <s>Sughoṣa</s> and <s>Maṇipuṣpaka</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 1.16 //

children.text: kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahā-rathaḥ |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Kāśī</s>, the supreme archer, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the great chariot-warrior,

children.text: dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ ||BhG_1.17||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and the unconquered <s>Sātyaki</s>; // <s>BhG</s> 1.17 //

children.text: drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivī-pate |
children.translated_text: <s>Drupada</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, all together, O lord of the earth,

children.text: saubhadraś ca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||BhG_1.18||
children.translated_text: and the mighty-armed son of <s>Subhadrā</s> — blew their conches, each separately. // <s>BhG</s> 1.18 //

children.text: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
children.translated_text: That tumultuous sound pierced the hearts of the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,

children.text: nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan ||BhG_1.19||
children.translated_text: making both the sky and the earth reverberate. // <s>BhG</s> 1.19 //

children.text: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapi-dhvajaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> arrayed, the monkey-bannered one (<s>Arjuna</s>),

children.text: pravṛtte śastra-saṃpāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||BhG_1.20||
children.translated_text: as the clash of weapons was about to begin, raising his bow, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, // <s>BhG</s> 1.20 //

children.text: hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyam idam āha mahī-pate |
children.translated_text: spoke these words to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), O lord of the earth:

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta ||BhG_1.21||
children.translated_text: 'Place my chariot between the two armies, O <s>Acyuta</s>, // <s>BhG</s> 1.21 //

children.text: yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān |
children.translated_text: while I observe these [warriors] arrayed here, eager to fight —

children.text: kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇa-samudyame ||BhG_1.22||
children.translated_text: with whom I must fight in this commencement of battle. // <s>BhG</s> 1.22 //

children.text: yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṃ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Let me observe those who are about to fight, who have assembled here,

children.text: dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-cikīrṣavaḥ ||BhG_1.23||
children.translated_text: desiring to please the evil-minded son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in battle.' // <s>BhG</s> 1.23 //

children.text: evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Guḍākeśa</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), O descendant of <s>Bharata</s>,

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam ||BhG_1.24||
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, having stationed the best of chariots between the two armies, // <s>BhG</s> 1.24 //

children.text: bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
children.translated_text: in front of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and all the rulers of the earth,

children.text: uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti ||BhG_1.25||
children.translated_text: said: 'O <s>Pārtha</s>, behold these <s>Kurus</s> assembled together.' // <s>BhG</s> 1.25 //

children.text: tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝn atha pitāmahān |
children.translated_text: There <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) saw, standing [in both armies], fathers, grandfathers,

children.text: ācāryān mātulān bhrātṝn putrān pautrān sakhīṃs tathā ||BhG_1.26||
children.translated_text: teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends; // <s>BhG</s> 1.26 //

children.text: śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayor ubhayor api |
children.translated_text: fathers-in-law and well-wishers too, in both the armies.

children.text: tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān ||BhG_1.27||
children.translated_text: Seeing all those kinsmen arrayed, that son of <s>Kuntī</s>, // <s>BhG</s> 1.27 //

children.text: kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt |
children.translated_text: filled with deep compassion, despondent, spoke thus:

children.text: dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam ||BhG_1.28||
children.translated_text: 'Seeing these, my own kinsmen, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, arrayed eager to fight, // <s>BhG</s> 1.28 //

children.text: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati |
children.translated_text: my limbs sink, my mouth dries up,

children.text: vepathuś ca śarīre me romaharṣaś ca jāyate ||BhG_1.29||
children.translated_text: trembling arises in my body, and my hair stands on end. // <s>BhG</s> 1.29 //

children.text: gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate |
children.translated_text: The bow <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> slips from my hand, my skin burns all over,

children.text: na ca śaknomy avasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ ||BhG_1.30||
children.translated_text: I am unable to stand, and my mind seems to whirl. // <s>BhG</s> 1.30 //

children.text: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
children.translated_text: And I see adverse omens, O <s>Keśava</s>;

children.text: na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave ||BhG_1.31||
children.translated_text: nor do I foresee any good from slaying my own kinsmen in battle. // <s>BhG</s> 1.31 //

children.text: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
children.translated_text: I desire not victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.

children.text: kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā ||BhG_1.32||
children.translated_text: Of what use is kingdom to us, O <s>Govinda</s>, of what use are enjoyments or even life? // <s>BhG</s> 1.32 //

children.text: yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
children.translated_text: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures —

children.text: ta ime 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca ||BhG_1.33||
children.translated_text: they stand here in battle, having abandoned their lives and wealth: // <s>BhG</s> 1.33 //

children.text: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ |
children.translated_text: teachers, fathers, sons, and also grandfathers,

children.text: mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā ||BhG_1.34||
children.translated_text: maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other kinsmen. // <s>BhG</s> 1.34 //

children.text: etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: I do not wish to kill them, even though they kill [me], O <s>Madhusūdana</s> —

children.text: api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahī-kṛte ||BhG_1.35||
children.translated_text: not even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, much less for the sake of this earth! // <s>BhG</s> 1.35 //

children.text: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana |
children.translated_text: Having slain the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, what joy would be ours, O <s>Janārdana</s>?

children.text: pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ ||BhG_1.36||
children.translated_text: Sin alone would take hold of us, having killed these aggressors. // <s>BhG</s> 1.36 //

children.text: tasmān nārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān sva-bāndhavān |
children.translated_text: Therefore we ought not to kill the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, our own kinsmen.

children.text: svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava ||BhG_1.37||
children.translated_text: For how, having killed our own people, could we be happy, O <s>Mādhava</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 1.37 //

children.text: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahata-cetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even if these [men], their minds corrupted by greed, do not see

children.text: kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitra-drohe ca pātakam ||BhG_1.38||
children.translated_text: the evil caused by the destruction of the family, and the sin of treachery to friends, // <s>BhG</s> 1.38 //

children.text: kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum |
children.translated_text: why should we not know [enough] to turn away from this sin,

children.text: kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir janārdana ||BhG_1.39||
children.translated_text: we who clearly see the evil caused by the destruction of the family, O <s>Janārdana</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 1.39 //

children.text: kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
children.translated_text: In the destruction of the family, the eternal family <s>dharmas</s> perish;

children.text: dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta ||BhG_1.40||
children.translated_text: when <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, <s>adharma</s> (lawlessness) indeed overwhelms the entire family. // <s>BhG</s> 1.40 //

children.text: adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the predominance of <s>adharma</s>, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the women of the family become corrupted;

children.text: strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṃkaraḥ ||BhG_1.41||
children.translated_text: when women are corrupted, O descendant of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, the intermixture of <s>varṇas</s> (classes) arises. // <s>BhG</s> 1.41 //

children.text: saṃkaro narakāyaiva kula-ghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
children.translated_text: The intermixture [leads] to hell alone — for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself;

children.text: patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ lupta-piṇḍodaka-kriyāḥ ||BhG_1.42||
children.translated_text: their forefathers fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water. // <s>BhG</s> 1.42 //

children.text: doṣair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṃ varṇa-saṃkara-kārakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By these faults of the family-destroyers, which cause the intermixture of <s>varṇas</s>,

children.text: utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ ||BhG_1.43||
children.translated_text: the eternal <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>jāti</s> (caste) and of the family are destroyed. // <s>BhG</s> 1.43 //

children.text: utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana |
children.translated_text: For men whose family <s>dharmas</s> have been destroyed, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma ||BhG_1.44||
children.translated_text: a dwelling in hell is certain — so we have heard.' // <s>BhG</s> 1.44 //

children.text: aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
children.translated_text: Alas! We are resolved to commit a great sin,

children.text: yad rājya-sukha-lobhena hantuṃ svajanam udyatāḥ ||BhG_1.45||
children.translated_text: in that we are prepared to slay our own kinsmen out of greed for the pleasures of kingship. ||<s>BhG</s> 1.45||

children.text: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ śastra-pāṇayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, weapons in hand, were to slay me in battle,

children.text: dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||BhG_1.46||
children.translated_text: unresisting and unarmed — that would be more beneficial for me. ||<s>BhG</s> 1.46||

children.text: evam uktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, <s>Arjuna</s> sat down on the seat of the chariot,

children.text: visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śoka-saṃvigna-mānasaḥ ||BhG_1.47||
children.translated_text: casting aside his bow together with its arrows, his mind overwhelmed with grief. ||<s>BhG</s> 1.47||

children.text:
iti śaṅkarācārya-kṛte gītā-bhāṣye prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
||1||
children.translated_text:
Thus ends the first chapter in the <s>Gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>.
||1||

children.text: BhG 2
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 2

children.text: dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: The Second Chapter

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjaya</s> said:

children.text: taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: To him who was thus overcome with compassion, whose eyes were filled and agitated with tears,

children.text: viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ ||BhG_2.1||
children.translated_text: who was despondent — <s>Madhusūdana</s> (the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>) spoke these words: ||<s>BhG</s> 2.1||

children.text: kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
children.translated_text: Whence has this impurity come upon you in this crisis,

children.text: anārya-juṣṭam asvargyam akīrti-karam arjuna ||BhG_2.2||
children.translated_text: unbecoming of a noble, not leading to heaven, causing disgrace, O <s>Arjuna</s>? ||<s>BhG</s> 2.2||

children.text: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate |
children.translated_text: Do not yield to unmanliness (<s>klaibyam</s>), O <s>Pārtha</s> — this does not befit you;

children.text: kṣudraṃ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha paraṃtapa ||BhG_2.3||
children.translated_text: abandon this petty weakness of heart and arise, O scorcher of foes (<s>Paraṃtapa</s>)! ||<s>BhG</s> 2.3||

children.text: kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: How can I fight in battle against <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana ||BhG_2.4||
children.translated_text: with arrows — they who are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies (<s>Arisūdana</s>)? ||<s>BhG</s> 2.4||

children.text: gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvāñ
children.translated_text: Rather than slaying the great-souled elders (<s>gurus</s>),

children.text: śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyam apīha loke |
children.translated_text: it would be better to live in this world even on alms;

children.text: hatvārtha-kāmāṃs tu gurūn ihaiva
children.translated_text: but having slain the elders driven by desire for wealth — here in this world

children.text: bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān ||BhG_2.5||
children.translated_text: I would enjoy pleasures smeared with blood. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.5||

children.text: na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo
children.translated_text: Nor do we know which is the greater [good] for us —

children.text: yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
children.translated_text: whether we should conquer or they should conquer us;

children.text: yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas
children.translated_text: those whom having slain we would not wish to live —

children.text: te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ ||BhG_2.6||
children.translated_text: those very sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> stand arrayed before us. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.6||

children.text: kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: My nature overwhelmed by the fault of faintheartedness (<s>kārpaṇya</s>),

children.text: pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetāḥ |
children.translated_text: my mind confused about <s>dharma</s>, I ask you:

children.text: yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me
children.translated_text: tell me decisively what is the greater good —

children.text: śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam ||BhG_2.7||
children.translated_text: I am your disciple; instruct me, who have taken refuge in you. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.7||

children.text: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād
children.translated_text: For I do not see what could dispel

children.text: yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām |
children.translated_text: this grief that dries up my senses —

children.text: avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṃ
children.translated_text: even if I were to obtain on earth a prosperous kingdom without rival,

children.text: rājyaṃ surāṇām api cādhipatyam ||BhG_2.8||
children.translated_text: or even sovereignty over the gods. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.8||

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjaya</s> said:

children.text: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (Lord of the senses), <s>Guḍākeśa</s> (Conqueror of sleep), the scorcher of foes,

children.text: na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha ||BhG_2.9||
children.translated_text: having said 'I shall not fight' to <s>Govinda</s>, fell silent. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.9||

children.text: tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata |
children.translated_text: To him, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, as if smiling, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye viṣīdantam idaṃ vacaḥ ||BhG_2.10||
children.translated_text: spoke these words, in the midst of the two armies, to the despondent one: ||<s>BhG</s> 2.10||

children.text:
atra ca dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkam ity ārabhya yāvat na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha ity etad-antaḥ prāṇināṃ śoka-mohādi-saṃsāra-bīja-bhūta-doṣodbhava-kāraṇa-pradarśanārthatvena vyākhyeyo granthaḥ | tathā hi -- arjunena rājya-guru-putra-mitra-suhṛt-svajana-saṃbandhi-bāndhaveṣu aham eteṣām mamaite ity evaṃ bhrānti-pratyaya-nimitta-sneha-vicchedādi-nimittau ātmanaḥ śoka-mohau pradarśitau | kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye ity ādinā | śoka-mohābhyāṃ hy abhibhūta-viveka-vijñānaḥ svata eva kṣatra-dharme yuddhe pravṛtto 'pi tasmād yuddhād upararāma | para-dharmaṃ ca bhikṣā-jīvanādikaṃ kartuṃ pravavṛte | tathā ca sarva-prāṇināṃ śoka-mohādi-doṣāviṣṭa-cetasāṃ svabhāvata eva svadharma-parityāgaḥ pratiṣiddha-sevā ca syāt | sva-dharme pravṛttānām
api teṣāṃ vāṅ-manaḥ-kāyādīnāṃ pravṛttiḥ phalābhisaṃdhi-pūrvikaiva sāhaṃkārā ca bhavati | tatraivaṃ sati dharmādharmopacayād iṣṭāniṣṭa-janma-sukha-duḥkhādi-prāpti-lakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāro 'nuparato bhavati | ity ataḥ saṃsāra-bīja-bhūtau śoka-mohau | tayoś ca sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-pūrvakād ātma-jñānāt nānyato nivṛttir iti tad-upadidikṣuḥ sarva-lokānugrahārtham arjunaṃ nimittīkṛtya āha bhagavān vāsudevaḥ--- aśocyān ityādi |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And here, the text from 'having seen the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>' up to 'having said "I shall not fight" to <s>Govinda</s>, he fell silent' — this entire passage is to be explained as intended for demonstrating the cause of the arising of the defects that form the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), such as grief, delusion, etc., among living beings. For indeed — <s>Arjuna</s> displayed his own grief and delusion, caused by affection rooted in the erroneous cognition 'I am theirs, they are mine' regarding kings, teachers, sons, friends, well-wishers, kinsmen, relatives, and family members — along with other causes such as the severance of that affection — 'How can I fight <s>Bhīṣma</s> in battle?' etc. For indeed, one whose discriminative wisdom is overpowered by grief and delusion, even though engaged by his very nature in the <s>kṣatriya-dharma</s> (warrior's duty) of battle, withdrew from that battle; and he proceeded to undertake another's <s>dharma</s>, such as living on alms. And thus, for all living beings whose minds are possessed by the defects of grief, delusion, etc., there would naturally be the abandonment of one's own <s>dharma</s> (<s>svadharma</s>) and the adoption of prohibited conduct. And even for those who are engaged in their own <s>dharma</s>, the activity of their speech, mind, body, etc. is preceded by the desire for results and accompanied by ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>). Under such conditions, through the accumulation of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> — characterized by the attainment of desirable and undesirable births, pleasures, and pains — continues without cessation. Therefore, grief and delusion are the seeds of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And their cessation comes from nothing other than <s>ātma-jñāna</s> (Self-knowledge) preceded by the complete renunciation of all actions (<s>sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa</s>). Wishing to teach that, for the benefit of all the world, the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> spoke, taking <s>Arjuna</s> as the occasion — '<s>aśocyān</s>' (those not to be grieved for) etc.

children.text:
atra kecid āhuḥ-sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-pūrvakād ātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā-mātrād eva kevalāt kaivalyaṃ na prāpyata eva | kiṃ tarhi ? agnihotrādi-śrauta-smārta-karma-sahitāt jñānāt kaivalya-prāptir iti sarvāsu gītāsu niścito 'rtha iti | jñāpakaṃ cāhur asyārthasya --
atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi [Gītā 2.33] karmaṇy evādhikāras te [Gītā 2.47], kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvam [Gītā 4.15] ity ādi | hiṃsādi-yuktatvāt vaidikaṃ karma adharmāya itīyam apy āśaṅkā na kāryā | katham ? kṣātraṃ karma yuddha-lakṣaṇaṃ guru-bhrātṛ-putrādi-hiṃsā-lakṣaṇam atyantaṃ krūram api sva-dharma iti kṛtvā nādharmāya | tad-akaraṇe ca tataḥ sva-dharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi [Gītā 2.33] iti bruvatā yāvaj jīvādi-śruti-coditānāṃ paśv-ādi-hiṃsā-lakṣaṇānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ prāg eva nādharmatvam iti suniścitam uktaṃ bhavati -- iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Here some say — <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) is not attained from the mere steadfastness in Self-knowledge preceded by the complete renunciation of all actions alone; rather, <s>kaivalya</s> is attained from knowledge combined with <s>Vedic</s> (<s>śrauta</s>) and traditional (<s>smārta</s>) actions such as <s>Agnihotra</s> etc. — this, they say, is the established meaning in all the <s>Gītā</s> [chapters]. And they cite as evidence for this meaning: 'But if you will not fight this righteous war' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.33], 'Your right is to action alone' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.47], 'Therefore perform action' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.15], etc. [They argue:] the apprehension that <s>Vedic</s> action leads to <s>adharma</s> because it involves violence etc. should not be entertained. Why? Because <s>kṣatriya</s> action in the form of battle — even though extremely cruel, involving the killing of teachers, brothers, sons, etc. — being one's own <s>dharma</s> (<s>svadharma</s>), does not lead to <s>adharma</s>. And by saying that failure to perform it leads to: 'then, abandoning your own <s>dharma</s> and fame, you will incur sin' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.33] — it is firmly established that the actions enjoined by scriptures such as 'as long as life lasts' (<s>yāvaj jīva</s>) and those involving violence to animals etc. are even more certainly not <s>adharma</s> — thus [they argue].

children.text:
tad asat | jñāna-karma-niṣṭhayor vibhāga-vacanād buddhi-dvayāśrayayoḥ | aśocyān ity ādinā bhagavatā yāvat svadharmam api cāvekṣya ity etad-antena granthena yat-paramārthātma-tattva-nirūpaṇaṃ kṛtam, tat sāṃkhyam | tad-viṣayā buddhir ātmano janmādi-ṣaḍ-vikriyābhāvād akartā ātmeti prakaraṇārtha-nirūpaṇād yā jāyate, sā sāṃkhya-buddhiḥ | sā yeṣāṃ jñāninām ucitā bhavati, te sāṃkhyāḥ | etasyā buddher janmanaḥ prāk ātmano dehādivyatiriktatvakartṛtvabhoktṛtvabhoktṛtvādyapekṣo dharmādharma-viveka-pūrvako mokṣa-sādhanānuṣṭhāna-lakṣaṇo yogaḥ | tad-viṣayā buddhiḥ yoga-buddhiḥ | sā yeṣāṃ karmiṇām ucitā bhavati te yoginaḥ | tathā ca bhagavatā vibhakte dve buddhī nirdiṣṭe eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu iti | tayoś
ca sāṃkhya-buddhy-āśrayāṃ jñāna-yogena niṣṭhāṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ vibhaktāṃ vakṣyati purā vedātmanā mayā proktā iti | tathā ca yoga-buddhy-āśrayāṃ karma-yogena niṣṭhāṃ vibhaktāṃ vakṣyati - karma-yogena yoginām iti | evaṃ sāṃkhya-buddhiṃ yoga-buddhiṃ ca āśritya dve niṣṭhe vibhakte bhagavataiva ukte jñāna-karmaṇoḥ kartṛtvākartṛtvaikatvānekatva-buddhy-āśrayayoḥ yugapad-eka-puruṣāśrayatvāsaṃbhavaṃ paśyatā | yathā etad-vibhāga-vacanam tathaiva darśitaṃ śātapathīye brāhmaṇe - etam eva pravrājino lokam icchanto brāhmaṇāḥ pravrajanti [BAU 4.4.22] iti sarva-karma-saṃnyāsaṃ vidhāya tac-cheṣeṇa kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yam ātmāyaṃ lokaḥ [BAU 4.4.22] iti | tatraiva ca prāg dāra-parigrahāt puruṣa ātmo prākṛto dharma-jijñāsottara-kālaṃ
loka-traya-sādhanam | putraṃ, dvi-prakāraṃ ca vittaṃ mānuṣaṃ dvi-prakāraṃ ca | tatra mānuṣaṃ karma-rūpaṃ pitṛ-loka-prāpti-sādhanaṃ vidyāṃ ca daivaṃ vittaṃ deva-loka-prāpti-sādhanam | so 'kāmayata [BAU 1.4.17] iti avidyā-kāmavata eva sarvāṇi karmāṇi śrautādīni darśitāni | tebhyo vyutthāya, pravrajanti [BAU 4.4.22] iti vyutthānam ātmānam eva lokam icchato 'kāmasya vihitam | tad etad vibhāga-vacanam anupapannaṃ syād yadi śrauta-karma-jñānayoḥ samuccayo 'bhipretaḥ syād bhagavataḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That is incorrect — because the Lord has stated the distinction between the two paths (<s>niṣṭhās</s>) of knowledge and action, which are based on two [different] forms of understanding (<s>buddhi</s>). The Lord's exposition of the ultimate truth of the Self (<s>paramārthātma-tattva</s>) through the passage from '<s>aśocyān</s>' (those not to be grieved for) up to 'and considering your own <s>dharma</s>' — that is <s>Sāṃkhya</s>. The understanding concerning that [truth] — the understanding that the Self is not an agent because of the absence of the six modifications beginning with birth — which arises from the determination of the contextual meaning, that is <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> (the understanding pertaining to <s>Sāṃkhya</s>). Those <s>jñānins</s> (knowers) for whom this understanding is appropriate are the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>. Prior to the arising of this understanding, <s>yoga</s> consists of the practice of the means to liberation (<s>mokṣa-sādhana</s>) preceded by discrimination between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, which requires the presupposition of the Self's distinction from the body etc. and of its agency and experiencer-ship. The understanding concerning that is <s>yoga-buddhi</s>. Those performers of action (<s>karmins</s>) for whom this understanding is appropriate are the <s>yogins</s>. And thus the Lord has distinguished and stated the two understandings: 'This understanding has been declared to you from the standpoint of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>; now hear it from the standpoint of <s>Yoga</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.39]. And the distinct path of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> based on <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), he will declare separately: 'formerly proclaimed by me to the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> through the <s>Veda</s>.' And likewise, the distinct path based on <s>yoga-buddhi</s> through <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action), he will declare separately: 'through <s>karma-yoga</s> for the <s>yogins</s>.' Thus, based on <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> and <s>yoga-buddhi</s>, the two distinct paths have been stated by the Lord himself — seeing the impossibility of the two being simultaneously practiced by one and the same person, based on understandings of agency and non-agency, unity and multiplicity. Just as this statement of distinction [is found in the <s>Gītā</s>], so has it been shown in the <s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'Desiring this very world, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> go forth as renunciants' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.22], where total renunciation of all actions is enjoined; and as a corollary: 'What shall we do with offspring, we for whom this Self is our world?' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.22]. And there too, prior to marriage, the person is described as follows — in his natural state, after the desire for knowledge of <s>dharma</s> arises, [he seeks] the means of the three worlds: sons, and wealth of two kinds — human and divine. The human [wealth] in the form of ritual action is the means to the world of the <s>Pitṛs</s>, and learning as divine wealth is the means to the world of the gods. 'He desired' [<s>BAU</s> 1.4.17] — thus all actions including <s>śrauta</s> ones have been shown as belonging to those possessed of ignorance and desire. 'Rising above these, they go forth as renunciants' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.22] — this rising above is enjoined for one who is free from desire and who seeks the Self alone as his world. This statement of distinction would be unjustified if the Lord intended a combination (<s>samuccaya</s>) of <s>śrauta</s> ritual action and knowledge.

children.text: na cārjunasya praśna upapanno bhavati jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te [Gītā 3.1] ity ādiḥ | eka-puruṣānuṣṭheyatvāsaṃbhavaṃ buddhi-karmaṇoḥ bhagavatā pūrvam anuktaṃ katham arjuno 'śrutaṃ buddhā ca karmaṇo jyāyastvaṃ bhagavaty adhyāropayen mṛṣaiva jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhiḥ iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Nor would <s>Arjuna's</s> question 'If you consider understanding (<s>buddhi</s>) to be superior to action' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.1] etc. be justified. For how could <s>Arjuna</s>, without the Lord having previously stated the impossibility of both understanding and action being practiced by one person, falsely attribute to the Lord the superiority of understanding over action that he had not heard — 'If understanding is considered by you to be superior to action'?

children.text: kiṃ ca -- yadi buddhi-karmaṇoḥ sarveṣāṃ samuccaya uktaḥ syāt arjunasyāpi sa ukta eveti, yac chrāya etayor ekaṃ tan me brūhi suniścitam iti katham ubhayor upadeśe sati anyatara-viṣaya eva praśnaḥ syāt ? na hi pitta-praśamanārthinaḥ vaidyena madhuraṃ śītalaṃ ca bhoktavyam ity upadiṣṭe tayor anyatarat-pitta-praśamana-kāraṇaṃ brūhi iti praśnaḥ saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Furthermore — if the combination of understanding and action had been taught for everyone, then it would have been taught to <s>Arjuna</s> as well; [in that case,] how could the question 'tell me decisively which one of these two is the better' pertain to only one of the two, when both have been taught? For when a physician prescribes to one who seeks to alleviate a bilious condition, 'you should eat what is sweet and cooling,' the question 'tell me which one of the two alleviates the bilious condition' is impossible.

children.text: athārjunasya bhagavad-ukta-vacanārtha-vivekānavadhāraṇa-nimittaḥ praśnaḥ kalpyeta, tathāpi bhagavatā praśnānurūpaṃ prativacanaṃ deyam -- mayā buddhi-karmaṇoḥ samuccaya uktaḥ kim artham itthaṃ tvaṃ bhrānto 'si -- iti | na tu punaḥ prativacanam ananurūpaṃ pṛṣṭād anyad eva dve niṣṭhā mayā purā proktā iti vaktuṃ yuktam |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Even if one were to suppose that <s>Arjuna's</s> question arose from his failure to discern the meaning of the Lord's words — even then, the Lord should have given an answer conforming to the question: 'I taught the combination of understanding and action — why are you thus confused?' — but it is not appropriate for the reply to be something entirely different from what was asked: 'Two paths were formerly declared by me.'

children.text: nāpi smārtenaiva karmaṇā buddheḥ samuccaye abhiprete vibhāga-vacanādi sarvam upapananam | kiṃ ca -- kṣatriyasya yuddhaṃ smārtaṃ karma sva-dharma iti jānataḥ tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghoro māṃ niyojayasi ity upālambho 'nupapannaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Nor is the statement of distinction and all [related passages] justified if the intended combination were only with <s>smārta</s> (traditional/customary) action. Furthermore — for a <s>kṣatriya</s> who knows that warfare, which is <s>smārta</s> action, is his own <s>dharma</s>, the reproach 'why do you engage me in this terrible action?' would be unjustified.

children.text:
tasmād gītā-śāstre īṣan-mātreṇāpi śrautena smārtena vā karmaṇā ātma-jñānasya samuccayo na kenacid darśayituṃ śakyaḥ | yasya tv ajñānāt rāgādi-doṣato vā karmaṇi pravṛttasya yajñena dānena tapasā vā viśuddha-sattvasya jñānam utpannaṃ paramārtha-tattva-viṣayam ekam evedaṃ sarvaṃ brahma akartṛ ca iti, tasya karmaṇi karma-prayojane ca nivṛtte 'pi loka-saṃgrahārthaṃ yatna-pūrvaṃ yathā pravṛttiḥ, tathaiva pravṛttasya yat pravṛtti-rūpaṃ dṛśyate na tat karma yena buddheḥ samuccayaḥ syāt | yathā bhagavato vāsudevasya kṣatra-dharma-ceṣṭitaṃ na jñānena samuccīyate puruṣārtha-siddhaye, tadvat tat-phalābhisaṃdhy-ahaṃkārābhāvasya tulyatvād viduṣaḥ | tattvavin nāhaṃ karomīti manyate, na ca tat-phalam abhisandhatte | yathā ca svargādi-kāmārthino 'gnihotrādi-karma-lakṣaṇa-dharmānuṣṭhānāya
āhitāgneḥ kāmye eva agnihotrādau pravṛttasya sāmi kṛte vinaṣṭā 'pi kāme tad eva agnihotrādy-anutiṣṭhato 'pi na tat-kāmyam agnihotrādi bhavati | tathā ca darśayati bhagavān - kurvann api na lipyate na karoti na lipyate iti tatra tatra ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, in the teaching of the <s>Gītā</s>, no one can demonstrate even the slightest combination of Self-knowledge with either <s>śrauta</s> or <s>smārta</s> action. But for one who, due to ignorance or defects such as attachment etc., has engaged in action — when through sacrifice, charity, or austerity, his <s>sattva</s> (being/mind) has become purified and knowledge has arisen concerning the ultimate reality — 'all this is nothing but <s>Brahman</s> alone, and the Self is a non-agent' — for such a one, even though action and its purpose have ceased, the deliberate activity that continues for the sake of the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) — the activity that is seen in him who is thus engaged — is not action such as could be combined with knowledge. Just as the <s>kṣatriya-dharma</s> activity of the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> himself is not combined with knowledge for the purpose of attaining the <s>puruṣārthas</s> (human goals), so too for the wise one, because of the equal absence of desire for results and ego-sense. The knower of truth thinks 'I do not act,' nor does he desire the result of action. And just as for one who has established the sacred fires (<s>āhitāgni</s>) for the purpose of performing <s>Agnihotra</s> and other rites for the sake of attaining heaven etc. — when, after the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) rites have been performed, the desire [for heaven] is destroyed, even though he continues to perform the same <s>Agnihotra</s> etc., those [rites] do not become desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>). And thus the Lord shows: 'though acting, he is not tainted,' 'he does not act, he is not tainted' — in various places.

children.text: yac ca pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ iti, tat tu pravibhajya vijñeyam | tat katham ? yadi tāvat pūrve janakādayaḥ tattva-vido 'pi pravṛtta-karmāṇaḥ syuḥ, te loka-saṃgrahārtham guṇā guṇeṣu vartante iti jñānenaiva saṃsiddhim āsthitāḥ, karma-saṃnyāse prāpte 'pi karmaṇā sahaiva saṃsiddhim āsthitāḥ, na karma-saṃnyāsaṃ kṛtavanta ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: And as for what was done by the ancients — '<s>karmaṇā eva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā Janakādayaḥ</s>' (indeed, <s>Janaka</s> and others attained perfection through action alone) [BhG 3.20] — that should be understood by making a distinction. How so? If the ancients, <s>Janaka</s> and others, while being knowers of the truth (<s>tattvavid</s>), were nonetheless engaged in action, then they attained perfection through knowledge alone — [understanding that] '<s>guṇā guṇeṣu vartante</s>' (the <s>guṇas</s> operate among the <s>guṇas</s>) — and were established in perfection along with action even though renunciation of action had been appropriate; the meaning is that they did not renounce action.

children.text: atha na te tattva-vidaḥ | īśvara-samarpitena karmaṇā sādhana-bhūtena saṃsiddhiṃ sattva-śuddhim, jñānotpatti-lakṣaṇāṃ vā saṃsiddhim, āsthitā janakādaya iti vyākhyeyam | etam evārthaṃ vakṣyati bhagavān sattva-śuddhaye karma kurvanti iti | sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ ity uktvā siddhiṃ prāptasya punar-jñāna-niṣṭhāṃ vakṣyati -- siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma ity ādinā ||
children.translated_text: Or, if they were not knowers of the truth: then it should be explained that <s>Janaka</s> and others attained perfection (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>) — meaning purification of <s>sattva</s>, or perfection characterized by the arising of knowledge — through action offered to the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) as a means of purification. The Blessed Lord will state this very meaning: 'they perform action for the purification of <s>sattva</s>.' Having said 'by worshipping Him through one's own duty, a person attains perfection,' He will further state the establishment in knowledge for one who has attained perfection — by [the verse] '<s>siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma</s>' (having attained perfection, how [one reaches] <s>Brahman</s>) etc.

children.text: tasmād gītā-śāstre kevalād eva tattva-jñānān mokṣa-prāptiḥ na karma-samuccitāt iti niścito 'rthaḥ | yathā cāyam arthaḥ, tathā prakaraṇaśo vibhajya tatra tatra darśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the teaching of the <s>Gītā</s>, the established meaning is that liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is attained from knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>) alone, not from [knowledge] combined with action. And we shall show how this meaning [holds], by dividing [the text] section by section, in the relevant places.

children.text: tatraiva dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetaso mithyā-jñānavato mahati śoka-sāgare nimagnasya arjunasya anyatrātma-jñānād uddharaṇam apaśyan bhagavān vāsudevaḥ tataḥ kṛpayā arjunam uddidhārayiṣuḥ ātma-jñānāyāvatārayann āha -
children.translated_text: Therein, seeing no means of rescue for <s>Arjuna</s> — whose mind was confused about <s>dharma</s>, who held false knowledge, and who was submerged in the great ocean of grief — other than the knowledge of the Self (<s>ātmajñāna</s>), the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, out of compassion, desiring to uplift <s>Arjuna</s>, leading him toward Self-knowledge, said —

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñā-vādāṃś ca bhāṣase |
children.translated_text: You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom;

children.text: gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||BhG_2.11||
children.translated_text: the wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living. // <s>BhG</s> 2.11 //

children.text:
na śocyā aśocyāḥ bhīṣma-droṇādayaḥ | sad-vṛttatvāt paramārtha-svarūpeṇa ca nityatvāt, tān aśocyān anvaśoco 'nuśocitavān asi te mriyante man-nimittam, ahaṃ tair vinābhūtaḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmi rājya-sukhādinā iti | tvaṃ prajñā-vādān prajñāvatāṃ buddhimatāṃ vādāṃś ca vacanāni ca bhāṣase | tad etat mauḍhyaṃ pāṇḍityaṃ ca viruddham ātmani darśayasi unmatta iva ity abhiprāyaḥ | yasmāt gatāsūn gata-prāṇān mṛtān, agatāsūn agata-prāṇān jīvataś ca
nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ātmajñāḥ | paṇḍā ātma-viṣayā buddhir yeṣāṃ te hi paṇḍitāḥ, pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya [BAU 3.5.1] iti śruteḥ | paramārthatas tu tān nityān aśocyān anuśocasi, ato mūḍho 'si ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.11||
children.translated_text:
Not to be grieved for — <s>aśocya</s> — are <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and others, because of their virtuous conduct and because of their eternality in their ultimate nature (<s>paramārthasvarūpa</s>). You have grieved for those who should not be grieved for — [thinking] 'they will die on my account; bereft of them, what shall I do with royal pleasures and the like?' And you speak words of wisdom (<s>prajñāvāda</s>) — the speeches of the wise, the sayings of the intelligent. Thus you display in yourself this contradictory combination of foolishness and learning, like a madman — this is the purport. Because the wise (<s>paṇḍita</s>) — those who know the Self (<s>ātmajña</s>) — do not grieve for the dead (<s>gatāsu</s>), those whose life-breaths have departed, nor for the living (<s>agatāsu</s>), those whose life-breaths have not departed.
<s>Paṇḍitāḥ</s> (the wise) are those who possess <s>paṇḍā</s>, intellect pertaining to the Self — as per the <s>Śruti</s>: '<s>pāṇḍityaṃ nirvidya</s>' (having transcended learning) [<s>BAU</s> 3.5.1]. But in the ultimate sense, you grieve for those who are eternal and not to be grieved for — therefore the purport is: you are deluded. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.11 //

children.text: kutas te aśocyāḥ ? yato nityāḥ | katham ?
children.translated_text: Why are they not to be grieved for? Because they are eternal. How so?

children.text: na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ |
children.translated_text: Never indeed was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these rulers of men;

children.text: na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param ||BhG_2.12||
children.translated_text: nor shall we ever cease to exist hereafter. // <s>BhG</s> 2.12 //

children.text: na tv eva jātu kadācid ahaṃ nāsam kintv āsam eva | atīteṣu dehotpatti-vināśeṣu ghaṭādiṣu viyad iva nitya eva aham āsam ity abhiprāyaḥ | tathā na tvaṃ nāsīḥ, kintv āsīr eva | tathā neme janādhipā āsan kintv āsann eva | tathā na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ, kintu bhaviṣyāma eva, sarve vayam ato 'smād deha-vināśāt param uttara-kāle 'pi | triṣv api kāleṣu nityā ātma-svarūpeṇa ity arthaḥ | dehābhedānuvṛttyā bahu-vacanam, nātma-bhedābhiprāyeṇa ||BhGS_2.12||
children.translated_text: Never indeed (<s>na tu eva jātu</s>) — at no time was I non-existent; rather, I existed indeed. The purport is: through the past productions and destructions of bodies, like space in pots etc., I, as the eternal [Self], indeed existed. Likewise, you were not non-existent — rather, you existed indeed. Likewise, these rulers of men were not non-existent — rather, they existed indeed. Likewise, we shall not cease to exist — rather, we shall certainly exist, all of us, after (<s>param</s>) this destruction of the body, in the future time as well. The meaning is: in all three times, [we are] eternal in our essential nature as the Self. The use of the plural is in accordance with the continuity of bodily distinctions, not with the intention of [implying] a multiplicity of Selves. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.12 //

children.text: tatra katham iva nitya ātmeti dṛṣṭāntam āha -
children.translated_text: There, to illustrate how the Self is eternal, He gives an example —

children.text: dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
children.translated_text: Just as in this body the embodied [Self] [passes through] childhood, youth, and old age,

children.text: tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati ||BhG_2.13||
children.translated_text: so too is the attainment of another body; the wise person is not deluded by this. // <s>BhG</s> 2.13 //

children.text: deho 'sya astīti dehī, tasya dehino dehavataḥ ātmano 'smin vartamāne dehā yathā yena prakāreṇa kaumāraṃ kumāra-bhāvo bālyāvasthā, yauvanaṃ yūno bhāvo madhyamāvasthā, jarā vayo-hāniḥ jīrṇāvasthā, ity etāḥ tisro 'vasthāḥ anyonya-vilakṣaṇāḥ | tāsāṃ prathamāvasthā-nāśe na nāśaḥ, dvitīyāvasthopajane na upajana ātmanaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ?avikriyasyaiva dvitīya-tṛtīyāvasthā-prāptiḥ ātmano dṛṣṭā | tathā tadvad eva dehād anyo deho dehāntaram, tasya prāptiḥ dehāntara-prāptiḥ avikriyasyaiva ātmana ity arthaḥ | dhīro dhīmān tatraivaṃ sati na muhyati na moham āpadyate ||BhGS_2.13||
children.translated_text: One who has a body (<s>deha</s>) is the embodied one (<s>dehin</s>). Of that embodied one, that Self possessing a body, in this present body — just as, in whatever manner — childhood (<s>kaumāra</s>), the state of being a child, the stage of infancy; youth (<s>yauvana</s>), the state of being young, the middle stage; old age (<s>jarā</s>), the decline of age, the stage of decrepitude — these three stages are mutually distinct from one another. Upon the destruction of the first stage, there is no destruction [of the Self]; upon the arising of the second stage, there is no arising of the Self. What then? The attainment of the second and third stages is observed for the Self which itself remains unchanged (<s>avikriya</s>). Similarly, just so — another body from a body is '<s>dehāntara</s>' (another body); its attainment is '<s>dehāntaraprāpti</s>' (attainment of another body) — of the Self which itself remains unchanged — this is the meaning. The wise one (<s>dhīra</s>), the intelligent one, in that case, is not deluded — does not fall into delusion. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.13 //

children.text:
==============================
yadyapy ātma-vināśa-nimitto moho na saṃbhavati nitya ātmā iti vijānataḥ, tathāpi śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-prāpti-nimitto moho laukiko dṛśyate, sukha-viyoga-nimitto moho duḥkha-saṃyoga-nimitta ca śokaḥ | ity etad arjunasya vacanam āśaṅkaya bhagavān āha -
children.translated_text:
==============================
Even though delusion caused by the destruction of the Self is not possible for one who knows the Self to be eternal, still, delusion caused by the attainment of cold, heat, pleasure, and pain is seen in the world — delusion caused by separation from pleasure, and grief caused by conjunction with pain. Anticipating this as <s>Arjuna</s>'s objection, the Blessed Lord said —

children.text: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkhadāḥ |
children.translated_text: The contacts of the senses with their objects, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, which give rise to cold, heat, pleasure, and pain —

children.text: āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṃs titikṣasva bhārata ||BhG_2.14||
children.translated_text: they come and go, they are impermanent; endure them, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 2.14 //

children.text: mātrā ābhiḥ mīyante śabdādaya iti śrotrādīni indriyāṇi | mātrāṇāṃ sparśāḥ śabdādibhiḥ saṃyogāḥ | te śītoṣṇasukha-duḥkha-dāḥ śītam uṣṇaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca prayacchantīti | athavā spṛśyanta iti sparśā viṣayāḥ śabdādayaḥ | mātrāś ca sparśāś ca śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ | śītaṃ kadācit sukhaṃ kadācit duḥkham | tathā uṣṇam api aniyata-svarūpam | sukha-duḥkhe punaḥ niyata-rūpe yato na vyabhicarataḥ | atas tābhyāṃ pṛthak śītoṣṇayoḥ grahaṇam | yasmāt te mātrā-sparśādayaḥ āgamāpāyinaḥ āgamāpāyaśīlāḥ tasmāt anityāḥ | ataḥ tān śītoṣṇādīn titikṣasva prasahasva | teṣu harṣaṃ viṣādaṃ vā mā kārṣīḥ ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.14||
children.translated_text: '<s>Mātrāḥ</s>' — the senses such as hearing etc., by which sounds and other [objects] are measured (<s>mīyante</s>). The contacts (<s>sparśa</s>) of the <s>mātrās</s> are the conjunctions with sounds and other [objects]. They give cold, heat, pleasure, and pain — that is, they produce cold, heat, pleasure, and pain. Alternatively, '<s>sparśāḥ</s>' (contacts) — [meaning] things that are touched — are the objects: sound and the rest. Both the <s>mātrās</s> (senses) and the <s>sparśas</s> (objects) give cold, heat, pleasure, and pain. Cold is sometimes pleasant, sometimes painful; likewise, heat too is of an indeterminate nature. But pleasure and pain have a fixed nature, since they do not deviate. Therefore, cold and heat are mentioned separately from these two. Since those contacts of the senses etc. are '<s>āgamāpāyinaḥ</s>' — of the nature of coming and going — therefore they are impermanent (<s>anitya</s>). Hence, endure (<s>titikṣasva</s>) — bear with — those cold and heat etc. Do not give way to elation or despondency regarding them — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.14 //

children.text:
==============================
śītoṣṇādīn sahataḥ kiṃ syād iti śṛṇu ---
children.translated_text:
==============================
What would result from enduring cold, heat, etc.? Listen —

children.text: yaṃ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha |
children.translated_text: That person whom these [contacts] do not afflict, O best among men,

children.text: sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate ||BhG_2.15||
children.translated_text: who is equal in pain and pleasure, who is steadfast — he is fit for immortality. // <s>BhG</s> 2.15 //

children.text: yaṃ hi puruṣaṃ same duḥkha-sukhe yasya taṃ sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ sukha-duḥkha-prāptau harṣa-viṣāda-rahitaṃ dhīraṃ dhīmantaṃ na vyathayanti na cālayanti nityātma-darśanāt ete yathoktāḥ śītoṣṇādayaḥ, sa nityātma-svarūpa-darśa-niṣṭho dvandva-sahiṣṇuḥ amṛtatvāya amṛta-bhāvāya mokṣāyety arthaḥ kalpate samartho bhavati ||BhGS_2.15||
children.translated_text: That person for whom pain and pleasure are equal — i.e., who is free from elation and despondency upon the attainment of pleasure and pain — who is steadfast (<s>dhīra</s>), intelligent, whom these aforementioned [contacts of] cold, heat, etc. do not afflict, do not shake, because of the vision of the eternal Self — that person, established in the vision of the eternal nature of the Self, enduring the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>), is fit for immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), i.e., the state of being immortal, meaning <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — becomes capable [of attaining it]. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.15 //

children.text: itaś ca śoka-mohau akṛtvā śītoṣṇādi-sahanaṃ yuktam, yasmāt ---
children.translated_text: And for this further reason, it is proper to endure cold, heat, etc. without giving way to grief and delusion, because —

children.text: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ |
children.translated_text: Of the non-existent there is no coming into being; of the existent there is no cessation of being;

children.text: ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ ||BhG_2.16||
children.translated_text: the conclusion regarding both of these has been seen by the seers of truth. // <s>BhG</s> 2.16 //

children.text: na asato 'vidyamānasya śītoṣṇādeḥ sa-kāraṇasya na vidyate nāsti bhāvo bhavanam astitā ||
children.translated_text: Of the non-existent (<s>asat</s>) — of that which does not [truly] exist, namely cold, heat, etc. together with their causes — there is no being (<s>bhāva</s>), no coming into existence, no real existence.

children.text: na hi śītoṣṇādi sa-kāraṇaṃ pramāṇair nirūpyamāṇaṃ vastu sambhavati | vikāro hi saḥ, vikāraś ca vyabhicarati | yathā ghaṭādi-saṃsthānaṃ cakṣuṣā nirūpyamāṇaṃ mṛd-vyatirekeṇānupalabdher asat | tathā sarvo vikāraḥ kāraṇa-vyatirekeṇānupalabdher asat | janma-pradhvaṃsābhyāṃ prāg ūrdhvaṃ cānupalabdheḥ | kāryasya ghaṭādeḥ mṛd-ādi-kāraṇasya ca tat-kāraṇa-vyatirekeṇānupalabdher asattvam ||
children.translated_text: For cold, heat, etc. together with their causes, when examined by the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), do not have real existence (<s>vastu</s>). For it [the effect] is a modification (<s>vikāra</s>), and a modification is subject to deviation. Just as the configuration of a pot etc., when examined by sight, is non-existent (<s>asat</s>) because it is not perceived apart from clay — so too every modification is non-existent because it is not perceived apart from its cause; because it is not perceived before origination and after destruction. The non-existence of the effect such as pot etc. and of the cause such as clay etc. [follows] from non-perception apart from their respective causes.

children.text: tad-asattve sarvābhāva-prasaṅga iti cet, na | sarvatra buddhi-dvayopalabdheḥ, sad-buddhir asad-buddhir iti | yad-viṣayā buddhir na vyabhicarati, tat sat | yad-viṣayā vyabhicarati, tad asat | iti sad-asad-vibhāge buddhi-tantre sthite | sarvatra dve buddhī sarvair upalabhyete samānādhikaraṇe na nīlotpalavat, san ghaṭaḥ san paṭaḥ, san hastī iti | evaṃ sarvatra | tayor buddhyoḥ ghaṭādi-buddhir vyabhicarati | tathā ca darśitam | na tu sad-buddhiḥ | tasmāt ghaṭādi-buddhi-viṣayo 'san, vyabhicārāt | na tu sad-buddhi-viṣayaḥ, avyabhicārāt ||
children.translated_text: If [you say] that in the non-existence of that, the consequence would be the non-existence of everything — no, because everywhere two cognitions are perceived: the cognition 'it exists' and the cognition 'it is non-existent.' That with respect to which the cognition does not deviate is real (<s>sat</s>); that with respect to which it deviates is unreal (<s>asat</s>). Thus, when the distinction between real and unreal is established as dependent on cognition — everywhere, two cognitions are perceived by all [people] in the same substratum — not like 'blue lotus' [where the two refer to different things] — [but rather:] 'the pot exists,' 'the cloth exists,' 'the elephant exists' — thus everywhere. Of these two cognitions, the pot-cognition deviates [i.e., the pot is sometimes not perceived]. And this has been shown. But the existence-cognition does not [deviate]. Therefore, the object of the pot-cognition is unreal, because of deviation; but the object of the existence-cognition is not [unreal], because of non-deviation.

children.text: ghaṭe vinaṣṭe ghaṭa-buddhau vyabhicarantyāṃ sad-buddhir api vyabhicaratīti cet na | paṭād evapi sad-buddhi-darśanāt | viśeṣaṇa-viṣayaiva sā sad-buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Objection: when the pot is destroyed and the pot-cognition deviates, the existence-cognition also deviates. Reply: No, because the existence-cognition is seen [to persist] even with respect to cloth etc. That existence-cognition has as its object the qualifier [i.e., existence as a universal qualifier].

children.text: sad-buddhivat ghaṭa-buddhir api ghaṭāntarā dṛśyata iti cet, na | paṭādau adarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: just as with the existence-cognition, the pot-cognition too is seen [to arise again] in another pot. Reply: No, because it is not seen in cloth etc.

children.text: sad-buddhir api naṣṭe ghaṭe na dṛśyata iti cet, na | viśeṣyābhāvāt | sad-buddhir viśeṣaṇa-viṣayā satī viśeṣyābhāve viśeṣaṇānupapattau kiṃ-viṣayā syāt ? na tu punaḥ sad-buddheḥ viṣayābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: the existence-cognition too is not seen when the pot is destroyed. Reply: No, because of the absence of the qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>). The existence-cognition, having the qualifier as its object, when the qualificand is absent — since the qualifier cannot be established [without a qualificand] — what would be its object? But this does not mean that the object of the existence-cognition [itself] is absent.

children.text: ekādhikaraṇatvaṃ ghaṭādi-viśeṣyābhāve na yuktam iti cet, na | idam udakam iti marīcy-ādau anyatarābhāve 'pi sāmānādhikaraṇya-darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: co-residence (<s>ekādhikaraṇatva</s>) is not proper when the qualificand such as pot is absent. Reply: No, because co-residence is seen even when one [of the two referents] is absent, as in 'this is water' [said of a mirage] etc.

children.text: tasmād dehāder dvandvasya ca sa-kāraṇasya asato na vidyate bhāva iti | tathā sataś ca ātmano 'bhāvo 'vidyamānatā na vidyate, sarvatrāvyabhicārāt ity avocāma ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, of the non-existent — the body, the pairs of opposites, and their causes — there is no coming into being. Likewise, of the existent — of the Self — there is no non-existence, no state of non-being, because it is never subject to deviation anywhere — as we have stated.

children.text: evam ātmānātmanoḥ sad-asatoḥ ubhayor api dṛṣṭaḥ upalabdho 'nto nirṇayaḥ sat sad eva, asat asad eveti, tv anayoḥ yathoktayoḥ tattva-darśibhiḥ | tad iti sarva-nāma sarvaṃ ca brahma, tasya nāma tad iti, tad-bhāvas tattvam, brahmaṇo yāthātmyam | tad draṣṭuṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te tattva-darśinaḥ, tais tattva-darśibhiḥ | tvam api tattva-darśināṃ dṛṣṭim āśritya śokaṃ mohaṃ ca hitvā śītoṣṇādīni niyatāniyata-rūpāṇi dvandvāni vikāro 'yam asann eva marīci-jalavan mithyāvabhāsate iti manasi niścitya titikṣasva ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.16||
children.translated_text: Thus, regarding both — the existent and the non-existent, the Self and the non-Self — the conclusion (<s>anta</s>) has been seen, ascertained: the real is real alone, the unreal is unreal alone — by the seers of truth (<s>tattvadarśin</s>), regarding these two as described. '<s>Tat</s>' is a pronoun denoting everything; and everything is <s>Brahman</s>; its name is '<s>tat</s>' (that); '<s>tattva</s>' is the state of being '<s>tat</s>,' the true nature of <s>Brahman</s>. Those whose habit it is to see that are '<s>tattvadarśinaḥ</s>' (seers of truth); by such seers of truth. The purport is: you too, relying on the vision of the seers of truth, abandoning grief and delusion, having firmly determined in your mind that this modification [the world] is merely unreal, appearing falsely like water in a mirage — endure the pairs of opposites, whether of fixed or unfixed nature — [namely] cold, heat, etc. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.16 //

children.text: kiṃ punas tat yat sad eva sarvadaiva astīti | ucyate ---
children.translated_text: What then is that which always and forever exists as real? It is said —

children.text: avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam |
children.translated_text: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded;

children.text: vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaścit kartum arhati ||BhG_2.17||
children.translated_text: no one is able to cause the destruction of this imperishable [Self]. // <s>BhG</s> 2.17 //

children.text: avināśi na vinaṣṭuṃ śīlaṃ yasyeti | tu-śabdo 'sato viśeṣaṇārthaḥ | tat viddhi vijānīhi | kim ? yena sarvam idaṃ jagat tataṃ vyāptaṃ sad-ākhyena brahmaṇā sākāśam, ākāśenaiva ghaṭādayaḥ | vināśam adarśanam abhāvam | avyayasya na vyeti upacayāpacayau na yāti iti avyayaṃ tasya avyayasya | naitat sadākhyaṃ brahma svena rūpeṇa vyeti vyabhicarati, niravayavatvāt, dehādivat | nāpy ātmīyena, ātmīyābhāvāt | yathā devadatto dhana-hānyā vyeti, na tu evaṃ brahma vyeti | ato 'vyayasya asya brahmaṇaḥ vināśaṃ na kaścit kartum arhati, na kaścit atmānaṃ vināśayituṃ śaknoti īśvaro 'pi | ātmā hi brahma, svātmani ca kriyāvirodhāt ||BhGS_2.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Avināśi</s>' — that whose nature (<s>śīla</s>) it is not to perish. The word '<s>tu</s>' (but) serves to distinguish [the imperishable] from the unreal. '<s>Tat viddhi</s>' — know it, understand it. What? That by which all this world is pervaded (<s>tata</s>) — by <s>Brahman</s> called 'Being' (<s>sat</s>), together with space — as pots etc. [are pervaded] by space itself. '<s>Vināśa</s>' — disappearance, non-existence. '<s>Avyayasya</s>' — that which does not undergo increase or decrease is <s>avyaya</s> (imperishable); of that imperishable [<s>Brahman</s>]. This <s>Brahman</s> called 'Being' does not deviate from its own nature, because it is without parts, unlike the body etc. Nor [does it deviate] through [the loss of] what belongs to it, because it possesses nothing as its own. Just as <s>Devadatta</s> declines through loss of wealth — <s>Brahman</s> does not decline thus. Therefore, no one can bring about the destruction of this imperishable <s>Brahman</s>; no one can destroy the Self, not even God (<s>Īśvara</s>). For the Self is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, and with respect to one's own Self, action is contradictory. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.17||

children.text: kiṃ punas tad asat yat svātma-sattāṃ vyabhicaratīti, ucyate -
children.translated_text: What then is that 'unreal' which deviates from its own existence as the Self? It is stated:

children.text: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: These bodies of the eternal, indestructible embodied one

children.text: anāśino 'prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata ||BhG_2.18||
children.translated_text: are said to have an end — of the immeasurable one; therefore fight, O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||<s>BhG</s> 2.18||

children.text: antaḥ vināśaḥ vidyate yeṣāṃ te antavantaḥ | yathā mṛgatṛṣṇikādau sad-buddhiḥ anuvṛttā pramāṇanirūpaṇānte vicchidyate, sa tasya antaḥ | tathā ime dehāḥ svapnamāyādehādivaca antavantaḥ nityasya śarīriṇaḥ śarīravato 'nāśino 'prameyarya ātmano 'ntavanta iti uktāḥ vivekibhirity arthaḥ | nityasya anāśinaḥ iti na punaruktam | nityatvasya dvividhatvāt lokā, nāśasya ca | yathā deho bhasmībhūto 'darśanaṃ gato naṣṭa ucyate | vidyamāno 'pi yathā anyathā pariṇato vyādhyādi-yukto jāto naṣṭa ucyate | tatra nityasya ṭh anāśinaḥ iti dvividhenāpi nāśena asaṃbandho 'syety arthaḥ | anyathā pṛthivyādivad api nityatvaṃ syāt ātmanaḥ | tat mā bhūditi nityasya anāśinaḥ ityāha | aprameyamya na prameyasya pratyakṣādi-pramāṇaiḥ aparicchādyasyety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Antavantaḥ</s>' — those in which there is an end, i.e., destruction. Just as the cognition of reality superimposed on a mirage etc. is cut off when examined by the means of valid knowledge — that is its end. Similarly, these bodies — like bodies in dreams, magical illusions, etc. — have an end. 'Of the eternal embodied one' — of the one possessing a body — 'of the indestructible, immeasurable Self — they have an end' — thus it is declared by the discriminating, this is the meaning. 'Eternal' and 'indestructible' is not a repetition, because there are two kinds of eternality in common usage, and two kinds of destruction. For instance, a body that has been reduced to ashes and has disappeared is called 'destroyed.' And even an existing [thing] that has been transformed into something different — afflicted by disease etc. — is [also] called 'destroyed.' In this context, 'eternal' and 'indestructible' means that it is unconnected with destruction of either kind — this is the meaning. Otherwise, even the eternality of earth etc. would apply to the Self. Lest that be the case, he says 'eternal' and 'indestructible.' '<s>Aprameyasya</s>' — of that which is not measurable, i.e., not delimited by means of valid knowledge such as perception etc. — this is the meaning.

children.text: nanu āgamena ātmā paricchidyate, pratyakṣādinā ca pūrvam | na | ātmanaḥ svataḥsiddhatvāt | sirā hi ātmani pramātari pramitsoḥ pramāṇānveṣaṇā bhavati | na hi pūrvam itthamaham iti ātmānamapramāya pa cāt prameyaparicchādāya pravartate | na hi ātmā nāma kasyacit aprasiddho bhavati | śāstraṃ tu antyaṃ pramāṇam atad-dharmādhyāropaṇa-mātra-nivartakatvena pramāṇatvam ātmanaḥ pratipadyate, na hy ajñātārthajñāpakatvena | tathā ca śrutiḥ --- yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaraḥ [BAU 3.4.1] iti | yasmād evaṃ nityo 'vikriyaś cātmā tasmād yudhyasva, yuddhād uparamaṃ mā kārṣīḥ ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: the Self is delimited by scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and by perception etc. previously. No — because the Self is self-established (<s>svataḥsiddha</s>). For indeed, the search for a means of valid knowledge is undertaken by the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>) who desires to know, [and this search takes place] with respect to the Self. For one does not first not-know the Self in the form 'I am thus,' and then subsequently proceed to delimit the object of knowledge. For the Self is never unknown to anyone. Scripture, however, being the ultimate means of valid knowledge, attains the status of being a means of valid knowledge with respect to the Self only by removing the superimposition of properties that do not belong to it — not by making known what was previously unknown. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [declares]: 'That which is directly perceived, not remote — the <s>Brahman</s> that is the Self, innermost of all' [<s>BAU</s> 3.4.1]. Since the Self is thus eternal and without modification — 'therefore fight' — the meaning is: do not withdraw from battle.

children.text: na hy atra yuddha-kartavyatā vidhīyate, yuddhe pravṛtta eva hi asau śoka-moha-pratibaddhaḥ tūṣṇīm āste | ataḥ tasya pratibandhāpanayana-mātraṃ bhagavatā kriyate | tasmād yudhyasva iti anuvāda-mātram, na vidhiḥ ||BhGS_2.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For indeed, the duty of fighting is not being enjoined here; for he [<s>Arjuna</s>] was already engaged in battle, but hindered by grief and delusion, sat silent. Therefore, the Lord merely removes that obstruction. 'Therefore fight' is a mere restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), not an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.18||

children.text: śoka-mohādi-saṃsāra-kāraṇa-nivṛtty-arthaṃ gītā-śāstram, na pravartakam ity etasyārthasya sākṣi-bhūte ṛcau ānināya bhagavān | yat tu manyase yuddhā bhīṣmādayo mayā hanyante aham eva teṣāṃ hantā iti, eṣā buddhir mṛṣaiva te | katham ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The teaching of the <s>Gītā</s> is for the cessation of the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> such as grief, delusion, etc. — it is not a prompting [to action]. The Lord adduced two <s>Ṛc</s> verses as testimony to this meaning. As for what you think — 'by my fighting, <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others are slain; I am indeed their slayer' — this understanding of yours is entirely false. How?

children.text: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaś cainaṃ manyate hatam |
children.translated_text: He who thinks this [Self] to be the slayer, and he who thinks it to be slain —

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate ||BhG_2.19||
children.translated_text: both of them do not understand; this [Self] neither slays nor is slain. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.19||

children.text: ya enaṃ prakṛtaṃ dehinaṃ vetti vijānāti hantāraṃ hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartāraṃ ya ca enam anyo manyate hataṃ deha-hananena hato 'ham iti hanana-kriyāyāḥ karma-bhūtam | tau ubhau na vijānītaḥ na jñātavantau avivekena ātmānam | hantā ahaṃ, hato 'smy aham iti deha-hananena ātmānam ahaṃ pratyaya-viṣayaṃ yau vijānītaḥ tau ātma-svarūpānabhijñau ity arthaḥ | yasmāt na ayam atmā hanti na hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartā bhavati, na ca hanyate na ca karma bhavatīty arthaḥ, avikriyatvāt ||BhGS_2.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] He who knows (<s>vetti</s>) — understands — this being under discussion, the embodied one, to be the slayer — the agent of the act of killing; and another who thinks it to be slain — 'I am slain through the killing of the body' — the object of the act of killing. These two, both of them, do not understand — they have not known the Self, through lack of discrimination.
