Those who understand 'I am the slayer' and 'I am slain' through the killing of the body — regarding the Self which is the object of the 'I'-notion — they are ignorant of the true nature of the Self, this is the meaning. Because this Self does not slay — is not the agent of the act of killing — nor is it slain — nor is it the object — this is the meaning; because it is without modification (<s>avikriya</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.19||

children.text: katham avikriya ātmeti dvitīyo mantraḥ --
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How is the Self without modification? The second verse [states]:

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin
children.translated_text: It is never born, nor does it ever die;

children.text: nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: nor, having once been, will it ever cease to be again.

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo
children.translated_text: Unborn, eternal, everlasting, and primeval —

children.text: na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||BhG_2.20||
children.translated_text: it is not slain when the body is slain. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.20||

children.text: na jāyate notpadyate, jani-lakṣaṇā vastu-vikriyā na ātmano vidyate ity arthaḥ | tathā na mriyate vā | vā-śabdaḥ cārthe | na mriyate ca iti antyā vināśa-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate | kadācic chabdaḥ sarva-vikriyā-pratiṣedhaiḥ saṃbadhyate -- na kadācit jāyate, na kadācit mriyate, ity evam | yasmāt ayam ātmā bhūtvā bhavana-kriyām anubhūya paścāt abhavitā abhāvaṃ gantā na bhūyaḥ punaḥ, tasmāt na mriyate | yo hi bhūtvā na bhavitā sa mriyata ity ucyate lokā | vā-śabdāt na-śabdāc ca ayam ātmā abhūtvā vā bhavitā dehavat na bhūyaḥ | tasmāt na jāyate | yo hi abhūtvā bhavitā sa jāyata ity ucyate | naivam ātmā | ato na jāyate | yasmād evaṃ tasmāt ajaḥ, yasmāt na mriyate tasmāt nityaś ca |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Na jāyate</s>' — is not produced; the modification of a thing characterized by birth does not exist in the Self — this is the meaning. Likewise, '<s>na mriyate vā</s>' — the particle '<s>vā</s>' is in the sense of 'and' — 'and does not die' — the final modification characterized by destruction is negated. The word '<s>kadācit</s>' (ever) connects with all the negations of modifications: it is never born, it never dies — thus. Since this Self, having undergone the process of becoming (<s>bhavana</s>), is not going to subsequently become non-existent (<s>abhāva</s>) again — therefore it does not die. For in common usage, one who, having existed, will not [continue to] exist, is said to 'die.' From the particle '<s>vā</s>' and '<s>na</s>': this Self, not having existed previously, is not going to come into existence like a body — again. Therefore it is not born. For in common usage, one who, not having existed, comes into existence, is said to be 'born.' The Self is not like this. Therefore it is not born. Since this is so, therefore it is '<s>aja</s>' (unborn); and since it does not die, therefore it is '<s>nitya</s>' (eternal).

children.text: yadyapi ādy-antayor vikriyayoḥ pratiṣedhe sarvā vikriyāḥ pratiṣiddhā bhavanti, tathāpi madhya-bhāvinīnāṃ vikriyāṇāṃ sva-śabdair eva pratiṣedhaḥ kartavyo 'nuktānām api yauvanādi-samasta-vikriyāṇāṃ pratiṣedho yathā syāt ity āha-- śāśvata ity ādinā | śāśvata iti apakṣaya-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate | śaśvad-bhavaḥ śāśvataḥ | na apakṣīyate svarūpeṇa, niravayavatvāt | nāpi guṇa-kṣayeṇa apakṣayaḥ, nirguṇatvāt | apakṣaya-viparītāpi vṛddhi-lakṣaṇā vikriyā pratiṣidhyate --- purāṇa iti | yo hi avayavāgamena upacīyate sa vardhate abhinava iti ca ucyate | ayaṃ tu ātmā niravayavatvāt purāpi nava eveti purāṇaḥ na vardhate ity arthaḥ | tathā na hanyate | hantiḥ atra vipariṇāmārthe draṣṭavyo 'punaruktatāyai | na vipariṇamyate ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Although through the negation of the modifications at the beginning and end, all modifications are negated, nevertheless, the intermediate modifications must be explicitly negated by their own words, so that even the unstated modifications such as youth etc. may be negated — thus he says '<s>śāśvata</s>' etc. By '<s>śāśvata</s>' (everlasting), the modification characterized by decay is negated. That which exists perpetually is <s>śāśvata</s>. It does not decay in its own nature, because it is without parts. Nor is there decay through the diminution of qualities, because it is without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). The modification of growth, which is the opposite of decay, is also negated — by '<s>purāṇa</s>' (primeval). For that which is augmented by the accretion of parts grows and is called 'new.' But this Self, being without parts, is 'ever new even of old' — hence <s>purāṇa</s>, meaning it does not grow. Likewise, '<s>na hanyate</s>' — the root '<s>han</s>' here should be understood in the sense of transformation, to avoid redundancy. The meaning is: it does not undergo transformation.

children.text: hanyamāne vipariṇamyamāne 'pi śarīrāḥ | asmin mantre ṣaḍ-bhāva-vikārā laukika-vastu-vikriyā ātmani pratiṣidhyante | sarva-prakāra-vikriyā-rahita ātmā iti vākyārthaḥ | yasmād evaṃ tasmāt ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ iti pūrveṇa mantreṇa asya saṃbandhaḥ ||BhGS_2.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '[Not slain] when the body is being slain' — even when the body is undergoing transformation. In this verse, the six modifications of worldly things are negated with respect to the Self. The meaning of the sentence is: the Self is devoid of all kinds of modification. Since this is so, therefore 'both of them do not understand' — its connection is with the preceding verse. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.20||

children.text: ya enaṃ vetti hantāram ityanena mantreṇa hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartā karma ca na bhavati iti pratijñāya, na jāyate ity anena avikriyatvaṃ hetum uktvā pratijñātārtham upasaṃharati--
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having declared through the verse 'He who thinks this to be the slayer' that [the Self] is neither the agent nor the object of the act of killing, and having stated with '<s>na jāyate</s>' (it is not born) the reason — namely, its being without modification — he now concludes the proposition:

children.text: vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam |
children.translated_text: He who knows this [Self] to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and imperishable —

children.text: kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam ||BhG_2.21||
children.translated_text: how, O <s>Pārtha</s>, can that person cause anyone to slay, or slay anyone? ||<s>BhG</s> 2.21||

children.text: veda vijānāti avināśinam antya-bhāva-vikāra-rahitaṃ nityaṃ vipariṇāma-rahitaṃ yo veda iti saṃbandhaḥ | enaṃ pūrveṇa matreṇokta-lakṣaṇam ajaṃ janma-rahitam avyayam apakṣaya-rahitaṃ kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa sa vidvān puruṣo 'dhikṛtaḥ hanti hanana-kriyāṃ karoti, kathaṃ vā ghātayati hantāraṃ prayojayati | na kathaṃcit kaṃcit hanti, na kathaṃcit kaṃcit ghātayati iti ubhayatra ākṣepaḥ evārthaḥ praśnārthāsaṃbhavāt | hetv-arthasya ca avikriyatvasya tulyatvāt viduṣaḥ sarva-karma-pratiṣedha eva prakaraṇārtho 'bhipreto bhagavatā | hantes tu ākṣepaḥ udāharaṇārthatvena kathitaḥ | viduṣaḥ kaṃ karmāsaṃbhave hetu-viśeṣaṃ paśyan karmāṇy ākṣipati bhagavān kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Veda</s>' — knows it to be indestructible — devoid of the final modification of non-existence; eternal — devoid of transformation; the connection is: 'he who knows.' This [Self] of the characteristics stated in the preceding verse — unborn, devoid of birth; imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>), devoid of decay. How — by what means — can that learned person who is qualified slay — perform the act of killing; or how can he cause to slay — instigate a slayer? In no way does he slay anyone, in no way does he cause anyone to slay — in both cases the meaning is a rhetorical question (<s>ākṣepa</s>), since the possibility of a genuine question does not exist. Since the reason — namely, the absence of modification — applies equally, the meaning of the context intended by the Lord is the negation of all action for the knower of truth. The rhetorical question about killing is stated as an illustration. The Lord, seeing what specific reason for the impossibility of action the wise one has, rhetorically questions all actions — 'how can that person?'

children.text: nanu ukta evātmano 'vikriyatvaṃ sarva-karmāsaṃbhava-kāraṇa-viśeṣaḥ | satyam uktaḥ | na tu sa kāraṇa-viśeṣaḥ, anyatvāt viduṣo 'vikriyād ātmanaḥ | na hi avikriyaṃ sthāṇuṃ viditavataḥ karma na saṃbhavati iti cet, na | viduṣaḥ ātmatvāt | na dehādi-saṃghātasya vidvattā | ataḥ pāriśeṣyāt asaṃhata ātmā vidvān avikriyaḥ iti tasya viduṣaḥ karmāsaṃbhavāt ākṣepo yuktaḥ kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ iti | yathā buddhyādy āhṛtasya śabdādy-arthasya avikriya eva san buddhi-vṛtty-aviveka-vijñānena avidyayā upalabdhā ātmā kalpyate, evam eva ātmānātma-viveka-jñānena buddhi-vṛttyā vidyā asatya-rūpayaiva paramārthato 'vikriya eva ātmā vidvān ucyate | viduṣaḥ karmāsaṃbhava-vacanāt yāni karmāṇi śāstreṇa vidhīyante tāni aviduṣo vihitāni iti bhagavato niścayo 'vagamyate ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: the absence of modification of the Self has already been stated as the specific reason for the impossibility of all action. True, it has been stated. But that is not [merely] a general reason [for the impossibility of action], because the knower is different from the modification-free Self. For it cannot be said that action is impossible for one who has known an immovable post — [if this is the objection,] no, because the knower is the Self itself. Knowledge does not belong to the aggregate of body etc. Therefore, by elimination, the non-aggregate Self is the knower, and being without modification, action is impossible for that knower — hence the rhetorical question 'how can that person?' is justified. Just as the Self is attributed — though actually without modification — as the perceiver of the objects such as sound etc. brought [to it] by the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) etc., through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) consisting in the non-discrimination from the modifications of the intellect — in exactly the same way, the Self, which is in ultimate truth without modification, is called 'the knower' through the modification of the intellect in the form of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), which itself is of an unreal nature. Since [the Lord] states that action is impossible for the knower, it is understood that the Lord's conclusion is that the actions enjoined by scripture are enjoined for the non-knower.

children.text:
nanu vidyāpi aviduṣa eva vidhīyate, vidita-vidyasya piṣṭa-peṣaṇavat vidyā-vidhānānarthakyāt | tatra aviduṣaḥ karmāṇi vidhīyante na viduṣaḥ iti viśeṣo nopapadyate iti cet, na | anuṣṭheyasya bhāvābhāva-viśeṣopapatteḥ | agnihotrādi-vidhy-artha-jñānottara-kālam agnihotrādi-karma aneka-sādhanopasaṃhāra-pūrvakam anuṣṭheyaṃ kartā aham, mama kartavyam ity evaṃ prakāra-vijñānavato 'viduṣaḥ yathā anuṣṭheyaṃ bhavati, na tu tathā na jāyate ity ādy ātma-svarupa-vidhy-artha-jñānottara-kāla-bhāvi kiṃcid anuṣṭheyaṃ bhavati | kintu nāhaṃ kartā, nāhaṃ bhoktā ity ādy ātmaikatvākartṛtvādi-viṣaya-jñānāt nānyad utpadyate iti eṣa viśeṣa upapadyate | yaḥ punaḥ kartā aham iti vetti ātmānam, tasya mama idaṃ kartavyam iti avaśyaṃbhāvinī buddhiḥ syāt | tad-apekṣayā so 'dhikriyate
iti taṃ prati karmāṇi saṃbhavanti | sa ca avidvān ubhau tau na vijānītaḥ iti vacanāt viśeṣitasya ca viduṣaḥ karmākṣepa-vacanāt kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) too is enjoined only for the non-knower, since enjoining knowledge upon one who already possesses knowledge would be as purposeless as grinding what has already been ground. In that case, the distinction 'actions are enjoined for the non-knower, not for the knower' is unjustified. No — because the distinction regarding the presence or absence of something to be performed is justified. After knowing the meaning of the injunction regarding <s>Agnihotra</s> etc., the non-knower, who understands 'I am the agent, this is my duty to perform,' has something to be performed — requiring the collection of many requisites — just as the <s>Agnihotra</s> etc. is to be performed. But after knowing the meaning of the injunction regarding the nature of the Self — 'it is not born' etc. — there is nothing whatsoever to be subsequently performed. Rather, from the knowledge concerning the unity and non-agency of the Self — 'I am not the agent, I am not the experiencer' — nothing else arises. This is the justified distinction. But for one who knows the Self as 'I am the agent,' the understanding 'this is my duty to perform' necessarily arises. With reference to that, he is eligible [for action], and therefore actions are possible for him. And that person is a non-knower — from the statement 'both of them do not understand,' and from the rhetorical denial of action for the specifically characterized knower — 'how can that person?'

children.text: tasmāt viśeṣitasya avikriyātma-darśinaḥ viduṣaḥ mumukṣo ca sarva-karma-saṃnyāse eva adhikāraḥ | ata eva bhagavān nārāyaṇaḥ sāṃkhyān viduṣo 'viduṣa ca karmiṇaḥ pravibhajya dve niṣṭhe grāhayati-jñāna-yogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karma-yogena yoginām iti | tathā ca putrāya āha bhagavān vyāsaḥ - dvāv imāv atha panthānau [MahāŚā 241.6] ity ādi | tathā ca kriyā-pathaś caiva purastāt paścāt saṃnyāsaś ca iti | etam eva vibhāgaṃ punaḥ punar darśayiṣyati bhagavān --- atattvavit ahaṃkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate, tattvavit tu, nāhaṃ karomi iti | tathā ca sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste ityādi ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, the distinguished one — the wise person (<s>viduṣ</s>) who sees the unchanging Self, and the seeker of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) — has qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>) only for the complete renunciation of all actions. For this very reason, the Blessed Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, distinguishing the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> who are knowers and the <s>karmins</s> (performers of action) who are not, teaches the two distinct paths: 'through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, and through <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action) for the <s>yogins</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.3]. And likewise, the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> said to his son: 'These two are the paths' [<s>Mahā Śāntiparvan</s> 241.6] etc. And also: 'The path of action [is one], and renunciation is the other.' The Blessed Lord will show this very distinction again and again: 'The one who does not know the truth, deluded by ego-sense, thinks "I am the doer"; but the knower of truth [thinks] "I do not act"' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.27-28]. And also: 'Renouncing all actions mentally, [the embodied one] rests' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.13] etc. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.21 //

children.text:
tatra kecit paṇḍitaṃ-manyā vadanti --- janmādi-ṣaḍ-bhāva-vikriyā-rahito 'vikriyo 'kartā eko 'ham ātmā iti na kasyacit jñānam utpadyate, yasmin sati sarva-karma-saṃnyāsaḥ upadiśyate iti | tan na | na jāyate ityādi śāstropadeśānarthakya-prasaṅgāt | yathā ca śāstropadeśa-sāmarthyāt dharmādharmāstitva-vijñānaṃ kartuś ca dehāntara-saṃbandha-vijñānam utpadyate, tathā śāstrāt tasyaiva ātmano 'vikriyatvākartṛtvaikatvādi-vijñānaṃ kasmāt notpadyate iti praṣṭavyāḥ te | karaṇāgocaratvāt iti cet, na | manasaivānudraṣṭavyam [BAU 4.4.19] iti śruteḥ | śāstrācāryopadeśa-śama-damādi-saṃskṛtaṃ mana ātma-darśane karaṇam | tathā ca tad adhigamāya anumāne āgame ca sati jñānaṃ notpadyata iti sāhasa-mātram etat | jñānaṃ ca utpadyamānaṃ tad-viparītam ajñānam avaśyaṃ bādhate ity abhyupagantavyam
| tac ca ajñānaṃ darśitam hantā aham, hato 'smi iti ubhau tau na vijānīta iti | atra ca ātmanaḥ hanana-kriyāyāḥ kartṛtvaṃ karmatvaṃ hetu-kartṛtvaṃ ca ajñāna-kṛtaṃ darśitam | tac ca sarva-kriyāsv api samānaṃ kartṛtvādeḥ avidyā-kṛtatvam avikriyatvāt ātmanaḥ | vikriyāvān hi kartā ātmanaḥ karma-bhūtam anyaṃ prayojayati kuru iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Here, some who consider themselves learned say: 'No one can ever attain the knowledge "I am the one, unchanging, non-agent Self, free from the six modifications beginning with birth" — on the basis of which the complete renunciation of all actions is taught.' That is not so — because the consequence would be that the scriptural teaching 'It is not born' etc. would be purposeless. And [we ask them:] just as, through the power of scriptural teaching, there arises the knowledge of the existence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and the knowledge of the agent's connection with another body — why would not the knowledge of the unchangingness, non-agency, and oneness of that very Self arise from scripture? If [they say] 'because it is beyond the reach of the sense-organs' — no; because of the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text): 'It is to be realized by the mind alone' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.19]. The mind, purified by the instruction of scripture and teacher, and by <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), etc., is the instrument for Self-realization. And given that inference and scripture are available for its attainment, [to say] that knowledge does not arise is mere recklessness. And it must be accepted that knowledge, when it arises, necessarily sublates the ignorance that is its opposite. And that ignorance has been shown [in the verse]: 'Both of these do not know — [the one who thinks] "I am the slayer" and [the one who thinks] "I am slain"' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.19]. And here, regarding the Self, the agency of the act of killing, the objecthood [of being killed], and the instrumental agency — all have been shown as produced by ignorance. And this applies equally to all actions — the agency etc. being produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), because the Self is unchanging. For an agent who undergoes modification causes another, who has become the object of action, [to act], saying 'Do [this].'

children.text: tad etat aviśeṣeṇa viduṣaḥ sarva-kriyāsu kartṛtvaṃ hetu-kartṛtvaṃ ca pratiṣedhati bhagavān vāsudevo viduṣaḥ karmādhikārābhāva-pradarśanārthaṃ vedāvināśinaṃ, kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ ity ādinā | kva punaḥ viduṣo 'dhikāra iti etad uktaṃ pūrvam eva jñāna-yogena sāṃkhyānām iti | tathā ca sarva-karma-saṃnyāsaṃ vakṣyati sarva-karmāṇi manasā ity ādinā ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This very thing — without distinction, the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> negates both the agency and the instrumental agency of the wise person in all actions, for the purpose of showing the absence of qualification for action of the knower — with [the passage] 'Know that which pervades this entire [body] to be indestructible' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.17], 'How can that person...' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.21] etc. Where then is the qualification of the wise person? This was already stated: 'through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.3]. And likewise, he will state the complete renunciation of all actions: 'Renouncing all actions mentally' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.13] etc.

children.text: nanu manasā iti vacanāt na vācikānāṃ kāyikānā ca saṃnyāsaḥ iti cet, na | sarva-karmāṇi iti viśeṣitatvāt | mānasānām eva sarva-karmaṇām iti cet, na | mano-vyāpāra-pūrvakatvād vāk-kāya-vyāpārāṇāṃ mano-vyāpārābhāve tad-anupapatteḥ | śāstrīyāṇāṃ vāk-kāya-karmaṇāṃ kāraṇāni mānasāni karmāṇi varjayitvā anyāni sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyed iti cet, na | naiva kurvan na kārayan iti viśeṣaṇāt | sarva-karma-saṃnyāso 'yaṃ bhagavatā uktaḥ mariṣyato na jīvata iti cet, na | nava-dvāre pure dehī āste iti viśeṇānupapatteḥ | na hi sarva-karma-saṃnyāsena mṛtasya tad-dehe āsanaṃ saṃbhavati |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: Since 'mentally' is said, there is no renunciation of verbal and physical [actions]. No — because of the qualification 'all actions.' [Objection:] 'All actions' means all mental actions alone. No — because verbal and physical activities are preceded by mental activity, and in the absence of mental activity, they are impossible. [Objection:] Setting aside mental actions, which are the causes of scriptural verbal and physical actions, all other actions should be renounced mentally. No — because of the qualifier 'neither acting nor causing [others] to act' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.13]. [Objection:] This complete renunciation of all actions stated by the Lord is for one who is about to die, not for one who is living. No — because the qualifier 'the embodied one dwells happily in the city of nine gates' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.13] would be impossible [for a dead person]; for it is impossible for a dead person who has renounced all actions to dwell in that body.

children.text: akurvato 'kārayata ca dehe saṃnyasya iti saṃbandho na dehe āste iti cet, na | sarvatra ātmano 'vikriyatvāvadhāraṇāt | āsana-kriyāyāś cādhikaraṇāpekṣatvāt | tad-anapekṣatvāc ca saṃnyāsasya | saṃpūrvas tu nyāsa-śabdo 'tra tyāgārthaḥ, na nikṣepārthaḥ | tasmāt gītā-śāstre ātma-jñānavataḥ saṃnyāsa eva adhikāro na karmaṇīti tatra tatra upariṣṭāt ātma-jñāna-prakaraṇe darśayiṣyāmaḥ ||BhGS_2.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] The connection is 'renouncing in the body' for one who neither acts nor causes [others] to act — not 'dwells in the body.' No — because everywhere the unchangingness of the Self is being ascertained. And because the activity of dwelling requires a locus, and renunciation does not require such [a locus]. The word '<s>nyāsa</s>' (placing down) with the prefix '<s>sam</s>' here means abandonment (<s>tyāga</s>), not depositing. Therefore, in the <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>, the one who possesses Self-knowledge has qualification only for renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>), not for action — this we shall show in various places hereafter, in the context of Self-knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.21 //

children.text: prakṛtaṃ tu vakṣyāmaḥ | tatra ātmano 'vināśitvaṃ pratijñātam | tat kim iveti, ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But we shall speak of the topic at hand. There, the indestructibility of the Self has been asserted. What is it like? This is stated:

children.text: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya
children.translated_text: Just as a person, casting off worn-out garments,

children.text: navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi |
children.translated_text: takes other new ones,

children.text: tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāni
children.translated_text: so the embodied [Self], casting off worn-out bodies,

children.text: anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||BhG_2.22||
children.translated_text: enters other new ones. // <s>BhG</s> 2.22 //

children.text: vāsāṃsi vastrāṇi jīrṇāni durbalatāṃ gatāni yathā loke vihāya parityajya navāni abhinavāni gṛhṇāti upādatte naraḥ puruṣo 'parāṇi anyāni, tathā tadvad eva śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāni anyāni saṃyāti saṃgacchati navāni dehī ātmā puruṣavat avikriya evety arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Garments' means clothes; 'worn-out' means those that have become weak; just as in the world, casting off, i.e., discarding [them], one takes, i.e., accepts, 'new' meaning fresh ones — a 'person,' a man, [takes] 'other' ones — so too, in exactly the same way, the 'embodied one' (<s>dehī</s>), the Self, casting off worn-out bodies, enters, i.e., obtains, other new ones — like a person, being unchanged — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.22 //

children.text: kasmāt avikriya eveti, āha ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Why is [the Self] unchanged? He says:

children.text: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Weapons do not cut this [Self], fire does not burn this;

children.text: na cainaṃ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||BhG_2.23||
children.translated_text: waters do not wet this, nor does the wind dry [it]. // <s>BhG</s> 2.23 //

children.text: enaṃ prakṛtaṃ dehinaṃ na chindanti śastrāṇi, niravayavatvāt nāvayava-vibhāgaṃ kurvanti | śastrāṇi asy-ādīni | tathā nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ, agnir api na bhasmīkaroti | tathā na cainaṃ kledayanti āpaḥ | apāṃ hi sāvayavasya vastuna ādrībhāva-karaṇena avayava-viśleṣāpādane sāmarthyam | tan na niravayave ātmani saṃbhavati | tathā snehavat dravyaṃ sneha-śoṣaṇena nāśayati vāyuḥ | enaṃ tv ātmānaṃ na śoṣayati māruto 'pi ||BhGS_2.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This — the embodied Self under discussion — weapons do not cut, because being partless, they do not divide its parts. 'Weapons' means swords and the like. Likewise, fire (<s>pāvaka</s>) does not burn this, i.e., fire does not reduce it to ashes. Likewise, waters do not wet this. For the capacity of water is to dissolve a composite object by making it moist, causing the separation of its parts. That is not possible for the partless Self. Likewise, the wind destroys an oily substance by drying up its moisture. But this Self — even the wind does not dry. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.23 //

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmāt --
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca |
children.translated_text: This [Self] cannot be cut, this cannot be burnt, this cannot be wetted, and indeed cannot be dried;

children.text: nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ ||BhG_2.24||
children.translated_text: [It is] eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, and primordial. // <s>BhG</s> 2.24 //

children.text: yasmāt anyonya-nāśa-hetu-bhūtāni enam ātmānaṃ nāśayituṃ notsahante asyādīni tasmāt nityaḥ | nityatvāt sarvagataḥ | sarva-gatatvāt sthāṇur iva, sthira ity etat | sthiratvāt acalo 'yam ātmā | ataḥ sanātanaś cirantanaḥ, na kāraṇāt kutaścin niṣpannaḥ, abhinava ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since the things that are mutual causes of destruction — swords and the like — are not able to destroy this Self, therefore [It is] 'eternal' (<s>nitya</s>). Because of being eternal, [It is] 'all-pervading' (<s>sarvagata</s>). Because of being all-pervading, [It is] like a pillar (<s>sthāṇu</s>) — meaning stable. Because of being stable, this Self is 'immovable' (<s>acala</s>). Therefore [It is] 'primordial' (<s>sanātana</s>) — ancient; not produced from any cause; meaning: not newly arisen.

children.text: naiteṣāṃ lokānāṃ paunaruktyaṃ codanīyam, yataḥ ekenaiva lokān ātmanaḥ nityatvam avikriyatvaṃ coktam na jāyate mriyate vā ity ādinā | tatra yad eva ātma-viṣayaṃ kiṃcid ucyate, tad etasmāt lokārthān nātiricyate | kiṃcic chabdataḥ punaruktam, kiṃcid arthataḥ iti | durbodhatvāt ātma-vastunaḥ punaḥ punaḥ prasaṅgam āpādya śabdāntareṇa tad eva vastu nirūpayati bhagavān vāsudevaḥ kathaṃ nu nāma saṃsāriṇām asaṃsāritva-buddhi-gocaratām āpannaṃ sat avyaktaṃ tattvaṃ saṃsāra-nivṛttaye syāt iti ||BhGS_2.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The repetition among these [verses] should not be objected to, since the eternity and unchangingness of the Self have been stated by a single verse alone — 'It is not born, nor does it die' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.20] etc. Whatever is stated therein concerning the Self does not exceed the meaning of that verse. Some [expressions] are verbally repetitious, some are repetitious in meaning. Because the nature of the Self is difficult to understand, the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, bringing up the topic again and again, explains that very reality through different words — [thinking:] 'How indeed can this unmanifest reality, having entered the range of the non-transmigrating understanding of those who are [currently] transmigrating, lead to the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>?' // <s>BhGS</s> 2.24 //

children.text: avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate |
children.translated_text: This [Self] is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchangeable;

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitum arhasi ||BhG_2.25||
children.translated_text: therefore, knowing this thus, you should not grieve. // <s>BhG</s> 2.25 //

children.text: avyaktaḥ sarva-karaṇāviṣayatvāt na vyajyata iti avyakto 'yam ātmā | ataeva acintyo 'yam | yad dhi indriya-gocaras tac cintā-viṣayatvam āpadyate | ayaṃ tv ātmā anindriya-gocaratvāt acintyaḥ | ataeva avikāryaḥ, yathā kṣīraṃ dadhyātañcanādinā vikāri na tathā ayam ātmā | niravayavatvāc cāvikriyaḥ | na hi niravayavaṃ kiṃcit vikriyātmakaṃ dṛṣṭām | avikriyatvāt avikāryo 'yam ātmā ucyate | tasmāt evaṃ yathokta-prakāreṇa enam ātmānaṃ viditvā tvaṃ na anuśocitum arhasi hantāham eṣām, mayaite hanyanta iti ||BhGS_2.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Unmanifest' — because [the Self] is not an object of any sense-organ, it is not manifested; hence this Self is 'unmanifest.' For this very reason, [it is] 'inconceivable.' For what comes within the range of the senses becomes an object of thought. But this Self, not being within the range of the senses, is inconceivable. For this very reason, [it is] 'unchangeable' — just as milk is modified by curds, buttermilk, etc., this Self is not so [modified]. And being partless, it is unmodifiable. For nothing partless is seen to undergo modification. Because of being unmodifiable, this Self is said to be 'unchangeable.' Therefore, knowing this Self in the manner described, you should not grieve — [thinking] 'I am their slayer, they are slain by me.' // <s>BhGS</s> 2.25 //

children.text: ātmano 'nityatvam abhyupagamya idam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Assuming the non-eternality of the Self, this is stated:

children.text: atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
children.translated_text: But if you think this [Self] is perpetually born and perpetually dying,

children.text: tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitum arhasi ||BhG_2.26||
children.translated_text: even then, O mighty-armed one, you should not grieve thus. // <s>BhG</s> 2.26 //

children.text: atha ca iti abhyupagamārthaḥ | enaṃ prakṛtam ātmānaṃ nitya-jātaṃ loka-prasiddhayā praty aneka-śarīrotpatti jāto jāta iti manyase | tathā prati-tat-tad-vināśaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtaṃ mṛto mṛta iti | tathāpi tathābhāve 'py ātmani tvaṃ mahābāho, na evaṃ śocitum arhasi, janmavato nāśo nāśavato janma cety etāv avaśyaṃbhāvināv iti ||BhGS_2.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'But if' — this is in the sense of conceding [the opponent's view]. If you think this Self under discussion is 'perpetually born' — according to popular understanding, born with each new body, i.e., 'born, born [again and again].' And likewise, 'perpetually dying' with each successive destruction — you think [it is] 'dead, dead [again and again].' 'Even then' — even if the Self were so — you, O mighty-armed one, should not grieve thus; for birth necessarily follows death, and death necessarily follows birth — these two are inevitable. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.26 //

children.text: tathā ca sati--
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And this being so —

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
children.translated_text: For one who is born, death is certain; and certain is the birth of one who has died.

children.text: tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||BhG_2.27||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in a matter that is unavoidable, you should not grieve. // <s>BhG</s> 2.27 //

children.text: jātasya hi labdha-janmanaḥ dhruvo 'vyabhicārī mṛtyur maraṇaṃ dhruva janma mṛtasya ca | tasmād aparihāryo 'yaṃ janma-maraṇa-lakṣaṇo 'rthaḥ | tasminn aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||BhGS_2.27||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For one who is born — one who has obtained birth — death is certain, inevitable. And certain is the birth of one who has died. Therefore, this matter characterized by birth and death is unavoidable. In this unavoidable matter, you should not grieve. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.27 //

children.text: kārya-karaṇa-saṃghātātma-kānyapi bhūtāny uddiśya śoko na yuktaḥ kartum, yataḥ-
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Grief is not appropriate even regarding beings that are composites of body and sense-organs, because —

children.text: avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata |
children.translated_text: Beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their middle state, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: avyakta-nidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā ||BhG_2.28||
children.translated_text: and unmanifest again at death — what lamentation is there in this? // <s>BhG</s> 2.28 //

children.text: avyaktādīny avyaktam adarśanam anupalabdhiḥ ādir yeṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ putra-mitrādi-kārya-karaṇa-saṃghātātmakānāṃ tāni avyaktadīni bhūtāni prāg-utpatteḥ, utpannāni ca prāṅ-maraṇāt vyakta-madhyāni | avyakta-nidhanāny eva punar avyaktam adarśanaṃ nidhanaṃ maraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ tāni avyakta-nidhanāni | maraṇād ūrdhvam apy avyaktatām eva pratipadyante ity arthaḥ | tathā coktam ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Unmanifest in their beginning' — 'unmanifest' means unseen, unperceived; this is the beginning of those beings — composites of body, sense-organs, etc., such as sons, friends, etc. — they are unmanifest in their beginning, i.e., prior to birth. And having been born, prior to death, they are 'manifest in their middle state.' 'Unmanifest in their end' — again, 'unmanifest' means unseen; 'end' means death; they whose end is unmanifest are 'unmanifest in their end.' The meaning is: even after death, they return to the state of being unmanifest. And thus it has been said:

children.text: adarśanād āpatitaḥ punaś cādarśanaṃ gataḥ |
nāsau tava na tasya tvaṃ vṛthā kā paridevanā || [Mahā. Strī. 2.13] iti |
children.translated_text: he is not yours, nor are you his — what lamentation is there in vain?' [<s>Mbh</s>, <s>Strīparvan</s> 2.13]
'Having come from the unseen, and having gone again to the unseen,

children.text: tatra kā paridevanā ko vā pralāpo 'dṛṣṭa-dṛṣṭa-pranaṣṭa-bhrānti-bhūteṣu bhūteṣv ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What lamentation is there therein, or what bewailing, regarding beings that are like illusions — unseen, then seen, then vanished? — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.28 //

children.text: durvijñeyo 'thaṃ prakṛta ātmā | kiṃ tvāmevaikamupālabhe sādhāraṇe bhrāntinimitte | kathaṃ durvijñeyo 'yamātmā ityata āha ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, the Self under discussion is difficult to know. But why do I reproach you alone, when the cause of confusion is common [to all]? How is this Self difficult to know? To this he says:

children.text: āścaryavat paśyati kaścid enam
children.translated_text: One sees this [Self] as a wonder; another likewise speaks of it as a wonder;

children.text: āścaryavad vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ |
children.translated_text: and another hears of it as a wonder;

children.text: āścaryavac cainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: yet even having heard,

children.text: śrutvāpy enaṃ veda na caiva kaścit ||BhG_2.29||
children.translated_text: no one truly knows it. // <s>BhG</s> 2.29 //

children.text: āścaryavat āścaryam adṛṣṭa-pūrvam adbhutam akasmād dṛśyamānaṃ tena tulyaṃ āścaryavat āścaryam iva enam ātmānaṃ paśyati kaścit | āścaryavad enaṃ vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ | āścaryavac ca enam anyaḥ sṛṇoti | śrutvā dṛṣṭvā uktvāpi enam ātmānaṃ veda na caiva kaścit | athavā yo 'yam ātmānaṃ paśyati sa āścarya-tulyaḥ, yo vadati ya ca sṛṇoti so 'neka-sahasreṣu kaścid eva bhavati | ato durbodha ātmā ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.29||
children.translated_text: <s>Āścaryavat</s> — <s>āścarya</s> means something unprecedented, wondrous, appearing suddenly without cause; similar to that is <s>āścaryavat</s>, meaning 'as if a wonder' — someone sees this <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as a wonder. Another speaks of it likewise as a wonder. Yet another hears of it as a wonder. Even after hearing, seeing, and speaking about it, no one truly knows this <s>Ātman</s>. Alternatively, one who sees the <s>Ātman</s> is himself like a wonder, one who speaks of it and one who hears of it — such a person is found only among many thousands. Therefore the purport is that the <s>Ātman</s> is extremely difficult to comprehend.
[Section break]

children.text: athedānīṃ prakaraṇārtham upasaṃharan brūte -
children.translated_text: Now, summarizing the topic under discussion, he says —

children.text: dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
children.translated_text: The embodied Self is eternal and indestructible in the body of all, O <s>Bhārata</s>;

children.text: tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||BhG_2.30||
children.translated_text: therefore you ought not to grieve for any beings.

children.text: dehī śarīrī nityaṃ sarvadā sarvāvasthāsu avadhyaḥ niravayavatvān nityatvāc ca | tatra avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe śarīre sarvasya sarva-gatatvāt sthāvarādiṣu sthito 'pi sarvasya prāṇi-jātasya dehe vadhyamāne 'py ayaṃ dehī na vadhyo yasmāt, tasmād bhīṣmādīni sarvāṇi bhūtāni uddiśya na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||BhGS_2.30||
children.translated_text: The <s>dehī</s> (embodied Self), the indweller of the body, is eternal — at all times, in all states — and indestructible, because it is partless and eternal. There, this indestructible one dwells in the body of all beings; because it is all-pervading, even though situated in stationary beings and others, even when the body of any living creature is being destroyed, this embodied Self is not destroyed. Therefore, with reference to <s>Bhīṣma</s> and all other beings, you ought not to grieve.
[Section break]

children.text: iha paramārtha-tattvāpekṣāyāṃ śoko moho vā na saṃbhavatīty uktam | na kevalaṃ paramārtha-tattvāpekṣāyām eva, kiṃ tu ---
children.translated_text: It has been stated that from the standpoint of the ultimate reality, neither grief nor delusion is possible. And not only from the standpoint of ultimate reality, but also —

children.text: sva-dharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi |
children.translated_text: And considering your own <s>svadharma</s> (proper duty), you should not waver;

children.text: dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate ||BhG_2.31||
children.translated_text: for there exists nothing better for a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) than a righteous battle.

children.text: svadharmam api svo dharmaḥ kṣatriyasya yuddhaṃ tam api avekṣya tvaṃ na vikampituṃ pracalitum nārhasi kṣatriyasya svābhāvikād dharmād ātma-svābhāvyād ity abhiprāyaḥ | tac ca yuddhaṃ pṛthivī-jaya-dvāreṇa dharmārthaṃ prajā-rakṣaṇārthaṃ ceti dharmād anapetaṃ paraṃ dharmyam | tasmād dharmyād yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate hi yasmāt ||BhGS_2.31||
children.translated_text: <s>Svadharma</s> — one's own <s>dharma</s> (duty); for a <s>kṣatriya</s>, that is battle. Considering even that, you should not waver or falter — the purport being that it arises from the <s>kṣatriya</s>'s innate nature, from the Self's own inherent disposition. And that battle, through the means of conquering the earth, is for the sake of <s>dharma</s> and for the protection of subjects — thus it is not contrary to <s>dharma</s> but is supremely righteous. Therefore, there exists nothing better for a <s>kṣatriya</s> than a righteous battle, because —
[Section break]

children.text: kutaś ca tat yuddhaṃ kartavyam iti, ucyate ---
children.translated_text: And why should that battle be undertaken? It is said —

children.text: yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam |
children.translated_text: Coming of its own accord, an open gate to heaven —

children.text: sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam ||BhG_2.32||
children.translated_text: happy are the <s>kṣatriyas</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, who obtain such a battle.

children.text: yadṛcchayā ca aprārthitatayā upapannam āgataṃ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam udghāṭitaṃ ya etad īdṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ labhante kṣatriyāḥ he pārtha, kiṃ na sukhinas te ? ||BhGS_2.32||
children.translated_text: Coming of its own accord, that is, without being sought — an open gate to heaven, that is, a gate thrown wide open — those <s>kṣatriyas</s> who obtain this kind of battle, O <s>Pārtha</s>, are they not happy?

children.text:
==============================
etaṃ kartavyatā-prāptam api -
children.translated_text:
[Section break]
Even though this duty has presented itself —

children.text: atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: But if you will not undertake this righteous battle,

children.text: tataḥ sva-dharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi ||BhG_2.33||
children.translated_text: then, abandoning your own <s>svadharma</s> (duty) and glory, you will incur sin.

children.text: atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ dharmād anapetaṃ vihitaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ yuddhaṃ na kariṣyasi cet, tataḥ tad-akaraṇāt svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca mahā-devādi-samāgama-nimittāṃ hitvā kevalaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi ||BhGS_2.33||
children.translated_text: But if you will not undertake this righteous battle — that is, one not contrary to <s>dharma</s>, one that is ordained — this war, this fight; then, from not performing it, abandoning your <s>svadharma</s> and the glory occasioned by the assembly of great gods and others, you will incur nothing but sin.
[Section break]

children.text: na kevalaṃ svadharma-kīrti-parityāgaḥ -
children.translated_text: Not only will there be loss of <s>svadharma</s> and glory —

children.text: akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām |
children.translated_text: And all beings will speak of your everlasting infamy;

children.text: saṃbhāvitasya cākīrtir maraṇād atiricyate ||BhG_2.34||
children.translated_text: and for one who has been honored, infamy is worse than death.

children.text: akīrtiṃ cāpi yuddhā bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te tava avyayāṃ dīrgha-kālām | dharmātmā śūra ity evam ādibhiḥ guṇaiḥ saṃbhāvitasya ca akīrtiḥ maraṇāt atiricyate, saṃbhāvitasya ca akīrteḥ varaṃ maraṇam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.34||
children.translated_text: And beings will speak of your infamy — infamy from battle, that is — which will be <s>avyayā</s> (everlasting), lasting for a long time. And for one who has been honored with qualities such as 'he is righteous' and 'he is valiant,' infamy is worse than death; the meaning is that for one so honored, death is preferable to infamy.
[Section break]

children.text: kiṃ ca--
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: bhayād raṇād uparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
children.translated_text: The great warriors will think you have withdrawn from battle out of fear,

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam ||BhG_2.35||
children.translated_text: and you, who were held in high esteem by them, will come to be regarded lightly.

children.text: bhayāt karṇādibhyaḥ raṇāt yuddhāt uparataṃ nivṛttaṃ maṃsyante cintayiṣyanti na kṛpayeti tvāṃ mahārathāḥ duryodhana-prabhṛtayaḥ | yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ duryodhanādīnāṃ bahu-mato bahubhir guṇair yuktaḥ ity evaṃ mataḥ bahumato bhūtvā punar yāsyasi lāghavaṃ laghu-bhāvam ||BhGS_2.35||
children.translated_text: The great warriors — <s>Duryodhana</s> and others — will think, will conclude, that you withdrew and retreated from battle, from the fight, out of fear of <s>Karṇa</s> and others, not out of compassion. And you, who were held in high esteem by <s>Duryodhana</s> and the rest — regarded as endowed with many virtues — having been so esteemed, will come to be regarded lightly, will fall into insignificance.

[Section break]
Moreover —

children.text: avācya-vādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: And your enemies will speak many unspeakable words,

children.text: nindantas tava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ||BhG_2.36||
children.translated_text: disparaging your ability — what could be more painful than that?

children.text: avācya-vādān avaktavya-vādāṃś ca bahūn aneka-prakārān vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ śatravaḥ nindantaḥ kutsayantaḥ tava tvadīyaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nivāta-kavacādi-yuddha-nimittam | tatas tasmāt nindā-prāpter duḥkhāt duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ? tataḥ kaṣṭataraṃ duḥkhaṃ nāstīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.36||
children.translated_text: <s>Avācya-vādān</s> — words that ought not to be spoken, and many such words of various kinds, your enemies will speak, disparaging and denigrating your ability — the prowess demonstrated in battles such as that against <s>Nivātakavaca</s> and others. What could be more painful than that, than the attainment of such censure? The meaning is that there is no suffering worse than that.
[Section break]

children.text: yurā punaḥ kriyamāṇe karṇādibhiḥ-
children.translated_text: But if war is waged by <s>Karṇa</s> and the others —

children.text: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
children.translated_text: Slain, you will attain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth;

children.text: tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ ||BhG_2.37||
children.translated_text: therefore arise, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, resolved for battle.

children.text: hato vā prāpsyasi svargam, hataḥ san svargaṃ prāpsyasi | jitvā vā karṇādīn śūrān bhokṣyase mahīm | ubhayathāpi tava lābha evety abhiprāyaḥ | yata evaṃ tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtāni ca yaḥ jeṣyāmi śatrūn, mariṣyāmi vā iti niścayaṃ kṛtvety arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.37||
children.translated_text: Slain, you will attain heaven — having been killed, you will reach heaven. Or victorious over valiant warriors like <s>Karṇa</s> and others, you will enjoy the earth. Either way, the purport is that it is gain for you alone. Since this is so, therefore arise, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, for battle, having made a firm resolve — the meaning is: having determined 'I shall either conquer the enemies or die.'
[Section break]

children.text: tatra yuddhaṃ svadharma ity evaṃ yudhyamānasyopadeśam imaṃ sṛṇu -
children.translated_text: Now, since battle is your <s>svadharma</s> (proper duty), hear this instruction for one who fights thus —

children.text: sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
children.translated_text: Treating pleasure and pain alike, gain and loss, victory and defeat —

children.text: tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi ||BhG_2.38||
children.translated_text: then engage in battle; thus you shall not incur sin.

children.text: sukha-duḥkhe same tulye kṛtvā, rāga-dveṣāv apy akṛtvety etat | tathā lābhālābhau jayājayau ca samau kṛtvā tato yuddhāya yujyasva ghaṭāsva | na evaṃ yuddhaṃ kurvan pāpam avāpsyasi | ity eṣa upadeśaḥ prāsaṅgikaḥ ||BhGS_2.38||
children.translated_text: Making pleasure and pain equal, that is, alike — and this also means without generating attachment and aversion. Likewise, making gain and loss, victory and defeat equal — then engage in battle, strive for it. Thus fighting, you shall not incur sin. This instruction is incidental to the present context.
[Section break]

children.text: śoka-mohāpanayanāya laukiko nyāyaḥ svadharmam api cāvekṣya ity ādyaiḥ lokair uktaḥ, na tu tātparyeṇa | paramārtha-darśanam iha prakṛtam | tac coktam upasaṃhriyate -- eṣā te 'bhihitā iti śāstra-viṣaya-vibhāga-pradarśanāya | iha hi pradarśite punaḥ śāstra-viṣaya-vibhāge upariṣṭāt jñāna-yogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karma-yogena yoginām iti niṣṭhā-dvaya-viṣayaṃ śāstraṃ sukhaṃ pravartiṣyate, śrotāraś ca viṣaya-vibhāgena sukhaṃ grahīṣyanti ity ata āha ---
children.translated_text: The worldly reasoning stated through verses beginning with 'and considering your own <s>svadharma</s>' was presented for removing grief and delusion, but not as the primary purport. The vision of ultimate reality is the main subject here. That is now being summarized with 'this has been declared to you' — in order to demonstrate the division of subject matter of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture). For when this division of the <s>śāstra</s>'s subject matter is demonstrated here, the teaching pertaining to the two paths — '<s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the discipline of knowledge) for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and <s>karma-yoga</s> (the discipline of action) for the <s>Yogins</s>' — will proceed smoothly later on, and the listeners too will easily grasp it through the division of subject matter. Therefore he says —

children.text: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṃkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu |
children.translated_text: This <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) has been declared to you regarding <s>Sāṃkhya</s> (knowledge); now hear this regarding <s>Yoga</s> (practice) —

children.text: buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi ||BhG_2.39||
children.translated_text: endowed with which <s>buddhi</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, you will cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: eṣā te tubhyam abhihitā uktā sāṃkhye paramārtha-vastu-viveka-viṣaye buddhir jñānaṃ sākṣāt śoka-mohādi-saṃsāra-hetu-doṣa-nivṛtti-kāraṇam | yoge tu tat-prāpty-upāye niḥsaṅgatayā dvandva-prahāṇa-pūrvakam īśvarārādhanārthe karma-yoge karmānuṣṭhāne samādhi-yoge cemām anantaram evocyamānāṃ buddhiṃ śṛṇu | tāṃ ca buddhiṃ stauti prarocanārtham -- buddhyā yayā yoga-viṣayayā yuktaḥ | he pārtha, karma-bandhaṃ karmaiva dharmādharmākhyo bandhaḥ karma-bandhas taṃ prahāsyasi īśvara-prasāda-nimitta-jñāna-prāpter ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.39||
children.translated_text: This <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) has been declared, that is, stated to you, regarding <s>Sāṃkhya</s> — that is, regarding the discrimination of ultimate reality — this knowledge being the direct cause for the removal of the defects that constitute the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), such as grief and delusion. Regarding <s>Yoga</s>, however — that is, regarding the means of attaining that [knowledge], namely <s>karma-yoga</s> (the discipline of action) performed with detachment, preceded by the abandonment of pairs of opposites, for the sake of worshipping <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), as well as regarding <s>samādhi-yoga</s> (the discipline of meditation) — hear this <s>buddhi</s> that is about to be stated next. And he praises that <s>buddhi</s> to arouse interest: endowed with which <s>buddhi</s> pertaining to <s>Yoga</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, you will cast off <s>karma-bandha</s> (the bondage of action) — <s>karma</s> itself, characterized as <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), is the bondage; that bondage of <s>karma</s> you will cast off — the purport being: through the attainment of knowledge occasioned by the grace of <s>Īśvara</s>.
[Section break]

children.text: kiṃ cānyat --
children.translated_text: What else? —

children.text: nehābhikrama-nāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
children.translated_text: Here there is no loss of effort, nor is there any adverse result;

children.text: svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||BhG_2.40||
children.translated_text: even a little of this <s>dharma</s> (practice) protects one from great fear.

children.text: neha mokṣa-mārge karma-yoge abhikrama-nāśo 'bhikramaṇam abhikramaḥ prārambhas tasya nāśo nāsti yathā kṛṣyādeḥ | yoga-viṣaye prārambhasya na anaikāntika-phalatvam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ ca nāpi cikitsāvat pratyavāyo vidyate bhavati | kiṃ tu svalpam api asya dharmasya yoga-dharmasya anuṣṭhitaṃ trāyate rakṣati mahataḥ bhayāt saṃsāra-bhayāt janma-maraṇādi-lakṣaṇāt ||BhGS_2.40||
children.translated_text: Here, on this path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), in <s>karma-yoga</s>, there is no loss of effort — <s>abhikrama</s> means commencement, beginning; there is no destruction of that, unlike in agriculture and similar undertakings. The meaning is that the commencement in the domain of <s>Yoga</s> does not yield uncertain results. Moreover, there is no adverse consequence as in medical treatment. Rather, even a little of this <s>dharma</s> — this <s>dharma</s> of <s>Yoga</s> that has been practiced — protects one, saves one, from great fear — the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) characterized by birth, death, and the like.
[Section break]

children.text: yeyaṃ sāṃkhye buddhir uktā yoge ca, vakṣyamāṇa-lakṣaṇā sā -
children.translated_text: That <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) which has been spoken of regarding <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, whose characteristics are about to be described, is this —

children.text: vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana |
children.translated_text: Here, the resolute <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) is one-pointed, O <s>Kurunandana</s> (joy of the <s>Kurus</s>);

children.text: bahu-śākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām ||BhG_2.41||
children.translated_text: but the understandings of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

children.text:
vyavasāyātmikā niścaya-svabhāvā ekā eva buddhir itara-viparīta-buddhi-śākhā-bhedasya vādhikā, samyak-pramāṇa-janitatvāt, iha śreyo-mārge | he kurunandana ! yāḥ punar itarā viparīta-buddhayaḥ, yāsāṃ śākhā-bheda-pracāra-vaśāt ananto 'pāro 'nuparataḥ
saṃsāro nitya-pratato vistīrṇo bhavati, pramāṇa-janita-viveka-buddhi-nimitta-vaśāc ca uparatāsv ananta-bheda-buddhiṣu saṃsāro 'py uparamate tā buddhayo bahu-śākhāḥ bahvvayaḥ śākhāḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ bahu-śākhāḥ, bahu-bhedā ity etat | pratiśākhā-bhedena hy anantā ca buddhayaḥ | keṣām ? avyavasāyināṃ pramāṇa-janita-viveka-buddhi-rahitānām ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.41||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyavasāyātmikā</s> — of the nature of firm resolve — this <s>buddhi</s> is one alone, and it negates the branches of all contrary understandings, because it is born from valid means of knowledge. This is so here, on the path to the highest good, O <s>Kurunandana</s>. But the other, contrary understandings — through whose branching and proliferation <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) becomes endless, boundless, unceasing, eternally extended and vast — and when these endlessly branching understandings cease through the force of discriminative knowledge born from valid means of knowledge, <s>saṃsāra</s> too ceases; those understandings are many-branched — having many branches, meaning having many divisions. And branch by branch, the understandings are indeed endless. Of whom? Of the irresolute — meaning those devoid of discriminative understanding born from valid means of knowledge.
[Section break]

children.text: yeṣāṃ vyavasāyātmikā buddhir nāsti te--
children.translated_text: Those who lack resolute understanding —

children.text: yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The undiscerning ones proclaim this flowery speech,

children.text: veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ ||BhG_2.42||
children.translated_text: delighting in the letter of the <s>Veda</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, declaring 'there is nothing else.'

children.text: yām imāṃ vakṣyamāṇāṃ puṣpitāṃ puṣpita iva vṛkṣaḥ śobhamānāṃ śrūyamāṇa-ramaṇīyāṃ vācaṃ vākya-lakṣaṇāṃ pravadanti | ke ? avipaścito 'medhaso 'vivekina ity arthaḥ | veda-vāda-ratāḥ bahvy-artha-vāda-phala-sādhana-prakāśakeṣu veda-vākyeṣu ratāḥ he pārtha, na anyat svarga-prāpty-ādi-phala-sādhanebhyaḥ karmabhyo 'sti ity evaṃ vādinaḥ vadana-śīlāḥ ||BhGS_2.42||
children.translated_text: <s>Yām imām</s> — this speech about to be described, which is <s>puṣpitā</s> (flowery) — splendid like a tree in bloom, pleasant to hear — this speech, in the form of utterances, they proclaim. Who? The undiscerning, the unintelligent, the undiscriminating — that is the meaning. <s>Veda-vāda-ratāḥ</s> — those who delight in the statements of the <s>Veda</s> that describe the many means and fruits expounded in the <s>arthavāda</s> (eulogistic passages). O <s>Pārtha</s>, they are those who habitually declare that there is nothing other than the rituals that are the means for attaining fruits such as reaching heaven.
[Section break]

children.text: te ca --
children.translated_text: And they —

children.text: kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā janma-karma-phala-pradām |
children.translated_text: Full of desires, intent on heaven, [they proclaim speech that] yields rebirth as the fruit of actions,

children.text: kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṃ bhogaiśvarya-gatiṃ prati ||BhG_2.43||
children.translated_text: abounding in specific rituals, directed toward the attainment of enjoyment and power.

children.text: kāmātmānaḥ kāmasvabhāvāḥ, kāmaparā ity arthaḥ | svarga-parāḥ svargaḥ paraḥ puruṣārthaḥ yeṣāṃ te svarga-parāḥ svarga-pradhānāḥ | janma-karma-phala-pradāṃ karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ karma-phalaṃ janmaiva karma-phalaṃ janma-karma-phalaṃ tat pradadātīti janma-karma-phala-pradā, tāṃ vācam | pravadanti ity anuṣajyate | kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṃ kriyāṇāṃ viśeṣāḥ kriyā-viśeṣāḥ te bahulā yasyāṃ vāci tāṃ svarga-paśu-putrādy-arthāḥ yayā vācā bāhulyena prakāśyante | bhogaiśvarya-gatiṃ prati bhogaś ca aiśvaryaṃ ca bhogaiśvarye, tayor gatiḥ prāptiḥ bhogaiśvarya-gatiḥ, tāṃ prati sādhana-bhūtāḥ ye kriyā-viśeṣāḥ tad-bahulāṃ tāṃ vācaṃ pravadantaḥ mūḍhāḥ saṃsāre parivartante ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.43||
children.translated_text: '<s>Kāmātmānaḥ</s>' — those whose nature is desire, meaning those who are intent on desire. '<s>Svarga-parāḥ</s>' — those for whom heaven (<s>svarga</s>) is the supreme goal of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>); they are heaven-oriented. '<s>Janma-karma-phala-pradām</s>' — the fruit of action (<s>karma-phala</s>) is [rebirth as] birth itself (<s>janma</s>); that which bestows birth as the fruit of action is '<s>janma-karma-phala-pradā</s>' — [it modifies] that speech (<s>vācam</s>). '<s>Pravadanti</s>' (they proclaim) is to be connected. '<s>Kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulām</s>' — the particular forms of ritual actions are '<s>kriyā-viśeṣāḥ</s>'; that speech in which these are abundant — [i.e., the speech] by which the purposes of heaven, cattle, sons, etc. are extensively revealed. '<s>Bhogaiśvarya-gatim prati</s>' — enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) constitute '<s>bhogaiśvarya</s>'; their attainment (<s>gati</s>) is the reaching of enjoyment and sovereignty; those particular ritual actions that serve as means toward that — the speech that abounds in these. The purport is: those deluded ones who proclaim such speech revolve in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). // <s>BhGS</s> 2.43 //

children.text: teṣāṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And of those [desire-natured ones] —

children.text: bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛta-cetasām |
children.translated_text: For those attached to enjoyment and sovereignty, whose minds are carried away by that [speech],

children.text: vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||BhG_2.44||
children.translated_text: the resolute intellect (<s>vyavasāyātmikā buddhi</s>) is not established in <s>samādhi</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 2.44 //

children.text: bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānāṃ bhogaḥ kartavyaḥ caiśvaryaṃ ca iti bhogaiśvaryayor eva praṇayavatāṃ tad-ātma-bhūtānām | tayā kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulayā vācā apahṛta-cetasām ācchādita-viveka-prajñānāṃ vyavasāyātmikā sāṃkhye yoge vā buddhiḥ samādhau samādhīyate asmin puruṣopabhogāya sarvam iti samādhiḥ antaḥkaraṇaṃ buddhiḥ tasmin samādhau, na vidhīyate na bhavati ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.44||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhogaiśvarya-prasaktānām</s>' — of those who are devoted exclusively to enjoyment and sovereignty, [thinking] 'enjoyment must be had, and sovereignty too' — those who have become identified with those [pursuits]. By that speech, abounding in particular ritual actions, whose minds have been carried away (<s>apahṛta-cetasām</s>) — whose discriminative wisdom has been veiled — the resolute intellect (<s>vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ</s>), whether pertaining to <s>Sāṃkhya</s> or <s>Yoga</s>, in <s>samādhi</s> — '<s>samādhi</s>' is that in which [the thought] 'everything is for the enjoyment of <s>puruṣa</s>' is settled; <s>samādhi</s> is the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>); in that <s>samādhi</s> — is not established (<s>na vidhīyate</s>), meaning it does not arise. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.44 //

children.text: ya evaṃ viveka-buddhi-rahitāḥ teṣāṃ kāmātmanāṃ yat phalaṃ tad āha -
children.translated_text: For those who are thus devoid of discriminative intellect (<s>viveka-buddhi</s>), who are desire-natured — what fruit [awaits them], that He states —

children.text: traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> have the three <s>guṇas</s> as their domain; be free from the three <s>guṇas</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān ||BhG_2.45||
children.translated_text: free from the pairs of opposites, ever established in <s>sattva</s>, free from [concern for] acquisition and preservation, self-possessed. // <s>BhG</s> 2.45 //

children.text: traiguṇya-viṣayāḥ traiguṇyaṃ saṃsāro viṣayaḥ prakāśayitavyaḥ yeṣāṃ te vedāḥ traiguṇya-viṣayāḥ | tvaṃ tu nistraiguṇyo bhava arjuna, niṣkāmo bhava ity arthaḥ | nirdvandvaḥ sukha-duḥkha-hetū sa-pratipakṣau padārthau dvandva-śabda-vācyau | tataḥ nirgataḥ nirdvandvo bhava | nitya-sattva-sthaḥ sadā sattva-guṇāśrito bhava | tathā niryoga-kṣemo 'nupāttasya upādānaṃ yogaḥ, upāttasya rakṣaṇaṃ kṣemaḥ, yoga-kṣema-pradhānasya śreyasi pravṛttir duṣkarā ity ataḥ niryoga-kṣemo bhava | ātmavān apramattaś ca bhava | eṣa tava upadeśaḥ sva-dharmam anutiṣṭhataḥ ||BhGS_2.45||
children.translated_text: '<s>Traiguṇya-viṣayāḥ</s>' — the three <s>guṇas</s> constitute <s>traiguṇya</s>, [meaning] <s>saṃsāra</s>; that which is their domain (<s>viṣaya</s>), what is to be revealed — those are the <s>Vedas</s>: they have the three <s>guṇas</s> as their domain. But you, be free from the three <s>guṇas</s> (<s>nistraiguṇya</s>), O <s>Arjuna</s> — meaning: be free from desire. '<s>Nirdvandvaḥ</s>' — the causes of pleasure and pain, which are paired with their opposites, are denoted by the word '<s>dvandva</s>' (pair of opposites); be free from them. '<s>Nitya-sattva-sthaḥ</s>' — be always established in the quality of <s>sattva</s>. Likewise, '<s>niryoga-kṣemaḥ</s>' — the acquisition (<s>yoga</s>) of what is not yet obtained, and the preservation (<s>kṣema</s>) of what has been obtained: for one whose chief concern is acquisition and preservation, engagement in the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>) is difficult; therefore be free from [concern for] acquisition and preservation. '<s>Ātmavān</s>' — be self-possessed, be vigilant. This is the instruction for you as you carry out your own duty (<s>svadharma</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 2.45 //

children.text: sarveṣu vedokteṣu karmasu yāny uktāny anantāni phalāni tāni nāpekṣyante cet, kim arthaṃ tāni īśvarāyety anuṣṭhīyante ity ucyate | sṛṇu -
children.translated_text: If the innumerable fruits mentioned in all the actions prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> are not sought, then for what purpose are they performed as offerings to the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)? It is said — listen:

children.text: yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake |
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose is served by a well when water overflows on all sides,

children.text: tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ ||BhG_2.46||
children.translated_text: that much [purpose is served] in all the <s>Vedas</s> for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows. // <s>BhG</s> 2.46 //

children.text: yathā loke kūpa-taḍāgādy-anekasmin udapāne paricchinnodake yāvān yāvat-parimāṇaḥ snāna-pānādir arthaḥ phalaṃ prayojanaṃ sa sarvo 'rthaḥ sarvataḥ saṃplutodake 'pi yo 'rthaḥ tāvān eva saṃpadyate, tatra antarbhavatīty arthaḥ | evaṃ tāvān tāvat-parimāṇa eva saṃpadyate sarveṣu vedeṣu vedokteṣu karmasu yo 'rthaḥ yat karma-phalaṃ so 'rthaḥ brāhmaṇasya saṃnyāsinaḥ paramārtha-tattvaṃ vijānataḥ yo 'rthaḥ yat vijñāna-phalaṃ sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīyaṃ tasmin tāvān eva saṃpadyate tatraivāntarbhavatīty arthaḥ | yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃcit prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti yas tad veda yat sa veda [ChāU 4.1.2] iti śruteḥ | sarvaṃ karmākhilam iti ca vakṣyati | tasmāt prāk jñāna-niṣṭhādhikāra-prāpteḥ karmaṇy adhikṛtena
kūpa-taḍāgādy-artha-sthānīyam api karma kartavyam ||BhGS_2.46||
children.translated_text: even action that corresponds to the purpose of wells, ponds, etc. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.46 //

Just as in the world, in many water-reservoirs (<s>udapāna</s>) such as wells, ponds, and the like, where the water is limited — whatever purpose (<s>artha</s>) of measured extent there is, such as bathing, drinking, etc. — all that purpose is equally accomplished in water that overflows on all sides; it is included therein — this is the meaning. Similarly, whatever purpose, whatever fruit of action there is in all the <s>Vedas</s>, i.e., in the actions prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> — that purpose, of equal measure, for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), who knows the ultimate truth — is equally accomplished in that which corresponds to the water overflowing on all sides; it is included therein — this is the meaning. As per the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Just as all the lower throws of dice are contained in the <s>kṛta</s> [highest] throw, so whatever good <s>prajā</s> (beings) do, all that comes to the one who knows this, who knows what he knows' [<s>ChāU</s> 4.1.2]. And [the Lord] will state: 'all action in its entirety.' Therefore, prior to attaining eligibility for steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>), one who is qualified for action should perform

children.text: tava ca -
children.translated_text: And for you —

children.text: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana |
children.translated_text: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits;

children.text: mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||BhG_2.47||
children.translated_text: do not be the cause of the fruit of action; let there be no attachment to inaction for you. // <s>BhG</s> 2.47 //

children.text: karmaṇy evādhikāro na jñāna-niṣṭhāyāṃ te tava | tatra ca karma kurvataḥ mā phaleṣu adhikāro 'stu, karma-phala-tṛṣṇā mā bhūt kadācana kasyāṃcid apy avasthāyām ity arthaḥ | yadā karma-phale tṛṣṇā te syāt tadā karma-phala-prāpter hetuḥ syāḥ, evaṃ mā karma-phala-hetuḥ bhūḥ | yadā hi karma-phala-tṛṣṇā-prayuktaḥ karmaṇi pravartate tadā karma-phalasyaiva janmano hetur bhavet | yadi karma-phalaṃ neṣyate, kiṃ karmaṇā duḥkha-rūpeṇa ? iti mā te tava saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi akaraṇe prītir mā bhūt ||BhGS_2.47||
children.translated_text: Your right is to action alone — not to steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>). And while performing action, let there be no right to the fruits — let there be no craving for the fruit of action, at any time, in any state whatsoever — this is the meaning. Were you to have craving for the fruit of action, then you would be the cause of obtaining the fruit of action; thus, do not be the cause of the fruit of action. For when one, impelled by craving for the fruit of action, engages in action, one would become the cause of birth, which is the fruit of action. If the fruit of action is not desired, [one might think:] 'what is the use of action which is of the nature of suffering?' — therefore, let there be no attachment (<s>saṅga</s>) to inaction (<s>akarman</s>), no fondness for non-performance. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.47 //

children.text: yadi karma-phala-prayuktena na kartavyaṃ karma, kathaṃ tarhi kartavyam iti | ucyate -
children.translated_text: If action is not to be performed by one impelled by the desire for its fruit, then how is it to be performed? It is said —

children.text: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya |
children.translated_text: Established in <s>yoga</s>, perform actions, having abandoned attachment, O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>,

children.text: siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||BhG_2.48||
children.translated_text: becoming equal in success and failure; equanimity is called <s>yoga</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 2.48 //

children.text: yoga-sthaḥ san kuru karmāṇi kevalam īśvarārtham | tatrāpīśvaro me tuṣyatu iti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanaṃjaya | phala-tṛṣṇā-śūnyena kriyamāṇe karmaṇi sattva-śuddhijā jñāna-prāpti-lakṣaṇā siddhiḥ, tad-viparyayajā asiddhiḥ, tayoḥ siddhy-asiddhyor api samaḥ tulyo bhūtvā kuru karmāṇi | ko 'sau yogo yatra-sthaḥ kuru ity uktam ? idam eva tat --- siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||BhGS_2.48||
children.translated_text: Being established in <s>yoga</s>, perform actions solely for the sake of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). Even therein, [abandoning the thought] 'may the Lord be pleased with me' — having abandoned this attachment, O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>. When action is performed free from craving for results, success (<s>siddhi</s>), characterized by the attainment of knowledge born of purification of <s>sattva</s>, and failure (<s>asiddhi</s>), born of the opposite [i.e., non-purification] — becoming equal, even-minded regarding both success and failure, perform actions. What is that <s>yoga</s>, being established in which [He says] 'perform'? This is precisely it: equanimity in success and failure is called <s>yoga</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.48 //

children.text: yat punaḥ samatva-buddhi-yuktam īśvarārādhanārthaṃ karmoktam, etasmāt karmaṇaḥ --
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the action that has been described as endowed with the intellect of equanimity and performed for the sake of worshipping the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — compared to such action —

children.text: dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhi-yogād dhanaṃjaya |
children.translated_text: Action is far inferior to the <s>yoga</s> of intellect (<s>buddhi-yoga</s>), O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>;

children.text: buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ ||BhG_2.49||
children.translated_text: seek refuge in the intellect; wretched are those who are motivated by results. // <s>BhG</s> 2.49 //

children.text: dūreṇa ativiprakarṣeṇa atyantam eva hy avaram adhamaṃ nikṛṣṭaṃ karma phalārthinā kriyamāṇaṃ buddhi-yogāt samatva-buddhi-yuktāt karmaṇaḥ, janma-maraṇādi-hetutvāt | he dhanaṃjaya, yata evaṃ tataḥ yoga-viṣayāyāṃ buddhau tat-paripāka-jāyāṃ vā sāṃkhya-buddhau śaraṇam āśrayam abhaya-prāpti-kāraṇam anviccha prārthayasva, paramārtha-jñāna-śaraṇo bhavety arthaḥ | yato 'varaṃ karma kurvāṇāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ dīnāḥ phala-hetavaḥ phala-tṛṣṇā-prayuktāḥ santaḥ, yo vā etad akṣaraṃ gārgy aviditvāsmāl lokāt praiti sa kṛpaṇaḥ [BAU 3.8.10] iti śruteḥ ||BhGS_2.49||
children.translated_text: By far (<s>dūreṇa</s>), by a great distance, exceedingly inferior (<s>avara</s>), low, base is action performed by one who seeks its fruits, compared to <s>buddhi-yoga</s>, i.e., action endowed with the intellect of equanimity — because it is the cause of birth, death, etc. O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, since this is so, therefore seek refuge — seek shelter, the means of obtaining fearlessness — in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) pertaining to <s>yoga</s>, or in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s>-intellect born from the maturation thereof. The meaning is: become one who takes refuge in the knowledge of the ultimate reality. Because those who perform inferior action are wretched (<s>kṛpaṇa</s>), pitiable, being motivated by the desire for results — as per the <s>Śruti</s>: 'He who departs from this world without knowing this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, is wretched' [<s>BAU</s> 3.8.10]. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.49 //

children.text: samatva-buddhi-yuktaḥ san svadharmam anutiṣṭhan yat phalaṃ prāpnoti tac chṛṇu --
children.translated_text: Being endowed with the intellect of equanimity and carrying out one's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>), what fruit does one obtain? Listen to that —

children.text: buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte |
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with intellect (<s>buddhi-yukta</s>) abandons here [in this world] both merit and demerit;

children.text: tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam ||BhG_2.50||
children.translated_text: therefore, yoke yourself to <s>yoga</s>; <s>yoga</s> is skill in actions. // <s>BhG</s> 2.50 //

children.text: buddhi-yuktaḥ karma-samatva-viṣayayā buddhyā yukto buddhi-yuktaḥ saḥ jahāti parityajati iha asmin loke ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte puṇya-pāpe sattva-śuddhi-jñāna-prāpti-dvāreṇa yataḥ, tasmāt samatva-buddhi-yogāya yujyasva ghaṭāsva | yogo hi karmasu kauśalam sva-dharmākhyeṣu karmasu vartamānasya yā siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samatva-buddhir īśvarārpita-cetastayā tat kauśalaṃ kuśala-bhāvaḥ | tad dhi kauśalaṃ yad bandhana-svabhāvāny api karmāṇi samatva-buddhyā svabhāvān nivartante | tasmāt samatva-buddhi-yukto bhava tvam ||BhGS_2.50||
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhi-yuktaḥ</s>' — endowed with the intellect that has equanimity in action as its object; such a person abandons (<s>jahāti</s>), relinquishes, here in this world, both (<s>ubhe</s>) merit and demerit (<s>sukṛta-duṣkṛte</s>), i.e., virtue and sin — through the means of purification of <s>sattva</s> and attainment of knowledge. Therefore, yoke yourself to (<s>yujyasva</s>), strive for, the <s>yoga</s> of equanimity of intellect. For <s>yoga</s> is skill (<s>kauśala</s>) in actions — i.e., in actions called one's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>): for one engaged in such actions, the equanimity-intellect directed toward the Lord, that is the skill, the state of being skillful (<s>kuśala-bhāva</s>). For that indeed is skill: that even actions whose very nature is to bind, through the intellect of equanimity, are diverted from their [binding] nature. Therefore, be endowed with the intellect of equanimity. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.50 //

children.text: yasmāt -
children.translated_text: Because —

children.text: karmajaṃ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise, endowed with intellect, having abandoned the fruit born of action,

children.text: janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchanty anāmayam ||BhG_2.51||
children.translated_text: freed from the bondage of birth, go to the state that is free from affliction. // <s>BhG</s> 2.51 //

children.text: karmajaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā iti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ | iṣṭāniṣṭa-deha-prāptiḥ karmajaṃ phalaṃ karmabhyo jātaṃ buddhi-yuktāḥ samatva-buddhi-yuktāḥ santaḥ hi yasmāt phalaṃ tyaktvā parityajya manīṣiṇaḥ jñānino bhūtvā, janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ janmaiva bandhaḥ janma-bandhaḥ tena vinirmuktāḥ jīvanta eva janma-bandhāt vinirmuktāḥ santaḥ, padaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇoḥ mokṣākhyaṃ gacchanti anāmayaṃ sarvopadrava-rahitam ity arthaḥ | athavā buddhi-yogād dhanaṃjaya ity ārabhya paramārtha-darśana-lakṣaṇaiva sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīyā karma-yogaja-sattva-śuddha-janitā buddhir darśitā, sākṣāt-sukṛta-duṣkṛta-prahāṇādi-hetutva-śravaṇāt ||BhGS_2.51||
children.translated_text: '<s>Karmajam phalaṃ tyaktvā</s>' (having abandoned the fruit born of action) — is to be connected with the intervening [words]. The attainment of desirable and undesirable bodies is the fruit born of action (<s>karmaja phala</s>) — [that which is] produced from actions. Being endowed with the intellect of equanimity (<s>buddhi-yuktāḥ</s>), having abandoned, relinquished the fruit, the wise (<s>manīṣiṇaḥ</s>), having become knowers, freed from the bondage of birth — birth itself is bondage (<s>janma-bandha</s>); liberated from that — even while alive, being freed from the bondage of birth — they go to the supreme state (<s>pada</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is free from affliction (<s>anāmaya</s>), devoid of all distress — this is the meaning. Alternatively, beginning from '<s>buddhi-yogād dhanaṃjaya</s>' (O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, [action is far inferior] to <s>buddhi-yoga</s>), the intellect that corresponds to the water overflowing on all sides — characterized by the vision of ultimate reality, born of the purification of <s>sattva</s> produced by <s>karma-yoga</s> — has been shown, since we hear that it is directly the cause of the abandonment of merit and demerit, etc. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.51 //

children.text: yogānuṣṭhāna-janita-sattva-śuddhajā buddhiḥ kadā prāpsyate ity ucyate ---
children.translated_text: When will the intellect born of the purification of <s>sattva</s> produced by the practice of <s>yoga</s> be attained? It is said —

children.text: yadā te moha-kalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati |
children.translated_text: When your intellect crosses beyond the thicket of delusion,

children.text: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca ||BhG_2.52||
children.translated_text: then you will attain indifference toward what is yet to be heard and what has been heard. // <s>BhG</s> 2.52 //

children.text: yadā yasmin kāle te tava moha-kalilaṃ mohātmakam aviveka-rūpaṃ kāluṣyaṃ yena ātmānātma-viveka-bodhaṃ kaluṣīkṛtya viṣayaṃ pratyantaḥ-karaṇaṃ pravartate, tat tava buddhiḥ vyatitariṣyati vyatikramiṣyati, atiśuddha-bhāvam āpātryate ity arthaḥ | tadā tasmin kāle gantāsi prāpsyasi nirvedaṃ vairāgyaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca, tadā śrotavyaṃ śrutaṃ ca te niṣphalaṃ pratibhātīty abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.52||
children.translated_text: When (<s>yadā</s>), at which time, your intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) crosses beyond (<s>vyatitariṣyati</s>) the thicket of delusion (<s>moha-kalila</s>) — the impurity that is of the nature of delusion, of the form of non-discrimination, by which the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), having rendered turbid the awareness of the discrimination between Self and non-Self, operates toward sense-objects — [when] it will transcend that, will go beyond, meaning it will attain the state of extreme purity. Then (<s>tadā</s>), at that time, you will attain dispassion (<s>nirveda</s>) toward what is yet to be heard (<s>śrotavya</s>) and what has been heard (<s>śruta</s>); the purport is: then what is to be heard and what has been heard will appear fruitless to you. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.52 //

children.text: moha-kalilātyaya-dvāreṇa labdhātma-vivekaja-prajñaḥ kadā karma-yogajaṃ phalaṃ paramārtha-yogam avāpsyāmīti cet, tat sṛṇu --
children.translated_text: If [you ask:] 'Through the means of crossing beyond the thicket of delusion, having obtained the wisdom born of the discrimination of Self [and non-Self], when will I attain the fruit of <s>karma-yoga</s>, namely the <s>yoga</s> of the ultimate reality?' — then listen —

children.text: śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
children.translated_text: When your intellect, [now] perplexed by [conflicting] scriptural testimony, shall stand firm,

children.text: samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasyi ||BhG_2.53||
children.translated_text: unmoved in <s>samādhi</s>, then you will attain <s>yoga</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 2.53 //

children.text: śruti-vipratinnā aneka-sādhya-sādhana-saṃbandha-prakāśana-śrutibhiḥ śravaṇaiḥ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-lakṣaṇaiḥ vipratipannā nānā-pratinnā vikṣiptā satī te tava buddhir yadā yasmin kāle sthāsyati sthirībhūtā bhaviṣyati niścalā vikṣepa-calana-varjitā satī samādhau, samādhīyate cittam asminn iti samādhir ātmā, tasmin ātmani ity etat | acalā tatrāpi vikalpa-varjitā ity etat | buddhir antaḥkaraṇam | tadā tasmin kāle yogam avāpsyasi viveka-prajñāṃ samādhiṃ prāpsyasi ||BhGS_2.53||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śruti-vipratipannā</s>' — perplexed, distracted, pulled in various directions by the scriptural testimonies (<s>śruti</s>), the teachings that reveal the connections of various means and ends, characterized by engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and withdrawal (<s>nivṛtti</s>). When your intellect, which has been thus perplexed, shall stand firm (<s>sthāsyati</s>), shall become stable, at which time — unmoving (<s>niścalā</s>), free from the agitation of distraction — in <s>samādhi</s>: '<s>samādhi</s>' is that in which the mind is settled (<s>samādhīyate</s>); [it refers to] the Self (<s>ātman</s>) — in that Self. Immovable (<s>acalā</s>) therein too — meaning free from mental constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>). The intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) [is] the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). Then, at that time, you will attain <s>yoga</s> — you will attain the discriminative wisdom (<s>viveka-prajñā</s>), the <s>samādhi</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.53 //

children.text:
praśnabījaṃ pratilabhya arjuna uvācalabdhasamādhiprajñasya lakṣaṇabubhutsayā ---
arjuna uvāca-
children.translated_text:
[Śaṅkara's commentary:] Having obtained the seed of a question, <s>Arjuna</s> spoke, desiring to know the characteristics of one who has attained steadiness of wisdom in <s>samādhi</s> —
<s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: arjuna uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava |
children.translated_text: What is the description of one of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>), one established in <s>samādhi</s>, O <s>Keśava</s>?

children.text: sthita-dhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kim āsīta vrajeta kim ||BhG_2.54||
