children.translated_text: How does one of steady intellect (<s>sthitadhī</s>) speak? How does he sit? How does he move? // <s>BhG</s> 2.54 //

children.text: sthitā pratiṣṭhitā aham asmi paraṃ brahma iti prajñā yasya saḥ sthita-prajñas tasya sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā kiṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ vacanaṃ katham asau parair bhāṣyate samādhi-sthasya samādhau sthitasya he keśava | sthita-dhīḥ sthita-prajñaḥ svayaṃ vā kiṃ prabhāṣeta | kim āsīta vrajeta kim āsanaṃ vrajanaṃ vā tasya katham ity arthaḥ | sthita-prajñasya lakṣaṇam anena lokena pṛcchayate ||BhGS_2.54||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] One whose wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is established (<s>sthitā</s>), firmly rooted — [in the knowledge] 'I am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — is a <s>sthitaprajña</s> (one of steady wisdom). Of that <s>sthitaprajña</s>, what is the description (<s>bhāṣā</s>)? What is the speech, the utterance? How is he described by others? Of one established in <s>samādhi</s>, residing in <s>samādhi</s>, O <s>Keśava</s>. The <s>sthitadhī</s> — the one of steady wisdom — how does he himself speak? How does he sit? How does he move? — what is the manner of his sitting and walking? — this is the meaning. By this, the characteristics of the <s>sthitaprajña</s> are being asked about by this [questioner]. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.54 //

children.text: yo hy ādita eva saṃnyasya karmāṇi jñāna-yoga-niṣṭhāyāṃ pravṛttaḥ, yaś ca karma-yogena, tayoḥ prajahāti ity ārabhya ā adhyāya-parisamāpteḥ sthita-prajña-lakṣaṇaṃ sādhanaṃ copadiśyate | sarvatraiva hi adhyātma-śāstre kṛtārtha-lakṣaṇāni yāni tāny eva sādhanāni upadiśyante, yatna-sādhyatvāt | yāni yatna-sādhyāni sādhanāni lakṣaṇāni ca bhavanti tāni śrī-bhagavān uvāca--
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān |
children.translated_text: When a person abandons all desires, O <s>Pārtha</s>, that dwell in the mind,

children.text: ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadocyate ||BhG_2.55||
children.translated_text: satisfied in the Self alone, by the Self — then he is called one of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajña</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 2.55 //

[Śaṅkara's commentary:] Indeed, for both — he who from the very beginning, having renounced actions, is engaged in <s>jñānayoganiṣṭhā</s> (devotion to the path of knowledge), and he who [proceeds] through <s>karmayoga</s> (the path of action) — beginning from '<s>prajahāti</s>' (he abandons) up to the conclusion of the chapter, the characteristics and the means of [attaining] steady wisdom are taught. For in every spiritual teaching (<s>adhyātmaśāstra</s>), the characteristics of the accomplished one are themselves taught as the means [of attainment], since they are achievable through effort. Those that are achievable through effort and serve as means, and [also serve] as characteristics — the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: prajahāti prakarṣeṇa jahāti parityajati yadā yasmin kāle sarvān samastān kāmān icchā-bhedān he pārtha, mano-gatān manasi praviṣṭāan hṛdi praviṣṭān | sarva-kāma-parityāge tuṣṭi-kāraṇābhāvāt śarīra-dhāraṇa-nimitta-śeṣe ca sati unmatta-pramattasyeva pravṛttiḥ prāptā, ity ata ucyate --- ātmany eva pratyag-ātma-svarūpe eva ātmanā svenaiva bāhya-lābha-nirapekṣas tuṣṭāḥ paramārtha-darśanāmṛta-rasa-lābhena anyasmād alaṃ-pratyayavān sthita-prajñaḥ sthitā pratiṣṭhitā ātmānātma-vivekajā prajñā yasya saḥ sthita-prajñaḥ vidvān tadā ucyate | tyakta-putra-vitta-lokaiṣaṇaḥ saṃnyāsī ātmārāma ātma-krīḍāḥ sthita-prajña ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.55||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] '<s>Prajahāti</s>' — completely abandons, relinquishes. When — at what time — all, the entirety, of desires (<s>kāma</s>) — the varieties of wishes — O <s>Pārtha</s>, that have entered the mind, that have entered the heart. When all desires have been relinquished, since the cause of contentment would be absent, and since only what sustains the body remains, the conduct [of such a person] would be like that of a madman or one dazed — therefore it is said: satisfied in the Self alone — in the inner Self's own nature alone — by the Self alone, independent of external acquisitions, content — through the gain of the nectar-taste of the vision of the supreme truth, finding sufficiency apart from everything else — one of steady wisdom, one whose wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) born of the discrimination between Self and non-Self is established, firmly rooted — he is then called [a <s>sthitaprajña</s>]. One who has renounced the desires for progeny, wealth, and worlds — a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> (renunciant) who delights in the Self, who plays in the Self — this is the meaning of <s>sthitaprajña</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.55 //

children.text: kiṃ ca --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: duḥkheṣv anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ |
children.translated_text: One whose mind is not agitated in sorrows, who is free from longing for pleasures,

children.text: vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir ucyate ||BhG_2.56||
children.translated_text: from whom attachment, fear, and anger have departed — such a sage (<s>muni</s>) is called one of steady intellect (<s>sthitadhī</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 2.56 //

children.text: duḥkheṣv ādhyātmikādiṣu prāpteṣu na udvignaṃ na prakṣubhitaṃ duḥkha-prāptau mano yasya so 'yam anudvigna-manāḥ | tathā sukheṣu prāpteṣu vigatā spṛhā tṛṣṇā yasya, na agnir iva indhanādy-ādhāne sukhāny anu vivardhate sa vigata-spṛhaḥ | vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ rāga ca bhayaṃ ca krodha ca vītā vigatā yasmāt sa vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ | sthita-dhīḥ sthita-prajño muniḥ saṃnyāsī tadā ucyate ||BhGS_2.56||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In sorrows — those pertaining to the body (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and others — when they arise, one whose mind is not agitated, not disturbed upon the attainment of sorrow — he is '<s>anudvignamanāḥ</s>' (one of unperturbed mind). Likewise, when pleasures arise, one from whom longing (<s>spṛhā</s>), craving, has departed — who does not, like fire [fed] with fuel, grow [in desire] following pleasures — he is '<s>vigataspṛha</s>' (free from longing). '<s>Vītarāgabhayakrodha</s>' — attachment, fear, and anger — from whom these have departed, gone away — he is one from whom attachment, fear, and anger have departed. The <s>sthitadhī</s> — the one of steady wisdom — such a <s>muni</s>, a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), is then called [thus]. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.56 //

children.text: kiṃ ca--
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham |
children.translated_text: He who is without affection everywhere, who, obtaining this or that, whether good or bad,

children.text: nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhG_2.57||
children.translated_text: neither rejoices nor hates — his wisdom is firmly established. // <s>BhG</s> 2.57 //

children.text: yaḥ muniḥ sarvatra deha-jīvitādiṣv api anabhisneho 'bhisneha-varjitas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubhaṃ tat tat śubhaṃ aśubhaṃ vā labdhvā nābhinandati na dveṣṭi śubhaṃ prāpya na tuṣyati na hṛṣyati, aśubhaṃ ca prāpya na dveṣṭi ity arthaḥ | tasya evaṃ harṣa-viṣāda-varjitasya vivekajā prajñā pratiṣṭhitā bhavati ||BhGS_2.57||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] That <s>muni</s> who is without affection (<s>anabhisneha</s>) everywhere — even toward body, life, and such — devoid of attachment; who, obtaining this or that good or bad, having received the favorable or unfavorable, neither rejoices — upon gaining the good, he is not pleased, not delighted — and upon obtaining the bad, he does not hate — this is the meaning. Of such a one, free from elation and despondency, the wisdom born of discrimination is firmly established. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.57 //

children.text: kiṃ ca --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: And when this person withdraws, as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs, completely,

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhG_2.58||
children.translated_text: the senses from the objects of the senses — his wisdom is firmly established. // <s>BhG</s> 2.58 //

children.text: yadā saṃharate samyag upasaṃharate cāyaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhāyāṃ pravṛtto yatiḥ kūrmo 'ṅgāni iva yathā kūrmo bhayāt svāny aṅgāni upasaṃharati sarvaśaḥ sarvataḥ, evaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhaḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ sarva-viṣayebhya upasaṃharate | tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ity uktārthaṃ vākyam ||BhGS_2.58||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] When this ascetic (<s>yati</s>), engaged in devotion to knowledge, completely withdraws — properly draws back — as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs, just as a tortoise, out of fear, draws in its own limbs from all sides — so too the one established in knowledge withdraws the senses from the objects of the senses, from all sense-objects. 'His wisdom is firmly established' — this is a statement whose meaning has already been explained. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.58 //

children.text: tatra viṣayān anāharataḥ āturasyāpi indriyāṇi kūrmāṅgānīva saṃhriyante na tu tad-viṣayo rāgaḥ sa kathaṃ saṃhriyate ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In that case, even for one who is ill and abstains from sense-objects, the senses are withdrawn like the limbs of a tortoise — but the attachment (<s>rāga</s>) toward those objects is not [withdrawn]. How then is that withdrawn? It is stated —

children.text: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
children.translated_text: The sense-objects turn away from the embodied one who abstains from food,

children.text: rasa-varjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||BhG_2.59||
children.translated_text: except for the taste (<s>rasa</s>); but even that taste turns away upon seeing the Supreme. // <s>BhG</s> 2.59 //

children.text: yadyapi viṣayāḥ viṣayopalakṣitāni viṣaya-śabda-vācyāni indriyāṇi nirāhārasya anāhriyamāṇa-viṣayasya kaṣṭe tapasi sthitasya mūrkhasyāpi vinivartante dehino dehavataḥ rasa-varjaṃ raso rāgo viṣayeṣu yas taṃ varjayitvā | rasa-śabdo rāge prasiddhaḥ, sva-rasena pravṛttaḥ rasikaḥ rasajñaḥ, ity ādi-darśanāt | so 'pi raso rañjana-rūpaḥ sūkṣmo 'sya yateḥ paraṃ paramārtha-tattvaṃ brahma dṛṣṭvā upalabhya aham eva tat iti vartamānasya nivartate nirbījaṃ viṣaya-vijñānaṃ saṃpadyate ity arthaḥ | nāsati samyag-darśane rasasya ucchedaḥ | tasmāt samyag-darśanātmikāyāḥ prajñāyāḥ sthairyaṃ kartavyam ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_2.59||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Although the sense-objects — the senses denoted by the word 'sense-objects' as characterized by [their] objects — turn away from the embodied one, the one possessing a body, who abstains from food, who refrains from bringing in sense-objects, who abides in severe austerity — even of a fool — except for the taste (<s>rasa</s>). <s>Rasa</s> means attachment (<s>rāga</s>) toward sense-objects — the taste that remains. The word '<s>rasa</s>' is well-known in the sense of attachment, as seen from [expressions like] '<s>svarasena pravṛttaḥ</s>' (proceeding by natural inclination), '<s>rasika</s>' (one of refined taste), '<s>rasajña</s>' (a connoisseur), etc. Even that <s>rasa</s> — that subtle inclination of the nature of attachment — for this ascetic (<s>yati</s>), upon seeing, upon realizing the Supreme (<s>param</s>), the ultimate reality (<s>paramārthatattva</s>), <s>Brahman</s> — abiding [in the knowledge] 'I am indeed That' — turns away; the cognition of sense-objects becomes seedless — this is the meaning. Without right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), there is no eradication of <s>rasa</s> (attachment). Therefore, the purport is: one should strive for the steadiness of the wisdom characterized by right knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.59 //

children.text: samyag-darśana-lakṣaṇa-prajñā-sthairyaṃ cikīrṣatā ādau indriyāṇi sva-vaśe sthāpayitavyāni, yasmāt tad-anavasthāpane doṣam āha ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] One who desires to achieve steadiness of the wisdom characterized by right knowledge must first bring the senses under control, because he states the fault of not restraining them —

children.text: yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the turbulent senses, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, of even a striving person of discernment,

children.text: indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ ||BhG_2.60||
children.translated_text: forcibly carry away the mind. // <s>BhG</s> 2.60 //

children.text: yatataḥ prayatnaṃ kurvataḥ hi yasmāt kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ medhāvino 'pi iti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ | indriyāṇi pramāthīni pramathana-śīlāni viṣayābhimukhaṃ hi puruṣaṃ vikṣobhayanti ākulīkurvanti, ākulīkṛtya ca haranti prasabhaṃ prasahya prakāśam eva paśyato viveka-vijñāna-yuktaṃ manaḥ ||BhGS_2.60||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Of one who is striving — making effort — because, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, of a person of discernment (<s>vipaścit</s>) — even of an intelligent one — the connection is with an intervening [word]. The senses, which are turbulent (<s>pramāthin</s>) — of a violent nature — for they agitate, confuse a person whose mind is directed toward sense-objects; and having confused [him], they forcibly carry away — openly, even as he watches — the mind endowed with the knowledge of discrimination. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.60 //

children.text: yatas tasmāt--
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ |
children.translated_text: Having restrained all of them, one should sit disciplined, devoted to Me;

children.text: vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhG_2.61||
children.translated_text: for one whose senses are under control — his wisdom is firmly established. // <s>BhG</s> 2.61 //

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya saṃyamanaṃ vaśīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yuktaḥ samāhitaḥ san āsīta mat-paro 'haṃ vāsudevaḥ sarva-pratyag-ātmā paro yasya sa mat-paraḥ, nānyo 'haṃ tasmāt ity āsīta ity arthaḥ | evam āsīnasya yater vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi vartante abhyāsa-balāt tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhGS_2.61||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Having restrained all of them — having performed <s>saṃyamana</s> (restraint), i.e., subjugation [of the senses] — being <s>yukta</s>, concentrated, one should sit devoted to Me — I, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, am the innermost Self of all; one whose highest [object] is Me is '<s>matpara</s>'; [the meaning is:] 'I am not different from that [Self]' — thus one should sit. For such an ascetic who sits thus, one whose senses are under control through the power of practice — his wisdom is firmly established. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.61 //

children.text: athedānīṃ parābhaviṣyataḥ sarvānartha-mūlam idam ucyate --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Now, for one who is about to fall, this is declared as the root of all misfortune —

children.text: dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate |
children.translated_text: When a person contemplates sense-objects, attachment to them arises;

children.text: saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate ||BhG_2.62||
children.translated_text: from attachment, desire is born; from desire, anger arises. // <s>BhG</s> 2.62 //

children.text: krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ |
children.translated_text: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory;

children.text: smṛti-bhraṃśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati ||BhG_2.63||
children.translated_text: from the loss of memory, destruction of the intellect; from the destruction of the intellect, one perishes. // <s>BhG</s> 2.63 //

children.text: dhyāyataś cintayato viṣayāt śabdādīn viṣaya-viśeṣān ālocayataḥ puṃsaḥ puruṣasya saṅgaḥ āsaktiḥ prītis teṣu viṣayeṣu upajāyate utpadyate | saṅgāt prīteḥ saṃjāyate samutpadyate kāmas tṛṣṇā | kāmāt kutaścit pratihatāt krodho 'bhijāyate |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Of a person who contemplates — who thinks about sense-objects, who reflects upon the particular [qualities of] objects such as sound etc. — attachment (<s>saṅga</s>), fondness, affection toward those sense-objects arises, is produced. From attachment, from that fondness, desire (<s>kāma</s>), craving, is born. From desire, when it is somehow obstructed, anger arises.

children.text: krodhād bhavati saṃmoho 'vivekaḥ kāryākārya-viṣayaḥ | kruddho hi saṃmūḍhaḥ san gurum apy ākrośati | saṃmohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ śāstrācāryopadeśāhita-saṃskāra-janitāyāḥ smṛte syāt vibhramo bhraṃśaḥ smṛty-utpatti-nimitta-prāptau anutpattiḥ | tataḥ smṛti-bhraṃśāt buddhi-nāśaḥ buddhi-nāśaḥ | kāryākārya-viṣaya-vivekāyogyatā antaḥ-karaṇasya buddher nāśa ucyate | buddher nāśāt praṇaśyati | tāvad eva hi puruṣaḥ yāvad antaḥkaraṇaṃ tadīyaṃ kāryākārya-viṣaya-viveka-yogyam | tad-ayogyatve naṣṭa eva puruṣo bhavati | ataḥ tasyāntaḥ-karaṇasya buddher nāśāt praṇaśyati puruṣārthāyogyo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.62-63||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] From anger comes delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>) — absence of discrimination regarding what should and should not be done. For when confused by anger, one reviles even one's teacher. From delusion, confusion of memory — of the memory that arises from the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by the teachings of scripture and preceptor, there is confusion, loss — when the occasion for the arising of memory is present, it fails to arise. Then, from the loss of memory, destruction of the intellect — the incapacity of the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) for discriminating what should and should not be done is called the destruction of the intellect. From the destruction of the intellect, one perishes. For a person is [truly a person] only so long as his inner faculty is capable of discriminating what should and should not be done. When that capacity is lost, the person is as good as destroyed. Therefore, from the destruction of that inner faculty, the intellect, one perishes — becomes unfit for the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.62-63 //

children.text: sarvānarthasya mūlamuktaṃ viṣayābhidhyānam | atha idānīṃ mokṣakāraṇamidamucyate --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The root of all misfortune has been stated as brooding on sense-objects. Now the cause of liberation is stated —

children.text: rāga-dveṣa-viyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran |
children.translated_text: But one who moves among sense-objects with senses freed from attachment and aversion,

children.text: ātma-vaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati ||BhG_2.64||
children.translated_text: with senses under the control of the Self, self-governed — attains serenity (<s>prasāda</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 2.64 //

children.text: rāga-dveṣa-viyuktai rāgaś ca dveṣaś ca rāga-dveṣau, tat-puraḥsarā hi indriyāṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ svābhāvikī, tatra yo mumukṣuḥ bhavati saḥ tābhyāṃ viyuktaiḥ śrotrādibhir indriyair viṣayān avarjanīyān caran upalabhamānaḥ ātma-vaśyair ātmano vaśyāni vaśībhūtāni indriyāṇi tair ātma-vaśyair vidheyātmā icchātaḥ vidheya ātmā antaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ prasādam adhigacchati | prasādaḥ prasannatā svāsthyam ||BhGS_2.64||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] With senses freed from attachment and aversion — attachment and aversion are <s>rāgadveṣa</s>; for the natural activity of the senses is preceded by these two. One who seeks liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), with senses free from these two — with the senses of hearing etc. — moving among sense-objects that are unavoidable, experiencing [them]; with senses under the control of the Self — senses that are submissive, brought under control; such a one, with a self-governed (<s>vidheyātmā</s>) mind — one whose inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is governable at will — attains <s>prasāda</s>. <s>Prasāda</s> means serenity, clarity, tranquility of mind. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.64 //

children.text: prasāde sati kiṃ syāt ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] When serenity is attained, what follows? It is stated —

children.text: prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṃ hānir asyopajāyate |
children.translated_text: Upon the attainment of serenity, the destruction of all his sorrows arises;

children.text: prasanna-cetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ||BhG_2.65||
children.translated_text: for the intellect of one whose mind is serene quickly becomes firmly established. // <s>BhG</s> 2.65 //

children.text: prasāde sarva-duḥkhānām ādhyātmikādīnāṃ hānir vināśo 'sya yater upajāyate | kiṃ ca - prasanna-cetasaḥ svasthāntaḥ-karaṇasya hi yasmāt āśu śīghraṃ buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ākāśam iva pari samantāt avatiṣṭhate, ātma-svarūpeṇaiva niścalībhavatīty arthaḥ |
evaṃ prasanna-cetaso 'vasthita-buddhiḥ kṛta-kṛtyatā yataḥ, tasmāt rāga-dveṣa-viyuktair indriyaiḥ śāstrā-viruddheṣu avarjanīyeṣu yuktaḥ samācaret iti vākyārthaḥ ||BhGS_2.65||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since for one whose mind is serene, wisdom becomes established and the state of having accomplished one's purpose is [achieved] — therefore, with senses freed from attachment and aversion, in matters not contrary to scripture and unavoidable, one should, being disciplined (<s>yukta</s>), conduct oneself — this is the meaning of the passage. // <s>BhGS</s> 2.65 //

[Śaṅkara's commentary:] Upon the attainment of serenity (<s>prasāda</s>), the destruction — the cessation — of all sorrows, those pertaining to the body (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and others, arises for this ascetic. Moreover — for the <s>prasannacetas</s> (one whose mind is serene), one whose inner faculty is tranquil — because, quickly, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) becomes firmly established, standing firm on all sides like space — becoming steadfast in the very nature of the Self — this is the meaning.

children.text: seyaṃ prasannatā stūyate --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] This serenity is now praised —

children.text: nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
children.translated_text: There is no wisdom for the undisciplined, nor is there meditation for the undisciplined;

children.text: na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ||BhG_2.66||
children.translated_text: and for one who does not meditate, there is no peace — for the peaceless, whence happiness? // <s>BhG</s> 2.66 //

children.text: nāsti na vidyate na bhavatīty arthaḥ, buddhiḥ ātma-svarūpa-viṣayā ayuktasya asamāhitāntaḥ-karaṇasya | na ca asti ayuktasya bhāvanā ātma-jñānābhiniveśaḥ | tathā -- na cāsty abhāvayata ātma-jñānābhiniveśam akurvataḥ śāntir upaśamaḥ | aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ? indriyāṇāṃ hi viṣaya-sevā-tṛṣṇātaḥ nivṛttir yā tat-sukham, na viṣaya-viṣayā tṛṣṇā | duḥkham eva hi sā | na tṛṣṇāyāṃ satyāṃ sukhasya gandha-mātram apy upapadyate ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.66||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Nāsti</s>' — does not exist, does not arise — this is the meaning; the understanding concerning the true nature of the Self — for one who is not disciplined (<s>ayukta</s>), whose inner faculty is not concentrated. Nor does there exist for the undisciplined one <s>bhāvanā</s> — absorption in Self-knowledge. Likewise — nor is there for one who does not cultivate — who does not engage in Self-knowledge — peace (<s>śānti</s>), i.e., tranquility. And whence is happiness for one without peace? For happiness is the cessation of the senses' thirst for the enjoyment of sense-objects — it is not the desire that has sense-objects as its object. For that [desire] is indeed pain alone. The meaning is: when thirst exists, not even a trace of happiness is possible. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.66||

children.text: ayuktasya kasmād buddhir nāsti ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Why does understanding not exist for the undisciplined? It is stated:

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate |
children.translated_text: For the mind that follows in the wake of the wandering senses

children.text: tad asya harati prajñāṃ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi ||BhG_2.67||
children.translated_text: carries away one's wisdom, as the wind carries away a ship on the waters. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.67||

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ hi yasmāt caratāṃ sva-sva-viṣayeṣu pravartamānānāṃ yat mano 'nuvidhīyate anupravartate tat indriya-viṣaya-vikalpanena pravṛttaṃ mano 'sya yateḥ harati prajñām ātmānātma-vivekajāṃ nāśayati | katham ? vāyuḥ nāvam iva ambhasi udake jigamiṣatāṃ mārgāduddhṛtya unmārge yathā vāyuḥ nāvaṃ pravartayati, evam ātma-viṣayāṃ prajñāṃ hṛtvā mano viṣaya-viṣayāṃ karoti ||BhGS_2.67||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Of the senses' — since the senses are wandering, i.e., operating in their respective objects, the mind that follows them, that operates after them — that mind, engaged in the conceptualization of sense-objects, carries away the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) of this aspirant (<s>yati</s>), i.e., destroys the wisdom born of the discrimination between Self and non-Self. How? As the wind [carries away] a ship on the waters — just as the wind, seizing a ship of those who wish to travel from its path on the water, propels it onto a wrong path — in the same way, the mind, having carried away the wisdom pertaining to the Self, makes it pertain to sense-objects. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.67||

children.text: yatato hi ity upanyastasyārthasya anekadhā upapattim uktvā taṃ cārtham upapādya upasaṃharati ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having introduced the topic with 'for the one who strives' and having stated its justification in many ways and established that meaning, he now concludes:

children.text: tasmād yasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, he whose senses are completely restrained

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhG_2.68||
children.translated_text: from their objects — his wisdom is firmly established. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.68||

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ pravṛttau doṣa upapādito yasmāt tasmāt yasya yateḥ he mahābāho, nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ mānasādi-bhedaiḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ śabdādibhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||BhGS_2.68||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since the defect in the functioning of the senses has been established — therefore, the aspirant whose senses are completely restrained — in all ways, by the distinctions of mental [restraint] etc. — from sense-objects such as sound etc. — O mighty-armed one — his wisdom is firmly established. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.68||

children.text: yo 'yaṃ laukiko vaidika ca vyavahāraḥ sa utpanna-viveka-jñānasya sthita-prajñasya avidyākāryatvāt avidyā-nivṛttau nivartate, avidyāyā ca vidyā-virodhāt nivṛttiḥ, ity etam arthaṃ sphuṭīkurvann āha ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This worldly and <s>Vedic</s> activity — for the one of steady wisdom (<s>sthita-prajña</s>) in whom discriminative knowledge has arisen, since it is an effect of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — ceases when <s>avidyā</s> ceases; and <s>avidyā</s> ceases because of its opposition to <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). Making this meaning clear, he says:

children.text: yā niśā sarva-bhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
children.translated_text: That which is night for all beings — therein the self-controlled one is awake;

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||BhG_2.69||
children.translated_text: that in which beings are awake — that is night for the seeing sage (<s>muni</s>). ||<s>BhG</s> 2.69||

children.text: yā niśā rātriḥ sarva-padārthānām aviveka-karī tamaḥ-svabhāvatvāt sarva-bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām | kiṃ tat paramārtha-tattvaṃ sthita-prajñasya viṣayaḥ | yathā naktaṃ-carāṇām ahar eva sad anyeṣāṃ niśā bhavati, tadvat naktaṃ-cara-sthānīyānām ajñānāṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ niśeva niśā paramārtha-tattvam, agocaratvād atad-buddhīnām | tasyāṃ paramārtha-tattva-lakṣaṇāyām ajñāna-nidrāyāḥ prabuddho jāgarti saṃyamī saṃyamavān, jitendriyo yogīty arthaḥ | yasyāṃ grāhya-grāhaka-bheda-lakṣaṇāyām avidyā-niśāyāṃ prasuptāny eva bhūtāni jāgrati iti ucyante, yasyāṃ niśāyāṃ prasuptā iva svapna-dṛśaḥ, sā niśā avidyā-rūpatvāt paramārtha-tattvaṃ paśyato muneḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'That which is night' — night is that which causes non-discrimination of all things, because of its darkness-nature — for all beings, for all creatures. What is that? The ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha-tattva</s>), which is the domain of the one of steady wisdom. Just as the day for nocturnal creatures is night for others, so too for all beings — who are in the position of nocturnal creatures, being ignorant — the ultimate reality is as if night, i.e., is night, because it is beyond their cognition, since they have no understanding of it. 'Therein' — in that which has the character of ultimate reality — the one who has awakened from the sleep of ignorance 'is awake' — the self-controlled one (<s>saṃyamī</s>), the one endowed with self-restraint, a <s>yogin</s> who has conquered the senses — this is the meaning. And that in which beings are said to 'be awake' — the night of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), characterized by the distinction between grasper and grasped — [in which] the beings are as if asleep, seeing as in a dream — that is night, because of its <s>avidyā</s>-nature, for the sage who sees the ultimate reality.

children.text: ataḥ karmāṇi avidyāvasthāyām eva codyante, na vidyāvasthāyām | vidyāyāṃ hi satyām udite savitari śārvaram iva tamaḥ praṇāśam upagacchati avidyā | prāk vidyotpatteḥ avidyā pramāṇa-buddhyā gṛhyamāṇā kriyā-kāraka-phala-bheda-rūpā satī sarva-karma-hetutvaṃ pratipadyate | na apramāṇa-buddhyā gṛhyamāṇāyāḥ karma-hetutvopapattiḥ, pramāṇa-bhūtena vedena mama coditaṃ kartavyaṃ karma iti hi karmaṇi kartā pravartate, na avidyā-mātram idaṃ sarvaṃ bheda-jātam iti jñānaṃ tasya ātmajñasya sarva-karma-saṃnyāse eva adhikāro na pravṛttau | tathā ca darśayiṣyati --- tad-buddhayas tad-ātmānaḥ ity ādinā jñāna-niṣṭhāyām eva tasya adhikāram |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, actions are enjoined only in the state of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), not in the state of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). For when knowledge has truly arisen, <s>avidyā</s> is destroyed, just as the darkness of night [is destroyed] when the sun has risen. Before the arising of knowledge, <s>avidyā</s> — when grasped by the cognition of being a valid means of knowledge — taking the form of the distinction between action, agent, and result, becomes the cause of all actions. But for <s>avidyā</s> that is not grasped by the cognition of being a valid means [of knowledge], there is no logical possibility of its being the cause of action. For an agent engages in action [thinking] 'the action enjoined upon me by the <s>Veda</s>, which is a valid means of knowledge, is to be performed' — but the [cognition] 'all this differentiation is nothing but <s>avidyā</s>' — the knowledge that [arises for] that knower of the Self: his qualification is only for the complete renunciation of all actions, not for engagement [in action]. And thus [the Lord] will show — by 'with their understanding fixed on That, their selves absorbed in That' etc. — his qualification is solely for steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>).

children.text: tatrāpi pravartaka-pramāṇābhāve pravṛtty-anupapattiḥ iti cet, na | svātma-viṣayatvād ātma-vijñānasya | na hy ātmanaḥ svātmani pravartaka-pramāṇāpekṣatā, ātmatvād eva | tad-antatvāc ca sarva-pramāṇānāṃ pramāṇatvasya | na hy ātma-svarūpādhigame sati punaḥ pramāṇa-prameya-vyavahāraḥ saṃbhavati | pramātṛtvaṃ hy ātmanaḥ nivartayati antyaṃ pramāṇam | nivartayad eva cāpramāṇībhavati, svapna-kāla-pramāṇam iva prabodhe | loke ca vastv-adhigame pravṛtti-hetutvādarśanāt pramāṇasya | tasmān nātma-vidaḥ karmaṇy adhikāra iti siddham ||BhGS_2.69||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If [one objects:] even there, in the absence of a prompting means of valid knowledge, engagement is unjustified — No, because Self-knowledge pertains to one's own Self. For the Self does not require a prompting means of valid knowledge with respect to its own Self, precisely because it is the Self. And because the validity of all means of valid knowledge terminates in it [the Self]. For after the realization of the true nature of the Self, the transaction involving means of knowledge and objects of knowledge is no longer possible. For the ultimate means of valid knowledge negates the knower-status (<s>pramātṛtva</s>) of the Self. And in negating it, it itself becomes non-authoritative, just as the means of valid knowledge operative during dream [becomes non-authoritative] upon awakening. And because in the world, the means of valid knowledge is not seen to be the cause of engagement [in action] upon the realization of a thing. Therefore, it is established that the knower of the Self has no qualification for action. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.69||

children.text: viduṣas tyaktaiṣaṇasya sthita-prajñasya yater eva mokṣa-prāptiḥ, na tu asaṃnyāsinaḥ kāma-kāminaḥ ity etam arthaṃ dṛṣṭāntena pratipādayiṣyan āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Liberation is attained only by the one of steady wisdom who is a renunciant (<s>yati</s>) who has abandoned all desires — not by one who has not renounced, who desires objects of desire. Intending to establish this meaning through an illustration, he says:

children.text: āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as waters enter the ocean, which is being filled from all sides

children.text: samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
children.translated_text: yet remains unmoved in its foundation —

children.text: tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve
children.translated_text: so too, he into whom all desires enter [without disturbing him] —

children.text: sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī ||BhG_2.70||
children.translated_text: he attains peace, not the desirer of desires. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.70||

children.text: āpūryamāṇam adbhir acala-pratiṣṭham acalatayā pratiṣṭhā avasthitiḥ yasya tam acala-pratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ sarvato gatāḥ praviśanti svātmastham avikriyam eva santaṃ yadvat, tadvat kāmāḥ viṣaya-saṃnidhāv api sarvataḥ icchā-viśeṣāḥ yaṃ puruṣam --- samudram iva āpaḥ -- avikurvantaḥ praviśanti sarve ātmany eva pralīyante na svātma-vaśaṃ kurvanti, sa śāntir mokṣam āpnoti, netaraḥ kāma-kāmī, kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ viṣayāḥ tān kāmayituṃ śīlaṃ yasya saḥ kāma-kāmī, naiva prāpnotīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.70||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Being filled' — by waters; 'of unmoved foundation' — that whose stability is characterized by immovability — that ocean, [into which] waters from all sides enter — the ocean remaining unchanged and self-contained — just as [this happens]; similarly, desires — particular wants — even in the proximity of sense-objects, from all sides, enter that person — like waters entering the ocean — without causing perturbation, all dissolving into the Self itself, not bringing him under their sway. He attains peace (<s>śānti</s>), i.e., liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>); not the other, the desirer of desires — '<s>kāma-kāmī</s>' — the objects that are desired are <s>kāmas</s>, i.e., sense-objects; he whose disposition is to desire them is a <s>kāma-kāmī</s>; he does not attain [peace] — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.70||

children.text: yasmād evaṃ tasmāt -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati niḥspṛhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The person who, abandoning all desires, lives free from longing,

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||BhG_2.71||
children.translated_text: without 'mine'-ness, without ego-sense — he attains peace. ||<s>BhG</s> 2.71||

children.text: vihāya parityajya kāmān yaḥ saṃnyāsī pumān sarvān aśeṣataḥ kārtsnyena carati, jīvana-mātra-ceṣṭāśeṣaḥ paryaṭatīty arthaḥ | niḥspṛhaḥ śarīra-jīvana-mātre 'pi nirgatā spṛhā yasya saḥ niḥspṛhaḥ san nirmamaḥ śarīra-jīvana-mātrākṣipta-parigrahe 'pi mamedam ity abhiniveśa-varjitaḥ, nirahaṃkāraḥ vidyāvattvādi-nimittātma-saṃbhāvanā-rahitaḥ ity etat | sa evaṃbhūtaḥ sthita-prajñaḥ brahmavit śāntiṃ sarva-saṃsāra-duḥkhoparama-lakṣaṇāṃ nirvāṇākhyām adhigacchati prāpnoti brahma-bhūto bhavati ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_2.71||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Abandoning' — completely relinquishing; 'desires' — all of them, without remainder, entirely — the renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsī</s>) 'lives' — his only activity being the effort to sustain life — the meaning is: wanders about. '<s>Niḥspṛha</s>' — one from whom longing has departed even for the mere sustenance of the body — being thus; '<s>nirmama</s>' — even regarding the possessions acquired incidentally for mere bodily sustenance, free from the attachment 'this is mine'; '<s>nirahaṃkāra</s>' — free from self-identification caused by the idea of being learned etc. — this is [the meaning]. Such a one — the one of steady wisdom, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> — attains peace (<s>śānti</s>), characterized by the cessation of all <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering, called <s>nirvāṇa</s> — attains it, i.e., becomes <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.71||

children.text: saiṣā jñāna-niṣṭhā stūyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>) is praised:

children.text: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
children.translated_text: This is the <s>brāhmī</s> state (<s>Brāhmī sthitiḥ</s>), O <s>Pārtha</s> — having attained it, one is not deluded;

children.text: sthitvāsyām anta-kāle 'pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati ||BhG_2.72||
children.translated_text: abiding in it even at the time of death, one attains <s>brahma-nirvāṇa</s> (the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> / liberation). ||<s>BhG</s> 2.72||

children.text: eṣā yathoktā brāhmī brahmaṇi bhavā iyaṃ sthitiḥ sarvaṃ karma saṃnyasya brahma-rūpeṇaiva avasthānam ity etat | he pārtha, naināṃ sthitiṃ prāpya labdhvā na vimuhyati na mohaṃ prāpnoti | sthitvāsyāṃ sthitau brāhmyāṃ yathoktāyāṃ anta-kāle 'pi antye vayasy api brahma-nirvāṇaṃ brahma-nirvṛtiṃ mokṣam ṛcchati gacchati | kim u vaktavyaṃ brahmacaryād eva saṃnyasya yāvaj jīvaṃ yo brahmaṇy eva avatiṣṭhate sa brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati iti ||BhGS_2.72||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'This' — as described — '<s>brāhmī</s>' — pertaining to <s>Brahman</s> — 'this state' — having renounced all actions, abiding in the form of <s>Brahman</s> alone — this is [the meaning]. O <s>Pārtha</s>, having attained — having obtained — this state, one is not deluded, does not attain delusion. Abiding in this state — the <s>brāhmī</s> state as described — 'even at the time of death' — even at the end of life — one attains <s>brahma-nirvāṇa</s>, the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, liberation. What need is there to say that one who, having renounced from the very stage of <s>brahmacarya</s> (studenthood), abides in <s>Brahman</s> alone for one's entire life, attains <s>brahma-nirvāṇa</s>? ||<s>BhGS</s> 2.72||

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter in the blessed <s>Bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, who was the foremost among the supreme renunciants and wandering monks. ||

children.text: BhG 3
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 3

children.text: tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ śaṅkara-bhāṣyam
children.translated_text: Third Chapter — <s>Śaṅkara's</s> Commentary

children.text:
śāstrasya pravṛtti-nivṛtti-viṣaya-bhūte dve buddhī bhagavatā nirdiṣṭe, sāṅkhye buddhir yoge buddhir iti ca | tatra prajahāti yadā kāmān ity ārabhya ā adhyāya-parisamāpteḥ sāṅkhya-buddhy-āśritānāṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kartavyam uktvā teṣāṃ tan-niṣṭhatayaiva ca kṛtārthatā uktā eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ iti | arjunāya ca karmaṇy evādhikāras te, mā saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi iti karma eva kartavyam uktavān yoga-buddhim āśritya, na tata eva śreyaḥ-prāptim uktavān | tad etad ālakṣya paryākulībhūta-buddhir arjuna uvāca - kathaṃ bhaktāya śreyo 'rthine yat sākṣāt śreyaḥ-sādhanaṃ sāṅkhya-buddhi-niṣṭhāṃ śrāvayitvā māṃ karmaṇi dṛṣṭānekānartha-yukte pāramparyeṇāpi anaikāntika-śreyaḥ-prāpti-phale niyuñjyād iti yuktaḥ paryākulībhāvo 'rjunasya | tad-anurūpa-praśnaḥ jyāyasī
cet ity ādiḥ | praśnāpākaraṇa-vākyaṃ ca bhagavatā uktaṃ yathokta-vibhāga-viṣaye śāstre |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The Lord has indicated two understandings pertaining to the twofold subject-matter of the scripture — engagement and withdrawal: <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> (the understanding pertaining to knowledge) and <s>yoga-buddhi</s> (the understanding pertaining to action). Therein, from 'When a person abandons all desires' up to the end of the chapter, having stated that those who resort to <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> must practice renunciation, and that their fulfillment is through steadfastness in that alone — 'This is the <s>brāhmī</s> state.' And to <s>Arjuna</s>, having said 'Your right is to action alone, not to inaction' — [the Lord] taught that action alone is to be performed, resorting to <s>yoga-buddhi</s>, but did not state that the highest good (<s>śreyas</s>) is attained from that [action] itself. Perceiving this, <s>Arjuna</s>, with his understanding bewildered, said [in effect]: 'How is it that, having communicated to a devoted seeker of the highest good the steadfastness in <s>Sāṃkhya-buddhi</s> which is the direct means to the highest good, [the Lord] would engage me in action — which is seen to have many defects and whose attainment of the highest good is uncertain even indirectly?' Thus <s>Arjuna's</s> bewilderment is justified. The question conforming to it is 'If you consider...' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.1] etc. And the Lord's resolving statement was spoken in accordance with the scripture as it deals with the subject of the stated distinction.

children.text: kecit tu arjunasya praśnārtham anyathā kalpayitvā tat-pratikūlaṃ bhagavataḥ prativacanaṃ varṇayanti | yathā ca ātmanā sambandha-granthe gītārtho nirūpitas tat-pratikūlaṃ ceha punaḥ praśna-prativacanayor arthaṃ nirūpayanti | kathaṃ ? tatra sambandha-granthe tāvat sarveṣām āśramiṇāṃ jñāna-karmaṇoḥ samuccayo gītā-śāstre nirūpito 'rtha ity uktam | punaḥ viśeṣitaṃ ca yāvaj-jīva-śruti-coditāni karmāṇi parityajya kevalād eva jñānān mokṣaḥ prāpyata ity etad ekāntenaiva pratiṣiddham iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But some, having imagined <s>Arjuna's</s> question to mean something different, describe the Lord's answer as contrary to it. And they describe the meaning of the question and answer here as contrary to the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> as determined by themselves in their introductory work (<s>sambandha-grantha</s>). How? In that introductory work, they stated that the meaning established in the <s>Gītā-śāstra</s> is the combination (<s>samuccaya</s>) of knowledge and action for all those belonging to the [four] stages of life (<s>āśramins</s>). And further, they specifically stated that liberation is attained from the renunciation of actions enjoined by the '<s>yāvaj jīva</s>' (lifelong) <s>śruti</s> through knowledge alone — this has been categorically rejected.

children.text: iha tv āśrama-vikalpaṃ darśayatā yāvaj-jīva-śruti-coditānām eva karmaṇāṃ parityāga uktaḥ | tat katham īdṛśaṃ viruddham artham arjunāya brūyād bhagavān, śrotā vā kathaṃ viruddham artham avadhārayet | tatraitat syād gṛhasthānām eva śrauta-karma-parityāgena kevalād eva jñānān mokṣaḥ pratiṣidhyate na tv āśramāntarāṇām iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But here, by presenting the alternative of life-stages (<s>āśrama-vikalpa</s>), only the renunciation of actions enjoined by the '<s>yāvaj jīva</s>' <s>śruti</s> has been stated. How then would the Lord speak such a contradictory meaning to <s>Arjuna</s>, or how would the listener ascertain a contradictory meaning? It might be argued here that liberation through knowledge alone, with the renunciation of <s>śrauta</s> action, is rejected only for householders, not for those in other stages of life.

children.text: etad api pūrvottar-viruddham eva | kathaṃ, sarvāśramiṇāṃ jñāna-karmaṇoḥ samuccayo gītā-śāstre niścito 'rtha iti pratijñāya iha kathaṃ tad-viruddhaṃ kevalād eva jñānān mokṣaṃ brūyād āśramāntarāṇām |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This too is contradictory to [their own] previous and subsequent [statements]. How? Having declared that the combination of knowledge and action is the established meaning of the <s>Gītā-śāstra</s> for those in all stages of life, how could one here state the contrary — liberation through knowledge alone — for those in other stages of life?

children.text: atha mataṃ śrauta-karmāpekṣayaitad-vacanaṃ kevalād eva jñānāt śrauta-karma-rahitād gṛhasthānāṃ mokṣaḥ pratiṣidhyate iti | tatra gṛhasthānāṃ vidyamānam api smārtaṃ karmāvidyamānavad upekṣya jñānād eva kevalān na mokṣa ity ucyata iti | etad api viruddham | katham ? gṛhasthasyaiva smārta-karmaṇā samuccitād jñānān mokṣaḥ pratiṣidhyate na tu āśramāntarāṇām iti kathaṃ vivekibhiḥ śakyam avadhārayitum |
children.translated_text: Now, if it be held that this statement [of the <s>Gītā</s>] is with reference to Vedic ritual (<s>śrautakarma</s>), [meaning] that liberation is denied to householders from mere knowledge alone devoid of Vedic ritual — then, even though householders do possess <s>smārta</s> (traditional) rituals, these are disregarded as if non-existent, and it is said that 'from mere knowledge alone, devoid [of ritual], there is no liberation.' This too is contradictory. How? How could discriminating persons determine that liberation is denied to householders from knowledge combined with <s>smārta</s> ritual, but not to those in other stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>)?

children.text: kiṃ ca, yadi mokṣa-sādhanatvena smārtāni karmāṇi ūrdhva-retasāṃ samuccīyante tathā gṛhasthasyāpi iṣyatāṃ smārtair eva samuccayo na śrautaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if <s>smārta</s> rituals are combined [with knowledge] as means to liberation for celibate renouncers (<s>ūrdhvaretaḥ</s>), then let the combination with <s>smārta</s> rituals alone — not with Vedic rituals — be accepted for the householder as well.

children.text: atha śrautaiḥ smārtaiś ca gṛhasthasyaiva samuccayo mokṣāya ūrdhva-retasāṃ tu smārta-karma-mātra-samuccitāj jñānān mokṣa iti | tatraivaṃ sati gṛhasthasyāyāsa-bāhulyaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ ca bahu-duḥkha-rūpaṃ karma śirasi aropitaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: If, however, the combination with both Vedic and <s>smārta</s> rituals is for the householder alone for the sake of liberation, while for the celibate renouncers liberation comes from knowledge combined with <s>smārta</s> rituals alone — then, in that case, the householder would have an excessive burden of toil, with the heavy, painful load of both Vedic and <s>smārta</s> rituals placed upon his head.

children.text: atha gṛhasthasyaivāyāsa-bāhulya-kāraṇān mokṣaḥ syān nāśramāntarāṇāṃ śrauta-nitya-karma-rahitatvād iti | tad apy asat | sarvopaniṣatsu itihāsa-purāṇa-yoga-śāstre ca jñānāṅgatvena mumukṣoḥ sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-vidhānād āśrama-vikalpa-samuccaya-vidhānāc ca śruti-smṛtyoḥ |
children.translated_text: If, then, liberation would belong to the householder alone because of his excessive toil, and not to those in other stages of life because they lack obligatory Vedic rituals — that too is incorrect. For in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, in the <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇas</s>, and in the <s>Yogaśāstra</s>, the renunciation of all <s>karmas</s> is prescribed for the seeker of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) as an auxiliary to knowledge; and both the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (traditional scripture) prescribe either the choice among stages of life or their combination.

children.text: siddhas tarhi sarvāśramiṇāṃ jñāna-karmaṇoḥ samuccayaḥ ? na, mumukṣoḥ sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-vidhānāt | vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti [BAU 3.5.1], tasmāt saṃnyāsam eṣāṃ tapasām atiriktam āhuḥ [NāU 2.79], nyāsa evātyarecayet [NāU 2.78], iti | na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike 'mṛtatvam ānaśuḥ [NāU 2.12] iti ca | brahmacaryād eva pravrajet [JāvāU 4] ity ādyāḥ śrutayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Is then the combination of knowledge and action established for those in all stages of life? No — because the renunciation of all <s>karmas</s> is prescribed for the seeker of liberation. [The scriptures state:] 'Having risen, they live the life of mendicancy' (<s>BAU</s> 3.5.1); 'Therefore they declare renunciation as surpassing these austerities' (<s>NāU</s> 2.79); 'Renunciation alone excels' (<s>NāU</s> 2.78). And: 'Not by <s>karma</s>, not by progeny, not by wealth — by renunciation alone did some attain immortality' (<s>NāU</s> 2.12). And: 'One should go forth as a wandering mendicant directly from the student stage (<s>brahmacaryāśrama</s>)' (<s>JāvāU</s> 4). These and other <s>śruti</s> passages [support this].

children.text: tyaja dharmam adharmaṃ ca ubhe satyānṛte tyaja |
children.translated_text: 'Abandon <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty) and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteous duty); abandon both truth and untruth;

children.text: ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā yena tyajasi tat tyaja ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned both truth and untruth, abandon that by which you abandon.'

children.text:
saṃsāram eva niḥsāraṃ dṛṣṭvā sāra-didṛkṣayā |
pravrajanty akṛtodvāhāḥ paraṃ vairāgyam āśritāḥ || iti bṛhaspatir api kacaṃ prati |
children.translated_text:
'Seeing <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) to be without essence, and desiring to see the essence,
those who have not married go forth, having resorted to supreme dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>).' Thus spoke <s>Bṛhaspati</s> to <s>Kaca</s>.

children.text: karmaṇā badhyate jantur vidyayā ca vimucyate |
tasmāt karma na kurvanti yatayaḥ pāra-darśinaḥ || [Mbh 12.241.7] iti śukānuśāsanam |
children.translated_text: therefore, ascetics who see the farther shore do not perform <s>karma</s>.' [<s>Mbh</s> 12.241.7] — This is the instruction of <s>Śuka</s>.
'A creature is bound by <s>karma</s> (action) and liberated by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge);

children.text: ihāpi sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasya ity ādi | mokṣasya cākāryatvān mumukṣoḥ karmānarthakyam | nityāni pratyavāya-parihārārtham anuṣṭheyāni iti cet, na | asaṃnyāsi-viṣayatvāt pratyavāya-prāpteḥ | na hi agnikāryādy-akaraṇāt saṃnyāsinaḥ pratyavāyaḥ kalpayituṃ śakyo yathā brahmacāriṇām asaṃnyāsinām api karmiṇām | na tavan nityānāṃ karmaṇām abhāvād eva bhāva-rūpasya pratyavāyasya utpattiḥ kalpayituṃ śakyā katham asataḥ sajjāyate [ChāU 6.2.2] iti asataḥ sajjanmāsambhava-śruteḥ |
children.translated_text: Here too [in the <s>Gītā</s>] it is said: 'Mentally renouncing all <s>karmas</s>' and so forth. And since liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is not something to be produced by action, <s>karma</s> is purposeless for the seeker of liberation. If it be said: 'Obligatory rites (<s>nitya karmas</s>) must be performed to ward off sin (<s>pratyavāya</s>)' — no, because the incurrence of sin applies only to those who have not renounced. For one cannot impute sin to a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) for not performing the fire-ritual and the like, just as [it cannot be imputed to] celibate students (<s>brahmacārin</s>) who are non-renunciants but are ritual performers. In the first place, it is not possible to impute the arising of sin — which has a positive nature — from the mere absence of obligatory rites, [for the <s>śruti</s> states:] 'How can being arise from non-being?' (<s>ChāU</s> 6.2.2) — the <s>śruti</s> [declares] the impossibility of the production of the existent from the non-existent.

children.text: yadi vihitākaraṇād asambhāvyam api pratyavāyaṃ brūyād vedas tadā anartha-karo vedaḥ apramāṇam ity uktaṃ syāt | vihitasya karaṇākaraṇayoḥ duḥkha-mātra-phalatvāt | tathā ca kārakaṃ śāstraṃ na jñāpakam iti anupapannārthaṃ kalpitaṃ syāt | na caitad iṣṭam | tasmān na saṃnyāsināṃ karmāṇi ato jñāna-karmaṇoḥ samuccayānupapattiḥ | jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir iti | arjunasya praśnānupapatteś ca |
children.translated_text: If the <s>Veda</s> were to declare that even an impossible sin arises from not performing what is enjoined, then the <s>Veda</s> would be a producer of harm and thus non-authoritative. For both the performance and non-performance of what is enjoined would have suffering alone as their result. And accordingly, the [position that] scripture is prescriptive rather than informative would be a fabrication of an untenable meaning. But this is not acceptable. Therefore, there are no ritual duties for renunciants — hence the combination of knowledge and action is untenable. 'If you consider <s>buddhi</s> (knowledge) to be superior to <s>karma</s> (action)' [<s>BhG</s> 3.1] — and <s>Arjuna</s>'s question would also be untenable [if a combination were intended].

children.text: yadi hi bhagavatā dvitīye adhyāye jñānaṃ karma ca samuccayena tvayānuṣṭheyam ity uktaṃ syāt tato 'rjunasya praśno 'nupapanno jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana iti | arjunāya ced buddhi-karmaṇī tvayānuṣṭheye iti ukte yā karmaṇo jyāyasī buddhiḥ sā apy uktā eveti tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava iti praśno na kathaṃcana upapadyate |
children.translated_text: For if the <s>Bhagavān</s> had said in the second chapter, 'Knowledge and action are to be combined and performed by you,' then <s>Arjuna</s>'s question — 'If you consider <s>buddhi</s> to be superior to <s>karma</s>, O <s>Janārdana</s>' — would be untenable. If <s>Arjuna</s> had been told, 'Both knowledge and action are to be performed by you,' then since the <s>buddhi</s> that is superior to <s>karma</s> has also been stated, the question 'Then why do you urge me to terrible action, O <s>Keśava</s>?' would be completely untenable.

children.text: na cārjunasyaiva jyāyasī buddhir nānuṣṭheyeti bhagavatoktaṃ pūrvam iti kalpayituṃ yuktam, yena jyāyasī ced iti praśnaḥ syāt | yadi punar ekasya puruṣasya jñāna-karmaṇor virodhād yugapad anuṣṭhānaṃ na sambhavatīti bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyatvaṃ bhagavatā pūrvam uktaṃ syāt tato 'yaṃ praśna upapannaḥ jyāyasī ced ity ādiḥ |
children.translated_text: And it is not proper to suppose that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had previously told <s>Arjuna</s> that the superior <s>buddhi</s> is not to be practiced [by him] — such that the question 'If the superior...' would arise. If, however, [one supposes that] because the simultaneous practice of knowledge and action is impossible for one person due to their mutual opposition, the <s>Bhagavān</s> had previously stated that they are to be practiced by different persons — then this question 'If [<s>buddhi</s> is] superior...' and so forth would be appropriate.

children.text: avivekataḥ praśna-kalpanāyām api bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyatvena bhagavataḥ prativacanaṃ nopapadyate | na cājñāna-nimittaṃ bhagavat-prativacanaṃ kalpyam | asmāc ca bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyatvena jñāna-karma-niṣṭhayor bhagavataḥ prativacana-darśanāt, jñāna-karmaṇoḥ samuccayānupapattiḥ | tasmāt kevalād eva jñānān mokṣa ity eṣo 'rtho niścito gītāsu sarvopaniṣatsu ca | jñāna-karmaṇor ekaṃ vada niścitya iti ca eka-viṣayaiva prārthanānupapannobhayoḥ samuccaya-sambhave |
children.translated_text: Even if one imagines the question to arise from lack of discrimination, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s reply as being about the practice by different persons would not be appropriate [on the samuccaya view]. And it is not proper to suppose the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s reply to be born of ignorance. And from this — that the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s reply shows that the disciplines of knowledge and action are to be practiced by different persons — the combination of knowledge and action is untenable. Therefore, liberation results from knowledge alone — this is the settled meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> and all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. And the prayer 'Tell me one thing decisively — knowledge or action' — this request for just one [of the two] would be inappropriate if the combination of both were possible.

children.text: kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvam iti ca jñāna-niṣṭhā-sambhavam arjunasyāvadhāraṇena darśayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, do perform action alone' [<s>BhG</s> 4.15] — [the <s>Bhagavān</s>] will demonstrate, by the restrictive particle [<s>eva</s>], that the discipline of knowledge is not possible for <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: arjuna uvāca
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana |
children.translated_text: If you consider <s>buddhi</s> (knowledge/intellect) to be superior to <s>karma</s> (action), O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava ||BhG_3.1||
children.translated_text: then why do you urge me to terrible action, O <s>Keśava</s>? ||<s>BhG</s> 3.1||

children.text: jyāyasī śreyasī cet yadi karmaṇaḥ sakāśāt te tava matā abhipretā buddhir jñānam | he janārdana ! yadi buddhi-karmaṇī samuccite iṣṭe tadaikaṃ śreyaḥ-sādhanam iti karmaṇo jyāyasī buddhir iti karmaṇo 'tirikta-karaṇaṃ buddher anupapannam arjunena kṛtaṃ syāt | na hi tad eva tasmāt phalato 'tiriktaṃ syāt | tathā ca, karmaṇaḥ śreyaskarī bhagavatoktā buddhiḥ | aśreyaskaraṃ ca karma kurv iti māṃ pratipādayati, tat kiṃ nu kāraṇam iti bhagavata upālambham iva kurvan tat kiṃ kasmāt karmaṇi ghore krūre hiṃsā-lakṣaṇe māṃ niyojayasi keśava iti ca yad āha, tac ca nopapadyate | atha smārtenaiva karmaṇā samuccayaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhagavatokto 'rjunena cāvadhārita cet, tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi ity ādi kathaṃ yuktaṃ vacanam ||BhGS_3.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>'s commentary:] 'Superior' (<s>jyāyasī</s>) — if <s>buddhi</s>, i.e., knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), is better than action, [being] your considered opinion, O <s>Janārdana</s>! If both <s>buddhi</s> and <s>karma</s> were intended as a combination, then <s>Arjuna</s>'s singling out <s>buddhi</s> as superior to <s>karma</s> — 'one means to the good' — saying '<s>buddhi</s> is superior to <s>karma</s>' as something over and above action would be untenable. For that which is the same [as action] cannot be different from it in respect of the fruit. And thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared <s>buddhi</s> to be more beneficial than action. But he instructs me to do action that is less beneficial — 'Then why?' — as if reproaching the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Why do you urge me to terrible (<s>ghora</s>), cruel action characterized by killing, O <s>Keśava</s>?' — and what he says is also untenable [on the samuccaya view]. But if the <s>Bhagavān</s> had stated a combination with <s>smārta</s> rituals alone for all, and if <s>Arjuna</s> had understood this, then how would the statement 'Why do you urge me to terrible action?' and so forth be appropriate? ||<s>BhGS</s> 3.1||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me |
children.translated_text: With a seemingly contradictory statement, you seem to confuse my <s>buddhi</s> (understanding).

children.text: tad ekaṃ vada niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām ||BhG_3.2||
children.translated_text: Tell me decisively that one [thing] by which I may attain the good. ||<s>BhG</s> 3.2||

children.text: vyāmiśreṇeva, yadyapi vivaktābhidhāyī bhagavān, tathāpi mama manda-buddher vyāmiśram iva bhagavad-vākyaṃ pratibhāti | tena mama buddhiṃ mohayasīva, mama buddhi-vyāmohāpanayāya hi pravṛttas tvaṃ tu kathaṃ mohayasi ? ataḥ bravīmi | buddhiṃ mohayasi iva me mama iti | tvaṃ tu bhinna-kartṛkayoḥ jñāna-karmaṇor eka-puruṣānuṣṭhānāsaṃbhavaṃ yadi manyase, tatraivaṃ sati tat tayor ekaṃ buddhiṃ karma vā idam evārjunasya yogyaṃ buddhi-śakty-avasthānurūpam iti niścitya vada brūhi, yena jñānena karmaṇā vā anyatareṇa śreyo 'ham āpnuyāṃ prāpnuyām |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>'s commentary:] 'Seemingly contradictory' (<s>vyāmiśreṇa iva</s>) — although the <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks with the intention of stating [his meaning] clearly, still to me, of dull intellect, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words appear as if contradictory (<s>vyāmiśra</s>). By that, 'You seem to confuse my understanding' — yet you have set out to remove the confusion of my intellect; how then do you confuse it? Therefore I say: 'You seem to confuse my understanding.' But if you consider that, for knowledge and action which belong to different agents, the simultaneous practice by one person is impossible — then, that being so, 'tell me' (<s>vada</s>) decisively, determining 'this — knowledge or action — is suitable for <s>Arjuna</s>, in accordance with his state of intellectual capacity,' that one thing by which — by knowledge or by action, whichever one — 'I may attain the good,' i.e., I may obtain [it]. If knowledge, even as subordinate to the discipline of action, had been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, then how would <s>Arjuna</s>'s desire to hear about 'that one' be a request for just one [of the two]? For the <s>Bhagavān</s> had not previously said: 'I shall speak of only one of knowledge and action, not both' — such that [<s>Arjuna</s>], thinking the impossibility of obtaining both, would request just one. ||<s>BhGS</s> 3.2||

children.text: yadi hi karma-niṣṭhāyāṃ guṇa-bhūtam api jñānaṃ bhagavatoktaṃ syāt | tat kathaṃ tayor ekaṃ vada ity eka-viṣayaivārjunasya śuśrūṣā syāt | na hi bhagavatā pūrvam uktam anyatarad eva jñāna-karmaṇoḥ vakṣyāmi, naiva dvayam iti, yena ubhaya-prāpty-asaṃbhavam ātmano manyamāna ekam eva prārthayet ||BhGS_3.2||
children.translated_text: [continued from above, contained in segment 524]

children.text: praśnānurūpam eva prativacanaṃ -
children.translated_text: The reply is in accordance with the question —

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: loke 'smin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha |
children.translated_text: In this world, O sinless one, a twofold discipline (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) was taught by Me of old:

children.text: jñāna-yogena sāṃkhyānāṃ karma-yogena yoginām ||BhG_3.3||
children.translated_text: the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, and the <s>yoga</s> of action (<s>karmayoga</s>) for the <s>yogins</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 3.3||

children.text: loke 'smin śāstrārthānuṣṭhānādhikṛtānāṃ traivarṇikānāṃ dvi-vidhā dvi-prakārā niṣṭhā sthitiḥ anuṣṭheya-tātparyaṃ purā pūrvaṃ sargādau prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā tāsām abhyudaya-niḥśreyasa-prāpti-sādhanaṃ vedārtha-saṃpradāyam āviṣkurvatā proktā mayā sarvajñena īśvareṇa he anaghāpāpa | tatra kā sā dvividhā niṣṭhā ity āha - tatra jñāna-yogena jñānam eva yogas tena sāṃkhyānām ātmānātma-viṣaya-viveka-vijñānavatāṃ brahmacaryāśramād eva kṛta-saṃnyāsānāṃ vedānta-vijñāna-suniścitārthānāṃ paramahaṃsa-parivrājakānāṃ brahmaṇy evāvasthitānāṃ niṣṭhā proktā | karma-yogena karma eva yogaḥ karma-yogas tena karma-yogena yogināṃ karmiṇāṃ niṣṭhā proktā ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara</s>'s commentary:] 'In this world' — for those among the three castes (<s>traivarṇika</s>) who are qualified for the practice of scriptural injunctions, a twofold, i.e., two-fold, discipline (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) — meaning a settled mode of practice, the purport of what is to be practiced — was taught 'of old' (<s>purā</s>), formerly, at the beginning of creation, by Me — the omniscient Lord — who, having created beings, revealed to them the tradition of Vedic meaning as the means for attaining prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). O sinless one (<s>anagha</s>)! What is that twofold discipline? He says: of those — through the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) — knowledge itself is the <s>yoga</s>, through that — for the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, i.e., those who possess the discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekavijñāna</s>) of Self and not-Self, who have renounced from the very stage of celibate studentship (<s>brahmacaryāśrama</s>), who are firmly established in the meaning ascertained through <s>Vedānta</s> knowledge, who are <s>paramahaṃsa</s> wandering mendicants established in <s>Brahman</s> alone — for them the discipline was taught. Through the <s>yoga</s> of action (<s>karmayoga</s>) — action itself is the <s>yoga</s>, the <s>yoga</s> of action, through that <s>yoga</s> of action — for the <s>yogins</s>, i.e., the performers of ritual action — the discipline was taught. This is the meaning.

children.text: yadi caikena puruṣeṇa ekasmai puruṣārthāya jñānaṃ karma ca samuccityānuṣṭheyaṃ bhagavatā iṣṭam uktaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ vā gītāsu vedeṣu coktam, katham ihārjunāya upasannāya priyāya viśiṣṭābhinna-puruṣa-kartṛke eva jñāna-karma-niṣṭhe brūyāt ? yadi punar arjuno jñānaṃ karma ca dvayaṃ śrutvā svayam evānuṣṭhāsyati anyeṣāṃ tu bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyatāṃ vakṣyāmi iti mataṃ bhagavataḥ kalpyeta, tadā rāga-dveṣavān apramāṇa-bhūto bhagavān kalpitaḥ syāt | tac cāyuktam | tasmāt kayāpi yuktyā na samuccayo jñāna-karmaṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>Bhagavān</s> had intended, stated, or was going to state in the <s>Gītā</s> and the <s>Vedas</s> that knowledge and action are to be combined and practiced by one person for one human goal — how could he tell <s>Arjuna</s>, who had approached him as a dear [disciple], about the two disciplines of knowledge and action as belonging distinctly to different persons? If, however, one were to suppose that the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s intention was: '<s>Arjuna</s>, hearing both knowledge and action, will practice them himself; but I shall declare their practice by different persons for others' — then the <s>Bhagavān</s> would be imagined as having partiality and aversion, as not being an authority. And that is not appropriate. Therefore, by no reasoning whatsoever is the combination of knowledge and action [tenable].

children.text: yad arjunenoktaṃ karmaṇo jyāyastvaṃ buddhes tac ca sthitam anirākaraṇāt | tasyāś ca jñāna-niṣṭhāyāḥ saṃnyāsinām evānuṣṭheyatvam , bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyatva-vacanāt | bhagavata evam evānumatam iti gamyate ||BhGS_3.3||
children.translated_text: What <s>Arjuna</s> stated — the superiority of <s>buddhi</s> to <s>karma</s> — that stands unrebutted. And that discipline of knowledge is to be practiced only by renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), since it was stated as belonging to different persons. It is understood that the <s>Bhagavān</s> approves of exactly this. ||<s>BhGS</s> 3.3||

children.text: māṃ ca bandha-kāraṇe karmaṇy eva niyojayasi iti viṣaṇṇa-manasam arjunam karma nārabhe ity evaṃ manvānam ālakṣya āha bhagavān - na karmaṇāman ārambhād iti | athavā - jñāna-karma-niṣṭhayoḥ paraspara-virodhād ekena puruṣeṇa yugapad anuṣṭhātum aśakyatve sati itaretarānapekṣayor eva puruṣārtha-hetutve prāpte karma-niṣṭhāyā jñāna-niṣṭhā-prāpti-hetutvena puruṣārtha-hetutvam, na svātantryeṇa | jñāna-niṣṭhā tu karma-niṣṭhopāya-labdhātmikā satī svātantryeṇa puruṣārtha-hetuḥ anyānapekṣā, ity etam arthaṃ pradarśayiṣyan āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Arjuna</s> to be distressed in mind — [thinking] 'he is engaging me in action, which is the cause of bondage' — and perceiving that he thought 'I shall not undertake action,' the <s>Bhagavān</s> says: 'Not by non-commencement of action...' Alternatively: since the two disciplines of knowledge and action, being mutually opposed, cannot be simultaneously practiced by one person, and since each independently is a means to the human goal without depending on the other — the discipline of action serves as a means to the human goal through being a cause for attaining the discipline of knowledge, not independently. But the discipline of knowledge, having obtained its essential nature through the means of the discipline of action, is independently the cause of the human goal, not depending on anything else. To demonstrate this meaning, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says:

children.text: na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute |
children.translated_text: Not by non-commencement of actions does a person attain freedom from action (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>);

children.text: na ca saṃnyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati ||BhG_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: nor by mere renunciation does he attain perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). ||<s>BhG</s> 3.4||

children.text: na karmaṇā kriyāṇāṃ yajñādīnām iha janmani janmāntare vā anuṣṭhitānām upātta-durita-kṣaya-hetutvena sattva-śuddhi-kāraṇānāṃ tat-kāraṇatvena ca jñānotpatti-dvāreṇa jñāna-niṣṭhā-hetūnām,
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Not by action — by actions such as <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) etc., whether performed in this life or in another life, which serve as causes for the destruction of accumulated sin and thereby as causes for the purification of the mind (<s>sattva-śuddhi</s>), and which, as causes of that [purification], are causes of <s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s> (steadfastness in knowledge) through the gateway of the arising of knowledge —

children.text: jñānam utpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayāt pāpasya karmaṇaḥ |
yathādarśatala-prakhye paśyaty ātmānam ātmani || [Mbh 12 208.8] ity ādi smaraṇāt |
children.translated_text: as in the surface of a clean mirror, one sees the Self in the self' [<s>Mbh</s> 12.208.8] — thus from the <s>smṛti</s> text.
'Knowledge arises in a person from the destruction of sinful <s>karma</s>;

children.text:
anārambhād ananuṣṭhānāt naiṣkarmyaṃ niṣkarma-bhāvaṃ karma-śūnyatāṃ jñāna-yogena niṣṭhāṃ niṣkriyātma-svarūpeṇaivāvasthānam iti yāvat | puruṣo nāśnute na prāpnotīty arthaḥ |
karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ nāśnuta iti vacanāt tad-viparyayāt teṣām ārambhān naiṣkarmyam aśnuta iti gamyate | kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ nāśnute iti ? ucyate, karmārambhasyaiva naiṣkarmyopāyatvāt | na hy upāyam antareṇa upeya-prāptir asti | karma-yogopāyatvaṃ ca naiṣkarmya-lakṣaṇasya jñāna-yogasya, śrutau iha ca pratipādanāt | śrutau tāvat prakṛtasyātma-lokasya vedyasya vedanopāyatvena tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena [BAU 4.4.22] ity ādinā karma-yogasya jñāna-yogopāyatvaṃ pratipāditam | ihāpi ca - saṃnyāsas tu mahābāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ [kraītā 5.6], yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātmaśuddhaye [kraītā 5.11], yajño dānaṃ tapaś caiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām [kraītā 18.5] ity ādi pratipādayiṣyati
|
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] By non-commencement, by non-performance, <s>naiṣkarmya</s> (actionlessness) — the state of being free from action, the emptiness of action — [means] steadfastness through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), i.e., abiding in one's own nature as the actionless Self — this is the purport. A person does not attain, does not reach — this is the meaning.
From the statement 'by non-commencement of actions one does not attain <s>naiṣkarmya</s>,' the opposite is understood: by their commencement one attains <s>naiṣkarmya</s>. For what reason, then, does one not attain <s>naiṣkarmya</s> by non-commencement of actions? It is said: because the commencement of action itself is the means to <s>naiṣkarmya</s>. For there is no attainment of the goal without the means. And that <s>karma-yoga</s> is the means to <s>jñāna-yoga</s>, characterized as <s>naiṣkarmya</s>, is established both in the <s>śruti</s> (Vedic texts) and here [in the Gītā]. In the <s>śruti</s>, first: the means to knowing the Self (<s>ātma-loka</s>) that is the subject matter — '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know this through Vedic recitation, sacrifice' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.22] etc. — thereby the status of <s>karma-yoga</s> as a means to <s>jñāna-yoga</s> has been established. And here too, he will establish: 'But renunciation, O mighty-armed one, is difficult to attain without yoga' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.6], '<s>Yogins</s> perform action, abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.11], 'Sacrifice, charity, and austerity are indeed purifiers for the wise' [<s>Gītā</s> 18.5] etc.

children.text: nanu cābhayaṃ sarva-bhūtebhyo dattvā naiṣkarmyam ācaret ity ādau kartavya-karma-saṃnyāsād api naiṣkarmya-prāptiṃ darśayati | loke ca karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyam iti prasiddhataram | ataś ca naiṣkarmyārthinaḥ kiṃ karmārambheṇa ? iti prāptam | ata āha- na ca saṃnyasanād eveti | nāpi saṃnyasanād eva kevalāt karma-parityāga-mātrād eva jñāna-rahitāt siddhiṃ naiṣkarmya-lakṣaṇāṃ jñāna-yogena niṣṭhāṃ samadhigacchati na prāpnoti ||BhGS_3.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: 'Having given fearlessness to all beings, one should practice <s>naiṣkarmya</s>' — [this passage] at the outset shows the attainment of <s>naiṣkarmya</s> even from the renunciation of prescribed action. And in the world, it is well known that <s>naiṣkarmya</s> [comes] from the non-commencement of actions. Therefore, for one who seeks <s>naiṣkarmya</s>, what need is there for commencing action? — this is the expected [objection]. To this he says: 'Nor by renunciation alone.' Not even by renunciation alone — by mere abandonment of action alone, devoid of knowledge — does one reach perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) characterized as <s>naiṣkarmya</s>, the steadfastness in <s>jñāna-yoga</s>; one does not attain [it]. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.4 //

children.text: kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt karma-saṃnyāsa-mātrād eva kevalāt jñāna-rahitāt siddhiṃ naiṣkarmya-lakṣaṇāṃ puruṣo nādhigacchati iti hetv-ākāṅkṣāyām āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For what reason, then, does a person not attain perfection characterized as <s>naiṣkarmya</s> by mere renunciation of action alone, devoid of knowledge? In anticipation of the reason, he says:

children.text: na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt |
children.translated_text: No one ever remains even for a moment without performing action;

children.text: kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijair guṇaiḥ ||BhG_3.5||
children.translated_text: for everyone is made to act helplessly by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // <s>BhG</s> 3.5 //

children.text: na hi yasmāt kṣaṇam api kālaṃ jātu kadācit kaścit tiṣṭhaty akarma-kṛt san | kasmāt ? kāryate pravartyate hi yasmād avaśa evāsvatantra eva karma sarvaḥ prāṇī prakṛti-jaiḥ prakṛtito jātaiḥ sattva-rajas-tamobhiḥ guṇaiḥ | ajña iti vākya-śeṣaḥ, yato vakṣyati guṇair yo na vicālyate iti | sāṃkhyānāṃ pṛthak-karaṇāt ajñānām eva hi karma-yogaḥ, na jñāninām | jñānināṃ tu guṇair acālyamānānāṃ svataś calanābhāvāt karma-yogo nopapadyate | tathā ca vyākhyātam vedāvināśinam [kraītā 2.21] ity atra ||BhGS_3.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'No one' — for since no one ever, at any time, remains even for a moment without performing action — why? Because everyone, every living being, is made to act, i.e., caused to engage — helplessly, without autonomy — in action by the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>, i.e., born from <s>Prakṛti</s> — namely <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. 'The ignorant one' is the completion of the sentence, since he will say later: 'who is not disturbed by the <s>guṇas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.28]. Because of the separate mention of the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> [in <s>Gītā</s> 3.3], <s>karma-yoga</s> is indeed for the ignorant only, not for the knowers. For the knowers, who are not swayed by the <s>guṇas</s> and who have no inherent movement of their own, <s>karma-yoga</s> is not appropriate. And thus it was explained under 'Know [that which pervades this entire body] to be indestructible' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.21]. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.5 //

children.text: yat tv anātmajñaḥ coditaṃ karma nārabhate iti tad asad evety āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But the [view] that one who does not know the Self does not commence the enjoined action — that too is wrong. He says:

children.text: karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
children.translated_text: One who, restraining the organs of action, sits

children.text: indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate ||BhG_3.6||
children.translated_text: remembering with the mind the objects of the senses —

children.text: karmendriyāṇi hastādīni saṃyamya saṃhṛtya ya āste tiṣṭhati manasā smaran cintayan indriyārthān viṣayān vimūḍhātmā vimūḍhāntaḥ-araṇo mithyācāro mṛṣācāraḥ pāpācāraḥ sa ucyate ||BhGS_3.6||
children.translated_text: that one, of deluded understanding, is called a hypocrite. // <s>BhG</s> 3.6 //

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] One who, restraining — withdrawing — the organs of action, namely hands and the like, sits — remains — remembering, i.e., thinking with the mind about the objects of the senses, i.e., sense-objects — that one, of deluded self (<s>vimūḍhātmā</s>), i.e., of deluded inner being, is called a hypocrite (<s>mithyācāra</s>) — one of false conduct, sinful conduct. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.6 //

children.text: yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate 'rjuna |
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate ||BhG_3.7||
children.translated_text: But one who, controlling the senses with the mind, undertakes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: yas tu punaḥ karmaṇy adhikṛto 'jñaḥ buddhīndriyāṇi manasā niyamya ārabhate arjuna karmendriyaiḥ vāk-pāṇy-ādibhiḥ | kim ārabhate ity āha-karma-yogam asaktaḥ san phalābhisandhi-varjitaḥ sa viśiṣyate itarasmāt mithyācārāt ||BhGS_3.7||
children.translated_text: <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action) with the organs of action, without attachment — that one excels. // <s>BhG</s> 3.7 //

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But one who, being qualified for action, ignorant, controlling the cognitive senses (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>) with the mind, undertakes, O <s>Arjuna</s>, with the organs of action — speech, hands, and the like — what does he undertake? — <s>karma-yoga</s>, being unattached, i.e., free from desire for the fruits of action — that one excels, i.e., is superior to the other one, the hypocrite. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.7 //

children.text: yataḥ evam ataḥ-
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasidhyed akarmaṇaḥ ||BhG_3.8||
children.translated_text: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is superior to inaction;

children.text: niyataṃ nityaṃ śāstropadiṣṭam | yo yasmin karmaṇy adhikṛtaḥ phalāya cāśrutaṃ tan niyataṃ karma, tat kuru tvaṃ he arjuna ! yataḥ karma jyāyo 'dhikataraṃ phalataḥ | hi yasmād akarmaṇo 'karaṇāt anārambhāt | katham ? śarīra-yātrā śarīra-sthitir api ca te tava na prasidhyet prasiddhiṃ na gacchet akarmaṇo 'karaṇāt | ato dṛṣṭaḥ karmākarmaṇor viśeṣo loke ||BhGS_3.8||
children.translated_text: and even the maintenance of your body would not be accomplished through inaction. // <s>BhG</s> 3.8 //

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Prescribed' means constant, ordained by scripture. That action in which one is qualified and for which no fruit has been heard [prescribed] — that is 'prescribed action.' Perform that, you, O <s>Arjuna</s>! Since action is superior, i.e., greater in result. For — since [it is superior] to inaction, i.e., non-performance, non-commencement. How so? Even the maintenance of the body (<s>śarīra-yātrā</s>), i.e., the sustenance of the body, would not be accomplished for you through inaction, i.e., through non-performance. Therefore, the distinction between action and inaction is evident in the world. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.8 //

children.text: yac ca manyase bandhārthatvāt karma na kartavyam iti tad apy asat | katham ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And if you think action should not be performed because it leads to bondage — that too is wrong. How so?

children.text: yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karma-bandhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Other than action performed for the sake of sacrifice, this world is bound by action;

children.text: tad arthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgaḥ samācara ||BhG_3.9||
