children.translated_text: for that purpose, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, perform action free from attachment. // <s>BhG</s> 3.9 //

children.text: yajño vai viṣṇuḥ [TaittS 1.7.4] iti śruter yajña īśvaraḥ | tad-arthaṃ yat kriyate tat yajñārthaṃ karma | tasmāt karmaṇo 'nyatrānyena karmaṇā loko 'yam adhikṛtaḥ karma-kṛt karma-bandhanaḥ [Taitt.Bhā. 3.1.6] karma bandhanaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ karma-bandhano lokaḥ, na tu yajñārthāt | atas tad-arthaṃ yajñārthaṃ karma kaunteya, mukta-saṅgaḥ karma-phala-saṅga-varjitaḥ san samācāra nirvartaya ||BhGS_3.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] From the <s>śruti</s> '<s>Yajña</s> (sacrifice) is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>' [<s>TaittS</s> 1.7.4], <s>yajña</s> means the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). That which is done for His sake is action performed for the sake of <s>yajña</s>. Other than that action — by any other action — this world, the qualified performer of action, is bound by action (<s>karma-bandhana</s>) — action is the bondage for this one, hence 'bound by action'; but not [by action performed] for the sake of <s>yajña</s>. Therefore, for that purpose, for the sake of <s>yajña</s>, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, perform action being free from attachment (<s>mukta-saṅga</s>), i.e., being free from attachment to the fruits of action. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.9 //

children.text: itaś cādhikṛtena karma kartavyam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And for another reason too, the qualified person must perform action —

children.text: saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having created beings together with sacrifice, <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of creatures) said of old:

children.text: anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk ||BhG_3.10||
children.translated_text: 'By this [sacrifice] may you prosper; may this be the wish-fulfilling cow for you.' // <s>BhG</s> 3.10 //

children.text: saha-yajñāḥ yajña-sahitāḥ prajās trayo varṇās tāḥ sṛṣṭvotpādya purā pūrvaṃ sargādāv uvāca uktavān prajāpatiḥ prajānāṃ srāṣṭā | anena yajñena prasaviṣyadhvaṃ prasavo vṛddhir utpattis tāṃ kurudhvam | eṣa yajño vo yuṣmākam astu bhavatu iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk | iṣṭān abhipretān kāmān phala-viśeṣān dogdhīti iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk ||BhGS_3.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Together with sacrifice' means accompanied by sacrifice. 'Beings' — the three <s>varṇas</s> (classes) — having created them, i.e., having produced them, 'of old,' formerly, at the beginning of creation, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the creator of beings, said, i.e., spoke [thus]: 'By this sacrifice, may you prosper' — may you multiply, may you increase, may you grow. 'May this sacrifice be for you the wish-fulfilling cow' — that which milks, i.e., yields, desired objects, i.e., wished-for particular fruits — [such is] the 'wish-fulfilling cow' (<s>iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 3.10 //

children.text: devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nourish the gods by this [sacrifice], and may those gods nourish you;

children.text: parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha ||BhG_3.11||
children.translated_text: thus nourishing one another, you shall attain the supreme good. // <s>BhG</s> 3.11 //

children.text: devān indrādīn bhāvayata vardhayatānena yajñena | te devā bhāvayantu āpyāyayantu vṛṣṭy-ādinā vo yuṣmān | evaṃ parasparam anyonyaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paraṃ mokṣa-lakṣaṇaṃ vijñāna-prāpti-krameṇāvāpsyatha | svargaṃ vā paraṃ śreyo 'vāpsyatha ||BhGS_3.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Nourish the gods' — <s>Indra</s> and the others — 'nourish' means sustain, increase, by this sacrifice. And 'may those gods nourish you,' i.e., may they strengthen you through rain and the like. Thus, nourishing each other — mutually sustaining one another — you shall attain the supreme good (<s>śreyas</s>), characterized as <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), through the gradual attainment of knowledge. Or else, you shall attain heaven (<s>svarga</s>) as the supreme good. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.11 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The gods, nourished by sacrifice, will give you the desired enjoyments;

children.text: tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ ||BhG_3.12||
children.translated_text: one who enjoys what is given by them without offering [anything] in return — that one is indeed a thief. // <s>BhG</s> 3.12 //

children.text: iṣṭān abhipretān bhogān hi vo yuṣmabhyaṃ devā dāsyante vitariṣyanti | strī-paśu-putrādīn yajña-bhāvitā yajñair vardhitās toṣitā ity arthaḥ | tair devair dattān bhogān apradāyādattvā, ānṛṇyam akṛtvety arthaḥ | ebhyo devebhyaḥ | yo bhuṅkte sva-dehendriyāṇy eva tarpayati stena eva taskara eva sa devādi-svāpahārī ||BhGS_3.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Desired' means wished-for. 'Enjoyments' — the gods, nourished by sacrifice, i.e., increased and gratified by sacrifices, will give, will bestow upon you — wives, cattle, sons, and the like. One who enjoys what is given by those gods without offering [anything in return], i.e., without giving back — meaning without discharging one's debt — to these gods; one who enjoys, i.e., who merely gratifies one's own body and senses — that one is indeed a thief (<s>stena</s>), a robber — one who steals what belongs to the gods and others. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.12 //

children.text: ye punaḥ-
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But those who —

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The righteous ones who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins;

children.text: bhuñjate te tv aghaṃ pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt ||BhG_3.13||
children.translated_text: but those sinful ones who cook for their own sake — they eat sin. // <s>BhG</s> 3.13 //

children.text: deva-yajñādīn nirvartya tac-chiṣṭam aśanam amṛtākhyam aśituṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ sarva-pāpaiś cully-ādi-pañca-sūnākṛtaiḥ pramāda-kṛta-hiṃsādi-janitaiś cānyaiḥ | ye tv ātmaṃbharayo bhuñjate te tv aghaṃ pāpaṃ svayam api pāpā ye pacanti pākaṃ nirvartayanti ātma-kāraṇāt ātma-hetoḥ ||BhGS_3.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having performed sacrifices to the gods and the like, those whose habit it is to eat the remnants thereof — called <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) — are 'those who eat the remnants of sacrifice' (<s>yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ</s>). Being righteous, they are freed from all sins — all transgressions arising from the five daily sources of harm such as the cooking-hearth etc., and from other [sins] caused by inadvertent killing and the like. But those who are self-centered, who eat — they eat sin (<s>agha</s>), evil — those sinful ones who cook, i.e., who prepare food, for their own sake, i.e., for themselves alone. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.13 //

children.text: itaś cādhikṛtena karma kartavyam | jagac-cakra-pravṛtti-hetur hi karma | katham ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And for another reason too, the qualified person must perform action. For action is the cause of the turning of the cosmic wheel. How? This is stated:

children.text: annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-saṃbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: From food beings come into being; from rain is the production of food;

children.text: yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ ||BhG_3.14||
children.translated_text: from sacrifice rain comes into being; sacrifice is born of action. // <s>BhG</s> 3.14 //

children.text: annād bhuktāl lohita-retaḥ-pariṇatāt pratyakṣaṃ bhavanti jāyante bhūtāni | parjanyād vṛṣṭer annasya saṃbhavo 'nna-saṃbhavaḥ | yajñād bhavati parjanyaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] From food that has been eaten, transformed into blood and semen, beings evidently come into being, i.e., are born. From rain (<s>parjanya</s>), from rainfall, is the production of food. From sacrifice, rain comes into being —

children.text: agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyag ādityam upatiṣṭhate |
ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭir vṛṣṭer annaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ || [Manu 3.76] iti smṛteḥ |
children.translated_text: from the sun rain is produced; from rain, food; from that, creatures' [<s>Manu</s> 3.76] — thus from the <s>smṛti</s> text.
'An oblation properly offered into the fire reaches the sun;

children.text: yajño 'pūrvam | sa ca yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ | ṛtvig-yajamānayoś ca vyāpāraḥ karma, tad-samudbhavo yasya yajñasyāpūrvasya sa yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ ||BhGS_3.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Sacrifice' means the unseen merit (<s>apūrva</s>). And this sacrifice is 'born of action.' The activity of the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) and the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) is 'action'; that sacrifice — the <s>apūrva</s> — whose origin is from that [action], is 'sacrifice born of action.' // <s>BhGS</s> 3.14 //

children.text: tac caivaṃvidhaṃ karma kuto jātam ity āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And from where does action of this kind originate? He says:

children.text: karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣara-samudbhavam |
children.translated_text: Know that action originates from <s>Brahman</s> (the Veda), and <s>Brahman</s> originates from the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>);

children.text: tasmāt sarva-gataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||BhG_3.15||
children.translated_text: therefore, the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> is eternally established in sacrifice. // <s>BhG</s> 3.15 //

children.text: karma brahmodbhavaṃ | brahma vedaḥ | sa udbhavaḥ kāraṇaṃ prakāśako yasya tat karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi vijānīhi | brahma punaḥ vedākhyam akṣara-samudbhavam akṣaraṃ brahma paramātmā samudbhavo yasya tat akṣara-samudbhavam | brahma veda ity arthaḥ | yasmāt sākṣāt paramātmākhyād akṣarāt puruṣa-niḥśvāsavat samudbhūtaṃ brahma tasmāt sarvārtha-prakāśakatvāt sarva-gatam | sarva-gatam api sat nityaṃ sadā yajña-vidhi-pradhānatvāt yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||BhGS_3.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Action originates from <s>Brahman</s>' — <s>Brahman</s> means the Veda. That [Veda] is the origin, the cause, the illuminator of that [action] — thus action originates from <s>Brahman</s>; know this, understand this. And <s>Brahman</s>, the Veda, 'originates from the Imperishable' — the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self, whose origin is from that — thus it originates from the Imperishable. The meaning is: <s>Brahman</s>, the Veda. Since it arises directly from the Supreme Self called the Imperishable, like a person's breath, therefore — because it illuminates all things — [it is] 'all-pervading.' Though all-pervading, it is eternally, always, 'established in sacrifice,' because the injunctions of sacrifice are its principal content. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.15 //

children.text: evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here [in this world],

children.text: aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ||BhG_3.16||
children.translated_text: living in sin, delighting in the senses — that one lives in vain, O son of <s>Pṛthā</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 3.16 //

children.text:
evam ittham īśvareṇa veda-yajña-pūrvakaṃ jagac-cakraṃ pravartitaṃ nānuvartayatīha loke yaḥ karmaṇy adhikṛtaḥ sann aghāyur aghaṃ pāpam āyur jīvanaṃ yasya so 'ghāyuḥ pāpa-jīvana iti yāvat | indriyārāmaḥ indriyair ārāmaḥ āramaṇam ākrīḍā viṣayeṣu yasya sa indriyārāmo moghaṃ vṛthā he pārtha, sa jīvati | tasmād ajñenādhikṛtena kartavyam eva karmeti prakaraṇārthaḥ | prāg ātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā-yogyatā-prāptes tādarthyena karma-yogānuṣṭhānam adhikṛtenānātmajñena kartavyam evety etan na karmaṇām anārambhād [Gītā 3.4] ity ata ārabhya śarīra-yātrāpi ca te na prasidhyed akarmaṇa [Gītā 3.8] ity evam antena pratipādya, yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra [Gītā 3.9] ity ādinā moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ity evam antenāpi granthena prāsaṅgikam adhikṛtasyānātmavidaḥ karmānuṣṭhāne
bahu kāraṇam uktam | tad-akaraṇe ca doṣa-saṃkīrtanaṃ kṛtam ||BhGS_3.16||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in this manner, one who, being qualified for action, does not follow in this world the cosmic wheel set in motion by the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) through the <s>Vedas</s> and sacrifices — he is '<s>aghāyuḥ</s>': one whose life (<s>āyus</s>) is sinful (<s>agha</s>), meaning one of sinful livelihood. '<s>Indriyārāmaḥ</s>' — one whose delight (<s>ārāma</s>), enjoyment, play is in sense-objects through the senses — he is one who delights in the senses. In vain (<s>mogham</s>), O <s>Pārtha</s>, he lives. Therefore, the meaning of the passage is: action must indeed be performed by the ignorant person who is qualified [for it]. Prior to attaining eligibility for steadfastness in Self-knowledge (<s>ātmajñāna-niṣṭhā</s>), <s>karma-yoga</s> must be practiced for that purpose by the qualified non-knower of the Self — this has been established. Beginning from 'Not by non-performance of actions' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.4] up to 'even the maintenance of your body would not be accomplished through inaction' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.8], and then by the passage beginning with 'Other than action done for the sake of sacrifice' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.9] up to 'he lives in vain, O <s>Pārtha</s>' — in this incidentally arisen passage, many reasons have been stated for the performance of action by the qualified non-knower of the Self,
and the faults of non-performance have been declared. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.16 //

children.text: evaṃ sthite kim evaṃ pravartitaṃ caktraṃ sarveṇānuvartanīyam ? āho svit pūrvokta-karma-yogānuṣṭhānopāya-prāpyām anātma-vidā jñāna-yogenaiva niṣṭhām ātma-vidbhiḥ sāṃkhyair anuṣṭheyām aprāptenaiva ? ity evam artham arjunasya praśnam āśaṅkaya svayam eva vā śāstrārthasya viveka-pratipatty-artham etaṃ vai tam ātmānaṃ viditvā nivṛtta-mithyā-jñānāḥ santo brāhmaṇā mithyā-jñānavadbhyo 'vaśyaṃ kartavyebhyaḥ putraiṣaṇādibhyo vyutthāyātha bhikṣā-caryaṃ śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayuktaṃ caranti | na teṣām ātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā-vyatirekeṇānyat kāryam asti [BAU 3.5.1] ity evaṃ śruty-artham iha gītā-śāstre pratipipādayiṣitam āviṣkurvann āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: This being the case, must this cosmic wheel thus set in motion be followed by everyone? Or rather, can those <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, the knowers of the Self, who have not [yet] attained [that steadfastness], directly accomplish the steadfastness through <s>jñāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) alone — which is to be attained by the non-knower of the Self through the means of practicing <s>karma-yoga</s> as stated above? Anticipating this as <s>Arjuna</s>'s question, or for the purpose of discerning comprehension of the teaching's meaning, making manifest the <s>Śruti</s> meaning — 'Having known this very Self, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, freed from false knowledge, rise above the desires for sons etc. that are necessarily to be performed by those possessing false knowledge, and then adopt the mendicant life, practicing only what is required for the mere maintenance of the body. For them, there is no duty other than steadfastness in Self-knowledge' [<s>BAU</s> 3.5.1] — wishing to establish this meaning here in the teaching of the <s>Gītā</s>, the Blessed Lord said —

children.text: yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś ca mānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: But one who delights in the Self alone, who is satisfied in the Self,

children.text: ātmany eva ca saṃtuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate ||BhG_3.17||
children.translated_text: and who is content in the Self alone — for him there is no duty to perform. // <s>BhG</s> 3.17 //

children.text: yas tu sāṃkhya ātma-jñāna-niṣṭha ātma-ratiḥ ātmany eva ratir na viṣayeṣu yasya sa ātma-ratir eva syād bhaved ātma-tṛptaś cātmanaiva tṛpto nānna-rasādinā sa mānavo manuṣyaḥ saṃnyāsī ātmany eva ca santuṣṭaḥ | santoṣo hi bāhyārtha-lābhe sarvasya bhavati, tam anapekṣya ātmany eva ca santuṣṭaḥ sarvato vīta-tṛṣṇa ity etat | ya īdṛśaḥ ātma-vit tasya kāryaṃ karaṇīyaṃ na vidyate nāstīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.17||
children.translated_text: But one who is a <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, established in Self-knowledge — '<s>ātma-rati</s>' — one whose delight (<s>rati</s>) is in the Self alone, not in sense-objects; '<s>ātma-tṛpta</s>' — satisfied by the Self alone, not by food, drink, and the like — such a person (<s>mānava</s>), a human being, a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), and content in the Self alone. For normally, contentment arises from the acquisition of external objects; but independent of that, one who is content in the Self alone — one whose craving has entirely ceased — this is the meaning. For such a knower of the Self, there is no duty (<s>kārya</s>), nothing to be done — meaning it does not exist. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.17 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
children.translated_text: For him there is no purpose served by action done, nor any [loss] by action not done here;

children.text: na cāsya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ ||BhG_3.18||
children.translated_text: nor does he have any dependence on any being whatsoever for any purpose. // <s>BhG</s> 3.18 //

children.text: naiva tasya paramātma-rateḥ kṛtena karmaṇārthaḥ prayojanam asti | astu tarhy akṛtenākaraṇena pratyavāyākhyo 'narthaḥ | nākṛteneha loke kaścana kaścid api pratyavāya-prāpti-rūpaḥ ātma-hāni-lakṣaṇo vā naivāsti | na cāsya sarva-bhūteṣu brahmādi-sthāvarānteṣu bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ prayojana-nimitta-kriyā-sādhyo vyapāśrayaḥ | vyapāśrayaṇam ālambanaṃ kaṃcit bhūta-viśeṣam āśritya na sādhyaḥ kaścid artho 'sti, yena tad-arthā kriyā anuṣṭheyā syāt | na tvam etasmin sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīye samyag-darśane vartase ||BhGS_3.18||
children.translated_text: For that one who delights in the Supreme Self, there is no purpose (<s>artha</s>), no benefit, from action that has been performed. Let there then be some disadvantage, some harm in the form of demerit (<s>pratyavāya</s>), from action not done — no, from non-performance here in this world, there is none whatsoever — not even any loss characterized by the destruction of the Self. Nor does he have, among all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable [entities], any dependence on any purpose — no purpose to be accomplished through action depending on any particular being. There is no goal whatsoever that he might accomplish by relying on some specific being, for which he would need to perform some action directed toward that purpose. You, however, do not stand in this [realization] which corresponds to the water overflowing on all sides — in this right knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.18 //

children.text: yataḥ evam -
children.translated_text: Since this is so —

children.text: tasmād asaktaḥ satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
children.translated_text: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the action that is to be done;

children.text: asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ ||BhG_3.19||
children.translated_text: for by performing action without attachment, a person attains the Supreme. // <s>BhG</s> 3.19 //

children.text: tasmāt asaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ satataṃ sarvadā kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ nityaṃ karma samācara nirvartaya | asakto hi yasmāt samācaran īśvarārthaṃ karma kurvan paraṃ mokṣam āpnoti pūruṣaḥ sattvaśuddhidvāreṇa ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.19||
children.translated_text: Therefore, without attachment (<s>asakta</s>), free from clinging, always, at all times, perform the action that is to be done — the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) action — carry it out. For since one who performs action without attachment, performing action for the sake of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), attains the Supreme (<s>param</s>), i.e., <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — through the means of purification of <s>sattva</s> — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.19 //

children.text: yasmāc ca -
children.translated_text: And because —

children.text: karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Indeed, through action alone, <s>Janaka</s> and others attained perfection;

children.text: loka-saṃgraham evāpi saṃpaśyan kartum arhasi ||BhG_3.20||
children.translated_text: even just considering the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>), you ought to act. // <s>BhG</s> 3.20 //

children.text: karmaṇaiva hi yasmāt pūrve kṣatriyāḥ vidvāṃsaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ mokṣaṃ gantum āsthitāḥ pravṛttāḥ | ke ? janakādayaḥ janakā vapatiprabhṛtayaḥ | yadi te prāptasamyagdarśanāḥ, tataḥ lokasaṃgrahārthaṃ prārabdhakarmatvāt karmaṇā sahaivāsaṃnyasyaiva karma saṃsiddhimāsthitā ity arthaḥ | athāprāptasamyagadarśanāḥ janakādayaḥ, tadā karmaṇā sattvaśuddhisādhanabhūtena ktrameṇa saṃsiddhimāsthitā iti vyākhyeyaḥ lokaḥ | atha manyase pūrverapi janakādibhiḥ ajānadbhireva kartavyaṃ karma kṛtam | tāvatā nāvaśyamanyena kartavyaṃ samyagdarśanavatā kṛtātheneti | tathāpi prārabdhakarmāyattaḥ tvaṃ lokasaṃgraham evāpi lokasya unmārgapravṛttinivāraṇaṃ lokasaṃgrahaḥ, tamevāpi prayojanaṃ saṃpaśyan kartum arhasi ||BhGS_3.20||
children.translated_text: Through action alone — for the former <s>kṣatriyas</s> who were learned undertook to proceed toward perfection (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>), i.e., liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Who? <s>Janaka</s> and others — <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Aśvapati</s>, and the like. If they had attained right knowledge (<s>samyagdarśana</s>), then, for the sake of the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>), because their action had already commenced, the meaning is: they attained perfection together with action, without renouncing action. But if <s>Janaka</s> and others had not attained right knowledge, then the passage should be explained thus: they attained perfection through action, which served as the means of purification of <s>sattva</s>, gradually. Now, if you think: even the ancients such as <s>Janaka</s> performed action while not knowing [the truth], and that does not mean that someone else who possesses right knowledge must necessarily perform [action] when his purpose is already accomplished — even so, since you are one whose action has already commenced, considering even just the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) — the prevention of people from pursuing the wrong path is <s>loka-saṃgraha</s> — considering even that alone as purpose, you ought to act. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.20 //

children.text: loka-saṃgrahaḥ kim arthaṃ kartavya ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: For what reason should the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) be undertaken? It is said —

children.text: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever a great person does, that alone the common people do;

children.text: sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate ||BhG_3.21||
children.translated_text: whatever standard he sets, the world follows that. // <s>BhG</s> 3.21 //

children.text: yadyat karma ācarati karoti śreṣṭhaḥ pradhānaḥ tattadeva karma ācarati itaro 'nyaḥ janaḥ tadanugataḥ | kiṃ ca saḥ śreṣṭhaḥ yat pramāṇaṃ kurute laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vā lokaḥ tat anuvartate tadeva pramāṇīkaroti ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.21||
children.translated_text: Whatever action a great person (<s>śreṣṭha</s>), an eminent one, performs — that very action the common people (<s>itara jana</s>), the others, perform, following him. Moreover, whatever standard that eminent one establishes, whether worldly or Vedic — the world follows that, adopts that very thing as authoritative — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.21 //

children.text: yady atra te loka-saṃgraha-kartavyatāyāṃ vipratipattis tarhi māṃ kiṃ na paśyasi ?
children.translated_text: If you have any doubt regarding your obligation to maintain the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>), then why do you not look at Me?

children.text: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcana |
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever, O <s>Pārtha</s>, that I must do in the three worlds;

children.text: nānavāptam avāptavyaṃ vartaiva ca karmaṇi ||BhG_3.22||
children.translated_text: nothing unobtained that needs to be obtained — yet I engage in action. // <s>BhG</s> 3.22 //

children.text: na me mama pārtha nāsti na vidyate kartavyaṃ triṣv api lokeṣu kiṃcana kiṃcid api | kasmāt ? nānavāptam aprāptam avāptavyaṃ prāpaṇīyam | tathāpi varta eva ca karmaṇy aham ||BhGS_3.22||
children.translated_text: There is nothing for Me, O <s>Pārtha</s> — there does not exist any duty that must be done in all the three worlds, not even the slightest. Why? Because there is nothing unobtained that needs to be obtained. Yet, even so, I engage indeed in action. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.22 //

children.text: yadi hy ahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ |
children.translated_text: For if I were not to engage in action at all, tirelessly,

children.text: mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||BhG_3.23||
children.translated_text: people would follow My path in every way, O <s>Pārtha</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 3.23 //

children.text: yadi hi punar ahaṃ na varteya jātu kadācit karmaṇy atandrito 'nalasaḥ san mama śreṣṭhasya sato vatrma mārgam anuvartante manuṣyāḥ | he pārtha ! sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ ||BhGS_3.23||
children.translated_text: For if I were not to engage at any time (<s>jātu</s>) in action, being untiring (<s>atandrita</s>), not lazy — people would follow the path of Me, the eminent one — O <s>Pārtha</s>, in every way, by all manner of means. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.23 //

children.text: utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṃ karma ced aham |
children.translated_text: These worlds would be ruined if I did not perform action;

children.text: saṃkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ ||BhG_3.24||
children.translated_text: I would be the author of confusion (<s>saṃkara</s>), and I would destroy these beings. // <s>BhG</s> 3.24 //

children.text: utsīdeyur vinaśyeyur ime sarve lokāḥ loka-sthiti-nimittasya karmaṇo 'bhāvāt na kuryāṃ karma ced aham | kiṃ ca, saṃkarasya ca kartā syām | tena kāraṇena upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ | prajānām anugrahāya pravṛtta upahatim upahananaṃ kuryām ity arthaḥ | mama īśvarasyānanurūpam āpadyate ||BhGS_3.24||
children.translated_text: These worlds would be ruined — would perish — because of the absence of the action that is the cause of the world's sustenance, if I did not perform action. Moreover, I would be the author of confusion (<s>saṃkara</s>), the intermixture [of castes]. For that reason, I would destroy (<s>upahanyām</s>) these beings (<s>prajāḥ</s>). Though set in motion for the benefit of beings, I would inflict harm, cause destruction — this is the meaning. This would be unbecoming of Me, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 3.24 //

children.text: yadi punar aham iva tvaṃ kṛtārtha-buddhiḥ, ātmavid anyo vā, tasyāpi ātmanaḥ kartavyābhāve 'pi parānugraha eva kartavya ity āha -
children.translated_text: If, however, like Me, you are one who considers himself to have accomplished his purpose — a knower of the Self, or any other [such person] — even for him, though there is no duty for himself, the benefiting of others alone is to be done. Thus He says —

children.text: saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
children.translated_text: As the ignorant act with attachment to action, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: kuryād vidvāṃs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur loka-saṃgraham ||BhG_3.25||
children.translated_text: so should the wise act, but without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world. // <s>BhG</s> 3.25 //

children.text: saktāḥ karmaṇy asya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ mama bhaviṣyatīti kecid avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata, kuryād vidvān ātmavit tathāsaktaḥ san | tadvat kim arthaṃ karoti ? tat sṛṇu - cikīrṣuḥ kartum icchuḥ loka-saṃgraham ||BhGS_3.25||
children.translated_text: Some ignorant people act with attachment to action — [thinking] 'the fruit of this action will be mine' — O <s>Bhārata</s>; just as [they act], so should the wise one (<s>vidvān</s>), the knower of the Self, act, but without attachment. For what purpose does he act thus? Listen: desiring to accomplish (<s>cikīrṣu</s>) the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 3.25 //

children.text: evaṃ loka-saṃgrahaṃ cikīrṣer na mamātma-vidaḥ kartavyam asti anyasya vā loka-saṃgrahaṃ muktvā | tatas tasya ātma-vidaḥ idam upadiśyate -
children.translated_text: Thus, for the knower of the Self who desires the welfare of the world, there is no duty for himself, nor for any other [knower], except for the welfare of the world. Therefore, this is the instruction given to that knower of the Self —

children.text: na buddhi-bhedaṃ janayed ajñānāṃ karma-saṅginām |
children.translated_text: Let him not cause a disruption in the understanding of the ignorant who are attached to action;

children.text: joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran ||BhG_3.26||
children.translated_text: the wise one, being disciplined and performing all actions himself, should cause them to engage [in action]. // <s>BhG</s> 3.26 //

children.text: buddhi-bhedo buddhi-bhedo mayā idaṃ kartavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ cāsya karmaṇaḥ phalam iti niścaya-rūpāyā buddher bhedanaṃ cālanaṃ buddhi-bhedas taṃ na janayen notpādayed ajñānām avivekināṃ karma-saṅgināṃ karmaṇy āsaktānāṃ āsaṅgavatām | kiṃ nu kuryāt ? joṣayet kārayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān svayaṃ tad evāviduṣāṃ karma yukto 'bhiyuktaḥ samācaran ||BhGS_3.26||
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhi-bheda</s>' (disruption of understanding) — the disruption, the unsettling, of the understanding that is of the nature of the conviction 'this is to be done by me, and this is the fruit of this action to be enjoyed' — let him not produce, let him not cause, among the ignorant, among those lacking discrimination, who are attached to action, who have fondness [for it]. What then should he do? He should cause them to engage (<s>joṣayet</s>), should make them perform, all actions. The wise one (<s>vidvān</s>) himself, being disciplined (<s>yukta</s>), devoted, should perform those very actions that the ignorant [perform]. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.26 //

children.text: avidvān ajñaḥ kathaṃ karmasu sajjate ? ity āha -
children.translated_text: How does the ignorant person become attached to actions? He says —

children.text: prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: All actions are performed in every way by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature);

children.text: ahaṃkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate ||BhG_3.27||
children.translated_text: one whose self is deluded by egoism (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) thinks 'I am the doer.' // <s>BhG</s> 3.27 //

children.text: prakṛteḥ prakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ sattva-rajas-tamasāṃ guṇānāṃ sāmyāvasthā | tasyāḥ prakṛteḥ guṇaiḥ vikāraiḥ kārya-karaṇa-rūpaiḥ kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi laukikāni śāstrīyāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakārair ahaṃkāra-vimūḍhātmā kārya-karaṇa-saṃghātātma-pratyayo 'haṃkāras tena vividhaṃ nānāvidhaṃ mūḍha ātmā antaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ kārya-karaṇa-dharmā kārya-karaṇābhimānī avidyayā karmāṇi ātmani manyamānaḥ tat-tat-karmaṇām ahaṃ karteti manyate ||BhGS_3.27||
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> — <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Matter), the state of equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>: <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. By the <s>guṇas</s> of that <s>Prakṛti</s> — by [its] modifications (<s>vikāra</s>) in the form of the body and senses (<s>kārya-karaṇa</s>) — all actions, both worldly and scriptural, are performed in every way, by all manner of means. '<s>Ahaṃkāra-vimūḍhātmā</s>' — <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (egoism) is the self-notion directed toward the aggregate of body and senses; by that, the inner faculty (<s>ātmā</s>, i.e., <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is variously deluded — one whose inner faculty is thus deluded. This person, who attributes the properties of the body and senses [to the Self] and identifies with the body and senses through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), imagining actions to belong to the Self, thinks 'I am the doer' regarding each and every action. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.27 //

children.text: yaḥ punar vidvān -
children.translated_text: But one who is wise —

children.text: tattvavit tu mahābāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ |
children.translated_text: But the knower of the truth (<s>tattvavit</s>), O mighty-armed one, regarding the divisions of <s>guṇas</s> and actions,

children.text: guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate ||BhG_3.28||
children.translated_text: [knowing that] the <s>guṇas</s> operate among the <s>guṇas</s> — thinking thus, he does not become attached. // <s>BhG</s> 3.28 //

children.text: tattvavit tu mahābāho | kasya tattvavit ? guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ guṇavibhāgasya karmavibhāgasya ca tattvavit ity arthaḥ | guṇāḥ karaṇātmakāḥ guṇeṣu viṣayātmakeṣu vartante na ātmā iti matvā na sajjate saktiṃ na karoti ||BhGS_3.28||
children.translated_text: The knower of the truth (<s>tattvavit</s>), O mighty-armed one — of the truth of what? Of the divisions of the <s>guṇas</s> and actions (<s>guṇa-karma-vibhāga</s>): the knower of the truth of the division of the <s>guṇas</s> and the division of actions — this is the meaning. The <s>guṇas</s>, which are of the nature of the senses (<s>karaṇa</s>), operate among the <s>guṇas</s>, which are of the nature of the sense-objects — not the Self — thinking thus, he does not become attached, does not form attachment. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.28 //

children.text: ye punaḥ -
children.translated_text: But those who —

children.text: prakṛter guṇa-saṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu |
children.translated_text: Those deluded by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> become attached to the actions of the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsnavin na vicālayet ||BhG_3.29||
children.translated_text: the one who knows the whole should not unsettle those of incomplete understanding who are dull. // <s>BhG</s> 3.29 //

children.text: prakṛteḥ guṇaiḥ samyak mūḍhāḥ saṃmohitāḥ santaḥ sajjante guṇānāṃ karmasu guṇa-karmasu vayaṃ karma kurmaḥ phalāya iti | tān karma-saṅgino 'kṛtsna-vidaḥ karma-phala-mātra-darśino mandān manda-prajñān kṛtsna-vit ātma-vit svayaṃ na vicālayet buddhi-bheda-karaṇam eva cālanaṃ tan na kuryāt ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.29||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Those who are thoroughly deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) — bewildered — by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), become attached to the actions of the <s>guṇas</s> — [thinking] 'we perform actions for the sake of their fruits.' Those who are attached to action, those of incomplete knowledge (<s>akṛtsnavid</s>) — who see only action and its fruit — those of dull intellect (<s>manda</s>), a knower of the whole (<s>kṛtsnavid</s>), a knower of the Self, should not unsettle [them]. The meaning is: he should not cause confusion of their intellect — that is the unsettling that should not be done. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.29 //

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ karmaṇy adhikṛtenājñena mumukṣuṇā karma kartavyam iti, ucyate --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] But how should an ignorant person who is eligible for action and seeks liberation perform action? It is stated —

children.text: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātma-cetasā |
children.translated_text: Renouncing all actions in Me, with a mind focused on the Self (<s>adhyātmacetas</s>),

children.text: nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ ||BhG_3.30||
children.translated_text: being free from desire, free from the sense of 'mine' — fight, free from [mental] fever! // <s>BhG</s> 3.30 //

children.text: mayi vāsudeve parameśvare sarvajñe sarvātmani sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya nikṣipyādhyātma-cetasā viveka-buddhyā, ahaṃ kartā īśvarāya bhṛtyavat karomi ity anayā buddhyā | kiṃ ca, nirāśīs tyaktāśīḥ nirmamo mama-bhāvaś ca nirgato yasya tava sa tvaṃ nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaro vigata-santāpo vigata-śokaḥ sann ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.30||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In Me — in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme Lord, the omniscient, the Self of all — renouncing, consigning all actions, with a mind focused on the Self — with the intellect of discrimination — [thinking] 'I am the agent; I act for the Lord, like a servant' — with this understanding. Moreover, being without desire (<s>nirāśīḥ</s>) — one who has abandoned desire; and free from the sense of 'mine' (<s>nirmama</s>) — one from whom the feeling of 'mine' has departed — being such, fight, free from [mental] fever — free from anguish, free from grief — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.30 //

children.text: yad etan mama mataṃ karma kartavyam iti sa-pramāṇam uktaṃ tat tathā -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] This view of Mine — that action should be performed — has been stated with authority. And accordingly —

children.text: ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those persons who constantly follow this teaching of Mine,

children.text: śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ ||BhG_3.31||
children.translated_text: endowed with faith and free from envy — they too are liberated from actions. // <s>BhG</s> 3.31 //

children.text: ye me madīyam idaṃ mataṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti anuvartante mānavā manuṣyāḥ śraddhāvantaḥ śraddadhānā anasūyanto 'sūyāṃ ca mayi parama-gurau vāsudeve 'kurvanto, mucyante te 'py evaṃbhūtāḥ karmabhir dharmādharmākhyaiḥ ||BhGS_3.31||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Those who constantly follow — adhere to — this teaching of Mine, persons, human beings, endowed with faith (<s>śraddhāvat</s>), having conviction, and free from envy (<s>anasūyat</s>) — not harboring resentment toward Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supreme teacher — they too, being of this nature, are liberated from actions — [actions] called <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.31 //

children.text: ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
children.translated_text: But those who, finding fault, do not follow My teaching —

children.text: sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ ||BhG_3.32||
children.translated_text: know them to be deluded in all knowledge, lost, and mindless. // <s>BhG</s> 3.32 //

children.text: ye tu tad-viparītā etan mama matam abhyasūyanto nindanto nānutiṣṭhanti nānuvartante me matam | sarveṣu jñāneṣu vividhaṃ mūḍhās te | sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi jānīhi naṣṭān nāśaṃ gatān acetaso 'vivekinaḥ ||BhGS_3.32||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] But those who are the opposite of the above — finding fault with, condemning this teaching of Mine — do not follow, do not adhere to My teaching. They are deluded in all forms of knowledge — variously confused. Know them — understand them — to be lost, gone to destruction, mindless, lacking discrimination. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.32 //

children.text: kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt tvadīyaṃ mataṃ nānutiṣṭhantaḥ para-dharmān anutiṣṭhanti ? sva-dharmaṃ ca nānuvartante ? tvat-pratikūlāḥ kathaṃ na bibhyati tvac-chāsanātikrama-doṣāt ? tatrāha -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] But for what reason do they not follow Your teaching and instead follow the duties of others? And [why] do they not follow their own duty? Being opposed to You, why do they not fear the fault of transgressing Your command? To this he says —

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api |
children.translated_text: Even a person of knowledge acts in accordance with his own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>);

children.text: prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati ||BhG_3.33||
children.translated_text: beings follow [their] nature — what will restraint accomplish? // <s>BhG</s> 3.33 //

children.text: sadṛśam anurūpaṃ ceṣṭate ceṣṭāṃ karoti | kasyāḥ ? svasyāḥ svakīyāyāḥ prakṛteḥ | prakṛtir nāma pūrva-kṛta-dharmādharmādi-saṃskārā vartamāna-janmādāv abhivyaktāḥ | sā prakṛtiḥ | tasyāḥ sadṛśam eva sarvo jantur jñānavān api ceṣṭate, kiṃ punar mūrkhaḥ ? tasmāt prakṛtiṃ yānty anugacchanti bhūtāni prāṇinaḥ | nigraho niṣedha-rūpaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati mama vānyasya vā ? durnigrahā prakṛtir iti vākya-śeṣaḥ ||BhGS_3.33||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] One acts in a manner conforming to — corresponding to — one's own nature. Of what? Of one's own <s>prakṛti</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s> means the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, etc. formed in previous lives, which have become manifest at the beginning of the present birth and onward. That is <s>prakṛti</s>. In accordance with that, every creature — even one possessed of knowledge — acts; how much more so a fool? Therefore, beings follow — conform to — their nature. What will restraint (<s>nigraha</s>) — in the form of prohibition — accomplish, whether mine or another's? The completion of the sentence is: nature is difficult to restrain. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.33 //

children.text: yadi sarvo jantur ātmanaḥ prakṛti-sadṛśam eva ceṣṭate, na ca prakṛti-śūnyaḥ kaścid asti, tataḥ puruṣakārasya viṣayānupapatteḥ śāstrānarthakya-prāptāv idam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] If every creature acts only in conformity with its own nature, and no one is devoid of nature, then, since there would be no scope for human effort, the objection arises that scripture would become purposeless — to this it is said:

children.text: indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau |
children.translated_text: Attachment and aversion are established with respect to the object of each sense;

children.text: tayor na vaśam āgacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau ||BhG_3.34||
children.translated_text: one should not come under the sway of these two, for they are one's adversaries on the path. // <s>BhG</s> 3.34 //

children.text: indriyasyendriyasyārthe sarvendriyāṇām arthe śabdādi-viṣaye iṣṭe rāgo 'niṣṭe dveṣa ity evaṃ pratīndriyārthaṃ rāgadveṣāv avaśyaṃbhāvinau tatrāyaṃ puruṣakārasya śāstrārthasya ca viṣaya ucyate | śāstrārthe pravṛttaḥ pūrvam eva rāga-dveṣayor vaśaṃ nāgacchet | yā hi puruṣasya prakṛtiḥ sā rāga-dveṣa-puraḥsaraiva sva-kārye puruṣaṃ pravartayati | tadā svadharma-parityāgaḥ para-dharmānuṣṭhānaṃ ca bhavati | yadā punā rāga-dveṣau tat-pratipakṣeṇa niyamayati tadā śāstra-dṛṣṭir eva puruṣo bhavati, na prakṛti-vaśaḥ | tasmāt tayo rāga-dveṣayor vaśaṃ nāgacchet | yatas tau hy asya puruṣasya paripanthinau śreyo-mārgasya vighna-kartārau taskarāv iva pathīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.34||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] With respect to the object of each and every sense — in the domain of all senses, namely the objects such as sound etc. — toward the agreeable there is attachment (<s>rāga</s>), toward the disagreeable there is aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). Thus, with respect to each sense-object, attachment and aversion inevitably arise. Herein lies the scope of human effort and the purpose of scripture: one who is engaged in the purpose of scripture should not, from the very outset, come under the sway of attachment and aversion. For a person's nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), preceded by attachment and aversion, impels the person to its own [corresponding] action. Then there occurs the abandonment of one's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>) and the performance of another's duty (<s>paradharma</s>). But when one restrains attachment and aversion through their antidote, then one becomes a person guided by scripture, not one subject to nature. Therefore, one should not come under the sway of these two — attachment and aversion. Because these two are this person's adversaries (<s>paripanthin</s>) — obstructors on the path to the highest good, like robbers on a road — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.34 //

children.text: tatra rāga-dveṣa-prayukto manyate śāsrārtham apy anyathā para-dharmo 'pi dharmatvād anuṣṭheya eva iti, tad asat -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In that case, one impelled by attachment and aversion thinks, even regarding the purpose of scripture, otherwise — [thinking] 'the duty of another (<s>paradharma</s>), being a duty, should indeed be performed' — this is wrong:

children.text: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt |
children.translated_text: One's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>), though devoid of merit, is better than the duty of another (<s>paradharma</s>), well performed;

children.text: sva-dharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||BhG_3.35||
children.translated_text: death in one's own duty is better; the duty of another is fraught with danger. // <s>BhG</s> 3.35 //

children.text: śreyān praśasyataraḥ svo dharmaḥ svadharmo viguṇo 'pi vigata-guṇo 'pi anuṣṭhīyamānaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt sādguṇyena saṃpāditād api | sva-dharme sthitasya nidhanaṃ maraṇam api śreyaḥ para-dharme sthitasya jīvitāt | kasmāt ? para-dharmaḥ bhayāvahaḥ narakādi-lakṣaṇaṃ bhayam āvahatīti yataḥ ||BhGS_3.35||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Better — more praiseworthy — is one's own duty (<s>svadharma</s>), even devoid of excellence, even when being performed [imperfectly], than the duty of another, even if well performed — even if accomplished with excellence. For one who abides in one's own duty, death itself is better than living while abiding in the duty of another. Why? Because the duty of another is fraught with danger — it brings fear characterized by hell etc. — this is the reason. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.35 //

children.text: yadyapi anartha-mūlam dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsa [Gītā 2.62] iti rāga-dveṣau hy asya paripanthinau [Gītā 3.34] iti coktam | vikṣiptam anavadhāritaṃ ca tad uktam | tat saṃkṣiptaṃ niścitaṃ ca idam eveti jñātum icchan arjuna uvāca jñāte hi tasmin tad-ucchedāya yatnaṃ kuryām iti arjuna uvāca-
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Although it was stated that 'contemplation of sense-objects' [<s>BhG</s> 2.62] is the root of all misfortune, and that 'these two [attachment and aversion] are one's adversaries' [<s>BhG</s> 3.34] — that was stated in a scattered and undetermined manner. Wishing to know it in a condensed and definitive form — 'this alone is the [root cause]' — and thinking 'having known it, I shall exert myself for its eradication,' <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: atha kena prayukto 'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then by what is a person impelled to commit sin,

children.text: anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ ||BhG_3.36||
children.translated_text: even against his will, O <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>, as if driven by force? // <s>BhG</s> 3.36 //

children.text: atha kena hetu-bhūtena prayuktaḥ san rājñeva bhṛtyo 'yaṃ pāpaṃ karma carati ācarati pūruṣaḥ puruṣaḥ svayam anicchann api he vārṣṇeya vṛṣṇi-kula-prasūta ! balād iva niyojito rājñevety ukto dṛṣṭāntaḥ ||BhGS_3.36||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Then, by what — by what as the motivating cause — impelled, as a servant [is impelled] by a king — this person commits, performs, sinful action, even against his will, O <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>, born of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineage! — as if driven by force — 'as if by a king' is the stated analogy. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.36 //

children.text: śṛṇu tvaṃ taṃ vairiṇaṃ sarvānartha-karaṃ yaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasīti bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] 'Listen! [I shall tell you about] that enemy, the cause of all misfortune, about which you ask' — the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: It is desire (<s>kāma</s>), it is anger (<s>krodha</s>), born of the quality of <s>rajas</s> (passion);

children.text: mahāśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam ||BhG_3.37||
children.translated_text: it is the great devourer, the great sinner — know this to be the enemy here [in this world]. // <s>BhG</s> 3.37 //

children.text: aiśvaryasya samagrasya dharmasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of sovereignty in its entirety, of <s>dharma</s>, of fame, of prosperity,

children.text: vairāgyasyātha mokṣasya ṣaṇṇāṃ bhaga itīṅganā || [ViP 6.5.74]
children.translated_text: of renunciation, and of liberation — [the possession of] these six is called <s>bhaga</s>. // [<s>ViP</s> 6.5.74] //

children.text: ity aiśvaryādi-ṣaṭkaṃ yasmin vāsudeve nityam apratibaddhatvena sāmastyena ca vartate,
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Thus, the six-fold [wealth] beginning with sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) that eternally resides in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, unobstructed and in its totality —

children.text: utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim |
children.translated_text: [He who] knows the origin and dissolution of beings, their coming and going,

children.text: vetti vidyām avidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavān iti || [ViP 6.5.78]
children.translated_text: knowledge and ignorance — he is to be called <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Blessed Lord). // [<s>ViP</s> 6.5.78] //

children.text: utpatty-ādi-viṣayaṃ ca vijñānaṃ yasya sa vāsudevo vācyo bhagavān iti |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And he who possesses the knowledge pertaining to creation etc. — that <s>Vāsudeva</s> is to be called <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: kāma iti | kāma eṣa sarva-loka-śatrur yan-nimittā sarvānartha-prāptiḥ prāṇinām | sa eṣa kāmaḥ pratihataḥ kenacit krodhatvena pariṇamate | ataḥ krodho 'py eṣa eva rajo-guṇa-samudbhavo rajaś ca tad-guṇaś ca rajo-guṇaḥ sa samudbhavo yasya sa kāmo rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ | rajo-guṇasya vā samudbhavaḥ | kāmo hy udbhūto rajaḥ pravartayan puruṣaṃ pravartayati | tṛṣṇayā hy ahaṃkārita iti duḥkhināṃ rajaḥ-kārye sevādau pravṛttānāṃ pralāpaḥ śrūyate | mahāśano mahad aśanaṃ asyeti mahāśanaḥ | ataeva mahā-pāpmā | kāmena hi prerito jantuḥ pāpaṃ karoti | ato viddhy enaṃ kāmam iha saṃsāre vairiṇam ||BhGS_3.37||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] '<s>Kāma</s>' (desire) — this desire is the enemy of the entire world, on whose account all misfortune befalls living beings. This desire, when obstructed by something, transforms into anger (<s>krodha</s>). Therefore, anger too is this very [desire]. Born of <s>rajoguṇa</s> — <s>rajas</s> and its quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is <s>rajoguṇa</s>; that from which it arises — such is desire, born of <s>rajoguṇa</s>. Or, it is the source of <s>rajoguṇa</s>. For desire, having arisen, by activating <s>rajas</s>, impels the person [to action]. For the lamentation of suffering people engaged in the effects of <s>rajas</s> — such as servitude etc. — is heard: 'Ah, driven by craving and egoism!' '<s>Mahāśana</s>' (the great devourer) — one whose consumption is great — therefore it is a great sinner (<s>mahāpāpmā</s>). For impelled by desire, a creature commits sin. Therefore, know this desire to be the enemy here in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). // <s>BhGS</s> 3.37 //

children.text: kathaṃ vairī ? iti dṛṣṭāntaiḥ pratyāyayati -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] How is it an enemy? He illustrates with examples —

children.text: dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena ca |
children.translated_text: As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust,

children.text: yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam ||BhG_3.38||
children.translated_text: as an embryo is covered by the membrane — so is this [knowledge] covered by that [desire]. // <s>BhG</s> 3.38 //

children.text: dhūmena sahajenāvriyate vahniḥ prakāśātmako 'prakāśātmakena, yathā vā ādarśo malena ca, yatholbena ca jarāyuṇā garbha-veṣṭanena cāvṛta ācchādito garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam ||BhGS_3.38||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Fire, whose nature is luminosity, is enveloped by smoke — which is of a non-luminous nature — that is innate [to fire]. Or, as a mirror [is covered] by dust. And as an embryo is covered, enveloped by the womb-membrane (<s>ulba</s>), the fetal covering — so by that [desire], this [knowledge] is covered. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.38 //

children.text: kiṃ punas tad idaṃ-śabda-vācyaṃ yat kāmenāvṛtam ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] But what is this thing denoted by the word 'this' that is said to be covered by desire? It is stated —

children.text: āvṛtaṃ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā |
children.translated_text: Knowledge is covered by this, the eternal enemy of the knower,

children.text: kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca ||BhG_3.39||
children.translated_text: in the form of desire, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, an insatiable fire. // <s>BhG</s> 3.39 //

children.text: āvṛtam etena jñānaṃ jñānino nitya-vairiṇā, jñānī hi jānāty anenāham anarthe prayuktaḥ pūrvam eveti | duḥkhī ca bhavati nityam eva | ato 'sau jñānino nitya-vairī, na tu mūrkhasya | sa hi kāmaṃ tṛṣṇā-kāle mitram iva paśyan tat-kārye duḥkhe prāpte jānāti tṛṣṇayāhaṃ duḥkhitvam āpādita iti, na pūrvam eva | ato jñānina eva nitya-vairī | kiṃ-rūpeṇa ? kāma-rūpeṇa kāma icchaiva rūpam asyeti kāmarūpas tena duṣpūreṇa duḥkhena pūraṇam asyeti duṣpūras tenānalena nāsyālaṃ paryāptir vidyata ity analas tena ca ||BhGS_3.39||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Knowledge is covered by this — the eternal enemy of the knower. For the knower indeed knows: 'by this [desire] I have been impelled toward misfortune in the past.' And he suffers constantly. Therefore, it is the eternal enemy of the knower, but not of a fool. For a fool, seeing desire at the time of craving as if it were a friend, only when the suffering that results from it arrives, comes to know 'by craving I have been brought to suffering' — not before. Therefore, it is the eternal enemy of the knower alone. Of what form? In the form of desire — desire, i.e., craving itself, is its form; it is insatiable (<s>duṣpūra</s>) — difficult to satiate; and [it is] a fire (<s>anala</s>) — one for which there is never enough, never satisfaction. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.39 //

children.text: kim adhiṣṭhānaḥ punaḥ kāmo jñānasyāvaraṇatvena vairī sarvasya lokasya ? ity apekṣāyām āha, jñāte hi śatror adhiṣṭhāne sukhena nibarhaṇaṃ kartuṃ śakyata iti-
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] What then is the seat (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of desire, which, by covering knowledge, is the enemy of the whole world? In anticipation of this [question], he says — for when the enemy's seat is known, it can easily be destroyed:

children.text: indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate |
children.translated_text: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat;

children.text: etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam ||BhG_3.40||
children.translated_text: through these, it deludes the embodied one by covering knowledge. // <s>BhG</s> 3.40 //

children.text: indriyāṇi mano buddhiś cāsya kāmasyādhiṣṭhānam āśraya ucyate | etair indriyādibhir āśrayair vimohayati vividhaṃ mohayaty eṣa kāmo jñānam āvṛtya ācchādya dehinaṃ śarīriṇam ||BhGS_3.40||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be the seat, the abode, of this desire. Through these — the senses and other abodes — it variously deludes — this desire, having covered, having veiled knowledge, deludes the embodied one, the one who dwells in a body. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.40 //

children.text: yata evam -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since this is so —

children.text: tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having first restrained the senses, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>,

children.text: pāpmānaṃ prajahi hy enaṃ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam ||BhG_3.41||
children.translated_text: slay this sinful one, the destroyer of knowledge and realization (<s>vijñāna</s>)! // <s>BhG</s> 3.41 //

children.text: tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau pūrvam eva niyamya vaśīkṛtya bharatarṣabha pāpmānaṃ pāpācāraṃ kāmaṃ prajahihi parityaja enaṃ prakṛtaṃ vairiṇaṃ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanaṃ jñānaṃ śāstrata ācāryataś cātmādīnām avabodhaḥ | vijñānaṃ viśeṣatas tad-anubhavas tayor jñāna-vijñānayoḥ śreyaḥ-prāpti-hetvor nāśanaṃ nāśa-karaṃ prajahihi ātmanaḥ parityajety arthaḥ ||BhGS_3.41||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Therefore, having first restrained — having brought under control — the senses, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>, slay — completely abandon — this sinful one, this one of sinful conduct — desire — the aforementioned enemy — the destroyer of knowledge and realization (<s>vijñāna</s>). Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the understanding of the Self and such [truths] from scripture and teacher. Realization (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the particular direct experience of those [truths]. Of these two — knowledge and realization — which are the means to the attainment of the highest good — [desire is] the destroyer, the cause of destruction. Slay it — abandon it from your self — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 3.41 //

children.text: indriyāṇy ādau niyamya kāmaṃ śatruṃ jahihi ity uktam | tatra kim āśrayaḥ kāmaṃ jahyāt ity ucyate --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] It was said: 'having first restrained the senses, slay desire, the enemy.' In that case, relying on what should one slay desire? It is stated:

children.text: indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: The senses, they say, are superior [to the body]; superior to the senses is the mind;

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ ||BhG_3.42||
children.translated_text: but superior to the mind is the intellect; and that which is superior to the intellect is He [the Self]. // <s>BhG</s> 3.42 //

children.text: indriyāṇi śrotrādīni pañca | dehaṃ sthūlaṃ bāhyaṃ paricchinnaṃ cāpekṣya saukṣmyāntaratva-vyāpitvādy-apekṣayā parāṇi prakṛṣṭāny āhuḥ paṇḍitāḥ | tathā indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ saṃkalpa-vikalpātmakam | tathā manasas tu parā buddhir niścayātmikā | tathā yaḥ sarva-dṛśyebhyo buddhy-antebhyo 'bhyantaro yaṃ dehinam indriyādibhir āśrayair yuktaḥ kāmo jñānāvaraṇa-dvāreṇa mohayatīty uktam | buddheḥ paratas tu sa | sa buddher draṣṭā | para ātmā ||BhGS_3.42||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The senses — the five [senses] beginning with hearing. Compared to the body — the gross, external, limited [body] — in terms of subtlety, interiority, pervasiveness, etc., they are said to be superior (<s>parāṇi</s>), i.e., more excellent, by the learned. Likewise, superior to the senses is the mind (<s>manas</s>), whose nature is deliberation and imagination. Likewise, superior to the mind is the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), whose nature is determination. And the one who — the embodied one, more interior than all visible things ending with the intellect — whom desire, through the door of obscuring knowledge, deludes — this has been stated. But superior to the intellect is he — he is the seer of the intellect. The supreme Self. ||<s>BhGS</s> 3.42||

children.text: tataḥ kim --
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Then what [follows]?

children.text: evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: Thus, knowing that which is superior to the intellect, steadying the self by the Self,

children.text: jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāma-rūpaṃ durāsadam ||BhG_3.43||
children.translated_text: slay the enemy, O mighty-armed one, in the form of desire, which is difficult to assail. ||<s>BhG</s> 3.43||

children.text: evaṃ buddheḥ param ātmānaṃ buddhvā jñātvā saṃstabhya samyak stambhanaṃ kṛtvātmānaṃ svenaivātmanā saṃskṛtena manasā samyak samādhāyety arthaḥ | jahy enaṃ śatruṃ he mahābāho ! kāma-rūpaṃ durāsadaṃ duḥkhenāsada āsādanaṃ prāptir yasya taṃ durāsadaṃ durvijñeyāneka-viśeṣam iti ||BhGS_3.43||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Thus' — knowing that which is superior to the intellect, i.e., the Self — having known it, having realized it; 'steadying' — having properly stabilized; the self — by one's own self, i.e., by the purified mind — the meaning is: having properly composed [the mind]. Slay this enemy, O mighty-armed one! — in the form of desire, which is difficult to assail (<s>durāsada</s>) — that whose approach, i.e., attainment, is difficult — meaning that which is hard to comprehend, having manifold forms. ||<s>BhGS</s> 3.43||

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
||3||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter in the blessed <s>Bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, who was the foremost among the supreme renunciants and wandering monks. ||3||

children.text: BhG 4
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 4

children.text:
atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
(śaṅkara-bhāṣyaḥ)
children.translated_text: Fourth Chapter — <s>Śaṅkara's</s> Commentary

children.text: yo 'yaṃ yogo 'dhyāya-dvayenokto jñāna-niṣṭhā-lakṣaṇaḥ sa sannyāsaḥ karma-yogopāyaḥ | yasmin vedārthaḥ parisamāptaḥ pravṛtti-lakṣaṇo nivṛtti-lakṣaṇaś ca gītāsu ca sarvāsv ayam eva yogo vivakṣito bhagavatā | ataeva parisamāptaḥ pravṛttiṃ vedārthaṃ manvānas taṃ vaṃśa-kathanena stauti śrī-bhagavān |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This <s>yoga</s> that has been described in the two [preceding] chapters, characterized by steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>), is renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>), [having] <s>karma-yoga</s> as its means. In it the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> is concluded, both in its active (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and cessative (<s>nivṛtti</s>) aspects; and in all the chapters of the <s>Gītā</s>, this very <s>yoga</s> is what the Lord intends to expound. Therefore, considering that the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> in its active aspect has been concluded, the Blessed Lord praises it through the lineage-narrative:

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavān aham avyayam |
children.translated_text: I taught this imperishable <s>yoga</s> to <s>Vivasvat</s>;

children.text: vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣvākave 'bravīt ||BhG_4.1||
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvat</s> communicated it to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> told it to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.1||

children.text: imam adhyāya-dvayenoktaṃ yogaṃ vivasvate ādityāya sargādau proktavān aham | jagat-paripālayitṝṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ balādhānāya | tena yoga-balena yuktāḥ samarthā bhavanti brahma parirakṣituṃ, brahma-kṣatre paripālite jagat paripālayitum alam | avyayam avyaya-phalatvāt | na hy asya samyag darśana-niṣṭhā-lakṣaṇasya mokṣākhyaṃ phalaṃ vyeti | sa ca vivasvān manave prāha | manur ikṣvākave sva-putrāyādirājāyābravīt ||BhGS_4.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'This' — the <s>yoga</s> described in the two [preceding] chapters — I taught to <s>Vivasvat</s>, i.e., to the Sun (<s>Āditya</s>), at the beginning of creation, for the purpose of strengthening the power of the <s>kṣatriyas</s> who protect the world. Endowed with the power of this <s>yoga</s>, they become capable of protecting <s>Brahman</s> (the sacred tradition); and when <s>Brahman</s> and the <s>kṣatra</s> (warrior-class) are protected, they are capable of protecting the world. 'Imperishable' — because it has an imperishable fruit; for the fruit of this [<s>yoga</s>], characterized by steadfastness in right vision, called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), does not perish. And that <s>Vivasvat</s> communicated it to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> told it to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, his own son, the first king. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.1||

children.text: evaṃ paramparā-prāptam imaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus received through succession, the royal sages knew this [<s>yoga</s>];

children.text: sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa ||BhG_4.2||
children.translated_text: but through the long passage of time, this <s>yoga</s> was lost here [in this world], O scorcher of foes. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.2||

children.text: evaṃ kṣatriya-paramparā-prāptam imaṃ rājarṣayo rājānaś ca te ṛṣayaś ca rājarṣayo vidur imaṃ yogam | sa yogaḥ kāleneha mahatā dīrgheṇa naṣṭo vicchinna-sampradāyaḥ saṃvṛtto he parantapa ! ātmano vipakṣa-bhūtāḥ para ucyante tān śaurya-tejo-gabhastibhir bhānur iva tāpayatīti parantapaḥ śatru-tāpana ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Thus received' — through the <s>kṣatriya</s> succession — the royal sages (<s>rājarṣis</s>), who are both kings and sages, 'knew' — knew this <s>yoga</s>. That <s>yoga</s>, 'through time' — through a great, long time — 'was lost here,' i.e., the tradition was broken — this is the meaning. O scorcher of foes (<s>parantapa</s>) — those who are adversaries are called <s>para</s>; he who scorches them with the rays of his valour and energy, like the sun, is <s>parantapa</s> — meaning: tormentor of enemies. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.2||

children.text: durlabhān ajitendriyān prāpya naṣṭaṃ yogam imam upalabhya lokaṃ cāpuruṣārtha-sambandhinam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having reached [the point of scarcity due to] persons of uncontrolled senses being rare, and having found this <s>yoga</s> to be lost, and the world to be connected with non-<s>puruṣārtha</s> (non-human-goals) —

children.text: sa evāyaṃ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: That very same ancient <s>yoga</s> has been declared by me to you today,

children.text: bhakto 'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hy etad uttamam ||BhG_4.3||
children.translated_text: since you are my devotee and friend — for this is a supreme secret. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.3||

children.text: sa evāyam mayā te tubhyam adya idānīṃ yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ | bhakto 'si me sakhā cāsīti | rahasyaṃ hi yasmād etad uttamaṃ yogo jñānam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'That very same' — by me, to you, today, i.e., now — this <s>yoga</s> has been declared — 'ancient,' i.e., of old. Since you are my devotee and my friend — for this is indeed a supreme secret — meaning: this <s>yoga</s> is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.3||

children.text: bhagavatā vipratiṣiddham uktam iti mā bhūt kasyacid buddhir iti parihārārthaṃ codyam iva kurvann arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Lest anyone think that the Lord has stated something contradictory, <s>Arjuna</s>, as if raising an objection for the purpose of resolving this, said:

children.text: aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Your birth is later; the birth of <s>Vivasvat</s> is earlier.

children.text: katham etad vijānīyāṃ tvam ādau proktavān iti ||BhG_4.4||
children.translated_text: How am I to understand this — that you taught it in the beginning? ||<s>BhG</s> 4.4||

children.text: aparam arvāg vasudeva-gṛhe bhavato janma paraṃ pūrvaṃ sargādau janma utpattiḥ vivasvata ādityasya | tat katham etad vijānīyām aviruddhārthatayā yas tvam evādau proktavān imaṃ yogam | sa eva tvam idānīṃ mahyaṃ proktavān asīti ||BhGS_4.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Later' — more recent, in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s> — is your birth; 'earlier' — prior, at the beginning of creation — is the birth, i.e., the origin, of <s>Vivasvat</s>, the Sun. Then how am I to understand this in a non-contradictory way — that you, the very same one, taught this <s>yoga</s> in the beginning; and that very same you have now taught it to me? ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.4||

children.text: yā vāsudeve anīśvarāsarvajñāśaṅkā mūrkhāṇāṃ tāṃ pariharan śrī-bhagavān uvāca padartho hy arjunasya praśnaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Dispelling the suspicion of the ignorant that <s>Vāsudeva</s> is neither omniscient nor omnipotent, the Blessed Lord said — for <s>Arjuna's</s> question indeed calls for this [answer]:

children.text: bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna |
children.translated_text: Many births of mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa ||BhG_4.5||
children.translated_text: I know them all, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.5||

children.text: bahūni me mama vyatītāni atikrāntāni janmāni tava ca he arjuna tāny ahaṃ veda jāne sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha jānīṣe | dharmādharmādi-pratibaddha-jñāna-śaktitvāt | ahaṃ punar nitya-śuddha-buddha-mukta-svabhāvatvād anāvaraṇa-jñāna-śaktir iti vedāham | he parantapa ||BhGS_4.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Many' — of mine — have passed, i.e., gone by — 'births,' and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>. 'I know them all' — I know [them]; you do not know — because the power of your knowledge is obstructed by <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, etc. But I, being of the nature of eternal purity, consciousness, and freedom, having unobstructed power of knowledge — therefore I know. O scorcher of foes! ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.5||

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi tava nityeśvarasya dharmādharmābhāve 'pi janma ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How then is there birth for you who are the eternal Lord, even in the absence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>? It is stated:

children.text: ajo 'pi sann avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san |
children.translated_text: Though I am unborn, though I am of imperishable nature, though I am the Lord of all beings,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmy ātma-māyayā ||BhG_4.6||
children.translated_text: yet, presiding over my own <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), I come into being through my own <s>Māyā</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.6||

children.text: ajo 'pi janma-rahito 'pi san, tathāvyayātmākṣīṇa-jñāna-śakti-svabhāvo 'pi san, tathā bhūtānāṃ brahmādi-stamba-paryantānām īśvara īśana-śīlo 'pi san | prakṛtiṃ svāṃ mama vaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ triguṇātmikāṃ yasyā vaśe sarvam idaṃ jagad vartate | yayā mohitaṃ jagat sat svam ātmānaṃ vāsudevaṃ na jānāti | tāṃ prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya vaśīkṛtya saṃbhavāmi dehavān iva bhavāmi jāta ivātma-māyayātmano māyayā, na paramārthato lokavat ||BhGS_4.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Though I am unborn (<s>aja</s>), i.e., devoid of birth; though I am of imperishable nature (<s>avyayātmā</s>), i.e., of undiminished power of knowledge; though I am the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) of all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass, i.e., possessed of the nature of sovereignty — yet, presiding over, i.e., controlling my own <s>Prakṛti</s> — my <s>Vaiṣṇavī Māyā</s>, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, under whose power this entire world exists, by which the world is deluded and does not know the Self, <s>Vāsudeva</s> — that <s>Prakṛti</s> of mine, having subjugated it, I come into being (<s>saṃbhavāmi</s>), i.e., I appear as if embodied, as if born, through my own <s>Māyā</s> — not in ultimate reality, not like worldly beings. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.6||

children.text: tac ca janma kadā kim-arthaṃ ca ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And when does that birth [occur], and for what purpose? It is stated:

children.text: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: Whenever there is a decline of <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham ||BhG_4.7||
children.translated_text: and a rise of <s>adharma</s> — then I create myself. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.7||

children.text: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir hānir varṇāśramādi-lakṣaṇasya prāṇinām abhyudaya-niḥśreyasa-sādhanasya bhavati | bhārata ! abhyutthānam udbhavo 'dharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy ahaṃ māyayā ||BhGS_4.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Whenever' — whenever indeed there is a decline, i.e., diminution, of <s>dharma</s> — characterized by the <s>varṇāśrama</s> (class-and-stage) system, which is the means to the prosperity and ultimate good of living beings — O <s>Bhārata</s>! — and a rise, i.e., an increase, of <s>adharma</s> — then I create myself, i.e., through <s>Māyā</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.7||

children.text: kim-artham ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For what purpose?

children.text: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
children.translated_text: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the wicked,

children.text: dharma-saṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge ||BhG_4.8||
children.translated_text: for the establishment of <s>dharma</s>, I come into being in every age. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.8||

children.text: paritrāṇāya parirakṣaṇāya sādhūnāṃ san-mārga-sthānām | vināśāya ca duṣkṛtāṃ pāpa-kāriṇām | kiṃ ca dharma-saṃsthāpanārthāya dharmasya samyak-sthāpanaṃ tad-arthaṃ sambhavāmi | yuge yuge pratiyugam ||BhGS_4.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'For the protection' — for the preservation — 'of the righteous,' i.e., of those who abide on the virtuous path. 'For the destruction of the wicked' — of the evil-doers. Furthermore — 'for the establishment of <s>dharma</s>' — for the proper establishment of <s>dharma</s> — for that purpose — I come into being, in every age (<s>yuge yuge</s>), i.e., in each age. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.8||

children.text: janma karma ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who knows in truth my divine birth and action —

children.text: tyaktvā dehaṃ punar janma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna ||BhG_4.9||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the body, he is not born again; he comes to me, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.9||

children.text: taj-janma māyā-rūpaṃ, karma ca sādhu-paritrāṇādi, me mama divyam aprākṛtam aiśvaram evaṃ yathoktaṃ yo vetti tattvatas tattvena yathāvat tyaktvā deham imaṃ punar janma punar utpattiṃ naiti na prāpnoti, mām ety āgacchati, sa mucyate he 'rjuna ||BhGS_4.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That birth, which is of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>, and action — such as the protection of the righteous etc. — of mine, are 'divine' (<s>divya</s>), i.e., supernatural, pertaining to the Lord (<s>aiśvara</s>). 'Thus' — as described — he who knows in truth (<s>tattvatas</s>), i.e., as it really is — having abandoned this body, he does not undergo rebirth (<s>punar janma</s>), i.e., does not attain another birth. He comes to me — he is liberated, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.9||

children.text: naiṣa mokṣa-mārga idānīṃ pravṛttaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ? pūrvam api -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This path to liberation has not commenced only now. Rather, even before —

children.text: vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in me, taking refuge in me,

children.text: bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ ||BhG_4.10||
children.translated_text: many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have attained my state of being. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.10||

children.text: vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhāḥ - rāgaś ca bhayaṃ ca krodhaś ca rāga-bhaya-krodhāḥ, vītā vigatā rāga-bhaya-krodhā yebhyas te vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhāḥ | man-mayā brahma-vida īśvarābheda-darśinaḥ | mām eva parameśvaram upāśritāḥ | kevala-jñāna-niṣṭhā ity arthaḥ | bahavo 'neke jñāna-tapasā jñānam eva ca paramātma-viṣayaṃ tapaḥ | tena jñāna-tapasā | pūtāḥ parāṃ śuddhiṃ gatāḥ santaḥ | mad-bhāvam īśvara-bhāvaṃ mokṣam āgatāḥ samanuprāptāḥ | itara-tapo-nirapekṣā jñāna-niṣṭhā ity asya liṅgaṃ jñāna-tapaseti viśeṣaṇam ||BhGS_4.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Freed from attachment, fear, and anger' — attachment, fear, and anger are <s>rāga-bhaya-krodha</s>; those from whom these have departed are 'freed from attachment, fear, and anger.' 'Absorbed in me' (<s>man-maya</s>) — knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, those who see no difference from the Lord. 'Taking refuge in me' — in me alone, the Supreme Lord. The meaning is: devoted solely to steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>). 'Many' — numerous. 'By the austerity of knowledge' — knowledge itself, pertaining to the Supreme Self, is the austerity; by that austerity of knowledge. 'Purified' — having attained supreme purity. 'Have attained my state of being' (<s>mad-bhāva</s>) — the state of the Lord, i.e., <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — they have reached, i.e., fully attained. The fact that <s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s> is independent of other austerities is indicated by the qualifying expression 'austerity of knowledge.' ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.10||

children.text: tava tarhi rāga-dveṣau staḥ | yena kebhyaścit evātma-bhāvaṃ prayacchasi, na sarvebhyaḥ | ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Do you then have attachment and aversion — since you grant your own state of being only to some, not to all? This is replied to:

children.text: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham |
children.translated_text: In whatever way people approach me, in that very way I reward them;

children.text: mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||BhG_4.11||
children.translated_text: human beings follow my path in all ways, O <s>Pārtha</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.11||

children.text: ye yathā yena prakāreṇa yena prayojanena yat-phalārthitayā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva tat-phala-dānena bhajāmy anugṛhṇāmy aham ity etat | teṣāṃ mokṣaṃ pratyanarthitvāt | na hy ekasya mumukṣutvaṃ phalārthitvaṃ ca yugapat sambhavati | ato ye yat-phalārthinas tāṃs tat-phala-pradānena, ye yathokta-kāriṇas tv aphalārthino mumukṣavaś ca tān jñāna-pradānena | ye jñāninaḥ sannyāsino mumukṣavaś ca tān mokṣa-pradānena, tathārtānārti-haraṇena ity evaṃ yathā prapadyante ye tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmīty arthaḥ | na punār rāga-dveṣa-nimittaṃ moha-nimittaṃ vā kaṃcid bhajāmi | sarvathāpi sarvāvasthasya mameśvarasya vartma mārgam anuvartante manuṣyāḥ | yat-phalārthitayā yasmin karmaṇy adhikṛtā ye prayatante te manuṣyā atra ucyante he pārtha sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ ||BhGS_4.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'In whatever way' — by whatever means, with desire for whatever fruit — people approach me, 'in that very way' — through the bestowal of that [corresponding] fruit — I reward them, i.e., I grace them — this is [the meaning]. This is because they do not desire liberation. For a single person cannot simultaneously be a seeker of liberation and a desirer of [other] fruits. Therefore, those who desire particular fruits — [I reward them] with the bestowal of those fruits; those who perform the prescribed actions without desiring fruits and who seek liberation — [I reward them] with the bestowal of knowledge; those who are <s>jñānins</s> (knowers), renunciants, and seekers of liberation — [I reward them] with the bestowal of <s>mokṣa</s>; likewise, the afflicted — with the removal of their affliction. Thus, in whatever way people approach me, in that very way I reward them — this is the meaning. And it is not that I reward anyone out of attachment, aversion, or delusion. In all ways, in all conditions — of me, the Lord — human beings follow my path. Those who, with desire for particular fruits, are qualified for particular actions and exert themselves — those human beings are spoken of here, O <s>Pārtha</s>, in all ways (<s>sarvaśaḥ</s>), i.e., in all manners. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.11||

children.text: yadi taveśvarasya rāgādi-doṣābhāvāt sarva-prāṇiṣv anujighṛkṣāyāṃ tulyāyāṃ sarva-phala-pradāna-samarthe ca tvayi sati vāsudevaḥ sarvaṃ [Gītā 7.19] iti jñānenaiva mumukṣavaḥ santaḥ kasmāt tvām eva sarve na pratipadyante ? iti śṛṇu tatra kāraṇam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If, since you as the Lord are free from defects such as attachment etc., your benevolence toward all beings is equal, and you are capable of bestowing all fruits — then, since '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything' [<s>BhG</s> 7.19], why do not all people, being seekers of liberation through knowledge alone, approach you? Listen to the reason for this:

children.text: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Desiring the success of actions, they worship the gods here;

children.text: kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā ||BhG_4.12||
children.translated_text: for quickly in the human world does success born of action come about. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.12||
