children.text: kāṅkṣanto 'bhīpsantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ phala-niṣpattiṃ prārthayanto yajanta ihāsmin loke devatā indrādgny-ādyāḥ | atha yo 'nyāṃ devatām upāste 'nyo 'sāv anyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda, yathā paśuḥ | evaṃ sa devānām [BAU 1.4.10] iti śruteḥ | teṣāṃ hi bhinna-devatāyājināṃ phalākāṅkṣiṇāṃ kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ hi yasmān mānuṣe loke | manuṣya-loke hi śāstrādhikāraḥ | kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke iti viśeṣaṇāt | anyeṣv api karma-phala-siddhiṃ darśayati bhagavān | mānuṣe loke varṇāśramādi-karmādhikāra iti viśeṣaḥ | teṣāṃ ca varṇāśramādhikāriṇāṃ karmiṇāṃ phala-siddhiḥ kṣipraṃ bhavati karmajā karmaṇo jātā ||BhGS_4.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Desiring — wishing for — the success of actions, i.e., the fruition of results, they worship, here in this world, the deities such as <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and others. 'But one who worships another deity, [thinking] "He is one and I am another" — he does not know; he is like a domestic animal to the gods' [<s>BAU</s> 1.4.10] — thus from the <s>śruti</s>. For those worshippers of separate deities who desire fruits, quickly — swiftly — since [it is] in the human world. For the qualification for scriptural [action] exists in the human world. From the specific mention 'quickly in the human world,' the Blessed Lord shows the fruition of action in other [worlds] too. [But] the specific point is that the qualification for <s>varṇāśrama</s> duties exists in the human world. And for those qualified performers of <s>varṇāśrama</s> duties, the success of results comes quickly, born of action — arisen from action. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.12 //

children.text: mānuṣa eva loke varṇāśramādi-karmādhikāraḥ | nānyeṣu lokeṣv iti niyamaḥ kiṃ-nimittaḥ ? iti | athavā varṇāśramādi-pravibhāgopetā manuṣyā mama vartmānuvartante sarvaśa [Gītā 4.11] ity uktaṃ kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇān niyamena tavaiva vartmānuvartante, nānyasya kim ? ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The qualification for <s>varṇāśrama</s> duties exists in the human world alone, not in other worlds — what is the reason for this restriction? Or alternatively: It has been said that human beings, endowed with the classification of <s>varṇāśrama</s>, 'follow My path in every way' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.11]. For what reason do they follow Your path exclusively, and not that of another? It is said:

children.text: cātur-varṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The four-<s>varṇa</s> system was created by Me according to the division of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>karma</s> (actions);

children.text: tasya kartāram api māṃ viddhy akartāram avyayam ||BhG_4.13||
children.translated_text: though I am the creator of that, know Me to be the non-agent, the imperishable. // <s>BhG</s> 4.13 //

children.text:
cāturvarṇyaṃ catvāra eva varṇāś cāturvarṇyaṃ mayeśvareṇa sṛṣṭam utpāditaṃ brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīt [Ṛk 8.4.19.2, Yajuḥ 32.11] ity ādi śruteḥ | guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśo guṇa-vibhāgaśaḥ karma-vibhāgaśaś ca | guṇāḥ sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi | tatra sāttvikasya sattva-pradhānasya brāhmaṇasya śamo damas tapaḥ [Gītā 18.42] ity ādīni karmāṇi | sattvopa-sarjana-rajaḥ-pradhānasya kṣatriyasya śaurya-tejaḥ-prabhṛtīni karmāṇi | tama-upasarjana-rajaḥ-pradhānasya vaiśyasya kṛṣy-ādīni karmāṇi | raja-upasarjana-tamaḥ-pradhānasya śūdrasya śuśrūṣaiva karma | ity evaṃ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaś cāturguṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭam ity arthaḥ | tac cedaṃ cāturvarṇyaṃ nānyeṣu lokeṣu | ato mānuṣe loke iti viśeṣaṇam | hanta tarhi cāturvarṇya-sargādeḥ karmaṇaḥ kartṛtvāt
tat-phalena yujyase 'to na tvaṃ nitya-mukto nityeśvaraś ceti | ucyate - yadyapi māyā-saṃvyavahāreṇa tasya karmaṇaḥ kartāram api santaṃ māṃ paramārthato viddhy akartāraṃ, ataevāvyayam asaṃsāriṇaṃ ca māṃ viddhi ||BhGS_4.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The four-<s>varṇa</s> system (<s>cāturvarṇya</s>) — the four <s>varṇas</s> themselves — was created, produced by Me, the Lord, [as stated in] the <s>śruti</s>: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth' [<s>Ṛk</s> 8.4.19.2, <s>Yajuḥ</s> 32.11] etc. According to the division of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>karma</s> — according to the division of <s>guṇas</s> and according to the division of <s>karma</s>. The <s>guṇas</s> are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Among these: for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who is <s>sattva</s>-predominant, the actions are 'tranquility, self-restraint, austerity' [<s>Gītā</s> 18.42] etc. For the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, in whom <s>rajas</s> predominates with <s>sattva</s> as subordinate, the actions are valor, splendor, and the like. For the <s>Vaiśya</s>, in whom <s>rajas</s> predominates with <s>tamas</s> as subordinate, the actions are agriculture and the like. For the <s>Śūdra</s>, in whom <s>tamas</s> predominates with <s>rajas</s> as subordinate, service alone is the action. Thus, according to the division of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>karma</s>, the four-<s>varṇa</s> system was created by Me — this is the meaning. And this four-<s>varṇa</s> system does not exist in other worlds; therefore the specification 'in the human world.' Well then, since You are the agent of the creation of the four-<s>varṇa</s> system and such actions, You must be subject to their fruits and hence not eternally liberated nor the eternal Lord! It is said: Even though, by conventional dealings through <s>māyā</s>, I am the agent of that action, know Me to be, in the ultimate sense, the non-agent; and for this very reason, know Me to be imperishable — not subject to <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.13 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu karmaṇāṃ kartāraṃ māṃ manyase paramārthatas teṣām akartaivāham | yato -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Of those actions of which you consider Me to be the agent in the ultimate sense — of those I am indeed the non-agent. Since —

children.text: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā |
children.translated_text: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have desire for the fruits of action;

children.text: iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate ||BhG_4.14||
children.translated_text: one who thus knows Me is not bound by actions. // <s>BhG</s> 4.14 //

children.text: na māṃ tāni karmāṇi limpanti dehādy-ārambhakatvenāhaṅkārābhāvāt | na ca teṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ phale me mama spṛhā tṛṣṇā | yeṣāṃ tu saṃsāriṇām ahaṃ kartety ābhimānaḥ karmasu spṛhā tat-phaleṣu ca tān karmāṇi limpantīti yuktam | tad-abhāvān na māṃ karmāṇi limpantīti | evaṃ yo 'nye 'pi mām ātmatvenābhijānāti nāhaṃ kartā na me karma-phale spṛheti na karmabhir na badhyate | tasyāpi na dehādy-ārambhakāni karmāṇi bhavantīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those actions do not taint Me, because of the absence of ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) as the initiator of body and the rest. Nor do I have desire (<s>spṛhā</s>), i.e., craving, for the fruits of those actions. But for those in <s>saṃsāra</s> who have the conceit 'I am the agent' regarding actions and who have desire for their fruits — it is fitting that actions taint them. Due to the absence of that [ego and desire], actions do not taint Me. Thus, whoever else also knows Me as the Self — [thinking] 'I am not the agent, I have no desire for the fruits of action' — that one too is not bound by actions. The meaning is: for that person too, actions that initiate body etc. do not arise. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.14 //

children.text: nāhaṃ kartā, na me karma-phale spṛheti -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'I am not the agent, I have no desire for the fruits of action' —

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having known thus, action was performed even by the ancients who sought liberation;

children.text: kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam ||BhG_4.15||
children.translated_text: therefore, you too perform action alone, as was performed by the ancients of old. // <s>BhG</s> 4.15 //

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtam karma pūrvair apy atikrāntair mumukṣubhiḥ | kuru tena karmaiva tvam | na tuṣṇīm āsanaṃ nāpi saṃnyāsaḥ kartavyaḥ | tasmāt tvat-pūrvair apy anuṣṭhitatvād yady anātmajñas tvaṃ tad ātma-śuddhy-artham | tattvavic cet loka-saṃgrahārtham | pūrve janakādibhiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam | nādhunātana-kṛtaṃ nivartitam ||BhGS_4.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having known thus, action was performed even by the ancients, i.e., those who have passed, who sought liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>). Therefore, perform action alone. Not sitting silently, nor should renunciation be adopted [by you]. Therefore, since it was practiced even by those before you — if you lack Self-knowledge, then for the purification of the self; and if you are a knower of the truth, then for the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>). 'Previously performed by the ancients' — performed by those prior [to you], such as <s>Janaka</s> and others. It is not something newly instituted that has been discontinued. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.15 //

children.text: tatra karma cet kartavyaṃ tvad-vacanād eva karomy aham | kiṃ viśeṣitena ? pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam [Gītā 4.15] iti | ucyate -- yasmān mahad vaiṣamyaṃ karmaṇi | katham ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If, then, action is to be performed, I shall perform it simply by Your command alone. Why the need for further specification — 'as was performed by the ancients of old' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.15]? It is said — because there is great difficulty in [understanding] action. How so?

children.text: kiṃ karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ |
children.translated_text: What is action? What is inaction? — even the wise are confused about this;

children.text: tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||BhG_4.16||
children.translated_text: I shall declare to you that action, knowing which you shall be freed from evil. // <s>BhG</s> 4.16 //

children.text: kiṃ karma kim cākarmeti kavayo medhāvino 'py atrāsmin karmādi-viṣaye mohitā mohaṃ gatāḥ | atas te tubhyam ahaṃ karmākarma ca pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā viditvā karmādi mokṣyase 'śubhāt saṃsārāt ||BhGS_4.16||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'What is action? And what is inaction?' — even the wise, i.e., the intelligent ones, are confused — have fallen into delusion — in this matter, i.e., in this subject of action and the rest. Therefore, I shall declare to you action and inaction, knowing which — having understood action and the rest — you shall be freed from evil, i.e., from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.16 //

children.text: na caitat tvayā mantavyaṃ, karma nāma dehādi-ceṣṭā loka-prasiddhaṃ, akarma nāma tad-akriyā tūṣṇīm āsanam | kiṃ tatra boddhavyam ? iti | kasmāt ? ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And you should not think: 'Action is simply bodily movement and the like, well-known in the world, and inaction is simply the cessation of that — sitting still. What is there to understand?' Why not? It is said:

children.text: karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the nature of action must be understood, and the nature of prohibited action (<s>vikarma</s>) must be understood;

children.text: akarmaṇaś ca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ ||BhG_4.17||
children.translated_text: and the nature of inaction must be understood — for the way of action is profound. // <s>BhG</s> 4.17 //

children.text: karmaṇaḥ śāstra-vihitasya hi yasmād apy asti boddhavyam | boddhavyam cāsty eva vikarmaṇaḥ pratiṣiddhasya | tathākarmaṇaś ca tūṣṇīmbhāvasya boddhavyam astīti triṣv apy adhyāhāraḥ kartavyaḥ | yasmād gahanā viṣamā durjñānā karmaṇa ity upalakṣaṇārthaṃ karmādīnāṃ karmākarma-vikarmaṇāṃ gatir yāthātmyaṃ tattvam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Of action — that which is enjoined by scripture — there is indeed something to be understood. And there is something to be understood of <s>vikarma</s> (prohibited action). Likewise, of inaction — of sitting still — there is something to be understood. In all three cases the verb 'must be understood' is to be supplied. Since the way (<s>gati</s>) — the true nature, the reality — of action is profound (<s>gahanā</s>), meaning difficult to traverse, difficult to know. This is a representative term (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for [the nature of] action, inaction, and <s>vikarma</s> collectively. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.17 //

children.text: kiṃ punas tattvaṃ karmāder yad boddhavyam vakṣyāmīti pratijñātam ? ucyate --
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What, then, is the truth about action and the rest that is to be understood, which was promised [to be declared]? It is said:

children.text: karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction —

children.text: sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt ||BhG_4.18||
children.translated_text: that one is wise among human beings; that one is a <s>yogin</s>, the performer of all action. // <s>BhG</s> 4.18 //

children.text: karmaṇi | karma kriyata iti karma vyāpāra-mātraṃ, tasmin karmaṇy akarma karmābhāvaṃ yaḥ paśyet | akarmaṇi ca karmābhāve kartṛ-tantratvāt pravṛtti-nivṛttyor vastv aprāpyaiva hi sarva eva kriyākārakādi-vyavahāro 'vidyābhūmāv eva karma yaḥ paśyet paśyati | sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu, sa yukto yogī ca kṛtsna-karma-kṛt samasta-karma-kṛc ca sa iti stūyate karmākarmaṇor itaretara-darśī |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'In action' — action is that which is done, mere activity; in that action, one who would see inaction, i.e., the absence of action. 'And in inaction' — in the absence of action — since engagement and disengagement are dependent on the agent, and since without actually reaching the [real] entity, all transactional dealings such as action, instruments, etc. exist only in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — one who would see action in [what appears to be] inaction. That one is wise among human beings; that one is a <s>yogin</s>, and the performer of all action — the doer of all actions. Thus is praised one who sees action and inaction as [appearing to be] each other.

children.text: nanu kim idaṃ viruddham ucyate karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed iti | akarmaṇi ca karma iti | na hi karmākarma syād akarma vā karma, tatra viruddhaṃ kathaṃ paśyed draṣṭā ? na | akarmaiva paramārthataḥ sat-karmavad avabhāsate mūḍha-dṛṣṭer lokasya, tathā karmaivākarmavat | tatra yathābhūta-darśanārtham āha bhagavān karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed ity ādi | ato na viruddham buddhimattvādy-upapatteś ca | boddhavyam iti ca yathābhūta-darśanam ucyate | na ca viparīta-jñānād aśubhān mokṣaṇaṃ syāt yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt [Gītā 4.16] iti coktam | tasmāt karmākarmaṇī viparyayeṇa gṛhīte prāṇibhis tad-viparyaya-grahaṇa-nivṛtty-arthaṃ bhagavato vacanaṃ karmaṇy akarma yaḥ ity ādi |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: Is this not contradictory — 'one who sees inaction in action' and 'action in inaction'? For action cannot be inaction, nor inaction action. How then can one see what is contradictory? No — for what is in reality inaction alone appears as action to the deluded vision of the world, and likewise action alone [appears] as inaction. Therefore, for the purpose of seeing things as they truly are, the Blessed Lord says 'one who sees inaction in action' etc. Hence it is not contradictory, and the attribution of wisdom etc. is appropriate. And 'must be understood' indicates seeing things as they truly are. Nor could liberation from evil come from erroneous knowledge — and it has been said 'knowing which you shall be freed from evil' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.16]. Therefore, since action and inaction are apprehended by beings in a reversed manner, the Blessed Lord's statement 'one who sees inaction in action' etc. is for the purpose of reversing that reversed apprehension.

children.text: na cātra karmādhikaraṇa-karmāsti, kuṇḍe badarāṇīva | nāpy akarmādhikaraṇaṃ karmāsti karmābhāvatvād akarmaṇaḥ | ato viparīta-gṛhīte eva karmākarmaṇī laukikaiḥ, yathā mṛgatṛṣṇikāyām udakaṃ śuktikāyāṃ vā rajatam |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And here, action does not exist as a substrate of action, like berries in a bowl. Nor does action exist as a substrate of inaction, because inaction is the absence of action. Therefore, action and inaction are indeed apprehended in a reversed manner by worldly people — just as water [is seen] in a mirage, or silver in a mother-of-pearl shell.

children.text: nanu karma karmaiva sarveṣāṃ na kvacid vyabhicarati | tan na nau-sthasya nāvi gacchantyāṃ taṭasthesv agatiṣu nageṣu pratikūla-gati-darśanāt | dūreṣu cakṣuṣāsannikṛṣṭeṣu gacchatsu gaty-abhāva-darśanāt | evam ihāpy akarmaṇy ahaṃ karomīti karma-darśanaṃ karmaṇi cākarma-darśanaṃ viparīta-darśanaṃ yena, tan-nirākaraṇārtham ucyate karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyet ity ādi |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: Action is simply action for everyone; it never deviates. Not so — because for one standing in a boat, when the boat moves, the trees on the bank that are stationary appear to move in the opposite direction. And because distant objects that are actually moving appear to the eye as stationary when they are [seemingly] close. Similarly here too, the seeing of action — 'I am acting' — in what is [really] inaction, and the seeing of inaction in action, is a reversed perception; and for the removal of that, it is said: 'one who sees inaction in action' etc.

children.text:
tad etad ukta-prativacanam apy asakṛd atyanta-viparīta-darśana-bhāvitatayā momuhyamāno lokaḥ śrutam apy asakṛt tattvaṃ vismṛtya vismṛtya mithyā-prasaṅgam avatāryāvatārya codayatīti punaḥ punar uttaram āha bhagavān | durvijñeyatvaṃ cālakṣya vastunaḥ | avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yaṃ [Gītā 2.25], na jāyate mriyate [Gītā 2.27] ity ādinātmani karmābhāvaḥ śruti-smṛti-nyāya-prasiddha ukto vakṣyamāṇaś ca | tasminn ātmani karmābhāve 'karmaṇi karma-viparīta-darśanam atyanta-nirūḍham | yataḥ kiṃ karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ [Gītā 4.16] dehādy-āśrayaṃ karmātmany adhyāropya | ahaṃ kartā mamaitat karma, mayāsya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ bhoktavyam iti ca | tathā ahaṃ tūṣṇīṃ bhavāmi, yenāhaṃ nirāyāso 'karmā sukhī syām iti kārya-karaṇāśraya-vyāpāroparamaṃ tat-kṛtaṃ
casukhitvam ātmany adhyāropya na karomi kiṃcit tūṣṇīṃ sukham āsam ity abhimanyate lokaḥ | tatredaṃ lokasya viparīta-darśanāpanayanāyāha bhagavān karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed ity ādi |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And this answer, though stated repeatedly, — the world, bewildered by the force of deeply ingrained reversed perception, forgetting again and again the truth that has been heard, repeatedly brings up false objections after false objections, and the Blessed Lord repeatedly gives the answer. And noting the difficulty of understanding the subtle reality — 'This [Self] is unmanifest, this is inconceivable' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.25], 'It is not born, nor does it die' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.27] — by such [statements], the absence of action in the Self is well-known through <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and reasoning, and has been stated and will be stated [further]. In that Self where there is no action — in that inaction — the reversed perception of action is deeply entrenched. Because [people think] 'What is action? What is inaction? — even the wise are confused' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.16], superimposing action belonging to body etc. upon the Self — [thinking] 'I am the agent, this action is mine, and I must enjoy the fruit of this action.' And likewise, [thinking] 'I shall remain still, so that I may be effort-free, actionless, and happy' — superimposing upon the Self the cessation of activity that belongs to the body and sense-organs, and the happiness born thereof — the world imagines 'I do nothing, I sit still and happy.' Here, for the removal of this reversed perception of the world, the Blessed Lord says 'one who sees inaction in action' etc.

children.text: atra ca karma karmaiva sat kārya-karaṇāśrayaṃ karma-rahito 'vikriya ātmani sarvair adhyastam | yataḥ paṇḍito 'py ahaṃ karomīti manyate | atha ātma-samavetatayā sarva-loka-prasiddhe karmaṇi nadī-kula-stheṣv iva gatiḥ pratilaumyena | ato 'karma karmābhāvaṃ yathā-bhūtaṃ gaty-abhāvam iva vṛkṣeṣu yaḥ paśyet | akarmaṇi ca kārya-karaṇa-vyāpāroparame karmavad ātmany adhyāropite tūṣṇīm akurvan sukham āse ity ahaṅkārābhisandhi-hetutvāt tasminn akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ paśyet | ya evaṃ karmākarma-vibhāgajñaḥ sa buddhimān paṇḍito manuṣyeṣu | sa yukto yogī kṛtsna-karma-kṛc ca | so 'śubhān mokṣitaḥ kṛta-kṛtyo bhavatīty arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And here, action — being nothing but action, residing in body, senses, and their substrate — is superimposed by everyone upon the Self, which is free from action and unchanging. Because even a learned person thinks 'I am acting.' Now, in action that is universally experienced as belonging to the self — as [one sees] movement in trees on a river bank [when one is moving] — in the opposite direction. Therefore, one who would see inaction, i.e., the absence of action, as it truly is — like the absence of movement in the trees — [that one is wise]. And in inaction, i.e., in the cessation of activity of body and sense-organs, which is superimposed upon the Self as though it were inaction — [thinking] 'I sit still doing nothing, I am happy' — since [such cessation] is the cause of ego-sense and purposeful intent, in that inaction one who would see action — [that one is wise]. One who thus knows the distinction between action and inaction, that one is wise, learned, among human beings. That one is a <s>yogin</s>, and the performer of all actions. That one is freed from evil; that one has accomplished all that is to be accomplished — this is the meaning.

children.text:
ayaṃ śloko 'nyathā vyākhyātaḥ kaiścit | katham ? nityānāṃ kila karmaṇām īśvarārthe 'nuṣṭhīyamānānāṃ tat-phalābhāvād akarmāṇi tāny ucyante gauṇyā vṛttyā | teṣāṃ cākaraṇam akarma | tac ca pratyavāya-phalatvāt karmocyate gauṇyaiva vṛttyā | tatra nitye karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyet phalābhāvāt | yathā dhenur api gaur agaur ucyate kṣīrākhyaṃ phalaṃ na prayacchatīti tadvat | tathā nityākaraṇe tv akarmaṇi karmaḥ āśyen narakādi-pratyavāya-phalaṃ prayacchatīti | naitad yuktaṃ vyākhyānam | evaṃ-jñānād aśubhān mokṣānupapatteḥ | yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt [Gītā 4.16] iti bhagavatoktaṃ vacanaṃ bodhyeta | katham ? nityānām anuṣṭhānād aśubhāt syān nāma mokṣaṇam | na tu teṣāṃ phalābhāva-jñānāt | na hi nityānāṃ phalābhāva-jñānam aśubha-mukti-phalatvena
coditaṃ nitya-karma-jñānaṃ vā | na ca bhagavativehoktam |
children.translated_text:
This verse has been interpreted otherwise by some. How? They say that obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) actions, when performed for the sake of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), are called '<s>akarma</s>' (non-action) in a secondary sense, because they produce no fruit. And the non-performance of those [obligatory actions] is '<s>akarma</s>' (non-action); and that too is called '<s>karma</s>' (action) in a secondary sense, because it produces the fruit of sin (<s>pratyavāya</s>). Therein, 'one who sees <s>akarma</s> in <s>karma</s>' — who sees fruitlessness in obligatory action — just as a barren cow is also called 'cow' though she does not yield the fruit called milk — similarly. And in the non-performance of obligatory action, which is '<s>akarma</s>' (non-action), one should see '<s>karma</s>' — [i.e.,] it yields the fruit of punishment such as hell etc. This interpretation is not valid. Because liberation from evil (<s>aśubha</s>) is not possible from such knowledge. The statement of the Blessed Lord — 'knowing which you shall be freed from evil' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.16] — should be considered. How? From the performance of obligatory actions, there may indeed be liberation from evil; but not from the knowledge of their fruitlessness. For the knowledge of the fruitlessness of obligatory actions has not been enjoined as having the fruit of liberation from evil,
nor has the knowledge of obligatory action [been so enjoined]. And this is not stated by the Blessed Lord here.

children.text: etenākarmaṇi karma-darśanaṃ pratyuktam | na hy akarmaṇi karmeti darśanaṃ kartavyatayeha codyate, nityasya tu kartavyatā-mātram | na cākaraṇān nityasya pratyavāyo bhavatīti vijñānāt kiṃcit phalaṃ syāt | nāpi nityākaraṇaṃ jñeyatvena coditam | nāpi karmākarmeti mithā-darśanād aśubhān mokṣaṇam | buddhimattvaṃ, yuktatā, kṛtsna-karma-kṛttvādi ca phalam upapadyate stutir vā | mithyā-jñānam eva hi sākṣād aśubha-rūpaṃ kuto 'nyasmād aśubhān mokṣaṇam ? na hi tamas tamaso nivartakaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: By this, the 'seeing of <s>karma</s> in <s>akarma</s>' [interpretation] is also refuted. For the seeing of '<s>karma</s>' in '<s>akarma</s>' is not enjoined here as something that must be done; rather, only the obligatoriness of the obligatory [action] itself [is enjoined]. Nor would any fruit result from the knowledge that non-performance of the obligatory [action] leads to sin (<s>pratyavāya</s>). Nor is the non-performance of the obligatory [action] enjoined as something to be known. Nor does liberation from evil result from the false seeing [that takes] action and non-action [in a secondary sense]. But the fruits of being wise, being disciplined, and being a performer of all actions — these are justified [as results of the correct interpretation], or [the verse serves as] a eulogy. For false knowledge itself is directly of the nature of evil — whence then liberation from evil through something else [based on false knowledge]? For darkness cannot remove darkness.

children.text:
nanu karmaṇi yad akarma-darśanam akarmaṇi vā karma-darśanaṃ, na tan-mithyā-jñānam | kiṃ tarhi gauṇaṃ phala-bhāvābhāva-nimittam ? na, karmākarma-vijñānād api gauṇāt phalasyāśravaṇāt | nāpi śruta-hānya-śruta-parikalpanayā kaścid viśeṣo labhyate | sva-śabdenāpi śakyaṃ vaktuṃ nitya-karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ nāsty akaraṇāc ca teṣāṃ naraka-pātaḥ syād iti | tatra vyājena para-vyāmoha-rūpeṇa karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed ity ādinā kim ? tatraiva vyācakṣāṇena bhagavatoktaṃ vākyaṃ loka-vyāmohārtham iti vyaktaṃ kalpitaṃ syāt | na caitac chadma-rūpeṇa vākyena rakṣaṇīyaṃ vastu, nāpi śabdāntareṇa punaḥ punar ucyamānaṃ subodhaṃ syād ity evaṃ vaktuṃ yuktam | karmaṇy evādhikāras te [Gītā 2.47] ity atra hi sphuṭatara ukto 'rtho na punar vaktavyo bhavati | sarvatra ca praśastaṃ
boddhavyaṃ ca kartavyam eva, na niṣprayojanaṃ boddhavyam ity ucyate |
children.translated_text:
Objection: The seeing of non-action in action, or of action in non-action, is not false knowledge — rather, it is secondary [metaphorical], based on the presence or absence of fruit. Reply: No, because even from the secondary knowledge of action and non-action, no fruit is heard [in scripture to result]. Nor is any advantage gained by fabricating what is not heard [in scripture] at the expense of what is heard. For it is possible to state in direct terms: 'Obligatory actions have no fruit, and from their non-performance there is a fall into hell.' In that case, what purpose is served by the device — which is of the nature of confusing others — of saying 'one who sees <s>akarma</s> in <s>karma</s>' etc.? For the commentator who explains [the verse] in this way would clearly be fabricating [the claim] that the Blessed Lord's statement was intended to confuse the world. And it is not proper that a matter requiring protection should be [expressed] through a deceptive statement; nor is it proper to say that what is repeatedly stated in other words would be easier to understand — [for that would be redundant]. Since in '<s>karmaṇy evādhikāras te</s>' (your right is to action alone) [<s>Gītā</s> 2.47], the meaning was already stated most clearly and need not be restated. And everywhere, what is praiseworthy
and worthy of being understood is something that must actually be done — it is not said that what is purposeless should be understood.

children.text: na ca mithyā-jñānaṃ boddhavyaṃ bhavati tat-pratyupasthāpitaṃ vā vastv-ābhāsam | nāpi nityānām akaraṇād abhāvāt prayavāya-bhāvotpattiḥ | nāsato vidyate bhāvo [Gītā 2.16] iti vacanāt | tat-katham asataḥ saj jāyate [ChāU 6.2.2] iti ca darśitam | asataḥ saj-janma-pratiṣedhād asataḥ sad-utpattiṃ bruvatā 'sad eva sad bhavet | sac cāsad bhaved ity uktaṃ syāt | tac cāyuktaṃ, sarva-pramāṇa-virodhāt | na ca niṣphalaṃ vidadhyāt karma śāstraṃ duḥkha-svarūpatvāt | duḥkhasya ca buddhi-pūrvakatayā kāryatvānupapatteḥ | tad-akaraṇe ca naraka-pātābhyupagame 'narthāyaiva | ubhayathāpi karaṇe 'karaṇe ca śāstraṃ niṣphalaṃ kalpitaṃ syāt | svābhyupagama-virodhaś ca nityaṃ niṣphalaṃ karmety abhyupagamya mokṣa-phalāyeti bruvataḥ | tasmād yathā-śruta evārthaḥ karmaṇy akarma ya ity ādeḥ | tathā ca vyākhyāto
'smābhiḥ ślokaḥ ||BhGS_4.18||
children.translated_text: And thus has this verse been explained by us. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.18 //

And false knowledge cannot be something worthy of being understood, nor the semblance of reality produced by it. Nor does the coming-into-being of the [fruit of] sin (<s>pratyavāya</s>) arise from the non-existence [of the performance] of the obligatory — because of the statement 'of the non-existent there is no coming into being' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.16]. And it has been shown: 'How can the existent arise from the non-existent?' [<s>ChāU</s> 6.2.2]. By denying the birth of the existent from the non-existent, one who asserts that the existent arises from the non-existent would be saying that the non-existent becomes existent, and that the existent becomes non-existent — and that is unjustified, because it contradicts all means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Nor would scripture enjoin action that is fruitless, since [action] is of the nature of suffering. And it is not possible for suffering to be something to be intentionally brought about, since it is done with deliberate purpose (<s>buddhi-pūrvaka</s>). And if non-performance leads to a fall into hell, that too would be for the sake of misfortune alone. In both cases — whether one performs or does not perform — scripture would be rendered purposeless. And there would be a contradiction with one's own position: for having accepted that obligatory action is fruitless, one then claims it leads to the fruit of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Therefore, the meaning of 'one who sees <s>akarma</s> in <s>karma</s>' etc. is just as stated [literally].

children.text: tad etat karmaṇy akarmādi-darśanaṃ stūyate -
children.translated_text: This seeing of non-action in action etc. is now praised —

children.text: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṃkalpa-varjitāḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose every undertaking is free from desire and willful resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>),

children.text: jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṃ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ ||BhG_4.19||
children.translated_text: whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge — him the wise call a <s>paṇḍita</s> (learned one). // <s>BhG</s> 4.19 //

children.text: yasya yathokta-darśinaḥ sarve yāvantaḥ samārambhāḥ karmāṇi samārabhyanta iti samārambhāḥ | kāma-saṃkalpa-varjitāḥ kāmaistat-kāraṇaiś ca saṅkalpa-varjitā mudhaiva ceṣṭā-mātrā anuṣṭhīyante | pravṛttena cel loka-saṅgrahārthaṃ, nivṛttena cej jīvana-mātrārthaṃ, taṃ jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṃ karmādāv akarmādi-darśanaṃ jñānaṃ, tad evāgnis tena jñānāgninā dagdhāni śubhāśubha-lakṣaṇāni karmāṇi yasya | tam āhuḥ paramārthataḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ brahma-vidaḥ ||BhGS_4.19||
children.translated_text: Of one who has the aforementioned vision — all of his undertakings (<s>samārambha</s>), all actions that are initiated — are free from desire and the resolves (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) that are its cause. They are performed as mere activity, purposelessly. If [the person is] one who is [still] engaged [in action], it is for the sake of the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>); if [he is] one who has withdrawn, it is merely for the sake of sustaining life. Him — one whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge (<s>jñānāgni-dagdha-karman</s>): the seeing of non-action etc. in action etc. is the knowledge; that itself is the fire; by that fire of knowledge, the actions characterized as merit and demerit (<s>śubhāśubha</s>) have been burned — him the wise (<s>budha</s>), the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, call a <s>paṇḍita</s> (learned one) in the truest sense. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.19 //

children.text: yas tu karmādāv akarmādi-darśī so 'karmādi-darśanād eva niṣkarmā sannyāsī jīvana-mātrārtha-ceṣṭaḥ san karmaṇi na pravartate, yadyapi prāg-vivekataḥ pravṛttaḥ | yas tu prārabdha-karmā sann uttara-kālam utpannātma-samyag-darśanaḥ syāt, sa sarva-karmaṇi prayojanam apaśyan sa-sādhanaṃ karma pariyajaty eva | sa kutaścin nimittāt karma-parityāgāsambhave sati karmaṇi tat-phale ca saṅga-rahitatayā sva-prayojanābhāvāl loka-saṅgrahārthaṃ pūrvavat karmaṇi pravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃcit karoti jñānāgni-dagdha-karmatvāt tadīyaṃ karmākarmaiva sampadyata ity etam arthaṃ darśayiṣyann āha -
children.translated_text: Now, one who sees non-action etc. in action — by virtue of that very seeing — becomes a non-doer (<s>niṣkarmā</s>), a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), one who exerts himself only for the maintenance of the body, and does not engage in action, even though he was previously engaged [in action] before [the arising of] discrimination. But one who, having already commenced actions, subsequently attains right knowledge of the Self — he, seeing no purpose in any action, renounces all action along with its means. If, for some reason, the complete renunciation of action is not possible, then, being free from attachment to action and its fruits, having no purpose of his own — though engaged in action as before, for the sake of the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) — he does nothing at all, because his actions are burned by the fire of knowledge. His action becomes non-action itself. Wishing to show this meaning, He says —

children.text: tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṃ nitya-tṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action, ever content, without dependence,

children.text: karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃcit karoti saḥ ||BhG_4.20||
children.translated_text: even though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all. // <s>BhG</s> 4.20 //

children.text: tyaktvā karmasv abhimānaṃ phalāsaṅgaṃ ca yathoktena jñānena nitya-tṛpto nirākāṅkṣo viṣayeṣv ity arthaḥ | nirāśraya āśraya-rahitaḥ | āśrayo nāma yad āśritya puruṣārthaṃ sisādhayiṣati | dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-phala-sādhanāśraya-rahita ity arthaḥ | viduṣā kriyamāṇaṃ karma paramārthato 'karmaiva | tasya niṣkriyātma-darśana-sampannatvāt | tenaivambhūtena sva-prayojanābhāvāt sa-sādhanaṃ karma parityaktavyam eveti prāpte, tato nirgamāsambhavāl loka-saṅgraha-cikīrṣayā śiṣṭa-vigarhaṇāparijihīrṣayā vā pūrvavat karmaṇy-abhipravṛtto 'pi niṣkryātma-darśana-sampannatvān naiva kiṃcit karoti saḥ ||BhGS_4.20||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the sense of doership in actions and the attachment to fruits — through the knowledge described — ever content (<s>nitya-tṛpta</s>), free from craving for sense-objects — this is the meaning. Without dependence (<s>nirāśraya</s>) — devoid of any support. 'Support' (<s>āśraya</s>) means that depending on which one seeks to accomplish the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). [He is] devoid of dependence on any means to seen or unseen fruits — this is the meaning. The action performed by the wise one is, in the ultimate sense, non-action itself — because he has attained the vision of the actionless Self. Therefore, though such a person, having no purpose of his own, should renounce all action along with its means — when departure from [the world of action] is not possible, due to his desire for the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) or his wish to avoid the censure of the righteous — even though fully engaged in action as before, he does nothing at all, because he has attained the vision of the actionless Self. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.20 //

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ pūrvokta-viparītaḥ prāg eva karmāmbhād brahmaṇi sarvāntare pratyag-ātmani niṣkriye saṃjātātma-darśanaḥ, sa dṛṣṭādṛṣṭeṣṭa-viṣayāśīr vivarjitatayā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭārthe karmaṇi prayojanam apyaśyan sa-sādhanaṃ karma saṃnyasya śarīra-yātrā-mātra-ceṣṭo yatir jñāna-niṣṭho mucyata iti | etad arthaṃ darśayitum āha-
children.translated_text: On the other hand, one who is the opposite of the aforementioned — who, prior to [commencing] the ocean of action, has attained the vision of the Self in <s>Brahman</s>, the inner Self of all, which is actionless — he, being free from expectations directed toward seen and unseen objects, seeing no purpose in any action directed toward seen or unseen ends, renounces all action along with its means, and, being a renunciant (<s>yati</s>), exerting himself merely for the maintenance of the body, established in the steadfastness of knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>), is liberated. To show this meaning, He says —

children.text: nirāśīr yata-cittātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Free from expectations (<s>nirāśīḥ</s>), with mind and body restrained, having abandoned all possessions,

children.text: śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam ||BhG_4.21||
children.translated_text: performing action merely for the [maintenance of the] body alone, he incurs no sin. // <s>BhG</s> 4.21 //

children.text: nirāśīr nirgatā āśiṣo yasmāt sa nirāśīḥ | yata-cittātmā cittam antaḥ-karaṇam | ātmā bāhyaḥ kārya-karaṇa-saṃghātaḥ | tāv ubhāv api yatau saṃyatau yasya sa yata-cittātmā | tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ - tyaktaḥ sarvaḥ parigraho yena sa tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ | śārīraṃ śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ kevalaṃ tatrāpi abhimāna-varjitaṃ karma kurvan | nāpnoti na prāpnoti kilbiṣam aniṣṭa-rūpaṃ pāpaṃ dharmaṃ ca | dharmo 'pi mumukṣor aniṣṭa-rūpaṃ kilbiṣam eva | bandhāpādakatvāt | tasmāt tābhyāṃ mukto bhavati, saṃsārān mukto bhavatīty arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirāśīḥ</s>' — one from whom expectations (<s>āśīḥ</s>) have departed. '<s>Yata-cittātmā</s>' — '<s>citta</s>' is the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>); '<s>ātmā</s>' is the external aggregate of body and senses; both of these being restrained (<s>yata</s>) — one whose mind and body are restrained. '<s>Tyakta-sarva-parigraha</s>' — one by whom all possessions have been abandoned. Performing action merely for the sake of bodily maintenance alone (<s>śārīra</s>) — and even therein, free from the sense of doership — '<s>kevala</s>' [signifies this]. He does not incur (<s>nāpnoti</s>) sin (<s>kilbiṣa</s>) — [i.e., he incurs] neither demerit (<s>pāpa</s>) nor merit (<s>dharma</s>). For even merit (<s>dharma</s>) is sin (<s>kilbiṣa</s>) for one who seeks liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), because it produces bondage. Therefore, he becomes free from both — free from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) — this is the meaning.

children.text:
kiṃ ca śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karmety atra kiṃ śarīra-nirvartyaṃ śārīraṃ karmābhipretam ? āho svic charīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ śārīraṃ karma ? iti | kiṃ cāto yadi śarīra-nirvartyaṃ śārīraṃ karma yadi vā śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ śarīram ? iti | ucyate -- yadā śarīra-nirvartyaṃ karma śārīram abhipretaṃ syāt tadā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-prayojanaṃ karma pratiṣiddham api śarīreṇa kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam iti bruvato viruddhābhidhānaṃ prasajyeta | śāstrīyaṃ ca karma dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-prayojanaṃ śarīreṇa kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam ity api bruvato 'prāpta-pratiṣedha-prasaṅgaḥ | śārīraṃ karma kurvan iti viśeṣaṇāt kevala-śabda-prayogāc ca vāṅ-manasa-nirvartyaṃ karma vidhi-pratiṣedha-viṣayaṃ dharmādharma-śabda-vācyaṃ kurvan prāpnoti kilbiṣam ity uktaṃ syāt
|
children.translated_text:
Furthermore, regarding '<s>śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma</s>' (action merely for the body) — is the intended meaning action that is accomplished by the body, or action whose purpose is merely the maintenance of the body? And what follows from each? It is said: if the intended meaning were action accomplished by the body, then the absurd consequence would arise that [the text] makes the contradictory statement: 'one who performs even prohibited action that has seen and unseen purposes, using the body, incurs no sin.' And if [the text meant] 'one who performs scriptural action having seen and unseen purposes with the body incurs no sin,' there would be the fallacy of prohibiting what has not been established [as problematic]. Since the qualification 'bodily action' and the use of the word '<s>kevala</s>' (merely) [are present], it would be implied that one who performs action accomplished by speech and mind — action that is the subject of injunctions and prohibitions, denoted by the words '<s>dharma</s>' and '<s>adharma</s>' —
incurs sin.

children.text: tatrāpi vāṅ-manasābhyāṃ vihitānuṣṭhāna-pakṣe kilbiṣa-prāpti-vacanaṃ viruddham āpadyeta | pratiṣiddha-sevi-pakṣe 'pi bhūtārthānuvāda-mātram anarthakaṃ syāt | yadā tu śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ śārīraṃ karmābhipretaṃ bhavet, tadā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-prayojanaṃ karma vidhi-pratiṣedha-gamyaṃ śarīra-vāṅ-manasa-nirvartyam anyad akruvaṃs tair eva śarīrādibhiḥ śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ kevala-śabda-prayogāt ahaṃ karomi ity abhimāna-varjitaḥ śarīrādi-ceṣṭā-mātraṃ loka-dṛṣṭyā kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam | evambhūtasya pāpa-śabda-vācya-kilbiṣa-prāpty-asambhavāt kilbiṣaṃ saṃsāraṃ nāpnoti | jñānāgni-dagdha-sarva-karmatvād apratibandhena mucyate eveti pūrvokta-samyag-darśana-phalānuvāda evaiṣaḥ | evaṃ śarīraṃ kevalaṃ karma ity asyārthasya parigrahe
niravadyaṃ bhavati ||BhGS_4.21||
children.translated_text: Thus, this interpretation of '<s>śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma</s>' is faultless. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.21 //

Even therein, in the case of performing what is enjoined by speech and mind, the statement that one incurs sin would be contradictory. And in the case of engaging in what is prohibited, it would be a mere purposeless restatement of what is already known. But when the intended meaning is action whose purpose is merely the maintenance of the body — then, not performing any other action that has seen or unseen purposes, that is ascertained through injunctions and prohibitions, that is accomplished by body, speech, and mind — but performing, with those very [instruments] of body etc., action whose purpose is merely bodily maintenance, free from the sense of doership because of the word '<s>kevala</s>' (merely), performing merely the activity of body etc. from the standpoint of the world — he incurs no sin. Since it is impossible for one of this nature to incur sin denoted by the word '<s>pāpa</s>' — he does not incur sin, i.e., <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). Because all his actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge, he is liberated without obstruction — this is merely a restatement of the fruit of the aforementioned right knowledge.

children.text: tyakta-sarva-parigrahasya yater annādeḥ śarīra-sthiti-hetorḥ parigrahasyābhāvād yācanādinā śarīra-sthitau kartavyatāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ ayācitam asaṃk ptam upapannaṃ yadṛcchayā [Mbh 14.46.19; Baudhayana-dharma-sūtra 21.8.12] ity ādinā vacanenānujñātaṃ yateḥ śarīra-sthiti-hetor annādeḥ prāpti-dvāram āviṣkurvann āha -
children.translated_text: For the renunciant (<s>yati</s>) who has abandoned all possessions, since there is an absence of possessions such as food etc. that are the means of bodily maintenance — when the question arises of the need for sustenance through begging and the like — making known the means of obtaining food etc. for the renunciant's bodily maintenance, which is sanctioned by the statement 'what comes unsought, unplanned, arrived of its own accord' [<s>MBh</s> 14.46.19; <s>Baudhāyana-dharma-sūtra</s> 21.8.12] etc., He says —

children.text: yadṛcchā-lābha-santuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Content with what comes of its own accord, transcending the pairs of opposites, free from envy,

children.text: samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate ||BhG_4.22||
children.translated_text: equal in success and failure — even having acted, he is not bound. // <s>BhG</s> 4.22 //

children.text:
yadṛcchā-lābha-santuṣṭaḥ prārthitopanato lābho yadṛcchā-lābhaḥ, tena santuṣṭaḥ saṃjātālaṃ-pratyayaḥ | dvandvātīto dvandvaiḥ śītoṣṇādibhir hanyamāno 'py aviṣaṇṇa-citto dvandvātīta ucyate | vimatsaro vigata-matsaro nirvaira-buddhiḥ | samas tulyo yadṛcchā-lābhasya siddhāv asiddhau ca, ya evambhūto yatir annādeḥ śarīra-sthiti-hetor lābhālābhayoḥ samo harṣa-viṣāda-varjitaḥ, karmādāv akarmādi-darśī, yathā-bhūtātma-darśana-niṣṭhaḥ san śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojane bhikṣāṭanādi-karmaṇi śarīrādi-nirvartye naiva kiṃcit karomīti [Gītā 5.8] guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta [Gītā 3.28] ity evaṃ sadā samparicakṣāṇa ātmanaḥ kartṛtvābhāvaṃ paśyann eva kiṃcid bhikṣāṭanādikaṃ karma karoti | loka-vyavahāra-sāmānya-darśanena tu laukikair āropita-kartṛtve
bhikṣāṭanādau karmaṇi kartā bhavati | svānubhavena tu śāstra-pramāṇādi-janitenākartraiva | sa evaṃ parādhyāropita-kartṛtvaṃ śarīra-sthiti-mātra-prayojanaṃ bhikṣāṭanādikaṃ karma kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate, bandha-hetoḥ karmaṇaḥ sahetukasya jñānāgninā dagdhatvād ity uktānuvāda evaiṣaḥ ||BhGS_4.22||
children.translated_text: Content with whatever comes by chance — a gain that arrives without being sought is a chance-gain (<s>yadṛcchā-lābha</s>); one who is content with it has attained the feeling of 'this is enough.' Beyond the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandvātīta</s>) — even when afflicted by pairs of opposites such as cold and heat, one whose mind is not dejected is called 'beyond the pairs of opposites.' Free from envy (<s>vimatsara</s>) — one from whom envy has departed, one whose mind is free from enmity. Equal (<s>sama</s>) — the same in success and failure regarding whatever comes by chance. One who is thus — a renunciant (<s>yati</s>) who is equal in gain and loss of food and other necessities for bodily sustenance, free from joy and sorrow, who sees non-action in action and so forth, being established in the vision of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as it truly is, even while performing actions such as going about for alms which serve merely the purpose of bodily sustenance and which are accomplished by the body and its instruments — he always reflects thus: 'I do not do anything at all' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.8], 'the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) act upon the <s>guṇas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.28], seeing the absence of agency in himself, he performs some action such as going about for alms. However, from the standpoint of ordinary worldly observation, agency is superimposed upon him by worldly people, and he becomes an agent in actions such as going about for alms. But from his own experience, born of scripture and other valid means of knowledge, he is verily a non-agent. He, though performing actions such as going about for alms — actions whose agency is superimposed by others and which serve merely the purpose of bodily sustenance — is not bound, because the action that is the cause of bondage, together with its cause, has been burnt by the fire of knowledge (<s>jñānāgni</s>). This is merely a restatement of what has already been said.
[Section break]

children.text: tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṃ [Gītā 4.20] ity anena ślokena yaḥ prārabdha-karmā san yadā niṣkriya-brahmātma-darśana-sampannaḥ syāt tadā tasyātmanaḥ kartṛ-karma-prayojanābhāva-darśinaḥ karma-parityāge prāpte kutaścin nimittāt tad-asambhave sati pūrvavat tasmin karmaṇy abhipravṛttasyāpi naiva kiṃcit karoti sa [Gītā 4.20] itikarmābhāvaḥ pradarśitaḥ | yasyaivaṃ karmābhāvo darśitas tasyaiva -
children.translated_text: By the verse 'Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.20], it was shown that when one who has already commenced action becomes endowed with the vision of the actionless <s>Brahman</s> as the Self, then, for him who sees the absence of agency, action, and purpose in the Self, when the occasion for abandoning action arises, but that is not possible for some reason, even though he continues to engage in that action as before — 'he does not do anything at all' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.20] — thus the absence of action was demonstrated. For the very one for whom the absence of action has been shown —

children.text: gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-cetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: For one whose attachment has departed, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge,

children.text: yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate ||BhG_4.23||
children.translated_text: Who acts for the sake of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) alone, all <s>karma</s> (action) completely dissolves.

children.text: gata-saṅgasya sarvato nivṛttāsakter muktasya nivṛtta-dharmādharmādi-bandhanasya, jñānāvasthita-cetaso jñāna evāvasthitaṃ ceto yasya so 'yaṃ jñānāvasthita-cetāḥ | tasya yajñāya yajña-nirvṛtty-artham ācarato nirvartayataḥ karma samagraṃ sahāgreṇa phalena vartata iti samagraṃ karma tat-samagraṃ pravilīyate vinaśyatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.23||
children.translated_text: For one whose attachment has departed (<s>gata-saṅga</s>) — whose clinging has completely ceased in all respects; who is liberated (<s>mukta</s>) — freed from the bondage of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the like; whose mind is established in knowledge (<s>jñānāvasthita-cetas</s>) — one whose mind (<s>cetas</s>) is established in knowledge alone, he is called 'one whose mind is established in knowledge.' For him, who acts for the sake of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) — for the purpose of accomplishing sacrifice, who performs action — all action completely (<s>samagram</s>), that is, together with its fruit, dissolves (<s>pravilīyate</s>) — meaning, it perishes.
[Section break]

children.text: kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt kriyamāṇaṃ karma svakāryārambham akurvat samagraṃ pravilīyata ity ucyate ? yataḥ -
children.translated_text: For what reason does action, even when being performed, not initiate its own effect and completely dissolve? It is said — because:

children.text: brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the offering-instrument, <s>Brahman</s> is the oblation, by <s>Brahman</s> is it offered into the fire of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahma-karma-samādhinā ||BhG_4.24||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached by him who contemplates <s>Brahman</s> in action.

children.text: brahmārpaṇaṃ yena karaṇena brahmavid havir agnāv arpayati | tad brahmaiveti paśyati tasyātma-vyatirekeṇābhāvaṃ paśyati | yathā śuktikāyāṃ rajatābhāvaṃ paśyati tad ucyate brahmaivārpaṇam iti | yathā yad rajataṃ tac chuktikaiveti | brahma arpaṇam ity asamaste pade yad-arpaṇa-buddhyā gṛhyate loke tad asya brahma-vido brahmaivety arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the offering-instrument (<s>brahmārpaṇam</s>) — the instrument by which the knower of <s>Brahman</s> offers the oblation into the fire; he sees that as <s>Brahman</s> alone, he sees its non-existence apart from the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). Just as one sees the non-existence of silver in a mother-of-pearl shell — that is what is meant by '<s>Brahman</s> alone is the offering-instrument.' Just as: 'that which is silver is nothing but the shell itself.' '<s>Brahman</s>' and '<s>arpaṇam</s>' (offering-instrument) — taking the words separately — what is apprehended in the world as the offering-instrument, that, for this knower of <s>Brahman</s>, is <s>Brahman</s> alone — this is the meaning.

children.text: brahma havis tathā yad dhavir buddhyā gṛhyamāṇaṃ tad brahmaivāsay | tathā brahmāgnau iti samastaṃ padam | agnir api brahmaiva | yatra hūyate brahmaṇā kartrā brahmaiva kartety arthaḥ | yat tena hutaṃ havana-kriyā tad brahmaiva | yat tena gantavyaṃ phalaṃ tad api brahmaiva | brahma-karma-samādhinā brahmaiva karma brahma-karma tasmin samādhir yasya sa brahma-karma-samādhis tena brahma-karma-samādhinā brahmaiva gantavyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the oblation (<s>havis</s>) — likewise, what is apprehended as the oblation, that too is <s>Brahman</s> alone for him. Similarly, '<s>brahmāgnau</s>' (in the fire of <s>Brahman</s>) is a compound word — the fire too is <s>Brahman</s> alone; where the offering is made, by <s>Brahman</s> as the agent — meaning, <s>Brahman</s> alone is the agent. That which is offered by him — the act of offering — that too is <s>Brahman</s> alone. That which is to be reached (<s>gantavyam</s>) by him — the fruit — that too is <s>Brahman</s> alone. By <s>brahma-karma-samādhi</s> (one whose absorption is in <s>Brahman</s> as action) — <s>Brahman</s> alone is action, hence <s>brahma-karma</s>; <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) in that is <s>brahma-karma-samādhi</s>; by such <s>brahma-karma-samādhi</s>, <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached.

children.text: evaṃ loka-saṅgrahaṃ cikīrṣuṇāpi kriyamāṇaṃ karam, paramārthato 'karma brahma-buddhy-upamṛditvāt | evaṃ sati nivṛtta-karmaṇo 'pi sarva-karma-sannyāsinaḥ samyag-darśana-stuty-arthaṃ yajñatva-sampādanaṃ jñānasya sutarām upapadyate | yad-arpaṇādy-adhiyajñe prasiddhaṃ tad asyādhyātmaṃ brahmaiva paramārtha-darśina iti | anyathā sarvasya brahmatve 'rpaṇādīnām eva viśeṣato brahmatvābhidhānam anarthakaṃ syāt | tasmād brahmaivedaṃ sarvam ity abhijānato viduṣaḥ sarva-karmābhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, even when action is performed by one who desires the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṅgraha</s>), it is, in the highest sense, non-action, because it is sublated by the cognition of <s>Brahman</s>. This being the case, the attribution of the character of sacrifice to knowledge — for the purpose of praising right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>) even for one who has renounced all actions, one from whom action has ceased — is all the more fitting. What is well-known in the context of the external sacrifice (<s>adhiyajña</s>) as the offering-instrument and so forth, that, for one who sees the highest reality, is <s>Brahman</s> alone in the context of the Self (<s>adhyātma</s>). Otherwise, if everything were already <s>Brahman</s>, then the specific mention of the offering-instrument and other components as <s>Brahman</s> would be meaningless. Therefore, for the wise one who realizes '<s>Brahman</s> alone is all this,' there is the absence of all action.

children.text: kāraka-buddhy-abhāvāc ca | nahi kāraka-buddhi-rahitaṃ yajñākhyaṃ karma dṛṣṭam | sarvam evāgni-hotrādikaṃ karma śabda-samarpita-devatā-viśeṣa-sampradānādi-kāraka-buddhimat-kartr-abhimāna-phalābhisandhimac ca dṛṣṭam | nopamṛdita-kriyākāraka-phala-bheda-buddhimat kartṛtvābhimāna-phalābhisandhi-rahitaṃ vā | idaṃ tu brahma-buddhy-upamṛditārpaṇādi-kāraka-kriyā-phala-bheda-buddhi karmāto 'karmaiva tat |
children.translated_text: And because of the absence of the cognition of instrumental factors (<s>kāraka</s>). For no action called sacrifice has ever been seen that is devoid of the cognition of instrumental factors. Every action such as the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-ritual) and others is seen to be accompanied by the cognition of instrumental factors — such as the particular deity designated by the Vedic word, the recipient, and so forth — and accompanied by the sense of agency in the performer and the intention toward a result. It is never seen to be accompanied by the sublation of the distinctions of action, instrumental factors, and result, nor devoid of the sense of agency and intention toward a result. But this action, in which the cognition of the distinctions of instrumental factors such as the offering-instrument and others, of action and result, is sublated by the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> — that is therefore non-action alone.

children.text: tathā ca darśitaṃ karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyet [Gītā 4.18], karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃcit karoti saḥ [Gītā 4.20], guṇā guṇeṣu vartante [Gītā 3.28], naiva kiṃcit karomīti yukto manyeta tattvavit [Gītā 5.8] ity ādibhiḥ | tathā ca darśayaṃs tatra tatra kriyā-kāraka-phala-bheda-buddhy-upamardaṃ karoti | dṛṣṭā ca kāmyāgnihotrādau kāmopamardena kāmyāgnihotrādi-hāniḥ | tathā mati-pūrvakām atipūrvakādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ kārya-viśeṣasyārambhakatvaṃ dṛṣṭam | tathehāpi brahma-buddhy-upamṛditārpaṇādi-kāraka-kriyā-phala-bheda-buddher bāhya-ceṣṭā-mātreṇa karmāpi viduṣo 'karma sampadyate | ata uktaṃ samagraṃ pravilīyate [Gītā 4.23] iti |
children.translated_text: And thus it has been shown: 'He who would see inaction in action' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.18], 'Though engaged in action, he does not do anything at all' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.20], 'The <s>guṇas</s> act upon the <s>guṇas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 3.28], 'The knower of truth should think, I do not do anything at all' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.8] — and so on. And thus, demonstrating this in each context, he effects the sublation of the cognition of the distinctions of action, instrumental factors, and result. And it is seen that in the case of the desire-motivated <s>agnihotra</s> and the like, when the desire is sublated, the desire-motivated <s>agnihotra</s> and the like are destroyed. Similarly, it is seen that actions performed deliberately (<s>mati-pūrvakam</s>) and others are capable of initiating specific effects. Likewise here too, when the cognition of the distinctions of instrumental factors such as the offering-instrument and others, of action and result, is sublated by the cognition of <s>Brahman</s>, even the action of the wise one, which consists of mere external bodily movement, becomes non-action. Therefore it is said, 'all of it completely dissolves' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.23].

children.text:
atra kecid āhuḥ - yad brahma tad arpaṇādīni | brahmaiva kilārpaṇādinā pañca-vidhena kārakātmanā vyavasthitaṃ sat tad eva karma karoti | tatra nārpaṇādi-buddhir nivartyate | kintv arpaṇādiṣu brahma-buddhir ādhīyate | yathā pratimādau viṣṇv-ādi-buddhiḥ, yathā vā nāmādau brahma-buddhir iti | satyam evam api syād yadi jñāna-yajña-stuty-arthaṃ prakaraṇaṃ na syāt | atra tu samyag-darśanaṃ jñāna-yajña-śabditam anekān yajña-śabditān kriyā-viśeṣān upanyasya śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa [Gītā 4.33] iti jñānaṃ stauti | atra ca samartham idaṃ vacanaṃ brahmārpaṇam ity ādi jñānasya yajñatva-sampādane, anyathā sarvasya brahmatve 'rpaṇādīnām eva viśeṣato brahmatvābhidhānam anarthakaṃ syāt | ye tv arpaṇādiṣu pratimāyāṃ viṣṇu-dṛṣṭivad brahma-dṛṣṭiḥ
kṣipyate | nāmādiṣv iva ceti bruvate, na teṣāṃ brahma-vidyokteha vivakṣitā syāt | arpaṇādi-viṣayatvāj jñānasya | na ca dṛṣṭi-sampādana-jñānena mokṣa-phalaṃ prāpyate | brahmaiva tena gantavyam iti cocyate |
children.translated_text: Here some say: that which is <s>Brahman</s>, that itself is the offering-instrument and the rest. <s>Brahman</s> itself, they claim, being established in a fivefold form as instrumental factors such as the offering-instrument and so on, performs that very action. In that case, the cognition of the offering-instrument and so forth is not negated; rather, the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> is superimposed upon the offering-instrument and the rest — just as the cognition of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is superimposed upon an idol, or just as the cognition of <s>Brahman</s> is superimposed upon name and the like. True, it could be so interpreted, if the context were not meant for praising the sacrifice of knowledge (<s>jñāna-yajña</s>). But here, right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>), designated by the term 'sacrifice of knowledge,' is being praised — after presenting many particular ritual actions designated by the word 'sacrifice,' it praises knowledge by saying 'Superior to the sacrifice of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, O <s>Parantapa</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.33]. And here, this statement beginning with '<s>brahmārpaṇam</s>' is effective in establishing the sacrificial character of knowledge; otherwise, if everything were already <s>Brahman</s>, the specific mention of the offering-instrument and the rest as <s>Brahman</s> would be meaningless. But those who say that the vision of <s>Brahman</s> is cast upon the offering-instrument and the rest — like the vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s> upon an idol, or like upon name and the rest — for them, the teaching of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-vidyā</s>) intended here would not apply, since knowledge would then have the offering-instrument and the rest as its objects. And through knowledge that merely effects a particular way of seeing, the fruit of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is not attained. Yet the text says, '<s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached by him.'

children.text: viruddhaṃ ca samyag-darśanam antareṇa mokṣa-phalaṃ prāpyata iti | prakṛti-virodhaś ca | samyag-darśanaṃ ca prakṛtaṃ karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyet [Gītā 4.18] ity atrānte ca samyag-darśanaṃ tasyaivopasaṃhārāt | śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa [Gītā 4.33] jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntiṃ [Gītā 4.39] ity ādinā samyag-darśana-stutim eva kurvann upakṣīṇo 'dhyāyaḥ | tatrākasmād arpaṇādau brahma-dṛṣṭir aprakaraṇe pratimāyām iva viṣṇu-dṛṣṭir ucyata ity anupapannam | tasmād yathā-vyākhyātārtha evāyaṃ ślokaḥ ||BhGS_4.24||
children.translated_text: And it would be contradictory to hold that the fruit of liberation is attained without right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>). There would also be a contradiction with the context. Right vision is the subject at hand, beginning with 'He who would see inaction in action' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.18], and at the end, right vision alone is concluded. The chapter draws to a close while praising right vision alone through statements such as 'Superior to the sacrifice of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, O <s>Parantapa</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.33], 'Having attained knowledge, one reaches supreme peace' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.39], and so on. Therefore, to say without cause that the vision of <s>Brahman</s> upon the offering-instrument and the rest — irrelevant to the context, like the vision of <s>Viṣṇu</s> upon an idol — is being taught here, is untenable. Therefore, this verse has the meaning just as we have explained it.
[Section break]

children.text: tatrādhunā samyag-darśanasya yajñatvaṃ sampādya tat-stuty-artham anye 'pi yajñā upakṣipyante -
children.translated_text: Now, having established the sacrificial character of right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>) and for the purpose of praising it, other sacrifices too are introduced —

children.text: daivam evāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Some <s>yogins</s> (practitioners) devoutly perform sacrifice to the gods alone,

children.text: brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati ||BhG_4.25||
children.translated_text: While others offer the self as sacrifice into the fire of <s>Brahman</s> by means of sacrifice itself.

children.text:
daivam eva devā ijyante yena yajñenāsau daivo yajñas tam evāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ karmiṇaḥ paryupāsate, kurvantīty arthaḥ | brahmāgnau satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma [TaittU 2.1] vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma [BAU 3.9.28], yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaraḥ [BAU 3.4.1], ity ādi vacanoktam aśanāyāpipāsādi-sarva-saṃsāra-dharma-varjitaṃ neti neti [BAU 4.4.22] iti nirastāśeṣa-viśeṣaṃ brahma-śabdenocyate | brahma ca tad-agniś ca sa homādhikaraṇatva-vivakṣayā brahmāgnis tasmin brahmāgnāv apare 'nye brahma-vido yajñaṃ yajña-śabda-vācya ātmā ātma-nāmasu yajña-śabdasya pāṭhāt [Nirukti 14.11] tam ātmānaṃ yajñaṃ paramārthataḥ param eva brahma santaṃ buddhyādy-upādhi-saṃyuktam adhyasta-sarvopādhi-dharmakam āhuti-rūpaṃ yajṇinaivātmanaivokta-lakṣaṇopajuhvati prakṣipanti,
sopādhikasyātmano nirupādhikena para-brahma-svarūpeṇaiva yad darśanaṃ, sa tasmin homas taṃ kurvanti, brahmātmaikatva-darśana-niṣṭhāḥ sannyāsina ity arthaḥ | so 'yaṃ samyag-darśana-lakṣaṇo yajño daiva-yajñādiṣu yajñeṣūpakṣipyante brahmārpaṇam ity ād-ślokaiḥ prastutaḥ śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa [Gītā 4.33] ity ādinā stuty-artham ||BhGS_4.25||
children.translated_text: The divine sacrifice (<s>daiva-yajña</s>) — that sacrifice by which the gods (<s>devāḥ</s>) are worshipped, that is the divine sacrifice; some other <s>yogins</s>, that is, performers of ritual action (<s>karmins</s>), devoutly perform (<s>paryupāsate</s>) that sacrifice — meaning, they carry it out. Into the fire of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmāgnau</s>) — <s>Brahman</s>, which is described in Vedic statements such as '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' [<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1], '<s>Brahman</s> is consciousness, bliss' [<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.28], 'That which is directly perceived, the <s>Brahman</s> which is the innermost Self of all' [<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.4.1] — that which is free from all attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) such as hunger, thirst, and the rest, from which all particular attributes have been negated by 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>) [<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.22] — that is what is denoted by the word '<s>Brahman</s>.' That <s>Brahman</s> is also the fire — it is called '<s>brahmāgni</s>' with the intention of denoting it as the locus of the oblation. Into that fire of <s>Brahman</s>, others — other knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — offer the sacrifice; the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is denoted by the word 'sacrifice,' since the word <s>yajña</s> is listed among the names of the <s>Ātman</s> [<s>Nirukta</s> 14.11]. That Self, which is the sacrifice, which in the highest reality is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, but which is conjoined with limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) such as the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the rest and upon which all the properties of the limiting adjuncts are superimposed — that, in the form of an oblation, they offer by means of sacrifice, that is, by the Self itself as described — they cast it in; the vision of the Self with limiting adjuncts as being identical in nature with the unconditioned supreme <s>Brahman</s> — that is the oblation into that fire; they perform it — they are renunciants (<s>sannyāsins</s>) established in the vision of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s>. This sacrifice, characterized by right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>), is introduced among the sacrifices beginning with the divine sacrifice through the verses beginning with '<s>brahmārpaṇam</s>' and is for the purpose of being praised by statements such as 'Superior to the sacrifice of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, O <s>Parantapa</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.33].
[Section break]

children.text: śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati |
children.translated_text: Others offer the senses such as hearing and the rest into the fires of restraint,

children.text: śabdādīn viṣayān anya indriyāgniṣu juhvati ||BhG_4.26||
children.translated_text: While others offer sense-objects such as sound and the rest into the fires of the senses.

children.text: śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye yoginaḥ saṃyamāgniṣu pratīndriyaṃ saṃyamo bhidyata iti bahu-vacanam | saṃyamā evāgnayas teṣu juhvati | indriya-saṃyamam eva kurvantīty arthaḥ | śabdādīn viṣayān anya indriyāgniṣu juhvati, indriyāṇy evāgnayas teṣv indriyāgniṣu juhvati śrotrādibhir aviruddha-viṣaya-grahaṇaṃ homaṃ manyante ||BhGS_4.26||
children.translated_text: Others — other <s>yogins</s> — offer the senses such as hearing and the rest into the fires of restraint (<s>saṃyamāgni</s>); the plural is used because restraint differs for each sense. The restraints themselves are the fires; into those they offer — meaning, they practice the restraint of the senses. Others offer sense-objects such as sound and the rest into the fires of the senses (<s>indriyāgni</s>); the senses themselves are the fires; into those fires of the senses they offer — they consider the apprehension of legitimate sense-objects through hearing and the other senses to be an oblation.
[Section break]

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi cāpare |
children.translated_text: And others offer all the activities of the senses and the activities of the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>)

children.text: ātma-saṃyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite ||BhG_4.27||
children.translated_text: Into the fire of self-restraint through <s>yoga</s> (union), kindled by knowledge.

children.text: sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi indriyāṇāṃ karmāṇīndriya-karmāṇi | tathā prāṇa-karmāṇi prāṇo vāyur ādhyātmikas tat-karmāṇy ākuñcana-prasāraṇādīni tāni cāpara ātma-saṃyama-yogāgnau, ātmani saṃyama ātma-saṃyamaḥ | sa eva yogāgnis tasminn ātma-saṃyama-yogāgnau juhvati prakṣipanti | jñāna-dīpite sneheneva pradīpite viveka-vijñānenojjvala-bhāvam āpādite pravilāpayantīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.27||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] All actions of the senses (<s>indriyakarma</s>) — the actions of the senses are <s>indriyakarmāṇi</s>. Likewise, the actions of <s>prāṇa</s> — <s>prāṇa</s> is the vital air pertaining to the body; its actions are contraction, expansion, and such. Others offer these in the fire of self-restraint-yoga (<s>ātmasaṃyamayogāgni</s>) — restraint of the self is <s>ātmasaṃyama</s>; that itself is the fire of yoga; in that fire of self-restraint-yoga, they offer, they cast [them] in. [This fire is] kindled by knowledge — as a lamp is kindled by oil — made ablaze by discriminative realization (<s>vivekavijñāna</s>) — they cause [the actions] to be dissolved — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.27 //

children.text: dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare |
children.translated_text: Some are performers of material sacrifice (<s>dravyayajña</s>), some of austerity-sacrifice (<s>tapoyajña</s>), some of yoga-sacrifice;

children.text: svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṃśita-vratāḥ ||BhG_4.28||
children.translated_text: and others are performers of scriptural study-sacrifice and knowledge-sacrifice — ascetics of sharpened vows. // <s>BhG</s> 4.28 //

children.text: dravya-yajñās tīrtheṣu dravya-viniyogaṃ yajña-buddhyā kurvanti ye te dravya-yajñāḥ | tapo-yajñās tapo yajño yeṣāṃ tapasvināṃ te tapo-yajñāḥ | yoga-yajñāḥ prāṇāyāma-pratyāhārādi-lakṣaṇo yogo yajño yeṣāṃ te yoga-yajñāḥ | tathāpare svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca svādhyāyo yathā-vidhi ṛg-ādy-abhyāso yajño yeṣāṃ te svādhyāya-yajñāḥ | jñāna-yajñā jñānaṃ śāstrārtha-parijñānaṃ yajño yeṣāṃ te jñāna-yajñāḥ | svādhyāya-yajñā jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayo yatana-śīlāḥ | śaṃsita-vratāḥ samyak śitāni tanūkṛtāni tīkṣṇīkṛtāni vratāni yeṣāṃ te saṃśita-vratāḥ ||BhGS_4.28||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Performers of material sacrifice (<s>dravyayajña</s>) — those who, with the understanding of sacrifice, make gifts of materials at sacred places — they are performers of material sacrifice. Performers of austerity-sacrifice (<s>tapoyajña</s>) — those ascetics for whom austerity is the sacrifice. Performers of yoga-sacrifice — those for whom yoga, characterized by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense-withdrawal), etc., is the sacrifice. And likewise others, performers of scriptural study-sacrifice and knowledge-sacrifice — <s>svādhyāya</s> (scriptural study) is the regulated recitation of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> etc. as prescribed; those for whom this is the sacrifice are performers of scriptural study-sacrifice. Knowledge-sacrifice — those for whom knowledge, the comprehensive understanding of the meaning of scripture, is the sacrifice — they are performers of knowledge-sacrifice. Performers of scriptural study-sacrifice and performers of knowledge-sacrifice — [these are] ascetics (<s>yati</s>), those given to exertion. Of sharpened vows (<s>saṃśitavrata</s>) — those whose vows have been properly attenuated, made keen, sharpened. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.28 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe 'pānaṃ tathāpare |
children.translated_text: Some offer the out-breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) into the in-breath (<s>apāna</s>), and the in-breath into the out-breath;

children.text: prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ ||BhG_4.29||
children.translated_text: others, having arrested the movements of out-breath and in-breath, are devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control). // <s>BhG</s> 4.29 //

children.text: apāne 'pāna-vṛttau juhvati pratikṣipanti prāṇaṃ prāṇa-vṛttiṃ, pūrakākhyaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ kurvantīty arthaḥ | prāṇe 'pānaṃ tathāpare juhvati | recakākhyaṃ ca prāṇāyāmaṃ kurvantīty etat | prāṇāpāna-gatī mukhya-nāsikābhyāṃ vāyor nirgamanaṃ prāṇasya gatis tad-viparyayeṇādho-gamanam apānasya gatis, te prāṇāpāna-gatī | ete ruddhvā nirudhya prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ prāṇāyāma-tat-parāḥ kumbhakākhyaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ kurvantīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.29||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In the <s>apāna</s> — in the function of the <s>apāna</s> — they offer, they cast, the <s>prāṇa</s>, the function of the <s>prāṇa</s>; the meaning is: they perform the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> called <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation). Others offer the <s>apāna</s> into the <s>prāṇa</s>; they perform the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) — this is the meaning. The movements of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> — the outgoing of air through the mouth and nostrils is the movement of <s>prāṇa</s>; the reverse, the downward movement, is the movement of <s>apāna</s>; these are the movements of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>. Having arrested these — having restrained them — those devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, intent upon <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, perform the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> called <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath-retention) — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.29 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati |
children.translated_text: Others, of regulated diet, offer the vital breaths into the vital breaths;

children.text: sarve 'py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||BhG_4.30||
children.translated_text: all these are knowers of sacrifice, whose impurities have been destroyed by sacrifice. // <s>BhG</s> 4.30 //

children.text: apare niyatāhārā niyataḥ parimita āhāro yeṣāṃ te niyatāhārāḥ santaḥ, prāṇān vāyu-bhedān prāṇeṣv eva juhvati | yasya yasya vāyor jayaḥ kriyata itarān vāyu-bhedān tasmin tasmin juhvati, te tatra praviṣṭā iva bhavanti | sarve 'py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapitakalmaṣā yajñair yathoktaiḥ kṣapito nāśitaḥ kalmaṣo yeṣāṃ te yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||BhGS_4.30||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Others, of regulated diet (<s>niyatāhāra</s>) — those whose food intake is regulated, measured — being such, they offer the vital breaths, the different forms of vital air, into the vital breaths themselves. Whichever vital air is being conquered, the other forms of vital air are offered into it — they become, as it were, absorbed into it. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose impurities have been destroyed by sacrifice — those whose impurities (<s>kalmaṣa</s>) have been destroyed, eliminated, by the aforementioned sacrifices. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.30 //

children.text: evaṃ yathoktān yajñān nirvatrya ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Having thus performed the aforementioned sacrifices —

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |
children.translated_text: Those who partake of the nectar-remnants of sacrifice go to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: nāyaṃ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kurusattama ||BhG_4.31||
children.translated_text: not even this world belongs to one who performs no sacrifice — how then the other, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 4.31 //

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yajñānāṃ śiṣṭaṃ yajña-śiṣṭaṃ yajña-śiṣṭaṃ ca tad amṛtaṃ ca yajña-śiṣṭāmṛtaṃ tad bhuñjata iti yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujaḥ | yathoktān yajñān kṛtvā tac-chiṣṭena kālena yathā-vidhi-coditam annam amṛtākhyaṃ bhuñjate iti yajña-śiṣṭāmṛta-bhujo yānti gacchanti brahma sanātanaṃ cirantanaṃ mumukṣavaś cet | kālātikramāpekṣayeti sāmarthyād gamyate | nāyaṃ lokaḥ sarva-prāṇi-sādhāraṇo 'py asti yathoktānāṃ yajñānām eko 'pi yajño yasya nāsti so 'yajñas tasya | kuto 'nyo viśiṣṭa-sādhana-sādhyaḥ kuru-sattama ||BhGS_4.31||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Those who partake of the nectar-remnants of sacrifice (<s>yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhuj</s>) — the remnant of sacrifices is <s>yajñaśiṣṭa</s>; that remnant is also nectar — <s>yajñaśiṣṭāmṛta</s>; those who partake of it are <s>yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujaḥ</s>. Having performed the aforementioned sacrifices, with the remaining time they eat food called nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) as prescribed — thus they are partakers of the nectar-remnants of sacrifice. They go — proceed — to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>, the ancient, if they are seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>). The implication 'awaiting the passage of time' is understood from the context. Not even this world — common to all living beings — belongs to one who performs no sacrifice; one for whom not even a single one of the aforementioned sacrifices exists is a non-performer of sacrifice; [not even this world belongs] to him. How then the other [world], O best of the <s>Kurus</s> — which is attainable through special means? // <s>BhGS</s> 4.31 //

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
children.translated_text: Thus, many kinds of sacrifices are spread forth in the mouth of <s>Brahman</s> (the Veda);

children.text: karmajān viddhi tān sarvān evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||BhG_4.32||
children.translated_text: know them all to be born of action — knowing thus, you shall be liberated. // <s>BhG</s> 4.32 //

children.text: evaṃ yathoktā bahu-vidhā bahu-prakārā yajñā vitatā vistīrṇā brahmaṇo vedasya mukhe dvāre veda-dvāreṇa avagamyamānā brahmaṇo mukhe vitatā ucyante | tad yathā vāci hi prāṇaṃ juhumaḥ ity ādayaḥ | karmajān kāyika-vācika-mānasa-karmodbhavān viddhi tān sarvān anātmajān, nirvyāpāro hy ātmā | ata evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase 'śubhāt | na mad-vyāpārā ime, nirvyāpāro 'ham udāsīna ity evaṃ jñātvāsmāt samyag-darśanān mokṣyase saṃsāra-bandhanād ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.32||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Thus, the aforementioned many kinds — many varieties — of sacrifices are spread forth, expanded, in the mouth (<s>mukha</s>) — the gateway — of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Veda</s>; they are known through the gateway of the <s>Veda</s> — they are said to be spread forth in the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>. Just as [one says]: 'in speech indeed we offer the <s>prāṇa</s>' and so on. Know them all to be born of action — born of bodily, verbal, and mental action — [and therefore] not born of the Self, for the Self is indeed without activity. Therefore, knowing thus, you shall be liberated from evil. [The meaning is:] 'These are not my activities; I am without activity, indifferent' — knowing thus, through this right vision, you will be liberated from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.32 //

children.text: brahmārpaṇam [Gītā 4.24] ity ādi lokena samyag-darśanasya yajñatvaṃ saṃpāditam | yajñāś cāneka upadiṣṭāḥ | taiḥ siddha-puruṣārtha-prayojanair jñānaṃ stūyate | katham ? ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Beginning with '<s>brahmārpaṇam</s>' [<s>BhG</s> 4.24], the status of right knowledge as a sacrifice was established by the passage. And many sacrifices have been taught. By means of these, whose purpose is the attainment of the human goals (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), knowledge is praised. How?

children.text: śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa |
children.translated_text: The sacrifice of knowledge (<s>jñānayajña</s>) is superior to the sacrifice of material things (<s>dravyamayayajña</s>), O scorcher of foes;

children.text: sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||BhG_4.33||
children.translated_text: all action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge. // <s>BhG</s> 4.33 //
