children.text: śreyān dravya-mayāt dravya-sādhana-sādhyād yajñāj jñāna-yajño he paraṃtapa | dravya-mayo hi yajñaḥ phalasyārambhakaḥ, jñāna-yajño na phalārambhakaḥ, ataḥ śreyān praśasyataraḥ | katham ? yataḥ sarvaṃ karma samastam akhilam apratibaddhaṃ pārtha jñāne mokṣa-sādhane sarvataḥ saṃplutodaka-sthānīye parisamāpyate antarbhavatīty arthaḥ | yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃcit prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti yas tad veda yat sa veda [ChāU 4.1.4] iti śruteḥ ||BhGS_4.33||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of material things — the sacrifice requiring material means and producing material results, O scorcher of foes. For the material sacrifice merely initiates results, while the knowledge-sacrifice does not initiate [karmic] results. Therefore it is superior, more praiseworthy. How? Because all action — the entirety, without remainder, O <s>Pārtha</s> — culminates in knowledge, [knowledge] which is the means to liberation, [occupying] the position of a fully flooded reservoir — [all action] is subsumed within it — this is the meaning. As [the <s>Śruti</s> states]: 'Just as [lower gains] flow into the winning throw, so does everything that creatures do well flow into one who knows this — one who knows this' [<s>ChāU</s> 4.1.4]. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.33 //

children.text: tad etad viśiṣṭāṃ jñānaṃ tarhi kena prāpyata ity ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Then, by what means is this distinguished knowledge obtained? It is stated —

children.text: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
children.translated_text: Know that through prostration, inquiry, and service;

children.text: upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ ||BhG_4.34||
children.translated_text: the knowers, the seers of truth, will teach you knowledge. // <s>BhG</s> 4.34 //

children.text: tat viddhi vijānīhi yena vidhinā prāpyate iti | ācāryān abhigamya, praṇipātena prakarṣeṇa nīcaiḥ patanaṃ praṇipāto dīrgha-namaskāras tena | kathaṃ bandhaḥ ? kathaṃ mokṣaḥ ? kā vidyā ? kā cāvidyā ? iti paripraśnena, sevayā guru-śuśrūṣayā evam ādinā | praśrayeṇāvarjitā ācāryā upadekṣyanti kathayiṣyanti te jñānaṃ yathokta-viśeṣaṇaṃ jñāninaḥ | jñānavanto 'pi kecid yathāvat tattva-darśana-śīlāḥ, apare na | ato viśinaṣṭi tattva-darśina iti | ye samyag-darśinas tair upadiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ kārya-kṣamaṃ bhavati | netarad iti bhagavato matam ||BhGS_4.34||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Know that — understand by what method it is obtained: by approaching teachers, through prostration (<s>praṇipāta</s>) — falling down completely, a full-length obeisance; through inquiry (<s>paripraśna</s>) — 'What is bondage? What is liberation? What is knowledge? What is ignorance?'; through service (<s>sevā</s>) — attendance upon the teacher — and so on. Teachers, won over by humility, will teach — will impart to you — knowledge of the aforementioned characteristics. The knowers — though some possess knowledge, only some habitually see the truth as it really is, others do not. Therefore he specifies: 'seers of truth' — those who are right seers. Knowledge imparted by them is effective. Not otherwise — this is the Lord's view. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.34 //

children.text: tathā ca satīdamapi samarthaṃ vacanam --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And this too is a potent statement —

children.text: yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
children.translated_text: Having known which, you will not again fall into delusion thus, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>;

children.text: yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi ||BhG_4.35||
children.translated_text: by which you will see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in Me. // <s>BhG</s> 4.35 //

children.text: yaj jñātvā yaj jñānaṃ tair upadiṣṭam adhigamya prāpya punar bhūyo moham evaṃ yathedānīṃ mohaṃ gato 'si punar evaṃ na yāsyasi he pāṇḍāva | kiṃ ca ---- yena jñānena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa brahmādīni stamba-paryantāni drakṣyasi sākṣād ātmani pratyag ātmani mat-saṃsthānīmāni bhūtānīty atho api mayi vāsudeve parameśvare cemānīti | kṣetrajñeśvaraikatvaṃ sarvopaniṣat-prasiddhaṃ drakṣyasīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.35||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Having known which — having attained, having obtained, the knowledge imparted by them — you will not again, once more, fall into delusion as you have now fallen into delusion, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. Moreover — by which knowledge you will see all beings without exception, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, in the Self — in the inner Self — [thinking] 'these beings are established in me'; and then also in Me, in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme Lord — 'and these [beings are established] in Him.' The unity of the individual self (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) and the Lord, well-known in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, you will see — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.35 //

children.text: kiṃ caitasya jñānasya māhātmyam ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover, this is the greatness of this knowledge —

children.text: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners,

children.text: sarvaṃ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi ||BhG_4.36||
children.translated_text: you will cross over all wickedness by the raft of knowledge alone. // <s>BhG</s> 4.36 //

children.text: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛdbhyaḥ sarvebhyo 'tiśayena pāpa-kṛt pāpa-kṛttamaḥ sarvaṃ jñāna-plavenaiva jñānam eva plavaṃ kṛtvā vṛjinaṃ vṛjinārṇavaṃ pāpa-samudraṃ saṃtariṣyasi | dharmo 'pīha mumukṣoḥ pāpam ucyate ||BhGS_4.36||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Even if you are, among all sinners — all evil-doers — the most sinful, the greatest sinner of all — you will cross over all wickedness — the ocean of wickedness, the sea of sin — by the raft of knowledge alone, making knowledge itself a raft. Even <s>dharma</s> (merit) is called sin here for the one who seeks liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 4.36 //

children.text: jñānaṃ kathaṃ nāśayati pāpam ? iti sa-dṛṣṭāntam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] How does knowledge destroy sin? It is stated with an illustration —

children.text: yathaidhāṃsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||BhG_4.37||
children.translated_text: so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes. // <s>BhG</s> 4.37 //

children.text: yathaidhāṃsi kāṣṭhāni samiddhaḥ samyag iddho dīpto 'gnir bhasmasāt bhasmībhāvaṃ kurute he arjuna, jñānam eva agnir jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā nirbījīkarotīty arthaḥ | na hi sākṣād eva jñānāgniḥ karmāṇīndhanavat bhasmīkartuṃ śaknoti | tasmāt samyag darśanaṃ sarva-karmaṇāṃ nirbījatve kāraṇam ity abhiprāyaḥ | sāmarthyād yena karmaṇā arīram ārabdhaṃ tat pravṛtta-phalatvād upabhogenaiva kṣīyate | tasya tāvad eva ciraṃ yāvan na vimokṣye 'tha sampatsye [ChāU 6.14.1] ato yāny apravṛtta-phalāni jñānotpatteḥ prāk kṛtāni jñāna-sahabhāvīni cātītāneka-janma-kṛtāni ca tāny eva sarvāṇi bhasmasāt kurute ||BhGS_4.37||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Just as a blazing fire — well-kindled, aflame — reduces firewood to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>; knowledge itself is the fire — the fire of knowledge — reduces all actions to ashes, likewise renders them seedless — this is the meaning. For the fire of knowledge cannot literally reduce actions to ashes like fuel. Therefore, the purport is: right knowledge is the cause of the seedlessness of all actions. It follows from the context that actions by which this body was initiated — those whose fruits have already begun to operate — are exhausted only through experience. 'For him there is delay only until he is freed [from the body]; then he will attain [<s>Brahman</s>]' [<s>ChāU</s> 6.14.2]. Therefore, those actions whose fruits have not yet begun to operate — those performed before the arising of knowledge, those co-existing with knowledge, and those performed in countless previous births — all of those are reduced to ashes. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.37 //

children.text: yataḥ evam ataḥ---
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram iha vidyate |
children.translated_text: Indeed, there is no purifier in this world equal to knowledge;

children.text: tat svayaṃ yoga-saṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati ||BhG_4.38||
children.translated_text: one who is perfected in yoga finds that [knowledge] in the Self, in due time. // <s>BhG</s> 4.38 //

children.text: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ tulyaṃ pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ śuddhi-karam iha vidyate | taj jñānaṃ svayam eva yoga-saṃsiddho yogena karma-yogena samādhi-yogena ca saṃsiddhaḥ saṃskṛto yogyatām āpannaḥ san mumukṣuḥ kālena mahatā ātmani vindati labhate ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_4.38||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Indeed, there is no purifier equal to — comparable to — knowledge; nothing purifying, nothing that produces purity, exists here [in this world]. That knowledge — one who is perfected in yoga (<s>yogasaṃsiddha</s>), one who has been refined, brought to readiness through yoga — both <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action) and <s>samādhiyoga</s> (the yoga of meditation) — a seeker of liberation, finds [that knowledge] in the Self, in due time — after a long period — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 4.38 //

children.text:
==============================
yenaikāntena jñāna-prāptir bhavati sa upāya upadiśyate ---
children.translated_text:
==============================
[Śaṅkara's commentary:] The exclusive means by which knowledge is attained is now taught —

children.text: śraddhāvāṃl labhate jñānaṃ tat-paraḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The one who has faith (<s>śraddhāvān</s>) obtains knowledge; one who is devoted to it, with senses restrained;

children.text: jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntim acireṇādhigacchati ||BhG_4.39||
children.translated_text: having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace. // <s>BhG</s> 4.39 //

children.text: śraddhāvān śraddhālur labhate jñānam | śraddhālutve 'pi bhavati kaścin manda-prasthānaḥ, ata āha --- tat-paraḥ | gurūpāsadanādāv abhiyukto jñāna-labdhy-upāye śraddhāvān | tat-paro 'py ajitendriyaḥ syāt ity ata āha --- saṃyatendriyaḥ | saṃyatāni viṣayebhyo nivartitāni yasyendriyāṇi sa saṃyatendriyaḥ | ya evaṃbhūtaḥ śraddhāvān tat-paraḥ saṃyatendriyaś ca so 'vaśyaṃ jñānaṃ labhate | praṇipātādis tu bāhyo 'naikāntiko 'pi bhavati, māyāvitvādi-saṃbhavāt | na tu tat śraddhāvattvādau ity ekāntato jñāna-labdhy-upāyaḥ | kiṃ punar jñāna-lābhāt syād ity ucyate -- jñānaṃ labdhvā paraṃ mokṣākhyāṃ śāntim uparatim acireṇa kṣipram evādhigacchati | samyag-darśanāt kṣipram eva mokṣo bhavatīti sarva-śāstra-nyāya-prasiddhaḥ suniścito 'rthaḥ ||BhGS_4.39||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The one who has faith (<s>śraddhāvān</s>), i.e., who is full of trust, obtains knowledge. Even though one may be faithful, one might be slow in one's progress; therefore he says: '<s>tat-para</s>' — devoted to that, diligent in the means of obtaining knowledge such as attending upon the teacher etc., and having faith. Even one who is devoted to that may have uncontrolled senses; therefore he says: 'with senses restrained' (<s>saṃyatendriya</s>) — one whose senses have been restrained, i.e., withdrawn from their objects, is <s>saṃyatendriya</s>. One who is of this nature — faithful, devoted to that, and with senses restrained — necessarily obtains knowledge. Prostration and the like, however, are external [means] and not infallible, because of the possibility of deceit etc. But they are not so with respect to faith etc. — therefore [faith etc.] is the infallible means of obtaining knowledge. What then results from the attainment of knowledge? It is said: having obtained knowledge, one quickly, swiftly indeed, attains supreme peace (<s>śānti</s>), i.e., cessation, called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). That liberation comes quickly from right vision is a well-established and firmly determined truth in all scriptures. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.39||

children.text: atra saṃśayo na kartavyaḥ, pāpiṣṭho hi saṃśayaḥ | katham ity ucyate ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Doubt should not be entertained here, for doubt is the most sinful [obstacle]. How? It is stated:

children.text: ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: The ignorant, the faithless, and the one of doubting self — [all] perish;

children.text: nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ ||BhG_4.40||
children.translated_text: for the one of doubting self, there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.40||

children.text: ajñaś cānātmajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca guru-vākya-śāstreṣv aviśvāsavāṃś ca saṃśayātmā ca saṃśaya-cittaś ca vinaśyati | ajñāśraddadhānau yadyapi vinaśyataḥ, na tathā yathā saṃśayātmā | saṃśayātmā tu pāpiṣṭhaḥ sarveṣām | katham ? nāyaṃ sādhāraṇo 'pi loko 'sti | tathā na paro lokaḥ | na sukham, tatrāpi saṃśayotpatteḥ saṃśayātmanaḥ saṃśaya-cittasya | tasmāt saṃśayo na kartavyaḥ ||BhGS_4.40||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'The ignorant' (<s>ajña</s>) — one who lacks Self-knowledge; 'the faithless' (<s>aśraddadhāna</s>) — one who has no trust in the words of the teacher and the scriptures; 'the one of doubting self' (<s>saṃśayātmā</s>) — one whose mind is given to doubt — [such a one] perishes. Although the ignorant and the faithless perish, they do not perish as much as the one of doubting self. The one of doubting self is the most sinful of all. How? Not even this ordinary world — the common world [available to all beings] — exists [for him]. Likewise, there is no other world. Nor is there happiness — because even there doubt arises — for the one of doubting self, for the one whose mind is given to doubt. Therefore, doubt should not be entertained. ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.40||

children.text: kasmāt ? ----
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Why [should doubt not be entertained]?

children.text: yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇaṃ jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayam |
children.translated_text: One who has renounced actions through <s>yoga</s>, whose doubt has been severed by knowledge,

children.text: ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||BhG_4.41||
children.translated_text: who is self-possessed — actions do not bind him, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 4.41||

children.text: yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇaṃ paramārtha-darśana-lakṣaṇena yogena saṃnyastāni karmāṇi yena paramārtha-darśinā dharmādharmākhyāni taṃ yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇam | kathaṃ yoga-saṃnyasta-karmā ? ity āha - jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayaṃ jñānenātmeśvaraikatva-darśana-lakṣaṇena saṃchinnaḥ saṃśayo yasya yo jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayaḥ | ya evaṃ yoga-saṃnyasta-karmā tam ātmavantam apramattaṃ guṇa-ceṣṭā-rūpeṇa dṛṣṭāni karmāṇi na nibadhnanty aniṣṭādi-rūpaṃ phalaṃ nārabhante | he dhanaṃjaya ||BhGS_4.41||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'One who has renounced actions through <s>yoga</s>' — through <s>yoga</s> characterized by the vision of ultimate reality, the one who has renounced actions — the seer of ultimate reality by whom actions called <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> have been renounced — that one is 'one who has renounced actions through <s>yoga</s>.' How does one renounce actions through <s>yoga</s>? He says: 'whose doubt has been severed by knowledge' — by knowledge characterized by the vision of the unity of the Self and the Lord, one whose doubt has been severed, cut asunder — that is one 'whose doubt has been severed by knowledge.' One who has thus renounced actions through <s>yoga</s> — that self-possessed one (<s>ātmavat</s>), i.e., the vigilant one — actions, seen in the form of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature), do not bind him — they do not produce fruits of an undesirable nature etc. O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>! ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.41||

children.text: yasmāt karma-yogānuṣṭhānād aśuddhi-kṣaya-hetuka-jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayo na nibadhyate karmabhir jñānāgni-dagdha-karmatvād eva, yasmāc ca jñāna-karmānuṣṭhāna-viṣaye saṃśayavān vinaśyati ---
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since one whose doubt has been severed by knowledge born of the elimination of impurity through the practice of <s>karma-yoga</s> is not bound by actions — precisely because actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge; and since one who doubts regarding the practice of knowledge and action perishes —

children.text: tasmād ajñāna-saṃbhūtaṃ hṛt-sthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having severed with the sword of knowledge this doubt of the self,

children.text: chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata ||BhG_4.42||
children.translated_text: born of ignorance, residing in the heart — take refuge in <s>yoga</s>; arise, O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||<s>BhG</s> 4.42||

children.text: tasmāt pāpiṣṭham ajñāna-saṃbhūtam ajñānād avivekāj jātaṃ hṛt-sthaṃ hṛdi buddhau sthitaṃ jñānāsinā śoka-mohādi-doṣa-haraṃ samyag darśanaṃ jñānaṃ tad evāsiḥ khaḍgas tena jñānāsinā ātmanaḥ svasya, ātma-viṣayatvāt saṃśayasya | na hi parasya saṃśayaḥ pareṇa cchettavyatāṃ prāptaḥ, yena svasyeti viśeṣyeta | ata ātma-viṣayo 'pi svasyaiva bhavati | chittvā enaṃ saṃśayaṃ sva-vināśa-hetu-bhūtam, yogaṃ samyag-darśanopāyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānam ātiṣṭha kurv ity arthaḥ | uttiṣṭha cedānīṃ yuddhāya bhārata iti ||BhGS_4.42||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, [having severed] this most sinful [doubt] — 'born of ignorance,' i.e., arising from ignorance, from non-discrimination; 'residing in the heart,' i.e., established in the heart, in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>); 'with the sword of knowledge' — right vision, which is knowledge that removes defects such as grief, delusion, etc. — that itself is the sword; with that sword of knowledge; 'of the self' (<s>ātmanaḥ</s>), i.e., one's own — because doubt pertains to the self. For another's doubt cannot be cut by another person, such that 'of the self' would need to be specified. Therefore, even though pertaining to the self, it is indeed one's own [doubt]. Having severed (<s>chittvā</s>) this doubt — the cause of one's own destruction; take refuge in <s>yoga</s> — the practice of action that is the means to right vision — this is the meaning. Arise now for battle, O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||<s>BhGS</s> 4.42||

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ
||4||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the blessed <s>Bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, who was the foremost among the supreme renunciants and wandering monks. ||4||

children.text: BhG 5
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 5

children.text:
atha pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
(śaṅkara-bhāṣya)
children.translated_text: Fifth Chapter — <s>Śaṅkara's</s> Commentary

children.text: arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
children.translated_text: You praise the renunciation of actions, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and again also <s>yoga</s> [of action];

children.text: yac chreya etayor ekaṃ tan me brūhi suniścitam ||BhG_5.1||
children.translated_text: tell me decisively which one of these two is the better. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.1||

children.text: saṃnyāsaṃ parityāgaṃ karmaṇāṃ āstrīyāṇām anuṣṭheya-viśeṣāṇām śaṃsasi praśaṃsasi kathayasīty etat | punar yogaṃ ca teṣām eva anuṣṭhānam avaśya-kartavyam śaṃsasi | ato me katarat śreyaḥ iti saṃśayaḥ - kiṃ karmānuṣṭhānaṃ śreyaḥ, kiṃ vā tad-dhānam iti | praśasyataraṃ cānuṣṭheyam | ataś ca yat śreyaḥ praśasyataram etayoḥ karma-saṃnyāsa-karma-yogayor yad-anuṣṭhānāt śreyo 'vāptir mama syād iti manyase, tad ekam anyatarat saha eka-puruṣānuṣṭheyatvāsaṃbhavāt me brūhi suniścitam abhipretaṃ taveti ||BhGS_5.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Renunciation' (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) — the complete abandonment — of actions, i.e., of the particular duties enjoined by scripture — 'you praise,' i.e., you commend, you speak of — this is the meaning. 'And again <s>yoga</s> also' — the practice of those very [actions] as absolutely necessary — you praise. Therefore my doubt is: which of the two is better — is it the performance of actions, or their abandonment? And the more praiseworthy is what should be practiced. Therefore, that which is better, more praiseworthy, of these two — the renunciation of action and the <s>yoga</s> of action — from the practice of which you consider I would attain the greater good — that one, one of the two, since the simultaneous practice by one person is impossible — tell me, with certainty, as your considered view. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.1||

children.text: svābhiprāyam ācakṣāṇo nirṇayāya śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Declaring his own considered view for the purpose of resolution, the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: saṃnyāsaḥ karma-yogaś ca niḥśreyasa-karāv ubhau |
children.translated_text: Both renunciation and the <s>yoga</s> of action lead to the highest good;

children.text: tayos tu karma-saṃnyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate ||BhG_5.2||
children.translated_text: but of the two, <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action) is superior to the renunciation of action. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.2||

children.text: saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇāṃ parityāgaḥ karma-yogaś ca teṣām anuṣṭhānaṃ tāv ubhāv api niḥśreyasa-karau mokṣaṃ kurvāte jñānotpatti-hetutvena | ubhau yadyapi niḥśreyasa-karau, tathāpi tayos tu niḥśreyasa-hetvoḥ karma-saṃnyāsāt kevalāt karma-yogo viśiṣyata iti karma-yogaṃ stauti ||BhGS_5.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Renunciation' (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) — the abandonment of actions; and '<s>karma-yoga</s>' — the performance of those [actions] — both of these lead to the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), i.e., they bring about liberation by being causes of the arising of knowledge. Although both lead to the highest good, nevertheless, of these two causes of the highest good, <s>karma-yoga</s> is superior to mere renunciation of action (<s>karma-saṃnyāsa</s>) — thus he praises <s>karma-yoga</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.2||

children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: kasmāt iti āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Why [is <s>karma-yoga</s> superior]? He says:

children.text: jñeyaḥ sa nitya-saṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
children.translated_text: He should be known as a perpetual renunciant who neither hates nor desires;

children.text: nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate ||BhG_5.3||
children.translated_text: for one who is free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed one, is easily liberated from bondage. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.3||

children.text: jñeyo jñātavyaḥ sa karma-yogī nitya-saṃnyāsī iti yo na dveṣṭi kiṃcit na kāṅkṣati duḥkha-sukhe tat-sādhane ca | evaṃvidho yaḥ, karmaṇi vartamāno 'pi sa nitya-saṃnyāsī iti jñātavya ity arthaḥ | nirdvandvo dvandva-varjito hi yasmāt mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhād anāyāsena pramucyate ||BhGS_5.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'He should be known' — he should be understood — that <s>karma-yogin</s> is a perpetual renunciant (<s>nitya-saṃnyāsī</s>) — one who neither hates anything nor desires [anything] — neither pain nor pleasure, nor the means to either. One who is of this nature — even while engaged in action — should be known as a perpetual renunciant — this is the meaning. One who is free from the pairs of opposites (<s>nirdvandva</s>), i.e., devoid of the pairs of opposites — for (<s>hi</s>), since — O mighty-armed one — is easily (<s>sukham</s>), without difficulty, liberated from bondage. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.3||

children.text: saṃnyāsa-karma-yogayor bhinna-puruṣānuṣṭheyayor viruddhayoḥ phale 'pi virodho yuktaḥ | na tūbhayor niḥśreyasa-karatvam eveti prāpta idam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since renunciation and <s>karma-yoga</s> are to be practiced by different persons and are mutually opposed, a contradiction in their results would also be appropriate. But both cannot lead to the highest good — anticipating this objection, this is said:

children.text: sāṃkhya-yogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Children, not the learned, speak of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as distinct;

children.text: ekam apy āsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam ||BhG_5.4||
children.translated_text: one who is properly established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.4||

children.text: sāṃkhya-yogau pṛthag viruddha-bhinna-phalau bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ | paṇḍitās tu jñānina ekaṃ phalam aviruddham icchanti | katham ? ekam api sāṃkhya-yogayoḥ samyag āsthitaḥ samyag anuṣṭhitavān ity arthaḥ, ubhayor vindate phalam | ubhayos tad eva hi niḥśreyasaṃ phalam | ato na phale virodho 'sti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>' — as yielding distinct, mutually opposed fruits — 'children' (<s>bāla</s>), i.e., the immature, declare [this], not the learned (<s>paṇḍita</s>). The learned, i.e., the knowers, recognize the fruit as one, non-contradictory. How? One who is properly established even in one of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> or <s>Yoga</s> — the meaning is: one who has properly practiced [either one] — obtains the fruit of both. For the fruit of both is indeed the same — the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). Therefore, there is no contradiction in the fruit.

children.text: nanu saṃnyāsa-karma-yoga-śabdena prastutya sāṃkhya-yogayoḥ phalaikatvaṃ katham ihāprakṛtaṃ bravīti ? naiṣa doṣaḥ - yadyapy arjunena saṃnyāsaṃ karma-yogaṃ ca kevalam abhipretya praśnaḥ kṛtaḥ | bhagavāṃs tu tad-aparityāgenaiva svābhipretaṃ ca viśeṣaṃ saṃyojya śabdāntara-vācyatayā prativacanaṃ dadau sāṃkhya-yogāv iti | tāv eva saṃnyāsa-karma-yogau jñāna-tad-upāya-sama-buddhitvādi-saṃyuktau sāṃkhya-yoga-śabda-vācyāv iti bhagavato matam | ato na aprakṛta-prakriyeti ||BhGS_5.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: Having introduced the subject with the terms 'renunciation' and '<s>karma-yoga</s>,' how is it that one speaks here of the unity of fruit for <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>, which are not the topic at hand? This is not a fault. Although <s>Arjuna's</s> question was posed with reference solely to renunciation and <s>karma-yoga</s>, the Blessed Lord, without abandoning those [concepts] and combining with them the distinction he himself intended, gave a reply using different terminology — '<s>Sāṃkhya</s>' and '<s>Yoga</s>.' Those very renunciation and <s>karma-yoga</s>, when combined with the understanding of knowledge and its means etc., are expressed by the terms '<s>Sāṃkhya</s>' and '<s>Yoga</s>' — this is the Lord's view. Therefore, the topic has not strayed to something unrelated. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.4||

children.text: ekasyāpi samyag anuṣṭhānāt katham ubhayoḥ phalaṃ vindate ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How does one who is properly established in even one of them obtain the fruit of both? It is stated:

children.text: yat sāṃkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tad yogair api gamyate |
children.translated_text: The state that is reached by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> (followers of knowledge) is also reached by the <s>Yogins</s> (followers of action);

children.text: ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||BhG_5.5||
children.translated_text: one who sees <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as one — that one truly sees. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.5||

children.text: yat sāṃkhyair jñāna-niṣṭhaiḥ saṃnyāsibhiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ mokṣākhyam tad yogair api jñāna-prāpty-upāyatveneśvare samarpya karmāṇy ātmanaḥ phalam anabhisaṃdhāyānutiṣṭhanti ye te yogā yoginaḥ | tair api paramārtha-jñāna-saṃnyāsa-prāpti-dvāreṇa gamyata ity abhiprāyaḥ | ata ekaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati phalaikatvāt sa paśyati samyak paśyatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The state that is reached by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> — the renunciants established in steadfastness in knowledge (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhā</s>) — called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — is also reached by the <s>Yogins</s>. Those who, offering their actions to the Lord as the means of attaining knowledge, practice without regard for their own reward, are <s>Yogas</s>, i.e., <s>Yogins</s>. By them too, through the attainment of the renunciation of ultimate-reality-knowledge — [that state] is reached — this is the purport. Therefore, one who sees <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as one — because of the unity of their fruit — that one truly sees, i.e., sees rightly — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.5||

children.text: evaṃ tarhi yogāt saṃnyāsa eva viśiṣyate | kathaṃ tarhīdam uktam tayos tu karma-saṃnyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate [Gītā 5.2] iti ? sṛṇu tatra kāraṇam - tvayā pṛṣṭāṃ kevalaṃ karma-saṃnyāsaṃ karma-yogaṃ cābhipretya tayor anyataraḥ kaḥ śreyān ? iti | tad-anurūpaṃ prativacanaṃ mayoktaṃ karma-saṃnyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate iti jñānam anapekṣya | jñānāpekṣas tu saṃnyāsaḥ sāṃkhyam iti mayābhipretaḥ | paramārtha-yogaś ca sa eva | yas tu karma-yogo vaidikaḥ sa ca tādarthyāt yogaḥ saṃnyāsa iti copacaryate | kathaṃ tādarthyam ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If so, then renunciation is indeed superior to <s>Yoga</s>. How then was it said 'of the two, <s>karma-yoga</s> is superior to the renunciation of action' [<s>BhG</s> 5.2]? Listen to the reason for that. You asked, having in mind solely the bare renunciation of action and <s>karma-yoga</s>: which of the two is better? In response, my answer — '<s>karma-yoga</s> is superior to renunciation of action' — was stated without reference to knowledge. But renunciation accompanied by knowledge is what I mean by '<s>Sāṃkhya</s>.' And that is the ultimate <s>Yoga</s> as well. But <s>Vedic karma-yoga</s> — that too, because it serves [the ultimate goal], is figuratively called '<s>Yoga</s>' and 'renunciation' (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>). How does it serve [the goal]? It is stated:

children.text: saṃnyāsas tu mahābāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ |
children.translated_text: But renunciation, O mighty-armed one, is difficult to attain without <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: yoga-yukto munir brahma nacireṇādhigacchati ||BhG_5.6||
children.translated_text: the sage endowed with <s>yoga</s> quickly attains <s>Brahman</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.6||

children.text: saṃnyāsas tu pāramārthiko duḥkham āptuṃ prāptum ayogato yogena vinā | yoga-yukto vaidikena karma-yogena vaidikena karma-yogeneśvara-samarpita-rūpeṇa phala-nirapekṣeṇa yukto muniḥ | mananād īśvara-svarūpasya muniḥ | brahma paramātma-jñāna-niṣṭhā-lakṣaṇatvāt prakṛtaḥ saṃnyāso brahmocyate | nyāsa iti brahmā brahmā hi paraḥ [MahānārU 78] iti śruteḥ | brahma paramārtha-saṃnyāsaṃ paramārtha-jñāna-niṣṭhā-lakṣaṇaṃ na cireṇa kṣipram evādhigacchati prāpnoti | ato mayoktam karma-yogo viśiṣyata iti ||BhGS_5.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'But renunciation' — the ultimate [renunciation] — is difficult to attain, to reach, without <s>yoga</s>, i.e., without the yoga [of action]. The sage endowed with <s>yoga</s> — endowed with <s>Vedic karma-yoga</s> performed in the spirit of offering to the Lord and without regard for results — is a <s>muni</s>; a '<s>muni</s>' because of contemplation (<s>manana</s>) of the nature of the Lord. '<s>Brahman</s>' — because it is characterized by steadfastness in the knowledge of the Supreme Self, the renunciation under discussion is called <s>Brahman</s>. [As the <s>Śruti</s> states:] '<s>Nyāsa</s> (renunciation) is <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Brahman</s> is indeed the Supreme' [<s>MahānārU</s> 78]. <s>Brahman</s> — the ultimate renunciation characterized by steadfastness in ultimate knowledge — is attained quickly, swiftly, without long delay. Therefore I stated that <s>karma-yoga</s> is superior. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.6||

children.text: yadā punar ayaṃ samyag-darśana-prāpty-upāyatvena -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And when this [practitioner], as the means to attaining right vision —

children.text: yoga-yukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Endowed with <s>yoga</s>, of purified self, of conquered self, with senses subdued,

children.text: sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate ||BhG_5.7||
children.translated_text: whose self has become the Self of all beings — even while acting, he is not tainted. ||<s>BhG</s> 5.7||

children.text: yogena yukto yoga-yukto viśuddhātmā viśuddha-sattvo vijitātmā vijita-deho jitendriyaś ca sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā sarveṣāṃ brahmādīnāṃ stamba-paryantānāṃ bhūtānām ātma-bhūta ātmā pratyak-cetano yasya sa sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā samyag-darśīty arthaḥ | sa tatraivaṃ vartamāno loka-saṃgrahāya karma kurvann api na lipyate na karmabhir badhyate ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Endowed with <s>yoga</s>' (<s>yoga-yukta</s>) — endowed with <s>yoga</s>; 'of purified self' (<s>viśuddhātmā</s>) — of purified <s>sattva</s> (being/inner faculty); 'of conquered self' (<s>vijitātmā</s>) — of conquered body; 'with senses subdued' (<s>jitendriya</s>); 'whose self has become the Self of all beings' (<s>sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā</s>) — the inner conscious Self of all beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass, has become his Self — he whose Self is thus is <s>sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā</s>, i.e., one of right vision — this is the meaning. He, being in such a state — for the welfare of the world (<s>loka-saṃgraha</s>) — even while performing action, is not tainted — is not bound by actions — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 5.7||

children.text: na cāsau paramārthataḥ karotīty ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And this is because he does not, in ultimate reality, act; therefore —

children.text: naiva kiṃ cit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit |
children.translated_text: 'I do not do anything at all' — thus should the one who is united [with <s>Brahman</s>] think, the knower of truth;

children.text: paśyañ śṛṇvan spṛśañ jighrann aśnan gacchan svapañ śvasan ||BhG_5.8||
children.translated_text: while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing — ||<s>BhG</s> 5.8||

children.text: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api |
children.translated_text: speaking, releasing, grasping, opening and closing the eyes —

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan ||BhG_5.9||
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'the senses operate among the sense-objects' — holding [this view]. // <s>BhG</s> 5.9 //

children.text: yuktaḥ samāhitaḥ san manyeta cintayet | tattvavid ātmano yāthātmyaṃ tattvaṃ vettīti tattva-vit paramārtha-darśīty arthaḥ | kadā kathaṃ vā tattvam avadhārayan manyeta ? ity ucyate | manyeteti pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ | yasyaivaṃ tattva-vidaḥ sarva-kārya-karaṇa-ceṣṭāsu karmasv akarmaiva paśyataḥ samyag-darśinas tasya sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa evādhikāraḥ karmaṇo 'bhāva-darśanāt | na hi mṛga-tṛṣṇikāyām udaka-buddhyā pānāya pravṛtta udakābhāva-jñāne 'pi tatraiva pāna-prayojanāya pravartate ||BhGS_5.8-9||
children.translated_text: Being disciplined (<s>yukta</s>), concentrated, he should think, should reflect. The knower of truth (<s>tattvavit</s>) — one who knows the true nature (<s>tattva</s>) of the Self — meaning one who sees the ultimate reality. When and how, while ascertaining the truth, should he think? It is said — 'he should think' is to be connected with the preceding [verse]. For such a knower of truth who sees non-action in all activities of the body, senses, and their functions — for one of right vision, the qualification is for the complete renunciation of all actions alone, because of seeing the non-existence of action. For one who, deluded by the perception of water in a mirage, proceeds to drink — even upon knowing the absence of water, he does not proceed to that very place for the purpose of drinking. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.8–9 //

children.text: yas tu punar atattva-vit pravṛttaś ca karma-yoge -
children.translated_text: But one who is not a knower of truth (<s>atattvavit</s>) and is engaged in <s>karma-yoga</s> —

children.text: brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who offers actions to <s>Brahman</s>, having abandoned attachment, and acts,

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā ||BhG_5.10||
children.translated_text: is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf [is not tainted] by water. // <s>BhG</s> 5.10 //

children.text: brahmaṇīśvara ādhāya nikṣipya tad-arthaṃ karma karomīti bhṛtya iva svāmy-arthaṃ sarvāṇi karmāṇi | mokṣe 'pi phale saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ sarva-karmāṇi, lipyate na sa pāpena na saṃbadhyate padma-patram ivāmbhasodakena ||BhGS_5.10||
children.translated_text: Offering, placing in <s>Brahman</s>, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — [thinking] 'I perform action for His sake' — like a servant for the sake of his master — all actions. Having abandoned attachment even to the fruit of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), one who performs all actions — he is not tainted by sin, is not besmirched, just as a lotus leaf [is not tainted] by water. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.10 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: kevalaṃ sattva-śuddhi-mātram eva phalaṃ tasya karmaṇaḥ syāt, yasmāt -
children.translated_text: The fruit of that action would be merely the purification of <s>sattva</s> alone, because —

children.text: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api |
children.translated_text: With the body, with the mind, with the intellect, with the mere senses alone,

children.text: yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātma-śuddhaye ||BhG_5.11||
children.translated_text: <s>yogins</s> perform action, having abandoned attachment, for the purification of the self. // <s>BhG</s> 5.11 //

children.text: kāyena dehena manasā buddhyā ca kevalair mamatva-varjitaiḥ īśvarāyaiva karma karomi, na mama phalāya iti mamatva-buddhi-śūnyair indriyair api - kevala-śabdaḥ kāyādibhir api pratyekaṃ saṃbadhyate, sarva-vyāpāreṣu mamatā-varjanāya | yoginaḥ karmiṇaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phala-viṣayam ātma-śuddhaye sattva-śuddhaya ity arthaḥ | tasmāt tatraiva tavādhikāra iti kuru karmaiva ||BhGS_5.11||
children.translated_text: With the body, with the mind, with the intellect — with these that are 'mere' (<s>kevala</s>), i.e., devoid of the sense of possessiveness — [thinking] 'I perform action for the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) alone, not for my own fruit' — with senses devoid of the attitude of possessiveness. The word '<s>kevala</s>' (mere) is to be connected individually with each — body etc. — for the purpose of removing the sense of possessiveness in all activities. The <s>yogins</s>, the performers of action, perform action having abandoned attachment to results, for the purification of the self (<s>ātma-śuddhi</s>), meaning purification of <s>sattva</s>. Therefore, your qualification too is in this alone — so perform action indeed. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.11 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: yasmāc ca -
children.translated_text: And because —

children.text: yuktaḥ karma-phalaṃ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
children.translated_text: The disciplined one, having abandoned the fruit of action, attains final peace;

children.text: ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate ||BhG_5.12||
children.translated_text: the undisciplined one, impelled by desire, attached to the fruit, is bound. // <s>BhG</s> 5.12 //

children.text: yukta īśvarāya karmaṇi karomi na mama phalāya ity evaṃ samāhitaḥ san karma-phalaṃ tyaktvā parityajya śāntiṃ mokṣākhyām āpnoti naiṣṭhikīṃ niṣṭhāyāṃ bhavāṃ sattva-śuddhi-jñāna-prāpti-sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-jñāna-niṣṭhā-krameṇeti vākya-śeṣaḥ | yas tu punar ayukto 'samāhitaḥ kāma-kāreṇa | karaṇaṃ kāraḥ kāmasya kāraḥ kāma-kāraḥ | tena kāma-kāreṇa kāma-preritatayety arthaḥ | mama phalāya idaṃ karomi karma ity evaṃ phale sakto nibadhyate | atas tvaṃ yukto bhava ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.12||
children.translated_text: The disciplined one (<s>yukta</s>) — one who is concentrated, [thinking] 'I perform action for the Lord; not for my own fruit' — having abandoned, relinquished, the fruit of action, attains peace (<s>śānti</s>) called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is final (<s>naiṣṭhikī</s>), pertaining to the ultimate goal — the completion of the sentence being: through the successive stages of purification of <s>sattva</s>, attainment of knowledge, renunciation of all actions, and steadfastness in knowledge. But one who is undisciplined (<s>ayukta</s>), unconcentrated, impelled by desire-impulse (<s>kāma-kāra</s>). '<s>Kāra</s>' means agency; '<s>kāma-kāra</s>' means the agency of desire; by that desire-impulse — meaning impelled by craving — [thinking] 'I perform this action for my fruit' — thus attached to the fruit, he is bound. Therefore, be disciplined — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.12 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: yas tu paramārtha-darśī saḥ -
children.translated_text: But one who is a seer of the ultimate reality —

children.text: sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī |
children.translated_text: Having renounced all actions mentally, the self-controlled embodied one sits happily

children.text: nava-dvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan ||BhG_5.13||
children.translated_text: in the nine-gated city, neither acting nor causing to act. // <s>BhG</s> 5.13 //

children.text: sarvāṇi karmāṇi sarva-karmāṇi saṃnyasya parityajya nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ ca | tāni sarvāṇi karmāṇi manasā viveka-buddhyā, karmādāv akarma-sandarśanena saṃtyajyety arthaḥ | āste tiṣṭhati sukham | tyakta-vāṅ-manaḥ-kāya-ceṣṭo nirāyāsaḥ prasanna-citta ātmano 'nyatra nivṛtta-sarva-bāhya-prayojana iti sukham āste ity ucyate | vaśī jitendriya ity arthaḥ | kva katham āste ? ity āha - nava-dvāre pure | sapta śīrṣāṇyāny ātmana upalabdhi-dvārāṇi, arvāk dve mūtra-purīṣa-visargārthe, tair dvārair nava-dvāraṃ puram ucyate śarīram puram iva puram | ātmaika-svāmikam, tad-artha-prayojanaiś ca indriya-mano-buddhi-viṣayair aneka-phala-vijñānasyotpādakaiḥ paurair ivādhiṣṭhitam | tasmin nava-dvāre pure dehī sarvaṃ karma saṃnyasyāste |
children.translated_text: Having renounced — relinquished — all actions: the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>), the occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), the desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>), and the prohibited. All those actions [are renounced] mentally — by the intellect of discrimination, by seeing non-action in action — this is the meaning. He sits (<s>āste</s>), abides, happily. One who has ceased from all activity of speech, mind, and body, who is free from exertion, whose mind is serene, who has turned away from all external purposes other than the Self — [of such a one] it is said: 'he sits happily.' '<s>Vaśī</s>' means one who has conquered the senses. Where and how does he sit? He says — in the nine-gated city. The seven openings in the head are the Self's gateways of perception; the two below [serve] for the discharge of urine and feces — by these gates, it is called the 'nine-gated city.' The body is a city, as it were. It has the Self alone as its lord, and is inhabited by the senses, mind, intellect, and objects — which serve the Self's purpose and produce various cognitions of results — like citizens [inhabiting a city]. In that nine-gated city, the embodied one (<s>dehin</s>), having renounced all action, sits.

children.text: kiṃ viśeṣaṇena ? sarvo hi dehī saṃnyāsy asaṃnyāsī vā dehe evāste | tatrānarthakaṃ viśeṣaṇam iti | ucyate - yas tv ajño dehī dehendriya-saṃghāta-mātrātma-darśī sa sarvo 'pi gehe bhūmāv āsane vā ' 'sa iti manyate | na hi deha-mātrātma-darśino geha iva dehe āsa iti pratyayaḥ saṃbhavati | dehādi-saṃghāta-vyatiriktātma-darśinas tu dehe āse iti pratyaya upapadyate | para-karmaṇāṃ ca parasminn ātmany avidyayayādhyāropitānāṃ vidyayā viveka-jñānena manasā saṃnyāsa upapadyate | utpanna-viveka-jñānasya sarva-karma-saṃnyāsino 'pi geha iva deha eva nava-dvāre pura āsanam | prārabdha-phala-karma-saṃskāra-śeṣānuvṛttyā deha eva viśeṣa-vijñānotpatteḥ | dehe evāsta ity asty eva viśeṣaṇa-phalam vidvad-avidvat-pratyaya-bhedāpekṣatvāt |
children.translated_text: What is the purpose of this qualifier? For every embodied being, whether a renunciant or not, dwells in the body alone. Therefore, the qualifier would be purposeless. It is replied: the ignorant embodied one, who sees the Self as nothing more than the aggregate of body and senses — he thinks he sits in a house, on the ground, or on a seat — 'I sit.' For one whose vision of the Self is limited to the body alone, the notion 'I sit in the body' — like 'I sit in a house' — is not possible. But for one who sees the Self as distinct from the aggregate of body etc., the notion 'I sit in the body' is justified. And the mental renunciation of the actions of others [i.e., of the body and senses], which have been superimposed on the Self through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), through knowledge — the discriminative understanding — is justified. For one in whom discriminative knowledge has arisen, who has renounced all actions — his sitting in the body, in the nine-gated city, is like [sitting] in a house, because of the continuation of the residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the actions that have already begun to bear fruit. For discriminative knowledge arises in the body alone. So 'he sits in the body' — this qualifier does indeed have a purpose, since it depends on the distinction between the cognitions of the wise and the unwise.

children.text: yadyapi kārya-karaṇa-karmāṇy avidyayātmany adhyāropitāni saṃnyasyāste ity uktam, tathāpi ātmasamavāyi tu kartṛtvaṃ kārayitṛtvaṃ ca syāt ity āśaṅkyāha - naiva kurvan svayam na kārya-karaṇāni kārayan kriyāsu pravartayan | kiṃ ? yat tat kartṛtvaṃ kārayitṛtvaṃ ca dehinaḥ svātma-samavāyi sat saṃnyāsān na saṃbhavati ? yathā gacchato gatir gamana-vyāpāra-parityāge na syāt tadvat ? kiṃ vā svata eva ātmano nāsti iti ? atrocyate - nāsty ātmanaḥ svataḥ kartṛtvaṃ kārayitṛtvaṃ ca | uktaṃ hi -- avikāryo 'yam ucyate [Gītā 2.55], śarīra-stho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate [Gītā 3.26] iti | dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva [BAU 4.3.7] iti ca śruteḥ ||BhGS_5.13||
children.translated_text: Although it has been said that he sits having renounced through the mind the actions of the body and senses that are superimposed on the Self through ignorance — still, one might suspect that agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) and the capacity to cause action (<s>kārayitṛtva</s>) are inherent in the Self. To this He says: 'neither acting' — not himself [acting], nor causing the body and senses to act, setting them in motion toward activities. What then? Is that agency and capacity-to-cause-action of the embodied one, being inherent in the Self, impossible upon renunciation — just as motion, which is the activity of going, would be impossible for a walker upon abandoning the activity of walking? Or does it simply not belong to the Self by its own nature? To this it is replied: agency and the capacity to cause action do not belong to the Self by its own nature. For it has been said: 'He is said to be unchangeable' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.25], and 'Though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, He neither acts nor is tainted' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.31]. And as per the <s>Śruti</s>: 'He seems to meditate, He seems to move' [<s>BAU</s> 4.3.7]. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.13 //

children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: The Lord (<s>prabhu</s>) creates for the world neither agency nor actions,

children.text: na karma-phala-saṃyogaṃ svabhāvas tu pravartate ||BhG_5.14||
children.translated_text: nor the connection of action with its fruit; but [one's own] nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) proceeds. // <s>BhG</s> 5.14 //

children.text: na kartṛtvaṃ svataḥ kurv iti nāpi karmāṇi ratha-ghaṭa-prāsādādīnīpsitatamāni lokasya sṛjaty utpādayati prabhur ātmā | nāpi rathādi kṛtavatas tat-phalena saṃyogaṃ na karma-phala-saṃyogam | yadi kiṃcid api svato na karoti na kārayati ca dehī, kas tarhi kurvan kārayan ca pravartata iti, ucyate - svabhāvas tu svo bhāvaḥ svabhāvo 'vidyā-lakṣaṇā prakṛtir māyā pravartate daivī hi [Gītā 7.14] ity ādinā vakṣyamāṇā ||BhGS_5.14||
children.translated_text: He does not create agency by His own nature; nor does the Lord (<s>prabhu</s>), the Self, create for the world actions — the most desired things like chariots, pots, palaces, and the like. Nor [does He create] the connection of the one who has made a chariot etc. with the fruit thereof — the connection of action with fruit. If the embodied one neither does anything nor causes anything to be done by its own nature, then who is it that acts and causes to act? It is said: but <s>svabhāva</s> — one's own nature — characterized by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Māyā</s> — which will be described as 'divine indeed' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.14] etc. — that proceeds [of its own accord]. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.14 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: paramārthatas tu -
children.translated_text: But in the ultimate sense —

children.text: nādatte kasya cit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ |
children.translated_text: The all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>) [Lord] takes on neither the sin nor the merit of anyone;

children.text: ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ ||BhG_5.15||
children.translated_text: knowledge is covered by ignorance; by that, beings are deluded. // <s>BhG</s> 5.15 //

children.text: nādatte na ca gṛhṇāti bhaktasyāpi kasyacit pāpam | na caivādatte sukṛtaṃ bhaktaiḥ prayuktaṃ vibhuḥ | kim-arthaṃ tarhi bhaktaiḥ pūjādi-lakṣaṇaṃ yāga-dāna-homādikaṃ ca sukṛtaṃ prayujyate ity āha - ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ viveka-vijñānam, tena muhyanti karomi kārayāmi bhokṣye bhojayāmīty evaṃ mohaṃ gacchanty avivekinaḥ saṃsāriṇo jantavaḥ ||BhGS_5.15||
children.translated_text: He does not take on, does not accept, the sin of anyone, even of a devotee. Nor does the all-pervading one (<s>vibhu</s>) take on the merit offered by devotees. Then why do devotees offer merit in the form of worship — sacrifice, charity, oblation, and the like? He says: knowledge — discriminative understanding — is covered by ignorance; by that [ignorance], beings are deluded — the non-discriminating creatures in <s>saṃsāra</s> go to delusion, [thinking] 'I do, I cause to be done, I shall enjoy, I cause to be enjoyed.' // <s>BhGS</s> 5.15 //

children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: jñānena tu tad ajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: But for those whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by knowledge,

children.text: teṣām ādityavaj jñānaṃ prakāśayati tatparam ||BhG_5.16||
children.translated_text: for them, knowledge, like the sun, illuminates that Supreme [Reality]. // <s>BhG</s> 5.16 //

children.text: jñānena tu yena ajñānena āvṛtāḥ muhyanti jantavas tat ajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ jantūnāṃ viveka-jñānena ātma-viṣayeṇa nāśitam ātmano bhavati, teṣāṃ jantūnām ādityavat yathādityaḥ samastaṃ rūpa-jātam avabhāsayati tadvat jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ vastu sarvaṃ prakāśayati tat paraṃ paramārtha-tattvam ||BhGS_5.16||
children.translated_text: But by the knowledge — by which [ignorance] covers beings and they are deluded — that very ignorance, for those beings whose [ignorance] has been destroyed by discriminative knowledge pertaining to the Self — for those beings, like the sun — just as the sun illuminates the entire range of visible forms — so too, knowledge illuminates the knowable, the entire reality — that Supreme (<s>param</s>), the ultimate truth. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.16 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: yat paraṃ jñānaṃ prakāśitam -
children.translated_text: The Supreme knowledge that has been illuminated —

children.text: tad-buddhayas tad-ātmānas tan-niṣṭhās tat-parāyaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those whose intellect is directed toward That, whose self is That, who are steadfast in That, whose ultimate refuge is That,

children.text: gacchanty apunar-āvṛttiṃ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ ||BhG_5.17||
children.translated_text: they go to the state of no return, their impurities washed away by knowledge. // <s>BhG</s> 5.17 //

children.text: tasmin brahmaṇi gatā buddhir yeṣāṃ te tad-buddhayaḥ, tad-ātmānas tad eva paraṃ brahma ātmā yeṣāṃ te tad-ātmanāḥ, tan-niṣṭhāḥ niṣṭhā abhiniveśas tātparyaṃ sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya tasmin brahmaṇy eva avasthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tan-niṣṭhāḥ, tat-parāyaṇā ca tad eva param ayanaṃ parā gatir yeṣāṃ bhavati te tat-parāyaṇāḥ kevalātma-rataya ity arthaḥ | yeṣāṃ jñānena nāśitam ātmano 'jñānaṃ te gacchanti evaṃ-vidyāḥ apunar-āvṛttim apunar-deha-saṃbandhaṃ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣā yathoktena jñānena nirdhūto nāśitaḥ kalmaṣaḥ pāpādi-saṃsāra-kāraṇa-doṣo yeṣāṃ te jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣā yatayaḥ ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.17||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tad-buddhayaḥ</s>' — those whose intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) has gone to That, <s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Tad-ātmānaḥ</s>' — those for whom That supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone is the Self. '<s>Tan-niṣṭhāḥ</s>' — '<s>niṣṭhā</s>' means fixity, devotion; having renounced all actions, those who abide in That <s>Brahman</s> alone — they are steadfast in That. '<s>Tat-parāyaṇāḥ</s>' — those for whom That alone is the supreme refuge (<s>ayana</s>), the ultimate destination — meaning those who delight in the Self alone. Those whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by knowledge — they, being of such knowledge, go to the state of no return (<s>apunar-āvṛtti</s>), i.e., no renewed connection with a body. Their impurities washed away by knowledge (<s>jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ</s>) — those whose defilements (<s>kalmaṣa</s>), the faults that cause <s>saṃsāra</s> such as sin etc., have been washed away, destroyed by the aforementioned knowledge — they are renunciants (<s>yati</s>) — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.17 //

children.text: - o)O(o -
children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: yeṣāṃ jñānena nāśitam ātmano 'jñānaṃ te paṇḍitāḥ kathaṃ tattvaṃ payantīty ucyate -
children.translated_text: Those learned ones (<s>paṇḍita</s>) whose ignorance of the Self has been destroyed by knowledge — how do they see reality? It is said —

children.text: vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
children.translated_text: In a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant,

children.text: śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ ||BhG_5.18||
children.translated_text: in a dog, and in a dog-eater (<s>śvapāka</s>) — the wise are equal-visioned (<s>sama-darśin</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 5.18 //

children.text: vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne vidyā ca vinayaś ca vidyā-vinayau, vinaya upāmaḥ, tābhyāṃ vidyā-vinayābhyāṃ saṃpanno vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanno vidvān vinītaś ca yo brāhmaṇas tasmin brāhmaṇe gavi hastini śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ | vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne uttama-saṃskāravati brāhmaṇe sāttvike, madhyamāyāṃ ca rājasyāṃ gavi, saṃskāra-hīnāyām atyantam eva kevala-tāmase hasty-ādau ca, sattvādi-guṇais taj-jaiś ca saṃskārais tathā rājasais tathā tāmasaiś ca saṃskārair atyantam evāspṛṣṭāṃ samam ekam avikriyaṃ tad brahma draṣṭuṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ ||BhGS_5.18||
children.translated_text: '<s>Vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanna</s>' — endowed with learning (<s>vidyā</s>) and humility (<s>vinaya</s>); '<s>vinaya</s>' means gentleness, modesty. One who is endowed with these two — learning and humility — such a learned and humble <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; in that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in a cow, in an elephant, in a dog, and in a dog-eater (<s>śvapāka</s>) — the wise are equal-visioned. In the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, endowed with the highest <s>saṃskāras</s> (refinements), who is <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>); in the cow, which is of middling, <s>rājasika</s> nature; in the elephant etc., which are utterly devoid of refinement, entirely <s>tāmasika</s> — through the <s>saṃskāras</s> of <s>sattva</s> etc. and the <s>rājasika</s> and <s>tāmasika</s> qualities and the impressions born of them — [the wise see] that which is utterly untouched by all of these: the one, unchanging <s>Brahman</s>. Those whose disposition (<s>śīla</s>) is to see that — they are the wise (<s>paṇḍita</s>), the equal-visioned. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.18 //

children.translated_text: - o)O(o -

children.text: nanv abhojyānnās te doṣavantaḥ, samāsamābhyāṃ viṣama-same pūjātaḥ [Gautama-dharma-sūtra 2.8.20] iti smṛteḥ | na te doṣavantaḥ | katham ? -
children.translated_text: Objection: Are they not those whose food is prohibited [i.e., defective], and therefore faulty? — [No], as per the <s>Smṛti</s>: 'For the equal and the unequal, through the unequal and the equal, [there is] worship' [<s>Gautama-dharma-sūtra</s> 2.8.20]. No, they are not faulty. How? —

children.text: ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even here [in this life], creation (<s>sarga</s>) has been conquered by those whose mind is established in equality;

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ ||BhG_5.19||
children.translated_text: for <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal — therefore they are established in <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 5.19 //

children.text:
ihaiva jīvadbhireva taiḥ samadarśibhiḥ paṇḍitair jito vaīkṛtaḥ sargo janma, yeṣāṃ sāmye sarva-bhūteṣu brahmaṇi samabhāve sthitaṃ ni calībhūtaṃ mano 'ntaḥkaraṇam | nirdoṣaṃ yadyapi doṣavatsu vapākādiṣu mūḍhais taddoṣair doṣavat iva vibhāvyate, tathāpi taddoṣair aspṛṣṭām iti nirdoṣaṃ doṣavarjitaṃ hi yasmāt | nāpi svaguṇabhedabhinnam, nirguṇatvāt caitanyasya | vakṣyati ca bhagavān icchādīnāṃ kṣetradharmatvam, anāditvānnirguṇatvāt iti ca | nāpy antyā viśeṣāḥ ātmano bhedakāḥ santi, pratiśarīraṃ teṣāṃ sattve pramāṇānupapatteḥ | ataḥ samaṃ brahma ekaṃ ca | tasmāt brahmaṇi eva te sthitāḥ | tasmāt na doṣagandhamātramapi tān spṛati, dehādisaṃghātātma-darśanābhimānābhāvāt teṣām | dehādisaṃghātātma-darśanābhimānavadviṣayaṃ
tu tat sūtram samāsamābhyāṃ viṣamasame pūjātaḥ iti, pūjāviṣayatvena viśeṣaṇāt | dṛśyate hi brahmavit ṣaḍāṅgavit caturvedavit iti pūjādānādau guṇaviśeṣasaṃbandhaḥ kāraṇam | brahma tu sarvaguṇadoṣasaṃbandhavarjitamityatar brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ iti yuktam | karmaviṣayaṃ ca samāsamābhyām ity ādi | idaṃ tu sarva-karma-saṃnyāsaviṣayaṃ prastutam, sarva-karmāṇi manasā ityārabhya ādhyāyaparisamāpteḥ ||BhGS_5.19||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Here in this very life, by those very same equal-visioned scholars, birth (<s>sarga</s>) has been conquered — overcome. For those whose mind, the inner faculty, is established in equanimity — steadied in the equal <s>Brahman</s>, in all beings. Flawless — although <s>Brahman</s> is perceived by the deluded as flawed through association with [the flaws of] bodies etc. such as inferior births, nevertheless it is untouched by those flaws — hence flawless, devoid of faults. Nor is it differentiated by its own distinct qualities, because consciousness is without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). And the Lord will state that desire etc. are properties of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), and also 'because it is beginningless and without qualities.' Nor do ultimate particularities (<s>antyā viśeṣāḥ</s>) serve as differentiators of the Self, since there is no valid means of establishing them in each body. Therefore <s>Brahman</s> is equal and one. Hence they are established in <s>Brahman</s> alone. Therefore, not even a trace of fault touches them, because they do not identify the self with the aggregate of body etc. The <s>sūtra</s> 'through equality and inequality, worship' etc. pertains to the identification of the Self with the aggregate of body etc., since it qualifies with reference to worship. For it is seen that distinctions of qualities — such as 'knower of <s>Brahman</s>,' 'knower of the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s>,' 'knower of four <s>Vedas</s>' — serve as the basis for worship, gifts, etc. But <s>Brahman</s> is free from all connection with qualities and faults — therefore 'they are established in <s>Brahman</s>' is apt. And the [sūtra] 'through equality and inequality' etc. pertains to action. But the present topic concerns the renunciation of all actions — from 'renouncing all actions mentally' to the end of the chapter. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.19 //

children.text: yasmāt nirdoṣaṃ samaṃ brahmātmā, tasmāt -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since the Self, <s>Brahman</s>, is flawless and equal, therefore —

children.text: na prahṛṣyet priyaṃ prāpya nodvijet prāpya cāpriyam |
children.translated_text: One should not rejoice upon obtaining the pleasant, nor be disturbed upon obtaining the unpleasant;

children.text: sthira-buddhir asaṃmūḍho brahmavid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ ||BhG_5.20||
children.translated_text: with steady intellect, undeluded, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is established in <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 5.20 //

children.text: na prahṛṣeyet praharṣaṃ na kuryāt priyam iṣṭāṃ prāpya labdhvā | nodvijet prāpya cāpriyam aniṣṭāṃ labdhvā | deha-mātrātma-darśināṃ hi priyāpriya-prāptī harṣa-viṣādau kurvāte, na kevalātma-darśinaḥ, tasya priyāpriya-prāpty-asaṃbhavāt | kiṃ ca - sarva-bhūteṣv ekaḥ samo nirdoṣa ātmeti sthirā nirvicikitsā buddhir yasya sa sthira-buddhir asaṃmūḍhaḥ saṃmoha-varjitaś ca syāt yathokta-brahmavid brahmaṇi sthito 'karma-kṛt sarva-karma-saṃnyāsīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.20||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] One should not rejoice — should not be elated — upon obtaining, upon receiving, the pleasant, the agreeable. Nor should one be disturbed upon obtaining the unpleasant, upon receiving the disagreeable. For those who see the Self as merely the body, the obtaining of pleasant and unpleasant [things] produces elation and despondency; not so for one who sees the Self alone, since the obtaining of pleasant and unpleasant [things] is impossible for such a one. Moreover — one whose intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) is firm — free from doubt — that the Self is one, equal, and flawless in all beings — such a one is of steady intellect (<s>sthirabuddhi</s>), undeluded, free from confusion; a knower of <s>Brahman</s> as described, established in <s>Brahman</s>, a non-performer of action, a renouncer of all actions — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.20 //

children.text: kiṃ ca, brahmaṇi sthitaḥ -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover, one who is established in <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: bāhya-sparśeṣv asaktātmā vindaty ātmani yat sukham |
children.translated_text: One whose self is unattached to external contacts (<s>sparśa</s>) finds the happiness that is in the Self;

children.text: sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute ||BhG_5.21||
children.translated_text: such a one, whose self is united with <s>Brahman</s> through yoga, attains imperishable happiness. // <s>BhG</s> 5.21 //

children.text: bāhya-sparśeṣu bāhyā ca te sparśāś ca bāhya-sparśāḥ | spṛśyante iti sparśāḥ śabdādayo viṣayās teṣu bāhya-sparśeṣu | asakta ātmā antaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya so 'yam asaktātmā viṣayeṣu prīti-varjitaḥ san vindati labhate | ātmani yat sukhaṃ tad vindatīty etat | sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā brahmaṇi yogaḥ samādhir brahma-yogas tena brahma-yogena yuktaḥ samāhitas tasmin vyāpṛta ātmā antaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya sa brahma-yoga-yuktātmā | sukham akṣayam aśnute vyāpnoti | tasmād bāhya-viṣaya-prīteḥ kṣaṇikāyā indriyāṇi nivartayed ātmany akṣaya-sukhārthīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.21||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In external contacts — external things that are also contacts — these are external contacts (<s>bāhyasparśa</s>); 'contacts' means objects such as sound etc. that are 'touched,' i.e., experienced; in those external contacts — one whose self, i.e., inner faculty, is unattached — free from affection for sense-objects — finds, obtains the happiness that is in the Self — that happiness, one obtains. Such a one, whose self is united with <s>Brahman</s> through yoga (<s>brahmayogayuktātman</s>) — yoga in <s>Brahman</s> is <s>samādhi</s>, that is <s>brahmayoga</s>; one whose inner faculty is united, concentrated, engaged in that <s>brahmayoga</s> — attains, reaches imperishable happiness. Therefore, one who desires imperishable happiness in the Self should withdraw the senses from the pleasure of external objects, which is momentary — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.21 //

[Śaṅkara's commentary:] And for this further reason one should withdraw [the senses] —

children.text: ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te |
children.translated_text: For pleasures that are born of contact are indeed wombs of suffering;

children.text: ādy-anta-vantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ ||BhG_5.22||
children.translated_text: they have a beginning and an end, O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — the wise one does not delight in them. // <s>BhG</s> 5.22 //

children.text: ye hi yasmāt saṃssparśajā viṣayendriya-saṃsparśebhyo jātā bhogā bhuktayo duḥkha-yonaya eva te, avidyā-kṛtatvāt | dṛśyante hy ādhyātmikādīni duḥkhāni tan-nimittāny eva | yathā iha-loke tathā para-loke 'pīti gamyate eva-śabdāt | na saṃsāre sukhasya gandha-mātram apy astīti buddhvā viṣaya-mṛga-tṛṣṇikāyā indriyāṇi nivartayet | na kevalaṃ duḥkha-yonaya eva, ādy-anta-vantaś ca, ādir viṣayendriya-saṃyogo bhogānām antaś ca tad-viyoga eva | ataḥ ādy-anta-vanto 'nityāḥ, madhya-kṣaṇa-bhāvitvāt ity arthaḥ | kaunteya, na teṣu bhogeṣu ramate budho viveky avagata-paramārtha-tattvaḥ | atyanta-mūḍhānām eva hi viṣayeṣu ratir dṛśyate, yathā paśu-prabhṛtīnām ||BhGS_5.22||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] For, since those pleasures that are born of contact — born from the contacts of senses with objects — those enjoyments are indeed wombs of suffering — sources of suffering — because they are produced by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). For it is seen that sufferings pertaining to the body (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) etc. have their cause in these very [contact-born pleasures]. As it is in this world, so it must be in the next world too — this is understood from the word 'indeed.' Having understood that in <s>saṃsāra</s> there is not even a trace of happiness, one should withdraw the senses from the mirage of sense-objects. Not only are they wombs of suffering, but they also have a beginning and an end — the beginning of enjoyments is the contact of senses with objects, and the end is the separation from that [contact]. Therefore, having a beginning and an end, they are impermanent — existing only for the middle moment — this is the meaning. O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, the wise one (<s>budha</s>), the discriminating one who has understood the ultimate truth, does not delight in those pleasures. For delight in sense-objects is seen only in the utterly deluded, such as animals and the like. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.22 //

children.text: ayaṃ ca śreyo-mārga-pratipakṣī kaṣṭatamo doṣaḥ sarvānartha-prāpti-hetur durnivāraś ceti tat-parihāre yatnādhikyaṃ kartavyam ity āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And this — the most formidable flaw, the cause of all misfortune, the adversary of the path to the highest good — is most difficult to overcome; therefore, the Lord says that the greatest effort must be made to overcome it —

children.text: śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: He who is able to withstand, right here [in this life], before the release from the body,

children.text: kāma-krodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ ||BhG_5.23||
children.translated_text: the impulse born of desire and anger — he is disciplined, he is the happy person. // <s>BhG</s> 5.23 //

children.text:
śaknoty utsahata ihaiva jīvann eva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prasahituṃ prāk pūrvam śarīravimokṣaṇāt ā maraṇāt ity arthaḥ | maraṇa-sīmā-karaṇaṃ jīvato 'vayaṃbhāvi hi kāma-krodhodbhavo vegaḥ, anantanimittavān hi saḥ iti yāvat maraṇaṃ tāvat na visrāmbhaṇīya ity arthaḥ | kāmaḥ indriyagocaraprāpte iṣṭo viṣaye śrūyamāṇe smaryamāṇe vā anubhūte sukhahetau yā gaṄdhas tṛṣṇā sa kāmaḥ | krodhaś cātmanaḥ pratikūleṣu duḥkha-hetuṣu dṛyamāneṣu śrūyamāṇeṣu smaryamāṇeṣu vā yo dveṣaḥ sa krodhaḥ | tau kāma-krodhāv udbhavo yasya vegasya sa kāma-krodhodbhavo vegaḥ | romāñcana-prahṛṣṭa-netra-vadanādi-liṅgo 'ntaḥ-karaṇa-prakṣobha-rūpaḥ kāmodbhavo vegaḥ | gātra-prakampa-prasveda-saṃdaṣṭauṣṭha-puṭa-rakta-netrādi-liṅgaḥ krodhodbhavo
vegaḥ | taṃ kāma-krodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ ya utsahate prasahate soḍhuṃ prasahitum, so yukto yogī sukhī ceha loke naraḥ || ||BhGS_5.23||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] He who is able — has the strength — right here, while still alive, to withstand, to endure, before the release from the body — before death, until death, is the meaning. The mention of death as a boundary [implies that] the impulse born of desire and anger is inevitable as long as one lives — for it arises from countless causes; therefore, until death, one should not be complacent — this is the meaning. Desire (<s>kāma</s>) — when a desirable sense-object is encountered, heard of, or remembered — that longing, that craving, which is the inclination toward a pleasurable cause that has been experienced — that is desire. And anger (<s>krodha</s>) — toward things that are adverse, that are causes of suffering, when seen, heard of, or remembered — that hatred is anger. The impulse that is born from desire and anger — the impulse born of desire is characterized by the signs of horripilation, gleaming eyes, joyful expression, etc. — a disturbance of the inner faculty. The impulse born of anger is characterized by the signs of trembling limbs, perspiration, bitten lips, red eyes, etc. He who has the strength to endure, to withstand that impulse born of desire and anger — he is disciplined (<s>yukta</s>), a <s>yogin</s>, and happy in this world. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.23 //

children.text: kathaṃ-bhūtaś ca brahmaṇi sthito brahma prāpnoti ? ity āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And what kind of person, being established in <s>Brahman</s>, attains <s>Brahman</s>? The Lord says —

children.text: yo 'ntaḥ-sukho 'ntarārāmas tathāntar-jyotir eva yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and likewise whose light is within —

children.text: sa yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṃ brahma-bhūto 'dhigacchati ||BhG_5.24||
children.translated_text: that <s>yogin</s>, having become <s>Brahman</s>, attains the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmanirvāṇa</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 5.24 //

children.text: yo 'ntaḥ-sukho 'ntar ātmani sukhaṃ yasya so 'ntaḥ-sukhaḥ, tathāntar evātmany ārāma āramaṇam ākrīḍā yasya so 'ntar-ārāmaḥ | tathaivāntar eva ātmany eva jyotiḥ prakāśo yasya so 'ntar-jyotir eva, ya īdṛśaḥ so yogī brahma-nirvāṇaṃ brahmaṇi nirvṛtiṃ mokṣam iha jīvann eva brahma-bhūtaḥ sann adhigacchati prāpnoti ||BhGS_5.24||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] He whose happiness is within — one whose happiness is in the inner Self — is <s>antaḥsukha</s> (one of inner happiness). Likewise, one whose delight (<s>ārāma</s>), recreation, play, is within, in the Self — is <s>antarārāma</s> (one of inner delight). Likewise, one whose light (<s>jyotis</s>), illumination, is within, in the Self alone — is <s>antarjyotis</s> (one of inner light). One who is such — that <s>yogin</s> attains <s>brahmanirvāṇa</s> — bliss in <s>Brahman</s>, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — right here, while still alive, having become <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.24 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: The seers (<s>ṛṣi</s>) whose impurities are destroyed, whose doubts are rent asunder,

children.text: chinna-dvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||BhG_5.25||
children.translated_text: who are self-restrained and devoted to the welfare of all beings — they attain the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 5.25 //

children.text: labhante brahma-nirvāṇaṃ mokṣam ṛṣayaḥ samyag-darśinaḥ saṃnyāsinaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ kṣīṇa-pāpā nirdoṣāś chinna-dvaidhāḥ chinna-saṃśayā yatātmānaḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ hite ānukūlye ratā ahiṃsakā ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.25||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The seers (<s>ṛṣi</s>) — those of right vision, renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) — whose impurities are destroyed, whose sins are eliminated, who are flawless; whose doubts are rent asunder, whose uncertainties have been cut; who are self-restrained (<s>yatātman</s>), with senses controlled; who are devoted to the welfare of all beings — delighting in what is beneficial, favorable, for all beings — meaning non-violent (<s>ahiṃsaka</s>) — they attain the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, liberation. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.25 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: kāma-krodha-viyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yata-cetasām |
children.translated_text: For those ascetics who are freed from desire and anger, whose minds are restrained,

children.text: abhito brahma-nirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām ||BhG_5.26||
children.translated_text: who have known the Self — the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> exists all around. // <s>BhG</s> 5.26 //

children.text: kāma-krodha-viyuktānāṃ kāmaś ca krodhaś ca kāma-krodhau tābhyāṃ viyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ saṃnyāsināṃ yata-cetasāṃ saṃyatāntaḥ-karaṇānām abhita ubhayato jīvatāṃ mṛtānāṃ ca brahma-nirvāṇaṃ mokṣo vartate viditātmanāṃ vidito jñāta ātmā yeṣāṃ te viditātmanāṃ teṣāṃ viditātmanāṃ samyag-darśinām ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_5.26||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] For those freed from desire and anger — desire and anger are <s>kāmakrodha</s>; for those freed from them — ascetics (<s>yati</s>), renunciants, whose minds are restrained, whose inner faculties are controlled — the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, liberation, exists all around (<s>abhitas</s>) — on both sides, both while living and after death — for those who have known the Self, those whose Self has been known and realized — for those of right vision — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.26 //

samyag darśana-niṣṭhānāṃ saṃnyāsināṃ sadyo-muktir uktā | karma-yogaś ca īśvarārpita-sarva-bhāveneśvare brahmaṇy ādhāya kriyamāṇaḥ sattva-śuddhi-jñāna-prāpti-sarva-karma-saṃnyāsa-krameṇa mokṣāya iti bhagavān pade pade 'bravīt, vakṣyati ca | athedānīṃ dhyāna-yogaṃ samyag-darśanasya antaraṅgaṃ vistareṇa vakṣyāmīti tasya sūtra-sthānīyān ślokān upadiśati sma -

- o)O(o -
[Śaṅkara's commentary:] Immediate liberation has been declared for renunciants established in right knowledge. And <s>karmayoga</s>, performed with the attitude of offering everything to the Lord, to <s>Brahman</s>, [leads to] liberation through the sequence of purification of the mind, attainment of knowledge, and renunciation of all actions — this the Lord has stated at every step, and will state [further]. Now, 'I shall elaborate on <s>dhyānayoga</s> (the yoga of meditation), which is the inner component of right knowledge' — saying this, he teaches verses that serve as aphorisms for it:

children.text: sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṃś cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ |
children.translated_text: Having excluded external contacts outside, and [fixing] the gaze between the eyebrows,

children.text: prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantara-cāriṇau ||BhG_5.27||
children.translated_text: having equalized the <s>prāṇa</s> (outgoing breath) and <s>apāna</s> (incoming breath), moving within the nostrils, // <s>BhG</s> 5.27 //

children.text: yatendriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: with senses, mind, and intellect restrained, the sage (<s>muni</s>) intent on liberation,

children.text: vigatecchā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ ||BhG_5.28||
children.translated_text: from whom desire, fear, and anger have departed — one who is always thus is verily liberated. // <s>BhG</s> 5.28 //

children.text: sparśān śabdādīn kṛtvā bahir bāhyān śrotrādi-dvāreṇāntar-buddhau praveśitāḥ śabdādayo viṣayās tān acintayato śabdādayo bāhyā bahir eva kṛtā bhavanti | tān evaṃ bahiḥ kṛtvā cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ kṛtvety anuṣajyate | tathā prāṇāpānau nāsābhyantara-cāriṇau samau kṛtvā | yatendriya-mano-buddhir yatāni saṃyatānīndriyāṇi mano buddhiś ca yasya sa yatendriya-mano-buddhiḥ | mananāt muniḥ saṃnyāsī | mokṣa-parāyaṇa evaṃ deha-saṃsthānān mokṣa-parāyaṇo mokṣa eva param ayanaṃ parā gatir yasya so 'yaṃ mokṣa-parāyaṇo munir bhavet | vigatecchā-bhaya-krodha icchā ca bhayaṃ ca krodhaś cecchā-bhaya-krodhās te vigatāḥ yasmāt sa vigatecchā-bhaya-krodhaḥ | ya evaṃ vartate sadā saṃnyāsī, mukta eva saḥ | na tasya mokṣo 'nyaḥ kartavyo 'sti ||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] External contacts — sounds and such — having excluded them outside. Sounds and other objects that have been admitted inward through the doorways of the ear and other [senses] into the inner intellect — when one ceases to attend to them, the sounds etc. become as if made external. Having thus made them external, and [fixing] the gaze between the eyebrows — 'having fixed' is to be supplied. Likewise, having equalized the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, moving within the nostrils. With senses, mind, and intellect restrained — one whose senses, mind, and intellect have been controlled, restrained — such a one. A <s>muni</s> — one who reflects, a renunciant. Intent on liberation — one for whom liberation alone is the supreme destination, the highest goal — such a <s>muni</s> should be, established in this bodily posture. From whom desire, fear, and anger have departed — desire, fear, and anger — these have departed from whom. One who lives thus always — such a renunciant — is verily liberated. There is no other liberation for him to achieve. //

children.text: bhoktāraṃ yajña-tapasāṃ sarva-loka-maheśvaram |
children.translated_text: [Knowing Me as] the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds,

children.text: suhṛdaṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntim ṛcchati ||BhG_5.29||
children.translated_text: the friend of all beings — knowing Me [thus], one attains peace. // <s>BhG</s> 5.29 //

children.text: evaṃ samāhita-cittena kiṃ vijñeyam ity ucyate | bhoktāraṃ yajña-tapasāṃ yajñānāṃ tapasāṃ ca kartṛ-rūpeṇa devatā-rūpeṇa ca, sarva-loka-maheśvaraṃ sarveṣāṃ lokānāṃ mahāntam īśvaraṃ suhṛdaṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ sarva-prāṇināṃ pratyupakāra-nirapekṣatayā upakāriṇaṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛdayeśayaṃ sarva-karma-phalādhyakṣaṃ sarva-pratyaya-sākṣiṇaṃ māṃ nārāyaṇaṃ jñātvā śāntiṃ sarva-saṃsāroparatim ṛcchati prāpnoti ||BhGS_5.29||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] What should be known by one whose mind is thus concentrated? It is stated: [knowing Me as] the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities — of sacrifices and austerities, both in the form of the agent [i.e., the one who enjoys the fruits] and in the form of the deity [to whom they are offered]; the great Lord of all worlds — the great ruler of all the worlds; the friend (<s>suhṛd</s>) of all beings — the benefactor of all living beings, without expectation of reciprocal benefit — the one who resides in the hearts of all beings, the superintendent of the fruits of all actions, the witness of all cognitions — [knowing] Me, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — one attains peace (<s>śānti</s>), the cessation of all <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 5.29 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
