children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>, composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most revered <s>paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya</s>, disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>.

children.text: BhG 6
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 6

children.text: atha ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the sixth chapter.

children.text: (śaṅkarācārya-bhāṣyaḥ)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śaṅkarācārya's</s> commentary)

children.text: atītānantarādhyāyānte dhyāna-yogasya samyag darśanaṃ praty antaraṅgasya sūtra-bhūtāḥ ślokāḥ sparśān kṛtvā bahiḥ [Gītā 5.27] ity ādaya upadiṣṭaḥ | teṣāṃ vṛtti-sthānīyo 'yaṃ ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāya ārabhyate | tatra dhyāna-yogasya bahiraṅgaṃ karmeti yāvad dhyāna-yogārohaṇa-samarthas tāvad gṛhasthenādhikṛtena kartavyaṃ karma ity atas tat stauti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] At the end of the immediately preceding chapter, the verses beginning with 'Having excluded external contacts' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.27] etc. — which serve as aphoristic threads for the complete vision of <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> (the yoga of meditation) as the inner limb — were taught. This sixth chapter, which stands as the elaboration of those [aphoristic verses], is now commenced. Therein, action is the external limb of <s>dhyāna-yoga</s>; so long as one is not capable of ascending to <s>dhyāna-yoga</s>, action must be performed by the qualified householder — therefore he praises it.

children.text: nanu kim-arthaṃ dhyāna-yogārohaṇa-sīmā-karaṇam, yāvatānuṣṭheyam eva vihitaṃ karma yāvajjīvam | na, ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate [Gītā 3.3] iti viśeṣaṇāt | ārūḍhasya ca śamenaiva saṃbandha-karaṇāt | ārurukṣor ārūḍhasya ca śamaḥ karmaś cobhayaṃ kartavyatvenābhipretaṃ cet syāt tadārurukṣor ārūḍhasya ceti śama-karma-viṣaya-bhedena viśeṣaṇaṃ vibhāga-karaṇaṃ cānarthakaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: Why is there a limit — the ascent to <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> — [for performing action]? Should not the enjoined action be performed throughout one's entire life? No — because of the specification 'For the sage who wishes to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.3]. And because, for one who has ascended, the connection is made with tranquility (<s>śama</s>) alone. If both tranquility and action were intended as obligatory for both the one wishing to ascend and the one who has ascended, then the specification and the division made according to the different subjects of tranquility and action — for the one wishing to ascend and the one who has ascended — would be purposeless.

children.text: tatrāśramiṇāṃ kaścid yogam ārurukṣur bhavati | ārūḍhaś ca kaścit | anye nārurukṣavaḥ | na cārūḍhāḥ | tān apekṣyārurukṣor ārūḍhasya ceti viśeṣaṇaṃ vibhāga-karaṇaṃ copapadyata eveti cet, na | tasyaiveti vacanāt | punar yoga-grahaṇāc ca yogārūḍhasyeti | ya āsīt pūrvaṃ yogam ārurukṣus tasyaivārūḍhasya śama eva kartavyaḥ | kāraṇaṃ yoga-phalaṃ pratyucyateti | ato na yāvaj-jīvaṃ kartavyatva-prāptiḥ kasyacid api karmaṇaḥ | yoga-vibhraṣṭa-vacanāc ca |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the <s>āśramins</s> (those in the stages of life), someone may wish to ascend to yoga, and another may have already ascended, while others neither wish to ascend nor have ascended. [Objection:] In view of those [others], the specification and division for the one wishing to ascend and the one who has ascended is indeed appropriate? No — because of the word 'of that very one' (<s>tasyaiva</s>) [in <s>Gītā</s> 6.3]. And because of the repeated use of the word 'yoga' in 'for one who has ascended to yoga' (<s>yogārūḍhasya</s>). For the very one who previously wished to ascend to yoga — for that very person, once ascended, tranquility alone is the duty. 'The means' is said to be the [means to the] fruit of yoga. Therefore, there is no entailment that any action whatsoever must be performed throughout one's entire life. And [this is confirmed] also by the statement regarding one who has fallen from yoga.

children.text: gṛhasthasya cet karmiṇo yogo vihitaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'dhyāye, sa yoga-vibhraṣṭo 'pi karma-gatiṃ karma-phalaṃ prāpnotīti tasya nāśāśaṅkānupapannā syāt | avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma kāmyaṃ nityaṃ vā mokṣasya nityatvād anārabhyatve svaṃ phalam ārabhata eva | nityasya ca karmaṇo veda-pramāṇāvabuddhatvāt phalena bhavitavyam ity avocāma | anyathā vedasyānarthārthatva-prasaṅgād iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If yoga is prescribed in the sixth chapter for a householder who is a performer of rituals, then even if fallen from yoga, he would still attain the result of action (<s>karma-gati</s>), the fruit of action, and the apprehension of destruction [of his efforts] would be groundless. For surely performed action — whether desire-motivated or obligatory — must produce its fruit, since [the aspirant's] liberation is eternal; and if action is not commenced, [the performed action] necessarily produces its own fruit. And we have stated that obligatory action, being known through the authority of the Veda, must have a fruit; otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that the Veda teaches what is purposeless.

children.text: na ca karmaṇi saty ubhaya-vibhraṣṭa-vacanam arthavat | karmaṇo vibhraṃśa-kāraṇānupapatteḥ | karma kṛtam īśvare saṃnyasyety ataḥ kartari karma phalaṃ nārabhateti cen, na | īśvare saṃnyāsasyādhikatara-phala-hetutvopapatteḥ | mokṣāyaiveti cet, sva-karmaṇāṃ kṛtānām īśvare nyāso mokṣāyaiva, na phalāntarāya yoga-sahitaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And if action is present, the statement about being 'fallen from both' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.38] has no meaning — because there is no ground for falling from action. [Objection:] Since action was performed and renounced to the Lord, therefore action does not produce its fruit for the agent? No — because the renunciation to the Lord is more appropriately a cause of greater fruit. [Objection:] It is for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) alone [that action is renounced]? The depositing of one's performed actions in the Lord is for <s>mokṣa</s> alone, not for any other fruit — [this applies] when combined with yoga.

children.text: yogāc ca vibhraṣṭa ity atas taṃ prati nāśa-śaṅkā yuktaiveti cet, na | ekākī yata-cittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ [Gītā 6.10] brahmacāri-vrate sthitaḥ [Gītā 6.14] iti karma-saṃnyāsa-vidhānāt | na cātra gṛhasthasya nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ ity ādi-vacanam anukūlam | ubhaya-vibhraṣṭa-praśnānupapatteś ca |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] Since he has also fallen from yoga, the apprehension of destruction regarding him is indeed justified? No — because the injunction of renunciation of action [is given by the text]: 'Alone, with mind and self controlled, free from expectations, without possessions' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.10], 'established in the vow of <s>brahmacarya</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.14]. And here, the statements 'free from expectations, without possessions' etc. are not compatible with a householder. And the question about being 'fallen from both' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.38] would be groundless [for a householder with accumulated merit from action].

children.text: anāśrita ity anena karmiṇa eva saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ coktam, pratiṣiddhaṃ ca niragneḥ akriyasya ca saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ ceti cet, na | dhyāna-yogaṃ prati bahiraṅgasya sataḥ karmaṇaḥ phalākāṅkṣā-saṃnyāsa-stuti-paratvāt |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] By 'one who, not depending [on the fruit of action]' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.1], the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> is stated for the performer of action alone, and the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> is denied for one who is without fire and without ritual activity? No — because [the verse] is intended to praise the renunciation of desire for fruits, since action is an external limb with respect to <s>dhyāna-yoga</s>.

children.text:
na kevalaṃ niragnir akriya eva saṃnyāsī yogī ca | kiṃ tarhi ? karmy api, karma-phalāsaṅgaṃ saṃnyasya karma-yogam anutiṣṭhan sattva-śuddhy-arthaṃ, sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca bhavatīti stūyate | na caikena vākyena karma-phalāsaṅga-saṃnyāsa-stutiś caturthāśrama-pratiṣedhaś copapadyate | na ca prasiddhaṃ niragner akriyasya paramārtha-saṃnyāsinaḥ śruti-smṛti-purāṇetihāsa-yoga-śāstreṣu vihitaṃ saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ ca pratiṣedhati bhagavān | sva-vacana-virodhāc ca - sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasya... naiva kurvan na kārayan āste [Gītā 5.13] maunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kenacit... aniketaḥ sthira-matiḥ [Gītā 12.19] vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati niḥspṛhaḥ [Gītā 2.71] sarvārambha-parityāgī [Gītā 12.16] iti ca tatra tatra bhagavatā sva-vacanāni darśitāni | tair virudhyetaś caturthāśrama-pratiṣedhaḥ
| tasmān muner yogam ārurukṣoḥ pratipanna-gārhasthyasyāgnihotrādi-karma phala-nirapekṣam anuṣṭhīyamānaṃ dhyāna-yogārohaṇa-sādhanatvaṃ sattva-śuddhi-dvāreṇa pratipadyata iti sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ceti stūyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Not only one who is without fire and without ritual activity is a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and a <s>yogin</s>. But who else? Even the performer of action — who, having renounced attachment to the fruits of action, continues to perform <s>karma-yoga</s> for the purification of the mind (<s>sattva-śuddhi</s>) — that one is praised as being a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and a <s>yogin</s>. And by a single sentence, both the praise of renouncing attachment to the fruits of action and the negation of the fourth <s>āśrama</s> (the order of renunciation) cannot be accomplished. Nor does the Blessed Lord negate the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> for the renunciant in the ultimate sense — one who is without fire and without ritual activity — which is well-established in the <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, <s>Itihāsa</s>, and yoga scriptures. And because of the contradiction with His own words: 'Renouncing all actions mentally... neither acting nor causing to act, [the embodied one] rests' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.13], 'Silent, content with anything... homeless, of firm resolve' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.19], 'One who, abandoning all desires, moves about without craving' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.71], 'one who has given up all undertakings' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.16] — these and similar statements have been shown by the Blessed Lord in various places. A negation of the fourth <s>āśrama</s> would contradict these. Therefore, for the sage who wishes to ascend to yoga and who has adopted the householder life, the performance of rituals such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> without regard for their fruits becomes a means for ascending to <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> through the purification of the mind — thus such a one is praised as 'a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and a <s>yogin</s>' —

children.text: anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who performs obligatory action without depending on the fruit of action —

children.text: sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ ||BhG_6.1||
children.translated_text: that one is the <s>saṃnyāsin</s> (renunciant) and the <s>yogin</s>; not merely one who is without fire, nor one who is without ritual activity. // <s>BhG</s> 6.1 //

children.text: anāśrito -- nāśrito 'nāśritaḥ | kim ? karma-phalaṃ karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ karma-phalaṃ yat tad-anāśritaḥ, karma-phala-tṛṣṇā-rahita ity arthaḥ | yo hi karma-phale tṛṣṇāvān sa karma-phalam āśrito bhavati | ayaṃ tu tad-viparītaḥ, ato 'nāśritaḥ karma-phalam | evaṃbhūtaḥ san kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ nityaṃ kāmya-viparītam agnihotrādikaṃ karma karoti nirvartayati | yaḥ kaścid īdṛśaḥ karmī sa karmy antarebhyo viśiṣyate | ity evam artham āha - sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ceti | saṃnyāsaḥ parityāgaḥ sa yasyāsti sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca | yogaś citta-samādhānaṃ sa yasyāsti sa yogī ceti evaṃguṇa-saṃpanno 'yaṃ mantavyaḥ | na kevalaṃ niragnir akriya eva saṃnyāsī yogī ceti mantavyaḥ | nirgatāḥ agnayaḥ karmāṅga-bhūtā yasmāt sa niragniḥ | akriyaś cānagni-sādhanāpy avidyamānāḥ
kriyās tapo-dānādikā yasyāsāv akriyaḥ ||BhGS_6.1||
children.translated_text: such as austerity, charity, and the like — that one is 'without activity.' // <s>BhGS</s> 6.1 //

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Not depending' (<s>anāśrita</s>) — not relying upon. On what? On the fruit of action — that which is the fruit of actions; not relying on that — meaning: free from craving for the fruit of action. For one who has craving for the fruit of action is one who relies upon the fruit of action. But this one is the opposite of that; therefore, [he is one] not relying on the fruit of action. Being such, one who performs — carries out — obligatory action (<s>kārya karma</s>), i.e., constant [duty], the opposite of desire-motivated [action], such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like. Whoever is such a performer of action excels among performers of action — with this purpose, [the Lord] says: 'that one is a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and a <s>yogin</s>.' <s>Saṃnyāsa</s> means abandonment; one who possesses that is a <s>saṃnyāsin</s>; and [that one is also] a <s>yogin</s>. Yoga means concentration of mind (<s>citta-samādhāna</s>); one who possesses that is a <s>yogin</s> — thus one endowed with such qualities should be understood. Not merely one who is without fire and without ritual activity should be considered a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and a <s>yogin</s>. 'Without fire' (<s>niragni</s>) — one from whom the sacrificial fires, which are limbs of ritual, have departed. And 'without activity' (<s>akriya</s>) — one who lacks even those activities that do not require fire as an instrument,

children.text: nanu ca niragneḥ akriyasyaiva śruti-smṛti-yoga-śāstreṣu saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ ca prasiddham | katham iha sāgneḥ sa-kriyasya ca saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ cāprasiddham ucyata iti | naiṣa doṣaḥ, kayācid guṇa-vṛttyā ubhayasya saṃpipādayiṣitatvāt | tat katham ? karma-phala-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsāt saṃnyāsitvam, yogāṅgatvena ca karmānuṣṭhānāt karma-phala-saṃkalpasya ca citta-vikṣepa-hetoḥ parityāgād yogitvaṃ ceti gauṇam ubhayam | na punar mukhyaṃ saṃnyāsitvaṃ yogitvaṃ cābhipretam ity etam arthaṃ darśayitum āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: But the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> for one who is without fire and without ritual activity is well-known in the <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and yoga scriptures. How can the unprecedented status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> for one who has fire and performs rituals be stated here? This is not a fault — because both [designations] are intended to be established through some secondary usage (<s>gauṇa-vṛtti</s>). How so? Through the renunciation of the intention for the fruit of action, [he has] the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s>; and through the performance of action as a limb of yoga and through the abandonment of the intention for the fruit of action — which is a cause of mental distraction — [he has] the status of <s>yogin</s>; both are secondary. It is not the primary sense of <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and <s>yogin</s> that is intended — to show this meaning, [the Lord] says:

children.text: yaṃ saṃnyāsam iti prāhur yogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
children.translated_text: What they call <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation), know that to be yoga, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>;

children.text: na hy asaṃnyasta-saṃkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||BhG_6.2||
children.translated_text: for no one who has not renounced [all] intentions becomes a <s>yogin</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 6.2 //

children.text:
yaṃ sarva-karma-tat-phala-parityāga-lakṣaṇaṃ paramārtha-saṃnyāsaṃ saṃnyāsam iti prāhuḥ śruti-smṛti-vidaḥ, yogaṃ karmānuṣṭhāna-lakṣaṇaṃ taṃ paramārtha-saṃnyāsaṃ viddhi jānīhi he pāṇḍāva | karma-yogasya pravṛtti-lakṣaṇasya tad-viparītena nivṛtti-lakṣaṇena paramārtha-saṃnyāsena kīdṛśaṃ sāmānyam aṅgīkṛtya tad-bhāva ucyate ity apekṣāyām idam ucyate - asti hi paramārtha-saṃnyāsena sādṛśyaṃ kartṛ-dvārakaṃ karma-yogasya | yo hi paramārtha-saṃnyāsī sa tyakta-sarva-karma-sādhanatayā sarva-karma-tat-phala-viṣayaṃ saṃkalpaṃ pravṛtti-hetu-kāma-kāraṇaṃ saṃnyasyati | ayam api karma-yogī karma kurvāṇa eva phala-viṣayaṃ saṃkalpaṃ saṃnyasyatīti | etam arthaṃ darśayiṣyann āha - na hi yasmād asaṃnyasta-saṃkalpo 'saṃnyasto 'parityaktaḥ saṅkalpo
'bhisandhir yena so 'saṃnyasta-saṅkalpaḥ kaścana kaścid api karmī yogī samādhānavān bhavati | na saṃbhavatīty arthaḥ | phala-saṃkalpasya citta-vikṣepa-hetutvāt | tasmād yaḥ kaścana karmī saṃnyasta-phala-saṃkalpo bhavet sa yogī samādhānavān avikṣipta-citto bhavet | citta-vikṣepa-hetoḥ phala-saṃkalpasya saṃnyastatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ | yogāṅgatvena karmānuṣṭhānāt karma-phala-saṅkalpasya vā citta-vikṣepa-hetoḥ parityāgāt yogitvaṃ ceti saṃnyāsitvaṃ cety abhipretam ucyate |[*NOTE: This last sentence not found in all editions.] ||BhGS_6.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That which — characterized as the complete abandonment of all actions and their fruits — is <s>saṃnyāsa</s> in the ultimate sense, which those who know the <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> call 'renunciation' — know that ultimate renunciation to be yoga, characterized as the performance of action, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. What commonality between <s>karma-yoga</s>, which is characterized by engagement, and ultimate renunciation, characterized by disengagement, has been accepted such that the latter's designation is applied [to the former]? — in response to this expectation, the following is said: There is indeed a resemblance between <s>karma-yoga</s> and ultimate renunciation, a resemblance mediated through the agent. For the one who is an ultimate renunciant — by virtue of having abandoned all means of action — renounces the intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) regarding all actions and their fruits, the intention that is the cause of desire motivating engagement. This <s>karma-yogin</s> too, even while performing action, renounces the intention regarding fruits. To show this point, [the Lord] says: 'For' — since — no one who has not renounced intention (<s>asaṃnyasta-saṃkalpa</s>) — one whose intention, i.e., purposeful resolve, has not been renounced, not abandoned — no performer of action whatsoever becomes a <s>yogin</s>, one of concentrated mind. This is not possible — this is the meaning. Because the intention for fruits is a cause of mental distraction. Therefore, whichever performer of action has renounced the intention for fruits would be a <s>yogin</s>, one of concentrated, undistracted mind. The purport is: because the intention for fruits, which is the cause of mental distraction, has been renounced. The status of <s>yogin</s> through the performance of action as a limb of yoga, and [the status of <s>saṃnyāsin</s>] through the abandonment of the intention for the fruit of action — which is a cause of mental distraction — is what is intended [as secondary]. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.2 //

children.text: evaṃ paramārtha-saṃnyāsa-karma-yogayoḥ kartṛ-dvārakaṃ saṃnyāsa-sāmānyam apekṣya yaṃ saṃnyāsam iti prāhur yogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍāva [Gītā 6.2] iti karma-yogasya stuty-arthaṃ saṃnyāsatvam uktam | dhyāna-yogasya phala-nirapekṣaḥ karma-yogo bahiraṅgaṃ sādhanam iti taṃ saṃnyāsatvena stutvādhunā karma-yogasya dhyāna-yoga-sādhanatvaṃ darśayati -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Thus, having considered the commonality of renunciation between ultimate <s>saṃnyāsa</s> and <s>karma-yoga</s> — mediated through the agent — the designation of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> was applied to <s>karma-yoga</s> for the purpose of praising it: 'What they call <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, know that to be yoga, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 6.2]. Having thus praised <s>karma-yoga</s> as <s>saṃnyāsa</s> — since <s>karma-yoga</s>, performed without regard for fruits, is an external means for <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> — [the Lord] now shows the instrumental relationship of <s>karma-yoga</s> to <s>dhyāna-yoga</s>:

children.text: ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate |
children.translated_text: For the sage who wishes to ascend to yoga, action is said to be the means;

children.text: yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate ||BhG_6.3||
children.translated_text: for that very one who has ascended to yoga, tranquility (<s>śama</s>) is said to be the means. // <s>BhG</s> 6.3 //

children.text: ārurukṣor āroḍhum icchataḥ, anārūḍhasya, dhyāna-yoge 'vasthātum aśaktasyaivety arthaḥ | kasya tasyārurukṣoḥ ? muneḥ, karma-phala-saṃnyāsina ity arthaḥ | kim ārurukṣoḥ ? yogam | karma kāraṇaṃ sādhanam ucyate | yogārūḍhasya punas tasyaiva śamar upaśamaḥ sarva-karmabhyo nivṛttiḥ kāraṇaṃ yogārūḍhasya sādhanam ucyate ity arthaḥ | yāvad yāvat karmabhya uparamate, tāvat tāvat nirāyāsasya jitendriyasya cittaṃ samādhīyate | tathā sati sa jhaṭiti yogārūḍho bhavati | tathā coktaṃ vyāsena -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Wishing to ascend' (<s>ārurukṣu</s>) — one who desires to climb up — one who has not yet ascended, one who is unable to remain established in <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> — this is the meaning. Of which such aspirant? Of the sage (<s>muni</s>) — meaning: one who has renounced the fruits of action. Wishing to ascend to what? To yoga. Action is said to be the means, the instrument. But for that very one who has ascended to yoga — for that same person — tranquility (<s>śama</s>), i.e., cessation from all actions, is said to be the means — the instrument for one who has ascended to yoga — this is the meaning. To the extent that one withdraws from actions, to that extent the mind of one who is effortless and has conquered the senses becomes concentrated. Being so, one quickly becomes established in yoga. And thus it has been said by <s>Vyāsa</s>:

children.text:
naitādṛśaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti vittaṃ
yathaikatā samatā satyatā ca |
śīlaṃ sthitir daṇḍa-nidhānam ārjavaṃ
tatas tataś coparamaḥ kriyābhyaḥ || [Mbh 12.175.37] iti ||BhGS_6.3||
children.translated_text:
'There is no wealth for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> equal to this:
unity, equanimity, truthfulness,
good conduct, steadiness, putting down the rod, straightforwardness,
and gradually, withdrawal from actions' [<s>Mbh</s> 12.175.37]. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.3 //

children.text: athedānīṃ kadā yogārūḍho bhavatīty ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, when does one become established in yoga (<s>yogārūḍha</s>)? It is said:

children.text: yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate |
children.translated_text: When one does not cling to sense-objects nor to actions,

children.text: sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsī yogārūḍhas tadocyate ||BhG_6.4||
children.translated_text: having renounced all intentions (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) — then one is said to have ascended to yoga. // <s>BhG</s> 6.4 //

children.text: yadā samādhīyamāna-citto yogī hīndriyārtheṣv indriyāṇām arthāḥ śabdādayas teṣv indriyārtheṣu karmasu ca nitya-naimittika-kāmya-pratiṣiddheṣu prayojanābhāva-buddhyā nānuṣajjate 'nuṣaṅgaṃ kartavyatā-buddhiṃ na karotīty arthaḥ | sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsī sarvān saṃkalpān ihāmutrārtha-kāma-hetūna saṃnyasituṃ śīlam asyeti sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsī | yogārūḍhaḥ prāpta-yoga ity etat, tadā tasmin kāla ucyate | sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsīti vacanāt sarvāṃś ca kāmān sarvāṇi ca karmāṇi saṃnyasyed ity arthaḥ | saṃkalpa-mūlā hi sarve kāmāḥ - saṃkalpa-mūlaḥ kāmo vai yajñāḥ saṃkalpa-saṃbhavāḥ [Manu 2.3]
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] When the <s>yogin</s> whose mind is being concentrated does not cling — in sense-objects, i.e., the objects of the senses such as sound etc., and in actions — whether obligatory (<s>nitya</s>), occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>), or prohibited (<s>pratiṣiddha</s>) — through the understanding that there is no purpose [in them], meaning he does not develop the attachment of a sense of obligation — [then he is called <s>yogārūḍha</s>]. 'Renouncer of all intentions' (<s>sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsī</s>) — one whose habit it is to renounce all intentions (<s>saṃkalpas</s>) that are the causes of desires for objects here and hereafter — that is a <s>sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsī</s>. '<s>Yogārūḍha</s>' — one who has attained <s>yoga</s> — this is the meaning; then, at that time, he is said [to have ascended to <s>yoga</s>]. From the statement 'renouncer of all intentions,' the meaning is that one should renounce all desires and all actions. For all desires are rooted in intention — 'Desire is indeed rooted in intention; sacrifices arise from intention' [<s>Manu</s> 2.3].

children.text: kāma jānāmi te mūlaṃ saṃkalpāt tvaṃ hi jāyase |
na tvāṃ saṃkalpayiṣyāmi tena me na bhaviṣyasi || [Mabh 12.177.25] ity ādi-smṛteḥ |
children.translated_text: I shall not intend you, and thereby you will cease to exist for me.' [<s>Mahābhārata</s> 12.177.25] — thus from the <s>smṛti</s> texts etc.
'O Desire, I know your root — you are born from intention;

children.text: sarva-kāma-parityāge ca sarva-karma-saṃnyāsaḥ siddho bhavati | sa yathā-kāmo bhavati tat-kratur bhavati yat kratur bhavati tat karma kurute [BAU 4.4.5] ity ādi śrutibhyaḥ | yad yad dhi kurute jantus tat tat kāmasya ceṣṭitam [Manu 2.4] ity ādi-smṛtibhyaś ca | nyāyāc ca - na hi sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāse kaścit spanditum api śaktaḥ | tasmāt sarva-saṃkalpa-saṃnyāsīti vacanāt sarvān kāmān sarvāṇi karmāṇi ca tyājayati bhagavān ||BhGS_6.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And when all desires are abandoned, the renunciation of all actions is accomplished. [As the <s>Śruti</s> states:] 'As is his desire, so is his will; as is his will, so is the action he performs' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.5] — from such <s>śruti</s> texts. And [as the <s>smṛti</s> states:] 'Whatever a creature does, that is the activity of desire' [<s>Manu</s> 2.4] — from such <s>smṛti</s> texts as well. And by reasoning — for when all intentions are renounced, one is not capable of even a movement. Therefore, by the statement 'renouncer of all intentions,' the Blessed Lord makes one renounce all desires and all actions. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.4||

children.text: yadaivaṃ yogārūḍhaḥ, tadā tena ātmā udbhṛto bhavati saṃsārād anartha-jātāt | ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] When one has thus ascended to <s>yoga</s>, then the Self is uplifted by him from <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is a mass of misfortunes. Therefore —

children.text: uddhared ātmanātmānaṃ nātmānam avasādayet |
children.translated_text: One should uplift the self by the Self; one should not degrade the self;

children.text: ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||BhG_6.5||
children.translated_text: for the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.5||

children.text: uddharet saṃsāra-sāgare nimagnam ātmanātmānaṃ tata ut ūrdhvaṃ hared uddharet, yogārūḍhatām āpādayed ity arthaḥ | nātmānam avasādayet nādho nayeta, nādho gamayet | ātmaiva hi yasmād ātmano bandhuḥ | na hy anyaḥ kaścit bandhuḥ, yaḥ saṃsāra-muktaye bhavati | bandhur api tāvat mokṣaṃ prati pratikūla eva, snehādi-bandhanāyatanatvāt | tasmāt yuktam avadhāraṇam ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur iti | ātmaiva ripuḥ śatruḥ | yo 'nyo 'pakārī bāhyaḥ śatruḥ so 'pi ātma-prayukta eveti yuktam evāvadhāraṇam ātmaiva ripur ātmana iti ||BhGS_6.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] One should uplift — the self that is submerged in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> — by the Self; one should draw it upward from there, i.e., one should lead it to the state of having ascended to <s>yoga</s> — this is the meaning. 'One should not degrade the self' — one should not lead it downward, should not cause it to descend. For the self alone is the friend of the self. For there is no other friend who could bring about liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even a kinsman (<s>bandhu</s>) is indeed adverse with respect to liberation, since he is a locus of bondage through attachment etc. Therefore, the emphatic assertion 'the self alone is the friend of the self' is justified. 'The self alone is the enemy' — the external enemy who does harm is also impelled by the self alone — therefore the emphatic assertion 'the self alone is the enemy of the self' is justified. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.5||

children.text: ātmaiva bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmana ity uktam | tatra kiṃ-lakṣaṇa ātmā ātmano bandhuḥ, kiṃ-lakṣaṇo vā ātmātmano ripur ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] It has been said 'the self alone is the friend of the self, the self alone is the enemy of the self.' In that regard — by what characteristic is the self the friend of the self, and by what characteristic is the self the enemy of the self? — this is stated:

children.text: bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The self is the friend of that self by which the self itself has been conquered;

children.text: anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||BhG_6.6||
children.translated_text: but for one who has not [conquered] the self, the self itself would act as an enemy, like a foe. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.6||

children.text: bandhur ātmātmanas tasya, tasyātmanaḥ sa ātmā bandhur yenātmanātmaiva jitaḥ | ātmā kārya-karaṇa-saṃghāto yena vaśīkṛtaḥ, jitendriya ity arthaḥ | anātmanas tv ajitātmanas tu śatrutve śatru-bhāve varteta ātmaiva śatruvat, yathānātmā śatrur ātmano 'pakārī, tathātmā ātmano 'pakāre varteta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'The self is the friend of that self' — of that self, that self is the friend — by which self the self itself has been conquered. 'The self' — the aggregate of body and instruments — by which [person] this has been subdued — meaning one whose senses are conquered. But for one who has not [conquered] the self (<s>anātmā</s>), i.e., for one whose self is unconquered — the self itself would act in enmity, i.e., like an enemy (<s>śatruvat</s>) — just as an external enemy does harm to the self, so too the self would act to the self's harm — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.6||

children.text: jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who has conquered the self, who is tranquil, the Supreme Self is fully composed;

children.text: śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ ||BhG_6.7||
children.translated_text: [such a one is the same] in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.7||

children.text: jitātmanaḥ kārya-karaṇa-saṃghāta ātmā jito yena sa jitātmā tasya jitātmanaḥ, praśāntasya prasannāntaḥ-karaṇasya sataḥ saṃnyāsinaḥ paramātmā samāhitaḥ sākṣād-ātma-bhāvena vartate ity arthaḥ | kiṃ ca śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu tathā māne 'pamāne ca mānāpamānayoḥ pūjā-paribhavayoḥ samaḥ syāt ||BhGS_6.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'For one who has conquered the self' (<s>jitātmā</s>) — the self, the aggregate of body and instruments, has been conquered by whom — that one is <s>jitātmā</s>; of that <s>jitātmā</s>, who is tranquil (<s>praśānta</s>), i.e., whose inner faculty is serene — being a renunciant — the Supreme Self (<s>paramātmā</s>) is composed (<s>samāhita</s>), i.e., abides in the direct experience of one's own Self — this is the meaning. Furthermore — [such a one is the same] in cold and heat, pleasure and pain; likewise in honor and dishonor (<s>mānāpamāna</s>), i.e., in worship and disrespect — he would be equal [in all these]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.7||

children.text: jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Satisfied in knowledge and realization, immovable, with senses conquered,

children.text: yukta ity ucyate yogī sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ ||BhG_6.8||
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s> who is equal toward a lump of earth, a stone, and gold is said to be 'united' (<s>yukta</s>). ||<s>BhG</s> 6.8||

children.text: jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā jñānaṃ śāstrokta-padārthānāṃ parijñānam, vijñānaṃ tu śāstrato jñātānāṃ tathaiva svānubhava-karaṇam, tābhyāṃ jñāna-vijñānābhyāṃ tṛptaḥ saṃjātālaṃ-pratyayaḥ ātmāntaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya sa jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā, kūṭāstho 'prakampyaḥ, bhavatīty arthaḥ | vijitendriyaś ca | ya īdṛśaḥ, yuktaḥ samāhita iti sa ucyate kathyate | sa yogī sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ loṣṭāśma-kāñcanāni samāni yasya saḥ sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ ||BhGS_6.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Satisfied in knowledge and realization' (<s>jñāna-vijñāna-tṛptātmā</s>) — '<s>jñāna</s>' is the comprehensive understanding of the meanings stated in scripture; '<s>vijñāna</s>' is the personal experience of those very things known from scripture; satisfied by these two — knowledge and realization — meaning one in whom the sense of 'enough' has arisen — whose inner faculty (<s>ātmā</s>) is thus — that is one 'satisfied in knowledge and realization.' '<s>Kūṭastha</s>' — immovable, unshakeable — this is the meaning. And 'with senses conquered.' One who is of this nature is said to be 'united' (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., concentrated — thus he is called. That <s>yogin</s> is '<s>sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcana</s>' — one for whom lumps of earth, stones, and gold are the same — that is <s>sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcana</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.8||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: suhṛn-mitrāry-udāsīna-madhya-stha-dveṣya-bandhuṣu |
children.translated_text: Among well-wishers, friends, enemies, the indifferent, neutrals, the hateful, and relatives,

children.text: sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu sama-buddhir viśiṣyate ||BhG_6.9||
children.translated_text: and among the virtuous and the sinful — one who has equal understanding excels. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.9||

children.text: suhṛd ity ādi lokārdham ekaṃ padam | suhṛt iti pratyupakāram anapekṣya upakartā, mitraṃ snehavān, ariḥ śatruḥ, udāsīno na kasyacit pakṣaṃ bhajate, madhya-stho yo viruddhayor ubhayoḥ hitaiṣī, dveṣya ātmano 'priyaḥ, bandhuḥ saṃbandhī ity eteṣu sādhuṣu śāstrānuvartiṣu api ca pāpeṣu pratiṣiddha-kāriṣu sarveṣv eteṣu sama-buddhiḥ | kaḥ kiṃ-karmā ity avyāpṛta-buddhir ity arthaḥ | viśiṣyate, vimucyate iti vā pāṭhāntaram | yogārūḍhānāṃ sarveṣām ayam uttama ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Suhṛt</s>' etc. — half a verse constitutes one unit. A '<s>suhṛt</s>' (well-wisher) is one who helps without expecting anything in return; a '<s>mitra</s>' (friend) is one who is affectionate; an '<s>ari</s>' (enemy) is a foe; an '<s>udāsīna</s>' (indifferent person) is one who sides with neither party; a '<s>madhyastha</s>' (neutral) is one who wishes well for both opposing parties; '<s>dveṣya</s>' (hateful) is one who is displeasing to oneself; '<s>bandhu</s>' (relative) is a kinsman — among all these, and among the virtuous (<s>sādhu</s>), i.e., those who follow the scriptures, and among the sinful (<s>pāpa</s>), i.e., those who engage in prohibited actions — one who has equal understanding, i.e., one whose mind is not occupied [with thoughts of] 'who is he' and 'what does he do' — excels (<s>viśiṣyate</s>). Or the alternate reading is '<s>vimucyate</s>' (is liberated). The meaning is: among all those who have ascended to <s>yoga</s>, this one is the highest. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.9||

children.text: ata evam uttama-phala-prāptaye -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, for the attainment of this supreme fruit —

children.text: yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> should constantly unite the mind, dwelling in solitude,

children.text: ekākī yata-cittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ ||BhG_6.10||
children.translated_text: alone, with mind and body controlled, free from expectations and possessiveness. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.10||

children.text: yogī dhyāyī yuñjīta samādadhyāt satataṃ sarvadātmānam antaḥ-karaṇaṃ rahasi ekānte giri-guhādau sthitaḥ san ekākī asahāyaḥ | rahasi sthitaḥ ekākī ceti viśeṣaṇāt saṃnyāsaṃ kṛtvā ity arthaḥ | yata-cittātmā cittam antaḥ-karaṇam ātmā dehaś ca saṃyatau yasya sa yata-cittātmā, nirāśīr vīta-tṛṣṇo 'parigrahaḥ parigraha-rahitaś cety arthaḥ | saṃnyāsitve 'pi tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ san yuñjīta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The <s>yogin</s>, the meditator, should unite (<s>yuñjīta</s>), i.e., should concentrate, constantly, always — the self (<s>ātman</s>), the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) — dwelling in solitude (<s>rahas</s>), in a secluded place such as a mountain cave etc. — being alone, without a companion. From the qualifications 'dwelling in solitude' and 'alone,' the meaning is: having taken <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation). '<s>Yata-cittātmā</s>' — one whose mind (<s>citta</s>), i.e., inner faculty, and body (<s>ātmā</s>) are restrained — that is <s>yata-cittātmā</s>. '<s>Nirāśīḥ</s>' — free from longing, i.e., free from craving. '<s>Aparigraha</s>' — without possessions — this is the meaning. Even being a renunciant, having abandoned all possessions, one should unite [the mind] — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.10||

children.text: athedānīṃ yogaṃ yuñjataḥ āsanāhāra-vihārādīnāṃ yoga-sādhanatvena niyamo vaktavyaḥ, prāpta-yogasya lakṣaṇaṃ tat-phalādi ca, ity ata ārabhyate | tatrāsanam eva tāvat prathamam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, the regulation of seat, diet, and conduct etc. as means to <s>yoga</s> for the one who practices <s>yoga</s> is to be stated, as well as the characteristics of one who has attained <s>yoga</s> and its fruit etc. — therefore [the exposition] begins. Therein, the seat is stated first:

children.text: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having established in a clean place a firm seat of one's own,

children.text: nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājina-kuśottaram ||BhG_6.11||
children.translated_text: neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin, and <s>kuśa</s> grass — ||<s>BhG</s> 6.11||

children.text: śucau śuddhe vivikte svabhāvataḥ saṃskārato vā, deśe sthāne pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram acalam ātmana āsanaṃ nātyucchritaṃ nātīva ucchritaṃ nāpy atinīcam, tac ca cailājina-kuśottaraṃ cailam ajinaṃ kuśāś cottare yasminn āsane tad āsanaṃ cailājina-kuśottaram | pāṭha-kramād viparīto 'tra kramaś cailādīnām ||BhGS_6.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'In a clean place' (<s>śucau</s>) — in a pure, secluded place, either naturally or by purification; 'in a place' (<s>deśe</s>) — having established (<s>pratiṣṭhāpya</s>) a firm (<s>sthira</s>), i.e., immovable, seat of one's own — neither too high, i.e., not excessively raised, nor too low. And that [seat] is '<s>cailājina-kuśottara</s>' — cloth, deerskin, and <s>kuśa</s> grass are the upper layers of that seat — that seat is <s>cailājina-kuśottara</s>. The order of the cloth etc. is the reverse of the order of the reading [i.e., <s>kuśa</s> grass at the bottom, then deerskin, then cloth on top]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.11||

children.text: pratiṣṭhāpya, kim ?
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having established [the seat], then what?

children.text: tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-cittendriya-kriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: There, making the mind one-pointed, with the activities of mind and senses controlled,

children.text: upaviśyāsane yuñjyād yogam ātma-viśuddhaye ||BhG_6.12||
children.translated_text: seated on the seat, one should practice <s>yoga</s> for the purification of the self. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.12||

children.text: tatra tasminn āsana upaviśya yogaṃ yuñjyāt | katham ? sarva-viṣayebhya upasaṃhṛtya ekāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-cittendriya-kriyaś cittaṃ cendriyāṇi ca cittendriyāṇi teṣāṃ kriyāḥ saṃyatā yasya sa yata-cittendriya-kriyaḥ | sa kim-arthaṃ yogaṃ yuñjyād ity āha - ātma-viśuddhaye 'ntaḥ-karaṇasya viśuddhy-artham ity etat ||BhGS_6.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] There, on that seat, having sat down, one should practice <s>yoga</s>. How? Having withdrawn [the mind] from all sense-objects, making the mind one-pointed (<s>ekāgra</s>); '<s>yata-cittendriya-kriyaḥ</s>' — the mind and the senses are the <s>cittendriya</s>; the activities of these are restrained by whom — that one is <s>yata-cittendriya-kriya</s>. For what purpose should one practice <s>yoga</s>? He says: for the purification of the self (<s>ātma-viśuddhi</s>), i.e., for the purification of the inner faculty — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.12||

children.text: bāhyam āsanam uktam | adhunā śarīra-dhāraṇaṃ katham ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The external seat has been described. Now, how should the body be held? This is stated:

children.text: samaṃ kāya-śiro-grīvaṃ dhārayann acalaṃ sthiraḥ |
children.translated_text: Holding the body, head, and neck erect, motionless, steady,

children.text: saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaś cānavalokayan ||BhG_6.13||
children.translated_text: gazing at the tip of one's own nose, and not looking in any direction — ||<s>BhG</s> 6.13||

children.text: samaṃ kāya-śiro-grīvaṃ kāyaś ca śiraś ca grīvā ca kāya-śiro-grīvaṃ tat samaṃ dhārayan acalaṃ ca | samaṃ dhārayataś calanaṃ saṃbhavati | ato viśinaṣṭi - acalam iti | sthiraḥ sthiro bhūtvā ity arthaḥ | svaṃ nāsikāgraṃ saṃprekṣya samyak prekṣaṇaṃ darśanaṃ kṛtvaiveti | iva-śabdo lupto draṣṭavyaḥ | na hi sva-nāsikāgra-saṃprekṣaṇam iha vidhitsitam | kiṃ tarhi ? cakṣuṣo dṛṣṭi-saṃnipātaḥ | sa cāntaḥ-karaṇa-samādhānāpekṣo vivakṣitaḥ | sva-nāsikāgra-saṃprekṣaṇam eva ced vivakṣitam, manas tatraiva samādhīyeta, nātmani | ātmani hi manasaḥ samādhānaṃ vakṣyati ātma-saṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtveti | tasmād iva-śabda-lopenākṣṇor dṛṣṭi-saṃnipāta eva saṃprekṣya ity ucyate | diśaś cānavalokayan diśāṃ cāvalokanam antarā kurvan ity etat ||BhGS_6.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Evenly' (<s>sama</s>) — the body, head, and neck — body and head and neck constitute '<s>kāya-śiro-grīva</s>' — that should be held evenly and motionlessly. For one holding [the body] evenly, movement is possible; therefore he specifies: 'motionless' (<s>acala</s>). 'Steady' (<s>sthira</s>) — having become steady, this is the meaning. 'Gazing at the tip of one's own nose' — having directed one's gaze properly, as it were. The word '<s>iva</s>' (as if) should be understood as elided. For the actual gazing at the tip of one's own nose is not intended here. What then? The convergence of the eyes' gaze [is intended]. And that is stated as dependent on the concentration of the inner faculty. For if gazing at the tip of one's own nose were literally intended, the mind would be fixed only there, not on the Self. But he will say that the mind should be fixed on the Self: 'fixing the mind on the Self' [<s>BhG</s> 6.25]. Therefore, with the elision of the word '<s>iva</s>,' only the convergence of the eyes' gaze is meant by 'gazing.' 'Not looking in any direction' — not looking around at the directions in between — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.13||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: praśāntātmā vigata-bhīr brahmacāri-vrate sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: With a tranquil self, free from fear, established in the vow of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy),

children.text: manaḥ saṃyamya mac-citto yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ ||BhG_6.14||
children.translated_text: controlling the mind, with thought fixed on me, the disciplined one should sit, devoted to me as the supreme [goal]. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.14||

children.text: praśāntātmā prakarṣeṇa śāntaḥ ātmāntaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ praśāntātmā, vigata-bhīḥ vigata-bhayaḥ, brahmacāri-vrate sthitaḥ | brahmacāriṇo vrataṃ brahmacaryaṃ guru-śuśrūṣā-bhikṣānna-bhukty-ādi tasmin sthitaḥ | tad-anuṣṭhātā bhaved ity arthaḥ | kiṃ ca, manaḥ saṃyamya manaso vṛttīr upasaṃhṛtya ity etat, mac-citto mayi parameśvare cittaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ mac-cittaḥ, yuktaḥ samāhitaḥ sann āsīta upaviśet | mat-paro 'haṃ paro yasya so 'yaṃ mat-paro bhavati | kaścit rāgī strī-cittaḥ, na tu striyam eva paratvena gṛhṇāti | kiṃ tarhi ? rājānaṃ mahā-devaṃ vā | ayaṃ tu mac-citto mat-paraś ca ||BhGS_6.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Praśāntātmā</s>' — one whose inner faculty (<s>ātmā</s>) is supremely tranquil — that is <s>praśāntātmā</s>. '<s>Vigata-bhī</s>' — one whose fear has departed. 'Established in the vow of <s>brahmacarya</s>' — the vow of a <s>brahmacārin</s> is <s>brahmacarya</s>, i.e., celibacy, service to the teacher, sustenance through begged food, etc. — one who is established in that, i.e., one who would practice it — this is the meaning. Moreover — 'controlling the mind' (<s>manaḥ saṃyamya</s>) — having withdrawn the activities of the mind — this is the meaning. '<s>Mac-citta</s>' — one whose thought (<s>citta</s>) is fixed on me, the Supreme Lord — that is <s>mac-citta</s>. Being 'united' (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., concentrated, one should sit (<s>āsīta</s>), i.e., should be seated. '<s>Mat-para</s>' — one for whom I am the supreme [goal] — that is <s>mat-para</s>. Someone attached [to a woman] may have his mind fixed on a woman, yet he does not take her alone as the supreme [goal]; rather, [he takes] a king or <s>Mahādeva</s> [as supreme]. But this one is both <s>mac-citta</s> and <s>mat-para</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.14||

children.text: athedānīṃ yoga-phalam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now the fruit of <s>yoga</s> is stated:

children.text: yuñjann evaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyata-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus constantly uniting the mind, the <s>yogin</s> of controlled mind

children.text: śāntiṃ nirvāṇa-paramāṃ mat-saṃsthām adhigacchati ||BhG_6.15||
children.translated_text: attains peace — the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) — which abides in me. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.15||

children.text: yujan samādhānāṃ kurvann evaṃ yathoktena vidhānena sadātmanāṃ sarvadā yogī niyata-mānaso niyataṃ saṃyataṃ mānasaṃ mano yasya so 'yaṃ niyata-mānasaḥ, śāntim uparatiṃ nirvāṇa-paramāṃ nirvāṇaṃ mokṣas tat paramā niṣṭhā yasyāḥ śānteḥ sā nirvāṇa-paramā tāṃ nirvāṇa-paramām. mat-saṃsthāṃ mad-adhīnām adhigacchati prāpnoti ||BhGS_6.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Uniting' (<s>yuñjan</s>) — i.e., concentrating — 'thus' — according to the method described — 'constantly' (<s>sadā</s>), always — the self (<s>ātman</s>) — the <s>yogin</s> of controlled mind (<s>niyata-mānasa</s>), i.e., one whose mind is restrained, subdued — [attains] peace (<s>śānti</s>), cessation. '<s>Nirvāṇa-paramā</s>' — that whose supreme goal is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, i.e., <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — that peace which has liberation as its highest culmination — that <s>nirvāṇa-paramā</s> [peace]. '<s>Mat-saṃsthā</s>' — dependent on me, abiding in me — he attains (<s>adhigacchati</s>), i.e., reaches it. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.15||

children.text: idānīṃ yoginaḥ āhārādi-niyama ucyate -
children.translated_text: Now the regulation of the <s>yogī</s>'s diet and so on is stated:

children.text: nātyaśnatas tu yogo 'sti na caikāntam anaśnataḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who eats too much, <s>yoga</s> is not [possible]; nor for one who does not eat at all;

children.text: naś cātisvapna-śīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna ||BhG_6.16||
children.translated_text: nor for one who is in the habit of sleeping too much, nor indeed for one who is [always] awake, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.16||

children.text: nātyaśnata ātma-saṃmitam anna-parimāṇam atītyāśnato 'tyaśnato na yogo 'sti | na caikāntam anaśnato yogo 'sti | yad u ha vā ātma-saṃmitam annaṃ tad avati tan na hinasti yad bhūyo hinasti tad yat kanīyo 'nnaṃ na tad avati [ŚatapathaB 9.2.1.2] iti śruteḥ | tasmāt yogī na ātma-saṃmitād annād adhikaṃ nyūnaṃ vāśnīyāt | athavā, yogino yoga-śāstre paripaṭhitād anna-parimāṇād atimātram aśnato yogo nāsti | uktaṃ hi -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'For one who eats too much' — for one who eats exceeding the measure of food proportionate to oneself, i.e., who overeats — <s>yoga</s> is not [possible]. Nor is <s>yoga</s> [possible] for one who does not eat at all (<s>ekāntam anaśnataḥ</s>). As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'That food which is proportionate to oneself — that it nourishes, that it does not harm; that which is more, harms; that which is less — that food does not nourish' [<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 9.2.1.2]. Therefore, the <s>yogī</s> should not eat more or less than the food proportionate to himself. Alternatively, for one who eats excessively beyond the measure of food prescribed in the <s>yoga-śāstra</s> (treatise on yoga), <s>yoga</s> is not [possible]. For it has been said:

children.text:
ardhaṃ sa-vyañjanānnasya tṛtīyam udakasya ca |
vāyoḥ saṃcaraṇārthaṃ tu caturtham avaśeṣayet || ity ādi parimāṇam |
children.translated_text: 'One should fill half [the stomach] with food accompanied by side-dishes, a third with water, and leave the fourth part for the movement of air.' Such is the prescribed measure.

children.text: tathā - na cātisvapna-śīlasya yogo bhavati naiva cātimātraṃ jāgrato bhavati cārjuna ||
children.translated_text: Likewise — nor does <s>yoga</s> come about for one who is in the habit of sleeping too much; nor indeed does it come about for one who is awake excessively, O <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: kathaṃ punar yogo bhavatīty ucyate -
children.translated_text: How then does <s>yoga</s> come about? This is stated:

children.text: yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu |
children.translated_text: For one who is regulated in food and recreation, who is regulated in exertion in [his] actions,

children.text: yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā ||BhG_6.17||
children.translated_text: who is regulated in sleep and waking — [for him] <s>yoga</s> becomes the destroyer of suffering. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.17||

children.text: yuktāhāra-vihārasya āhriyata ity āhāro 'nnam, viharaṇaṃ vihāraḥ pāda-kramaḥ, tau yuktau niyata-parimāṇau yasya sa yuktāhāra-vihāras tasya, tathā yukta-ceṣṭasya yuktā niyatā ceṣṭā yasya karmasu tasya | tathā yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yuktau svapnaś cāvabodhaś ca tau niyata-kālau yasya tasya, yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogino yogo bhavati duḥkhahā duḥkhāni sarvāṇi hantīti duḥkhahā, sarva-saṃsāra-duḥkha-kṣaya-kṛd yogo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'For one regulated in food and recreation' — that which is brought in (<s>āhriyate</s>) is food (<s>āhāra</s>), i.e., [solid] food; walking about is recreation (<s>vihāra</s>), i.e., movement on foot. These two being 'regulated' (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., of measured proportion — for one whose [food and recreation] are thus — for that person. Likewise, 'regulated in exertion' — for one whose exertion (<s>ceṣṭā</s>) in actions is regulated, i.e., disciplined. Likewise, 'regulated in sleep and waking' — for one whose sleep and waking are regulated, i.e., of fixed duration — for that <s>yogī</s> who is regulated in food and recreation, regulated in exertion in actions, regulated in sleep and waking, <s>yoga</s> becomes 'the destroyer of suffering' (<s>duḥkhahā</s>) — it destroys all sufferings, hence [it is called] <s>duḥkhahā</s>; the meaning is that <s>yoga</s> becomes the destroyer of all the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.17||

children.text: athādhunā kadā yukto bhavati ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: Now, when does one become 'united' (<s>yukta</s>)? This is stated:

children.text: yadā viniyataṃ cittam ātmany evāvatiṣṭhate |
children.translated_text: When the well-restrained mind abides in the self alone,

children.text: niḥspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā ||BhG_6.18||
children.translated_text: free from longing for all desires — then one is said to be 'united.' ||<s>BhG</s> 6.18||

children.text: yadā viniyataṃ viśeṣeṇa niyataṃ saṃyatam ekāgratām āpannaṃ cittaṃ hitvā bāhyārtha-cintām ātmany eva kevale 'vatiṣṭhate, svātmani sthitiṃ labhate ity arthaḥ | niḥspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyo nirgatā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-viṣayebhyaḥ spṛhā tṛṣṇā yasya yoginaḥ sa yuktaḥ samāhita ity ucyate tadā tasmin kāle ||BhGS_6.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'When the well-restrained' — specially restrained, controlled, having attained one-pointedness — the mind, having abandoned the thought of external objects, 'abides in the self alone' (<s>ātmany eva</s>), i.e., in the self exclusively — it obtains stability in one's own self; that is the meaning. 'Free from longing for all desires' — for that <s>yogī</s> whose longing (<s>spṛhā</s>), i.e., craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), for objects both seen and unseen has departed — he is said to be 'united' (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>), at that time. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.18||

children.text: tasya yoginaḥ samāhitaṃ yat cittaṃ tasyopamocyate -
children.translated_text: For that <s>yogī</s>, a simile is given for the concentrated mind:

children.text: yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — that simile is remembered

children.text: yogino yata-cittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ ||BhG_6.19||
children.translated_text: of the <s>yogī</s> of controlled mind who is practicing <s>yoga</s> of the self. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.19||

children.text: yathā dīpaḥ pradīpo nivāta-stho nivāte vāta-varjite deśe sthito neṅgate na calati, sopamā upamīyate 'nayety upamā yogajñaiś citta-pracāra-darśibhiḥ smṛtā cintitā yogino yata-cittasya saṃyatāntaḥ-karaṇasya yuñjato yogam anutiṣṭhata ātmanaḥ samādhim anutiṣṭhata ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'As a lamp' — a light — 'in a windless place' (<s>nivāta-stha</s>), i.e., situated in a place free from wind, 'does not flicker' — does not move. 'That simile' — [that by which something] is compared (<s>upamīyate</s>), hence an <s>upamā</s> (simile) — is 'remembered,' i.e., contemplated, by the knowers of <s>yoga</s> who observe the movements of the mind — of the <s>yogī</s> of controlled mind, whose inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is restrained, 'who is practicing <s>yoga</s> of the self' — who is performing <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); that is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.19||

children.text: evaṃ yogābhyāsa-balād ekāgrībhūtaṃ nivāta-pradīpa-kalpaṃ sat -
children.translated_text: Thus, by the power of the practice of <s>yoga</s>, having become one-pointed, like a lamp in a windless place —

children.text: yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yoga-sevayā |
children.translated_text: Where the mind, restrained by the practice of <s>yoga</s>, comes to rest,

children.text: yatra caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyann ātmani tuṣyati ||BhG_6.20||
children.translated_text: and where, seeing the self by the self, one is satisfied in the self; ||<s>BhG</s> 6.20||

children.text: yatra yasmin kāle uparamate cittam uparatiṃ gacchati niruddhaṃ sarvato nivārita-pracāraṃ yoga-sevayā yogānuṣṭhānena, yatra caiva yasmiṃś ca kāla ātmanā samādhi-pariśuddhenāntaḥ-karaṇenātmānaṃ paraṃ caitanyaṃ jyotiḥ-svarūpaṃ paśyann upalabhamānaḥ sva evātmani tuṣyati tuṣṭiṃ bhajate ||BhGS_6.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Where' — at which time the mind comes to rest (<s>uparamate</s>), i.e., attains cessation, 'restrained' — its movements entirely checked, by the practice of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yoga-sevā</s>), i.e., by the performance of <s>yoga</s>. 'And where' — and at which time, 'by the self' (<s>ātmanā</s>), i.e., by the inner instrument purified through <s>samādhi</s>, [one sees] 'the self' (<s>ātmānam</s>), i.e., the supreme consciousness (<s>para caitanya</s>), whose nature is light — 'seeing,' i.e., apprehending — one 'is satisfied in the self alone' (<s>ātmani tuṣyati</s>), i.e., becomes content. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.20||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: sukham ātyantikaṃ yat tad buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam |
children.translated_text: That infinite bliss which is grasped by the intellect and is beyond the senses —

children.text: vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaś calati tattvataḥ ||BhG_6.21||
children.translated_text: [when] one knows [that], and established [therein], does not deviate from the truth; ||<s>BhG</s> 6.21||

children.text: sukham ātyantikam atyantam eva bhavatīty ātyantikam anantam ity arthaḥ, yat tat buddhi-grāhyaṃ buddhyaiva indriya-nirapekṣayā gṛhyate iti buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam indriya-gocarātītam aviṣaya-janitam ity arthaḥ, vetti tad īdṛśaṃ sukham anubhavati yatra yasmin kāle, na caivāyaṃ vidvān ātma-svarūpe sthitas tasmān naiva calati tattvatas tattva-svarūpān na pracyavata ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Infinite bliss' (<s>ātyantikaṃ sukham</s>) — that which exists absolutely, hence 'infinite' (<s>ātyantika</s>), meaning boundless. 'That which' (<s>yat tat</s>) — 'grasped by the intellect' (<s>buddhi-grāhyam</s>), i.e., grasped by the intellect alone, independent of the senses — hence <s>buddhi-grāhya</s>; 'beyond the senses' (<s>atīndriya</s>), i.e., transcending the range of the senses, meaning not born from sense-objects. [One] 'knows' (<s>vetti</s>) — experiences such bliss — 'where,' i.e., at which time. 'And this [person], established [therein], does not deviate from the truth' — the meaning is that the wise one, established in the essential nature of the self, never falls away from that reality. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.21||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having gained which, one considers no other gain as superior to it;

children.text: yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate ||BhG_6.22||
children.translated_text: established in which, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow — ||<s>BhG</s> 6.22||

children.text: yaṃ labdhvā yam ātma-lābhaṃ labdhvā prāpyaś cāparam anyal lābhaṃ lābhāntaraṃ tato 'dhikam astīti na manyate na cintayati | kiṃ ca, yasmin ātma-tattve sthito duḥkhena śastra-nipātādi-lakṣaṇena guruṇā mahatāpi na vicālyate ||BhGS_6.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Having gained which' — having obtained which gain of the self — 'one does not consider' (<s>na manyate</s>) any other gain, any different acquisition, as superior to it. Moreover, 'established in which' — in the truth of the self — 'one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow' — even by great suffering characterized by the stroke of a weapon and the like. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.22||

children.text: yatroparamate ity ādyārabhya yāvadbhir viśeṣaṇair viśiṣṭa ātmāvasthā-viśeṣo yoga uktaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Beginning from 'where the mind comes to rest' and up to this point, the particular state of the self characterized by the various qualifying descriptions — that [state] is called <s>yoga</s>:

children.text: taṃ vidyād duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaṃ yoga-saṃjñitam |
children.translated_text: Let one know that disconnection from the connection with suffering to be what is called <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇa-cetasā ||BhG_6.23||
children.translated_text: that <s>yoga</s> should be practiced with determination and with a mind free from despondency. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.23||

children.text: taṃ vidyād vijānīyād duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaṃ duḥkhaiḥ saṃyogo duḥkha-saṃyogaḥ, tena viyogo duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaḥ, taṃ duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaṃ yoga ity eva saṃjñitaṃ viparīta-lakṣaṇena vidyād vijānīyād ity arthaḥ | yoga-phalam upasaṃhṛtya punar anvārambheṇa yogasya kartavyatocyate niścayānirvedayor yoga-sādhanatva-vidhānārtham | sa yathokta-phalo yogo niścayenādhyavasāyena yoktavyo 'nirviṇṇa-cetasā na nirviṇṇam anirviṇṇam | kiṃ tat ? cetas tena nirveda-rahitena cetasā cittenety arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Let one know' (<s>vidyāt</s>) — let one understand. 'Disconnection from the connection with suffering' — connection with suffering is <s>duḥkha-saṃyoga</s>; disconnection from that is <s>duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyoga</s> — that disconnection from the connection with suffering, designated by the name '<s>yoga</s>' — one should know it by its defining characteristic, which is the opposite [of suffering]; that is the meaning. Having summed up the fruit of <s>yoga</s>, once again, by way of resumption, the necessity of practicing <s>yoga</s> is stated — for the purpose of prescribing determination and freedom from despondency as means of <s>yoga</s>. That <s>yoga</s>, whose fruit has been described, 'should be practiced' (<s>yoktavya</s>) with determination (<s>niścaya</s>), i.e., with firm resolve, 'with a mind free from despondency' (<s>anirviṇṇa-cetasā</s>) — 'not despondent' is <s>anirviṇṇa</s>; what is that? The mind — with a mind free from weariness; that is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.23||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: saṃkalpa-prabhavān kāmāṃs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having abandoned all desires born of volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), entirely and without remainder,

children.text: manasaivendriya-grāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ ||BhG_6.24||
children.translated_text: restraining the group of senses completely by the mind alone — ||<s>BhG</s> 6.24||

children.text: saṃkalpa-prabhavān saṃkalpaḥ prabhavo yeṣāṃ kāmānāṃ te saṃkalpa-prabhavāḥ kāmās tān tyaktvā parityajya sarvān aśeṣato nirlepena | kiṃ ca, manasaiva viveka-yuktena indriya-grāmam indriya-samudāyaṃ viniyamya niyamanaṃ kṛtvā samantataḥ samantāt ||BhGS_6.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Born of volition' (<s>saṃkalpa-prabhava</s>) — those desires whose origin is volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) — those are 'born of volition'; having abandoned, i.e., having relinquished, all such desires, entirely and without remainder, with complete detachment. Moreover, 'by the mind alone' — by the mind endowed with discrimination — 'the group of senses' (<s>indriya-grāma</s>), i.e., the collection of senses — having restrained, i.e., having controlled, 'completely' (<s>samantataḥ</s>), i.e., from all sides. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.24||

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā |
children.translated_text: Gradually, gradually, one should come to rest, by the intellect held firm by steadfastness;

children.text: ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet ||BhG_6.25||
children.translated_text: having made the mind abide in the self, one should not think of anything at all. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.25||

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair na sahasoparamed uparatiṃ kuryāt | kayā ? buddhyā | kiṃ-viśiṣṭayā ? dhṛti-gṛhītayā dhṛtyā dhairyeṇa gṛhītayā dhṛti-gṛhītayā dhairyeṇa yuktayā ity arthaḥ | ātma-saṃstham ātmani saṃsthitam ātmaiva sarvaṃ na tato 'nyat kiṃcid astīty evam ātma-saṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet | eṣa yogasya paramo vidhiḥ ||BhGS_6.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Gradually, gradually' — not suddenly — 'one should come to rest' (<s>uparamet</s>), i.e., one should attain cessation. By what? By the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). Of what kind? 'Held firm by steadfastness' (<s>dhṛti-gṛhītayā</s>) — held by <s>dhṛti</s>, i.e., firmness; the meaning is: by an intellect endowed with steadfastness. 'Having made the mind abide in the self' (<s>ātma-saṃstham</s>) — established in the self, [knowing that] 'the self alone is everything; there is nothing other than it' — having thus made the mind abide in the self, 'one should not think of anything at all.' This is the supreme instruction of <s>yoga</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.25||

children.text: tatra evam ātma-saṃsthaṃ manaḥ kartuṃ pravṛtto yogī -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therein, the <s>yogī</s> who has thus set about making the mind abide in the self —

children.text: yato yato niścarati mana cañcalam asthiram |
children.translated_text: From whatever [cause] the restless, unsteady mind wanders away,

children.text: tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||BhG_6.26||
children.translated_text: from that, restraining it, one should bring it back under the control of the self alone. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.26||

children.text: yato yato yasmād yasmān nimittāt śabdāder niścarati nirgacchati svabhāva-doṣān manaś cañcalam atyarthaṃ calam, ata evāsthiram, tatas tatas tasmāt tasmāt śabdāder nimittān niyamya tat-tan-nimittaṃ yāthātmya-nirūpaṇena śabdādeḥ nimittān niyamya tat-tan-namittaṃ yāthātmya-nirūpaṇena ābhāsīkṛtya vairāgya-bhāvanayā ca etat mana ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ātma-vaśyatām āpādayet | evaṃ yogābhyāsa-balāt yogina ātmany eva praśāmyati manaḥ ||BhGS_6.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'From whatever, whatever' — from whatever cause such as sound and the like, the mind 'wanders away' (<s>niścarati</s>), i.e., goes out — being 'restless' (<s>cañcala</s>), i.e., excessively agitated, and therefore 'unsteady' (<s>asthira</s>). 'From that, that' — from that very cause such as sound and the like — 'restraining it' — by ascertaining the true nature of each such cause, and by rendering [it] apparent [as unreal], and through the cultivation of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — 'this mind, into the control of the self alone, one should bring' — one should make it subject to the self. Thus, by the power of the practice of <s>yoga</s>, the mind of the <s>yogī</s> comes to rest in the self alone. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.26||

children.text: praśānta-manasaṃ hy enaṃ yoginaṃ sukham uttamam |
children.translated_text: For the <s>yogī</s> whose mind is thoroughly tranquil, supreme bliss

children.text: upaiti śānta-rajasaṃ brahma-bhūtam akalmaṣam ||BhG_6.27||
children.translated_text: approaches — [he who is] of pacified <s>rajas</s>, who has become <s>Brahman</s>, and who is free from taint. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.27||

children.text: praśāntamanasaṃ prakarṣeṇa śāntaṃ mano yasya saḥ praśāntamanās taṃ praśāntamanasaṃ hi enaṃ yoginaṃ sukham uttamaṃ nitiśayam upaiti upagacchati śānta-rajasaṃ prakṣīṇa-mohādi-kleśa-rajasam ity arthaḥ, brahma-bhūtaṃ jīvanmuktam brahmaiva sarvam ity evaṃ niścayavantaṃ brahma-bhūtam akalmaṣaṃ dharmādharmādi-varjitam ||BhGS_6.27||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Of tranquil mind' (<s>praśānta-manasam</s>) — one whose mind is thoroughly tranquil — for that <s>yogī</s>, supreme bliss, i.e., unsurpassed [bliss], 'approaches' (<s>upaiti</s>), i.e., comes to [him]. 'Of pacified <s>rajas</s>' (<s>śānta-rajasam</s>) — meaning one in whom the defilement (<s>rajas</s>) of delusion and other afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) has subsided. 'Who has become <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahma-bhūtam</s>) — liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), one who has the firm conviction that '<s>Brahman</s> alone is everything.' 'Free from taint' (<s>akalmaṣam</s>) — free from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> (merit and demerit) and the like. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.27||

children.text: yuñjann evaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī vigata-kalmaṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus always engaging the self [in yoga], the <s>yogī</s>, free from taint,

children.text: sukhena brahma-saṃsparśam atyantaṃ sukham aśnute ||BhG_6.28||
children.translated_text: easily attains the infinite bliss of contact with <s>Brahman</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.28||

children.text: yuñjann evaṃ yathoktena krameṇa yogī yogāntarāya-varjitaḥ sadā sarvadātmānaṃ vigata-kalmaṣo vigata-pāpaḥ, sukhenānāyāsena brahma-saṃsparśaṃ brahmaṇā pareṇa saṃsparśo yasya tat brahma-saṃsparrśaṃ sukham atyantam antam atītya vartata ity atyantam utkṛṣṭaṃ niratiśayam aśnute vyāpnoti ||BhGS_6.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Thus always engaging' — by the method described, the <s>yogī</s>, free from obstacles to <s>yoga</s>, always, i.e., at all times, [engaging] the self — 'free from taint' (<s>vigata-kalmaṣa</s>), i.e., free from sin. 'Easily' (<s>sukhena</s>), i.e., without difficulty — 'the bliss of contact with <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>brahma-saṃsparśa</s>) — that bliss whose contact is with the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — 'infinite' (<s>atyanta</s>), i.e., surpassing all limits, meaning supremely excellent, unsurpassed — [he] 'attains' (<s>aśnute</s>), i.e., pervades, i.e., obtains. ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.28||

children.text: idānīṃ yogasya yat phalaṃ brahmaikatva-darśanaṃ sarva-saṃsāra-viccheda-kāraṇaṃ tat pradarśayate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now the fruit of <s>yoga</s> — the vision of oneness with <s>Brahman</s>, which is the cause of the severance of all <s>saṃsāra</s> — is set forth:

children.text: sarva-bhūta-stham ātmānaṃ sarva-bhūtāni cātmani |
children.translated_text: He sees the self abiding in all beings, and all beings in the self —

children.text: īkṣate yoga-yuktātmā sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ ||BhG_6.29||
children.translated_text: one whose self is united through <s>yoga</s>, seeing equality everywhere. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.29||

children.text: sarva-bhūta-sthaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu sthitaṃ svam ātmānaṃ sarva-bhūtāni ca ātmani brahmādīni stamba-paryantāni ca sarva-bhūtāni ātmany ekatāṃ gatāni īkṣate paśyati yoga-yuktātmā samāhitāntaḥ-karaṇaḥ sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ sarveṣu brahmādi-sthāvarānteṣu viṣameṣu sarva-bhūteṣu samaṃ nirviśeṣaṃ brahmātmaikatva-viṣayaṃ darśanaṃ jñānaṃ yasya sa sarvatra sama-darśanaḥ ||BhGS_6.29||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Abiding in all beings' — his own self situated in all beings; 'and all beings in the self' — all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, having become one with the self — 'he sees,' i.e., perceives. 'One whose self is united through <s>yoga</s>' (<s>yoga-yuktātmā</s>) — one whose inner instrument is concentrated. 'Seeing equality everywhere' (<s>sarvatra sama-darśana</s>) — in all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable beings, which are unequal, one whose vision (<s>darśana</s>), i.e., knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), is equal, i.e., without distinction — pertaining to the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> and the self — he is 'one who sees equally everywhere.' ||<s>BhGS</s> 6.29||

children.text: etasyātmaikatva-darśanasya phalam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The fruit of this vision of the oneness of the self is stated:

children.text: yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati |
children.translated_text: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me —

children.text: tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati ||BhG_6.30||
children.translated_text: to him I am never lost, and he is never lost to Me. ||<s>BhG</s> 6.30||

children.text: yo māṃ paśyati vāsudevaṃ sarvasyātmānaṃ sarvatra sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarvaṃ ca brahmādi-bhūta-jātaṃ mayi sarvātmani paśyati, tasya evaṃ ātmaikatva-darśino 'ham īśvaro na praṇaśyāmi na parokṣatāṃ gamiṣyāmi | sa ca me na praṇaśyati sa ca vidvān me mama vāsudevasya na praṇaśyati na parokṣo bhavati, tasya ca mama caikātmakatvāt | svātmā hi nāmātmanaḥ priya eva bhavati | yasmāc cāham eva sarvātmaikatva-darśī ||BhGS_6.30||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] One who sees Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, as the Self of all, everywhere in all beings, and sees everything — the entire multitude of beings beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> — in Me, the Self of all; for such a one, the seer of the oneness of the Self, I, the Lord, do not disappear, do not become remote. And that one does not disappear for Me — that knower does not become remote from Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, because of the oneness of Self between us. For indeed one's own Self is always dear to oneself. And because I alone am that seer of the oneness of the universal Self. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.30 //

children.text: ity etat pūrva-lokārthaṃ samyag darśanam anūdya tat-phalaṃ mokṣo 'bhidhīyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having restated this right vision for the benefit of the preceding [discussion], its fruit — liberation — is declared:

children.text: sarva-bhūta-sthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajaty ekatvam āsthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who worships Me as dwelling in all beings, established in oneness —

children.text: sarvathā vartamāno 'pi sa yogī mayi vartate ||BhG_6.31||
children.translated_text: that <s>yogin</s>, in whatever way living, abides in Me. // <s>BhG</s> 6.31 //

children.text: sarvathā sarva-prakāraiḥ vartamāno 'pi samyag-darśī yogī mayi vaiṣṇave parame pade vartate, nityam ukta eva saḥ, na mokṣaṃ prati kenacit pratibadhyate ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.31||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] In whatever way — in all manners — even while living [in the world], the <s>yogin</s> who has right vision abides in Me, in the supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. That one is as described — eternally [liberated]. The meaning is: that one is not obstructed by anything with regard to liberation. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.31 //

children.text: kiṃ cānyat -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: One who, through comparison with one's own self, sees equally everywhere, O <s>Arjuna</s> —

children.text: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ sa yogī paramo mataḥ ||BhG_6.32||
children.translated_text: whether happiness or suffering — that <s>yogin</s> is considered the highest. // <s>BhG</s> 6.32 //

children.text: ātmaupamyena ātmā svayam evopamīyate 'nayety upamā | tasyā upamāyā bhāva aupamyaṃ tenātmaupamyena, sarvatra sarva-bhūteṣu samaṃ tulyaṃ paśyati yo 'rjuna, sa ca kiṃ samaṃ paśyatīty ucyate - yathā mama sukham iṣṭaṃ tathā sarva-prāṇināṃ sukham anukūlam | vā-śabdaś cārthe | yadi vā yac ca duḥkhaṃ mama pratikūlam aniṣṭaṃ yathā tathā sarva-prāṇināṃ duḥkham aniṣṭaṃ pratikūlaṃ ity evam ātmaupamyena sukha-duḥkhe 'nukūla-pratikūle tulyatayā sarva-bhūteṣu samaṃ paśyati, na kasyacit pratikūlam ācarati, ahiṃsaka ity arthaḥ | yaḥ evam ahiṃsakaḥ samyag darśana-niṣṭhaḥ, sa yogī parama utkṛṣṭo mato 'bhipretaḥ sarva-yogināṃ madhye ||BhGS_6.32||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Through comparison with one's own self' (<s>ātmaupamya</s>) — the self itself is compared by means of this comparison; the state of that comparison is <s>aupamya</s>; by means of that self-comparison. One who sees equally — i.e., identically — everywhere, in all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>. And what does one see equally? This is stated: 'Just as happiness is desired by me, so is happiness agreeable to all living beings.' The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is in the sense of 'and.' 'Or if' — and whatever suffering is disagreeable and undesired by me, likewise suffering is undesired and disagreeable to all living beings. Thus, through self-comparison, seeing happiness and suffering — the agreeable and the disagreeable — as equal in all beings, one does not engage in anything disagreeable to anyone — meaning one is non-violent (<s>ahiṃsaka</s>). One who is thus non-violent and established in right vision — that <s>yogin</s> is considered the highest, the most excellent, the preferred among all <s>yogins</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.32 //

children.text: etasya yathoktasya samyag-darśana-lakṣaṇasya yogasya duḥkha-saṃpādyatām ālakṣya śuśruṣur dhruvaṃ tat-prāpty-upāyam arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Perceiving the difficulty of attaining this yoga characterized by right vision as described, <s>Arjuna</s>, desirous of hearing about a firm means for its attainment, said:

children.text: yo 'yaṃ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: This yoga that has been taught by You through equanimity, O <s>Madhusūdana</s> —

children.text: etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṃ sthirām ||BhG_6.33||
children.translated_text: I do not see its steady foundation, due to the restlessness [of the mind]. // <s>BhG</s> 6.33 //

children.text: yo 'yaṃ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena samatvena he madhusūdana etasya yogasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi nopalabhe, cañcalatvān manasaḥ | kim ? sthirām acalāṃ sthitim ||BhGS_6.33||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'This yoga that has been taught by You through equanimity' — through equality, O <s>Madhusūdana</s> — of this yoga, I do not see, do not perceive, due to the restlessness of the mind — what? — a firm, stable foundation. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.33 //

children.text: asiddham tat -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This is not established, because —

children.text: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavad dṛḍham |
children.translated_text: For the mind is restless, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, turbulent, powerful, and obstinate;

children.text: tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyor iva suduṣkaram ||BhG_6.34||
children.translated_text: I think its restraint is as difficult as [restraining] the wind. // <s>BhG</s> 6.34 //

children.text: cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ | kṛṣṇeti kṛṣater vilekhanārthasya rūpam | bhakta-jana-pāpādi-doṣākarṣāṇāt kṛṣṇaḥ, tasya saṃbuddhiḥ he kṛṣṇa | hi yasmāt manaś cañcalaṃ na kevalam atyarthaṃ cañcalam, pramāthi ca pramathana-śīlam, pramathnāti śarīram indriyāṇi ca vikṣipat sat para-vaśīkaroti | kiṃ ca - balavat prabalam, na kenacit niyantuṃ śakyam, durnivāratvāt | kiṃ ca - dṛḍhaṃ tantu-nāga-vad acchedyam | tasya evaṃbhūtasya manaso 'haṃ nigrahaṃ nirodhaṃ manye vāyor iva yathā vāyor duṣkaro nigrahas tato 'pi duṣkaraṃ manye ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_6.34||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'The mind is restless.' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — this is a form from the root <s>kṛṣ</s> meaning 'to draw'; because He draws away the sins and other faults of His devotees, He is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; the vocative is 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' 'For' — since — the mind is restless; not merely exceedingly restless, but also turbulent (<s>pramāthi</s>) — of a disturbing nature; disturbing the body and senses, scattering [them], it brings [them] under its own power. Moreover, it is powerful (<s>balavat</s>) — strong; it cannot be restrained by anyone, because it is impossible to prevent. Moreover, it is obstinate (<s>dṛḍha</s>) — firm like a thread-serpent, unbreakable. I think the restraint, the control, of such a mind is as difficult as the restraint of the wind — even more difficult than [restraining] the wind — this is the purport. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.34 //

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca, evam etad yathā bravīṣi -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The Blessed Lord said — it is indeed so, as you say:

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durṇigrahaṃ calam |
children.translated_text: Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed one, the mind is difficult to restrain and restless;

children.text: abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇaś ca gṛhyate ||BhG_6.35||
children.translated_text: but through practice and dispassion, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, it is controlled. // <s>BhG</s> 6.35 //

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ nāsti saṃśayo mano durnigrahaṃ calam ity atra he mahābāho | kiṃtv abhyāsena tv abhyāso nāmaś citta-bhūmau kasyāṃcit samāna-pratyayāvṛttiś cittasya | vairāgyeṇa vairāgyaṃ nāma dṛṣṭādṛṣṭeṣṭa-bhogeṣu doṣa-darśanābhyāsād vaitṛṣṇyam | tena ca vairāgyeṇa gṛhyate vikṣepa-rūpaḥ pracāraś cittasya | evaṃ tan mano gṛhyate nigṛhyate nirudhyata ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.35||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Undoubtedly — there is no doubt — that the mind is difficult to restrain and restless, O mighty-armed one. But through practice — practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) means the repetition of identical mental states (<s>pratyaya</s>) in a given ground of the mind. And through dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — dispassion means the absence of craving (<s>vaitṛṣṇya</s>) arising from the repeated perception of faults in the enjoyments of seen and unseen [objects]. By that dispassion, the wandering of the mind in the form of distraction is controlled. Thus that mind is controlled, restrained, checked — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.35 //

children.text: yaḥ punar asaṃyatātmā, tena -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But for one whose self is uncontrolled —

children.text: asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpeti me matiḥ |
children.translated_text: By one of uncontrolled self, yoga is difficult to attain — this is My view;
