children.text: vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo 'vāptum upāyataḥ ||BhG_6.36||
children.translated_text: but by one of controlled self who strives, it can be attained through [proper] means. // <s>BhG</s> 6.36 //

children.text: asaṃyatātmanābhyāsa-vairāgyābhyām asaṃyataḥ ātmāntaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya so 'yam asaṃyatātmā tenāsaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpo duḥkhena prāpyateti me matiḥ | yas tu punar vaśyātmābhyāsa-vairāgyābhyāṃ vaśyatvam āpāditaḥ ātmā mano yasya so 'yaṃ vaśyātmā tena vaśyātmanā tu yatatā bhūyo 'pi prayatnaṃ kurvatā śakyo 'vāptuṃ yogar upāyato yathoktād upāyāt ||BhGS_6.36||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Of uncontrolled self' — one whose inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) has not been controlled through practice and dispassion — that one is 'of uncontrolled self.' By such a person of uncontrolled self, yoga is difficult to attain — it is obtained only with difficulty — this is My view. But one whose self has been brought under control through practice and dispassion — that one is 'of controlled self.' By such a person of controlled self, who strives — who further exerts effort — yoga can be attained through the proper means as described. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.36 //

children.text: tatra yogābhyāsāṅgīkaraṇena ihaloka-paraloka-prāpti-nimittāni karmāṇi saṃnyastāni, yoga-siddhi-phalaṃ ca mokṣa-sādhanaṃ samyag darśanaṃ na prāptam iti, yogī yoga-mārgāt maraṇa-kāle calita-citta iti tasya nāśam āśaṅkayārjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] In this context, by accepting the practice of yoga, the actions that were the means of attaining this world and the next world have been renounced, and the fruit of yogic perfection — right vision, which is the means to liberation — has not been attained. The <s>yogin</s>'s mind has become distracted from the path of yoga at the time of death — apprehending the destruction [of such a one], <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāc calita-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who lacks effort yet is endowed with faith, whose mind has deviated from yoga —

children.text: aprāpya yoga-saṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati ||BhG_6.37||
children.translated_text: having failed to attain yogic perfection, to what destination does that one go, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 6.37 //

children.text: ayatir aprayatnavān yoga-mārge śraddhayāstikya-buddhyā copeto yogād anta-kāle ca calitaṃ mānasaṃ mano yasya sa calita-mānaso bhraṣṭa-smṛtiḥ so 'prāpya yoga-saṃsiddhiṃ yoga-phalaṃ samyag-darśanaṃ kāṃ gatiṃ he kṛṣṇa gacchati ||BhGS_6.37||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Lacking effort' (<s>ayati</s>) — one without exertion on the path of yoga; yet endowed with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), i.e., with the conviction of belief; 'deviated from yoga' — one whose mind has become deviated, i.e., distracted, at the time of death — one of lost recollection. Having failed to attain yogic perfection — the fruit of yoga, namely right vision — to what destination, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, does that one go? // <s>BhGS</s> 6.37 //

children.text: kaccin nobhaya-vibhraṣṭaś chinnābhram iva naśyati |
children.translated_text: Does this one, fallen from both [paths], not perish like a torn cloud,

children.text: apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi ||BhG_6.38||
children.translated_text: without any foundation, O mighty-armed one, deluded on the path to <s>Brahman</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 6.38 //

children.text: kaścit kiṃ na ubhaya-vibhraṣṭaḥ karma-mārgāt yoga-mārgāc ca vibhraṣṭaḥ san chinnābhram iva naśyati, kiṃ vā na naśyaty apratiṣṭho nirāśrayo he mahābāho vimūḍhaḥ san brahmaṇaḥ pathi brahma-prāpti-mārge ||BhGS_6.38||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Does not this one — fallen from both, i.e., fallen from the path of action and the path of yoga — perish like a torn cloud, or does one not perish? Without any foundation, without support, O mighty-armed one, being deluded on the path to <s>Brahman</s>, on the road to attaining <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.38 //

children.text: etan me saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇaś chettum arhasy aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: This doubt of mine, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, You should dispel completely;

children.text: tvad-anyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hy upapadyate ||BhG_6.39||
children.translated_text: for no other dispeller of this doubt can be found except You. // <s>BhG</s> 6.39 //

children.text: etan me mama saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇaś chettum apanetum arhasy aśeṣataḥ | tvad-anyas tvatto 'nyaḥ ṛṣir devo vā cchettā nāśayitā saṃśayasyāsya na hi yasmād upapadyate na saṃbhavati | atas tvam eva cchettum arhasīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_6.39||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This doubt of mine, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, You should dispel, remove completely. Other than You — no other sage or god is a dispeller, a destroyer of this doubt; for [such a one] is not possible, does not exist. Therefore You alone should dispel it — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.39 //

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate |
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, neither here nor hereafter is there destruction for that one;

children.text: na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścid durgatiṃ tāta gacchati ||BhG_6.40||
children.translated_text: for no one who does good, dear one, goes to a wretched end. // <s>BhG</s> 6.40 //

children.text: he pārtha naiva iha loke nāmutra parasmin vā loke vināśas tasya vidyate nāsti | nāśo nāma pūrvasmāt hīnajanmaprāptiḥ sa yogabhraṣṭasya nāsti | na hi yasmāt kalyāṇakṛt śubhakṛt kaścit durgatiṃ kutsitāṃ gatiṃ he tāta, tanoti ātmānaṃ putrarūpeṇeti pitā tāta ucyate | pitaiva putreti putro 'pi tāta ucyate | śiṣyo 'pi putra ucyate | yato na gacchati ||BhGS_6.40||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] O <s>Pārtha</s>, neither here in this world, nor hereafter in the next world, is there destruction for that one — it does not exist. 'Destruction' means the attainment of a birth inferior to the previous one — that does not befall one who has fallen from yoga. For — since — no one who does good (<s>kalyāṇa-kṛt</s>), who acts auspiciously, goes to a wretched end (<s>durgati</s>), a contemptible destination. 'Dear one' (<s>tāta</s>) — because a father extends himself through his son, the father is called <s>tāta</s>; and because the father himself [is reborn as] the son, the son too is called <s>tāta</s>; a disciple too is called a son. Because [such a one] does not [go to a wretched end]. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.40 //

children.text: kiṃ tv asya bhavati ? -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But what becomes of this one?

children.text: prāpya puṇya-kṛtāṃ lokān uṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having attained the worlds of the meritorious, and having dwelt [there] for everlasting years,

children.text: śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yoga-bhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate ||BhG_6.41||
children.translated_text: the one fallen from yoga is reborn in the house of the pure and prosperous. // <s>BhG</s> 6.41 //

children.text: yoga-mārge pravṛttaḥ saṃnyāsī sāmarthyāt prāpya gatvā puṇya-kṛtām aśvamedhādi-yājināṃ lokān, tatra coṣitvā vāsam anubhūya śāśvatīr nityāḥ samāḥ saṃvatsarān, tad-bhoga-kṣaye śucīnāṃ yathokta-kāriṇāṃ śrīmatāṃ vibhūti-matāṃ gehe gṛhe yoga-bhraṣṭaḥ abhijāyate ||BhGS_6.41||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The <s>saṃnyāsin</s> who had entered upon the path of yoga, by virtue of [his merit], having attained — having gone to — the worlds of the meritorious, i.e., those who perform <s>Aśvamedha</s> and other sacrifices, and having dwelt there — having experienced residence — for everlasting, i.e., permanent, years — when those enjoyments are exhausted — is reborn in the house of the pure, i.e., those who act righteously as prescribed, and the prosperous, i.e., those endowed with wealth. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.41 //

children.text: atha vā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām |
children.translated_text: Or else, one is born in a family of wise <s>yogins</s> themselves;

children.text: etad dhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yad īdṛśam ||BhG_6.42||
children.translated_text: for indeed such a birth as this is very difficult to obtain in this world. // <s>BhG</s> 6.42 //

children.text: athavā śrīmatāṃ kulāt anyasmin yoginām eva daridrāṇāṃ kule bhavati jāyate dhīmatāṃ buddhimatām | etat hi janma, yat daridrāṇāṃ yogināṃ kule, durlabhataraṃ duḥkha-labhyataraṃ pūrvam apekṣya loke janma yad īdṛśaṃ yathokta-viśeṣaṇe kule ||BhGS_6.42||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Or else, different from the family of the prosperous, one is born — takes birth — in a family of <s>yogins</s> themselves, [even if] poor, of wise, i.e., intelligent [ones]. This birth indeed — that which is in the family of poor <s>yogins</s> — is very difficult to obtain, i.e., more difficult to attain than the previous [option], in this world — a birth which has such characteristics as described, in such a family. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.42 //

children.text: yasmāt -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Because —

children.text: tatra taṃ buddhi-saṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam |
children.translated_text: There one regains the connection of wisdom from the previous body,

children.text: yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana ||BhG_6.43||
children.translated_text: and strives from that [point] even further toward perfection, O joy of the <s>Kurus</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 6.43 //

children.text: tatra yogināṃ kule taṃ buddhi-saṃyogaṃ buddhyā saṃyogaṃ buddhi-saṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikaṃ pūrvasmin dehe bhavaṃ paurvadehikam | yatate ca prayatnaṃ ca karoti tatas tasmāt pūrva-kṛtāt saṃskārāt bhūyo bahutaraṃ saṃsiddhau saṃsiddhi-nimittaṃ he kuru-nandana ||BhGS_6.43||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] There — in the family of <s>yogins</s> — one regains that connection of wisdom — the connection with the intellect, i.e., <s>buddhi-saṃyoga</s> — from the previous body, i.e., belonging to the former life. And one strives — exerts effort — from that, from those impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) produced in the previous life, even further, i.e., more intensely, toward perfection, toward the cause of perfection, O joy of the <s>Kurus</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 6.43 //

children.text: kathaṃ pūrva-deha-buddhi-saṃyogeti tad ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How [does one regain] the connection of wisdom from the previous body? That is stated:

children.text: pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hy avaśo 'pi saḥ |
children.translated_text: By that very previous practice one is carried forward even involuntarily;

children.text: jijñāsur api yogasya śabda-brahmātivartate ||BhG_6.44||
children.translated_text: even one who merely inquires about yoga transcends the word-<s>Brahman</s> (the Veda). // <s>BhG</s> 6.44 //

children.text: yaḥ pūrva-janmani kṛto 'bhyāsaḥ sa pūrvābhyāsaḥ, tenaiva balavatā hriyate saṃsiddhau hi yasmād avaśo 'pi sa yoga-bhraṣṭaḥ | na kṛtaṃ ced yogābhyāsajāt saṃskārāt balavattaram adharmādi-lakṣaṇaṃ karma, tadā yogābhyāsa-janitena saṃskāreṇa hriyate | adharmaś cet balavattaraḥ kṛtaḥ, tena yogajo 'pi saṃskāro 'bhibhūyata eva, tat-kṣaye tu yogajaḥ saṃskāraḥ svayam eva kāryam ārabhate, na dīrgha-kālasthasyāpi vināśas tasyāstīty arthaḥ | ato jijñāsur api yogasya svarūpaṃ jñātum icchann api yoga-mārge pravṛttaḥ saṃnyāsī yoga-bhraṣṭaḥ, sāmarthyāt so 'pi śabda-brahma vedokta-karmānuṣṭhāna-phalam ativartate 'tikrāmaty apākariṣyati | kim uta buddhvā yo yogaṃ tan-niṣṭho 'bhyāsaṃ kuryāt ||BhGS_6.44||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The practice undertaken in a previous birth is the 'previous practice' (<s>pūrvābhyāsa</s>); by that powerful [practice] one is carried forward toward perfection, for even involuntarily that one who has fallen from yoga [is carried]. If the <s>karma</s> characterized by <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the like that has been performed is not stronger than the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of yoga-practice, then one is carried by the impression generated by yoga-practice. But if a stronger <s>adharma</s> has been performed, then even the impression born of yoga is overpowered by it; but upon its exhaustion, the yoga-born impression spontaneously initiates its effect — meaning there is no destruction of it even after a long period. Therefore, even one who merely inquires about yoga — who merely desires to know the nature of yoga — a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> who has entered the path of yoga but has fallen from it — even that one, by virtue of [this impression], transcends, surpasses, will go beyond the word-<s>Brahman</s>, i.e., the fruit of performing rites prescribed in the Veda. How much more so one who, having understood yoga, becomes established in it and practices! // <s>BhGS</s> 6.44 //

children.text: kutaś ca yogitvaṃ śreya iti -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And why is the state of a <s>yogin</s> superior? —

children.text: prayatnād yatamānas tu yogī saṃśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: But the <s>yogin</s> who strives with effort, purified of sins,

children.text: aneka-janma-saṃsiddhas tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||BhG_6.45||
children.translated_text: perfected through many births, then attains the supreme destination. // <s>BhG</s> 6.45 //

children.text: prayatnād yatamānaḥ, adhikaṃ yatamāna ity arthaḥ | tatra yogī vidvān saṃśuddha-kilbiṣo viśuddha-kilbiṣaḥ saṃśuddha-pāpo 'neka-janma-saṃsiddhir anekeṣu janmasu kiṃcit kiṃcit saṃskāra-jātam upacitya tena upacitenāneka-janma-kṛtena saṃsiddho 'neka-janma-saṃsiddhas tataḥ labdha-samyag-darśanaḥ san yāti parāṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ gatim ||BhGS_6.45||
children.translated_text: Striving with effort — meaning striving with greater effort. There, the <s>yogī</s>, the wise one, <s>saṃśuddha-kilbiṣa</s> (one whose sins are purified), meaning one whose sins are cleansed, whose evil is purified, <s>aneka-janma-saṃsiddhi</s> (one perfected through many births) — having accumulated little by little the aggregate of <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental impressions) over many births, and through that accumulated merit produced over many births having become perfected, thereupon having attained right vision, he goes to the supreme, the exalted goal. ||BhGS 6.45||

children.text: yasmād evaṃ tasmāt -
children.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: tapasvibhyo 'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo 'pi mato 'dhikaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> is superior to ascetics, and is considered superior even to the learned;

children.text: karmibhyaś cādhiko yogī tasmād yogī bhavārjuna ||BhG_6.46||
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> is also superior to ritualists — therefore, be a <s>yogī</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>! ||BhG 6.46||

children.text: tapasvibhyo 'dhiko yogī, jñānibhyo 'pi jñānam atra śāstrārtha-pāṇḍityam, tadvadbhyo 'pi mato jñāto 'dhikaḥ śreṣṭha iti | karmibhyaḥ, agnihotrādi karma, tadvadbhyo 'dhiko yogī viśiṣṭo yasmāt tasmād yogī bhavārjuna ||BhGS_6.46||
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> is superior to ascetics; even to the learned — here <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) means scholarly expertise in the meaning of scriptures — even to those possessing such knowledge, he is considered, that is known, to be superior, meaning excellent. Superior to ritualists — <s>karma</s> (ritual action) refers to <s>agnihotra</s> (fire sacrifice) and the like — the <s>yogī</s> is superior, that is distinguished, compared to those who perform such rituals. Since this is so, therefore be a <s>yogī</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>! ||BhGS 6.46||

children.text: yoginām api sarveṣāṃ mad-gatenāntarātmanā |
children.translated_text: Among all <s>yogīs</s>, the one whose inner self is absorbed in Me,

children.text: śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ ||BhG_6.47||
children.translated_text: Who worships Me with faith — he is considered by Me to be the most disciplined. ||BhG 6.47||

children.text: yoginām api sarveṣāṃ rūdrādityādi-dhyāna-parāṇāṃ madhye mad-gatena mayi vāsudeve samāhitenāntarātmanāntaḥ-karaṇena śraddhāvān śraddadhānaḥ san bhajate sevate yo mām, sa me mama yuktatamo 'tiśayena yukto mato 'bhipreta iti ||
children.translated_text: Among all <s>yogīs</s> — among those devoted to meditation on <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and other deities — the one whose inner self, that is, whose <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ), is absorbed in Me, in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who being full of faith, that is, being a person of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), worships, that is serves, Me — he is, in My view, the <s>yuktatama</s> (most disciplined), supremely united, considered to be My chosen one.

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛta śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: who is the most venerable among <s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryas</s> (supreme wandering ascetic teachers),

children.text: ṣaṣṭo 'dhyāyaḥ ||6||
children.translated_text: the sixth chapter. ||6||

children.text: BhG 7
children.translated_text: BhG 7

children.text: atha jñāna-vijñāna-yogākhyaḥ saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the seventh chapter called <s>Jñāna-vijñāna-yoga</s> (The Yoga of Knowledge and Realization)

children.text: (śaṅkara-bhāṣyaḥ)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary)

children.text:
yoginām api sarveṣāṃ mad-gatenāntarātmanā |
śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ [Gītā 6.47]
children.translated_text:
Among all <s>yogīs</s>, the one whose inner self is absorbed in Me,
who worships Me with faith — he is considered by Me to be the most disciplined. [Gītā 6.47]

children.text: iti praśna-bījam upanyasya, svayam eva īdṛśaṃ madīyaṃ tattvam, evaṃ mad-gatāntar-ātmā syād ity etat vivakṣuḥ śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: Having thus introduced the seed of inquiry, the blessed Lord spoke, Himself wishing to declare: 'Such is My true nature; thus one whose inner self is absorbed in Me would be' —

children.text: mayy āsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjan madāśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: With mind attached to Me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, practicing <s>yoga</s> and taking refuge in Me,

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tac chṛṇu ||BhG_7.1||
children.translated_text: Hear how you shall know Me completely and without doubt. ||BhG 7.1||

children.text: mayi vakṣyamāṇa-viśeṣaṇe parameśvare āsaktaṃ mano yasya saḥ mayy āsakta-manāḥ, he pārtha ! yogaṃ yuñjan manaḥ-samādhānaṃ kurvan, mad-āśrayo 'ham eva parameśvaraḥ āśrayo yasya saḥ mad-āśrayaḥ | yo hi kaścit puruṣārthena kenacit arthī bhavati sa tat-sādhanaṃ karmāgnihotrādi tapo dānaṃ vā kiṃcid āśrayaṃ pratipadyate, ayaṃ tu yogī mām evāśrayaṃ pratipadyate, hitvānyat sādhanāntaraṃ mayy eva āsakta-manā bhavati | yas tvaṃ evaṃ-bhūtaḥ san asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ samastaṃ vibhūti-bala-śakty-aiśvaryādi-guṇa-saṃpannaṃ māṃ yathā yena prakāreṇa jñāsyasi saṃśayam antareṇaivam eva bhagavān iti, tat sṛṇu ucyamānaṃ mayā ||BhGS_7.1||
children.translated_text: 'Attached to Me' — the one whose mind is attached to Me, the Supreme Lord who will be described with specific attributes, he is <s>mayy āsakta-manāḥ</s> (one whose mind is attached to Me). O <s>Pārtha</s>! Practicing <s>yoga</s>, that is performing mental concentration; <s>mad-āśraya</s> (taking refuge in Me) — the one whose refuge is I, the Supreme Lord, alone. For whoever desires any human goal takes recourse to some means such as ritual action like <s>agnihotra</s> (fire sacrifice), or austerity, or charity as their refuge; but this <s>yogī</s> takes Me alone as refuge, abandoning all other means, and becomes one whose mind is attached to Me alone. You who are thus, hear from Me how you shall know Me — who am endowed with <s>vibhūti</s> (divine manifestation), <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), and other qualities — completely, entirely, without doubt, knowing with certainty: 'the Lord is indeed thus.' Listen to what is being spoken by Me. ||BhGS 7.1||

children.text: tac ca mad-viṣayam -
children.translated_text: And that knowledge concerning Me —

children.text: jñānaṃ te 'haṃ sa-vijñānam idaṃ vakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: I shall declare to you this knowledge together with realization, in full,

children.text: yaj jñātvā neha bhūyo 'nyaj jñātavyam avaśiṣyate ||BhG_7.2||
children.translated_text: Knowing which, nothing further remains here to be known. ||BhG 7.2||

children.text: jñānaṃ te tubhyam ahaṃ sa-vijñānaṃ vijñāna-sahitaṃ svānubhava-yuktam idaṃ vakṣyāmi kathayiṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ kārtsnyena | taj jñānaṃ vivakṣitaṃ stauti śrotuḥ abhimukhīkaraṇāya - yaj jñātvā yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā neha bhūyaḥ punar anyat jñātavyaṃ puruṣārtha-sādhanam avaśiṣyate nāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati | iti mat-tattva-jño yaḥ, sa sarvajño bhavatīty arthaḥ | ato viśiṣṭa-phalatvāt durlabhaṃ jñānam ||BhGS_7.2||
children.translated_text: Knowledge — to you, I shall declare, that is I shall tell, this knowledge together with <s>vijñāna</s> (realization), that is accompanied by direct personal experience, completely, in its entirety. He praises that intended knowledge in order to make the listener attentive — knowing which, that is, having known which knowledge, nothing else that is a means to the human goal remains to be known here again; it does not remain. The meaning is: one who knows My true nature becomes omniscient. Therefore, because it yields such a distinguished result, this knowledge is difficult to attain. ||BhGS 7.2||

children.text: katham ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: How so — it is said:

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaś cid yatati siddhaye |
children.translated_text: Among thousands of human beings, scarcely one strives for perfection;

children.text: yatatām api siddhānāṃ kaś cin māṃ vetti tattvataḥ ||BhG_7.3||
children.translated_text: Even among those who strive and are perfected, scarcely one knows Me in truth. ||BhG 7.3||

children.text: manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye sahasreṣu anekeṣu kaścit yatati prayatnaṃ karoti siddhaye siddhy-artham | teṣāṃ yatatām api siddhānām, siddhā eva hi te ye mokṣāya yatante, teṣāṃ kaścid eva hi māṃ vetti tattvato yathāvat ||BhGS_7.3||
children.translated_text: Among human beings, among the many thousands, scarcely one strives, that is makes effort, for perfection, for the sake of attainment. Among those who strive — among the perfected, for indeed those who strive for liberation are truly the perfected — scarcely one indeed knows Me in truth, as I really am. ||BhGS 7.3||

children.text: śrotāraṃ prarocanenābhimukhīkṛtyāha -
children.translated_text: Having made the listener receptive through arousing interest, He says —

children.text: bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca |
children.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect,

children.text: ahaṃkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā ||BhG_7.4||
children.translated_text: And <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) — thus is My <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) divided eightfold. ||BhG 7.4||

children.text: bhūmiḥ pṛthivī-tanmātram ucyate, na sthūlā | bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā iti vacanāt | tathāb-ādayo 'pi tanmātrāṇy eva ucyante - āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ kham | mana iti manasaḥ kāraṇam ahaṃkāro gṛhyate | buddhir ity ahaṃkāra-kāraṇaṃ mahat-tattvam | ahaṃkāra ity avidyā-saṃyuktam avyaktam | yathā viṣa-saṃyuktam annaṃ viṣam ity ucyate, evam ahaṃkāra-vāsanāvad avyaktaṃ mūla-kāraṇam ahaṃkāra ity ucyate, pravartakatvāt ahaṃkārasya | ahaṃkāra eva hi sarvasya pravṛtti-bījaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ loke | itīyaṃ yathoktā prakṛtir me mamaiśvarī māyā-śaktir aṣṭadhā bhinnā bhedam āgatā ||BhGS_7.4||
children.translated_text: 'Earth' refers to the <s>pṛthivī-tanmātra</s> (subtle element of earth), not the gross element, because the text says 'nature divided eightfold.' Similarly, water and the others also refer to the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) alone — water, fire, air, space. By 'mind' is understood <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), which is the cause of mind. By 'intellect' is meant <s>mahat-tattva</s> (the great principle), which is the cause of ego. By '<s>ahaṃkāra</s>' is meant the <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest) conjoined with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Just as food mixed with poison is called 'poison,' so the <s>avyakta</s>, the root cause, pervaded by the impression of ego, is called '<s>ahaṃkāra</s>' because ego is the impelling force. For ego alone is seen in the world as the seed of all activity. 'Thus' — this <s>prakṛti</s> as described is My divine <s>māyā-śakti</s> (power of illusion), divided eightfold, that is, having undergone differentiation. ||BhGS 7.4||

children.text: apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām |
children.translated_text: This is the lower; but know My other <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), the higher one,

children.text: jīva-bhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat ||BhG_7.5||
children.translated_text: Which has become the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), O mighty-armed one, by which this world is sustained. ||BhG 7.5||

children.text: aparā na parā nikṛṣṭāśuddhānartha-karī saṃsāra-bandhanātmikeyam | ito 'syāḥ yathoktāyās tv anyāṃ viśuddhāṃ prakṛtiṃ mamātma-bhūtāṃ viddhi me parāṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ jīva-bhūtāṃ kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇāṃ prāṇa-dhāraṇa-nimitta-bhūtāṃ he mahābāho, yayā prakṛtyedaṃ dhāryate jagad antaḥ-praviṣṭayā ||BhGS_7.5||
children.translated_text: <s>Aparā</s> (lower) — not the higher, meaning inferior, impure, productive of misfortune, having the nature of the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — this is that. But other than this one as described, know My pure <s>prakṛti</s> which is of My own essential nature, the higher one, which has become the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), characterized as <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), which is the cause of sustaining life, O mighty-armed one — by which <s>prakṛti</s>, having entered within, this world is sustained. ||BhGS 7.5||

children.text: etad-yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya |
children.translated_text: Know that all beings have these as their source.

children.text: ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā ||BhG_7.6||
children.translated_text: I am the origin and also the dissolution of the entire universe. ||BhG 7.6||

children.text: etad-yonīni ete parāpare kṣetra-kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇe prakṛtī yonir yeṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ tāni etad-yonīni, bhūtāni sarvāṇīti evam upadhāraya jānīhi | yasmāt mama prakṛti yoniḥ kāraṇaṃ sarva-bhūtānām, ato 'haṃ kṛtsnasya samastasya jagataḥ prabhava utpattiḥ pralayo vināśas tathā | prakṛti-dvaya-dvāreṇāhaṃ sarvajña īśvaro jagataḥ kāraṇam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_7.6||
children.translated_text: Having these as their source — these two, the higher and the lower, characterized as <s>kṣetra</s> (field) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), are the <s>prakṛtis</s> (natures) that are the source of beings; those beings that have these as their source are 'having these as their source.' All beings — thus understand, that is know. Since My <s>prakṛti</s> is the source, the cause, of all beings, therefore I am the origin, the arising, and the dissolution, the destruction, of the entire, the whole, universe. Through the medium of My two <s>prakṛtis</s>, I, the omniscient Lord, am the cause of the universe — this is the meaning. ||BhGS 7.6||

children.text: yatas tasmāt -
children.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiṃcid asti dhanaṃjaya |
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>;

children.text: mayi sarvam idaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva ||BhG_7.7||
children.translated_text: All this is strung on Me, like gems on a thread. ||BhG 7.7||

children.text: mattaḥ parameśvarāt parataram anyat kāraṇāntaraṃ kiṃcit nāsti na vidyate, aham eva jagat-kāraṇam ity arthaḥ, he dhanaṃjaya | yasmād evaṃ tasmāt mayi parameśvare sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvam idaṃ jagat protam anusyūtam anugatam anuviddhaṃ grathitam ity arthaḥ | dīrgha-tantuṣu paṭavat, sūtre ca maṇi-gaṇā iva ||BhGS_7.7||
children.translated_text: Than Me, the Supreme Lord, there is nothing higher, no other cause whatsoever; I alone am the cause of the universe — this is the meaning, O <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>. Since this is so, therefore on Me, the Supreme Lord, all beings, all this universe, is strung, that is threaded through, pervaded, permeated, woven together — this is the meaning. Like cloth on long threads, and like gems strung on a thread. ||BhGS 7.7||

children.text: kena kena dharmeṇa viśiṣṭo tvayi sarvam idaṃ protam ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: By what specific attribute are You such that all this is strung on You — this is stated:

children.text: raso 'ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ |
children.translated_text: I am the taste in water, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the radiance in the moon and sun,

children.text: praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu ||BhG_7.8||
children.translated_text: The <s>praṇava</s> (syllable Oṃ) in all the <s>Vedas</s>, sound in space, and manliness in men. ||BhG 7.8||

children.text: raso 'ham, apāṃ yaḥ sāraṃ sa rasaḥ, tasmin rasa-bhūte mayi āpaḥ protā ity arthaḥ | evaṃ sarvatra | yathāham apsu rasaḥ, evaṃ prabhāsmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ | praṇava oṃkāraḥ sarva-vedeṣu, tasmin praṇava-bhūte mayi sarve vedāḥ protāḥ | tathā khe ākāśe śabdaḥ sāra-bhūtaḥ, tasmin mayi khaṃ protam | tathā pauruṣaṃ puruṣasya bhāvaḥ pauruṣaṃ yataḥ puṃ-buddhir nṛṣu, tasmin mayi puruṣāḥ protāḥ ||BhGS_7.8||
children.translated_text: I am the taste — the essence of water is taste; in Me who am that taste, the waters are strung — this is the meaning. And so everywhere. Just as I am the taste in water, similarly I am the radiance in the moon and sun. The <s>praṇava</s>, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, in all the <s>Vedas</s> — in Me who am that <s>praṇava</s>, all the <s>Vedas</s> are strung. Similarly, in space, sound is the essential element; in Me who am that, space is strung. Similarly, <s>pauruṣa</s> (manliness) — the quality of being a man, that by which the notion of manhood arises — in men; in Me who am that, men are strung. ||BhGS 7.8||

children.text: gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau |
children.translated_text: And I am the fragrance in earth, and the brilliance in fire;

children.text: jīvanaṃ sarva-bhūteṣu tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu ||BhG_7.9||
children.translated_text: I am the life-force in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics. ||BhG 7.9||

children.text: puṇyaḥ surabhir gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ cāham | tasmin mayi gandha-bhūte pṛthivī protā | puṇyatvaṃ gandhasya svabhāvata eva pṛthivyāṃ darśitam ab-ādiṣu rasādeḥ puṇyatvopalakṣaṇārtham | apuṇyatvaṃ tu gandhādīnām avidyā-dharmādy-apekṣaṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃsarga-nimittaṃ bhavati | tejaś ca dīptiś cāsmi vibhāvasau agnau | tathā jīvanaṃ sarva-bhūteṣu, yena jīvanti sarvāṇi bhūtāni tat jīvanam | tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu, tasmin tapasi mayi tapasvinaḥ protāḥ ||BhGS_7.9||
children.translated_text: I am the pure, sweet fragrance in earth. In Me who am that fragrance, the earth is strung. The purity of fragrance is shown as natural to earth, and serves as an indicator of the purity of taste and other qualities in water and the rest. The impurity of fragrance and the like, however, depends on <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and other <s>dharmas</s> (properties), and arises for beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) due to contact with particular material elements. I am the brilliance, the radiance, in <s>vibhāvasu</s> (fire). Similarly, I am the life-force in all beings — that by which all beings live is the life-force. And I am the austerity in ascetics; in Me who am that austerity, the ascetics are strung. ||BhGS 7.9||

children.text: bījaṃ māṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
children.translated_text: Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings, O <s>Pārtha</s>;

children.text: buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham ||BhG_7.10||
children.translated_text: I am the intelligence of the intelligent, and the brilliance of the brilliant. ||BhG 7.10||

children.text: bījaṃ praroha-kāraṇaṃ māṃ viddhi sarva-bhūtānāṃ he pārtha sanātanaṃ cirantanam | kiṃ ca, buddhir viveka-śaktir antaḥ-karaṇasya buddhimatāṃ viveka-śaktimatām asmi | tejaḥ prāgalbhyaṃ tadvatāṃ tejasvinām aham ||BhGS_7.10||
children.translated_text: Know Me as the seed, the cause of growth, of all beings, O <s>Pārtha</s>, the eternal, the ancient. Moreover, I am the <s>buddhi</s> (intelligence), the power of discrimination belonging to the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ), of the intelligent, of those possessing the power of discrimination. I am the <s>tejas</s> (brilliance), the boldness, of those who possess it, of the brilliant. ||BhGS 7.10||

children.text: balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam |
children.translated_text: And I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and attachment;

children.text: dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharatarṣabha ||BhG_7.11||
children.translated_text: I am that desire in beings which is not opposed to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), O <s>Bharatarṣabha</s> (best of the <s>Bharatas</s>). ||BhG 7.11||

children.text: balaṃ sāmarthyam ojo balavatām aham | tac ca balaṃ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam | kāmaś ca rāgaś ca kāma-rāgau | kāmas tṛṣṇā-saṃnikṛṣṭeṣu viṣayeṣu, rāgo rañjanā prāpteṣu viṣayeṣu - tābhyāṃ kāma-rāgābhyāṃ vivarjitaṃ dehādi-dhāraṇa-mātrārthaṃ balaṃ sattvam aham asmi | na tu yat saṃsāriṇāṃ tṛṣṇā-rāga-kāraṇam | kiṃ ca - dharmāviruddhaḥ | dharmeṇa śāstrārthenāviruddho yaḥ prāṇiṣu bhūteṣu kāmaḥ, yathā deha-dhāraṇa-mātrādy-artho 'śana-pānādi-viṣayaḥ, sa kāmo 'smi | he bharatarṣabha ||BhGS_7.11||
children.translated_text: I am the strength, the capacity, the vigor, of the strong. And that strength is devoid of desire and attachment. <s>Kāma</s> (desire) and <s>rāga</s> (attachment) together form <s>kāma-rāga</s>. <s>Kāma</s> is craving for objects that are near at hand; <s>rāga</s> is the coloring of delight in objects already obtained. Devoid of these two, desire and attachment — the strength that serves merely the purpose of sustaining the body and so forth, that <s>sattva</s> (pure strength) I am; but not that which is the cause of craving and attachment for those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). Moreover — not opposed to <s>dharma</s>: that desire which is not opposed to <s>dharma</s>, the teaching of scripture, which exists in living beings — such as desire pertaining to eating and drinking merely for the purpose of sustaining the body and the like — that desire I am. O <s>Bharatarṣabha</s> (best of the <s>Bharatas</s>)! ||BhGS 7.11||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye |
children.translated_text: And whatever states of being are <s>sāttvika</s> (of goodness), <s>rājasa</s> (of passion), or <s>tāmasa</s> (of darkness),

children.text: matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi ||BhG_7.12||
children.translated_text: Know them to be from Me alone; yet I am not in them — they are in Me. ||BhG 7.12||

children.text: ye caiva sāttvikāḥ sattva-nirvṛttā bhāvāḥ padārthāḥ, rājasāḥ rajo-nirvṛttās tāmasās tamo-nirvṛttāś ca, ye kecit prāṇināṃ sva-karma-vaśāt jāyante bhāvāḥ, tān matta eva jāyamānān iti evaṃ viddhi sarvān samastān eva | evaṃ yady api te matto jāyante, tathāpi na tv ahaṃ teṣu tad-adhīnas tad-vaśaḥ, yathā saṃsāriṇaḥ | te punar mayi mad-vaśāḥ mad-adhīnāḥ ||BhGS_7.12||
children.translated_text: Whatever states are <s>sāttvika</s> (born of <s>sattva</s>), whatever things are <s>rājasa</s> (born of <s>rajas</s>), and <s>tāmasa</s> (born of <s>tamas</s>) — whatever states arise in living beings due to their own <s>karma</s> (actions) — know all of them, each and every one, as arising from Me alone. Although they arise from Me, yet I am not in them, not subject to them, not under their control, as are those in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). They, however, are in Me — under My control, subject to Me. ||BhGS 7.12||

children.text: evaṃ-bhūtam api parameśvaraṃ nitya-śuddha-buddha-mukta-svabhāvaṃ sarva-bhūtātmānaṃ nirguṇaṃ saṃsāra-doṣa-bīja-pradāha-kāraṇaṃ māṃ nābhijānāti jagad ity anukrośaṃ darśayati bhagavān | tac ca kiṃ-nimittaṃ jagato 'jñānam ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The <s>Bhagavān</s> shows compassion, saying that the world does not recognize Me, who am such — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and liberated, the Self of all beings, beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, the cause of burning away the seed of the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And what is the cause of this ignorance of the world? This is stated —

children.text: tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: By these three states (<s>bhāvas</s>) composed of the <s>guṇas</s>, this entire world

children.text: mohitaṃ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam ||BhG_7.13||
children.translated_text: is deluded and does not recognize Me, who am beyond these, supreme and imperishable. ||BhG_7.13||

children.text: tribhir guṇa-mayaiḥ guṇa-vikāraiḥ rāga-dveṣa-mohādi-prakārair bhāvaiḥ padārthair ebhir yathoktaiḥ sarvam idaṃ prāṇi-jātaṃ jagan mohitam avivekitām āpāditaṃ san nābhijānāni mām | ebhyo yathoktebhyo guṇebhyaḥ paraṃ vyatiriktaṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ cāvyayaṃ vyaya-rahitaṃ janmādi-sarva-bhāva-vikāra-varjitam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_7.13||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] By three — that is, by modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>, by states (<s>bhāvas</s>), meaning things of the nature of attachment, aversion, delusion, and the like — by these as described, this entire world of living beings, being deluded, that is, brought to a state of non-discrimination, does not recognize Me. Beyond these <s>guṇas</s> as described means different from them, of a distinct nature, and imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>) means free from decay, devoid of all modifications of existence such as birth and the rest — this is the meaning. ||BhGS_7.13||

children.text: kathaṃ punar daivīm etāṃ triguṇātmikāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ māyām atikrāmatīty ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Now, how does one cross beyond this divine <s>māyā</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>? This is stated —

children.text: daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā |
children.translated_text: For this divine <s>māyā</s> of Mine, consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>, is difficult to cross beyond;

children.text: mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te ||BhG_7.14||
children.translated_text: those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond this <s>māyā</s>. ||BhG_7.14||

children.text:
daivī devasya mameśvarasya viṣṇoḥ svabhāva-bhūtā hi yasmād eṣā yathoktā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā duḥkhenātyayo 'tikramaṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā duratyayā | tatraivaṃ sati sarva-dharmān parityajya mām eva māyāvinaṃ svātma-bhūtaṃ sarvātmanā ye prapadyante te
māyām etāṃ sarva-bhūta-mohinīṃ taranty atikrāmanti | te saṃsāra-bandhanān mucyanta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_7.14||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Divine (<s>daivī</s>) means belonging to the <s>Deva</s>, that is, to Me, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being of His very nature; for since this <s>māyā</s> of Mine, as described, consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>, is difficult to cross beyond — meaning that which is hard to transcend or surmount, that is <s>duratyayā</s>. This being so, abandoning all <s>dharmas</s>, those who take refuge with their whole being in Me alone, the wielder of <s>māyā</s>, who am their very Self, they cross beyond, they transcend this <s>māyā</s> that deludes all beings. They are freed from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. ||BhGS_7.14||

children.text: yadi tvāṃ prapannāḥ māyām etāṃ taranti, kasmāt tvām eva sarve na prapadyante ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] If those who have taken refuge in You cross beyond this <s>māyā</s>, why do not all take refuge in You alone? This is stated —

children.text: na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ |
children.translated_text: The evil-doers (<s>duṣkṛtins</s>), the deluded, the lowest among men, do not take refuge in Me,

children.text: māyayāpahṛta-jñānā āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ ||BhG_7.15||
children.translated_text: those whose knowledge has been stolen by <s>māyā</s>, who have resorted to a demonic (<s>āsura</s>) disposition. ||BhG_7.15||

children.text: na māṃ parameśvaraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ duṣkṛtinaḥ pāpa-kāriṇaḥ mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamā narāṇāṃ madhye 'dhamāḥ nikṛṣṭaḥ | te ca māyayāpahṛta-jñānāḥ saṃmuṣita-jñānā āsuraṃ bhāvaṃ hiṃsānṛtādi-lakṣaṇam āśritāḥ ||BhGS_7.15||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The evil-doers (<s>duṣkṛtins</s>), those who perform sinful actions, the deluded, do not take refuge in Me, the Supreme Lord, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; the lowest among men (<s>narādhamāḥ</s>) means the most base among human beings. And they are those whose knowledge has been stolen by <s>māyā</s>, whose knowledge has been robbed away, who have resorted to a demonic disposition characterized by violence, falsehood, and the like. ||BhGS_7.15||

children.text: ye punar narottamāḥ puṇya-karmāṇaḥ -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] On the other hand, those who are the best among men, of meritorious deeds —

children.text: catur-vidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, O <s>Arjuna</s>:

children.text: ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha ||BhG_7.16||
children.translated_text: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of knowledge, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>. ||BhG_7.16||

children.text: catur-vidhāś catuḥ-prakārā bhajante sevante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtinaḥ puṇya-karmāṇo he 'rjuna | ārta ārti-parigṛhītas taskara-vyāghra-rogādinābhibhūta āpannaḥ | jijñāsur bhagavat-tattvaṃ jñātum icchati yaḥ | arthārthī dhana-kāmaḥ | jñānī viṣṇos tattva-vic ca he bharatarṣabha ||BhGS_7.16||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Four kinds, of four types, worship, serve Me — these people of meritorious deeds, of virtuous actions, O <s>Arjuna</s>. The distressed (<s>ārta</s>) is one seized by affliction, overcome by thieves, tigers, disease, and the like. The seeker of knowledge (<s>jijñāsu</s>) is one who wishes to know the true nature of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The seeker of wealth (<s>arthārthī</s>) is one who desires riches. And the man of knowledge (<s>jñānī</s>) is one who knows the true nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>. ||BhGS_7.16||

children.text: teṣāṃ jñānī nitya-yukta eka-bhaktir viśiṣyate |
children.translated_text: Among these, the man of knowledge, ever steadfast and single in devotion, excels;

children.text: priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ ||BhG_7.17||
children.translated_text: for I am exceedingly dear to the man of knowledge, and he is dear to Me. ||BhG_7.17||

children.text: teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ madhye jñānī tattva-vit tattva-vittvān nitya-yukto bhavati | eka-bhaktiś ca, anyasya bhajanīyasyādarśanāt | ataḥ sa eka-bhaktir viśiṣyate viśeṣam ādhikyam āpadyate, atiricyata ity arthaḥ | priyo hi yasmād aham ātmā jñānino 'tas tasyāham atyarthaṃ priyaḥ | prasiddhaṃ hi loke ātmā priyo bhavatīti | tasmāj jñānina ātmatvād vāsudevaḥ priyo bhavatīty arthaḥ | sa ca jñānī mama vāsudevasya ātmaiveti mamātyarthaṃ priyaḥ ||BhGS_7.17||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Among these four, the man of knowledge (<s>jñānī</s>), the knower of truth, being a knower of truth is ever steadfast (<s>nitya-yukta</s>). And he is of single devotion (<s>eka-bhakti</s>), since he sees no other object worthy of worship. Therefore he, being of single devotion, excels, attains distinction, surpasses the others — this is the meaning. For since I am the Self of the man of knowledge, therefore I am exceedingly dear to him. For it is well known in the world that the Self is dear. Therefore, because <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the Self of the man of knowledge, <s>Vāsudeva</s> is dear to him — this is the meaning. And that man of knowledge is exceedingly dear to Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, for he is My very Self. ||BhGS_7.17||

children.text: na tarhy ārtādayas trayo vāsudevasya priyāḥ ? na | kiṃ tarhi ? -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Are then the distressed and the other three not dear to <s>Vāsudeva</s>? No. What then? —

children.text: udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam |
children.translated_text: All these are indeed noble, but the man of knowledge I regard as My very Self;

children.text: āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṃ gatim ||BhG_7.18||
children.translated_text: for he, with mind steadfast, is established in Me alone as the supreme goal. ||BhG_7.18||

children.text: udārā utkṛṣṭāḥ sarva evaite | trayo 'pi mama priyā evety arthaḥ | na hi kaścin mad-bhakto vāsudevasyāpriyo bhavati | jñānī tv atyarthaṃ priyo bhavatīti viśeṣaḥ | tat kasmāt ? ity ata āha - jñānī tv ātmaiva, nānyo matta iti me mama mataṃ niścayaḥ | āsthita āroḍhuṃ pravṛttaḥ sa jñānī hi yasmād aham eva bhagavān vāsudevo nānyo 'smīty evaṃ yuktātmā samāhita-cittaḥ san mām eva paraṃ brahma gantavyam anuttamāṃ gatiṃ gantuṃ pravṛtta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_7.18||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Noble, meaning exalted, are all these indeed. Even the other three are dear to Me — this is the meaning. For no devotee of Mine is unloved by <s>Vāsudeva</s>. But the man of knowledge is exceedingly dear — this is the distinction. Why is that? To this he says — the man of knowledge is My very Self, not different from Me; this is My firm conviction. He has set out, that man of knowledge has embarked, for since he is of steadfast mind (<s>yuktātmā</s>), of concentrated thought, considering 'I am none other than the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vāsudeva</s>,' he has set out to attain Me alone, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the unsurpassed goal — this is the meaning. ||BhGS_7.18||

children.text: jñānī punar api stūyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The man of knowledge is praised once again —

children.text: bahūnāṃ janmanām ante jñānavān māṃ prapadyate |
children.translated_text: At the end of many births, the man of knowledge takes refuge in Me,

children.text: vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ ||BhG_7.19||
children.translated_text: realizing that <s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything — such a great soul (<s>mahātmā</s>) is very rare. ||BhG_7.19||

children.text: bahūnāṃ janmanāṃ jñānārtha-saṃskārāśrayāṇām ante samāptau jñānavān prāpta-paripāka-jñāno māṃ vāsudevaṃ pratyag-ātmānaṃ pratyakṣataḥ prapadyate | katham ? vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti | ya evaṃ sarvātmānaṃ māṃ nārāyaṇaṃ pratipadyate, sa mahātmā | na tat-samo 'nyo 'sti, adhiko vā | ataḥ sudurlabhaḥ, manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣv iti hy uktam ||BhGS_7.19||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] At the end, at the completion, of many births that have served as the ground for accumulated impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) aimed at knowledge, the man of knowledge, whose knowledge has reached full maturity, takes refuge in Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the inner Self, directly. How? Realizing that '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything.' He who thus realizes Me, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, as the Self of all — he is a great soul (<s>mahātmā</s>). There is none equal to him, nor superior. Therefore he is very rare, for it has been said 'among thousands of men' [BhG 7.3]. ||BhGS_7.19||

children.text: ātmaiva sarvṃ vāsudeva ity evam apratipattau kāraṇam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The cause of the failure to realize that <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone is the Self of all is now stated —

children.text: kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those whose knowledge has been carried away by various desires take refuge in other deities,

children.text: taṃ taṃ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā ||BhG_7.20||
children.translated_text: following this or that observance, constrained by their own nature. ||BhG_7.20||

children.text: kāmais tais taiḥ putra-paśu-svargādi-viṣayair hṛta-jñānāḥ apahṛta-viveka-vijñānāḥ prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ prāpnuvanti vāsudevād ātmano 'nyā devatāḥ | taṃ taṃ niyamaṃ devatārādhane prasiddho yo yo niyamas taṃ tam āsthāya āśritya prakṛtyā svabhāvena janmāntarārjita-saṃskāra-viśeṣeṇa niyatāḥ niyamitāḥ svayātmīyayā ||BhGS_7.20||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Those whose knowledge, whose discriminative understanding, has been carried away by various desires pertaining to sons, cattle, heaven, and the like, take refuge in, that is, resort to other deities — deities other than <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Self. Following this or that observance, meaning adopting whatever particular observance is well known for the worship of that deity, constrained by their own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), that is, by the particular impressions acquired in previous births. ||BhGS_7.20||

children.text: teṣāṃ ca kāminām -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And for those who are driven by desires —

children.text: yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati |
children.translated_text: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith,

children.text: tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham ||BhG_7.21||
children.translated_text: I make that faith of his firm and unwavering. ||BhG_7.21||

children.text: yo yaḥ kāmī yāṃ yāṃ devatā-tanuṃ śraddhayā saṃyukto bhaktaś ca sann arcituṃ pūjayitum icchati, tasya tasya kāmino 'calāṃ sthirāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmi sthirīkaromi ||BhGS_7.21||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Whatever person driven by desire, whatever form of a deity he, endowed with faith and being a devotee, wishes to worship and honor — of that person driven by desire, I make firm and steady that very faith. ||BhGS_7.21||

children.text: yayaiva pūrvaṃ pravṛttaḥ svabhāvato yo yāṃ devatā-tanuṃ śraddhayārcitum icchati -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Impelled by that very prior inclination, one who by his own nature wishes to worship a particular form of a deity with faith —

children.text: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyā rādhanam īhate |
children.translated_text: Endowed with that faith, he seeks the propitiation of that deity,

children.text: labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān ||BhG_7.22||
children.translated_text: and from that he obtains his desires, which are indeed ordained by Me alone. ||BhG_7.22||

children.text: sa tayā mad-vihitayā śraddhayā yuktaḥ san tasyā devatā-tanvā rādhanam ārādhanam īhate ceṣṭate | labhate ca tatas tasyā ārādhitāyā devatā-tanvāḥ kāmān īpsitān mayaiva parameśvareṇa sarvajñena karma-phala-vibhāga-jñatayā vihitān nirmitān tān, hi yasmāt te bhagavatā vihitāḥ kāmās tasmāt tān avaśyaṃ labhate ity arthaḥ | hitān iti pada-cchede hitatvaṃ kāmānām upacaritaṃ kalpyam | na hi kāmā hitāḥ kasyacit ||BhGS_7.22||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] He, endowed with that faith ordained by Me, seeks, that is, strives for the propitiation, the worship, of that form of the deity. And from that, from that worshipped form of the deity, he obtains the desired objects, which are indeed ordained, that is, arranged by Me alone, the Supreme Lord, the Omniscient One, by virtue of knowing the proper distribution of the fruits of action. Since those desires are ordained by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, therefore he necessarily obtains them — this is the meaning. If the word is read as <s>hitān</s> (beneficial), then the beneficial nature of the desires is figurative and must be construed as such, for desires are never truly beneficial to anyone. ||BhGS_7.22||

children.text: yasmād antavat sādhana-vyāpārāvivekinaḥ kāminaś ca te | ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since the means they employ are finite, and since they are persons of desire who lack discrimination, therefore —

children.text: antavat tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhavaty alpa-medhasām |
children.translated_text: But the fruit that accrues to those of small understanding is finite;

children.text: devān deva-yajo yānti mad-bhaktā yānti mām api ||BhG_7.23||
children.translated_text: the worshippers of the gods go to the gods, but My devotees come to Me as well. ||BhG_7.23||

children.text: antavad vināśi tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhavaty alpa-medhasām alpa-prajñānām | devān deva-yajo yānti devān yajantīti deva-yajaḥ, te devān yānti | mad-bhaktā yānti mām api | evaṃ samāne 'py āyāse mām eva na prapadyante 'nanta-phalāya | aho khalu kaṣṭaṃ vartata ity anukrośaṃ darśayati bhagavān ||BhGS_7.23||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Finite, meaning perishable, is the fruit that accrues to those of small understanding, those of limited intellect. The worshippers of the gods go to the gods — those who worship the gods are god-worshippers, and they go to the gods. But My devotees come to Me as well. Thus, though the effort is the same, they do not take refuge in Me alone for the sake of infinite fruit. Alas, what a pity indeed! — thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> shows compassion. ||BhGS_7.23||

children.text: kiṃ-nimittaṃ mām eva na prapadyanta ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The reason why they do not take refuge in Me alone is now stated —

children.text: avyaktaṃ vyaktim āpannaṃ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The unintelligent regard Me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifestation,

children.text: paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mamāvyayam anuttamam ||BhG_7.24||
children.translated_text: not knowing My supreme nature, which is imperishable and unsurpassed. ||BhG_7.24||

children.text: avyaktam aprakāśaṃ vyaktim āpannaṃ prakāśaṃ gatam idānīṃ manyante māṃ nitya-prasiddham īśvaram api santam abuddhayo 'vivekinaḥ paraṃ bhāvaṃ param ātma-svarūpam ajānanto 'vivekinaḥ mamāvyayaṃ vyaya-rahitam anuttamaṃ niratiśayaṃ madīyaṃ bhāvam ajānanto manyanta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_7.24||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The unmanifest, meaning not evident, as having come into manifestation, meaning as having become visible now — thus they regard Me, though I am the eternally well-known Lord. The unintelligent, the undiscriminating, not knowing My supreme nature — My supreme essential nature, which is imperishable, free from decay, and unsurpassed, without anything higher — not knowing this nature of Mine, they think thus — this is the meaning. ||BhGS_7.24||

children.text: tad-ajñānaṃ kiṃ-nimittam ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] What is the cause of that ignorance? This is stated —

children.text: nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am not manifest to all, being veiled by <s>yoga-māyā</s>;

children.text: mūḍho 'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam ||BhG_7.25||
children.translated_text: this deluded world does not recognize Me, the unborn and imperishable. ||BhG_7.25||

children.text: nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya lokasya, keṣāṃcid eva mad-bhaktānāṃ prakāśo 'ham ity abhiprāyaḥ | yoga-māyā-samāvṛto yogo guṇānāṃ yuktir ghaṭanaṃ saiva māyā yoga-māyā | tayā yogamāyayā samāvṛtaḥ, saṃchanna ity arthaḥ | ata eva mūḍho loko 'yaṃ nābhijānāti mām ajam avyayam ||BhGS_7.25||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] I am not manifest to all people — the implication is that I am manifest only to certain devotees of Mine. Veiled by <s>yoga-māyā</s> — <s>yoga</s> is the conjunction, the combination of the <s>guṇas</s>; that itself is <s>māyā</s>, hence <s>yoga-māyā</s>. By that <s>yoga-māyā</s> I am veiled, meaning concealed — this is the sense. Therefore indeed this deluded world does not recognize Me, the unborn and imperishable. ||BhGS_7.25||

children.text: vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna |
children.translated_text: I know the beings that have passed, those that are present, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana ||BhG_7.26||
children.translated_text: and those that are yet to be; but no one knows Me. ||BhG_7.26||

children.text: yayā yogamāyayā samāvṛtaṃ māṃ loko nābhijānāti, nāsau yogamāyā madīyā satī mameśvarasya māyāvino jñānaṃ pratibadhnāti | yathānyasyāpi māyāvino māyā jñānaṃ tadvat | yataḥ evam, ataḥ -- ahaṃ tu veda jāne samatītāni samatikrāntāni bhūtāni, vartamānāni cārjuna, bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni vedāham | māṃ tu veda na kaścana mad-bhaktaṃ mac-charaṇam ekaṃ muktvā | mat-tattva-vedanābhāvād eva na māṃ bhajate ||BhGS_7.26||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] By that <s>yoga-māyā</s> through which the world, being veiled, does not recognize Me — that <s>yoga-māyā</s>, being Mine, belonging to Me the Lord, the wielder of <s>māyā</s>, does not obstruct My knowledge, just as the <s>māyā</s> of any other magician does not obstruct his own knowledge. Since this is so, therefore — I know, I am aware of beings that have passed, that have gone by, those that are present, O <s>Arjuna</s>, and those that are yet to be — I know them all. But no one knows Me — except My devotee who has taken sole refuge in Me. It is precisely because of the absence of knowledge of My true nature that no one worships Me. ||BhGS_7.26||

children.text: kena punar mat-tattva-vedana-pratibandhena pratibaddhāni santi jāyamānāni sarva-bhūtāni māṃ na vidanti ? ity apekṣāyām idam āha -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] By what obstruction to the knowledge of My true nature are all beings, from the moment of their birth, obstructed so that they do not know Me? In anticipation of this question, this is stated —

children.text: icchā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata |
children.translated_text: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: sarva-bhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa ||BhG_7.27||
children.translated_text: all beings fall into complete delusion at the time of creation, O scorcher of foes. ||BhG_7.27||

children.text:
icchā-dveṣa-samutthena icchā ca dveṣaś cecchā-dveṣau | tābhyāṃ samuttiṣṭhatītīcchā-dveṣa-samutthas tenecchā-dveṣa-samutthena | keneti viśeṣāpekṣāyām idam āha - dvandva-mohena dvandva-nimitto moho dvandva-mohas tena | tāv eva icchā-dveṣau śītoṣṇavat paraspara-viruddhau sukha-duḥkha-tad-dhetu-viṣayau yathā-kālaṃ sarva-bhūtaiḥ saṃbadhyamānau dvandva-śabdenābhidhīyete | tatra yadecchā-dveṣau sukha-duḥkha-tad-dhetu-saṃprāptyā labdhātmakau bhavataḥ, tadā tau sarva-bhūtānāṃ prajñāyāḥ sva-vaśāpādana-dvāreṇa paramārthātma-tattva-viṣaya-jñānotpatti-pratibandha-kāraṇaṃ mohaṃ janayataḥ | na hīcchā-dveṣa-doṣa-vaśīkṛta-cittasya yathā-bhūtārtha-viṣaya-jñānam utpadyate bahir api | kim u vaktavyaṃ tābhyām āviṣṭa-buddheḥ saṃmūḍhasya pratyag-ātmani
bahu-pratibandhe jñānaṃ notpadyateti | atas tena icchā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena, bhārata bharatānvayaja, sarva-bhūtāni saṃmohitāni santi saṃmohaṃ saṃmūḍhatāṃ sarge janmani, utpatti-kāle ity etat, yānti gacchanti he paraṃtapa | moha-vaśāny eva sarva-bhūtāni jāyamānāni jāyanta ity abhiprāyaḥ | yata evam atas tena dvandva-mohena pratibaddha-prajñānāni sarva-bhūtāni saṃmohitāni mām ātma-bhūtaṃ na jānanti | ata eva ātma-bhāvena māṃ na bhajante ||BhGS_7.27||
children.translated_text: "Arising from desire and aversion" — <s>icchā</s> (desire) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) together are <s>icchā-dveṣa</s>; that which arises from these two is <s>icchā-dveṣa-samuttha</s>, by that which arises from desire and aversion. When the question "by what?" expects a specific answer, he says — "by the delusion of the pairs of opposites": the delusion caused by the pairs is <s>dvandva-moha</s> (delusion of opposites), by that. Those very desire and aversion, mutually opposed like cold and heat, having as their objects pleasure and pain and their causes, being associated with all beings according to the occasion, are denoted by the word <s>dvandva</s> (pair of opposites). There, when desire and aversion become actualized through the attainment of pleasure and pain and their causes, then those two, by means of bringing the understanding under their control, produce <s>moha</s> (delusion) which is the cause of obstruction to the arising of knowledge concerning the truth of the supreme Self. For even regarding external objects, knowledge of things as they truly are does not arise for one whose mind is overpowered by the defects of desire and aversion; how much more need it be said that for one whose intellect is possessed by those two and who is thoroughly deluded, knowledge does not arise regarding the inner Self, where there are many obstructions. Therefore, by that <s>dvandva-moha</s> (delusion of opposites) arising from desire and aversion, O <s>Bhārata</s>, descendant of <s>Bharata</s>'s lineage, all beings are deluded — they go to delusion, to complete bewilderment, at birth, at the time of origination, this is the meaning — they go, O <s>Paraṃtapa</s> (scorcher of foes). The purport is that all beings are born subject to delusion. Since this is so, therefore all beings, whose understanding is obstructed by that <s>dvandva-moha</s>, being deluded, do not know Me who am the Self. For this very reason they do not worship Me as their own Self. ||BhGS 7.27||

children.text: ke punar anena dvandva-mohena nirmuktāḥ santas tvāṃ viditvā yathā-śāstram ātma-bhāve bhajanta ity apekṣitam arthaṃ darśayitum ucyate -
children.translated_text: To show the expected meaning — "Who then, being freed from this <s>dvandva-moha</s> (delusion of opposites), knowing You, worship You as the Self in accordance with the scriptures?" — it is said:

children.text: yeṣāṃ tv anta-gataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇya-karmaṇām |
children.translated_text: But those persons of meritorious deeds whose sin has come to an end,

children.text: te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍha-vratāḥ ||BhG_7.28||
children.translated_text: They, freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me with firm vows. ||BhG 7.28||

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu punar anta-gataṃ samāpta-prāyaṃ kṣīṇaṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇya-karmaṇāṃ puṇyaṃ karma yeṣāṃ sattva-śuddhi-kāraṇaṃ vidyate te puṇya-karmāṇas teṣāṃ puṇya-karmaṇām, te dvandva-moha-nirmuktā yathoktena dvandva-mohena nirmuktā bhajante māṃ paramātmanāṃ dṛḍha-vratāḥ | evam eva paramārtha-tattvaṃ nānyathety evaṃ sarva-parityāga-vratena niścita-vijñānā dṛḍha-vratā ucyante ||BhGS_7.28||
children.translated_text: But those persons whose sin has "come to an end" — has nearly ended, has been exhausted — who are "of meritorious deeds," meaning those who possess meritorious action (<s>puṇya-karma</s>) which is the cause of purification of <s>sattva</s> (inner being), they are "of meritorious deeds." They, "freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites" — freed from the <s>dvandva-moha</s> as described — "worship Me," the Supreme Self, "with firm vows." Those who have settled conviction through the vow of complete renunciation that "This alone is the ultimate truth and not otherwise" are called "of firm vows" (<s>dṛḍha-vratāḥ</s>). ||BhGS 7.28||

children.text: te kim-arthaṃ bhajante ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: For what purpose do they worship? This is stated:

children.text: jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye |
children.translated_text: Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me,

children.text: te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam ||BhG_7.29||
children.translated_text: They know that <s>Brahman</s> completely, as well as <s>adhyātma</s> (the Self) and <s>karma</s> (action) in its entirety. ||BhG 7.29||

children.text: jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya jarā-maraṇayor mokṣārthaṃ māṃ parameśvaram āśritya mat-samāhita-cittāḥ santo yatanti prayatante ye, te yad brahma paraṃ tad viduḥ kṛtsnaṃ samastam adhyātmaṃ pratyag-ātma-viṣayaṃ vastu tad viduḥ | karma cākhilaṃ samastaṃ viduḥ ||BhGS_7.29||
children.translated_text: "For liberation from old age and death" — for the purpose of liberation from old age and death, having taken refuge in Me, the Supreme Lord, with minds absorbed in Me, those who strive, who make effort — they know that supreme <s>Brahman</s> completely, in its entirety; they know <s>adhyātma</s>, the reality pertaining to the inner Self; and they know <s>karma</s> (action) entirely, in full. ||BhGS 7.29||

children.text: sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who know Me together with <s>adhibhūta</s> (the physical realm) and <s>adhidaiva</s> (the divine realm), and together with <s>adhiyajña</s> (the sacrificial realm),

children.text: prayāṇa-kāle 'pi ca māṃ te vidur yukta-cetasaḥ ||BhG_7.30||
children.translated_text: They, with minds absorbed in yoga, know Me even at the time of departure. ||BhG 7.30||

children.text: sādhibhūtādhidaivam adhibhūtaṃ cādhidaivaṃ cādhibhūtādhidaivam, sahādhibhūtādhidaivena vartata iti sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ ca māṃ ye viduḥ | sādhiyajñaṃ ca sahādhiyajñena sādhiyajñaṃ ye viduḥ, prayāṇa-kāle maraṇa-kāle 'pi ca māṃ te viduḥ | yukta-cetasaḥ samāhita-cittā iti ||BhGS_7.30||
children.translated_text: "Together with <s>adhibhūta</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s>" — <s>adhibhūta</s> (the physical realm) and <s>adhidaiva</s> (the divine realm) together are <s>adhibhūtādhidaiva</s>; that which exists together with <s>adhibhūtādhidaiva</s> is <s>sādhibhūtādhidaiva</s> — those who know Me thus. "And together with <s>adhiyajña</s>" — together with <s>adhiyajña</s> (the sacrificial realm) is <s>sādhiyajña</s> — those who know [Me thus]. They know Me even at the time of departure, at the time of death. "With minds absorbed in yoga" means with concentrated minds. ||BhGS 7.30||

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus in the blessed commentary on the <s>Śrīmad Bhagavad Gītā</s>, composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, the disciple of the revered feet of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavat</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: who is the <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya</s> (supreme renunciant and wandering teacher),

children.text: saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ends the seventh chapter.

children.text: BhG 8
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> Chapter 8

children.text:
atha brahmākṣara-nirdeśo nāma
aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the eighth chapter, named "The Teaching on the Imperishable <s>Brahman</s>" (<s>Brahmākṣara-nirdeśa</s>).

children.text: (śrīmac-chaṅkarācārya-bhagavat-pāda-viracita-bhāṣyaḥ)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavatpāda</s>)

children.text: te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam ity ādinā bhagavatārjunasya praśna-bījāni upadiṣṭani | atas tat-praśnārtham arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: By the statement "They know that <s>Brahman</s> completely" and so forth, the Lord indicated the seeds of <s>Arjuna</s>'s questions. Therefore, for the purpose of asking those questions, <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama |
children.translated_text: What is that <s>Brahman</s>? What is <s>adhyātma</s> (the Self)? What is <s>karma</s> (action), O <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person)?

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktam adhidaivaṃ kim ucyate ||BhG_8.1||
children.translated_text: What is declared as <s>adhibhūta</s> (the physical realm)? And what is called <s>adhidaiva</s> (the divine realm)? ||BhG 8.1||

children.text: adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: Who and how is the <s>adhiyajña</s> (the Lord of sacrifice) here in this body, O <s>Madhusūdana</s> (slayer of Madhu)?

children.text: prayāṇa-kāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo 'si niyatātmabhiḥ ||BhG_8.2||
children.translated_text: And how are You to be known at the time of departure by those of controlled selves? ||BhG 8.2||

children.text: eṣāṃ praśnānāṃ yathā-kramaṃ nirṇayāya śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: To determine these questions in their proper order, the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate |
children.translated_text: The imperishable is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; one's own nature is called <s>adhyātma</s> (the Self);

children.text: bhūtabhāvodbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṃjñitaḥ ||BhG_8.3||
children.translated_text: The creative act that brings about the origination of the existence of beings is designated as <s>karma</s> (action). ||BhG 8.3||

children.text:
akṣaraṃ na kṣaratīty akṣaraṃ para ātmā, etasya vākṣarasya praśāsane gārgi [BAU 3.8.9] iti śruteḥ | oṃkārasya ca om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma [Gītā 8.13] iti pareṇa viśeṣaṇād agrahaṇam | paramam iti ca niratiśaye brahmaṇy akṣare upapannataram viśeṣaṇam | tasyaiva parasya brahmaṇaḥ pratidehaṃ pratyag-ātma-bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ | svo bhāvaḥ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate | ātmānaṃ deham adhikṛtya pratyag-ātmatayā pravṛttaṃ paramārtha-brahmāvasānaṃ vastu svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate 'dhyātma-śabdenābhidhīyate | bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karo bhūtānāṃ bhāvo bhūta-bhāvas tasya udbhavo bhūta-bhāvodbhavas taṃ karotīti bhūta-bhāvodbhava-karaḥ, bhūta-vastūtpatti-kara ity arthaḥ | visargo visarjanaṃ devatoddeśena caru-puroḍāśāder dravyasya parityāgaḥ | sa eṣa visarga-lakṣaṇo yajñaḥ
karma-saṃjñitaḥ karma-śabdita ity etat | etasmāt hi bīja-bhūtād vṛṣṭyaḍādi-krameṇa sthāvara-jaṅgamāni bhūtāny udbhavanti ||BhGS_8.3||
children.translated_text: "<s>Akṣara</s>" (the imperishable) — that which does not perish is <s>akṣara</s>, the Supreme Self, as the <s>śruti</s> states: "Under the rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>" [BAU 3.8.9]. And <s>Oṃkāra</s> is not taken here because it is later qualified separately as "<s>Om</s>, the single-syllable <s>Brahman</s>" [Gītā 8.13]. The qualifier "supreme" (<s>parama</s>) is more fitting for the unsurpassed <s>Brahman</s>, the Imperishable. The individual self-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of that very supreme <s>Brahman</s> in each body is <s>adhyātma</s>: one's own (<s>sva</s>) being (<s>bhāva</s>) is <s>svabhāva</s>, called <s>adhyātma</s>. That reality which, in reference to the body (<s>deha</s>), operates as the inner Self and culminates in the ultimate <s>Brahman</s>, is <s>svabhāva</s>, denoted by the term <s>adhyātma</s>. "That which brings about the origination of the existence of beings" — <s>bhūta-bhāva</s> is the existence of beings; <s>udbhava</s> is the origination of that; that which produces it is <s>bhūta-bhāvodbhava-kara</s>, meaning "that which causes the production of material entities." <s>Visarga</s> (offering) is the giving away, the relinquishing of substances such as <s>caru</s> (oblation) and <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) for the sake of deities. This sacrifice characterized by <s>visarga</s> (offering) is designated by the word <s>karma</s> (action). For from this, which is the seed, through the sequence of rain and so forth, movable and immovable beings originate. ||BhGS 8.3||

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś cādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: <s>Adhibhūta</s> (the physical realm) is the perishable nature of things; and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Cosmic Person) is <s>adhidaivata</s> (the presiding deity);

children.text: adhiyajño 'ham evātra dehe deha-bhṛtāṃ vara ||BhG_8.4||
children.translated_text: The <s>adhiyajña</s> (Lord of sacrifice) is none other than Myself here in this body, O best of the embodied ones. ||BhG 8.4||

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ prāṇi-jātam adhikṛtya bhavatīti | ko 'sau ? kṣaraḥ kṣaratīti kṣaro vināśī, bhāvo yat kiṃcit janimat vastv ity arthaḥ | puruṣaḥ pūrṇam anena sarvam iti, puri śayanāt vā, puruṣaḥ ādityāntargato hiraṇyagarbhaḥ, sarva-prāṇi-karaṇānām anugrāhakaḥ, so 'dhidaivatam | adhiyajñaḥ sarva-yajñābhimāninī viṣṇv-ākhyā devatā, yajño vai viṣṇuḥ [TaittS 1.7.4] iti śruteḥ | sa hi viṣṇur aham eva | atrāsmin dehe yo yajñas tasyāham adhiyajñaḥ | yajño hi deha-nirvartyatvena deha-samavāyīti dehādhikaraṇo bhavati, deha-bhṛtāṃ vara ! ||BhGS_8.4||
children.translated_text: <s>Adhibhūta</s> is that which exists in reference to living beings. What is it? <s>Kṣara</s> (the perishable) — that which perishes is <s>kṣara</s>, meaning destructible; <s>bhāva</s> means whatever entity is subject to birth. <s>Puruṣa</s> — so called because everything is filled by Him, or because He lies in the city (of the body) — is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the golden embryo) dwelling within the sun, the benefactor of the sense organs of all living beings; He is <s>adhidaivata</s> (the presiding deity). <s>Adhiyajña</s> (the Lord of sacrifice) is the deity called <s>Viṣṇu</s> who presides over all sacrifices, as the <s>śruti</s> states: "The sacrifice is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>" [TaittS 1.7.4]. That <s>Viṣṇu</s> is none other than Myself. In this body, I am the <s>adhiyajña</s> of whatever sacrifice takes place. For sacrifice, being accomplished through the body, inheres in the body, and thus the body is its locus — O best of the embodied ones! ||BhGS 8.4||

children.text: anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram |
children.translated_text: And at the final hour, remembering Me alone, whoever departs leaving the body,

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ ||BhG_8.5||
children.translated_text: He attains My state of being; there is no doubt about this. ||BhG 8.5||

children.text: anta-kāle maraṇa-kāle ca mām eva parameśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ smaran muktvā parityajya kalevaraṃ śarīraṃ yaḥ prayāti gacchati | sa mad-bhāvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tattvaṃ yāti | nāsti na vidyate 'trāsminn arthe saṃśayaḥ - yāti vā na veti ||
children.translated_text: "At the final hour" — at the time of death, remembering Me alone, the Supreme Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, "leaving" — abandoning — "the body," whoever departs, goes — he attains "My state of being," the reality that is <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s nature). There is no doubt about this matter — whether he attains it or not.

children.text: na mad-viṣaya evāyaṃ niyamaḥ | kiṃ tarhi ? -
children.translated_text: This rule does not apply only to Me. What then?

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram |
children.translated_text: Whatever state of being one remembers when giving up the body at the end,

children.text: taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ ||BhG_8.6||
children.translated_text: That very state one attains, O <s>Kaunteya</s> (son of <s>Kuntī</s>), always being absorbed in that thought. ||BhG 8.6||

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ vāpi yaṃ yaṃ bhāvaṃ devatā-viśeṣaṃ smaran cintayan tyajati parityajaty ante 'nta-kāle prāṇa-viyoga-kāle kalevaraṃ śarīraṃ taṃ tam eva smṛtaṃ bhāvam eva eti nānyaṃ kaunteya, sadā sarvadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitas tasmin bhāvas tad-bhāvaḥ sa bhāvitaḥ smaryamāṇatayābhyasto yena sa tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ san ||BhGS_8.6||
children.translated_text: "Whatever" — whatever <s>bhāva</s> (state of being), whatever particular deity one remembers, thinks of, when one gives up, abandons, at the end, at the final hour, at the time of separation of the vital breath, the body — that very remembered state of being alone one attains, and no other, O <s>Kaunteya</s>. "Always being absorbed in that thought" (<s>sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ</s>) — <s>tad-bhāva</s> is the thought of that; being <s>bhāvita</s> means cultivated through repeated practice of remembrance; one who is thus is <s>tad-bhāva-bhāvita</s>. ||BhGS 8.6||

children.text: yasmād evam antyā bhāvanā dehāntara-prāptau kāraṇam -
children.translated_text: Since thus the final contemplation is the cause of attaining another body —

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca |
children.translated_text: Therefore, at all times remember Me, and fight.

children.text: mayy arpita-mano-buddhir mām evaiṣyasy asaṃśayaḥ ||BhG_8.7||
children.translated_text: With mind and intellect offered to Me, you shall surely come to Me, without doubt. ||BhG 8.7||

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yathā-śāstram | yudhyaś ca yuddhaṃ sva-dharmaṃ kuru | mayi vāsudeve 'rpite mano-buddhī yasya tava sa tvaṃ mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ san mām eva yathā-smṛtam eṣyasy āgamiṣyasi | asaṃśayo na saṃśayo 'tra vidyate ||BhGS_8.7||
children.translated_text: Therefore, at all times, remember Me in accordance with the scriptures. And fight — perform your own <s>dharma</s> (duty) of battle. Having offered mind and intellect to Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, you, being one whose mind and intellect are thus offered to Me, shall come to Me, as remembered — you shall attain Me. There is no doubt, no uncertainty about this. ||BhGS 8.7||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena cetasā nānya-gāminā |
children.translated_text: With a mind engaged in the yoga of practice, not wandering elsewhere,

children.text: paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan ||BhG_8.8||
children.translated_text: One goes to the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), the divine, O <s>Pārtha</s> (son of <s>Pṛthā</s>), constantly meditating. ||BhG 8.8||

children.text: abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena mayi citta-samarpaṇa-viṣaya-bhūta ekasmiṃs tulya-pratyayāvṛtti-lakṣaṇo vilakṣaṇa-pratyayānantarito 'bhyāsaḥ sa cābhyāso yogas tena yuktaṃ tatraiva vyāpṛtaṃ yoginaś cetas tena | cetasā nānya-gāminā nānyatra viṣayāntare gantuṃ śīlam asyeti nānya-gāmi tena nānya-gāminā, paramaṃ niratiśayaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ divi sūrya-maṇḍāle bhavaṃ yāti gacchati he pārthānucintayan śāstrācāryopadeśam anudhyāyan ity etat ||BhGS_8.8||
children.translated_text: "Engaged in the yoga of practice" — <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) is the repetition of identical mental states directed toward a single object, namely the offering of the mind to Me, uninterrupted by dissimilar mental states; that <s>abhyāsa</s> itself is the <s>yoga</s>; the mind of the <s>yogin</s> engaged in that, occupied with that alone, is the instrument. "With a mind not wandering elsewhere" — one whose nature is not to go to any other object is <s>nānya-gāmin</s> (not wandering elsewhere); with such a mind one goes to, reaches the supreme, unsurpassed <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), the divine one who dwells in the orb of the sun — O <s>Pārtha</s>, constantly meditating, meaning reflecting in accordance with the teaching of scripture and teacher. ||BhGS 8.8||

children.text: kiṃ-viśiṣṭaṃ ca puraṣaṃ yāti ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: And what kind of <s>Puruṣa</s> does one attain? This is stated:

children.text: kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram
children.translated_text: The omniscient one, the ancient, the ruler,

children.text: aṇor aṇīyāṃsam anusmared yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Subtler than the subtle — whoever meditates on Him,

children.text: sarvasya dhātāram acintya-rūpam
children.translated_text: The sustainer of all, of inconceivable form,

children.text: āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ||BhG_8.9||
children.translated_text: Luminous like the sun, beyond darkness — ||BhG 8.9||

children.text: kaviṃ krānta-darśinaṃ sarva-jñaṃ purāṇaṃ cirantanam anuśāsitāraṃ sarvasya jagataḥ praśāsitāram aṇoḥ sūkṣmād apy aṇīyāṃsaṃ sūkṣmataram anusmared anucintayed yaḥ kaścit, sarvasya karma-phala-jātasya dhātāraṃ vidhātāraṃ vicitratayā prāṇibhyo vibhaktāram, acintya-rūpaṃ nāsya rūpaṃ niyataṃ vidyamānam api kenacit cintayituṃ śakyata ity acintya-rūpas tam, āditya-varṇam ādityasyeva nitya-caitanya-prakāśo varṇo yasya tam āditya-varṇam, tamasaḥ parastāt, ajñāna-lakṣaṇān mohāndhakārāt paraṃ tam anucintayad yātīti pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ ||BhGS_8.9||
children.translated_text: "<s>Kavi</s>" (omniscient) — one of all-pervading vision, omniscient; "<s>purāṇa</s>" (ancient) — existing from time immemorial; "the ruler" (<s>anuśāsitṛ</s>) — the governor of the entire universe; "subtler than the subtle" — more subtle than even the subtle, most minute.
