Whoever meditates on, contemplates Him — the "sustainer of all" (<s>dhātṛ</s>) — the ordainer, the one who distributes in diverse ways the entire collection of the fruits of <s>karma</s> among living beings; "of inconceivable form" — though His form truly exists, it cannot be conceived by anyone, hence He is <s>acintya-rūpa</s>; "luminous like the sun" (<s>āditya-varṇa</s>) — one whose brilliance is the eternal radiance of consciousness like that of the sun; "beyond darkness" — beyond the darkness of ignorance characterized by delusion — one who meditates on Him thus attains Him; this connects with the previous verse. ||BhGS 8.9||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: prayāṇa-kāle manasācalena
children.translated_text: At the time of departure, with an unmoving mind,

children.text: bhaktyā yukto yoga-balena caiva |
children.translated_text: Endowed with devotion and also with the power of yoga,

children.text: bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak
children.translated_text: Having properly placed the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) between the eyebrows,

children.text: sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam ||BhG_8.10||
children.translated_text: He reaches that supreme divine <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person). ||BhG 8.10||

children.text: prayāṇa-kāle maraṇa-kāle manasācalena calana-varjitena bhaktyā yukto bhajanaṃ bhaktis tayā yukto yoga-balena caiva yogasya balaṃ yoga-balaṃ samādhija-saṃskāra-pracaya-janita-citta-sthairya-lakṣaṇaṃ yoga-balaṃ tena ca yukta ity arthaḥ | pūrvaṃ hṛdaya-puṇḍārīke vaśīkṛtya cittaṃ tata ūrdhva-gāminyā nāḍyā bhūmi-jaya-krameṇa bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya sthāpayitvā samyag-āpramattaḥ san, sa evaṃ buddhimān yogī kaviṃ purāṇam ity ādi-lakṣaṇaṃ taṃ paraṃ parataraṃ puruṣam upaiti pratipadyate divyaṃ dyotanātmakam ||BhGS_8.10||
children.translated_text: At the time of departure (<s>prayāṇa-kāla</s>), that is, at the time of death, with an unwavering mind — one free from movement — endowed with <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), that is, endowed with worship (<s>bhajana</s>), and also endowed with the strength of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yoga-bala</s>) — the strength of yoga means the firmness of mind characterized by the accumulation of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); endowed with that is the meaning. Having first brought the mind under control in the lotus of the heart, then through the upward-moving channel (<s>nāḍī</s>), by the progressive mastery of the stages, having placed the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) between the eyebrows and established it there, being fully vigilant and attentive — such a wise <s>yogī</s> attains, that is, reaches that supreme, most exalted <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) characterized by such descriptions as 'the omniscient, the ancient' and so forth — the divine one, whose nature is luminosity. ||BhGS_8.10||

children.text: yoga-mārgānugamanenaiva brahma-vidyām antareṇāpi brahma prāpyata ity evaṃ prāptam idam ucyate
children.translated_text: The objection that <s>Brahman</s> can be attained merely by following the path of <s>yoga</s>, even without the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-vidyā</s>), having thus arisen, this is stated:

children.text: punar api vakṣyamāṇenopāyena pratipitsitasya brahmaṇo veda-vidvad-anādi-viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣyasyābhidhānaṃ karoti bhagavān -
children.translated_text: Again, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) gives the designation of <s>Brahman</s> — which is to be attained by the means to be described, and which is qualified by the attributes beginning with 'known by the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>' —

children.text: yad akṣaraṃ veda-vido vadanti
children.translated_text: That which the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> call the Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>),

children.text: viśanti yad yatayo vīta-rāgāḥ |
children.translated_text: which the ascetics (<s>yatayaḥ</s>), free from passion, enter,

children.text: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti
children.translated_text: desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) —

children.text: tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye ||BhG_8.11||
children.translated_text: that goal (<s>pada</s>) I shall declare to you in brief. ||BhG_8.11||

children.text: yad akṣaraṃ na kṣaratīty akṣaram avināśi vedavido vedārthajñāḥ vadanti | tad vā etad akṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadanti [BAU 3.8.8] iti śruteḥ | sarva-viśeṣa-nivartakatvenābhivadanty asthūlam aṇv ity ādi | kiṃ ca - viśanti praviśanti samyag-darśana-prāptau satyāṃ yad yatayo yatana-śīlāḥ saṃnyāsino vīta-rāgāḥ vīto vigataḥ rāgo yebhyas te vīta-rāgāḥ | yac cākṣaram icchanto jñātum iti vākya-śeṣaḥ brahmacaryaṃ gurau caranti ācaranti, tat te padaṃ tad akṣarākhyaṃ padaṃ padanīyaṃ te tava saṃgraheṇa, saṃgrahaḥ saṃkṣepas tena, saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣye kathayiṣyāmi ||BhGS_8.11||
children.translated_text: That which is <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable) — it is called <s>akṣara</s> because it does not perish (<s>na kṣarati</s>), meaning it is indestructible — the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s>, those who know the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>, speak of it. This is based on the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): 'This imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> declare' [BAU 3.8.8]. They describe it by negating all particular attributes — 'not gross, not subtle' and so on. Moreover — those <s>yatayaḥ</s> (ascetics), those given to exertion, the <s>saṃnyāsins</s> (renunciants), who are free from passion (<s>vīta-rāga</s>) — those from whom passion has departed — enter, that is, fully enter it when right vision is attained. And desiring to know this <s>akṣara</s> — this is the completion of the sentence — they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) under a teacher. That goal (<s>pada</s>), the goal called <s>akṣara</s>, that which is to be attained, to you — in brief (<s>saṃgraheṇa</s>), meaning in summary — I shall declare, that is, I shall tell. ||BhGS_8.11||

children.text: sa yo ha vai tad bhagavan manuṣyeṣu prāyaṇāntam oṃkāram abhidhyāyīta | katamaṃ vāva sa tena lokaṃ jayatīti | tasmai sa hovāca - etad vai satya-kāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yad oṃkāraḥ [PraśnaU 5.1-2] ity upakramya, yaḥ punar etaṃ trimātreṇa om ity etenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣam abhidhyāyīta sa sāmabhir unnīyate brahma-lokam [PraśnaU 5.5] ity ādinā vacanena, anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād [KaṭhU 1.2.14] iti copakramya
children.translated_text: 'He indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who among men meditates on <s>Oṃkāra</s> until the time of departure — which world does he win by that?' To him he said: 'This indeed, O <s>Satyakāma</s>, is the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>, namely <s>Oṃkāra</s>' [PraśnaU 5.1-2] — beginning thus, and then 'He who meditates on the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> with this very syllable <s>Om</s> consisting of three <s>mātrās</s> (measures), he is led up by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns to <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahmā</s>)' [PraśnaU 5.5] — through such statements; and beginning with 'Beyond <s>dharma</s> (merit) and beyond <s>adharma</s> (demerit)' [KaṭhU 1.2.14] —

children.text:
sarve vedā yat padam āmananti
tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti |
yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti
tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmy om ity etad [KaṭhU 1.2.15]
children.translated_text:
'All the <s>Vedas</s> declare that goal,
all austerities (<s>tapas</s>) speak of it,
desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> —
that goal I tell you in brief: it is <s>Om</s>' [KaṭhU 1.2.15]

children.text: ity ādibhiś ca vacanaiḥ parasya brahmaṇo vācaka-rūpeṇa, pratimāvat pratīka-rūpeṇa vā, para-brahma-pratipatti-sādhanatvena manda-madhyama-buddhīnāṃ vivakṣitasya oṃkārasyopāsanaṃ kālāntare mukti-phalam uktaṃ yat, tad evehāpi kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram [Gītā 8.9] yad akṣaraṃ veda-vido vadanti [Gītā 8.11] iti copanyastasya parasya brahmaṇaḥ pūrvokta-rūpeṇa pratipatty-upāya-bhūtasya oṃkārasya kālāntara-mukti-phalam upāsanaṃ yogadhāraṇā-sahitaṃ vaktavyam | prasaktānuprasaktaṃ ca yat kiṃcid ity evam artha uttare grantha ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: — through these and other statements, the meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, which serves as a means for attaining the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — either in the form of a verbal symbol (<s>vācaka</s>) of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, or in the form of a representative image (<s>pratīka</s>), like a statue — has been declared to yield liberation in due course (<s>kālāntare</s>) for those of dull and middling intellect. That very same thing is to be stated here as well: the meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, which is the means of attaining the supreme <s>Brahman</s> described as 'the omniscient, the ancient, the ruler' [Gītā 8.9] and 'that which the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> call imperishable' [Gītā 8.11], combined with <s>yoga-dhāraṇā</s> (yogic concentration), yielding liberation in due course. And whatever is connected and incidentally relevant — with this purpose the following passage begins:

children.text: sarva-dvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
children.translated_text: Restraining all the gates (<s>dvāras</s>), and confining the mind in the heart,

children.text: mūrdhny ādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yoga-dhāraṇām ||BhG_8.12||
children.translated_text: placing one's own <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) in the head, established in <s>yoga-dhāraṇā</s> (yogic concentration) — ||BhG_8.12||

children.text: sarva-dvārāṇi sarvāṇi ca tāni dvārāṇi ca sarva-dvārāṇy upalabdhau, tāni sarvāṇi saṃyasya saṃyamanaṃ kṛtvā mano hṛdi hṛdaya-puṇḍārīke nirūdhya nirodhaṃ kṛtvā niṣpracāram āpādya, tatra vaśīkṛtena manasā hṛdayād ūrdhva-gāminyā nāḍyordhvam ārūhya mūrdhny ādhāya ātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthitaḥ pṛvṛtto yoga-dhāraṇāṃ dhārayitum ||BhGS_8.12||
children.translated_text: All the gates (<s>sarva-dvārāṇi</s>) — all of them are gates, that is, the gates of perception — restraining all of them, having performed restraint; confining the mind in the heart, in the lotus of the heart (<s>hṛdaya-puṇḍarīka</s>), having performed confinement, having rendered it motionless; then with the mind thus brought under control in the heart, ascending upward through the upward-moving channel (<s>nāḍī</s>), placing one's own <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) in the head — having established oneself in, that is, having commenced, <s>yoga-dhāraṇā</s> (yogic concentration), the practice of holding. ||BhGS_8.12||

children.text: tatraiva ca dhārayan -
children.translated_text: And while maintaining concentration there —

children.text: om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran |
children.translated_text: Uttering <s>Om</s>, the single-syllable <s>Brahman</s>, remembering Me —

children.text: yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||BhG_8.13||
children.translated_text: he who departs, abandoning the body, he goes to the supreme goal (<s>paramā gati</s>). ||BhG_8.13||

children.text: om iti ekākṣaraṃ brahma brahmaṇo 'bhidhāna-bhūtam oṃkāraṃ vyāharan ucārayan, tad-artha-bhūtaṃ mām īśvaram anusmaran anucintayan yaḥ prayāti mriyate, sa tyajan parityajan dehaṃ śarīram - tyajan deham iti prayāṇa-viśeṣaṇārtham deha-tyāgena prayāṇam ātmanaḥ, na svarūpa-nāśenety arthaḥ - sa evaṃ yāti gacchati paramāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatim ||BhGS_8.13||
children.translated_text: <s>Om</s> — the single-syllable <s>Brahman</s>, that is, <s>Oṃkāra</s> which serves as the designation of <s>Brahman</s> — uttering, that is, pronouncing it; remembering Me, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), who am the referent of that syllable, that is, contemplating Me; he who departs, that is, dies — he, abandoning, that is, relinquishing the body, the physical form. 'Abandoning the body' qualifies the manner of departure — the departure of the self is through relinquishing the body, not through destruction of its own nature; this is the meaning. He thus goes, that is, reaches the supreme (<s>paramā</s>), the most excellent goal (<s>gati</s>). ||BhGS_8.13||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ananya-cetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose mind is on nothing else, who remembers Me constantly, at all times —

children.text: tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ ||BhG_8.14||
children.translated_text: for that ever-disciplined <s>yogī</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, I am easy to attain. ||BhG_8.14||

children.text: ananya-cetā nānya-viṣaye ceto yasya so 'yam ananya-cetāḥ | yogī satataṃ sarvadā yo māṃ parameśvaraṃ smarati | nityaśaḥ satatam iti nairantaryam ucyate, nityaśaḥ iti dīrgha-kālatvam ucyate | na ṣaṇ-māsaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ vā | kiṃ tarhi ? yāvaj-jīvaṃ nairantaryeṇa yo māṃ smaratīty arthaḥ | tasya yogino 'haṃ sulabhaḥ sukhena labhyo he pārtha, nitya-yuktasya sadā samāhita-cittasya yoginaḥ | yata evam, ato 'nanya-cetāḥ san mayi sadā samāhito bhavet ||BhGS_8.14||
children.translated_text: <s>Ananya-cetāḥ</s> (one whose mind is not on anything else) — he whose mind (<s>cetas</s>) is not directed to any other object, he is <s>ananya-cetāḥ</s>. The <s>yogī</s> who constantly (<s>satatam</s>), that is, always, remembers Me, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). 'Constantly' (<s>satatam</s>) denotes uninterruptedness; 'at all times' (<s>nityaśaḥ</s>) denotes long duration — not for six months or a year. But what then? For the entire span of life, without interruption, he who remembers Me — this is the meaning. For that <s>yogī</s>, I am easy to attain (<s>sulabha</s>), easily obtained, O <s>Pārtha</s>, for the ever-disciplined one (<s>nitya-yukta</s>), the one whose mind is always concentrated. Since this is so, therefore one should be of undivided mind and always absorbed in Me. ||BhGS_8.14||

children.text: tava saulabhyena kiṃ syāt ? ity ucyate | sṛṇu tan mama saulabhyena yad bhavati -
children.translated_text: What results from Your being easy to attain? This is stated. Listen to what comes from My being easy to attain —

children.text: mām upetya punar-janma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam |
children.translated_text: Having attained Me, the great souls (<s>mahātmānaḥ</s>) do not undergo rebirth,

children.text: nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ ||BhG_8.15||
children.translated_text: which is the abode of suffering and impermanent;

children.text: mām upetya mām īśvaram upetya mad-bhāvam āpadya punar janma punar utpattiṃ nāpnuvanti na prāpnuvanti | kiṃ-viśiṣṭaṃ punar-janma na prāpnuvanti ? iti, tad-viśeṣaṇam āha - duḥkhālayaṃ duḥkhānām ādhyātmikādīnām ālayaṃ āśrayam | ālīyante yasmin duḥkhānīti duḥkhālayaṃ janma | na kevalaṃ duḥkhālayam, aśāśvatam anavasthita-svarūpaṃ ca | nāpnuvanti īdṛśaṃ punar-janma mahātmāno yatayaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ mokṣākhyāṃ paramāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatāḥ prāptāḥ | ye punar māṃ na prāpnuvanti te punar āvartante ||BhGS_8.15||
children.translated_text:
they have reached the highest perfection (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>). ||BhG_8.15||
Having attained Me (<s>mām upetya</s>), having reached Me the Lord, having attained My nature — they do not undergo rebirth, they do not obtain another birth. What kind of rebirth do they not obtain? — to this, the qualifying description is given: an abode of suffering (<s>duḥkhālaya</s>) — the resting place of sufferings such as those pertaining to the self (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and others; that in which sufferings come to rest is the abode of suffering, namely birth. Not only an abode of suffering, but also impermanent (<s>aśāśvata</s>), of unstable nature. Such rebirth the great souls (<s>mahātmānaḥ</s>), the ascetics, who have reached, that is, attained the highest, the most excellent perfection called liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), do not obtain. But those who do not attain Me return again. ||BhGS_8.15||

children.text: kiṃ punas tvatto 'nyat prāptāḥ punar āvartante ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: Do those who have attained something other than You return again? This is stated —

children.text: ā brahma-bhuvanāl lokāḥ punar-āvartino 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: All worlds up to the realm of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Brahmaloka</s>) are subject to return, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: mām upetya tu kaunteya punar-janma na vidyate ||BhG_8.16||
children.translated_text: but having attained Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, there is no rebirth. ||BhG_8.16||

children.text: ā brahma-bhuvanāt bhavanty asmin bhūtānīti bhuvanam | brahmaṇo bhuvanaṃ brahma-bhuvanam, brahma-loka ity arthaḥ | ā brahma-bhuvanāt saha brahma-bhuvanena lokāḥ sarve punar-āvartinaḥ punar-āvartana-svabhāvāḥ | he 'rjuna | mām ekam upetya tu kaunteya punar-janma punar-utpattiḥ na vidyate ||BhGS_8.16||
children.translated_text: Up to the realm of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>brahma-bhuvana</s>) — <s>bhuvana</s> means that in which beings exist; the <s>bhuvana</s> of <s>Brahmā</s> is <s>brahma-bhuvana</s>, meaning <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahmā</s>). Up to and including <s>brahma-bhuvana</s>, all worlds are subject to return (<s>punar-āvartin</s>), having the nature of return. O <s>Arjuna</s>! But having attained Me alone, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, there is no rebirth, no further birth. ||BhGS_8.16||

children.text: brahma-loka-sahitā lokāḥ kasmāt punar-āvartinaḥ ? kāla-paricchinnatvāt | katham ? -
children.translated_text: Why are the worlds including <s>Brahmaloka</s> subject to return? Because they are delimited by time. How so? —

children.text: sahasra-yuga-paryantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ |
children.translated_text: They know the day of <s>Brahmā</s> which ends after a thousand <s>yugas</s> (ages),

children.text: rātriṃ yuga-sahasrāntāṃ te 'ho-rātra-vido janāḥ ||BhG_8.17||
children.translated_text: and the night which ends after a thousand <s>yugas</s> — they are the knowers of day and night. ||BhG_8.17||

children.text: sahasra-yuga-paryantaṃ sahasrāṇi yugāni paryantaḥ paryavasānaṃ yasyāhnas tat ahaḥ sahasra-yuga-paryantam | brahmaṇaḥ prajāpater virājo viduḥ | rātrim api yuga-sahasrāntām ahaḥ-parimāṇām eva | ke vidur ity āha - te 'ho-rātra-vidaḥ kāla-saṃkhyā-vido janā ity arthaḥ | yata evaṃ kāla-paricchinnās te, ataḥ punar-āvartino lokāḥ ||BhGS_8.17||
children.translated_text: Ending after a thousand <s>yugas</s> (<s>sahasra-yuga-paryanta</s>) — a thousand <s>yugas</s> constitute the limit, the conclusion of that day; that day ends after a thousand <s>yugas</s>. This is the day of <s>Brahmā</s>, of <s>Prajāpati</s>, of <s>Virāj</s>, they know. The night also extends for a thousand <s>yugas</s>, equal in measure to the day. Who knows this? — he says: they, the knowers of day and night (<s>aho-rātra-vid</s>), meaning those who know the reckoning of time. Since these worlds are thus delimited by time, therefore the worlds are subject to return. ||BhGS_8.17||

children.text: prajāpater ahani yad bhavati rātrau ca, tad ucyate -
children.translated_text: What happens during the day and the night of <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of creatures) is stated —

children.text: avyaktād vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavanty ahar-āgame |
children.translated_text: From the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), all manifest beings come forth at the arrival of day;

children.text: rātry-āgame pralīyante tatraivāvyakta-saṃjñake ||BhG_8.18||
children.translated_text: at the arrival of night, they dissolve into that very same, called the unmanifest. ||BhG_8.18||

children.text: avyaktād avyaktaṃ prajāpateḥ svāpāvasthā | tasmād avyaktād vyaktayo vyajyanta iti vyaktayaḥ sthāvara-jaṅgama-lakṣaṇāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ prabhavanty abhivyajyante, ahna āgamo 'har-āgamas tasmin ahar-āgame kāle brahmaṇaḥ prabodha-kāle | tathā rātry-āgame brahmaṇaḥ svāpa-kāle pralīyante sarvā vyaktayas tatraiva pūrvokte 'vyakta-saṃjñake ||BhGS_8.18||
children.translated_text: From the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) — the unmanifest is the state of sleep of <s>Prajāpati</s>. From that unmanifest, the manifest beings (<s>vyaktayaḥ</s>) — they are called manifest because they become manifested — characterized as stationary and moving beings, all creatures come forth, become manifest, at the arrival of day (<s>ahar-āgama</s>), at the time of <s>Brahmā</s>'s awakening. Likewise, at the arrival of night, at the time of <s>Brahmā</s>'s sleep, all manifest beings dissolve into that very same aforementioned one called the unmanifest. ||BhGS_8.18||

children.text: akṛtābhyāgama-kṛta-vipraṇāśa-doṣa-parihārārthaṃ bandha-mokṣa-śāstra-pravṛtti-sāphalya-pradarśanārtham avidyādi-kleśa-mūla-karmāśaya-vaśāc cāvaśo bhūta-grāmo bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyata ity ataḥ saṃsāre vairāgya-pradarśanārthaṃ cedam āha -
children.translated_text: In order to avert the defect of obtaining what has not been earned and losing what has been earned, to demonstrate the fruitfulness of the scripture dealing with bondage and liberation, and to show dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — because the multitude of beings, impelled helplessly by the store of <s>karma</s> rooted in the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and others, coming into being again and again, dissolves — this is stated:

children.text: bhūta-grāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate |
children.translated_text: This very same multitude of beings (<s>bhūta-grāma</s>), coming into being again and again, dissolves helplessly

children.text: rātry-āgame 'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavaty ahar-āgame ||BhG_8.19||
children.translated_text: at the arrival of night, O <s>Pārtha</s>; and comes forth again at the arrival of day. ||BhG_8.19||

children.text: bhūta-grāmo bhūta-samudāyaḥ sthāvara-jaṅgama-lakṣaṇo yaḥ pūrvasmin kalpa āsīt sa evāyaṃ nānyaḥ | bhūtvā bhūtvāhar-āgame | pralīyate punaḥ punaḥ rātry-āgame 'hnaḥ kṣaye 'vaśo 'svatantra eva | he pārtha | prabhavati jāyate 'vaśa evāhar-āgame ||BhGS_8.19||
children.translated_text: The multitude of beings (<s>bhūta-grāma</s>), the aggregate of beings characterized as stationary and moving, which existed in the previous cycle of creation (<s>kalpa</s>) — this very same one, not another. Coming into being again and again at the arrival of day, it dissolves again and again at the arrival of night, at the end of the day — helplessly, not of its own accord. O <s>Pārtha</s>! It comes forth, is born — helplessly indeed — at the arrival of day. ||BhGS_8.19||

children.text: yad upanyastam akṣaram, tasya prāpty-upāyo nirdiṣṭa om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma [Gītā 8.13] ity ādinā | athedānīm akṣarasyaiva svarūpa-nirdidikṣayedam ucyate, anena yoga-mārgeṇedaṃ gantavyam iti -
children.translated_text: The <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable) that was introduced — for which the means of attainment was specified as '<s>Om</s>, the single-syllable <s>Brahman</s>' [Gītā 8.13] and so forth — now, with the desire to indicate the true nature of this very <s>akṣara</s>, and that this is the destination to be reached by this path of <s>yoga</s>, this is stated:

children.text: paras tasmāt tu bhāvo 'nyo 'vyakto 'vyaktāt sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: But there is another state (<s>bhāva</s>), higher than that unmanifest, itself unmanifest and eternal (<s>sanātana</s>),

children.text: yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati ||BhG_8.20||
children.translated_text: which, when all beings perish, does not perish. ||BhG_8.20||

children.text: paro vyatirikto bhinnaḥ | kutaḥ ? tasmāt pūrvoktāt | tu-śabdo 'kṣarasya vivakṣitasyāvyaktād vailakṣaṇya-viśeṣaṇārthaḥ | bhāvo 'kṣarākhyaṃ paraṃ brahma | vyatiriktatve saty api sālakṣaṇya-prasaṅgo 'stīti tad-vinivṛtty-artham āha - anya iti | anyo vilakṣaṇaḥ | sa cāvyakto 'nindriya-gocaraḥ | paras tasmād ity uktam | kasmāt punaḥ paraḥ ? pūrvoktād bhūta-grāma-bīja-bhūtād avidyā-lakṣaṇād avyaktāt | anyo vilakṣaṇo bhāva ity abhiprāyaḥ | sanātanaś cirantano yaḥ sa bhāvaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu brahmādiṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati ||BhGS_8.20||
children.translated_text: Higher (<s>para</s>) means distinct, different. From what? From the aforementioned one. The word 'but' (<s>tu</s>) serves to distinguish the intended <s>akṣara</s> from the unmanifest. The state (<s>bhāva</s>) is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> called <s>akṣara</s> (imperishable). Even though it is distinct, there might be a presumption of similarity, so to negate that he says 'other' (<s>anya</s>) — meaning dissimilar. And it is unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), not accessible to the senses. 'Higher than that' has already been stated. Higher than what again? Than the aforementioned unmanifest characterized by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is the seed of the multitude of beings. The meaning is: a state that is dissimilar. And this eternal (<s>sanātana</s>), ancient state — when all beings, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, perish, it does not perish. ||BhGS_8.20||

children.text: avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim |
children.translated_text: That which is called the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), they call that the supreme goal;

children.text: yaṃ prāpya na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama ||BhG_8.21||
children.translated_text: Having attained which they do not return — that is My supreme abode. ||BhG 8.21||

children.text: yo 'sāv avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam evākṣara-saṃjñakam avyaktaṃ bhāvam āhuḥ paramāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatim | yaṃ paraṃ bhāvaṃ prāpya gatvā na nivartante saṃsārāya, tad dhāma sthānaṃ paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ mama, viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_8.21||
children.translated_text: That which has been described as the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) — that very entity designated as <s>akṣara</s>, the unmanifest state, they call the supreme, the most excellent goal. Having attained, having reached that supreme state, they do not return to <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) — that is the abode, the supreme, the most excellent place, which is Mine; the meaning is: the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. ||BhGS 8.21||

children.text: tal-labdher upāya ucyate -
children.translated_text: The means for attaining that is now stated —

children.text: puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyas tv ananyayā |
children.translated_text: That supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is attainable through single-pointed devotion (<s>bhakti</s>);

children.text: yasyāntaḥ-sthāni bhūtāni yena sarvam idaṃ tatam ||BhG_8.22||
children.translated_text: Within whom all beings abide, and by whom all this is pervaded. ||BhG 8.22||

children.text: puruṣaḥ puri śayanāt pūrṇatvād vā | sa paraḥ pārtha, paro niratiśayaḥ, yasmāt puruṣān na paraṃ kiṃcit | sa bhaktyā labhyas tu jñāna-lakṣaṇayānanyayā ātma-viṣayayā | yasya puruṣasyāntaḥ-sthāni madhya-sthāni bhūtāni kārya-bhūtāni | kāryaṃ hi kāraṇasyāntarvarti bhavati | yena puruṣeṇa sarvaṃ idaṃ jagat tataṃ vyāptam ākāśeneva ghaṭādi ||BhGS_8.22||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> — so called because He rests in the city (of the body), or because of His fullness. He is supreme, O <s>Pārtha</s> — supreme means unsurpassed, since there is nothing higher than this <s>Puruṣa</s>. He is attainable through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), but only through exclusive devotion characterized by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), directed toward the Self. Within this <s>Puruṣa</s> all beings — which are effects — abide in the middle. For the effect always exists within the cause. By this <s>Puruṣa</s>, all this universe is pervaded, as a pot and the like are pervaded by space. ||BhGS 8.22||

children.text: prakṛtānāṃ yogināṃ praṇavāveśita-brahma-buddhīnāṃ kālāntara-mukti-bhājāṃ brahma-pratipattaya uttaro mārgo vaktavya iti yatra kāle ity ādi vivakṣitārtha-samarpaṇārtham ucyate, āvṛtti-mārgopanyāsaḥ itara-mārga-stuty-artham ucyate -
children.translated_text: For those <s>yogins</s> who have been initiated, whose intellects are established in <s>Brahman</s> through the practice of <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), and who attain liberation at a later time — the northern path (<s>uttara-mārga</s>) leading to the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> is to be stated. Thus, beginning with 'at what time' is spoken for the purpose of conveying the intended meaning, while the presentation of the path of return is stated for the purpose of praising the other path —

children.text: yatra kāle tv anāvṛttim āvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ |
children.translated_text: At what time departing, <s>yogins</s> go to non-return or to return;

children.text: prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha ||BhG_8.23||
children.translated_text: That time I shall declare to you, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>. ||BhG 8.23||

children.text: yatra kāle prayātā iti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ | yatra yasmin kāle tv anāvṛttim apunar-janma āvṛttiṃ tad-viparītāṃ caiva | yogina iti yoginaḥ karmiṇaś cocyante | karmiṇas tu guṇataḥ karma-yogena yoginām iti viśeṣaṇād yoginaḥ | yatra kāle prayātā mṛtā yogino 'nāvṛttiṃ yānti, yatra kāle ca prayātāḥ āvṛttiṃ yānti, taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: 'At what time departing' — the connection is with an intervening word. At what time, indeed, to non-return, meaning no rebirth, and to return, which is the opposite of that. The term '<s>yogins</s>' refers to both <s>yogins</s> and performers of rituals (<s>karmin</s>). The ritualists are called <s>yogins</s> by virtue of their qualification through <s>karma-yoga</s>, as indicated by the qualifier 'of the <s>yogins</s>.' At what time, having departed, having died, the <s>yogins</s> go to non-return; and at what time, having departed, they go to return — that time I shall declare, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>.

children.text: taṃ kālam āha -
children.translated_text: That time is now stated —

children.text: agnir jyotir ahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam |
children.translated_text: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern solstice (<s>uttarāyaṇa</s>);

children.text: tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahma-vido janāḥ ||BhG_8.24||
children.translated_text: Departing by that path, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> go to <s>Brahman</s>. ||BhG 8.24||

children.text: agniḥ kālābhimāninī devatā | tathā jyotir api devataiva kālābhimāninī | athavā, agni-jyotiṣī yathā śrute eva devate | bhūyasā tu nirdeśo yatra kāle taṃ kālam iti āmra-vanavat | tathāhar devatāhar-abhimāninī | śuklaḥ śukla-pakṣa-devatā | ṣaṇ-māsā uttarāyaṇam, tatrāpi devataiva mārga-bhūtā [BAU 4.3.4] iti sthito 'nyatrāyaṃ nyāyaḥ | tatra tasmin mārge prayātā mṛtā gacchanti brahma brahma-vido brahmopāsakā brahmopāsana-parā janāḥ | krameṇeti vākya-śeṣaḥ | na hi sadyo-mukti-bhājāṃ samyag darśana-niṣṭhānāṃ gatir āgatir vā kvacid asti | na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti [BAU 4.4.6] iti śruteḥ | brahmasaṃlīnaprāṇaiva te brahmamayā brahma-bhūtaiva te |
children.translated_text: Fire — the deity presiding over that period of time. Similarly, light (<s>jyotis</s>) is also a deity presiding over time. Alternatively, fire and light are deities just as mentioned in the <s>Śruti</s>. The description is predominantly temporal, as in 'at what time, that time,' like a mango grove (where the predominant element names the whole). Similarly, 'day' refers to the deity presiding over the day. 'Bright' (<s>śukla</s>) refers to the deity of the bright fortnight. 'The six months of the northern solstice' — there too the deity alone constitutes the path [BAU 4.3.4]; this principle is established elsewhere. On that path, having departed, having died, they go to <s>Brahman</s> — the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, those devoted to the worship of <s>Brahman</s>, the people dedicated to meditation on <s>Brahman</s>. 'Gradually' is the completion of the sentence. For those who attain immediate liberation (<s>sadyo-mukti</s>), who are established in right knowledge (<s>samyag-darśana</s>), there is neither going nor coming anywhere. As the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'His vital breaths do not depart' [BAU 4.4.6]. Their vital breaths are already merged in <s>Brahman</s>; they are already filled with <s>Brahman</s>, already become <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: dhūmo rātris tathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇ-māsā dakṣiṇāyanam |
children.translated_text: Smoke, night, likewise the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern solstice (<s>dakṣiṇāyana</s>);

children.text: tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotir yogī prāpya nivartate ||BhG_8.25||
children.translated_text: Attaining the lunar light there, the <s>yogī</s> returns. ||BhG 8.25||

children.text: dhūmo rātrir dhūmābhimāninī rātry-abhimāninī ca devatā | tathā kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇa-pakṣa-devatā | ṣaṇ-māsā dakṣiṇāyanam iti ca pūrvavat devataiva | tatra candramasi bhavaṃ cāndramasaṃ jyotiḥ phalam iṣṭādi-kārī yogī karmī prāpya bhuktvā tat-kṣayād iha punar nivartate ||BhGS_8.25||
children.translated_text: Smoke and night — the deity presiding over smoke and the deity presiding over night. Similarly, 'dark' (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>) refers to the deity of the dark fortnight. 'The six months of the southern solstice' — here too, as before, it is the deity alone. There, the lunar light (<s>cāndramasa jyotis</s>) is the result; the <s>yogī</s>, meaning the performer of rituals (<s>karmin</s>) who has performed sacrifices (<s>iṣṭa</s>) and similar rites, having attained and enjoyed it, returns here again when its merit is exhausted. ||BhGS 8.25||

children.text: śukla-kṛṣṇe gatī hy ete jagataḥ śāśvate mate |
children.translated_text: These bright and dark paths of the world are considered eternal;

children.text: ekayā yāty anāvṛttim anyayāvartate punaḥ ||BhG_8.26||
children.translated_text: By one, one goes to non-return; by the other, one returns again. ||BhG 8.26||

children.text: śukla-kṛṣṇe śuklā ca kṛṣṇā ca śukla-kṛṣṇe, jñāna-prakāśakatvāt śuklā, tadabhāvāt kṛṣṇā | ete śukla-kṛṣṇe hi gatī jagataḥ ity adhikṛtānāṃ jñāna-karmaṇoḥ, na jagataḥ sarvasyaiva ete gatī saṃbhavataḥ | śāśvate nitye, saṃsārasya nityatvāt, mate 'bhiprete | tatraikayā śuklayā yāty anāvṛttim, anyayā itarayā āvartate punar bhūyaḥ ||BhGS_8.26||
children.translated_text: Bright and dark — the bright (<s>śuklā</s>) and the dark (<s>kṛṣṇā</s>), called bright because it illuminates knowledge, and dark because of the absence thereof. These two, the bright and dark, are indeed the paths — of the world, meaning of those qualified for knowledge and action respectively, not that these two paths are possible for everyone in the world. They are eternal, permanent, because <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) is eternal; they are considered, that is, accepted as such. Of these, by one, the bright, one goes to non-return; by the other, the opposite one, one returns again. ||BhGS 8.26||

children.text: naite sṛtī pārtha jānan yogī muhyati kaścana |
children.translated_text: Knowing these two paths, O <s>Pārtha</s>, no <s>yogī</s> is ever deluded;

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yukto bhavārjuna ||BhG_8.27||
children.translated_text: Therefore, at all times, be steadfast in <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||BhG 8.27||

children.text: na ete yathokte sṛtī mārgau pārtha jānan saṃsārāya ekā, anyā mokṣāyeti | yogī na muhyati kaścana kaścid api | tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu yoga-yuktaḥ samāhito bhavārjuna ||BhGS_8.27||
children.translated_text: Knowing these two paths as described, O <s>Pārtha</s> — that one leads to <s>saṃsāra</s> and the other to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — no <s>yogī</s>, none whatsoever, is deluded. Therefore, at all times, be concentrated, be steadfast in <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||BhGS 8.27||

children.text: śṛṇu tasya yogasya māhātmyam -
children.translated_text: Hear now the greatness of that <s>yoga</s> —

children.text: vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva
children.translated_text: Whatever meritorious fruit is declared

children.text: dāneṣu yat puṇya-phalaṃ pradiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vedas</s>, in sacrifices, in austerities,

children.text: atyeti tat sarvam idaṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: And in gifts — all that the <s>yogī</s> transcends,

children.text: yogī paraṃ sthānam upaiti cādyam ||BhG_8.28||
children.translated_text: Having known this, and attains the supreme, primordial abode. ||BhG 8.28||

children.text: vedeṣu samyag-adhīteṣu yajñeṣu ca sādguṇyenānutiṣṭhiteṣu tapaḥsu ca sutapteṣu dāneṣu ca samyag-datteṣu yad eteṣu puṇya-phalaṃ puṇyasya phalaṃ puṇya-phalaṃ pradiṣṭaṃ śāstreṇa, atyety atītya gacchati sat sarvaṃ phala-jātam | idaṃ viditvā sapta-praśna-nirṇaya-dvāreṇoktam arthaṃ samyag avadhāryānuṣṭhāya yogī paraṃ prakṛṣṭam aiśvaraṃ sthānam upaiti ca pratipadyate | ādyam ādau bhavaṃ kāraṇaṃ brahmety arthaḥ ||BhGS_8.28||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vedas</s> when properly studied, in sacrifices when properly performed with excellence, in austerities when well practiced, and in gifts when properly given — whatever meritorious fruit, that is, the fruit of merit, is declared by the scriptures — the <s>yogī</s> transcends, goes beyond all that aggregate of fruits. Having known this — having properly ascertained and practiced the meaning stated through the determination of the seven questions — the <s>yogī</s> attains the supreme, the most excellent, the divine abode; and that which is primordial, existing at the beginning, the cause — the meaning is <s>Brahman</s>. ||BhGS 8.28||

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
brahmākṣara-nirdeśo nāma aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
||8||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter called 'The Designation of <s>Brahman</s> as the Imperishable' (<s>Brahmākṣara-nirdeśa</s>) in the blessed <s>Śrīmad Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya</s>, composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the foremost among wandering monks of the highest order. ||8||

children.text: BhG 9
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s>, Chapter 9

children.text:
atha rāja-vidyā-rāja-guhya-yogo nāma
navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the ninth chapter called 'The Yoga of Royal Knowledge and Royal Secret' (<s>Rāja-vidyā-rāja-guhya-yoga</s>).

children.text: (śāṅkara-bhāṣyaḥ)
children.translated_text: (<s>Śāṅkara Bhāṣya</s>)

children.text: aṣṭame nāḍy-ādi-dvāreṇa dhāraṇā-yogaḥ saguṇa uktaḥ | tasya ca phalam agny-arcir-ādi-krameṇa kālāntare brahma-prāpti-lakṣaṇam evānāvṛtti-rūpaṃ nirdiṣṭam | tatrānenaiva prakāreṇa mokṣa-prāpti-phalam adhigamyate, nānyathā iti tad āśaṅkā-vyāvivartayiṣayā śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: In the eighth chapter, <s>dhāraṇā-yoga</s> (meditation on the qualified <s>Brahman</s>) with attributes (<s>saguṇa</s>) was taught through the means of the <s>nāḍīs</s> and so forth. And its fruit was indicated as being in the form of non-return, characterized by the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> at a later time through the gradual path of fire, light, and so on. Lest there be a doubt that liberation can only be attained in this manner and not otherwise, the Blessed Lord said —

children.text: idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave |
children.translated_text: To you who are free from envy, I shall declare this most secret

children.text: jñānaṃ vijñāna-sahitaṃ yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||BhG_9.1||
children.translated_text: Knowledge combined with realization (<s>vijñāna</s>), knowing which you shall be freed from evil. ||BhG 9.1||

children.text: idaṃ brahma-jñānaṃ vakṣyamāṇam uktaṃ ca pūrveṣu adhyāyeṣu, tat buddhau saṃnidhīkṛtya idam ity āha | tu-śabdo viśeṣa-nirdhāraṇārthaḥ | idam eva tu samyag-jñānaṃ sākṣāt mokṣa-prāpti-sādhanam vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti [Gītā 7.12], ātmaivedaṃ sarvam [ChāU 7.25.2] ekam evādvitīyam [ChāU 6.2.1] ity ādi-śruti-smṛtibhyaḥ | nānyat, atha te ye 'nyathāto vidur anya-rājānas te kṣayya-lokā bhavanti [ChāU 7.25.2] ity ādi-śrutibhyaś ca | te tubhyaṃ guhyatamaṃ gopyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmi kathayiṣyāmy anasūyave 'sūyā-rahitāya | kiṃ tat ? jñānam | kiṃ-viśiṣṭam ? vijñāna-sahitam anubhava-yuktam, yaj jñātvā prāpya mokṣyase 'śubhāt saṃsāra-bandhanāt ||BhGS_9.1||
children.translated_text: This — the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> that is about to be stated and that was also stated in the earlier chapters — making that present in the mind, He says 'this.' The word 'tu' (but) is for the purpose of specifying a distinction. This alone is the true knowledge that is the direct means of attaining liberation — from <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> texts such as '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is all' [Gītā 7.19], 'The Self alone is all this' [ChāU 7.25.2], 'One alone without a second' [ChāU 6.2.1], and so forth. Not anything else — as known from <s>Śruti</s> texts such as 'Those who know otherwise, whose rulers are different, they have perishable worlds' [ChāU 7.25.2]. To you, the most secret of secrets, I shall declare, I shall tell, to you who are free from envy. What is it? Knowledge. Of what kind? Combined with <s>vijñāna</s> (realization), endowed with direct experience — knowing which, that is, having attained which, you shall be freed from evil, from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. ||BhGS 9.1||

children.text: tac ca -
children.translated_text: And that is —

children.text: rāja-vidyā rāja-guhyaṃ pavitram idam uttamam |
children.translated_text: This is the king of sciences, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier;

children.text: pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartum avyayam ||BhG_9.2||
children.translated_text: Directly realizable, righteous, easy to practice, and imperishable. ||BhG 9.2||

children.text:
rāja-vidyā vidyānāṃ rājā, dīpty-atiśayavattvāt | dīpyate hīyam atiśayena brahma-vidyā sarva-vidyānām | tathā rāja-guhyaṃ guhyānāṃ rājā | pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ idam uttamaṃ sarveṣāṃ pāvanānāṃ śuddhi-kāraṇaṃ brahma-jñānam utkṛṣṭatamam | aneka-janma-sahasra-saṃcitam api dharmādharmādi sa-mūlaṃ karma kṣaṇa-mātrād eva bhasmīkarotīty ataḥ kiṃ tasya pāvanatvaṃ vaktavyam ? kiṃ ca - pratyakṣāvagamaṃ pratyakṣeṇa sukhāder ivāvagamo yasya tat pratyakṣāvagamam | aneka-guṇavato 'pi dharma-viruddhatvaṃ dṛṣṭam, na tathātma-jñānaṃ dharma-virodhi, kiṃtu dharmyaṃ dharmād anapetam | evam api, syād duḥkha-saṃpādyam ity ata āha - susukhaṃ kartum, yathā ratna-viveka-vijñānam | tatrālpāyāsānām anyeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ sukha-saṃpādyānām alpa-phalatvaṃ
duṣkarāṇāṃ ca mahā-phalatvaṃ dṛṣṭam iti, idaṃ tu sukha-saṃpādyatvāt phala-kṣayāt vyetīti prāpte, āha - avyayam iti | nāsya phalataḥ karmavat vyayo 'stīty avyayam | ataḥ śraddheyam ātma-jñānam ||BhGS_9.2||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāja-vidyā</s> (king of sciences) — the sovereign among all forms of knowledge, because it shines with surpassing brilliance. For this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> shines most excellently among all sciences. Similarly, <s>rāja-guhya</s> (king of secrets) — the sovereign among secrets. This is the purifier, the sanctifier, this supreme, the most excellent among all means of purification — the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is the most exalted. Since it reduces to ashes in a mere instant all <s>karma</s> (action) accumulated over thousands of births, together with its root of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), what need is there to speak of its purifying power? Moreover — it is directly realizable (<s>pratyakṣāvagama</s>), meaning it is apprehended through direct experience, like pleasure and the like. Though possessed of many virtues, things are sometimes seen to be opposed to <s>dharma</s>; but Self-knowledge is not opposed to <s>dharma</s> — rather it is righteous (<s>dharmya</s>), not departing from <s>dharma</s>. Even so, it might be difficult to accomplish — hence He says: easy to practice (<s>susukha</s>), like the science of distinguishing gems. Now, among other practices that are easy and yield small results, and those that are difficult and yield great results — this being easy to accomplish, one might think its fruit would perish. Therefore He says: imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>). Unlike ritual action, its fruit does not diminish — hence it is imperishable. Therefore, Self-knowledge is worthy of faith. ||BhGS 9.2||

children.text: ye punaḥ -
children.translated_text: But those who —

children.text: aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya paraṃtapa |
children.translated_text: Those persons who lack faith in this <s>dharma</s>, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartmani ||BhG_9.3||
children.translated_text: Not attaining Me, they return to the path of death and <s>saṃsāra</s>. ||BhG 9.3||

children.text: aśraddadhānāḥ śraddhā-virahitā ātma-jñānasya dharmasyāsya svarūpe tat-phale ca nāstikāḥ pāpa-kāriṇaḥ, asurāṇām upaniṣadaṃ deha-mātrātma-darśanam eva pratipannāḥ | asutṛpaḥ pāpāḥ puruṣā aśraddadhānāḥ | paraṃtapa ! aprāpya māṃ parameśvaram, mat-prāptau naivāśaṅketi mat-prāpti-mārga-bheda-bhakti-mātram apy aprāpya ity arthaḥ | nivartante niścayena vartante | kva ? - mṛtyu-saṃsāra-vartmani mṛtyu-yuktaḥ saṃsāro mṛtyu-saṃsāras, tasya vartma naraka-tiryag-ādi-prāpti-mārgaḥ, tasminn eva vartanta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_9.3||
children.translated_text: Those who lack faith (<s>aśraddadhāna</s>) — devoid of faith in the nature and fruit of this <s>dharma</s> of Self-knowledge — are atheists, doers of evil, who have adopted the view of the <s>Asuras</s> (demons), namely the doctrine that the Self is nothing but the body. They are wretched sinners, persons devoid of faith. O scorcher of foes (<s>Paraṃtapa</s>)! Not attaining Me, the Supreme Lord — and there being no hope whatsoever of attaining Me, the meaning is: not even attaining any of the various paths of devotion leading to My attainment — they remain fixed, they certainly continue. Where? On the path of death and <s>saṃsāra</s> — <s>saṃsāra</s> conjoined with death is <s>mṛtyu-saṃsāra</s>, and its path is the road leading to hell, animal births, and the like; in that very path they continue — this is the meaning. ||BhGS 9.3||

children.text: stutyārjunam abhimukhīkṛtyāha -
children.translated_text: Having praised [this knowledge] and thereby drawn <s>Arjuna</s>'s attention, He says —

children.text: mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā |
children.translated_text: By Me, in My unmanifest form, all this universe is pervaded;

children.text: mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ ||BhG_9.4||
children.translated_text: All beings abide in Me, but I do not abide in them. ||BhG 9.4||

children.text: mayā mama yaḥ paro bhāvas tena tataṃ vyāptaṃ sarvam idaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā | na vyaktā mūrtiḥ svarūpaṃ yasya mama so 'ham avyakta-mūrtis tena mayāvyakta-mūrtinā, karaṇāgocara-svarūpeṇety arthaḥ | tasmin mayy avyakta-mūrtau sthitāni mat-sthāni, sarva-bhūtāni brahmādīni stamba-paryantāni | na hi nirātmakaṃ kiṃcit bhūtaṃ vyavahārāyāvakalpate | ato mat-sthāni mayātmanā ātmavattvena sthitāni | ato mayi sthitānīty ucyante | teṣāṃ bhūtānām aham evātmā ity atas teṣu sthita iti mūḍha-buddhīnām avabhāsate | ato bravīmi - na cāhaṃ teṣu bhūteṣv avasthitaḥ | mūrtavat saṃśleṣābhāvena ākāśasyāpy antaratamo hy aham | na hy asaṃsargi vastu kvacit ādheya-bhāvenāvasthitaṃ bhavati ||BhGS_9.4||
children.translated_text: By Me — by My supreme nature — all this universe is pervaded, by one whose form is unmanifest (<s>avyakta-mūrti</s>). The form, i.e. the essential nature, is not manifest — such am I, of unmanifest form; by Me of unmanifest form means: whose essential nature is beyond the range of the senses — this is the meaning. In that unmanifest form of Mine, all beings abide (<s>mat-sthāni</s>) — all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass. For no being that is devoid of Self can function in worldly activity. Therefore 'abiding in Me' means: they abide through Me as their Self, by virtue of possessing a Self. Therefore they are said to abide in Me. Since I alone am the Self of those beings, it appears to those of deluded intellect that I am situated in them. Therefore I say — nor am I situated in those beings. Because of the absence of contact as with material objects, I am even more interior than space itself. For a non-associating entity is never situated anywhere as something contained.

children.text: ata evāsaṃsargitvān mama -
children.translated_text: Precisely because of My non-association —

children.text: na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram |
children.translated_text: Nor do beings abide in Me — behold My divine <s>yoga</s> (power)!

children.text: bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ ||BhG_9.5||
children.translated_text: The sustainer of beings yet not dwelling in beings — My Self is the cause of beings.

children.text: na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni brahmādīni | paśya me yogaṃ yuktiṃ ghaṭānaṃ me mama aiśvaram īśvarasyemam aiśvaram, yogam ātmano yāthātmyam ity arthaḥ | tathā ca śrutir asaṃsargitvād asaṅgatāṃ darśayati - asaṅgo na hi sajjate [BAU 3.9.26] iti | idaṃ cāścaryam anyat paśya - bhūta-bhṛd asaṅgo 'pi san bhūtāni bibharti | na ca bhūta-sthaḥ | yathoktena nyāyena darśitatvāt bhūta-sthatvānupapatteḥ | kathaṃ punar ucyate 'sau mamātmeti ? vibhajya dehādi-saṅghātaṃ tasminn ahaṃkāram adhyāropya loka-buddhim anusaran vyapadiśati mamātmeti, na punar ātmana ātmānya iti lokavad ajānan | tathā bhūta-bhāvano bhūtāni bhāvayaty utpādayati vardhayatīti vā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ ||BhGS_9.5||
children.translated_text: Nor do beings — from <s>Brahmā</s> onward — abide in Me. Behold My <s>yoga</s> (power), My capacity, My joining together — this is the lordly power of Me, of the Lord; <s>yoga</s> means the true nature of the Self — this is the meaning. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) demonstrates non-attachment due to non-association: 'He is unattached, for He does not attach Himself' [<s>BAU</s> 3.9.26]. And behold this other wonder: the sustainer of beings, though unattached, sustains beings. Nor does He dwell in beings — because this has been demonstrated by the reasoning stated above, dwelling-in-beings is untenable. But how then is it said 'My Self'? By distinguishing the aggregate of body and so forth, superimposing the ego upon it, and following common understanding, He designates it as 'My Self' — not as though the Self has another self, not as one who is ignorant like the worldly person. Likewise, <s>bhūta-bhāvana</s> (nourisher of beings) means He causes beings to come into existence, produces them, or nourishes them.

children.text: yathoktena śloka-dvayenoktam arthaṃ dṛṣṭantenopapādayann āha -
children.translated_text: Establishing by an illustration the meaning stated in the preceding pair of verses, He says —

children.text: yathākāśa-sthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān |
children.translated_text: Just as the mighty wind, going everywhere, abides eternally in space,

children.text: tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthānīty upadhāraya ||BhG_9.6||
children.translated_text: so know that all beings abide in Me.

children.text: yathā loke ākāśa-sthita ākāśe sthito nityaṃ sadā vāyuḥ sarvatra gacchatīti sarvatra-go mahān parimāṇataḥ, tathā ākāśavat sarva-gate mayy asaṃśleṣeṇaiva sthitānīty evam upadhāraya vijānīhi ||BhGS_9.6||
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, the wind abides in space — situated in space always, perpetually — the wind goes everywhere, <s>mahān</s> (mighty) in magnitude; similarly, know, i.e. understand, that all beings abide in Me who am all-pervading like space, without any contact whatsoever.

children.text: evaṃ vāyur ākāśe iva mayi sthitāni sarva-bhūtāni sthiti-kāle | tāni -
children.translated_text: Thus, just as the wind in space, all beings abide in Me during the period of existence. Those beings —

children.text: sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām |
children.translated_text: All beings, O <s>Kaunteya</s> (son of Kuntī), pass into My <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature)

children.text: kalpa-kṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham ||BhG_9.7||
children.translated_text: at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle); at the beginning of a <s>kalpa</s>, I send them forth again.

children.text: sarva-bhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ triguṇātmikām aparāṃ nikṛṣṭaṃ yānti māmikāṃ madīyāṃ kalpa-kṣaye pralaya-kāle | punar bhūyas tāni bhūtāni utpatti-kāle kalpādau visṛjāmi utpādayāmy ahaṃ pūrvavat ||BhGS_9.7||
children.translated_text: All beings, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, pass into <s>Prakṛti</s> — the inferior nature consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — My own, belonging to Me, at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, at the time of dissolution. Again, once more, those beings at the time of creation, at the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, I send forth, I produce, as before.

children.text: evam avidyā-lakṣaṇām -
children.translated_text: Thus, resorting to that which has the character of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) —

children.text: prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Resorting to My own <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), I send forth again and again

children.text: bhūta-grāmam imaṃ kṛtsnam avaśaṃ prakṛter vaśāt ||BhG_9.8||
children.translated_text: this entire multitude of beings, helpless, by the force of <s>Prakṛti</s>.

children.text: prakṛtiṃ svāṃ svīyām avaṣṭabhya vaśīkṛtya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ prakṛtito jātaṃ bhūta-grāmaṃ bhūta-samudāyam imaṃ vartamānaṃ kṛtsnam avaśam asvatantram | avidyādi-doṣaiḥ paravaśīkṛtam | prakṛter vaśāt svabhāva-vaśāt ||BhGS_9.8||
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> — My own, belonging to Me — having brought under control, I send forth again and again this multitude of beings (<s>bhūta-grāma</s>), this assemblage of beings presently existing, the entire host, helpless, not independent — rendered subject to another's will by defects such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest — by the force of <s>Prakṛti</s>, by the force of their own nature.

children.text: tarhi tasya te parameśvarasya bhūta-grāmam imaṃ viṣamaṃ vidadhataḥ, tan-nimittābhyāṃ dharmādharmābhyāṃ saṃbandhaḥ syād itīdam āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: Then, for You the Supreme Lord who ordains this unequal multitude of beings, there would be connection with <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) which are the causes of that — to this the Blessed Lord says:

children.text: na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya |
children.translated_text: These actions do not bind Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (Arjuna),

children.text: udāsīnavad āsīnam asaktaṃ teṣu karmasu ||BhG_9.9||
children.translated_text: seated as one indifferent, unattached to those actions.

children.text: na ca mām īśvaraṃ tāni bhūta-grāmasya viṣama-sarga-nimittāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya | tatra karmaṇām asaṃbandhitve kāraṇam āha - udāsīnavat āsīnaṃ yathā udīsīna upekṣakaḥ kaścit tadvad āsīnam ātmano 'vikriyatvāt | asaktaṃ phalāsaṅga-rahitam, abhimāna-varjitam, ahaṃ karomīti teṣu karmasu | ato 'nyasyāpi kartṛtvābhimānābhāvaḥ phalāsaṅgābhāvaś cāsaṃbandha-kāraṇam, anyathā karmabhir badhyate mūḍhaḥ kośa-kāravad ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_9.9||
children.translated_text: These actions that are the causes of the unequal creation of the multitude of beings do not bind Me, the Lord, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. He states the reason for the non-connection with actions: 'seated as one indifferent' — just as an indifferent person, some onlooker, so am I seated, because of the non-modification of the Self; 'unattached' — devoid of attachment to results, free from the sense of doership, the notion 'I am doing' with respect to those actions. Therefore, for anyone else too, the absence of the sense of doership and the absence of attachment to results are the causes of non-bondage; otherwise the deluded person is bound by actions, like a silkworm — this is the purport.

children.text: tatra bhūta-grāmam imaṃ visṛjāmy udāsīnavad āsīnam iti ca viruddham ucyate, iti tat-parihārārtham āha -
children.translated_text: There, the statements 'I send forth this multitude of beings' and 'seated as one indifferent' are contradictory — to resolve this He says:

children.text: mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sa-carācaram |
children.translated_text: Under My supervision, <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) brings forth the world of moving and unmoving beings;

children.text: hetunānena kaunteya jagad viparivartate ||BhG_9.10||
children.translated_text: by this cause, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the world revolves.

children.text: mayādhyakṣeṇa sarvato dṛśi-mātra-svarupeṇāvikriyātmanādhyakṣeṇa mayā, mama māyā triguṇātmikāvidyā-lakṣaṇā prakṛtiḥ sūyate utpādayati sa-carācaraṃ jagat | tathā ca mantra-varṇaḥ -
children.translated_text: Under My supervision — by Me whose essential nature is pure witnessing consciousness alone, unchanging in nature, as supervisor — My <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) having the character of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), brings forth, produces the world of moving and unmoving beings. And thus the <s>Mantra</s> text declares:

children.text:
eko devaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ
sarva-vyāpī sarva-bhūtāntarātmā |
karmādhyakṣaḥ sarva-bhūtādhivāsaḥ
sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaś ca || [ŚvetU 6.11] iti |
children.translated_text: the witness, the consciousness, alone, and beyond the <s>guṇas</s> [<s>ŚvetU</s> 6.11].
The one God hidden in all beings, all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings, the overseer of actions, dwelling in all beings,

children.text:
hetunā nimittenānenādhyakṣatvena kaunteya jagat sa-carācaraṃ vyaktāvyaktātmakaṃ viparivartate sarvāvasthāsu | dṛśi-karmatvāpatti-nimittā hi jagataḥ sarvā pravṛttiḥ - aham idaṃ bhokṣye, paśyāmīdam, śṛṇomīdam, sukham anubhavāmi, duḥkham anubhavāmi, tad-artham idaṃ kariṣye, idaṃ jñāsyāmi, ity ādyāvagati-niṣṭhāvagaty-avasānaiva | yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman [Ṛk 8.7.17.7, TaittB 2.8.9] ity ādayaś ca mantrā etam arthaṃ darśayanti | tataś caikasya devasya sarvādhyakṣa-bhūta-caitanya-mātrasya paramārthataḥ sarva-bhogānabhisaṃbandhino 'nyasya cetanāntarasyābhāve bhoktur anyasyābhāvāt | kiṃ-nimitteyaṃ sṛṣṭir ity atra praśna-prativacane 'nupapanne, ko addhā veda ka iha pravocat | kuta ājātā kuta iyaṃ visṛṣṭiḥ [Ṛk 8.7.17.8] ity ādi-mantra-varṇebhyaḥ | darśitaṃ ca bhagavatā -
 ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ [Gītā 5.15] iti ||BhGS_9.10||
children.translated_text: By this cause, by this reason of being the supervisor, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the world of moving and unmoving, consisting of the manifest and unmanifest, revolves in all its states. For all activity of the world has as its occasion the becoming-an-object-of-seeing — 'I shall enjoy this,' 'I see this,' 'I hear this,' 'I experience pleasure,' 'I experience pain,' 'For that purpose I shall do this,' 'I shall know this' — thus all activity culminates in cognition, terminates in cognition. The <s>Mantra</s> texts such as 'He who is its overseer in the highest heaven' [<s>Ṛk</s> 8.7.17.7, <s>TaittB</s> 2.8.9] also demonstrate this meaning. And since there is, in ultimate reality, only one God who is the supreme overseer, pure consciousness alone, having no real connection with any enjoyment, and since there is no other conscious being as an enjoyer — the question 'What is the cause of this creation?' and its answer become untenable, as shown by the <s>Mantra</s> texts: 'Who truly knows? Who can declare here? Whence was it born, whence this creation?' [<s>Ṛk</s> 8.7.17.8] and so forth. And it has been shown by the Blessed Lord: 'Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance; thereby beings are deluded' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.15].

children.text: evaṃ māṃ nitya-śuddha-buddham ukta-svabhāvaṃ sarvajñaṃ sarva-jantūnām ātmānam api santam -
children.translated_text: Thus, though I am the Self of all beings, eternally pure, awakened, of the nature described above, omniscient —

children.text: avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanum āśritam |
children.translated_text: The deluded despise Me when I assume a human form,

children.text: paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaram ||BhG_9.11||
children.translated_text: not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of beings.

children.text: avajānanty avajñāṃ paribhavaṃ kurvanti māṃ mūḍhā avivekinaḥ | mānuṣīṃ manuṣyasaṃbandhinīṃ tanuṃ deham āśritam, manuṣyadehena vyavaharantamity etat, paraṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ bhāvaṃ param ātma-tattvam ākāśa-kalpam ākāśād apy antaratamam ajānanto mama bhūta-maheśvaraṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ mahāntam īśvaraṃ svātmānam | tataś ca tasya mamāvajñāna-bhāvanena āhatās te varākāḥ ||BhGS_9.11||
children.translated_text: They despise — show contempt for, disrespect — Me, the deluded, the undiscriminating. 'Having assumed a human form' means having assumed a body belonging to humans, i.e. one who conducts Himself through a human body — this is the meaning. Not knowing My supreme, exalted nature (<s>bhāva</s>), My supreme Self-reality, which is like space, even more interior than space, as the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) of all beings, i.e. My own Self. And therefore, struck by their attitude of contempt toward Me, those wretched ones —

children.text: katham ? -
children.translated_text: How so? —

children.text: moghāśā mogha-karmāṇo mogha-jñānā vicetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of vain hopes, vain actions, and vain knowledge, senseless,

children.text: rākṣasīm āsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ ||BhG_9.12||
children.translated_text: they resort to the deluding nature of <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) and <s>Asuras</s> (titans).

children.text: moghāśā vṛthā āśā āśiṣo yeṣāṃ te moghāśāḥ | tathā mogha-karmāṇo yāni cāgnihotrādīni tair anuṣṭhīyamānāni karmāṇi tāni ca, teṣāṃ bhagavat-paribhavāt, svātma-bhūtasyāvajñānāt moghāny eva niṣphalāni karmāṇi bhavantīti mogha-karmāṇaḥ | tathā mogha-jñānā moghaṃ niṣphalaṃ jñānaṃ yeṣāṃ te mogha-jñānāḥ, jñānam api teṣāṃ niṣphalam eva syāt | vicetaso vigata-vivekāś ca te bhavantīty abhiprāyaḥ | kiṃ ca - te bhavanti rākṣasīṃ rakṣasāṃ prakṛtiṃ svabhāvam āsurīm asurāṇāṃ ca prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ moha-karīṃ dehātma-vādinīṃ śritāḥ āśritāḥ, | chindhi, bhindhi, piba, khāda, parasvam apahara, ity evaṃ vadana-śīlāḥ krūra-karmāṇo bhavantīty arthaḥ | asuryā nāma te lokāḥ [ĪśaU 3] iti śruteḥ ||BhGS_9.12||
children.translated_text: Those whose hopes (<s>āśā</s>) are vain — whose desires and wishes are futile — are <s>moghāśāḥ</s> (of vain hopes). Likewise, <s>mogha-karmāṇaḥ</s> (of vain actions) — whatever rites such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and others are performed by them, those actions too, because of their contempt toward the Blessed Lord, because of their disrespect toward their own Self, become futile, fruitless — thus they are of vain actions. Likewise, <s>mogha-jñānāḥ</s> (of vain knowledge) — those whose knowledge is vain, fruitless; even their knowledge becomes fruitless. And they become <s>vicetasaḥ</s> (senseless), devoid of discrimination — this is the purport. Moreover, they become those who have resorted to the <s>Rākṣasī</s> (demoniac) nature of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and the <s>Āsurī</s> (titanic) nature of <s>Asuras</s>, which is deluding, which causes delusion, which holds the body to be the Self — 'Cut! Break! Drink! Eat! Steal others' property!' — those who are habitually given to such speech become performers of cruel actions — this is the meaning. As the <s>Śruti</s> states: 'Those worlds are called Āsurī (demoniac)' [<s>ĪśaU</s> 3].

children.text: ye punaḥ śraddadhānā bhagavad-bhakti-lakṣaṇe mokṣa-mārge pravṛttāḥ -
children.translated_text: But those who are faithful, who have entered upon the path of liberation characterized by devotion to the Blessed Lord —

children.text: mahātmānas tu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtim āśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: But the great souls, O <s>Pārtha</s> (son of Pṛthā), resorting to the divine nature,

children.text: bhajanty ananya-manaso jñātvā bhūtādim avyayam ||BhG_9.13||
children.translated_text: worship Me with undistracted mind, knowing Me as the imperishable origin of beings.

children.text: mahātamānas tv akṣudra-cittāḥ mām īśvaraṃ pārtha daivīṃ devānāṃ prakṛtiṃ śama-dama-dayā-śraddhādi-lakṣaṇām āśritāḥ santo bhajanti sevante 'nanya-manaso 'nanya-cittā jñātvā bhūtādiṃ bhūtānāṃ viyad-ādīnāṃ prāṇināṃ cādiṃ kāraṇam avyayam ||BhGS_9.13||
children.translated_text: But the <s>mahātmānaḥ</s> (great souls), those of no small mind, worship Me, the Lord, O <s>Pārtha</s>, having resorted to the <s>daivī prakṛti</s> (divine nature) of the gods, characterized by tranquility, self-restraint, compassion, faith, and the like; they worship, they serve, with undistracted mind (<s>ananya-manasaḥ</s>), with mind fixed on nothing else, having known Me as the <s>bhūtādi</s> (origin of beings), the cause of all beings beginning with space and of all living creatures, the imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>).

children.text: katham ? -
children.translated_text: How so? —

children.text: satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaś ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ |
children.translated_text: Constantly glorifying Me, striving with firm vows,

children.text: namasyantaś ca māṃ bhaktyā nitya-yuktā upāsate ||BhG_9.14||
children.translated_text: and bowing to Me with devotion, ever steadfast, they worship Me.

children.text: satataṃ sarvadā bhagavantaṃ brahma-svarūpaṃ māṃ kīrtayantaḥ, yatantaś ca indriyopasaṃhāra-śama-dama-dayāhiṃsādi-lakṣaṇair dharmaiḥ prayatantaś ca, dṛḍha-vratā dṛḍhaṃ sthiram acālyaṃ vrataṃ yeṣāṃ te dṛḍha-vratā namasyantaś ca māṃ hṛdayeśayam ātmānaṃ bhaktyā nitya-yuktāḥ santa upāsate sevante ||BhGS_9.14||
children.translated_text: Constantly, at all times, glorifying Me, the Blessed Lord whose essential nature is <s>Brahman</s>; and striving — exerting themselves through virtues characterized by withdrawal of the senses, tranquility, self-restraint, compassion, non-violence, and the like; of firm vows (<s>dṛḍha-vratāḥ</s>) — those whose vow is firm, steady, unshakable; and bowing to Me, the Self dwelling in the heart, with devotion; ever steadfast (<s>nitya-yuktāḥ</s>), they worship, they serve Me.

children.text: te kena kena prakāreṇa upāsate ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: By what various modes do they worship? This is stated —

children.text: jñāna-yajñena cāpy anye yajanto mām upāsate |
children.translated_text: And yet others, worshipping through the sacrifice of knowledge, worship Me

children.text: ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvato-mukham ||BhG_9.15||
children.translated_text: as the one, as the distinct, and as the manifold, the universal form.

children.text: jñāna-yajñena jñānam eva bhagavad-viṣayaṃ yajñas tena jñāna-yajñena, yajantaḥ pūjayantaḥ mām īśvaraṃ cāpy anye 'nyām upāsanāṃ parityajyopāsate | tac ca jñānam - ekatvenaikam eva paraṃ brahmeti paramārtha-darśanena yajanta upāsate | kecic ca pṛthaktvena āditya-candrādi-bhedena sa eva bhagavān viṣṇur avasthita ity upāsate | kecit bahudhāvasthitaḥ sa eva bhagavān sarvato-mukho viśva-rūpa iti taṃ viśva-rūpaṃ sarvato-mukhaṃ bahudhā bahu-prakāreṇopāsate ||BhGS_9.15||
children.translated_text: Through the sacrifice of knowledge (<s>jñāna-yajña</s>) — knowledge itself, having the Blessed Lord as its object, is the sacrifice; through that sacrifice of knowledge, worshipping, honoring Me, the Lord — yet others, abandoning other forms of worship, worship Me. And that knowledge is: through oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) — 'There is only one supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — through the vision of ultimate reality, they worship. Some through distinctness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) — through the differentiation of <s>Āditya</s> (sun), <s>Candra</s> (moon), and so forth — worship thus: 'That same Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established in these.' Some worship that same Blessed Lord established in manifold forms, as the universal form (<s>viśvato-mukha</s>), facing in all directions, in many ways.

children.text: yadi bahubhiḥ prakārair upāsate, kathaṃ tvām eva upāsata iti | ata āha -
children.translated_text: If He is worshipped in many ways, how is it that they worship You alone? To this He says —

children.text: ahaṃ kratur ahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣadham |
children.translated_text: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the medicinal herb,

children.text: mantro 'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṃ hutam ||BhG_9.16||
children.translated_text: I am the sacred formula (<s>mantra</s>); I am the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>); I am the fire; I am the oblation. // <s>BhG</s> 9.16 //

children.text: ahaṃ kratuḥ śrauta-karma-bhedo 'ham eva | ahaṃ yajñaḥ smārtaḥ | kiṃ ca svadhānnam aham, pitṛbhyo yad dīyate | aham auṣadhaṃ sarva-prāṇibhir yat adyate tat auṣadha-śabda-śabditaṃ vrīhi-yavādi-sādhāraṇam | athavā svadheti sarva-prāṇi-sādhāraṇam annam, auṣadham iti vyādhy-upaśamanārthaṃ bheṣajam | mantro 'ham, yena pitṛbhyo devatābhyaś ca havir dīyate | aham eva ājyaṃ haviś ca | aham agniḥ, yasmin hūte haviḥ so 'gnir aham | ahaṃ hutaṃ havana-karmaś ca ||BhGS_9.16||
children.translated_text: I am the <s>kratu</s> — a particular <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) sacrifice. I am the <s>yajña</s> — the <s>smārta</s> (traditional) sacrifice. Moreover, I am the <s>svadhā</s>, the food-offering that is given to the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>). I am the <s>auṣadha</s> (herb) — that which is eaten by all living beings, denoted by the word '<s>auṣadha</s>,' common to rice, barley, and the like. Alternatively, '<s>svadhā</s>' refers to food common to all living beings, and '<s>auṣadha</s>' refers to medicine for the alleviation of disease. I am the <s>mantra</s> — by which the oblation is offered to the ancestors and to the deities. I myself am the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>), the oblation (<s>havis</s>). I am the fire (<s>agni</s>) — that into which the oblation is offered. I am the oblation (<s>huta</s>), the act of offering. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.16 //

children.text: pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, the grandfather;

children.text: vedyaṃ pavitram oṃkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca ||BhG_9.17||
children.translated_text: I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, and the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> [<s>Vedas</s>]. // <s>BhG</s> 9.17 //

children.text: pitā janayitāham asya jagataḥ, mātā janayitrī, dhātā karma-phalasya prāṇibhyo vidhātā, pitāmahaḥ pituḥ pitā, vedyaṃ veditavyam, pavitraṃ pāvanam oṃkāraḥ, ṛk sāma yajue eva ca ||BhGS_9.17||
children.translated_text: I am the father, the begetter, of this universe; the mother, the bearer; the sustainer (<s>dhātā</s>), the dispenser of the fruits of action to living beings; the grandfather, the father's father. [I am] the object of knowledge (<s>vedya</s>), what is to be known; the purifier (<s>pavitra</s>), the purifying [agent]; the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>; and the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Yajus</s> [<s>Vedas</s>]. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.17 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt |
children.translated_text: [I am] the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the friend,

children.text: prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījam avyayam ||BhG_9.18||
children.translated_text: the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure, and the imperishable seed. // <s>BhG</s> 9.18 //

children.text: gatiḥ karma-phalam, bhartā poṣṭā, prabhuḥ svāmī, sākṣī prāṇināṃ kṛtākṛtasya, nivāso yasmin prāṇino nivasanti, śaraṇam ārtānām, prapannānām ārti-haraḥ | suhṛt pratyupakārānapekṣaḥ sann upakārī, prabhava utpattir jagataḥ, pralayaḥ pralīyate 'smin iti, tathā sthānaṃ tiṣṭhaty asminn iti, nidhānaṃ nikṣepaḥ kālāntaropabhogyaṃ prāṇinām, bījaṃ praroha-kāraṇaṃ praroha-dharmiṇām, avyayaṃ yāvat-saṃsāra-bhāvitvāt avyayam, na hy abījaṃ kiṃcit prarohati | nityaṃ ca praroha-darśanād bīja-saṃtatir na vyetīti gamyate ||BhGS_9.18||
children.translated_text: The goal (<s>gati</s>) — the fruit of action. The supporter (<s>bhartā</s>) — the nourisher. The Lord (<s>prabhu</s>) — the master. The witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) — of what is done and not done by living beings. The abode (<s>nivāsa</s>) — in which living beings dwell. The refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>) — the remover of affliction for those who are afflicted, for those who surrender. The friend (<s>suhṛt</s>) — one who renders help without expecting any return. The origin (<s>prabhava</s>) — the source of the universe's creation. The dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) — that into which [the universe] dissolves. The foundation (<s>sthāna</s>) — that in which [the universe] stands. The treasure (<s>nidhāna</s>) — the storehouse, that which is preserved for enjoyment at another time by living beings. The imperishable seed (<s>bījam avyayam</s>) — the seed, the cause of germination for all that has the nature of germinating. It is imperishable because it lasts as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> endures. For nothing germinates without a seed. And from the constant observation of germination, it is understood that the continuity of the seed does not cease. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.18 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: tapāmy aham ahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmy utsṛjāmi ca |
children.translated_text: I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain;

children.text: amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca sad asac cāham arjuna ||BhG_9.19||
children.translated_text: I am immortality and also death; I am being and non-being, O <s>Arjuna</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 9.19 //

children.text: tapāmy aham ādityo bhūtvā kaiścit raśmibhir ulbaṇaiḥ | ahaṃ varṣaṃ kaiścid raśmibhir utsṛjāmi | utsṛjya punar nigṛhṇāmi kaiścid raśmibhir aṣṭabhir māsaiḥ punar utsṛjāmi prāvṛṣi | amṛtaṃ caiva devānām, mṛtyuś ca martyānām | sad yasya yat saṃbandhitayā vidyamānaṃ tat, tad-viparītam asac caivāham arjuna | na punar atyantam evāsad bhagavān, svayaṃ kārya-kāraṇe vā sad-asatī ||BhGS_9.19||
children.translated_text: I give heat (<s>tapāmi</s>), having become the sun, with certain scorching rays. I release (<s>utsṛjāmi</s>) the rain with certain rays. Having released [it], I withhold (<s>nigṛhṇāmi</s>) [it] again with certain rays for eight months, and then release [it] again in the rainy season (<s>prāvṛṣ</s>). I am immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) — for the gods; and death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) — for mortals. '<s>Sat</s>' (being) — that which exists in relation to something [as its quality or attribute] is '<s>sat</s>'; the opposite of that is '<s>asat</s>' (non-being); I am both, O <s>Arjuna</s>. But the Blessed Lord is not absolutely non-existent (<s>asat</s>); rather, the effect and the cause are themselves being and non-being [respectively]. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.19 //

children.text: ye pūrvoktair nivṛtti-prakārair ekatva-pṛthaktvādi-vijñānair yajñair māṃ pūjayanta upāsate jñāna-vidaḥ, te yathā-vijñānaṃ mām eva prāpnuvanti | ye punar ajñāḥ kāma-kāmāḥ -
children.translated_text: Those who, through the previously described modes of withdrawal, through sacrifices characterized by the knowledge of unity, difference, and the like, worship and meditate on Me — the knowers of knowledge (<s>jñānavid</s>) — they attain Me alone, in accordance with their respective knowledge. But those who are ignorant, who desire objects of desire —

children.text: traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūta-pāpā
children.translated_text: The knowers of the three <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Soma</s>-drinkers, purified of sins,

children.text: yajñair iṣṭvā svar-gatiṃ prārthayante |
children.translated_text: having worshipped Me with sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven;

children.text: te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam
children.translated_text: they, having attained the meritorious world of the king of gods (<s>Indra</s>),

children.text: aśnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān ||BhG_9.20||
children.translated_text: enjoy in heaven the divine pleasures of the gods. // <s>BhG</s> 9.20 //

children.text: traividyā ṛg-yajuḥ-sāma-vido māṃ vasv-ādi-deva-rūpiṇaṃ somapāḥ somaṃ pibantīti somapāḥ, tenaiva soma-pānena pūta-pāpāḥ śuddha-kilbiṣāḥ, yajñair agniṣṭomādibhir iṣṭvā pūjayitvā svar-gatiṃ svarga-gamanaṃ svar eva gatiḥ svar-gatis tām, prārthayante | te ca puṇyaṃ puṇya-phalam āsādya saṃprāpya surendra-lokaṃ śatakratoḥ sthānam aśnanti bhuñjate divyān divi bhavān aprākṛtān deva-bhogān devānāṃ bhogān ||BhGS_9.20||
children.translated_text: The knowers of the three <s>Vedas</s> — those who know the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāma</s> [<s>Vedas</s>], [who worship] Me in the form of deities such as the <s>Vasus</s> etc. <s>Somapāḥ</s> — those who drink <s>Soma</s>; by that very drinking of <s>Soma</s>, they are '<s>pūta-pāpāḥ</s>' — purified of sins, cleansed of defilements. Having worshipped (<s>iṣṭvā</s>) with sacrifices such as <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> etc., they pray for the way to heaven (<s>svar-gati</s>) — '<s>svar</s>' itself is the goal; '<s>svar-gati</s>' is the going to heaven. They, having attained (<s>āsādya</s>) the meritorious fruit, the world of <s>Indra</s> (<s>surendra-loka</s>), the abode of the lord of a hundred sacrifices, enjoy (<s>aśnanti</s>) in heaven the divine (<s>divya</s>), supernatural, non-worldly pleasures of the gods. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.20 //

children.text: te taṃ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṃ viśālaṃ
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world,

children.text: kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṃ viśanti |
children.translated_text: when their merit is exhausted, they enter the mortal world;

children.text: evaṃ trayī-dharmam anuprapannā
children.translated_text: thus, those who follow the <s>dharma</s> of the three <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: gatāgataṃ kāma-kāmā labhante ||BhG_9.21||
children.translated_text: desiring objects of desire, obtain going and coming. // <s>BhG</s> 9.21 //

children.text: te taṃ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṃ viśālaṃ vistīrṇaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṃ viśanti āviśanti | evaṃ yathoktena prakāreṇa trayī-dharmaṃ kevalaṃ vaidikaṃ karmānuprapannā gatāgataṃ gataṃ cāgataṃ ca gatāgataṃ gamanāgamanaṃ kāma-kāmāḥ kāmān kāmayanta iti kāma-kāmā labhante gatāgatam eva, na tu svātantryaṃ kvacil labhanta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_9.21||
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed that vast, extensive heavenly world — when their merit is exhausted, they enter, they come back to, the mortal world. Thus, in the manner described, those who follow the <s>dharma</s> of the three <s>Vedas</s> — the merely Vedic ritual action alone — [obtain] going and coming (<s>gatāgata</s>), i.e., departure and return, being '<s>kāma-kāmāḥ</s>' (those who desire objects of desire). They obtain only going and coming — they never attain independence anywhere — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.21 //

children.text: ye punar niṣkāmāḥ samyag-darśinaḥ -
children.translated_text: But those who are desireless, who are seers of the ultimate truth —

children.text: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Those persons who, thinking of none other [than Me], worship Me exclusively,

children.text: teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ vahāmy aham ||BhG_9.22||
children.translated_text: for those ever-devoted ones, I carry their acquisition and preservation (<s>yoga-kṣema</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 9.22 //

children.text: ananyā apṛthag-bhūtāḥ paraṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇam ātmatvena gatāḥ santaś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ saṃnyāsinaḥ paryupāsate, teṣāṃ paramārtha-darśināṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ satatābhiyogināṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ yogo 'prāptasya prāpaṇaṃ kṣemas tad-rakṣaṇaṃ tad-ubhayaṃ vahāmi prāpayāmy aham | jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam [Gītā 7.18] sa ca mama priyaḥ [Gītā 7.17] yasmād tasmāt te mamātma-bhūtāḥ priyāś ceti |
children.translated_text: '<s>Ananyāḥ</s>' — those who are non-separate, who have realized the Supreme God <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as their own Self, and being such, contemplate Me — those persons, the renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>), who worship Me exclusively. For those — who are seers of the ultimate reality, who are ever devoted (<s>nityābhiyukta</s>), constantly engaged — I carry their <s>yoga-kṣema</s>: '<s>yoga</s>' is the acquisition of what is not yet obtained; '<s>kṣema</s>' is the preservation of that [which has been obtained]. I carry, I provide, both of these. For 'the <s>jñānin</s> (knower) is indeed My very self — this is My view' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.18], and 'he is dear to Me' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.17] — since that is so, they are as My very self and are dear [to Me].

children.text: nanv anyeṣām api bhaktānāṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ vahaty eva bhagavān | satyaṃ vahaty eva | kiṃtv ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ - anye ye bhaktās te ātmārthaṃ svayam api yoga-kṣemam īhante | ananya-darśinas tu nātmārthaṃ yoga-kṣemam īhante | na hi te jīvite maraṇe vātmano gṛddhiṃ kurvanti | kevalam eva bhagavac-charaṇās te | ato bhagavān eva teṣāṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ vahatīti ||BhGS_9.22||
children.translated_text: Objection: Does not the Blessed Lord carry the <s>yoga-kṣema</s> of other devotees as well? Reply: True, He does carry [theirs] indeed. But here is the distinction: other devotees strive for their <s>yoga-kṣema</s> on their own behalf as well.
