But those of exclusive vision (<s>ananya-darśin</s>) do not strive for <s>yoga-kṣema</s> on their own behalf. For they have no greed for either life or death. They are solely dependent on the Blessed Lord. Therefore, the Blessed Lord alone carries their <s>yoga-kṣema</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.22 //

children.text: nanv anyāpi devatās tvam eva cet tad-bhaktāś ca tvām eva yajante | satyam evam -
children.translated_text: Objection: If other deities are You alone, then the devotees of those deities also worship You alone. Reply: True, that is so —

children.text: ye 'py anya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even those devotees of other deities who worship with faith,

children.text: te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam ||BhG_9.23||
children.translated_text: they too worship Me alone, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, but not in the proper manner (<s>avidhi-pūrvakam</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 9.23 //

children.text: ye 'py anya-devatā-bhaktā anyāsu devatāsu bhaktā anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ santo yajante pūjayanti śraddhayā āstikya-buddhyānvitā anugatāḥ, te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam avidhir ajñānaṃ tat-pūrvakaṃ yajanta ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_9.23||
children.translated_text: Even those who are devotees of other deities — being devoted to other deities — worship, honor [them] endowed with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), with a spirit of belief — they too worship Me alone, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, but not in the proper manner (<s>avidhi-pūrvakam</s>) — '<s>avidhi</s>' means ignorance; [they worship] preceded by that — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.23 //

children.text: kasmāt te 'vidhi-pūrvakaṃ yajanta ity ucyate | yasmāt -
children.translated_text: Why do they worship in an improper manner? It is said — because:

children.text: ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca |
children.translated_text: For I am the enjoyer and also the lord of all sacrifices;

children.text: na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaś cyavanti te ||BhG_9.24||
children.translated_text: but they do not know Me in truth — therefore they fall. // <s>BhG</s> 9.24 //

children.text: ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ śrautānāṃ smārtānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ yajñānāṃ devatātmatvena bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca | mat-svāmiko hi yajñaḥ, adhiyajño 'ham evātra [Gītā 8.4] iti hy uktam | tathā na tu mām abhijānanti tattvena yathāvat | ataś cāvidhi-pūrvakam iṣṭvā yāga-phalāc cyavanti pracyavante te ||BhGS_9.24||
children.translated_text: For I am the enjoyer — being the Self of the deities — and the lord of all sacrifices, both <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>smārta</s> (traditional). For the sacrifice belongs to Me as its master; 'I am the <s>adhiyajña</s> (Lord of sacrifice) here' [<s>Gītā</s> 8.4] — this has already been stated. Likewise, but they do not know Me in truth (<s>tattva</s>), as I truly am. Therefore, having worshipped in an improper manner (<s>avidhi-pūrvakam</s>), they fall (<s>cyavanti</s>) from the fruit of sacrifice. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.24 //

children.text: ye 'py anya-devatā-bhakti-mattvenāvidhi-pūrvakaṃ yajante, teṣām api yāga-phalam avaśyaṃbhāvi | katham ? -
children.translated_text: Even for those who worship in an improper manner due to their devotion to other deities, the fruit of sacrifice inevitably comes. How? —

children.text: yānti deva-vratā devān pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ |
children.translated_text: Worshippers of the gods go to the gods; worshippers of the ancestors go to the ancestors;

children.text: bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino 'pi mām ||BhG_9.25||
children.translated_text: worshippers of the spirits go to the spirits; and My worshippers come to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 9.25 //

children.text: yānti gacchanti deva-vratā deveṣu vrataṃ niyamo bhaktiś ca yeṣāṃ te deva-vratā devān yānti | pitṝn agniṣv āttādīn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ śrāddhādi-kriyā-parāḥ pitṛ-bhaktāḥ | bhūtāni vināyaka-mātṛ-gaṇa-catur-bhaginyādīni yānti bhūtejyā bhūtānāṃ pūjakāḥ | yānti mad-yājino mad-yajana-śīlā vaiṣṇavā mām eva yānti | samāne 'py āyāse mām eva na bhajante 'jñānāt, tena te 'lpa-phala-bhājo bhavantīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_9.25||
children.translated_text: The '<s>deva-vratāḥ</s>' (those whose vow is to the gods) — those whose observance (<s>vrata</s>), commitment, and devotion is in the gods — they go to the gods. The '<s>pitṛ-vratāḥ</s>' (those whose vow is to the ancestors) — those devoted to the ancestors, engaged in rites such as <s>śrāddha</s> etc. — they go to the ancestors such as the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> and others. The '<s>bhūtejyāḥ</s>' (worshippers of spirits) — those who worship spirits such as <s>Vināyaka</s>, the <s>Mātṛ-gaṇas</s>, the four sisters, etc. — they go to those spirits. My worshippers (<s>mad-yājinaḥ</s>) — those whose habit is to worship Me, the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> — they come to Me alone. Despite the effort being the same, they do not worship Me due to ignorance; thereby they become recipients of meager fruit — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.25 //

children.text: na kevalaṃ mad-bhaktānām anāvṛtti-lakṣaṇam ananta-phalam, sukhārādhanaś cāham | katham ? -
children.translated_text: Not only do My devotees [obtain] the infinite fruit characterized by non-return, but I am also easy to worship. How? —

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
children.translated_text: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — whoever offers Me [these] with devotion,

children.text: tad ahaṃ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||BhG_9.26||
children.translated_text: that offering made with devotion, I accept from the pure-hearted one. // <s>BhG</s> 9.26 //

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyam udakaṃ yaḥ me mahyaṃ bhaktyā prayacchati, tat ahaṃ patrādi bhaktyā upahṛtaṃ bhakti-pūrvakaṃ prāpitaṃ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi gṛhṇāmi prayatātmanaḥ śuddha-buddheḥ ||BhGS_9.26||
children.translated_text: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — whoever offers to Me, to Myself, with devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — that [leaf etc.], offered with devotion, presented with devotion — I accept (<s>aśnāmi</s>), I receive, from the pure-hearted one (<s>prayatātmanaḥ</s>), one of purified mind. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.26 //

children.text: yataḥ evam, ataḥ -
children.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give,

children.text: yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam ||BhG_9.27||
children.translated_text: whatever austerity you practice, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, do that as an offering to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 9.27 //

children.text: yat karoṣi svataḥ prāptam, yad aśnāsi, yac ca juhoṣi havanaṃ nirvartayasi śrautaṃ smārtaṃ vā, yad dadāsi prayacchasi brāhmaṇādibhyo hiraṇyānnājyādi, yat tapasyasi tapaś carasi kaunteya, tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇaṃ mat-samarpaṇam ||BhGS_9.27||
children.translated_text: Whatever you do — what comes naturally; whatever you eat; whatever you offer in sacrifice — whether you perform a <s>śrauta</s> or <s>smārta</s> oblation; whatever you give — whatever you bestow upon <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, such as gold, food, clarified butter, etc.; whatever austerity you practice — whatever austerity you perform, O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — do that as an offering to Me, as a dedication to Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.27 //

children.text: evaṃ kurvatas tava yat bhavati, tat sṛṇu -
children.translated_text: What results for you who acts thus? Listen —

children.text: śubhāśubha-phalair evaṃ mokṣyase karma-bandhanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus you shall be freed from the bonds of action, which bear good and evil fruits;

children.text: saṃnyāsa-yoga-yuktātmā vimukto mām upaiṣyasi ||BhG_9.28||
children.translated_text: with your self united by the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa-yoga</s>), you shall be liberated and come to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 9.28 //

children.text: śubhāśubha-phalaiḥ śubhāśubhe iṣṭāniṣṭe phale yeṣāṃ tāni śubhāśubha-phalāni karmāṇi taiḥ śubhāśubha-phalaiḥ karma-bandhanaiḥ karmāṇy eva bandhanāni karma-bandhanāni taiḥ karma-bandhanair evaṃ mad-arpaṇaṃ kurvan mokṣyase | so 'yaṃ saṃnyāsa-yogo nāma, saṃnyāsaś cāsau mat-samarpaṇatayā karmatvād yogaś cāsāv iti, tena saṃnyāsa-yogena yukta ātmāntaḥ-karaṇaṃ yasya tava sa tvaṃ saṃnyāsa-yoga-yuktātmā san vimuktaḥ karma-bandhanair jīvann eva patite cāsmin śarīre mām upaiṣyasi āgamiṣyasi ||BhGS_9.28||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śubhāśubha-phalaiḥ</s>' — actions whose fruits are auspicious and inauspicious, i.e., desirable and undesirable — those actions which are bonds (<s>karma-bandhanaiḥ</s>), i.e., actions that are themselves bondage — from those bonds of action with good and evil fruits, you shall be freed by thus making [all] an offering to Me. This is called '<s>saṃnyāsa-yoga</s>' (the yoga of renunciation) — it is '<s>saṃnyāsa</s>' (renunciation) because of being dedicated to Me, and '<s>yoga</s>' because it is action — by that <s>saṃnyāsa-yoga</s>, the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is united (<s>yukta</s>) — you whose self is thus united by the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation — being thus liberated from the bonds of action, even while alive, and when this body falls — you shall come to Me, you shall reach Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.28 //

children.text: rāga-dveṣavāṃs tarhi bhagavān, yato bhaktān anugṛhṇāti, netarān iti tan na -
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Is the Blessed Lord then possessed of attachment and aversion — that He favors His devotees and not others? No, that is not so —

children.text: samo 'haṃ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyo 'sti na priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am equal toward all beings; none is hateful to Me, none is dear;

children.text: ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham ||BhG_9.29||
children.translated_text: but those who worship Me with devotion — they are in Me, and I am in them. // <s>BhG</s> 9.29 //

children.text: samas tulyo 'haṃ sarva-bhūteṣu | na me dveṣyo 'sti na priyaḥ | agnivad aham - dūra-sthānāṃ yathāgniḥ śītaṃ nāpanayati, samīpam upasarpatām apanayati | tathāhaṃ bhaktān anugṛhṇāmi, netarān | ye bhajanti tu mām īśvaraṃ bhaktyā mayi te - svabhāvata eva, na mama rāga-nimittam - vartante | teṣu cāpy ahaṃ svabhāvata eva varte, netareṣu | naitāvatā teṣu dveṣo mam ||BhGS_9.29||
children.translated_text: I am equal, impartial, toward all beings. None is hateful to Me, and none is dear. Like fire — just as fire does not remove the cold of those who are far away, but removes [it] for those who approach near — so I favor My devotees, not others. Those who worship Me, the Lord, with devotion — they are in Me. By nature — not due to any partiality on My part — they abide [in Me]. And I too, by nature, abide in them — not in others. But this does not mean that I have hatred toward them [others]. // <s>BhGS</s> 9.29 //

children.text: sṛṇu mad-bhakter māhātmyam -
children.translated_text: Hear the greatness of devotion to Me —

children.text: api cet sudurācāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk |
children.translated_text: Even if one of very wicked conduct worships me with undivided devotion,

children.text: sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ samyag vyavasito hi saḥ ||BhG_9.30||
children.translated_text: that one is to be regarded as righteous, for that one has rightly resolved. ||<s>BhG</s> 9.30||

children.text: api cet yady api sudurācāraḥ suṣṭhu durācāro 'tīva kutsitācāro 'pi bhajate mām ananya-bhāk ananya-bhaktiḥ san, sādhur eva samyag-vṛtta eva sa mantavyo jñātavyaḥ | samyag yathāvad vyavasito hi saḥ, yasmāt sādhu-niścayaḥ saḥ ||BhGS_9.30||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Even if' — even though one is of extremely wicked conduct (<s>sudurācāra</s>), i.e., of very despicable behavior, excessively vile in conduct — if one worships me with undivided devotion (<s>ananya-bhāk</s>), being of exclusive devotion, that one is to be regarded, i.e., understood, as righteous (<s>sādhu</s>), i.e., as one of right conduct indeed. For that one has rightly resolved — since that person has made a righteous determination. ||<s>BhGS</s> 9.30||

children.text: utsṛjyaś ca bāhyāṃ durācāratām antaḥ samyag-vyavasāya-sāmarthyāt -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And having cast off external wicked conduct, through the power of the inner right resolve —

children.text: kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvac-chāntiṃ nigacchati |
children.translated_text: Quickly one becomes righteous-souled and attains everlasting peace;

children.text: kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati ||BhG_9.31||
children.translated_text: O <s>Kaunteya</s>, proclaim that my devotee never perishes! ||<s>BhG</s> 9.31||

children.text: kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ bhavati dharmātmā dharma-citta eva | śaśvan nityaṃ śāntiṃ copaśamaṃ nigacchati prāpnoti | sṛṇu paramārtham, kaunteya pratijānīhi niścitāṃ pratijñāṃ kuru, na me mama bhakto mayi samarpitāntarātmā mad-bhakto na praṇaśyatīti ||BhGS_9.31||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Quickly' (<s>kṣipram</s>), i.e., swiftly, one becomes righteous-souled (<s>dharmātmā</s>), i.e., one of righteous mind. And one attains everlasting (<s>śāśvat</s>), i.e., eternal, peace (<s>śānti</s>), i.e., tranquility. Listen to the ultimate truth — O <s>Kaunteya</s>, proclaim, i.e., make a firm declaration: my devotee — one whose inner self is surrendered to me, a devotee of mine — never perishes. ||<s>BhGS</s> 9.31||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye 'pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ |
children.translated_text: For those who take refuge in me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, even though they be of sinful birth —

children.text: striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te 'pi yānti parāṃ gatim ||BhG_9.32||
children.translated_text: women, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and also <s>Śūdras</s> — even they attain the supreme destination. ||<s>BhG</s> 9.32||

children.text: māṃ hi yasmāt pārtha vyapāśritya mām āśrayatvena gṛhītvā ye 'pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ pāpā yonir yeṣāṃ te pāpa-yonayaḥ syur bhaveyuḥ | pāpa-yonayaḥ pāpā yonir yeṣāṃ te pāpa-yonayaḥ pāpa-janmānaḥ | ke te ? ity āha -striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te 'pi yānti gacchanti parāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatim ||BhGS_9.32||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For me (<s>hi</s>), i.e., because — O <s>Pārtha</s>, having taken refuge in me (<s>vyapāśritya</s>), having accepted me as their refuge — those who may be of sinful birth (<s>pāpa-yoni</s>) — those whose birth is sinful, i.e., those of sinful origin — who are they? He says: women, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and also <s>Śūdras</s> — even they attain, i.e., reach, the supreme (<s>parā</s>), i.e., the highest, destination (<s>gati</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 9.32||

children.text: kiṃ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayas tathā |
children.translated_text: How much more so the meritorious <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and the devoted royal sages!

children.text: anityam asukhaṃ lokam imaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām ||BhG_9.33||
children.translated_text: Having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship me! ||<s>BhG</s> 9.33||

children.text: kiṃ punar brāhmaṇāḥ puṇyāḥ puṇya-yonayo bhaktā rājarṣayas tathā rājānaś ca te ṛṣayaś ceti rājarṣayaḥ | yata evam, ato 'nityaṃ kṣaṇa-bhaṅguram asukhaṃ ca sukha-varjitam imaṃ lokaṃ manuṣya-lokaṃ prāpya puruṣārtha-sādhanaṃ durlabhaṃ manuṣyatvaṃ labdhvā bhajasva sevasva mām ||BhGS_9.33||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How much more the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, who are of meritorious birth, and the devoted royal sages (<s>rājarṣis</s>) — kings who are also sages are <s>rājarṣis</s>. Since this is so — therefore, [having come to] this impermanent, ephemeral, joyless, i.e., devoid of happiness, world — the human world — having reached it, having obtained the human birth which is the means to the human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>) and which is difficult to obtain — worship me, serve me! ||<s>BhGS</s> 9.33||

children.text: katham ? -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How?

children.text: man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṃ namaskuru |
children.translated_text: Fix your mind on me, be my devotee, my worshipper; bow down to me;

children.text: mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṃ mat-parāyaṇaḥ ||BhG_9.34||
children.translated_text: thus having disciplined yourself, with me as your supreme goal — you shall come to me alone. ||<s>BhG</s> 9.34||

children.text: mayi vāsudeve mano yasya tava sa tvaṃ man-manā bhava | tathā mad-bhakto bhava | mad-yājī mad-yajana-śīlo bhava | mām eva ca namaskuru | mām eveśvarasyāgamiṣyasi yuktvā samādhāya cittam | evam ātmānaṃ māṃ ahaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām ātmā parā ca gatiḥ param ayanaṃ taṃ mām evambhūtam eṣyastīty atītena padena sambandhaḥ | mat-parāyaṇaḥ sann ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_9.34||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Be one whose mind is in me, <s>Vāsudeva</s> — be <s>man-manā</s> (mind-fixed-on-me). Likewise, be my devotee (<s>mad-bhakta</s>). Be my worshipper (<s>mad-yājī</s>), i.e., one whose nature is to worship me. And bow down to me alone. You will come to me alone, the Lord, having united, i.e., concentrated, the mind. 'Thus the self' — for I am indeed the Self (<s>ātmā</s>) of all beings, and the supreme destination, the highest refuge — to me, who am of this nature, you will come — [this is connected] with the earlier word. Being one whose supreme refuge is me (<s>mat-parāyaṇa</s>) — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 9.34||

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
rāja-vidyā-rāja-guhya-yogo nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ
||9||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter — entitled '<s>Rāja-vidyā-rāja-guhya-yoga</s>' (The Yoga of the Royal Knowledge and the Royal Secret) — in the blessed <s>Bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, who was the foremost among the supreme renunciants and wandering monks. ||9||

children.text: BhG 10
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 10

children.text: atha vibhūti-yogo nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: The Tenth Chapter — entitled '<s>Vibhūti-yoga</s>' (The Yoga of Divine Manifestations)

children.text: (bhagavat-pāda-śrīmac-chaṅkarācārya-kṛta-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>)

children.text: saptame 'dhyāye bhagavatas tattvaṃ vibhūtayaś ca prakāśitāḥ, navame ca | athedānīṃ yeṣu yeṣu bhāveṣu cintyo bhagavāṃs te te bhāvā vaktavyāḥ | tattvaṃ ca bhagavato vaktavyam uktam api, durvijñeyatvāt, ity ataḥ śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] In the seventh chapter, the truth of the Lord and his <s>vibhūtis</s> (divine manifestations) were revealed, and also in the ninth chapter. Now, those entities in which the Lord is to be contemplated must be stated. And the truth of the Lord, though already stated, being difficult to comprehend, must be stated again. Therefore the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: bhūya eva mahā-bāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: Once more, O mighty-armed one, hear my supreme word,

children.text: yat te 'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hita-kāmyayā ||BhG_10.1||
children.translated_text: which I shall speak to you who are delighted [by it], out of a desire for your welfare. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.1||

children.text: bhūya eva bhūyaḥ punar he mahābāho sṛṇu me madīyaṃ paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ niratiśaya-vastunaḥ prakāśakaṃ vaco vākyaṃ yat paramaṃ te tubhyaṃ prīyamāṇāya - mad-vacanāt prīyase tvam atīvāmṛtam iva piban, tataḥ - vakṣyāmi hita-kāmyayā hitecchayā ||BhGS_10.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Once more' (<s>bhūya eva</s>), i.e., again — O mighty-armed one, hear my, i.e., mine, supreme (<s>parama</s>), i.e., exalted, word — a statement that reveals the unsurpassed reality — which supreme [word] I shall speak to you who are delighted — you delight greatly in my words, as if drinking nectar — therefore — out of a desire for your welfare (<s>hita-kāmyayā</s>), out of a wish for your good, I shall speak. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.1||

children.text: kim-artham ahaṃ vakṣyāmīty ata āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For what reason shall I speak? He says:

children.text: na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know my origin;

children.text: aham ādir hi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ||BhG_10.2||
children.translated_text: for I am the source of the gods and the great sages in every respect. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.2||

children.text: na me vidur na jānanti sura-gaṇā brahmādayaḥ | kiṃ te na viduḥ ? mama prabhavaṃ prabhāvaṃ prabhu-śakty-atiśayam, athavā prabhavaṃ prabhavanam utpattim | nāpi maharṣayo bhṛgv-ādayo viduḥ | kasmāt te na vidur ity ucyate - aham ādiḥ kāraṇaṃ hi yasmād devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ ||BhGS_10.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'They do not know' — the hosts of gods (<s>suragaṇas</s>), <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, do not know. What do they not know? My origin (<s>prabhava</s>), i.e., my power, the superabundance of lordly power. Or alternatively, <s>prabhava</s> means 'coming into being,' i.e., origin. Nor do the great sages (<s>maharṣis</s>) such as <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others know. Why do they not know? This is stated: because I am the source (<s>ādi</s>), i.e., the cause, of the gods and the great sages in every respect, in all ways. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.2||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: yo mām ajam anādiṃ ca vetti loka-maheśvaram |
children.translated_text: He who knows me as unborn, beginningless, the great Lord of the worlds —

children.text: asaṃmūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate ||BhG_10.3||
children.translated_text: that one, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.3||

children.text: yaḥ mām ajam anādiṃ ca, yasmāt aham ādir devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca, na mamānyaḥ ādiḥ vidyate | ato 'ham ajo 'nādi ca | anāditvam ajatve hetuḥ, taṃ mām ajam anādiṃ ca yo vetti vijānāti lokamaheśvaraṃ lokānāṃ mahāntam īśvaraṃ turīyam ajñānatatkāryavarjitam asaṃmūḍhaḥ saṃmohavarjitaḥ saḥ matryeṣu manuṣyeṣu, sarvapāpaiḥ sarveḥ pāpair mati-pūrvāmatipūrva-kṛtaiḥ pramucyate pramokṣyate ||BhGS_10.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] He who [knows] me as unborn (<s>aja</s>) and beginningless (<s>anādi</s>) — since I am the source of the gods and the great sages, there is no other source of me; therefore I am unborn and beginningless. Beginninglessness is the reason for being unborn. He who knows me, who am unborn and beginningless, as the great Lord of the worlds (<s>loka-maheśvara</s>), i.e., the great sovereign of the worlds — the fourth (<s>turīya</s>) [state], devoid of ignorance and its effects — that one, undeluded (<s>asaṃmūḍha</s>), i.e., free from delusion, among mortals, i.e., among human beings, is freed from all sins — all sins committed intentionally and unintentionally — is liberated. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.3||

children.text: itaś cāhaṃ maheśvaro lokānām -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And for this reason too I am the great Lord of the worlds —

children.text: buddhir jñānam asaṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, patience, truthfulness, self-control, tranquility,

children.text: sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo 'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayam eva ca ||BhG_10.4||
children.translated_text: pleasure, pain, becoming, non-becoming, fear, and fearlessness — ||<s>BhG</s> 10.4||

children.text: buddhir antaḥ-karaṇasya sūkṣmādy-arthāvabodhana-sāmarthyam, tadvantaṃ buddhimān iti hi vadanti | jñānam ātmādi-padārthānām avabodhaḥ | asaṃmohaḥ pratyutpanneṣu boddhavyeṣu viveka-pūrvikā pravṛttiḥ | kṣamā ākruṣṭasya tāḍitasya vāvikṛta-cittatā | satyaṃ yathā-dṛṣṭasya yathā-śrutasya cātmānubhavasya para-buddhi-saṃkrāntaye tathaivoucāryamāṇā vāk satyam ucyate | damo bāhyendriyopaśamaḥ | śamo 'ntaḥ-karaṇasyopaśamaḥ | sukham āhlādaḥ | duḥkhaṃ santāpaḥ | bhava udbhavaḥ | abhāvas tad-viparyayaḥ | bhayaṃ ca trāsaḥ, abhayam eva ca tad-viparītam ||BhGS_10.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Buddhi</s>' (intelligence) — the capacity of the inner faculty to comprehend subtle and other objects; one who possesses it is called 'intelligent' (<s>buddhimān</s>). '<s>Jñāna</s>' (knowledge) — the understanding of realities such as the Self etc. '<s>Asaṃmoha</s>' (freedom from delusion) — proceeding with discrimination when confronting matters that require understanding. '<s>Kṣamā</s>' (patience) — the unperturbed state of mind when reviled or struck. '<s>Satya</s>' (truthfulness) — speech that expresses one's experience of what has been seen and heard, communicated accurately for the conveyance to another's understanding — that is called truth. '<s>Dama</s>' (self-control) — the restraint of the external senses. '<s>Śama</s>' (tranquility) — the restraint of the inner faculty. '<s>Sukha</s>' (pleasure) — delight. '<s>Duḥkha</s>' (pain) — anguish. '<s>Bhava</s>' (becoming) — origination. '<s>Abhāva</s>' — the opposite of that [i.e., non-becoming]. '<s>Bhaya</s>' (fear) — fright. And '<s>abhaya</s>' (fearlessness) — the opposite of that. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.4||

children.text: ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭis tapo dānaṃ yaśo 'yaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy —

children.text: bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ ||BhG_10.5||
children.translated_text: these various states of beings arise from me alone. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.5||

children.text: ahiṃsāpīḍā prāṇinām | samatā sama-cittatā | tuṣṭiḥ saṃtoṣaḥ paryāpta-buddhir lābheṣu | tapa indriya-saṃyama-pūrvakaṃ śarīra-pīḍānam | dānaṃ yathā-śakti saṃvibhāgaḥ | yaśo dharma-nimittā kīrtiḥ | ayaśas tv adharma-nimittā kīrtiḥ | bhavanti bhāvā yathoktā buddhy-ādayo bhūtānāṃ prāṇināṃ matta eveśvarāt pṛthag-vidhāḥ nānā-vidhāḥ sva-karmānurūpeṇa ||BhGS_10.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Ahiṃsā</s>' (non-violence) — not causing pain to living beings. '<s>Samatā</s>' (equanimity) — evenness of mind. '<s>Tuṣṭi</s>' (contentment) — satisfaction, the sense of having enough in one's gains. '<s>Tapas</s>' (austerity) — bodily mortification preceded by sense-restraint. '<s>Dāna</s>' (charity) — sharing according to one's ability. '<s>Yaśas</s>' (fame) — renown arising from <s>dharma</s>. '<s>Ayaśas</s>' (infamy) — renown arising from <s>adharma</s>. These states — the aforementioned [qualities] beginning with intelligence — of beings, i.e., of living creatures — arise from me alone, from the Lord, in their various forms, according to their respective <s>karmas</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.5||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavas tathā |
children.translated_text: The seven great sages and the four ancient <s>Manus</s>,

children.text: mad-bhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ ||BhG_10.6||
children.translated_text: endowed with my nature, born of my mind — from them are these creatures in the world. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.6||

children.text: maharṣayaḥ sapta bhṛgv-ādayaḥ pūrve 'tīta-kāla-saṃbandhinaḥ, catvāro manavas tathā sāvarṇā iti prasiddhāḥ | te ca mad-bhāvā mad-gata-bhāvanā vaiṣṇavena sāmarthyena upetāḥ | mānasā manasaivotpāditā mayā jātā utpannāḥ | yeṣāṃ manūnāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sṛṣṭir loka imāḥ sthāvara-jaṅgama-lakṣaṇāḥ prajāḥ ||BhGS_10.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The seven great sages (<s>maharṣis</s>) — <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others — 'ancient' (<s>pūrve</s>), i.e., belonging to a former time; and the four <s>Manus</s> likewise — known as the <s>Sāvarṇas</s>. And they are 'endowed with my nature' (<s>mad-bhāva</s>), i.e., endowed with contemplation directed toward me, possessed of <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> power. 'Born of my mind' (<s>mānasā</s>) — produced by my mind alone, i.e., brought into being [by me]. From these <s>Manus</s> and great sages — their creation — are these creatures in the world, characterized as immobile and mobile beings. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.6||

children.text: etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who knows in truth this glory and <s>yoga</s> of mine —

children.text: so 'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||BhG_10.7||
children.translated_text: that one is united with unwavering <s>yoga</s>; there is no doubt about this. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.7||

children.text: etāṃ yathoktāṃ vibhūtiṃ vistāraṃ yogaṃ ca yuktiṃ cātmano ghaṭanam, athavā yogaiśvarya-sāmarthyaṃ sarva-jñatvaṃ yoga-jaṃ yoga ucyate, mama madīyaṃ yogaṃ yo vetti tattvatas tattvena yathāvad ity etat, so 'vikampenāpracalitena yogena samyag darśana-sthairya-lakṣaṇena yujyate saṃbadhyate | nātra saṃśayo nāsminn arthe saṃśayo 'sti ||BhGS_10.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'This' — as described — '<s>vibhūti</s>' (glory), i.e., expansion, manifestation; and '<s>yoga</s>' — union, the self's connection [with the divine]; or alternatively, the power born of <s>yoga</s>, i.e., the yogic might consisting of omniscience, is called <s>yoga</s>. He who knows mine, i.e., my <s>vibhūti</s> and <s>yoga</s>, in truth (<s>tattvatas</s>), i.e., as they really are — that one is united with unwavering (<s>avikampena</s>), i.e., unshakeable, <s>yoga</s> — characterized by firmness in right vision. There is no doubt about this matter. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.7||

children.text: kīdṛśenāvikampena yogena yujyate ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] With what kind of unwavering <s>yoga</s> is one united? This is stated:

children.text: ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate |
children.translated_text: I am the origin of all; from me everything proceeds;

children.text: iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ ||BhG_10.8||
children.translated_text: knowing this, the wise ones, endowed with devotion, worship me. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.8||

children.text: ahaṃ paraṃ brahma vāsudevākhyaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ prabhava utpattiḥ | matta eva sthiti-nāśa-kriyā-phalopabhoga-lakṣaṇaṃ vikriyā-rūpaṃ sarvaṃ jagat pravartate | ity evaṃ matvā bhajante sevante māṃ budhā avagata-paramārtha-tattvāḥ | bhāva-samanvitā bhāvo bhāvanā paramārtha-tattvābhiniveśas tena samanvitāḥ saṃyuktāḥ ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_10.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] I — the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> called <s>Vāsudeva</s> — am the origin (<s>prabhava</s>), the source, of the entire world. From me alone, in the form of activities such as sustenance, destruction, action, and the experience of fruits — the entire world, in its modified form, proceeds. 'Thus knowing' (<s>iti matvā</s>) — understanding this — the wise ones (<s>budhā</s>), those who have comprehended the ultimate truth, worship me, i.e., serve me. '<s>Bhāva-samanvitā</s>' — <s>bhāva</s> means devotion (<s>bhāvanā</s>), i.e., absorption in the ultimate truth; endowed with (<s>samanvita</s>), i.e., possessed of, that [devotion] — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.8||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: mac-cittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
children.translated_text: With their minds fixed on me, their life-breaths surrendered to me, enlightening one another,

children.text: kathayantaś ca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca ||BhG_10.9||
children.translated_text: and always speaking of me — they are content and they rejoice. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.9||

children.text: mac-cittāḥ, mayi cittaṃ yeṣāṃ te mac-cittāḥ | mad-gata-prāṇāḥ māṃ gatāḥ prāptāś cakṣur-ādayaḥ prāṇā yeṣāṃ te mad-gata-prāṇāḥ | mayy upasaṃhṛta-karaṇāḥ ity arthaḥ | athavā, mad-gata-prāṇāḥ mad-gata-jīvanā ity etat | bodhayanto 'vagamayantaḥ parasparam anyonyam, kathayantaś ca jñāna-bala-vīryādi-dharmair viśiṣṭaṃ mām | tuṣyanti ca paritoṣam upayānti ca ramanti ca ratiṃ ca prāpnuvanti priya-saṃgatyeva ||BhGS_10.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Mac-cittā</s>' — those whose minds (<s>citta</s>) are fixed on me — they are <s>mac-citta</s>. '<s>Mad-gata-prāṇā</s>' — those whose vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>), i.e., the senses beginning with the eyes, have gone to me, i.e., have reached me — they are <s>mad-gata-prāṇā</s>. The meaning is: those who have withdrawn their senses into me. Or alternatively, '<s>mad-gata-prāṇā</s>' means those whose very lives are dedicated to me. 'Enlightening' (<s>bodhayantaḥ</s>), i.e., making each other understand — one another (<s>parasparam</s>). 'And speaking of' (<s>kathayantaḥ</s>) me, who am distinguished by qualities such as knowledge, power, heroism, etc. They are content (<s>tuṣyanti</s>), i.e., they experience satisfaction; and they rejoice (<s>ramanti</s>), i.e., they experience delight, as if in the company of a beloved. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.9||

children.text: ye yathoktaiḥ prakārair bhajante māṃ bhaktāḥ santaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those who worship me as devotees in the aforementioned ways —

children.text: teṣāṃ satata-yuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prīti-pūrvakam |
children.translated_text: To those who are constantly united, who worship me with love,

children.text: dadāmi buddhi-yogaṃ taṃ yena mām upayānti te ||BhG_10.10||
children.translated_text: I give that <s>buddhi-yoga</s> (yoga of understanding) by which they come to me. ||<s>BhG</s> 10.10||

children.text: teṣāṃ satata-yuktānāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ nivṛtta-sarva-bāhyaiṣaṇānāṃ bhajatāṃ sevamānānām | kim arthitvādinā kāraṇena ? nety āha - -prīti-pūrvakaṃ prītiḥ snehas tat-pūrvakaṃ māṃ bhajatām ity arthaḥ | dadāmi prayacchāmi buddhi-yogaṃ buddhiḥ samyag darśanaṃ mat-tattva-viṣayaṃ tena yogo buddhi-yogas taṃ buddhi-yogam, yena buddhi-yogena samyag darśana-lakṣaṇena māṃ parameśvaram ātma-bhūtam ātmatvena upayānti pratipadyante | ke ? te ye mac-cittatvādi-prakārair māṃ bhajante ||BhGS_10.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] To those who are constantly united (<s>satata-yukta</s>), i.e., ever devoted, who have turned away from all external pursuits — who are worshipping, i.e., serving [me]. By what motivation? Not through self-interest, he says — 'with love' (<s>prīti-pūrvakam</s>), i.e., out of affection, with love as the motive — to those who worship me — this is the meaning. I give (<s>dadāmi</s>), i.e., I bestow, <s>buddhi-yoga</s> — <s>buddhi</s> means right vision pertaining to my true nature; the <s>yoga</s> with that [right vision] is <s>buddhi-yoga</s> — that <s>buddhi-yoga</s>. By which <s>buddhi-yoga</s> — characterized by right vision — they come to me, i.e., they attain me, the Supreme Lord, as their very Self. Who? Those who worship me in the ways described, such as having their minds fixed on me etc. ||<s>BhGS</s> 10.10||

children.text: kim-artham kasya vā tvat-prāpti-pratibandha-hetor nāśakaṃ buddhi-yogaṃ teṣāṃ tvad-bhaktānāṃ dadāsi ? ity apekṣāyām āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For what purpose, or for the destruction of what obstacle to attaining You, do You give the yoga of understanding (<s>buddhi-yoga</s>) to those devotees of Yours? In response to this expectation, He says:

children.text: teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñāna-jaṃ tamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for them alone, I, dwelling within their being,

children.text: nāśayāmy ātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā ||BhG_10.11||
children.translated_text: destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the luminous lamp of knowledge. // <s>BhG</s> 10.11 //

children.text: teṣām eva kathaṃ nu nāma śreyaḥ syāt ity anukampārthaṃ dayā-hetor aham ajñāna-jam avivekato jātaṃ mithyā-pratyaya-lakṣaṇaṃ mohāndhakāraṃ tamo nāśayāmi, ātma-bhāva-stha ātmano bhāvo 'ntaḥ-karaṇāśayas tasminn eva sthitaḥ san jñāna-dīpena viveka-pratyaya-rūpeṇa bhakti-prasāda-snehābhiṣiktena mad-bhāvanābhiniveśa-vāteritena brahmacaryādi-sādhana-saṃskāra-vat-prajñāvartinā viraktāntaḥ-karaṇādhāreṇa viṣaya-vyāvṛtta-citta-rāga-dveṣākaluṣita-nivātāpavaraka-sthena nitya-pravṛttaikāgrya-dhyāna-janita-samyag-darśana-bhāsvatā jñāna-dīpenety arthaḥ ||BhGS_10.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For them alone — [thinking] 'How indeed may their welfare come about?' — out of compassion, out of mercy, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance, i.e., the delusion-darkness that has arisen from lack of discrimination, characterized by false cognition. Dwelling within their being (<s>ātma-bhāva-stha</s>) — the being of the self is the inner organ, the seat of the mind; abiding therein. With the lamp of knowledge — having the form of discriminative cognition, anointed with the oil of devotion's grace, set in motion by the wind of absorption in meditation upon Me, equipped with the wick of the intellect refined by the impressions of the means [such as] <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and the rest, placed on the stand of a dispassionate inner organ, sheltered in the windless chamber of a mind withdrawn from sense-objects and unstained by desire and aversion, luminous through right vision generated by the one-pointed meditation that is constantly engaged — [such is] the lamp of knowledge — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.11 //

children.text: yathoktāṃ bhagavato vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca śrutvārjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having heard of the Blessed Lord's glory and power as described, <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |
children.translated_text: You are the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Abode, the Supreme Purifier;

children.text: puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyam ādi-devam ajaṃ vibhum ||BhG_10.12||
children.translated_text: the Eternal Divine Person, the Primal God, Unborn, All-Pervading. // <s>BhG</s> 10.12 //

children.text: paraṃ brahma paramātmā paraṃ dhāma paraṃ tejaḥ pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ bhavān | puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ nityaṃ divyaṃ divi bhavam ādi-devaṃ sarva-devānām ādau bhavam ādi-devam ajaṃ vibhuṃ vibhavana-śīlam ||BhGS_10.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — the Supreme Self. 'Supreme Abode' — the supreme light. 'Supreme Purifier' — the supreme means of purification — You are. 'Eternal Divine Person' — the eternal, permanent, divine, i.e., celestial, Person. 'Primal God' — the God who exists before all [other] gods. 'Unborn' — without birth. 'All-Pervading' (<s>vibhu</s>) — of a nature that pervades all. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.12 //

children.text: īdṛśam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [You are] of such a nature —

children.text: āhus tvām ṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣir nāradas tathā |
children.translated_text: All the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) declare this of You, as does the divine sage <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me ||BhG_10.13||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Asita</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Vyāsa</s>; and You Yourself tell me so. // <s>BhG</s> 10.13 //

children.text: āhuḥ kathayanti tvām ṛṣayo vasiṣṭhādayaḥ sarve devarṣir nāradas tathā | asito devalo 'pi evam evāha, vyāsaś ca, svayaṃ caiva tvaṃ ca bravīṣi me ||BhGS_10.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Declare' — proclaim — of You: the sages, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others, all [of them]; the divine sage <s>Nārada</s> likewise. <s>Asita</s> and <s>Devala</s> too say the same, and <s>Vyāsa</s> as well; and You Yourself tell me so. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.13 //

children.text: sarvam etad ṛtaṃ manye yan māṃ vadasi keśava |
children.translated_text: I hold all this to be true, what You tell me, O <s>Keśava</s>;

children.text: na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṃ vidur devā na dānavāḥ ||BhG_10.14||
children.translated_text: for neither the gods nor the demons know Your manifestation, O Blessed Lord. // <s>BhG</s> 10.14 //

children.text: sarvam etad yathoktam ṛṣibhis tvayā caitad ṛtaṃ satyam eva manye, yan māṃ prati vadasi bhāṣase he keśava | na hi te tava bhagavan vyaktiṃ prabhavaṃ vidur na devā na dānavāḥ ||BhGS_10.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] All this, as stated by the sages and by You — I hold this to be true, to be real, that which You tell me, O <s>Keśava</s>. For, O Blessed Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know Your manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>), Your power of appearance. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.14 //

children.text: yatas tvaṃ devādīnām ādiḥ, ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since You are the origin of the gods and others, therefore —

children.text: svayam evātmanātmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama |
children.translated_text: You alone know Yourself by Yourself, O Supreme Person,

children.text: bhūta-bhāvana bhūteśa deva-deva jagatpate ||BhG_10.15||
children.translated_text: O Creator of Beings, O Lord of Beings, O God of Gods, O Master of the Universe! // <s>BhG</s> 10.15 //

children.text: svayam eva ātmanātmānaṃ vettha jānāsi tvaṃ niratiśaya-jñānaiśvarya-balādi-śaktimantam īśvaraṃ | puruṣottama ! bhūtāni bhāvayatīti bhūta-bhāvanaḥ | he bhūtabhāvana ! bhūteśa ! bhūtānām īśitaḥ ! he deva-deva ! jagat-pate ! ||BhGS_10.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] You alone, by Yourself, know Yourself — [as one] possessed of unsurpassed power of knowledge, lordship, strength, and the like — the Lord. O Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>)! 'Creator of Beings' (<s>Bhūta-bhāvana</s>) — He who causes beings to exist. O Creator of Beings! 'Lord of Beings' (<s>Bhūteśa</s>) — the ruler of beings! O God of Gods (<s>Deva-deva</s>)! O Master of the Universe (<s>Jagat-pate</s>)! // <s>BhGS</s> 10.15 //

children.text: vaktum arhasy aśeṣeṇa divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Please describe without remainder Your divine self-manifestations,

children.text: yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṃs tvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi ||BhG_10.16||
children.translated_text: by which manifestations You pervade these worlds and abide [in them]. // <s>BhG</s> 10.16 //

children.text: vaktuṃ kathayitum arhasy aśeṣeṇa | divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ | ātmano vibhūtayo yās tāḥ vaktum arhasi | yābhir vibhūtibhir ātmano māhātmya-vistarair imān lokān tvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi ||BhGS_10.16||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Please describe, please tell, without remainder. For [Your] divine self-manifestations — the manifestations of Your own self — those You should describe. [Tell] by which manifestations, by which expansions of Your own greatness, You pervade these worlds and abide [in them]. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.16 //

children.text: kathaṃ vidyām ahaṃ yogiṃs tvāṃ sadā paricintayan |
children.translated_text: How may I know You, O <s>Yogin</s>, by constantly meditating [upon You]?

children.text: keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo 'si bhagavan mayā ||BhG_10.17||
children.translated_text: In what various forms, O Blessed Lord, are You to be contemplated by me? // <s>BhG</s> 10.17 //

children.text: kathaṃ vidyāṃ vijānīyām ahaṃ he yogin tvāṃ sadā paricintayan | keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu vastuṣu cintyo 'si dhyeyo 'si bhagavan mayā ||BhGS_10.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How may I know — how may I understand — You, O <s>Yogin</s>, by constantly meditating upon You? And in what various forms — in what various entities — are You to be contemplated, to be meditated upon, by me, O Blessed Lord? // <s>BhGS</s> 10.17 //

children.text: vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana |
children.translated_text: Tell me again in detail of Your yoga-power and Your manifestations, O <s>Janārdana</s>;

children.text: bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptir hi śṛṇvato nāsti me 'mṛtam ||BhG_10.18||
children.translated_text: for I am never sated hearing Your nectar[-like words]. // <s>BhG</s> 10.18 //

children.text: vistareṇātmano yogaṃ yogaiśvarya-śakti-viśeṣaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca vistaraṃ dhyeya-padārthānāṃ he janārdana, ardater gati-karmaṇo rūpam, asurāṇāṃ deva-pratipakṣa-bhūtānāṃ janānāṃ narakādi-gamayitṛtvāt janārdano 'bhyudaya-niḥśreyasa-puruṣārtha-prayojanaṃ sarvair janair yācyate iti vā | bhūyaḥ pūrvam uktam api kathaya | tṛptiḥ paritoṣo hi yasmān nāsti me mama śṛṇvatas tvan-mukha-niḥsṛta-vākyāmṛtam ||BhGS_10.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Tell in detail of Your yoga — the distinctive power of Your lordly yoga — and Your manifestations, the expansion of the objects of meditation, O <s>Janārdana</s>. '<s>Janārdana</s>' — from the root <s>ard</s> meaning 'to go'; because He sends the <s>asuras</s> (demons), who are antagonists of the gods, to hell and other [destinations], He is <s>Janārdana</s>; or because He is implored by all people for the human goals of prosperity and liberation. Tell again — even what was said before. For my satisfaction, my contentment, is never [complete] when hearing the nectar[-like words] flowing from Your mouth. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.18 //

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Well then, I shall tell you of My divine self-manifestations,

children.text: prādhānyataḥ kuru-śreṣṭha nāsty anto vistarasya me ||BhG_10.19||
children.translated_text: but only the chief ones, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>, for there is no end to My extent. // <s>BhG</s> 10.19 //

children.text: hanta idānīṃ te tava divyā divi bhavā ātma-vibhūtayo 'tmano mama vibhūtayo yās tāḥ kathayiṣyāmīty etat | prādhānyato yatra yatra pradhānā yā yā vibhūtis tāṃ tāṃ pradhānāṃ prādhānyataḥ kathayiṣyāmy ahaṃ kuru-śreṣṭha ! aśeṣatas tu varṣa-śatenāpi na śakyā vaktum, yato nāsty anto vistarasya me mama vibhūtīnām ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_10.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Well then' — now — I shall tell you. The divine, i.e., celestial, self-manifestations — the manifestations of My own self — those I shall tell. But only the chief ones (<s>prādhānyataḥ</s>) — whichever manifestation is preeminent in whatever domain, that preeminent one I shall tell, O best of the <s>Kurus</s>! To tell [them] completely, even in a hundred years, would be impossible, because there is no end to the extent of My manifestations — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.19 //

children.text: tatra prathamam eva tāvat sṛṇu -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] There, first of all, hear this —

children.text: aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūtāśaya-sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am the Self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, dwelling in the hearts of all beings;

children.text: aham ādiś ca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānām anta eva ca ||BhG_10.20||
children.translated_text: I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of beings. // <s>BhG</s> 10.20 //

children.text: aham ātmā pratyag-ātmā guḍākeśa, guḍākā nidrā tasyāḥ īśo guḍākeśaḥ, jita-nidra ity arthaḥ | ghana-keśeti vā | sarva-bhūtāśaya-sthitaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām āśaye 'ntar-hṛdi sthito 'ham ātmā pratyag-ātmā nityaṃ dhyeyaḥ | tad-aśaktena cottareṣu bhāveṣu cintyo 'ham | yasmād aham eva ādir bhūtānāṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā madhyaṃ ca sthitir antaḥ pralayaś ca ||BhGS_10.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] I am the Self — the inner Self (<s>pratyag-ātmā</s>). O <s>Guḍākeśa</s> — <s>guḍākā</s> means sleep; its master (<s>īśa</s>) is <s>Guḍākeśa</s> — meaning one who has conquered sleep. Or [it means] one with thick hair. Dwelling in the hearts of all beings — abiding in the heart, the inner recess, of all beings — I am the Self, the inner Self, to be constantly meditated upon. And for one unable to do that, I am to be contemplated in the following forms. Since I alone am the beginning, the cause of beings, and likewise the middle, i.e., their sustenance, and the end, i.e., their dissolution. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.20 //

children.text: evaṃ ca dhyeyo 'ham -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And thus I am to be meditated upon —

children.text: ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇur jyotiṣāṃ ravir aṃśumān |
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Ādityas</s>, I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>; among luminaries, the radiant sun;

children.text: marīcir marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī ||BhG_10.21||
children.translated_text: I am <s>Marīci</s> among the <s>Maruts</s>; among the stars, I am the moon. // <s>BhG</s> 10.21 //

children.text: ādityānāṃ dvādaśānāṃ viṣṇur nāma ādityo 'ham | jyotiṣāṃ raviḥ prakāśayitṝṇām aṃśumān raśmimān | marīcir nāma marutāṃ marud-devatā-bhedānām asmi | nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī candramāḥ ||BhGS_10.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, I am the <s>Āditya</s> named <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Among luminaries — among those that illuminate — [I am] the radiant, i.e., possessed of rays, sun. I am the one named <s>Marīci</s> among the <s>Maruts</s> — among the various classes of <s>Marut</s> deities. Among the stars, I am the moon (<s>śaśī</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 10.21 //

children.text: vedānāṃ sāma-vedo 'smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Among the Vedas, I am the <s>Sāma Veda</s>; among the gods, I am <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>);

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ manaś cāsmi bhūtānām asmi cetanā ||BhG_10.22||
children.translated_text: among the senses, I am the mind; and among beings, I am consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 10.22 //

children.text: vedānāṃ madhye sāma-vedo 'smi | devānāṃ rūdrādityādīnāṃ vāsava indro 'smi | indriyāṇām ekādaśānāṃ cakṣur-ādīnāṃ manaś cāsmi saṃkalpa-vikalpātmakaṃ manaś cāsmi | bhūtānām asmi cetanā kārya-karaṇa-saṃghāte nityābhivyaktā buddhi-vṛttiś cetanā ||BhGS_10.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the Vedas, I am the <s>Sāma Veda</s>. Among the gods — <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and others — I am <s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Indra</s>. Among the eleven senses — the eye and the others — I am the mind, which is of the nature of thought and deliberation. Among beings, I am consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>) — the function of the intellect that is ever manifest in the aggregate of body and sense-organs. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.22 //

children.text: rudrāṇāṃ śaṃkaraś cāsmi vitteśo yakṣa-rakṣasām |
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Rudras</s>, I am <s>Śaṃkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); among the <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, [I am] the Lord of Wealth (<s>Kubera</s>);

children.text: vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇām aham ||BhG_10.23||
children.translated_text: among the <s>Vasus</s>, I am Fire (<s>Pāvaka</s>); and among the peaked mountains, I am <s>Meru</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 10.23 //

children.text: rudrāṇām ekādaśānāṃ śaṃkaraś cāsmi | vitteśaḥ kuvero yakṣa-rakṣasāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ rakṣasāṃ ca | vasūnām aṣṭanāṃ pāvakaś cāsmy agniḥ | meruḥ śikhariṇāṃ śikharavatām aham ||BhGS_10.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, I am <s>Śaṃkara</s>. The Lord of Wealth, <s>Kubera</s>, [I am] among the <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. Among the eight <s>Vasus</s>, I am <s>Pāvaka</s>, i.e., Fire. <s>Meru</s>, among the peaked mountains — those that have peaks — I am. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.23 //

children.text: purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
children.translated_text: Among priests, know Me to be the chief, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>;

children.text: senānīnām ahaṃ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ ||BhG_10.24||
children.translated_text: among generals, I am <s>Skanda</s>; among bodies of water, I am the ocean. // <s>BhG</s> 10.24 //

children.text: purodhasāṃ ca rāja-purohitānāṃ ca mukhyaṃ pradhānaṃ māṃ viddhi he pārtha bṛhaspatim | sa hīndrasyeti mukhyaḥ syāt purodhāḥ | senānīnāṃ senāpatīnām ahaṃ skando deva-senāpatiḥ | sarasāṃ yāni deva-khātāni sarāṃsi teṣāṃ sarasāṃ sāgaro 'smi bhavāmi ||BhGS_10.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among priests — among royal chaplains — know Me to be the chief, the foremost, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>. For he, being [the chaplain] of <s>Indra</s>, would be the chief among chaplains. Among generals — among commanders of armies — I am <s>Skanda</s>, the general of the army of the gods. Among lakes — those that are divinely dug — among those bodies of water, I am the ocean. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.24 //

children.text: maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgur ahaṃ girām asmy ekam akṣaram |
children.translated_text: Among the great sages, I am <s>Bhṛgu</s>; among utterances, I am the single syllable [<s>Om</s>];

children.text: yajñānāṃ japa-yajño 'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ ||BhG_10.25||
children.translated_text: among sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of silent repetition (<s>japa-yajña</s>); among immovable things, the <s>Himālaya</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 10.25 //

children.text: maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgur aham | girāṃ vācāṃ pada-lakṣaṇānām ekam akṣaram oṃkāro 'smi | yajñānāṃ japa-yajño 'smi, sthāvarāṇāṃ sthiti-matāṃ himālayaḥ ||BhGS_10.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the great sages, I am <s>Bhṛgu</s>. Among utterances — among words characterized by syllables — I am the single syllable <s>Oṃkāra</s>. Among sacrifices, I am the sacrifice of silent repetition. Among immovable things — those that are stationary — [I am] the <s>Himālaya</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.25 //

children.text: aśvatthaḥ sarva-vṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
children.translated_text: Among all trees, [I am] the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree); and among the divine sages, <s>Nārada</s>;

children.text: gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ ||BhG_10.26||
children.translated_text: among the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>; among the perfected ones (<s>Siddhas</s>), the sage <s>Kapila</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 10.26 //

children.text: aśvatthaḥ sarva-vṛkṣāṇām, devarṣīṇāṃ ca nārado devāḥ eva santaḥ ṛṣitvaṃ prāptāḥ mantra-darśitvāt te devarṣayaḥ | teṣāṃ nārado 'smi | gandharvāṇāṃ citraratho nāma gandharvo 'smi | siddhānāṃ janmanaiva dharma-jñāna-vairāgyaiśvaryātiśayaṃ prāptānāṃ kapilo muniḥ ||BhGS_10.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [I am] the <s>Aśvattha</s> among all trees. Among the divine sages — those who, being gods, have attained the status of sages through their vision of <s>mantras</s> — they are the divine sages; among them, I am <s>Nārada</s>. Among the <s>Gandharvas</s>, I am the <s>Gandharva</s> named <s>Citraratha</s>. Among the <s>Siddhas</s> — those who from birth have attained supreme excellence of <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty — [I am] the sage <s>Kapila</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.26 //

children.text: uccaiḥśravasam aśvānāṃ viddhi mām amṛtodbhavam |
children.translated_text: Among horses, know Me as <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, born from the churning of nectar;

children.text: airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam ||BhG_10.27||
children.translated_text: among lordly elephants, <s>Airāvata</s>; and among men, the king. // <s>BhG</s> 10.27 //

children.text: ucaiḥśravasam a vānāṃ ucaiḥśravāḥ nāmā varājas taṃ māṃ viddhi vijānīhy amṛtodbhavam amṛta-nimitta-mathanodbhavam | airāvatam irāvatyāḥ apatyaṃ gajendrāṇāṃ hastīśvarāṇām, tam māṃ viddhīty anuvartate | narāṇāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ narādhipaṃ rājānaṃ māṃ viddhi jānīhi ||BhGS_10.27||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among horses, know Me to be <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> — the celebrated horse by that name — born from the churning for nectar, i.e., arising from the churning occasioned by the nectar. <s>Airāvata</s> — the offspring of <s>Irāvatī</s> — among lordly elephants, among the lords of elephants; know that to be Me — this is carried over [from the preceding]. Among men — among human beings — [know Me to be] the king, the ruler. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.27 //

children.text: āyudhānām ahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnām asmi kāma-dhuk |
children.translated_text: Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, I am <s>Kāmadhuk</s> (the wish-fulfilling cow);

children.text: prajanaś cāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||BhG_10.28||
children.translated_text: I am <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) as the progenitor; and among serpents, I am <s>Vāsuki</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 10.28 //

children.text: āyudhānām ahaṃ vajraṃ dadhīcy-asthi-saṃbhavam | dhenūnāṃ dogdhrīṇām asmi kāma-dhuk vasiṣṭhasya sarva-kāmānāṃ dogdhrī, sāmānyā vā kāma-dhuk | prajanaḥ prajanayitāsmi kandarpaḥ kāmaḥ | sarpāṇāṃ sarpa-bhedānām asmi vāsukiḥ sarpa-rājaḥ ||BhGS_10.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt, born from the bones of <s>Dadhīci</s>. Among cows — among milch cows — I am <s>Kāmadhuk</s>, the cow of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> that yields all desires; or it is the common wish-fulfilling cow. I am the progenitor — the one who causes procreation — <s>Kandarpa</s>, i.e., Desire (Kāma). Among serpents — among the varieties of serpents — I am <s>Vāsuki</s>, the king of serpents. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.28 //

children.text: anantaś cāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasām aham |
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Nāgas</s>, I am <s>Ananta</s>; among aquatic beings, I am <s>Varuṇa</s>;

children.text: pitṝṇām aryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatām aham ||BhG_10.29||
children.translated_text: among the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>), I am <s>Aryaman</s>; among controllers, I am <s>Yama</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 10.29 //

children.text: anantaś cāsmi nāgānāṃ nāga-viśeṣāṇāṃ nāgarājaś cāsmi | varuṇo yādasām aham ab-devatānāṃ rājāham | pitṝṇām aryamā nāma pitṛ-rājaś cāsmi | yamaḥ saṃyamatāṃ saṃyamanaṃ kurvatām aham ||BhGS_10.29||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Among the <s>Nāgas</s> — among the various types of <s>Nāgas</s> — I am <s>Ananta</s>, the king of <s>Nāgas</s>. <s>Varuṇa</s>, among aquatic beings — among the deities of water — I am the king. Among the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>), I am the one named <s>Aryaman</s>, the king of the <s>Pitṛs</s>. <s>Yama</s>, among those who exercise control — among those who restrain — I am. // <s>BhGS</s> 10.29 //

children.text: prahlādaś cāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Daityas</s> (demons), I am <s>Prahlāda</s>; among reckoners, I am Time (<s>Kāla</s>);

children.text: mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro 'haṃ vainateyaś ca pakṣiṇām ||BhG_10.30||
children.translated_text: among beasts, I am the king of beasts (the lion); and among birds, <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 10.30 //

children.text: prahlādo nāmaś cāsmi daityānāṃ diti-vaṃśyānām | kālaḥ kalayatāṃ kalanaṃ gaṇanaṃ kurvatām aham | mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendraḥ siṃho vyāghro vāham | vainateyaś ca garutmān vinatā-sutaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ patatriṇām ||BhGS_10.30||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] I am <s>Prahlāda</s> among the <s>Daityas</s> (descendants of <s>Diti</s>). I am <s>Kāla</s> (Time) among those who reckon — those who count and calculate. Among animals, I am <s>Mṛgendra</s> (the king of beasts) — the lion or tiger. And <s>Vainateya</s>, <s>Garutmān</s> (son of <s>Vinatā</s>), I am among birds, among winged creatures.

children.text: pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śastra-bhṛtām aham |
children.translated_text: Among purifiers I am the wind; among weapon-bearers I am <s>Rāma</s>;

children.text: jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraś cāsmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī ||BhG_10.31||
children.translated_text: among aquatic creatures I am the <s>Makara</s> (crocodile); and among rivers I am the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges).

children.text: pavano vāyuḥ pavatāṃ pāvayitaṝṇām asmi | rāmaḥ śastra-bhṛtām ahaṃ śastrāṇāṃ dhārayitṝṇāṃ dāśarathiḥ rāmo 'ham | jhaṣāṇāṃ matsyādīnāṃ makaro nāma jāti-viśeṣo 'ham | srotasāṃ sravantīnām asmi jāhnavī gaṅgā ||BhGS_10.31||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] <s>Pavana</s> means <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); I am among the purifiers, those who purify. I am <s>Rāma</s> among weapon-bearers — among those who wield weapons, I am <s>Rāma</s>, the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>. Among <s>jhaṣas</s> (fish and other aquatic creatures), I am the particular species called <s>Makara</s>. Among <s>srotases</s> (flowing rivers), I am <s>Jāhnavī</s>, the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: sargāṇām ādir antaś ca madhyaṃ caivāham arjuna |
children.translated_text: Of creations I am the beginning, the end, and also the middle, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatām aham ||BhG_10.32||
children.translated_text: among sciences I am the science of the Self (<s>adhyātma-vidyā</s>); of those who debate, I am <s>vāda</s> (reasoned argument).

children.text: sargāṇāṃ sṛṣṭīnām ādir antaś ca madhyaṃ caivāham utpatti-sthiti-layā aham arjuna | bhūtānāṃ jīvādhiṣṭhitānām eva ādir antaś cety ādy uktam upakrame, iha tu sarvasyaiva sarga-mātrasyeti viśeṣaḥ | adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṃ mokṣārthatvāt pradhānam asmi | vādo 'rtha-nirṇaya-hetutvāt pravadatāṃ pradhānam, ataḥ so 'ham asmi | pravaktṛ-dvāreṇa vadana-bhedānām eva vāda-jalpa-vitaṇḍānām iha grahaṇaṃ pravadatām iti ||BhGS_10.32||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Of <s>sargas</s> (creations), I am the beginning, end, and also the middle — I am the origination, sustenance, and dissolution, O <s>Arjuna</s>. Regarding beings presided over by individual souls, it was said at the outset that I am the beginning and the end, etc.; but here the distinction is that it refers to all creation whatsoever. Among sciences, <s>adhyātma-vidyā</s> (the science of the Self) is preeminent because it serves the purpose of liberation; hence I am that. <s>Vāda</s> (reasoned argument) is preeminent among those who discourse because it is the means for ascertaining truth; therefore I am that. Through the mention of speakers, the different modes of discourse — <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil) — are indicated here by the word 'among those who discourse.'

children.text: akṣarāṇām akāro 'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca |
children.translated_text: Among letters I am the letter 'A'; and among compounds I am the <s>Dvandva</s> (copulative compound);

children.text: aham evākṣayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṃ viśvato-mukhaḥ ||BhG_10.33||
children.translated_text: I alone am imperishable Time; I am the Creator facing in all directions.

children.text: akṣarāṇāṃ varṇānām akāro varṇo 'smi | dvandvaḥ samāso 'smi sāmāsikasya ca samāsa-samūhasya | kiṃ cāham evākṣayaḥ kālaḥ prasiddhaḥ kṣaṇādy-ākhyaḥ, athavā parameśvaraḥ kālasyāpi kālo 'smi | dhātāhaṃ karma-phalasya vidhātā sarva-jagato viśvato-mukhaḥ sarvato-mukhaḥ ||BhGS_10.33||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Among <s>akṣaras</s> (letters), I am the letter 'A' among the vowels and consonants. Among <s>sāmāsika</s> (the group of compounds), I am the <s>Dvandva</s> compound. Moreover, I alone am imperishable <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the well-known one designated by moments and so forth; or alternatively, I am the Supreme Lord who is the Time even of Time itself. I am the <s>Dhātā</s> (Dispenser), the ordainer of the fruits of action for the entire universe, <s>viśvatomukha</s> — facing in all directions.

children.text: mṛtyuḥ sarva-haraś cāham udbhavaś ca bhaviṣyatām |
children.translated_text: I am all-devouring Death, and I am the prosperity of those who are yet to be;

children.text: kīrtiḥ śrīr vāk ca nārīṇāṃ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ||BhG_10.34||
children.translated_text: among feminine qualities I am fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and patience.

children.text: mṛtyur dvividho dhanādi-haraḥ prāṇa-haraś ca | tatra yaḥ prāṇa-haraḥ, sa sarva-hara ucyate | so 'ham ity arthaḥ | athavā, para īśvaraḥ pralaye sarva-haraṇāt sarva-haraḥ, so 'ham | udbhava utkarṣaḥ abhyudayas tat-prāpti-hetuś cāham | keṣām ? bhaviṣyatāṃ bhāvi-kalyāṇānām, utkarṣa-prāpti-yogyānām ity arthaḥ | kīrtiḥ śrīḥ vāk ca nārīṇāṃ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ity etā uttamāḥ strīṇām aham asmi, yāsām ābhāsa-mātra-saṃbandhenāpi lokaḥ kṛtārtham ātmānaṃ manyate ||BhGS_10.34||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Death is of two kinds: one that takes away wealth and such, and one that takes away life. Of these, the one that takes away life is called 'all-devouring' (<s>sarva-hara</s>); that I am — this is the meaning. Alternatively, the Supreme Lord, because He takes away everything at the time of dissolution, is <s>sarva-hara</s> (all-devouring); that I am. <s>Udbhava</s> means excellence, prosperity, and I am the cause for attaining that. Of whom? Of those who are yet to come (<s>bhaviṣyatām</s>) — those destined for future auspiciousness, meaning those who are worthy of attaining excellence. Fame, fortune, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and patience — these excellent qualities among women, I am; by whose mere semblance of association the world considers itself fulfilled.

children.text: bṛhat-sāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasām aham |
children.translated_text: Likewise, among the <s>Sāmans</s> I am the <s>Bṛhat-sāma</s>; among meters I am <s>Gāyatrī</s>;

children.text: māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo 'ham ṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ ||BhG_10.35||
children.translated_text: among months I am <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>; among seasons I am the flower-bearer (spring).

children.text: bṛhat-sāma tathā sāmnāṃ pradhānam asmi | gāyatrī cchandasām ahaṃ gāyatry-ādi-cchando-viśiṣṭānām ṛcāṃ gāyatrī ṛg aham asmīty arthaḥ | māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo 'ham, ṛtūnāṃ kusumākaro vasantaḥ ||BhGS_10.35||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Among the <s>Sāmans</s>, I am the <s>Bṛhat-sāma</s>, which is preeminent. Among <s>chandas</s> (meters), I am <s>Gāyatrī</s> — meaning among the Ṛk verses distinguished by meters such as <s>Gāyatrī</s> and others, I am the Ṛk verse in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter. Among months I am <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>; among seasons I am <s>Kusumākara</s> (spring, the flower-bearer).

children.text: dyūtaṃ chalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham |
children.translated_text: I am the gambling of the deceitful; I am the splendor of the splendid;

children.text: jayo 'smi vyavasāyo 'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatām aham ||BhG_10.36||
children.translated_text: I am victory; I am resolve; I am the <s>sattva</s> (goodness) of those endowed with <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: dyūtam akṣa-devanādi-lakṣaṇaṃ chalayatāṃ chalasya kartṝṇām asmi | tejasvināṃ tejo 'ham | jayo 'smi jetṝṇām | vyavasāyo 'smi vyavasāyinām | sattvaṃ sattvavatāṃ sāttvikānām aham ||BhGS_10.36||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] <s>Dyūta</s> (gambling), characterized by dice-play and the like, I am among those who practice deceit — among those who employ trickery. I am the splendor of the splendid. I am the victory of the victorious. I am the resolve of the resolute. I am the <s>sattva</s> (goodness) of those endowed with <s>sattva</s>, of those who are <s>sāttvika</s> (virtuous).

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo 'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> I am <s>Vāsudeva</s>; among the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> I am <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>;

children.text: munīnām apy ahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśanā kaviḥ ||BhG_10.37||
children.translated_text: among sages I am <s>Vyāsa</s>; and among seers I am the seer <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ yādavānāṃ vāsudevo 'smy ayam evāhaṃ tvatsakhaḥ | pāṇḍāvānāṃ dhanaṃjayas tvam eva | munīnīṃ mananaśīlānāṃ sarvapadārthajñāninām apy ahaṃ vyāsaḥ, kavīnāṃ ktrāntadarśinām uśanā kavir asmi ||BhGS_10.37||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, the <s>Yādavas</s>, I am <s>Vāsudeva</s> — this very I who am your friend. Among the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s> — you yourself. Among <s>munis</s> (sages), those given to contemplation, who know all things, I am <s>Vyāsa</s>. Among <s>kavis</s> (seers), those who perceive the past and future, I am the seer <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣatām |
children.translated_text: I am the rod of punishment among those who chastise; I am the statesmanship of those who seek victory;

children.text: maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatām aham ||BhG_10.38||
children.translated_text: I am the silence of secrets; and I am the knowledge of the knowledgeable.

children.text: daṇḍo damayatāṃ damayitṝṇām asmy adāntānāṃ damana-kāraḥ | nītir asmi jigīṣatāṃ jetum icchatām | maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ gopyānām | jñānaṃ jñānavatām aham ||BhGS_10.38||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] I am the <s>daṇḍa</s> (rod of punishment) among those who chastise, among those who discipline — the means of subduing the undisciplined. I am the <s>nīti</s> (statesmanship) of those who seek to conquer, of those who desire victory. I am the <s>mauna</s> (silence) of secrets, of things to be kept hidden. I am the knowledge of the knowledgeable.

children.text: yac cāpi sarva-bhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tad aham arjuna |
children.translated_text: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that I am, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram ||BhG_10.39||
children.translated_text: there is no being, moving or unmoving, that can exist without Me.

children.text: yac cāpi sarva-bhūtānāṃ bījaṃ praroha-kāraṇam, tad aham arjuna | prakaraṇopa-saṃhārārthaṃ vibhūti-saṃkṣepam āha - na tad asti bhūtaṃ carācaraṃ caram acaraṃ vā, mayā vinā yat syāt bhavet | mayāpakṛṣṭaṃ parityaktaṃ nirātmakaṃ śūnyaṃ hi tat syāt | ato mad-ātmakaṃ sarvam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_10.39||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And whatever is the seed, the cause of sprouting forth, of all beings — that I am, O <s>Arjuna</s>. For the purpose of concluding the topic, He states a summary of the divine manifestations: there is no being, moving or unmoving — whether mobile or immobile — that could exist without Me. Withdrawn from Me, abandoned by Me, it would be without a Self, void. Therefore, everything has Me as its Self — this is the meaning.

children.text: nānto 'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa |
children.translated_text: There is no end to My divine manifestations, O <s>Parantapa</s> (scorcher of foes);

children.text: eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā ||BhG_10.40||
children.translated_text: but this expansion of My manifestations has been declared by Me merely by way of illustration.

children.text: nānto 'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ vistarāṇāṃ parantapa | na hīśvarasya sarvātmano divyānāṃ vibhūtīnām iyattā śakyā vaktuṃ jñātuṃ vā kenacit | eṣa tūddeśata eka-deśena prokto vibhūter vistaraḥ mayā ||BhGS_10.40||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] There is no end to My divine <s>vibhūtis</s> (manifestations), to their extent, O <s>Parantapa</s>. Indeed, the extent of the divine manifestations of the Lord who is the Self of all cannot be stated or known by anyone. But this expansion of My manifestations has been declared by Me merely by way of illustration, by indicating only a portion.

children.text: yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṃ śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā |
children.translated_text: Whatever being is endowed with glory, grace, or vigor —

children.text: tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo 'ṃśa-saṃbhavam ||BhG_10.41||
children.translated_text: know that to be born from a fragment of My splendor.

children.text: yad yal loke vibhūtimad vibhūti-yuktaṃ sattvaṃ vastu śrīmad ūrjitam eva vā śrīr lakṣmīs tayā sahitam utsāhopetaṃ vā | tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṃ jānīhi mameśvarasya tejo 'ṃśa-saṃbhavaṃ tejaso 'ṃśa eka-deśaḥ saṃbhavo yasya tat tejo 'ṃśa-saṃbhavam ity avagaccha tvam ||BhGS_10.41||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Whatever entity in the world is endowed with <s>vibhūti</s> (glory), possessed of magnificence, or is <s>śrīmat</s> (graced with fortune) — <s>Śrī</s> means <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), accompanied by that — or is <s>ūrjita</s> (vigorous), endowed with energy and enthusiasm — know all that to be born from a fragment of My, the Lord's, splendor. <s>Tejas</s> (splendor), whose <s>aṃśa</s> (fragment) — a portion — is the origin of that; thus it is <s>tejo'ṃśa-saṃbhava</s> (born from a fragment of splendor) — so understand.

children.text: atha vā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna |
children.translated_text: Or rather, what need is there for you to know all this in detail, O <s>Arjuna</s>?

children.text: viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat ||BhG_10.42||
children.translated_text: I stand supporting this entire universe with a single fragment of Myself.

children.text: athavā bahunaitena evam ādinā kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna syāt sāvaśeṣeṇa | aśeṣatas tvam ucyamānam arthaṃ sṛṇu - viṣṭabhya viśeṣataḥ stambhanaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvedaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad ekāṃśenaikāvayavenaika-pādena, sarva-bhūta-svarūpeṇety etat | tathā ca mantra-varṇaḥ - pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtāni [Ṛk 8.4.17.3] iti | sthito 'ham iti ||BhGS_10.42||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Or rather, what need is there for you, O <s>Arjuna</s>, to know all this elaborate detail, which would still leave a remainder? Hear the matter stated in its completeness: having pervaded and firmly established this entire universe with a single fragment, with one part, with one foot — that is, with the form that is the nature of all beings. And so the Vedic verse declares: 'One foot of His are all beings' [<s>Ṛk</s> 8.4.17.3]. Thus I stand.

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrīgovandibhagavatpūjyapāda-
children.translated_text: Thus in the blessed commentary on the <s>Śrīmad Bhagavad Gītā</s>, composed by the revered

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: disciple of the venerable <s>Śrī Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda</s>, the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>,

children.text: daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ends the tenth chapter.

children.text: BhG 11
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s>, Chapter 11

children.text:
athaikādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
viśva-rūpa-darśana-yogaḥ
children.translated_text:
Now begins the eleventh chapter:
<s>Viśvarūpa-darśana-yoga</s> (The Yoga of the Vision of the Cosmic Form)

children.text: (śrī-śaṅkarācārya-bhagavat-pāda-kṛta-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the blessed <s>Śrī Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavatpāda</s>)

children.text: bhagavato vibhūtaya uktāḥ | tatra ca viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat [Gītā 10.42] iti bhagavatābhihitaṃ śrutvā yat jagad-ātma-rūpam, ādyam aiśvaraṃ tat sākṣāt-kartum icchann arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The <s>vibhūtis</s> (divine manifestations) of the Lord have been described. And having heard the Lord's declaration, 'I stand supporting this entire universe with a single fragment of Myself' [<s>Gītā</s> 10.42], <s>Arjuna</s>, desiring to directly perceive that form of the Lord which is the Self of the universe — the primordial, divine form — spoke:

children.text: mad-anugrahāya paramaṃ guhyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam |
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for me, You have spoken the supreme secret known as <s>adhyātma</s> (the science of the Self);

children.text: yat tvayoktaṃ vacas tena moho 'yaṃ vigato mama ||BhG_11.1||
children.translated_text: by that word of Yours, this delusion of mine has departed.

children.text: mad-anugrahāya mamānugrahārthaṃ paramaṃ niratiśayaṃ guhyaṃ gopyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam ātmānātma-viveka-viṣayaṃ yat tvayoktaṃ vaco vākyaṃ tena te vacasā moho 'yaṃ vigato mama | aviveka-buddhir apagatety arthaḥ ||BhGS_11.1||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] 'For my benefit' (<s>mad-anugrahāya</s>) — for the sake of showing grace to me — the supreme, unsurpassed secret, that which is to be kept hidden, designated as <s>adhyātma</s> — pertaining to the discrimination between Self and non-Self — the words that You have spoken, by that speech of Yours, this delusion of mine has departed. The meaning is: the lack of discriminating understanding has been removed.

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā |
children.translated_text: For the origin and dissolution of beings have been heard by me in detail,

children.text: tvattaḥ kamala-patrākṣa māhātmyam api cāvyayam ||BhG_11.2||
children.translated_text: from You, O lotus-eyed one, as also Your imperishable greatness.

children.text: bhava utpattir apyayaḥ pralayas tau bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśaḥ mayā, na saṃkṣepataḥ | tvattas tvat-sakāśāt | kamala-patrākṣa kamalasya patraṃ kamala-patraṃ tadvad akṣiṇī yasya tava sa tvaṃ kamala-patrākṣo, he kamalapatrākṣa ! mahātmano bhāvo māhātmyam api cāvyayam akṣayam | śrutam ity anuvartate ||BhGS_11.2||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] <s>Bhava</s> means origination; <s>apyaya</s> means dissolution — these two, the origin and dissolution of beings, have been heard by me in detail, not merely in summary. From You, from Your presence. O lotus-eyed one (<s>kamala-patrākṣa</s>) — one whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus; O You of lotus-petal eyes! And also Your imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>), undecaying greatness — <s>māhātmya</s>, the quality of being a great soul — has been heard; this is to be supplied.

children.text: evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṃ parameśvara |
children.translated_text: It is so, just as You declare Yourself to be, O Supreme Lord;

children.text: draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṃ puruṣottama ||BhG_11.3||
children.translated_text: yet I desire to see Your divine form, O <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person).

children.text: evam etan nānyathā yathā yena prakāreṇa āttha kathayasi tvam ātmānaṃ parameśvara | tathāpi draṣṭum icchāmi te tava jñānaiśvarya-śakti-bala-vīrya-tejobhiḥ saṃpannam aiśvaraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ rūpaṃ puruṣottama ||BhGS_11.3||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] 'It is so' — not otherwise — 'just as,' in the manner in which You describe Yourself, O Supreme Lord. Nevertheless, I desire to see Your <s>aiśvara</s> (divine, sovereign) form — the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> form endowed with knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, valor, and splendor — O <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: manyase yadi tac chakyaṃ mayā draṣṭum iti prabho |
children.translated_text: If You think it possible for me to see that, O Lord,

children.text: yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānam avyayam ||BhG_11.4||
children.translated_text: then, O Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, reveal to me Your imperishable Self.

children.text: manyase cintayasi yadi mayārjunena tac chakyaṃ draṣṭum iti prabho ! svāmin ! yogeśvara yogino yogās teṣām īśvaro yogeśvaraḥ, he yogeśvara ! yasmād aham atīvārthī draṣṭum, tatas tasmān me mad-arthaṃ tvam ātmānam avyayam ||BhGS_11.4||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] If You consider that it is possible for me, <s>Arjuna</s>, to see that — O <s>Prabhu</s> (Lord), O Master! O <s>Yogeśvara</s> (Lord of Yoga) — the <s>yogins</s> are <s>yogas</s>, and their Lord is <s>Yogeśvara</s>; O Lord of <s>Yoga</s>! Since I am exceedingly desirous of seeing, therefore, for my sake, reveal Your imperishable Self.

children.text: evaṃ codito 'rjunena bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Thus urged by <s>Arjuna</s>, the Lord spoke:

children.text: paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Behold My forms, O <s>Pārtha</s>, by the hundreds and by the thousands,

children.text: nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇākṛtīni ca ||BhG_11.5||
children.translated_text: of various kinds, divine, and of various colors and shapes.

children.text: paśya me pārtha ! rūpāṇi śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ | anekaśa ity arthaḥ | tāni ca nānā-vidhāny aneka-prakārāṇi divi bhavāni divyāny aprākṛtāni nānā-varṇākṛtīni ca nānā vilakṣaṇā nīla-pītādi-prakārā varṇās tathākṛtayaś cāvayava-saṃsthāna-viśeṣo yeṣāṃ rūpāṇāṃ tāni nānā-varṇākṛtīnī ca ||BhGS_11.5||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Behold My forms, O <s>Pārtha</s>, by the hundreds and by the thousands — meaning innumerable.
