And those forms are of various kinds, of many sorts, <s>divya</s> (divine) — supernatural, not of the material world — and of various colors and shapes: <s>varṇa</s> means colors of different kinds such as blue, yellow, and so forth; and <s>ākṛti</s> means the distinctive configurations of limbs; those forms which have such varied colors and shapes are called <s>nānā-varṇākṛtīni</s>.

children.text: paśyādityān vasūn rudrān aśvinau marutas tathā |
children.translated_text: Behold the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> as well;

children.text: bahūny adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata ||BhG_11.6||
children.translated_text: behold many wonders never seen before, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: paśyādityān dvādaśa | vasūn aṣṭau | rudrān ekādaśa | aśvinau dvau | marutaḥ sapta-sapta-gaṇā ye tān | tathā ca bahūny anyāny apy adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi manuṣya-loke tvayā tvatto 'nyena vā kenacit | paśyāścaryāṇy adbhutāni bhārata ||BhGS_11.6||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Behold the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the eight <s>Vasus</s>, the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> — those who are in seven groups of seven. And also behold many other wonders never seen before in the world of mortals, by you or by anyone else. Behold these marvels, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: na kevalam etāvad eva -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Not only this much —

children.text: ihaikasthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sa-carācaram |
children.translated_text: Behold now the entire universe, moving and unmoving, gathered here in one place,

children.text: mama dehe guḍākeśa yac cānyad draṣṭum icchasi ||BhG_11.7||
children.translated_text: in My body, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s> (Conqueror of Sleep), and whatever else you wish to see. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.7||

children.text: ihaika-stham ekasminn eva sthitaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ samastaṃ paśyādya idānīṃ sa-carācaraṃ saha careṇācareṇa ca vartate mama dehe guḍākeśa | yac cānyat jaya-parājayādi | yat śaṅkase, yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyur [Gītā 2.6] iti yat avocaḥ, tad api draṣṭuṃ yadīcchasi ||BhGS_11.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Here in one place' (<s>ihaikastham</s>) — situated in one single [place]; the 'entire universe' (<s>jagat kṛtsnam</s>), i.e., the whole [world] — 'behold now' (<s>paśyādya</s>), i.e., see at this very moment — 'with the moving and the unmoving' (<s>sa-carācaram</s>), i.e., together with that which moves and that which does not move — in My body, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>. 'And whatever else' — such as victory and defeat, etc. What you feared — 'whether we shall conquer, or they shall conquer us' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.6] — what you said, that too, if you wish to see. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.7||

children.text: kiṃ tu -
children.translated_text: However —

children.text: na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭum anenaiva sva-cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: But you are not able to see Me with just these, your own eyes;

children.text: divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram ||BhG_11.8||
children.translated_text: I give you a divine eye — behold My lordly <s>yoga</s>! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.8||

children.text: na tu māṃ viśva-rūpa-dharaṃ śakyase draṣṭum anenaiva prākṛtena sva-cakṣuṣā svakīyena cakṣuṣā | yena tu śakyase draṣṭuṃ divyena, tad divyaṃ dadāmi te tubhyaṃ cakṣuḥ | tena paśya me yogam aiśvaram īśvarasya mama aiśvaraṃ yogaṃ yoga-śakty-atiśayam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_11.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'But you are not able to see Me' — Me who bear the cosmic form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>) — 'with just this,' i.e., with your ordinary, natural own eye, your own organ of sight. 'But that by which you are able to see' — with the divine [eye] — 'that divine [eye] I give to you.' With that, 'behold My lordly <s>yoga</s>' — the <s>yoga</s> of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), that is, My sovereign <s>yoga</s>, meaning the supreme power of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yoga-śakty-atiśaya</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.8||

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca -
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjaya</s> said:

children.text: evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yogeśvaro hariḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken, O King, <s>Hari</s>, the great Lord of <s>Yoga</s>,

children.text: darśayām āsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpam aiśvaram ||BhG_11.9||
children.translated_text: then showed to <s>Pārtha</s> (son of <s>Pṛthā</s>) the supreme, lordly form. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.9||

children.text: evaṃ yathokta-prakāreṇoktvā tato 'nantaraṃ rājan dhṛtarāṣṭra ! mahā-yogeśvaro mahāṃś cāsau yogeśvaraś mahā-yogeśvaro harir nārāyaṇo darśayāmāsa darśitavān pārthāya pṛthā-sutāya paramaṃ rūpaṃ viśva-rūpam aiśvaram ||BhGS_11.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having thus spoken in the manner described, 'then' (<s>tataḥ</s>), i.e., immediately after — O King, O <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>! — the great Lord of <s>Yoga</s> (<s>mahā-yogeśvara</s>), great and a Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, hence the great Lord of <s>Yoga</s> — <s>Hari</s>, i.e., <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — showed, i.e., displayed, to <s>Pārtha</s>, the son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, the supreme form, the cosmic form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>), the lordly [form]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.9||

children.text: aneka-vaktra-nayanam anekādbhuta-darśanam |
children.translated_text: With many mouths and eyes, with many wondrous sights,

children.text: aneka-divyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham ||BhG_11.10||
children.translated_text: with many divine ornaments, with many divine weapons raised — ||<s>BhG</s> 11.10||

children.text: aneka-vaktra-nayanam anekāni vaktrāṇi nayanāni ca yasmin rūpe tad aneka-vaktra-nayanam, anekādbhuta-darśanam anekāny adbhutāni vismāpakāni darśanāni yasmin rūpe tad anekādbhuta-darśanaṃ rūpam | tathāneka-divyābharaṇam anekāni divyāny ābharaṇāni yasmin tad aneka-divyābharaṇam | tathā divyānekodyatāyudhaṃ divyāny anekāny asyādīni udyatāny āyudhāni yasmin tad divyānekodyatāyudham | darśayāmāseti pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ ||BhGS_11.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'With many mouths and eyes' — that form in which there are many mouths and many eyes, that is 'with many mouths and eyes.' 'With many wondrous sights' — that form in which there are many wondrous, i.e., astonishing, sights, that [is described as having] 'many wondrous sights.' Likewise, 'with many divine ornaments' — that in which there are many divine ornaments, that is 'with many divine ornaments.' Likewise, 'with many divine weapons raised' — that in which there are many divine weapons such as discuses etc. that are raised, that is 'with many divine weapons raised.' This is connected with the previous [verb] 'showed.' ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.10||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: divya-mālyāmbara-dharaṃ divya-gandhānulepanam |
children.translated_text: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances,

children.text: sarvāścarya-mayaṃ devam anantaṃ viśvato-mukham ||BhG_11.11||
children.translated_text: all-wondrous, divine, infinite, with faces in every direction — ||<s>BhG</s> 11.11||

children.text: divya-mālyāmbara-dharaṃ divyāni mālyāni puṣpāṇy ambarāṇi vasrāṇi ca dhriyante yeneśvareṇa taṃ divya-mālyāmbara-dharam, divya-gandhānulepanaṃ divyaṃ gandhānulepanaṃ yasya taṃ divya-gandhānulepanam, sarvāścarya-mayaṃ sarvāścarya-prāyaṃ devam anantaṃ nāsyānto 'stīty anantas tam, viśvato-mukhaṃ sarvato-mukhaṃ sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtatvāt, taṃ darśayāmāsa | arjuno dadarśeti vādhyāhriyate ||BhGS_11.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Wearing divine garlands and garments' — the Lord by whom divine garlands, i.e., flowers, and garments, i.e., robes, are worn, Him, the wearer of divine garlands and garments. 'With divine fragrant ointment' — Him whose fragrant ointment is divine. 'All-wondrous' — consisting entirely of wonders. 'Divine.' 'Infinite' (<s>ananta</s>) — He whose end does not exist, hence infinite. 'With faces in every direction' (<s>viśvatomukha</s>) — having faces everywhere, because He is the Self of all beings. Him He showed; or it may be supplied [from context] that <s>Arjuna</s> beheld [Him]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.11||

children.text: yā punar bhagavato viśva-rūpasya bhāḥ, tasyā upamocyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, a simile is offered for the radiance of the Blessed Lord's cosmic form:

children.text: divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā |
children.translated_text: If the splendor of a thousand suns were to arise simultaneously

children.text: yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ ||BhG_11.12||
children.translated_text: in the sky, that might be like the radiance of that Great Soul. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.12||

children.text: antarikṣe vā divi sūryāṇāṃ sahasraṃ sūrya-sahasraṃ tasya yugapad utthitasya sūrya-sahasrasya yā yugapad utthitā bhāḥ, sā yadi, sadṛśī syāt tasya mahātmano viśva-rūpasyaiva bhāsaḥ | yadi vā na syāt, tato viśva-rūpasyaiva bhā atiricyate ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_11.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] In the sky (<s>divi</s>), or in the atmosphere — of a thousand suns (<s>sūrya-sahasra</s>) — the radiance (<s>bhāḥ</s>) that would arise simultaneously from a thousand suns risen all at once — if that were comparable to the radiance of that Great Soul, the cosmic form itself. Or if it were not [comparable], then the implication is that the radiance of the cosmic form itself exceeds [even that]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.12||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: tatraikasthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktam anekadhā |
children.translated_text: There, in the body of the God of gods, <s>Pāṇḍava</s> then beheld

children.text: apaśyad deva-devasya śarīre pāṇḍavas tadā ||BhG_11.13||
children.translated_text: the entire universe gathered in one place, divided into manifold [forms]. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.13||

children.text: tatra tasmin viśva-rūpa ekasmin sthitam eka-sthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktam anekadhā deva-pitṛ-manuṣyādi-bhedair apaśyad dṛṣṭavān deva-devasya hareḥ śarīre pāṇḍāvo 'rjunas tadā ||BhGS_11.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'There' — in that one cosmic form, 'gathered in one place' (<s>ekastham</s>), the entire universe, 'divided manifold' (<s>pravibhaktam anekadhā</s>) — into the divisions of gods, ancestors, humans, and so on — <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, i.e., <s>Arjuna</s>, 'beheld' (<s>apaśyat</s>), i.e., saw, in the body of the God of gods (<s>deva-deva</s>), <s>Hari</s>, at that time. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.13||

children.text: tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭa-romā dhanaṃjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>

children.text: praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata ||BhG_11.14||
children.translated_text: bowed his head before the God, and spoke with joined palms: ||<s>BhG</s> 11.14||

children.text: tatas taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vismayenāviṣṭo vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭāni romāṇi yasya so 'yaṃ hṛṣṭa-romā cābhavad dhanañjayaḥ | praṇamya prakarṣeṇa namanaṃ kṛtvā prahvī-bhūtaḥ san śirasā devaṃ viśva-rūpa-dharaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ namaskārārthaṃ saṃpuṭīkṛta-hastaḥ sann abhāṣata uktavān ||BhGS_11.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Then, having seen that, he — filled with wonder (<s>vismayāviṣṭa</s>), with his hair standing on end (<s>hṛṣṭa-roman</s>) — such was <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. Having bowed (<s>praṇamya</s>) — having bowed down deeply, having become humble — with his head, before the God who bore the cosmic form, with joined palms (<s>kṛtāñjali</s>), i.e., with hands cupped together in salutation, he spoke, i.e., said: ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.14||

children.text: katham ? yat tvayā darśitaṃ viśva-rūpam, tad ahaṃ paśyāmīti svānubhavam āviṣkurvann arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How? 'The cosmic form that You have shown — I behold it' — thus revealing his own experience, <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: paśyāmi devāṃs tava deva dehe
children.translated_text: I see all the gods in Your body, O God,

children.text: sarvāṃs tathā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃghān |
children.translated_text: and likewise all the multitudes of various beings;

children.text: brahmāṇam īśaṃ kamalāsana-stham
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> the Lord, seated on the lotus-throne,

children.text: ṛṣīṃś ca sarvān uragāṃś ca divyān ||BhG_11.15||
children.translated_text: and all the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), and the divine serpents. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.15||

children.text: paśyāmy upalabhe he deva, tava dehe devān sarvān, tathā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃghān bhūta-viśeṣāṇāṃ sthāvara-jaṅgamānāṃ nānā-saṃsthāna-viśeṣāṇāṃ saṃghā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃghās tān, kiṃ ca - brahmāṇaṃ catur-mukham īśam īśitāraṃ prajānāṃ kamalāsana-sthaṃ pṛthivī-padma-madhye meru-karṇikāsana-stham ity arthaḥ | ṛṣīṃś ca vasiṣṭhādīn sarvān, uragāṃś ca vāsuki-prabhṛtīn divyān divi bhavān ||BhGS_11.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'I see' (<s>paśyāmi</s>), i.e., I perceive — O God (<s>deva</s>), in Your body — all the gods; 'likewise the multitudes of various beings' (<s>bhūta-viśeṣa-saṃghān</s>) — the assemblies of particular beings, of the moving and unmoving, of various distinctive forms — those [multitudes]. Moreover — <s>Brahmā</s>, the four-faced one; 'the Lord' (<s>Īśam</s>), the ruler of beings; 'seated on the lotus-throne' (<s>kamalāsana-stham</s>) — meaning seated on <s>Meru</s> as the pericarp [of the lotus], in the middle of the earth-lotus. All the sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>) such as <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others; and the serpents (<s>uragas</s>) such as <s>Vāsuki</s> and others — divine, i.e., celestial. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.15||

children.text: aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṃ
children.translated_text: With many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes,

children.text: paśyāmi tvā sarvato 'nanta-rūpam |
children.translated_text: I see You everywhere, of infinite form;

children.text: nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punas tavādiṃ
children.translated_text: neither end, nor middle, nor again Your beginning

children.text: paśyāmi viśveśvara viśva-rūpa ||BhG_11.16||
children.translated_text: do I see, O Lord of the Universe, O Cosmic Form! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.16||

children.text: aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netram aneke bāhavar udarāṇi vaktrāṇi netrāṇi ca yasya tava sa tvam aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netras tam aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netram | paśyāmi tvā tvāṃ sarvataḥ sarvatrānanta-rūpam anantāni rūpāṇy asya ity ananta-rūpas tam ananta-rūpam | nāntam, anto 'vasānam, na madhyam, madhyaṃ nāma dvayoḥ koṭyor antaram | na punas tavādim - na devasyāntaṃ paśyāmi, na madhyaṃ paśyāmi, na punar ādiṃ paśyāmi | he viśveśvara viśva-rūpa ||BhGS_11.16||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'With many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes' — You whose arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes are many — You are that one with many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes — that [form] I [see]. 'I see You' — You — 'everywhere, of infinite form' — whose forms are infinite, hence of infinite form. 'Neither [Your] end' — end means conclusion; 'nor [Your] middle' — the middle is what lies between two extremities; 'nor again Your beginning' — I do not see the end of the God, nor the middle, nor again the beginning. O Lord of the Universe (<s>Viśveśvara</s>)! O Cosmic Form (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>)! ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.16||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Crowned, bearing the mace and discus,

children.text: tejo-rāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantam |
children.translated_text: a mass of splendor, shining in all directions;

children.text: paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ samantād
children.translated_text: I see You, hard to behold on all sides,

children.text: dīptānalārka-dyutim aprameyam ||BhG_11.17||
children.translated_text: with the radiance of blazing fire and sun, immeasurable. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.17||
Moreover —

children.text: kirīṭiānaṃ kirīṭāṃ nāma śirobhūṣaṇaviśeṣas tat yasyāsti saḥ kirīṭī taṃ kirīṭiānam, tathā gadinaṃ gadāsya vidyate iti gadī taṃ gadinam, tathā cakriṇaṃ caktram asyāstīti cakrī taṃ cakriṇaṃ ca, tejo-rāśiṃ tejaḥpujaṃ sarvatodīptimantaṃ sarvatodīptir asyāstīti sarvatodīptimān, taṃ sarvatodīptimantaṃ paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣyaṃ samantāt samantataḥ sarvatra dīptānalārkadyutim analaś cārkaś cānalārkau dīptau analārkau dīptānalārkau tayoḥ dīptānalārkayoḥ dyutiriva dyutis tejo yasya tava sa tvaṃ dīptānalārkadyutis taṃ tvāṃ dīptānalārkadyatim aprameyaṃ na prameyam aśakyaparicchedam ity etat ||BhGS_11.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Crowned' (<s>kirīṭinam</s>) — a crown (<s>kirīṭa</s>) is a particular head-ornament; he who has it is 'crowned.' Likewise, 'bearing a mace' (<s>gadinam</s>) — he who possesses a mace is a mace-bearer. Likewise, 'bearing a discus' (<s>cakriṇam</s>) — he who possesses a discus is a discus-bearer. 'A mass of splendor' (<s>tejo-rāśim</s>) — a heap of radiance. 'Shining in all directions' — he whose brilliance is in all directions. 'I see You, hard to behold on all sides' — hard to look at everywhere. 'With the radiance of blazing fire and sun' — fire and sun are 'blazing'; the two together are 'blazing fire and sun'; whose radiance is like theirs — You, of such radiance. 'Immeasurable' (<s>aprameya</s>) — not to be measured, impossible to fathom — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.17||

children.text: ita eva te yoga-śakti-darśanāt anuminomi -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] From this very vision of Your power of <s>yoga</s>, I infer —

children.text: tvam akṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ
children.translated_text: You are the imperishable, the supreme, to be known;

children.text: tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
children.translated_text: You are the ultimate resting-place of this universe;

children.text: tvam avyayaḥ śāśvata-dharma-goptā
children.translated_text: You are the inexhaustible guardian of the eternal <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: sanātanas tvaṃ puruṣo mato me ||BhG_11.18||
children.translated_text: You are, I believe, the primeval <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person). ||<s>BhG</s> 11.18||

children.text: tvam akṣaraṃ na kṣaratīti, paramaṃ brahma veditavyaṃ jñātavyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ | tvam asya viśvasya samastasya jagataḥ paraṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ nidhānaṃ nidhīyate 'sminn iti nidhānaṃ para āśraya ity arthaḥ | kiṃ ca, tvam avyayo na tava vyayo vidyata ity avyayaḥ | śāśvata-dharma-goptā śaśvad-bhavaḥ śāśvato nityo dharmas tasya goptā śāśvata-dharma-goptā | sanātanaś cirantanas tvaṃ puruṣaḥ paramaḥ mato 'bhipretaḥ me mama ||BhGS_11.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'You are the imperishable' (<s>akṣara</s>) — that which does not perish; 'the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' 'to be known' (<s>veditavya</s>), i.e., to be realized by those seeking liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>). 'You are the ultimate resting-place' (<s>nidhāna</s>) — the supreme, the most excellent abode — that in which [all] is deposited — meaning the ultimate support of this entire universe. Moreover, 'You are the inexhaustible one' (<s>avyaya</s>) — there is no decay for You. 'The guardian of the eternal <s>dharma</s>' (<s>śāśvata-dharma-goptā</s>) — <s>śāśvata</s> means perpetual, eternal; <s>dharma</s> — its guardian. 'The primeval <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>sanātana</s>) — the ancient, supreme Person — 'I believe' (<s>mata</s>), i.e., such is my conviction. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.18||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
anādi-madhyāntam ananta-vīryam
children.translated_text: Without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite power,

children.text: ananta-bāhuṃ śaśi-sūrya-netram |
children.translated_text: with infinite arms, with the moon and sun as eyes;

children.text: paśyāmi tvāṃ dīpta-hutāśa-vaktraṃ
children.translated_text: I see You, with blazing fire as Your mouth,

children.text: sva-tejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantam ||BhG_11.19||
children.translated_text: scorching this entire universe with Your own radiance. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.19||
Moreover —

children.text: anādi-madhyāntam ādi ca madhyaṃ cāntaś ca na vidyate yasya so 'yam anādi-madhyāntas, taṃ tvām anādi-madhyāntam | ananta-vīryaṃ na tava vīryasyānto 'stīty ananta-vīryas, taṃ tvām ananta-vīryam | tathānanta-bāhum anantā bāhavo yasya tava sa tvam, ananta-bāhus taṃ tvām ananta-bāhum | śaśi-sūrya-netraṃ śaśi-sūryau netre yasya tava sa tvaṃ śaśi-sūrya-netras, taṃ tvāṃ śaśi-sūrya-netraṃ candrāditya-nayanam | paśyāmi tvāṃ dīpta-hutāśa-vaktraṃ dīptaś cāsau hutāśaś ca vaktraṃ yasya tava sa tvaṃ dīpta-hutāśa-vaktras, taṃ tvāṃ dīpta-hutāśa-vaktram | sva-tejasā viśvam idaṃ samastaṃ tapantam ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Without beginning, middle, or end' (<s>anādi-madhyānta</s>) — He whose beginning, middle, and end do not exist — You, without beginning, middle, or end. 'Of infinite power' (<s>ananta-vīrya</s>) — whose power has no limit, hence of infinite power. Likewise, 'with infinite arms' (<s>ananta-bāhu</s>) — You whose arms are infinite. 'With the moon and sun as eyes' (<s>śaśi-sūrya-netra</s>) — You whose eyes are the moon and the sun, having the moon and the sun as Your eyes. 'I see You, with blazing fire as Your mouth' (<s>dīpta-hutāśa-vaktra</s>) — whose mouth is a blazing fire. 'Scorching this entire universe with Your own radiance.' ||

children.text: dyāv-āpṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hi
children.translated_text: This space between heaven and earth is indeed

children.text: vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaś ca sarvāḥ |
children.translated_text: pervaded by You alone, and all the directions too;

children.text: dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ rūpam idaṃ tavograṃ
children.translated_text: having seen this wondrous and terrible form of Yours,

children.text: loka-trayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman ||BhG_11.20||
children.translated_text: the three worlds tremble, O Great Soul! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.20||

children.text: dyāv-āpṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hy antarikṣaṃ vyāptaṃ tvayaikena viśva-rūpa-dhareṇa diśaś ca sarvā vyāptāḥ | dṛṣṭvā upalabhyādbhutaṃ vismāpakaṃ rūpam idaṃ tavograṃ krūraṃ lokānāṃ trayaṃ loka-trayaṃ pravyathitaṃ bhītaṃ pracalitaṃ vā | he mahātman ! akṣudra-svabhāva ||BhGS_11.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Between heaven and earth' — this intervening space, i.e., the atmosphere, is 'pervaded by You alone' — by You who bear the cosmic form — and 'all the directions' too are pervaded. 'Having seen' (<s>dṛṣṭvā</s>), i.e., having perceived, 'this wondrous' (<s>adbhuta</s>), i.e., astonishing, 'form of Yours, terrible' (<s>ugra</s>), i.e., fierce — 'the three worlds' (<s>loka-traya</s>) are 'struck with terror' (<s>pravyathita</s>), i.e., frightened, or shaken. O Great Soul (<s>Mahātman</s>)! — O one of no mean nature! ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.20||

children.text: athādhunā purā yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ [Gītā 2.6] ity arjunasya yaḥ saṃśaya āsīt, tan-nirṇayāya pāṇḍava-jayam aikāntikaṃ darśayāmīti pravṛtto bhagavān | taṃ paśyann āha | kiṃ ca -
amī hi tvā sura-saṃghā viśanti
children.translated_text: Indeed, these hosts of gods enter into You;

children.text: kecid bhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti |
children.translated_text: some, terrified, praise You with joined palms;

children.text: svastīty uktvā maharṣi-siddha-saṃghāḥ
children.translated_text: crying 'Hail!' (<s>svasti</s>), the hosts of great sages and <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings)

children.text: stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ ||BhG_11.21||
children.translated_text: extol You with abundant hymns of praise. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.21||

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, formerly <s>Arjuna</s> had the doubt: 'whether we shall conquer, or they shall conquer us' [<s>Gītā</s> 2.6]. To resolve that doubt, the Blessed Lord, having set out to show the certain victory of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, [reveals the cosmic form]. Seeing it, [<s>Arjuna</s>] says. Moreover —

children.text: amī hi yudhyamānā yoddhāras tvā tvāṃ sura-saṃghāḥ ye 'tra bhū-bhārāvatārāyāvatīrṇā vasv-ādi-deva-saṃghā manuṣya-saṃsthānās tvāṃ viśanti praviśanto dṛśyante | tatra kecit bhītāḥ prāñjalayaḥ santo gṛṇanti stuvanti tvām anye palāyane 'py aśaktāḥ santaḥ | yuddhe pratyupasthita utpātādi-nimittāni upalakṣya svasty astu jagata iti uktvā maharṣi-siddha-saṃghāḥ maharṣīṇāṃ siddhānāṃ ca saṃghāḥ stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ saṃpūrṇābhiḥ ||BhGS_11.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] These (<s>amī</s>) fighting warriors — the hosts of gods who descended here for the purpose of lightening the burden of the earth, such as the <s>Vasus</s> and other divine hosts in human forms — are entering you, are seen entering you. Among them, some, being frightened, with palms joined, praise you; others, being incapable even of fleeing, [also praise you]. With the battle at hand, having observed the portents and other signs, having said 'May there be well-being for the world!' — the hosts of great seers and <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings) praise you with abundant, complete hymns of praise. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.21||

children.text: kiṃ cānyat -
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Sādhyas</s>,

children.text: viśve 'śvinau marutaś coṣmapāś ca |
children.translated_text: the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the <s>Uṣmapas</s> (manes who drink steam);

children.text: gandharva-yakṣāsura-siddha-saṃghā
children.translated_text: the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s> —

children.text: vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāś caiva sarve ||BhG_11.22||
children.translated_text: they all gaze upon you, struck with wonder. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.22||
And what else?

children.text: rudrādityāḥ vasavo ye ca sādhyāḥ rudrādayo gaṇāḥ viśve-devā aśvinau ca devau marutaś ca ūṣmapā ca pitaraḥ, gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṃghāḥ gandharṣaḥ hāhāhūhūprabhṛtayo yakṣāḥ kuberaprabhṛtayo 'surāḥ virocanaprabhṛtayaḥ siddhāḥ kapilādayas teṣāṃ saṃghāḥ gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṃghāḥ, te vīkṣante paśyanti tvāṃ vismitāḥ vismayamāpannāḥ santas te eva sarve ||BhGS_11.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Sādhyas</s> — the groups of <s>Rudra</s> and the others; the <s>Viśvedevas</s> and the two <s>Aśvin</s> deities; the <s>Maruts</s>; and the <s>Uṣmapas</s>, that is, the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors). The hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s> — <s>Gandharvas</s> such as <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s>; <s>Yakṣas</s> such as <s>Kubera</s> and others; <s>Asuras</s> such as <s>Virocana</s> and others; <s>Siddhas</s> such as <s>Kapila</s> and others — their hosts are the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s>. They gaze upon, that is, behold, you — struck with wonder, that is, having attained astonishment — all of them indeed. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.22||

children.text: yasmāt -
rūpaṃ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṃ
children.translated_text: Your great form, with many faces and eyes,

children.text: mahā-bāho bahu-bāhūru-pādam |
children.translated_text: O mighty-armed one, with many arms, thighs, and feet,

children.text: bahūdaraṃ bahu-daṃṣṭrā-karālaṃ
children.translated_text: with many bellies, and terrible with many tusks —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tathāham ||BhG_11.23||
children.translated_text: seeing [it], the worlds are greatly agitated, and so am I. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.23||
Because —

children.text: rūpaṃ mahad atipramāṇaṃ te tava bahu-vaktra-netraṃ bahūni vaktrāṇi mukhāni cakṣūṃṣi ca yasmin tad rūpaṃ bahu-vaktra-netram | he mahā-bāho ! bahu-bāhūru-pādaṃ bahavo bāhava ūravaḥ pādāś ca yasmin rūpe tad bahu-bāhūru-pādam | kiṃ ca, bahūdaraṃ bahūni udarāṇi yasminn iti bahūdaram | bahu-daṃṣṭrā-karālaṃ bahvībhir daṃṣṭrābhiḥ karālaṃ vikṛtaṃ tad bahu-daṃṣṭrā-karālam | dṛṣṭvā rūpam īdṛśaṃ lokā laukikāḥ prāṇinaḥ pravyathitāḥ pracalitā bhayena | tathāham api ||BhGS_11.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Your great form — of immense measure — with many faces and eyes, that is, having many faces, mouths, and eyes — such is that form, with many faces and eyes. O mighty-armed one! With many arms, thighs, and feet — that is, the form in which there are many arms, thighs, and feet. Moreover, with many bellies — that in which there are many bellies. Terrible with many tusks — made hideous, deformed, by the many tusks — such is that form, terrible with many tusks. Seeing such a form, the worlds — the worldly creatures — are greatly agitated, shaken by fear. And so am I likewise. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.23||

children.text: tatredaṃ kāraṇam -
nabhaḥ-spṛśaṃ dīptam aneka-varṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Touching the sky, blazing, of many colors,

children.text: vyāttānanaṃ dīpta-viśāla-netram |
children.translated_text: with gaping mouths, with blazing, vast eyes —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā
children.translated_text: seeing you thus, my inner self is greatly agitated,

children.text: dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo ||BhG_11.24||
children.translated_text: and I find neither firmness nor peace, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.24||
Here is the reason for that —

children.text: nabhaḥ-spṛśaṃ dyu-sparśam ity arthaḥ | dīptaṃ prajvalitam | aneka-varṇam aneke varṇā bhayaṅkarāḥ nānā-saṃsthānā yasmin tvayi taṃ tvām aneka-varṇam | vyāttānanaṃ vyāttāni vivṛtāni ānanāni mukhāni yasmin tvayi taṃ tvāṃ vyāttānanam | dīpta-viśāla-netraṃ dīptāni prajvalitāni viśālāni vistīrṇāni netrāṇi yasmin tvayi taṃ tvāṃ dīpta-viśāla-netraṃ dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā pravyathitaḥ prabhīto 'ntarātmā mano yasya mama so 'haṃ pravyathitāntarātmā san dhṛtiṃ dhairyaṃ na vindāmi na labhe śamaṃ copaśamanaṃ manas-tuṣṭim | he viṣṇo ||BhGS_11.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Touching the sky' — touching heaven, that is the meaning. 'Blazing' — radiant, flaming. 'Of many colors' — many colors, fearsome, of various forms, in you — thus, you of many colors. 'With gaping mouths' — having mouths that are open, spread wide, in you — thus, you with gaping mouths. 'With blazing, vast eyes' — having eyes that are blazing, flaming, vast, expansive, in you — thus, you with blazing, vast eyes. 'Seeing you thus' — having seen you thus; 'my inner self is greatly agitated' — my inner self, that is, my mind, is greatly agitated, greatly frightened. I who have become one whose inner self is agitated — 'I find no firmness,' that is, I do not obtain courage; 'nor peace,' that is, tranquility, contentment of mind. O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.24||

children.text: kasmāt ?
daṃṣṭrā-karālāni ca te mukhāni
children.translated_text: And seeing your mouths, terrible with tusks,

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva kālānala-saṃnibhāni |
children.translated_text: resembling the fire of the end of time —

children.text: diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
children.translated_text: I know not the directions, and I find no refuge.

children.text: prasīda deveśa jagan-nivāsa ||BhG_11.25||
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.25||
Why?

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-karālāni daṃṣṭrābhiḥ karālāni vikṛtāni te tava mukhāni dṛṣṭvaivopalabhya kālānala-saṃnibhāni pralaya-kāle lokānāṃ dāhako 'gniḥ kālānalas tat-sadṛśāni kālānala-saṃnibhāni mukhāni dṛṣṭvety etat | diśaḥ pūrvāpara-vivekena na jāne diṅ-mūḍho jāto 'smi | ato na labhe ca nopalabhe ca śarma sukham | ataḥ prasīda prasanno bhava he deveśa, jagan-nivāsa ||BhGS_11.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Terrible with tusks' — made hideous by tusks; your mouths, having seen them, 'resembling the fire of the end of time' — the fire that burns the worlds at the time of dissolution is <s>kālānala</s>; resembling that, resembling the fire of the end of time — seeing such mouths. 'I know not the directions' — I cannot distinguish east from west; I have become confused about directions. Therefore, 'I find no refuge,' that is, I do not obtain happiness. Therefore, 'be gracious,' that is, be pleased, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe! ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.25||

children.text: yebhyo mama parājayāśaṅkā yāsīt sā cāpagatā | yataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those regarding whom I had the apprehension of defeat — that [apprehension] has now departed. For —

children.text: amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ
children.translated_text: And these sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> — all of them —

children.text: sarve sahaivāvanipāla-saṃghaiḥ |
children.translated_text: together with the hosts of earthly kings,

children.text: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūta-putras tathāsau
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and that son of the charioteer (<s>Karṇa</s>),

children.text: sahāsmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ ||BhG_11.26||
children.translated_text: together with our own chief warriors too — ||<s>BhG</s> 11.26||

children.text: amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ duryodhana-prabhṛtayaḥ - tvaramāṇāḥ viśantīti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ - sarve sahaiva sahitāḥ avani-pāla-saṃghair avaniṃ pṛthvīṃ pālayantīty avani-pālās teṣāṃ saṃghaiḥ, kiṃ ca bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūta-putraḥ karṇas tathāsau sahāsmadīyair api dhṛṣṭadyumna-prabhṛtibhir yodha-mukhyair yodhānāṃ mukhyaiḥ pradhānaiḥ saha ||BhGS_11.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And these sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, beginning with <s>Duryodhana</s> — 'hastening, they enter' — this is the connection with what follows (the verb is separated). All of them, together with the hosts of earthly kings — those who protect the earth are the protectors of the earth; with their hosts. Moreover, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the son of the charioteer (<s>sūtaputra</s>), that is <s>Karṇa</s>; and also together with our own chief warriors, the foremost among warriors, beginning with <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.26||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti
children.translated_text: They hurry and enter your mouths,

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni |
children.translated_text: terrible with tusks, fearsome.

children.text: kecid vilagnā daśanāntareṣu
children.translated_text: Some are seen stuck between the teeth

children.text: sandṛśyante cūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ ||BhG_11.27||
children.translated_text: with their heads crushed. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.27||
Moreover —

children.text: vaktrāṇi mukhāni te tava tvaramāṇās tvarā-yuktāḥ santo viśanti | kiṃ-viśiṣṭani mukhāni ? daṃṣṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni bhayaṅkarāṇi | kiṃ ca, kecit mukhāni praviṣṭānāṃ madhye vilagnā daśanāntareṣu māṃsam iva bhakṣitaṃ saṃdṛśyanta upalabhyante cūrṇitaiś cūrṇīkṛtair uttamāṅgaiḥ śirobhiḥ ||BhGS_11.27||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Your mouths — they enter, hastening with speed. Of what character are the mouths? Terrible with tusks, fearsome — causing terror. Moreover, some among those who have entered the mouths are seen stuck between the teeth — like flesh that has been chewed — they are perceived with their heads, their uppermost limbs, crushed to powder. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.27||

children.text: kathaṃ praviśanti mukhāni ? ity āha -
children.translated_text: How do they enter the mouths? He says —

children.text: yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo 'mbu-vegāḥ
children.translated_text: As the many currents of rivers' waters

children.text: samudram evābhimukhā dravanti |
children.translated_text: flow toward the ocean alone,

children.text: tathā tavāmī nara-loka-vīrā
children.translated_text: so these heroes of the human world

children.text: viśanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti ||BhG_11.28||
children.translated_text: enter your blazing mouths. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.28||

children.text: yathā nadīnāṃ sravantīnāṃ bahavo 'neke 'mbūnāṃ vegā ambu-vegās tvarā-viśeṣāḥ samudram evābhimukhāḥ pratimukhā dravanti praviśanti | tathā tadvat tavāmī bhīṣmādayo nara-loka-vīrā manuṣya-loke śūrāḥ viśanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti prakāśamānāni ||BhGS_11.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] As — of flowing rivers, the many, the numerous, torrents of water — the currents of water, the surges of speed — flow toward, that is, enter, the ocean alone, facing it. Similarly, these — <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the others — heroes of the human world, valiant in the world of humans, enter your mouths that are blazing, that is, shining forth. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.28||

children.text: te kim-arthaṃ praviśanti kathaṃ ca ? ity āha -
children.translated_text: For what purpose do they enter, and how? He says —

children.text: yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgā
children.translated_text: As moths enter a blazing fire

children.text: viśanti nāśāya samṛddha-vegāḥ |
children.translated_text: to their destruction, with great speed,

children.text: tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokās
children.translated_text: even so do these people enter your mouths

children.text: tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddha-vegāḥ ||BhG_11.29||
children.translated_text: to their destruction, with great speed. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.29||

children.text: yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanam agniṃ pataṅgāḥ pakṣiṇo viśanti nāśāya vināśāya samṛddha-vegāḥ samṛddha udbhūto vego gatir yeṣāṃ te samṛddha-vegāḥ | tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokāḥ prāṇinas tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddha-vegāḥ ||BhGS_11.29||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] As — moths, winged insects, enter a blazing fire, a flame — to their destruction, that is, for their annihilation, with great speed — those whose velocity, whose movement, has swelled, increased — they are the ones with great speed. Even so, to their destruction, these people — living beings — enter your mouths too, with great speed. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.29||

children.text: tvaṃ punaḥ -
children.translated_text: And you —

children.text: lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl
children.translated_text: You lick up, devouring on all sides,

children.text: lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: all the worlds entirely, with blazing mouths.

children.text: tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṃ
children.translated_text: Filling the entire universe with radiance,

children.text: bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo ||BhG_11.30||
children.translated_text: your fierce rays scorch, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.30||

children.text: lelihyase āsvādayasi grasamāno 'ntaḥ praveśayan samantāt samantataḥ lokān samagrān samastān vadanair vaktrair jvaladbhir dīpyamānais tejobhir āpūrya saṃvyāpya jagat samagraṃ sahāgreṇa samastam ity etat | kiṃ ca, bhāso dīptayas tavogrāḥ krūrāḥ pratapanti pratāpaṃ kurvanti he viṣṇo vyāpana-śīla ||BhGS_11.30||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'You lick up' — you savor; devouring, that is, pushing them inside; on all sides, from every direction; all the worlds entirely — all of them — with mouths, faces, that are blazing, that is, flaming. 'Filling the entire universe with radiance' — pervading the universe that is complete, entire — this is the meaning. Moreover, your rays, your blazes of light, fierce, that is, cruel, scorch, inflict burning heat, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose nature is to pervade! ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.30||

children.text: yataḥ evam ugra-svabhāvaḥ, ataḥ -
children.translated_text: Since you are of such a fierce nature, therefore —

children.text: ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpo
children.translated_text: Tell me, who are you, of fierce form?

children.text: namo 'stu te deva-vara prasīda |
children.translated_text: Salutation to you! Be gracious, O best of gods!

children.text: vijñātum icchāmi bhavantam ādyaṃ
children.translated_text: I wish to know you, the primeval one;

children.text: na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim ||BhG_11.31||
children.translated_text: for I do not understand your activity. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.31||

children.text: ākhyāhi kathaya me mahyaṃ ko bhavān ugra-rūpaḥ krūrākāraḥ | namo 'stu te tubhyaṃ he deva-vara devānāṃ pradhāna, prasīda prasādaṃ kuru | vijñātuṃ viśeṣeṇa jñātum icchāmi bhavantam ādyam ādau bhavam ādyam, na hi yasmāt prajānāmi tava tvadīyāṃ pravṛttiṃ ceṣṭam ||BhGS_11.31||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Tell me, declare to me, who you are, of fierce form, that is, of a cruel appearance. Salutation to you! O best of gods, that is, the foremost among the gods, be gracious, that is, show your grace! I wish to know, to know particularly, you, the primeval one — the one who exists at the beginning, the first. For I do not understand your activity, that is, your endeavor. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.31||

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
kālo 'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho
children.translated_text: I am Time (<s>Kāla</s>), the destroyer of the worlds, fully grown,

children.text: lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: engaged here in annihilating the worlds.

children.text: ṛte 'pi tvā na bhaviṣyanti sarve
children.translated_text: Even without you, all these warriors

children.text: ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ ||BhG_11.32||
children.translated_text: arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.32||
The Blessed Lord said —

children.text: kālo 'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt lokānāṃ kṣayaṃ karotīti loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho vṛddhiṃ gataḥ | yad-arthaṃ pravṛddhas tac chṛṇu - lokān samāhartuṃ saṃhartum ihāsmin kāle pravṛttaḥ | ṛte 'pi vināpi tvā tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti bhīṣma-droṇa-karṇa-prabhṛtayaḥ sarve, yebhyas tava āśaṅkā, ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu anīkam anīkaṃ prati pratyanīkeṣu pratipakṣa-bhūteṣu anīkeṣu yodhā yoddhāraḥ ||BhGS_11.32||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'I am Time, the destroyer of the worlds' — that which brings about the destruction of the worlds is 'the destroyer of the worlds'; 'fully grown,' that is, one who has reached maturation. The purpose for which it has grown — hear that: 'engaged here in annihilating the worlds,' that is, engaged in destroying the worlds at this time. 'Even without you' — even without you, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and all the others regarding whom you had apprehension — 'shall cease to exist'; those who are 'arrayed in the opposing armies' — in the armies that stand face to face (<s>pratyanīka</s>), that is, the hostile forces — these warriors, these fighters. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.32||

children.text: yasmād evam -
tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
children.translated_text: Therefore, arise! Win glory!

children.text: jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham |
children.translated_text: Having conquered your enemies, enjoy a prosperous kingdom!

children.text: mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
children.translated_text: These have already been slain by me;

children.text: nimitta-mātraṃ bhava savyasācin ||BhG_11.33||
children.translated_text: be merely the instrument, O <s>Savyasācin</s> (ambidextrous archer)! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.33||
Since this is so —

children.text: tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha bhīṣma-prabhṛtayo 'tirathā ajeyā devair apy arjunena jitā iti yaśaḥ labhasva | kevalaṃ puṇyair hi tat prāpyate | jitvā śatrūn duryodhana-prabhṛtīn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham asapatnam akaṇṭakam | mayaivaite nihatā niścayena hatāḥ prāṇair viyojitāḥ pūrvam eva | nimitta-mātraṃ bhava tvam | he savyasācin ! savyena vāmenāpi hastena śarāṇāṃ kṣepāt savyasācīty ucyate 'rjunaḥ ||BhGS_11.33||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, arise! '<s>Bhīṣma</s> and the other great chariot-warriors, who are unconquerable even by the gods, have been conquered by <s>Arjuna</s>' — thus win glory! For that [glory] is obtained solely by merit. Having conquered your enemies, <s>Duryodhana</s> and the rest, enjoy a prosperous kingdom — without rivals, free from thorns. 'These have already been slain by me' — slain with certainty, separated from their lives, even before [this]. 'Be merely the instrument' — you be merely the instrument. O <s>Savyasācin</s>! He is called <s>Savyasācin</s> because he hurls arrows even with his left hand — thus <s>Arjuna</s> [is addressed]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.33||

children.text: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Jayadratha</s>,

children.text: karṇaṃ tathānyān api yodha-vīrān |
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s>, and other warrior-heroes as well —

children.text: mayā hatāṃs tvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā
children.translated_text: slain by me, slay them! Do not be distressed!

children.text: yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān ||BhG_11.34||
children.translated_text: Fight! You shall conquer your enemies in battle. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.34||

children.text: droṇaṃ ca, yeṣu yeṣu yodheṣv arjunasyāśaṅkā tāṃs tān vyapadiśati bhagavān mayā hatān iti | tatra droṇa-bhīṣmayos tāvat prasiddham āśaṅkā-kāraṇam | droṇas tu dhanur-vedācāryo divyāstra-saṃpannaḥ | ātmanaś ca viśeṣato gurur gariṣṭhaḥ | bhīṣmaś ca svacchanda-mṛtyur divyāstra-saṃpannaś ca paraśurāmeṇa dvandva-yuddham agamat, na ca parājitaḥ | tathā jayadrathaḥ | yasya pitā tapaś carati mama putrasya śiro bhūmau nipātayiṣyati yaḥ, tasyāpi śiraḥ patiṣyatīti | karṇo 'pi vāsava-dattayā śaktyā tv amoghayā saṃpannaḥ sūrya-putraḥ kānīno yataḥ, atas tan-nāmnaiva nirdeśaḥ | mayā hatān tvaṃ jahi nimitta-mātreṇa | mā vyathiṣṭhās tebhyo bhayaṃ mā kārṣīḥ | yudhyasva jetāsi duryodhana-prabhṛtīn raṇe yuddhe sapatnān śatrūn ||BhGS_11.34||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] <s>Droṇa</s> — and regarding whichever warriors <s>Arjuna</s> had apprehension, those very ones the Blessed Lord designates as 'slain by me.' Therein, as for <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s>, the cause for apprehension regarding them is well known. <s>Droṇa</s> was the teacher of the science of archery (<s>dhanurveda</s>), endowed with divine weapons, and especially the most honored teacher of [<s>Arjuna</s>] himself. And <s>Bhīṣma</s> — who had death at will, endowed with divine weapons, and who fought a duel with <s>Paraśurāma</s> and was not defeated. Likewise <s>Jayadratha</s> — whose father performed austerities [with the vow]: 'Whoever causes my son's head to fall to the ground — his head too shall fall.' And <s>Karṇa</s> too — endowed with the unfailing spear given by <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), being the son of <s>Sūrya</s>, born out of wedlock — and therefore he is designated by that name alone [<s>sūtaputra</s>]. 'Slain by me — you slay them' — merely as an instrument. 'Do not be distressed' — do not be afraid of them! 'Fight! You shall conquer' — <s>Duryodhana</s> and the rest — in battle, in war — your enemies, your foes. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.34||

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca -
children.translated_text: <s>Sañjaya</s> said —

children.text: etac chrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: kṛtāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī |
children.translated_text: the crowned one (<s>Kirīṭī</s>), with joined palms, trembling,

children.text: namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ
children.translated_text: having bowed down, spoke again to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: sa-gadgadaṃ bhīta-bhītaḥ praṇamya ||BhG_11.35||
children.translated_text: in a faltering voice, deeply frightened, prostrating. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.35||

children.text: etat śrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya pūrvoktaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ san vepamānaḥ kampamānaḥ kirīṭī namaskṛtvā | bhūyaḥ punar evāhoktavān kṛṣṇaṃ sa-gadgadaṃ bhayāviṣṭasya duḥkhābhighātāt snehāviṣṭasya ca harṣodbhavāt, aśru-pūrṇa-netratve sati śleṣmaṇā kaṇṭhāvarodhaḥ | tataś ca vāco 'pāṭavaṃ manda-śabdatvaṃ yat sa-gadgadas tena saha vartateti sa-gadgadaṃ vacanam āheti vacana-kriyā-viśeṣaṇam etat | bhīta-bhītaḥ punaḥ punar bhayāviṣṭa-cetāḥ san praṇamya prahvo bhūtvā | āheti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ ||BhGS_11.35||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having heard these aforementioned words of <s>Keśava</s>, with joined palms, trembling, i.e., shaking, the crowned one (<s>Kirīṭī</s>), having bowed down; again he spoke to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in a faltering voice (<s>sa-gadgadam</s>) — for one seized by fear, from the impact of grief, and for one seized by affection, from the arising of joy, when the eyes are filled with tears, there is obstruction of the throat by phlegm. From that comes indistinctness of speech, soft-spokenness — that is a faltering voice (<s>gadgada</s>); 'together with that' means his speech was accompanied by it — this qualifies the act of speaking. Deeply frightened (<s>bhīta-bhīta</s>) — repeatedly seized by fear in his mind, prostrating (<s>praṇamya</s>), i.e., having become bowed down. The connection is with 'spoke' (<s>āha</s>), which is syntactically separated [from the rest]. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.35||

children.text: arjuna uvāca -
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā
children.translated_text: It is fitting, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, that by the proclamation of Your [glory]

children.text: jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate ca |
children.translated_text: the world rejoices and is filled with love;

children.text: rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti
children.translated_text: the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, terrified, flee in all directions,

children.text: sarve namasyanti ca siddha-saṃghāḥ ||BhG_11.36||
children.translated_text: and all the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> bow down [to You]. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.36||
<s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: sthāne yuktam | kiṃ tat ? tava prakītryā tvan-māhātmya-kīrtanena śrutena | he hṛṣīkeśa ! yat jagat prahṛṣyati praharṣam upaiti, tat sthāne yuktam ity arthaḥ | athavā viṣaya-viśeṣaṇaṃ sthāna iti | yukto harṣādi-viṣayo bhagavān, yata īśvaraḥ sarvātmā sarva-bhūta-suhṛc ceti | tathānurajyate 'nurāgaṃ copaiti | tac ca viṣaya iti vyākhyeyam | kiṃ ca, rakṣāṃsi bhītāni bhayāviṣṭani diśo dravanti gacchanti | tac ca sthāne viṣaye | sarve namasyanti namaskurvanti ca siddha-saṃghāḥ siddhānāṃ samudāyāḥ kapilādīnām, tac ca sthāne ||BhGS_11.36||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'It is fitting' (<s>sthāne</s>) — it is appropriate. What is? That by the proclamation of Your glory, i.e., when the celebration of Your greatness is heard — O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>! — the world rejoices, i.e., experiences joy — that is fitting, that is appropriate — this is the meaning. Or alternatively, '<s>sthāna</s>' qualifies the object, meaning: the Lord is a fitting, appropriate object for joy etc., since He is the sovereign, the Self of all, and the friend of all beings. Likewise, the world 'is filled with love' (<s>anurajyate</s>), i.e., experiences deep attachment — and this too is fitting, its proper object. Moreover, the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, terrified, i.e., seized with fear, flee in all directions — and this too is fitting. All the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> — the assemblies of perfected beings such as <s>Kapila</s> and others — bow down, pay homage — and this too is fitting. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.36||

children.text: bhagavato harṣādi-viṣayatve hetuṃ darśayati -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] He shows the reason for the Lord being the fitting object of joy etc.:

children.text: kasmāc ca te na nameran mahātman
children.translated_text: And why should they not bow to You, O Great Soul,

children.text: garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādi-kartre |
children.translated_text: greater even than <s>Brahmā</s>, the original creator?

children.text: ananta deveśa jagan-nivāsa
children.translated_text: O Infinite One, Lord of the gods, Abode of the universe —

children.text: tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tat-paraṃ yat ||BhG_11.37||
children.translated_text: You are the Imperishable, Being and Non-being, and that which is beyond both. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.37||

children.text: kasmāc ca hetos te tubhyaṃ na nameran namaskuryur he mahātman ! garīyase gurutarāya | yato brahmaṇo hiraṇyagarbhasyāpi ādi-kartā kāraṇam atas tasmād ādi-kartre | katham ete na namaskuryuḥ ? ato harṣādīnāṃ namaskārasya ca sthānaṃ tvam arho viṣaya ity arthaḥ | he 'nanta deveśa he jagan-nivāsa tvam akṣaraṃ tat param, yad vedānteṣu śrūyate | kiṃ tat ? sad asad iti | sad vidyamānam, asac ca yatra nāstīti buddhiḥ | ta upadhāna-bhūte sad-asatī yasyākṣarasya, yad-dvāreṇa sad asad ity upacaryate | paramārthatas tu sad-asatoḥ paraṃ tat akṣaraṃ yad akṣaraṃ veda-vido vadanti [Gītā 8.11] | tat tvam eva, nānyad ity abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_11.37||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'And why' — for what reason — should they not bow, i.e., should they not pay homage to You, O Great Soul (<s>Mahātman</s>)! — to You who are greater (<s>garīyas</s>), i.e., weightier, more venerable. Since You are the original creator (<s>ādi-kartṛ</s>), i.e., the cause, even of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — therefore to the original creator. How could these not bow down? Therefore You are the fitting, worthy object of joy, homage, etc. — this is the meaning. O Infinite One (<s>Ananta</s>)! O Lord of the gods (<s>Deveśa</s>)! O Abode of the universe (<s>Jagan-nivāsa</s>)! You are the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) — that Supreme, which is heard of in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts. What is that? Being and Non-being (<s>sat</s> and <s>asat</s>). '<s>Sat</s>' — that which exists, the manifest. '<s>Asat</s>' — that regarding which there is the cognition 'it does not exist.' Those two — Being and Non-being — serve as the substrata of the Imperishable; through them the Imperishable is figuratively spoken of as Being and Non-being. But in ultimate reality, that Imperishable is beyond (<s>para</s>) Being and Non-being — that Imperishable 'which the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> call the Imperishable' [<s>BhG</s> 8.11]. That You are, and nothing else — this is the purport. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.37||

children.text: punar api stauti -
tvam ādi-devaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇas
children.translated_text: You are the primal God, the ancient Person;

children.text: tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
children.translated_text: You are the supreme resting place of this universe;

children.text: vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
children.translated_text: You are the knower, the knowable, and the supreme abode;

children.text: tvayā tataṃ viśvam ananta-rūpa ||BhG_11.38||
children.translated_text: by You this universe is pervaded, O One of infinite forms! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.38||
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] He praises again —

children.text: tvam ādi-devo jagataḥ sraṣṭṛtvāt | puruṣaḥ, puri śayanāt purāṇaś cirantanas tvam evāsya viśvasya paraṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ nidhānaṃ nidhīyate 'smin jagat sarvaṃ mahā-pralayādāv iti | kiṃ ca, vettāsi, veditāsi sarvasyaiva vedya-jātasya | yac ca vedyaṃ vedanārhaṃ tac cāsi paraṃ ca dhāma paramaṃ padaṃ vaiṣṇavam | tvayā tataṃ vyāptaṃ viśvaṃ samastam | he 'nanta-rūpa ! anto na vidyate tava rūpāṇām ||BhGS_11.38||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] You are the primal God (<s>ādi-deva</s>) — because of being the creator of the world. The Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>) — because of lying in the city [of the body] (<s>puri śayanāt</s>). The ancient one (<s>purāṇa</s>) — the time-honored. You are the supreme (<s>para</s>), i.e., the exalted, resting place (<s>nidhāna</s>) of this universe — that in which the entire world is deposited at the time of the great dissolution etc. Moreover, You are the knower (<s>vettā</s>) — the cognizer of the entire realm of the knowable. And You are the knowable (<s>vedya</s>) — that which is worthy of being known — that too You are. And the supreme abode (<s>paraṃ dhāma</s>) — the supreme state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. By You this universe — the entirety — is pervaded (<s>tata</s>). O One of infinite forms (<s>ananta-rūpa</s>)! — there is no end to Your forms. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.38||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
vāyur yamo 'gnir varuṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: You are <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the Moon,

children.text: prajāpatis tvaṃ prapitāmahaś ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the Great-grandfather;

children.text: namo namas te 'stu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ
children.translated_text: salutations, salutations to You a thousand times!

children.text: punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te ||BhG_11.39||
children.translated_text: And again, once more — salutations, salutations to You! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.39||
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: vāyus tvaṃ yamaś cāgniḥ varuṇo 'pāṃ patiḥ śaśāṅkaś candramāḥ prajāpatis tvaṃ kaśyapādiḥ prapitāmahaś ca pitāmahasyāpi pitā prapitāmahaḥ, brahmaṇo 'pi pitā ity arthaḥ | namo namas te tubhyam astu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ | punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te | bahuśo namaskāra-kriyābhyāsāvṛtti-gaṇanaṃ kṛtva-sucocyate | punaś ca bhūyo 'pīti śraddhā-bhakta-yati-śayād aparitoṣam ātmano darśayati ||BhGS_11.39||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] You are <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), and <s>Yama</s> (Death), and <s>Agni</s> (Fire), and <s>Varuṇa</s>, the lord of waters, and the Moon (<s>Śaśāṅka</s>). You are <s>Prajāpati</s>, i.e., <s>Kaśyapa</s> and the others, and the Great-grandfather (<s>prapitāmaha</s>) — the father even of the Grandfather [<s>Brahmā</s>], the great-grandfather — meaning the father even of <s>Brahmā</s>. Salutations, salutations to You, a thousand times! And again, once more — salutations, salutations to You! The counting of the repeated acts of obeisance is expressed by the suffix '-<s>kṛtvas</s>.' 'And again, once more' — by this he shows his dissatisfaction [with the limited number of salutations], arising from the intensity of his faith and devotion. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.39||

children.text: tathā -
namaḥ purastād atha pṛṣṭhatas te
children.translated_text: Salutations from the front, and from behind —

children.text: namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
children.translated_text: salutations to You from every side, O All!

children.text: ananta-vīryāmita-vikramas tvaṃ
children.translated_text: Of infinite valor and immeasurable prowess,

children.text: sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ ||BhG_11.40||
children.translated_text: You pervade all; therefore You are all. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.40||
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Likewise —

children.text: namaḥ purastāt pūrvasyāṃ diśi tubhyam, atha pṛṣṭhatas te pṛṣṭhato 'pi ca te namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarvāsu dikṣu sarvatra sthitāya | he sarva ! ananta-vīryāmita-vikramo 'nantaṃ vīryam asya, amito vikramo 'sya | vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ vikramaḥ parākramaḥ | vīryavān api kaścit śatru-vadhādi-viṣaye na parākramate, manda-parākramo vā | tvaṃ tv ananta-vīryo 'mita-vikramaś cety ananta-vīryāmita-vikramaḥ | sarvaṃ samastaṃ jagat samāpnoṣi samyag ekenātmanā vyāpnoṣi yataḥ, tatas tasmād asi bhavasi sarvas tvam | tvayā vinābhūtaṃ na kiṃcid astīty abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_11.40||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Salutations from the front, i.e., in the eastern direction, to You; and from behind (<s>pṛṣṭhataḥ</s>), also from the back, salutations to You from every side, from all directions — to You who are present everywhere. O All (<s>Sarva</s>)! Of infinite valor and immeasurable prowess (<s>ananta-vīryāmita-vikrama</s>) — infinite is Your valor, immeasurable is Your prowess. Valor (<s>vīrya</s>) means capacity; prowess (<s>vikrama</s>) means valor in action. One may be valorous but may not exert prowess in matters such as slaying enemies, or may be of feeble prowess. But You are of infinite valor and immeasurable prowess — hence <s>ananta-vīryāmita-vikrama</s>. You pervade (<s>samāpnoṣi</s>), i.e., you thoroughly permeate, the entire universe with a single Self. Because of this, therefore You are all (<s>sarva</s>). The purport is: there is nothing whatsoever that exists apart from You. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.40||

children.text: yato 'haṃ tvan-māhātmyāparijñānād aparāddhaḥ | ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since I, not knowing Your greatness, have offended — therefore:

children.text: sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yad uktaṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever I have said presumptuously, thinking [You to be merely] a friend —

children.text: he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Yādava</s>! O friend!' —

children.text: ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ
children.translated_text: not knowing this majesty of Yours,

children.text: mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi ||BhG_11.41||
children.translated_text: through negligence or even through affection — ||<s>BhG</s> 11.41||

children.text: sakhā samāna-vayā iti matvā jñātvā viparīta-buddhyā prasabham abhibhūya prasahya yad uktaṃ he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti cājānatājñāninā mūḍhena | kim ajānatā ? ity āha - mahimānaṃ māhātmyaṃ tavedam īśvarasya viśva-rūpam | tavedaṃ mahimānam ajānateti vaiyadhikaraṇyena saṃbandhaḥ | tavemam iti pāṭho yady asti, tadā sāmānādhikaraṇyam eva | mayā pramādāt vikṣipta-cittatayā, praṇayena vāpi | praṇayo nāma sneha-nimitto visrambhaḥ | tenāpi kāraṇena yad uktavān asmi ||BhGS_11.41||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Thinking [You to be] a friend (<s>sakhā</s>), i.e., one of equal age, with a mistaken understanding — 'presumptuously' (<s>prasabham</s>), i.e., overriding propriety, overpowering [decorum] — whatever was said: 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Yādava</s>! O friend!' — by one who did not know (<s>ajānatā</s>), i.e., by an ignorant, deluded person. What did he not know? He says: this majesty (<s>mahimāna</s>), i.e., this greatness of Yours, the Lord — [namely] the cosmic form. 'Your majesty not knowing' — the connection is through grammatical non-apposition. If the reading is '<s>tavemam</s>' (this of yours), then it would be a case of grammatical apposition. By me — through negligence (<s>pramāda</s>), i.e., through distraction of mind; or even through affection (<s>praṇaya</s>). '<s>Praṇaya</s>' means intimate trust born of friendship — for that reason too, whatever I have said. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.41||

children.text: yac cāvahāsārtham asatkṛto 'si
children.translated_text: And if I have treated You disrespectfully, for the sake of jest,

children.text: vihāra-śayyāsana-bhojaneṣu |
children.translated_text: while at play, resting, sitting, or dining,

children.text: eko 'tha vāpy acyuta tat-samakṣaṃ
children.translated_text: whether alone or in the presence of others, O <s>Acyuta</s> —

children.text: tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam ||BhG_11.42||
children.translated_text: I ask Your forgiveness, You who are immeasurable. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.42||

children.text: yac cāvahāsārthaṃ parihāsa-prayojanāyāsatkṛtaḥ paribhūto 'si bhavasi | kva ? vihāra-śayyāsana-bhojaneṣu | viharaṇaṃ vihāraḥ pāda-vyāyāmaḥ, śayanaṃ śayyā, āsanam āsthāyikā, bhojanam adanam, ity eteṣu vihāra-śayyāsana-bhojaneṣu, ekaḥ parokṣaḥ sann asatkṛto 'si paribhūto 'si | athavāpi he 'cyuta ! tat samakṣam, tac-chabdaḥ kriyā-viśeṣaṇārthaḥ, pratyakṣaṃ vāsatkṛto 'si tat sarvam aparādha-jātaṃ kṣāmaye kṣamāṃ kāraye tvām aham aprameyaṃ pramāṇātītam ||BhGS_11.42||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'And whatever' — for the purpose of jest (<s>avahāsa</s>), i.e., for fun — You were treated disrespectfully (<s>asatkṛta</s>), i.e., slighted. Where? While at play (<s>vihāra</s>) — recreation, walking about; resting (<s>śayyā</s>) — lying down; sitting (<s>āsana</s>) — taking one's seat; or dining (<s>bhojana</s>) — eating — in these [situations]. When alone (<s>eka</s>), i.e., out of sight [of others], You were treated disrespectfully. Or alternatively, O <s>Acyuta</s>! In the presence of others (<s>tat-samakṣam</s>) — the word 'tat' qualifies the action — openly, You were treated disrespectfully. For all that mass of offenses, I ask Your forgiveness (<s>kṣāmaye</s>), i.e., I seek Your pardon — You who are immeasurable (<s>aprameya</s>), i.e., beyond the scope of any means of knowledge. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.42||

children.text: yatas tvam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Because You are —

children.text: pitāsi lokasya carācarasya
children.translated_text: You are the Father of this world, of the moving and the unmoving;

children.text: tvam asya pūjyaś ca gurur garīyān |
children.translated_text: You are the one to be worshipped and the teacher, the most venerable.

children.text: na tvat-samo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyo
children.translated_text: There is none equal to You — how then could there be another greater

children.text: loka-traye 'py apratima-prabhāva ||BhG_11.43||
children.translated_text: even in the three worlds, O One of incomparable power? ||<s>BhG</s> 11.43||

children.text: pitāsi janayitāsi lokasya prāṇi-jātasya carācarasya sthāvara-jaṅgamasya | na kevalaṃ tvam asya jagataḥ pitā | pūjyaś ca pūjārhaḥ, yato gurur garīyān gurutaraḥ | kasmād gurutaras tvam ity āha - na tvat-samas tvat-tulyo 'sti | na hīśvara-dvayaṃ saṃbhavati, aneke varatve vyavahārānupapatteḥ | tvat-sama eva tāvad anyo na saṃbhavati | kuta evānyo 'bhyadhikaḥ syāt loka-traye 'pi sarvasmin ? apratima-prabhāva ! pratimīyate yayā sā pratimā, na vidyate pratimā yasya tava prabhāvasya sa tvam apratima-prabhāvo he 'pratima-prabhāva niratiśaya-prabhāva ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_11.43||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] You are the Father (<s>pitā</s>), i.e., the progenitor, of the world, of all living beings, of the moving and unmoving (<s>carācara</s>), i.e., of the mobile and immobile. Not only are You the Father of this universe — You are also the one to be worshipped (<s>pūjya</s>), worthy of worship, because You are the teacher (<s>guru</s>), the most venerable (<s>garīyān</s>), i.e., the most weighty. Why are You the most venerable? He says: there is none equal to You (<s>tvat-sama</s>), i.e., none who is Your equal. For there cannot be two Lords, since [if there were,] the transaction of being supreme would be impossible for both. Not even one equal to You is possible — how then could there be another who is greater, even in the three worlds, in the entirety [of existence]? O One of incomparable power (<s>apratima-prabhāva</s>)! — that by which one is measured is a measure (<s>pratimā</s>); there is no measure for Your power — You are <s>apratima-prabhāva</s>, O One of incomparable power — meaning: of unsurpassed power. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.43||

children.text: yata evam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since this is so —

children.text: tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, bowing down, laying my body prostrate,

children.text: prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam |
children.translated_text: I beseech You, the Lord, the praiseworthy;

children.text: piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
children.translated_text: as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend,

children.text: priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum ||BhG_11.44||
children.translated_text: a beloved with a beloved — so deign to bear with [me], O God! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.44||

children.text: tasmāt praṇamya namaskṛtya, praṇidhāya prakarṣeṇa nīcair dhṛtvā kāyaṃ śarīram, prasādaye prasādaṃ kāraye tvām aham īśam īśitāram, īḍyaṃ stutyam | tvaṃ punaḥ putrasyāparādhaṃ pitā yathā kṣamate, sarvaṃ sakheva sakhyur aparādham, yathā vā priyaḥ priyāyā aparādhaṃ kṣamate | evam arhasi he deva ! soḍhuṃ prasahitum kṣantum ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_11.44||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, bowing down (<s>praṇamya</s>), i.e., having made obeisance; laying down (<s>praṇidhāya</s>), i.e., having placed low with great intensity, the body (<s>kāya</s>), i.e., the physical form; I beseech (<s>prasādaye</s>), i.e., I seek the grace of, You, the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), i.e., the sovereign; the praiseworthy (<s>īḍya</s>), i.e., worthy of praise. You, indeed — as a father (<s>pitā</s>) bears with the offense of a son, and as a friend (<s>sakhā</s>) bears with the offense of a friend, or as a beloved (<s>priya</s>) bears with the offense of a beloved — in the same way, deign (<s>arhasi</s>), O God (<s>Deva</s>)! to bear with (<s>soḍhum</s>), to tolerate, to forgive — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.44||

children.text: adṛṣṭa-pūrvaṃ hṛṣito 'smi dṛṣṭvā
children.translated_text: Having seen what was never seen before, I am filled with joy,

children.text: bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
children.translated_text: yet my mind is trembling with fear;

children.text: tad eva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: show me that very [familiar] form, O God!

children.text: prasīda deveśa jagan-nivāsa ||BhG_11.45||
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.45||

children.text: adṛṣṭa-pūrvaṃ na kadācid api dṛṣṭa-pūrvam idaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ tava mayānyairvā, tat ahaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣito 'smi | bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ manaḥ me | atas tad eva me mama darśaya he deva rūpaṃ yat matsakham | prasīda deveśa, jagan-nivāsa jagato nivāso jagan-nivāsaḥ, he jagan-nivāsa ||BhGS_11.45||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Never seen before' — never previously seen — this cosmic form of Yours, by me or by any others. Having seen it, I am filled with joy (<s>hṛṣita</s>). Yet my mind is trembling (<s>pravyathita</s>) with fear. Therefore, show me, O God, that very form — the one familiar to me as [Your] companion. Be gracious (<s>prasīda</s>), O Lord of the gods (<s>Deveśa</s>)! O Abode of the universe (<s>Jagan-nivāsa</s>) — You who are the abode of the world. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.45||

children.text: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakra-hastam
children.translated_text: I wish to see You crowned, bearing the mace, with discus in hand,

children.text: icchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭum ahaṃ tathaiva |
children.translated_text: just as before;

children.text: tenaiva rūpeṇa catur-bhujena
children.translated_text: assume that very four-armed form,

children.text: sahasra-bāho bhava viśva-mūrte ||BhG_11.46||
children.translated_text: O thousand-armed One, O cosmic-formed One! ||<s>BhG</s> 11.46||

children.text: kirīṭinaṃ kirīṭavantaṃ tathā gadinaṃ gadāvantaṃ cakra-hastam icchāmi tvāṃ prārthaye tvāṃ draṣṭum aham, tathaiva pūrvavad ity arthaḥ | yata evam, tasmāt tenaiva rūpeṇa vasudeva-putra-rūpeṇa catur-bhujena, sahasra-bāho ! vārtamānikena viśva-rūpeṇa, bhava viśva-mūrte | upasaṃhṛtya viśva-rūpam, tenaiva rūpeṇa bhavety arthaḥ ||BhGS_11.46||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Crowned' (<s>kirīṭinam</s>) — wearing a crown; likewise 'bearing the mace' (<s>gadinam</s>) — possessing a mace; 'with discus in hand' — I wish, I desire to see You; just as before (<s>tathaiva</s>), as formerly — this is the meaning. Since this is so, therefore, with that very form — the form of the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> — four-armed; O thousand-armed One! — [withdrawing] the present cosmic form; assume [that form], O cosmic-formed One (<s>Viśva-mūrte</s>)! Having withdrawn the cosmic form, assume that very [familiar] form — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 11.46||

children.text: arjunaṃ bhītam upalabhya, upasaṃhṛtya viśva-rūpam, priya-vacanena āśvāsayan śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Perceiving <s>Arjuna</s> to be frightened, having withdrawn the cosmic form, and consoling him with kind words, the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ
children.translated_text: By me, being gracious, this supreme form has been shown to you, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitam ātma-yogāt |
children.translated_text: through my own <s>yoga</s> [power];

children.text: tejo-mayaṃ viśvam anantam
children.translated_text: this form, made of radiance, universal, infinite,

children.text: ādyaṃ yan me tvad-anyena na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam ||BhG_11.47||
children.translated_text: and primeval — which has never before been seen by anyone other than you. ||<s>BhG</s> 11.47||

children.text: mayā prasannena, prasādo nāma tvayy anugraha-buddhiḥ, tadvatā prasannena mayā tava | he 'rjuna ! idaṃ paraṃ rūpaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ darśitam ātma-yogād ātmana aiśvaryasya sāmarthyāt | tejo-mayaṃ tejaḥ-prāyaṃ viśvaṃ samastam anantam anta-rahitaṃ ādau bhavam ādyaṃ, yad rūpaṃ me mama tvad-anyena tvatto 'nyena kenacin na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam ||BhGS_11.47||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] By Me who am pleased — 'being pleased' means having the disposition of grace toward you — by Me thus pleased, for you, O <s>Arjuna</s>, this supreme form, the cosmic form, has been shown through My own yoga-power (<s>ātma-yoga</s>), through My own lordly capacity. [It is] resplendent — predominantly luminous; universal — complete; infinite — without limit; primeval — existing from the beginning. This form of Mine has never been seen before by anyone other than you. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.47 //

children.text: ātmano mama rūpa-darśanena kṛtārtha eva tvaṃ saṃvṛtta iti tat stauti -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] You have indeed become fulfilled by seeing My own form — thus He praises it:

children.text: na veda yajñādhyayanair na dānair
children.translated_text: Neither through the Vedas nor through sacrificial study, neither through charity,

children.text: na ca kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ |
children.translated_text: nor through rituals, nor through fierce austerities,

children.text: evaṃ-rūpaḥ śakya ahaṃ nṛ-loke
children.translated_text: can I, in this form, in the world of men,

children.text: draṣṭuṃ tvad-anyena kuru-pravīra ||BhG_11.48||
children.translated_text: be seen by anyone other than you, O hero of the <s>Kurus</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 11.48 //

children.text: na veda-yajñādhyayanaiś caturṇām api vedānām adhyayanair yathāvat yajñādhyayanaiś ca - vedādhyayanair eva yajñādhyayanasya siddhatvāt pṛthak yajñādhyayana-grahaṇaṃ yajña-vijñānopalakṣaṇārtham - tathā na dānais tulā-puruṣādibhiḥ, na ca kriyābhir agnihotrādibhiḥ śrautādibhiḥ, nāpi tapobhir ugraiś cāndrāyaṇādibhir ugrair ghoraiḥ, evaṃ-rūpo yathā-darśitaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ yasya so 'ham evaṃ-rūpo na śakyo 'haṃ nṛ-loke manuṣya-loke draṣṭuṃ tvad-anyena tvatto 'nyena kura-pravīra ||BhGS_11.48||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Not through Vedic sacrificial study — through the study of all four Vedas — <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajuḥ</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> — and their sacrificial study; since mastery of sacrificial study is accomplished by Vedic study itself, the separate mention of 'sacrificial study' is for the purpose of indicating knowledge of the science of sacrifice. Likewise, not through charity — gifts of land, gold, cows, and the like. Nor through rituals — <s>Agnihotra</s> and other <s>Śrauta</s> rites. Nor through fierce austerities — severe [practices] like the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> fast and the like, which are extreme, terrible. I, who am of such a form — having the cosmic form as shown — cannot be seen in the world of men, the human world, by anyone other than you, O hero of the <s>Kurus</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.48 //

children.text: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍha-bhāvo
children.translated_text: Let there be no distress and no bewilderment for you,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoram īdṛṅ mamedam |
children.translated_text: having seen this terrible form of Mine;

children.text: vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṃ
children.translated_text: free from fear, with a gladdened heart, once again

children.text: tad eva me rūpam idaṃ prapaśya ||BhG_11.49||
children.translated_text: behold this very form of Mine. // <s>BhG</s> 11.49 //

children.text: mā te vyathā mā bhūt te bhayam, mā ca vimūḍha-bhāvo vimūḍha-cittatā, dṛṣṭvopalabhya rūpaṃ ghoram īdṛk yathā-darśitaṃ mamedam | vyapeta-bhīr vigata-bhayaḥ, prīta-manāś ca san punar bhūyas tvaṃ tad eva catur-bhujaṃ rūpaṃ śaṅkha-cakra-gadādharaṃ taveṣṭaṃ rūpam idaṃ prapaśya ||BhGS_11.49||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Let there be no distress for you' — let there be no fear for you, nor bewilderment, i.e., mental confusion, having seen — having perceived — this terrible form of Mine as shown. Being free from fear, with gone-away fear, and with a gladdened heart — behold once again this very form of Mine — the four-armed form bearing conch, discus, and mace — [that form] which is dear to you. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.49 //

children.text: saṃjaya uvāca -
ity arjunaṃ vāsudevas tathoktvā
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken to <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>

children.text: svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: showed His own form again;

children.text: āśvāsayām āsa ca bhītam enaṃ
children.translated_text: and reassured the frightened one,

children.text: bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapur mahātmā ||BhG_11.50||
children.translated_text: the Great Soul having resumed His gentle form. // <s>BhG</s> 11.50 //
<s>Sañjaya</s> said:

children.text: ity evam arjunaṃ vāsudevas tathā-bhūtaṃ vacanam uktvā, svakaṃ vasudevasya gṛhe jātaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa darśitavān bhūyaḥ punaḥ | āśvāsayāmāsa ca āśvāsitavān bhītam enam, bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapuḥ prasanna-deho mahātmā ||BhGS_11.50||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having thus spoken such words to <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s> showed His own form — the form born in the house of <s>Vasudeva</s> — showed [it] again, once more. And He reassured the frightened one — [namely <s>Arjuna</s>] — the Great Soul, having resumed a gentle body, a serene form. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.50 //

children.text: arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana |
children.translated_text: Seeing this human form of Yours, gentle [and] pleasing, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: idānīm asmi saṃvṛttaḥ sa-cetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ ||BhG_11.51||
children.translated_text: I have now become composed, with my mind restored to its natural state. // <s>BhG</s> 11.51 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ mat-sakhaṃ prasannaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana, idānīm, adhunāsmi saṃvṛttaḥ saṃjātaḥ | kim ? sa-cetāḥ prasanna-cittaḥ prakṛtiṃ svabhāvaṃ gataś cāsmi ||BhGS_11.51||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Seeing this human form of Yours, [the form of] my friend, serene, gentle, O <s>Janārdana</s> — now, at this moment, I have become composed. What [has happened]? I have become one with a settled mind (<s>sa-cetāḥ</s>), with a tranquil mind, and I have returned to my own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), my natural state. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.51 //

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: sudurdarśam idaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama |
children.translated_text: This form of Mine that you have seen is very difficult to behold;

children.text: devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṃ darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||BhG_11.52||
children.translated_text: even the gods are ever desirous of a vision of this form. // <s>BhG</s> 11.52 //

children.text: sudurdarśaṃ suṣṭhu duḥkhena darśanam asyeti sudurdarśam | idaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama, devā apy asya mama rūpasya nityaṃ sarvadā darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ | darśanepsavo 'pi na tvam iva dṛṣṭavantaḥ, na drakṣyanti cety abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_11.52||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Very difficult to behold' (<s>sudurdarśam</s>) — that whose seeing is extremely difficult to achieve — thus [it is] 'very difficult to behold.' This form of Mine you have seen. Even the gods are ever, always, desirous of a vision of this form of Mine. Even though desirous of seeing [it], they have not seen [it] as you have, nor will they see [it] — this is the purport. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.52 //

children.text: kasmāt ? -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Why is that?

children.text: nāhaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na cejyayā |
children.translated_text: Neither through the Vedas, nor through austerity, nor through charity, nor through sacrifice

children.text: śakya evaṃ-vidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi māṃ yathā ||BhG_11.53||
children.translated_text: can I be seen in this form, as you have seen Me. // <s>BhG</s> 11.53 //

children.text: nāhaṃ vedaiḥ ṛg-yajuḥ-sāmātharva-vedaiś caturbhir api, na tapasā ugreṇa cāndrāyaṇādinā, na dānena go-bhū-hiraṇyādinā, na cejyayā yajñena pūjayā vā śakyaḥ evaṃ-vidho yathā-darśita-prakāro draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi māṃ yathā tvam ||BhGS_11.53||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Not through the Vedas — not even through all four Vedas, <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajuḥ</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s>; not through austerity — fierce [austerity] such as the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> fast and the like; not through charity — of cows, land, gold, and the like; and not through sacrifice (<s>ijyā</s>) — through <s>yajña</s> or worship. I cannot be seen in this form — in the manner in which the cosmic form has been shown — as you have seen Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.53 //
