children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ śakya ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] How, then, can [I] be [seen]? It is said:

children.text: bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃ-vidho 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: But through exclusive devotion (<s>ananya-bhakti</s>), O <s>Arjuna</s>, I, in this form, can be

children.text: jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa ||BhG_11.54||
children.translated_text: known, truly seen, and entered into, O scorcher of foes. // <s>BhG</s> 11.54 //

children.text: bhaktyā tu kiṃ-viśiṣṭayā ity āha - ananyayāpṛthag-bhūtayā, bhagavato 'nyatra pṛthaṅ na kadācid api yā bhavati sā tv ananyā bhaktiḥ | sarvair api karaṇaiḥ vāsudevād anyan na upalabhyate yayā, sānanyā bhaktiḥ, tayā bhaktyā śakyo 'ham evaṃ-vidho viśva-rūpa-prakāro he 'rjuna, jñātuṃ śāstrataḥ | na kevalaṃ jñātuṃ śāstrataḥ, draṣṭuṃ ca sākṣāt-kartuṃ tattvena tattvataḥ, praveṣṭuṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca gantuṃ parantapa ||BhGS_11.54||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Through devotion' — but of what kind? He says: exclusive (<s>ananyā</s>) — not directed elsewhere; [devotion] that never exists separately from, i.e., apart from, the Blessed Lord — that is exclusive devotion. [Devotion] by which, through all the organs, nothing other than <s>Vāsudeva</s> is perceived — that is exclusive devotion. Through such devotion, I, of this form — of the cosmic form as shown — O <s>Arjuna</s>, can be known, i.e., known through scripture. Not merely known through scripture, but also truly seen, i.e., directly realized in truth. And entered into, i.e., attained in liberation, O scorcher of foes. // <s>BhGS</s> 11.54 //

children.text: adhunā sarvasya gītā-śāstrasya sāra-bhūto 'rtho niḥśreyasārtho 'nuṣṭheyatvena samuccityocyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now the meaning that constitutes the essence of the entire <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>, serving as the supreme good, is gathered together as [something] to be practiced:

children.text: mat-karma-kṛn mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who works for Me, who holds Me as the supreme [goal], who is devoted to Me, free from attachment,

children.text: nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava ||BhG_11.55||
children.translated_text: and free from enmity toward all beings — that one comes to Me, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 11.55 //

children.text: mat-karma-kṛn mad-arthaṃ karma mat-karma, tat karotīti mat-karma-kṛt | mat-paramaḥ - karoti bhṛtyaḥ svāmi-karma, na tv ātmanaḥ paramā pretya gantavyā gatir iti svāminaṃ pratipadyate | ayaṃ tu mat-karma-kṛn mām eva paramāṃ gatiṃ pratipadyate iti mat-paramaḥ, ahaṃ paramaḥ parā gatir yasya so 'yaṃ mat-paramaḥ | tathā mad-bhakto mām eva sarva-prakāraiḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ sarvātmanā sarvotsāhena bhajate iti mad-bhaktaḥ | saṅga-varjito dhana-putra-mitra-kalatra-bandhu-vargeṣu saṅga-varjitaḥ saṅgaḥ prītiḥ snehas tad-varjitaḥ | nirvairo nirgata-vairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu śatru-bhāva-rahita ātmano ' tyantāpakāra-pravṛtteṣv api | ya īdṛśo mad-bhaktaḥ sa mām eti | aham eva tasya parā gatiḥ, nānyā gatiḥ kācit bhavati | ayaṃ tavopadeśa iṣṭo mayā upadiṣṭaḥ | he pāṇḍāva ! iti ||BhGS_11.55||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'One who works for Me' (<s>mat-karma-kṛt</s>) — work done for My sake is 'My work'; one who does that is 'one who works for Me.' 'Who holds Me as the supreme' (<s>mat-parama</s>) — a servant performs the work of his master, yet he does not consider the master to be the supreme destination to be reached after death. But this one who works for Me considers Me alone to be the supreme destination — hence 'Me-as-supreme'; I am the supreme, the highest goal for this person. Likewise, 'devoted to Me' (<s>mad-bhakta</s>) — one who worships Me alone through every means, with all one's being, with all one's enthusiasm — that one is 'devoted to Me.' 'Free from attachment' (<s>saṅga-varjita</s>) — free from attachment, i.e., affection, clinging love, toward wealth, sons, friends, wife, and relatives. 'Free from enmity' (<s>nirvaira</s>) — free from hostility toward all beings, devoid of the attitude of enmity, even toward those who are engaged in extreme harm to oneself. One who is such a devotee of Mine — that one comes to Me. I alone am that one's supreme destination; there is no other destination for that person. This is the teaching that I have instructed for you, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>! // <s>BhGS</s> 11.55 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary on the Blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṃkara Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda</s>,

children.text: ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||11||
children.translated_text: the supreme wandering ascetic (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s>), [ends] the eleventh chapter. // 11 //

children.text: BhG 12
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 12

children.text: atha bhakti-yogo nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now [begins] the twelfth chapter called <s>Bhakti-yoga</s> (the Yoga of Devotion).

children.text: (śrī-śaṅkarācārya-bhagavat-pāda-kṛta-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavat-pāda</s>)

children.text: dvitīyādhyāya-prabhṛtiṣu vibhūty-anteṣu adhyāyeṣu paramātmano brahmaṇo 'kṣarasya vidhvasta-sarvopādhi-viśeṣasyopāsanam uktam | sarva-yogaiśvarya-sarva-jñāna-śaktimat-sattvopādher īśvarasya tatra copāsanaṃ tatra tatroktam | viśva-rūpādhyāye tv aiśvaram ādyaṃ samasta-jagad-ātma-rūpaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ tvadīyaṃ darśitam upāsanārtham eva tvayā | tac ca darśayitvā uktavān asi mat-karma-kṛd [Gītā 11.55] ity ādi | ato 'ham anayor ubhayoḥ pakṣayor viśiṣṭatara-bubhutsayā tvāṃ pṛcchāmīty arjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] In the chapters beginning with the second and ending with the <s>Vibhūti</s> [chapter], the worship of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), <s>Brahman</s>, the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), devoid of all limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), has been taught. And the worship of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), conditioned by the limiting adjunct of <s>sattva</s> endowed with all yogic powers and all-knowing capacity, has also been taught in various places. In the chapter on the Cosmic Form, the lordly, primeval, universal cosmic form — the form that is the Self of the entire universe — was shown by You for the very purpose of meditation. And having shown that, You said 'one who works for Me' [<s>Gītā</s> 11.55] etc. Therefore, I, wishing to know which of these two alternatives is superior, ask You — thus <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Those devotees who, being ever steadfast, worship You,

children.text: ye cāpy akṣaram avyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yoga-vittamāḥ ||BhG_12.1||
children.translated_text: and those also who [worship] the Imperishable Unmanifest — among these, who are the greatest knowers of yoga? // <s>BhG</s> 12.1 //

children.text: evam ity atītānantara-lokena uktam arthaṃ parāmṛśati mat-karma-kṛd ity ādinā | evaṃ satata-yuktāḥ, nairantaryeṇa bhagavat-karmādau yathokte 'rthe samāhitāḥ santaḥ pravṛttā ity arthaḥ | ye bhaktā ananya-śaraṇāḥ santas tvāṃ yathā-darśitaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ paryupāsate dhyāyanti | ye cānye 'pi tyakta-sarveṣaṇāḥ saṃnyasta-sarva-karmāṇo yathā-viśeṣitaṃ brahmākṣaraṃ nirasta-sarvopādhitvād avyaktam akaraṇa-gocaram | yad dhi karaṇa-gocaraṃ tad vyaktam ucyate, añjer dhātos tat-karmakatvāt | idaṃ tv akṣaraṃ tad-viparītam, śiṣṭau ca ucyamānair viśeṣaṇair viśiṣṭam, tad ye cāpi paryupāsate, teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ madhye ke yogi-vittamāḥ ? ke 'tiśayena yoga-vida ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_12.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Thus' (<s>evam</s>) — by this word, he refers back to the meaning stated in the immediately preceding passage, namely 'one who works for Me' [<s>Gītā</s> 11.55] etc. 'Ever steadfast' — those who are continuously, uninterruptedly, concentrated upon and engaged in the devotional work etc. of the Blessed Lord as described — this is the meaning. 'Those devotees' — those who have no other refuge, who worship You, the cosmic form as shown, [who] meditate [upon You]. 'And those also' — others who, having abandoned all desires and renounced all actions, [worship] the Imperishable <s>Brahman</s> as specifically described — unmanifest because it is beyond the range of the senses, since that which is within the range of the senses is called 'manifest,' the root <s>añj</s> taking it as its object. But this Imperishable is the opposite of that — and is further qualified by the attributes stated below. Those who also worship that — among both these groups, who are the greatest knowers of yoga? Who are the most excellent knowers of yoga — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.1 //

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca - ye tv akṣaropāsakāḥ samyag-darśino nivṛttaiṣaṇās te tāvat tiṣṭhantu | tān prati yad vaktavyam, tad upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ | ye tv itare -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The Blessed Lord said: As for those who worship the Imperishable, the seers of right vision, who have abandoned all desires — let them stand aside for now. What is to be said regarding them, We shall say later below. But those others —

children.text: mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nitya-yuktā upāsate |
children.translated_text: Those who, fixing their minds on Me, worship Me, being ever steadfast,

children.text: śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ ||BhG_12.2||
children.translated_text: endowed with supreme faith — they are considered by Me to be the most accomplished in yoga. // <s>BhG</s> 12.2 //

children.text: mayi viśva-rūpe parameśvara āveśya samādhāya mano ye bhaktāḥ santaḥ, māṃ sarva-yoge varāṇām adhīśvaraṃ sarvajñaṃ vimukta-rāgādi-kleśa-timira-dṛṣṭim, nitya-yuktā atītānantarādhyāyāntokta-ślokārtha-nyāyena satata-yuktāḥ santa upāsate śraddhayā parayā prakṛṣṭayopetāḥ, te me mama matā abhipretā yuktatamā iti | nairantaryeṇa hi te mac-cittatayāho-rātram ativāhayanti | ato yuktaṃ tān prati yuktatamā iti vaktum ||BhGS_12.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those devotees who, fixing — concentrating — their minds on Me, the Supreme Lord of cosmic form, worship Me, the supreme Lord of all yoga-powers, the all-knowing one, whose vision is free from the darkness of afflictions such as desire and the rest — being ever steadfast, i.e., continuously concentrated in the manner described at the end of the preceding chapter, endowed with supreme faith, i.e., possessed of the most excellent faith — they are, in My opinion, the most accomplished in yoga. For they indeed pass their days and nights with their minds fixed on Me. Therefore, it is fitting to say of them 'the most accomplished in yoga.' // <s>BhGS</s> 12.2 //

children.text: kim itare yuktatamā na bhavanti ? na | kiṃtu tān prati yad vaktavyam, tac chṛṇu -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Are the others, then, not the most accomplished in yoga? No, [they are not inferior]. But what is to be said regarding them — listen:

children.text: ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: But those who worship the Imperishable, the Indefinable, the Unmanifest,

children.text: sarvatra-gam acintyaṃ ca kūṭastham acalaṃ dhruvam ||BhG_12.3||
children.translated_text: the All-Pervading, the Inconceivable, the Unchanging, the Immovable, the Constant — // <s>BhG</s> 12.3 //

children.text:
ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam, avyaktatvād aśabda-gocareti na nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyate, ato 'nirdeśyam | avyaktaṃ na kenāpi pramāṇena vyajyata ity avyaktaṃ paryupāsate pari samantād upāsate | upāsanaṃ nāma yathā-śāstram upāsyasyārthasya viṣayī-karaṇena sāmīpyam upagamya taila-dhārāvat samāna-pratyaya-pravāheṇa dīrgha-kālaṃ yad āsanam, tad upāsanam ācakṣate | akṣarasya viśeṣaṇam āha - sarvatra-gaṃ vyomavad vyāpy acintyaṃ cāvyaktatvād acintyam | yad dhi karaṇa-gocaram, tan manasāpi cintyam, tad-viparītatvād acintyam akṣaram, kūṭa-sthaṃ dṛśyamāna-guṇam antar-doṣaṃ vastu kūṭam | kūṭa-rūpam kūṭa-sākṣyam ity ādau kūṭa-śabdaḥ prasiddho loke | tathā cāvidyādy-aneka-saṃsāra-bījam antar-doṣavan māyā-vyākṛtādi-śabda-vācyatayā māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ
tu maheśvaram [ŚvetU 4.10], mama māyā duratyayā [Gītā 7.14] ity ādau prasiddhaṃ yat tat kūṭam, tasmin kūṭe sthitaṃ kūṭa-sthaṃ tad-adhyakṣatayā | athavā, rāśir iva sthitaṃ kūṭa-stham ata evācalam | yasmād acalam, tasmād dhruvam, nityam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_12.3||
children.translated_text: [Shankar's commentary:] Those who worship the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), the indescribable — because it is unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>), it is beyond the range of words, hence it cannot be described, therefore it is 'indescribable.' The unmanifest — that which is not revealed by any means of knowledge — thus it is unmanifest — they worship, they meditate upon from all sides. Worship (<s>upāsana</s>) means: having approached proximity to the object of worship as prescribed by scripture, by making it the content [of one's meditation], and sitting for a long time with a continuous flow of identical cognitions, like a stream of oil — that is what they call worship. He states the qualifications of the imperishable: all-pervading — pervading like space; and inconceivable — because it is unmanifest, it is inconceivable. For that which is within the range of the sense-organs can be thought of even by the mind; because the imperishable is the opposite of that, it is inconceivable. <s>Kūṭa-stha</s> (immovable) — a thing that has visible qualities but internal defects is called <s>kūṭa</s> (deceptive). The word <s>kūṭa</s> is well-known in common usage in expressions like 'of deceptive form,' 'of deceptive witness,' etc. And similarly, that which is the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) consisting of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest, having internal defects, designated by words such as '<s>māyā</s>-evolved' etc. — as is well-known in passages like 'Know <s>māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), and the wielder of <s>māyā</s> to be the Great Lord' [<s>ŚvetU</s> 4.10], 'My <s>māyā</s> is difficult to overcome' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.14] — that is <s>kūṭa</s>; established in that <s>kūṭa</s> means <s>kūṭa-stha</s>, as presiding over it. Or, standing like a heap — <s>kūṭa-stha</s> — and therefore immovable (<s>acala</s>). Because it is immovable, therefore it is permanent (<s>dhruva</s>), eternal — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.3 //

children.text: saṃniyamyendriya-grāmaṃ sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Completely restraining the group of senses, with equanimity everywhere,

children.text: te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||BhG_12.4||
children.translated_text: they attain Me alone, devoted to the welfare of all beings. // <s>BhG</s> 12.4 //

children.text: saṃniyamya samyak niyamya upasaṃhṛtya indriya-grāmam indriya-samudāyaṃ sarvatra sarvasmin kāle sama-buddhayaḥ samā tulyā buddhir yeṣām iṣṭāniṣṭa-prāptau te sama-buddhayaḥ | te ye evaṃ-vidhās te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ | na tu teṣāṃ vaktavyaṃ kiṃcit māṃ te prāpnuvantīti | jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam iti hy uktam | na hi bhagavat-svarūpāṇāṃ satāṃ yuktatamatvam ayuktatamatvaṃ vā vācyam ||BhGS_12.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having completely restrained — having properly controlled, withdrawn — the group of senses, the aggregate of senses; with equanimity everywhere — at all times, those whose intellect is equal, the same, in the attainment of the desirable and undesirable — they have equal intellect. Those who are of such nature — they attain Me alone, devoted to the welfare of all beings. But nothing needs to be said about them [separately] that they attain Me, for it has been stated: 'The man of knowledge is My very Self — such is My view' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.18]. Indeed, for those who are of the very nature of the Blessed Lord, it is not proper to speak of being most devoted or least devoted. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.4 //

children.text: kiṃ tu -
children.translated_text: However —

children.text: kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām avyaktāsakta-cetasām |
children.translated_text: Greater is the difficulty for those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest,

children.text: avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṃ dehavadbhir avāpyate ||BhG_12.5||
children.translated_text: for the unmanifest goal is attained with hardship by the embodied. // <s>BhG</s> 12.5 //

children.text: kleśo 'dhikataraḥ | yadyapi mat-karmādi-parāṇāṃ kleśo 'dhika eva | kleśo 'dhikataras tv akṣarātmanāṃ paramārtha-darśināṃ dehābhimāna-parityāga-nimittaḥ | avyaktāsakta-cetasām avyakta āsaktaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ te 'vyaktāsakta-cetasas teṣām avyaktāsakta-cetasām | avyaktā hi yasmād yā gatir akṣarātmikā duḥkhaṃ sā dehavadbhir dehābhimānavadbhir avāpyate | ataḥ kleśo 'dhikataraḥ | akṣaropāsakānāṃ yad vartanam, tad upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ ||BhGS_12.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The difficulty is greater. Although for those devoted to My works and the rest, the difficulty is indeed great, the difficulty is greater for those of the nature of the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), for those who see the highest truth — on account of the need to abandon identification with the body. For those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest — those whose consciousness is attached to the unmanifest — for them the difficulty is greater. For indeed, the unmanifest goal — the path whose nature is the imperishable — is attained with hardship by the embodied, by those who have identification with the body. Therefore the difficulty is greater. We shall describe below the conduct of the worshippers of the imperishable. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.5 //

children.text: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-parāḥ |
children.translated_text: But those who, renouncing all actions in Me, devoted to Me as the supreme,

children.text: ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate ||BhG_12.6||
children.translated_text: by undivided <s>yoga</s> (discipline), meditate upon Me and worship [Me] — // <s>BhG</s> 12.6 //

children.text: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayīśvare saṃnyasya mat-parā ahaṃ paro yeṣāṃ te mat-parāḥ santo 'nanyenaivāvidyamānam anyat ālambanaṃ viśva-rūpaṃ devam ātmānaṃ muktvā yasya so 'nanyas tenānanyenaiva | kena ? yogena samādhinā māṃ dhyāyantaś cintayanta upāsate ||BhGS_12.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But those who, renouncing all actions in Me, the Lord — those for whom I am the supreme (<s>mat-parāḥ</s>) — being devoted to Me as the supreme, by undivided [<s>yoga</s>] — [meaning] there is no other support; having given up every other object [of meditation] except the cosmic-formed (<s>viśva-rūpa</s>) God, the Self — that which has no other is undivided, by that very undivided [<s>yoga</s>]. By what? By <s>yoga</s>, i.e., by <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) — meditating upon Me, contemplating Me — they worship. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.6 //

children.text: teṣāṃ kim ? -
children.translated_text: What happens for them? —

children.text: teṣām ahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt |
children.translated_text: For them, I am the deliverer from the ocean of death and <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration),

children.text: bhavāmi nacirāt pārtha mayy āveśita-cetasām ||BhG_12.7||
children.translated_text: before long, O <s>Pārtha</s>, for those whose minds are fixed on Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.7 //

children.text: teṣāṃ mad-upāsanaika-parāṇām aham īśvaraḥ samuddhartā | kutaḥ ? ity āha - mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarān mṛtyu-yuktaḥ saṃsāro mṛtyu-saṃsāraḥ, sa eva sāgara iva sāgaraḥ, dustaratvāt, tasmāt mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt ahaṃ teṣāṃ samuddhartā bhavāmi na cirāt | kiṃ tarhi ? kṣipram eva he pārtha, mayi āveśita-cetasāṃ mayi viśva-rūpa āveśitaṃ samāhitaṃ ceto yeṣāṃ te mayy āveśita-cetasas teṣām ||BhGS_12.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] For them, who are solely devoted to worshipping Me, I, the Lord, am the deliverer. From what? — he says — from the ocean of death and <s>saṃsāra</s>: <s>saṃsāra</s> conjoined with death is 'death-<s>saṃsāra</s>'; that very thing is like an ocean (<s>sāgara</s>), because it is difficult to cross — from that ocean of death and <s>saṃsāra</s>, I am their deliverer. I become [their deliverer] not after a long time, but rather quickly, O <s>Pārtha</s> — for those whose minds are fixed on Me, whose consciousness is directed toward and concentrated on Me, the cosmic-formed (<s>viśva-rūpa</s>) — for them. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.7 //

children.text: yata evam, tasmāt -
children.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya |
children.translated_text: Fix your mind on Me alone, let your intellect dwell in Me;

children.text: nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||BhG_12.8||
children.translated_text: you shall abide in Me alone hereafter — there is no doubt. // <s>BhG</s> 12.8 //

children.text: mayy eva viśva-rūpa īśvare manaḥ saṃkalpa-vikalpātmakaṃ ādhatsva sthāpaya | mayy evādhyavasāyaṃ kurvatīṃ buddhim ādhatsva niveśaya | tatas te kiṃ syād iti sṛṇu - nivasiṣyasi nivatsyasi niścayena mad-ātmanā mayi nivāsaṃ kariṣyasi | evātaḥ śarīra-pātād ūrdhvam | na saṃśayaḥ, saṃśayo 'tra na kartavyaḥ ||BhGS_12.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] On Me alone — on the Lord of cosmic form (<s>viśva-rūpa</s>) — fix your mind, which is of the nature of thought and deliberation — place it, establish it. In Me alone — cause your intellect, which makes determinations, to enter — fix it, place it [in Me]. Then what shall be yours — hear: you shall abide — you shall dwell; assuredly, with your self identified with Me, you shall make your abode in Me. Thus, after the fall of the body, hereafter. There is no doubt — no doubt should be entertained here. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.8 //

children.text: atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
children.translated_text: Now, if you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me,

children.text: abhyāsa-yogena tato mām icchāptuṃ dhanañjaya ||BhG_12.9||
children.translated_text: then seek to attain Me by the <s>yoga</s> (discipline) of repeated practice, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 12.9 //

children.text: atha evaṃ yathāvocaṃ tathā mayi cittaṃ samādhātuṃ sthāpayituṃ sthiram acalaṃ na śaknoṣi cet, tataḥ paścād abhyāsa-yogena | cittasyaikasmin ālambane sarvataḥ samāhṛtya punaḥ punaḥ sthāpanam abhyāsaḥ | tat-pūrvako yogaḥ samādhāna-lakṣaṇas tenābhyāsa-yogena māṃ viśva-rūpam iccha prārthayasva āptuṃ prāptum | he dhanañjaya ||BhGS_12.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, if you are unable to fix your mind — to establish it — steadily, without wavering, on Me as I have described, then afterwards, by the <s>yoga</s> of repeated practice: the repeated establishing of the mind on a single object after withdrawing it from everywhere — that is practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>). The <s>yoga</s> characterized by mental concentration, preceded by that [practice] — by that <s>yoga</s> of practice, seek — desire — to attain Me, to reach Me, the cosmic-formed (<s>viśva-rūpa</s>). O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>! // <s>BhGS</s> 12.9 //

children.text: abhyāse 'py asamartho 'si mat-karma-paramo bhava |
children.translated_text: If you are unable even in practice, be one whose supreme aim is action for Me;

children.text: mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi ||BhG_12.10||
children.translated_text: even performing actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection. // <s>BhG</s> 12.10 //

children.text: abhyāse 'py asamartho 'sy aśakto 'si, tarhi mat-karma-paramo bhava mad-arthaṃ karma mat-karma tat-paramaḥ mat-karma-paramaḥ, mat-karma-pradhāna ity arthaḥ | abhyāsena vinā mad-artham api karmāṇi kevalaṃ kurvan siddhiṃ sattva-śuddhi-yoga-jñāna-prāpti-dvāreṇāvāpsyasi ||BhGS_12.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If you are unable even in practice — if you are incapable — then be one whose supreme aim is action for Me: action performed for My sake is 'action for Me'; one for whom that is supreme is 'one whose supreme aim is action for Me' — meaning one for whom action for Me is primary. Even without practice, merely performing actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection through the door of purification of the mind (<s>sattva-śuddhi</s>), <s>yoga</s>, and the attainment of knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.10 //

children.text: athaitad apy aśakto 'si kartuṃ mad-yogam āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, if you are unable to do even this, taking refuge in My <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān ||BhG_12.11||
children.translated_text: then renounce the fruits of all actions, being self-controlled. // <s>BhG</s> 12.11 //

children.text: atha punar etad api yad uktaṃ mat-karma-paramatvam, tat kartum aśakto 'si, mad-yogam, āśrito mayi kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi saṃnyasya yat karaṇaṃ teṣām anuṣṭhānaṃ sa mad-yogaḥ, tam āśritaḥ san, sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ phala-saṃnyāsaṃ sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ tato 'nantaraṃ kuru yatātmavān saṃyata-cittaḥ san ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_12.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, again, if you are unable to do even this — what was stated as having one's supreme aim in action for Me — then, having resorted to My <s>yoga</s> — the performing of actions while renouncing them in Me, that conduct of theirs, that practice is 'My <s>yoga</s>' — having resorted to that, renounce the fruits of all actions — the renunciation of the fruits of all actions is 'renunciation of all action-fruits' — do that subsequently, being self-controlled, meaning being one whose mind is restrained. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.11 //

children.text: idānīṃ sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ stauti -
children.translated_text: Now he praises the renunciation of the fruits of all actions —

children.text: śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
children.translated_text: Better indeed is knowledge than [mechanical] practice; meditation is superior to knowledge;

children.text: dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgas tyāgāc chāntir anantaram ||BhG_12.12||
children.translated_text: from meditation, renunciation of the fruits of action [is superior]; from renunciation, peace follows immediately. // <s>BhG</s> 12.12 //

children.text: śreyo hi praśasyataraṃ jñānam | kasmāt ? viveka-pūrvakād abhyāsāt | tasmād api jñānāj jñāna-pūrvakaṃ dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate | jñānavato dhyānād api karma-phala-tyāgo viśiṣyata ity anuṣajyate | evaṃ karma-phala-tyāgāt pūrva-viśeṣaṇavataḥ śāntir upaśamaḥ sa-hetukasya saṃsārasyānantaram eva syāt, na tu kālāntaram apekṣate |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Better indeed — more praiseworthy — is knowledge. Than what? Than practice preceded by discrimination. Than that knowledge too, meditation preceded by knowledge is superior. From the meditation of one possessed of knowledge, renunciation of the fruits of action is superior — this is to be connected. Thus, from the renunciation of the fruits of action, possessed of the aforesaid qualifications, cessation — the subsidence of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) together with its cause — follows immediately, not requiring any further interval of time.

children.text: ajñasya karmaṇi pravṛttasya pūrvopadiṣṭopāyānuṣṭhānāśaktau sarva-karmaṇāṃ phala-tyāgaḥ śreyaḥ-sādhanam upadiṣṭam, na prathamam eva | ataś ca śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsād ity uttarottara-viśiṣṭatvopadeśena sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaḥ stūyate, saṃpanna-sādhanānuṣṭhānāśaktau anuṣṭheyatvena śrutatvāt | kena sādharmyeṇa stutitvam ? yadā sarve pramucyanta iti sarva-kāma-prahāṇād amṛtatvam uktam | tat prasiddham | kāmāś ca sarve śrauta-smārta-karmaṇāṃ phalāni | tat-tyāge ca viduṣo dhyāna-niṣṭhasyānantaraiva śāntir iti sarva-kāma-tyāga-sāmānyam ajña-karma-phala-tyāgasyāstīti tat-sāmānyāt sarva-karma-phala-tyāga-stutir iyaṃ prarocanārthā | yathāgastyena brāhmaṇena samudraḥ pīta itīdānīṃtanā api brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇatva-sāmānyāt stūyante, evaṃ karma-phala-tyāgāt
karma-yogasya śreyaḥ sādhanatvam abhihitam ||BhGS_12.12||
children.translated_text: the efficacy of <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action) as a means to the highest good has been declared. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.12 //

For one who is ignorant and engaged in action, when unable to practice the previously taught means, renunciation of the fruits of all actions has been taught as the means to the highest good — not as the first [resort]. And therefore, by the teaching that each successive [stage] is superior — 'Better indeed is knowledge than practice' — the renunciation of all action-fruits is praised, because it has been heard as something to be practiced when one is incapable of practicing the accomplished means. By what similarity is this a praise? It has been stated that immortality [results] from the abandonment of all desires, in 'When all [desires] are released' [<s>KaṭhU</s> 6.14]. That is well-known. And desires are the fruits of all Vedic and traditional (<s>smārta</s>) actions. When a wise person established in meditation renounces those, peace follows immediately — thus there is a similarity with the abandonment of all desires on the part of the ignorant person's renunciation of action-fruits, and because of that similarity, this praise of the renunciation of all action-fruits is for the purpose of encouragement. Just as because the ocean was drunk by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Agastya</s>, even present-day <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are praised because of the similarity of being <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — similarly, from the renunciation of the fruits of action,

children.text:
atra cātmeśvara-bhedam āśritya viśva-rūpa īśvare cetaḥ-samādhāna-lakṣaṇo yoga uktaḥ, īśvarārthaṃ karmānuṣṭhānādi ca | athaitad apy aśakto 'si [Gītā 12.11] ity ajñāna-kārya-sūcanān nābheda-darśino 'kṣaropāsakasya karma-yoga upapadyata iti darśayati | tathā karma-yogino 'kṣaropāsanānupapattim | te prāpnuvanti mām eva [Gītā 12.4] ity akṣaropāsakānāṃ kaivalya-prāptau svātantryam uktvā, itareṣāṃ pāratantryād īśvarādhīnatāṃ darśitavān teṣām ahaṃ samuddhartā [Gītā 12.7] iti | yadi hīśvarasyātma-bhūtās te matā abheda-darśitvāt, akṣara-svarūpā eva ta iti samuddharaṇa-karma-vacanaṃ tān praty apeśalaṃ syāt | yasmāc cārjunasyātyantam eva hitaiṣī bhagavān tasya samyag-darśanānanvitaṃ karma-yogaṃ bheda-dṛṣṭimantam eva upadiśati | na cātmānam īśvaraṃ pramāṇato
buddhvā kasyacid guṇa-bhāvaṃ jigamiṣati kaścid, virodhāt | tasmād akṣaropāsakānāṃ samyag darśana-niṣṭhānāṃ saṃnyāsināṃ tyakta-sarveṣaṇānām adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām ity ādi-dharma-pūgaṃ sākṣād amṛtatva-kāraṇaṃ vakṣyāmīti pravartate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And here, assuming the distinction between the individual self and the Lord, <s>yoga</s> in the form of fixing the mind on the Lord of cosmic form (<s>viśva-rūpa</s>) has been taught, as well as the performance of action for the Lord's sake and so on. By the indication of the effects of ignorance in 'Now, if you are unable to do even this' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.11], he shows that <s>karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action) is not possible for one who sees non-difference, for a worshipper of the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>). And similarly, the impossibility of worship of the imperishable for the practitioner of <s>karma-yoga</s>. Having stated the independence of the worshippers of the imperishable in attaining liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>) in 'They attain Me alone' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.4], he has shown the dependence upon the Lord — the subordination — of the others, in 'For them, I am the deliverer' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.7]. For if they, being of the very nature of the Lord due to their vision of non-difference, are considered as being of the nature of the imperishable itself, then the expression 'delivering' directed toward them would be inappropriate. And because the Blessed Lord is supremely desirous of <s>Arjuna's</s> welfare, He teaches <s>Arjuna</s> <s>karma-yoga</s> based on the vision of difference, which is not accompanied by right knowledge. And no one, having known through valid means of knowledge that the Self is the Lord, would wish to enter into the state of being a subordinate quality [of the Lord], because of the contradiction. Therefore, he proceeds to state the collection of virtues beginning with 'free from hatred toward all beings' — which is the direct cause of immortality — for the worshippers of the imperishable, the renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsins</s>) established in right knowledge, who have abandoned all desires —

children.text: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
children.translated_text: Free from hatred toward all beings, friendly and compassionate,

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī ||BhG_12.13||
children.translated_text: free from possessiveness, free from ego, equal in pain and pleasure, forgiving, // <s>BhG</s> 12.13 //

children.text: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṃ na dveṣṭā, ātmano duḥkha-hetum api na kiṃcid dveṣṭi, sarvāṇi bhūtāny ātmatvena hi paśyati | maitro mitra-bhāvo maitrī mitratayā vartata iti maitraḥ | karuṇa eva ca, karuṇā kṛpā duḥkhiteṣu dayā, tadvān karuṇaḥ, sarva-bhūtābhaya-pradaḥ, saṃnyāsīty arthaḥ | nirmamo mama-pratyaya-varjitaḥ | nirahaṃkāro nirgatāhaṃ-pratyayaḥ | sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ same duḥkha-sukhe dveṣa-rāgayor apravartake yasya sa sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ | kṣamī kṣamāvān, ākruṣṭo 'bhihato vāvikriya evāste ||BhGS_12.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Free from hatred toward all beings — one who does not hate; even toward that which causes oneself pain, one does not hate anything, for one sees all beings as one's own Self. Friendly — the state of being a friend is friendliness; one who behaves with friendliness is friendly. And compassionate indeed — compassion is mercy, sympathy toward the suffering; one who possesses that is compassionate — one who grants fearlessness to all beings — meaning a <s>saṃnyāsin</s> (renunciant). Free from possessiveness — devoid of the notion of 'mine.' Free from ego — one from whom the notion of 'I' has departed. Equal in pain and pleasure — one for whom pain and pleasure are equal, not giving rise to aversion and attachment — such a one has equanimity in pain and pleasure. Forgiving — possessed of forbearance; when reviled or struck, one remains without any reaction. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.13 //

children.text: saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Ever content, the <s>yogī</s>, self-controlled, of firm resolve,

children.text: mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||BhG_12.14||
children.translated_text: with mind and intellect offered to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.14 //

children.text: saṃtuṣṭaḥ satataṃ nityaṃ deha-sthiti-kāraṇasya lābhe 'lābhe ca utpannālaṃ-pratyayaḥ | tathā guṇaval-lābhe viparyaye ca saṃtuṣṭaḥ | satataṃ yogī samāhita-cittaḥ | yatātmā saṃyata-svabhāvaḥ | dṛḍha-niścayo dṛḍhaḥ sthiro niścayo 'dhyavasāyo yasyātma-tattva-viṣaye sa dṛḍha-niścayaḥ | mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ saṃkalpa-vikalpātmakaṃ manaḥ, adhyavasāya-lakṣaṇā buddhiḥ, te mayy evārpite sthāpite yasya saṃnyāsinaḥ sa mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ | ya īdṛśo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ | priyo hi jñānino 'ty artham ahaṃ sa ca mama priya iti saptame 'dhyāye sūcitam, tad iha prapañcyate ||BhGS_12.14||
children.translated_text: Ever content (<s>saṃtuṣṭa</s>) — one in whom the sense of 'enough' has arisen, whether in the obtaining or non-obtaining of the means for bodily sustenance, and likewise in the obtaining of something of quality or its opposite. Ever (<s>satatam</s>) a <s>yogin</s> — one of concentrated mind. Self-controlled (<s>yatātmā</s>) — one whose nature is restrained. Of firm resolve (<s>dṛḍha-niścaya</s>) — one whose resolve, i.e., determination, regarding the truth of the Self is firm and unshakeable. One whose mind and intellect are offered to Me (<s>mayy arpita-mano-buddhi</s>) — the mind, which is of the nature of thought and deliberation, and the intellect, characterized by determination — these two are offered, placed in Me — such a renunciant is one whose mind and intellect are offered to Me. Such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me. For it was indicated in the seventh chapter: 'exceedingly dear am I to the <s>jñānin</s>, and he is dear to Me' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.17]; that is here elaborated in detail. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.14 //

children.text: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world,

children.text: harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||BhG_12.15||
children.translated_text: who is free from elation, impatience, fear, and agitation — he too is dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.15 //

children.text: yasmāt saṃnyāsino nodvijate nodvegaṃ gacchati na santapyate na saṃkṣubhyati lokaḥ, tathā lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ, harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair harṣaś cāmarṣaś ca bhayaṃ codvegaś ca tair harṣāmarṣa-bhayodvegair muktaḥ | harṣaḥ priya-lābhe 'ntaḥ-karaṇasyotkarṣo romāñcanāśrupātādi-liṅgaḥ | amarṣo 'sahiṣṇutā | bhayaṃ trāsaḥ | udvega udvignatā | tair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||BhGS_12.15||
children.translated_text: He from whom — from this renunciant — the world does not shrink, does not recoil, is not distressed, is not agitated. And who does not shrink from the world — [who is] free from elation (<s>harṣa</s>), impatience (<s>amarṣa</s>), fear (<s>bhaya</s>), and agitation (<s>udvega</s>). Elation (<s>harṣa</s>) is the exaltation of the inner faculty upon obtaining something dear, marked by horripilation, tears, and the like. Impatience (<s>amarṣa</s>) is intolerance. Fear (<s>bhaya</s>) is terror. Agitation (<s>udvega</s>) is restlessness. One who is free from these — he too is dear to Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.15 //

children.text: anapekṣaḥ śucir dakṣa udāsīno gata-vyathaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without expectations, pure, skillful, impartial, free from distress,

children.text: sarvārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||BhG_12.16||
children.translated_text: renouncing all undertakings — such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.16 //

children.text: dehendriya-viṣaya-saṃbandhādiṣu apekṣā-viṣayeṣu anapekṣo niḥspṛhaḥ | śucir bāhyena ābhyantareṇa ca śaucena saṃpannaḥ | dakṣaḥ pratyutpanneṣu kāryeṣu sadyo yathāvat pratipattuṃ samarthaḥ | udāsīno na kasyacit mitrādeḥ pakṣaṃ bhajate yaḥ, sa udāsīno yatiḥ | gata-vyatho gata-bhayaḥ | sarvārambha-parityāgī ārabhyanteti | ārambhā ihāmutra-phala-bhogārthāni kāma-hetūni karmāṇi sarvārambhāḥ, tān parityaktuṃ śīlam asyeti sarvārambha-parityāgī yaḥ mad-bhaktaḥ saḥ me priyaḥ ||BhGS_12.16||
children.translated_text: Without expectations (<s>anapekṣa</s>) — free from craving regarding the objects of expectation, such as the connection with body, senses, sense-objects, etc. Pure (<s>śuci</s>) — endowed with both external and internal purity. Skillful (<s>dakṣa</s>) — capable of promptly and properly responding to tasks as they arise. Impartial (<s>udāsīna</s>) — a renunciant (<s>yati</s>) who does not take the side of any friend or the like. Free from distress (<s>gata-vyatha</s>) — free from fear. Renouncing all undertakings (<s>sarvārambha-parityāgī</s>) — '<s>ārambha</s>' means undertakings, i.e., actions motivated by desire, intended for enjoying fruits here and hereafter; all such undertakings are '<s>sarvārambhāḥ</s>'; one whose disposition is to renounce these is a '<s>sarvārambha-parityāgī</s>.' Such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.16 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
children.translated_text: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires,

children.text: śubhāśubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||BhG_12.17||
children.translated_text: who renounces both the auspicious and the inauspicious, who is full of devotion — he is dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.17 //

children.text: yo na hṛṣyatīṣṭa-prāptau, na dveṣṭy aniṣṭa-prāptau, na śocati priya-viyoge, na cāprāptaṃ kāṅkṣati, śubhāśubhe karmaṇī parityaktuṃ śīlam asyeti śubhāśubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||BhGS_12.17||
children.translated_text: One who does not rejoice upon obtaining the desired; who does not hate upon obtaining the undesired; who does not grieve upon separation from what is dear; who does not desire what is not yet obtained. One whose disposition is to renounce both auspicious and inauspicious actions — such a '<s>śubhāśubha-parityāgī</s>' who is full of devotion (<s>bhaktimān</s>) — he is dear to Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.17 //

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Equal toward enemy and friend, and likewise in honor and dishonor,

children.text: śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ ||BhG_12.18||
children.translated_text: in cold, heat, pleasure, and pain — equal, free from attachment — // <s>BhG</s> 12.18 //

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca, tathā mānāpamānayoḥ pūjā-paribhavayoḥ, śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu samaḥ | sarvatra ca saṅga-vivarjitaḥ ||BhGS_12.18||
children.translated_text: Equal toward enemy and friend; likewise in honor and dishonor — in worship and contempt. In cold, heat, pleasure, and pain — equal. And everywhere, free from attachment (<s>saṅga-vivarjita</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 12.18 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: tulya-nindā-stutir maunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kenacit |
children.translated_text: For whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with anything,

children.text: aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ ||BhG_12.19||
children.translated_text: homeless, of steady mind, full of devotion — that person is dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.19 //

children.text: tulya-nindā-stutiḥ | nindā ca stutiś ca nindā-stutī | te tulye yasya sa tulya-nindā-stutiḥ | maunī maunavān saṃyata-vāk | saṃtuṣṭaḥ yena kenacit śarīra-sthiti-hetu-mātreṇa | tathā coktam -
children.translated_text: '<s>Tulya-nindā-stuti</s>' — blame (<s>nindā</s>) and praise (<s>stuti</s>) are '<s>nindā-stutī</s>'; one for whom these two are equal is '<s>tulya-nindā-stuti</s>.' '<s>Maunī</s>' — one who possesses silence (<s>mauna</s>), i.e., of restrained speech. Content with anything — with whatever merely serves as the cause of bodily sustenance. And as it has been said:

children.text: yena kenacid ācchanno yena kenacid āśitaḥ |
yatra kvacana śāyī syāt taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ || [Mbh 12.245.12] iti |
children.translated_text: sleeping wherever he may — him the gods know as a [true] <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' [<s>MBh</s> 12.245.12]

children.text: kiṃ ca, aniketo niketa āśrayo nivāso niyato na vidyate yasya so 'niketaḥ, nāgāre ity ādi-smṛty-antarāt | sthira-matiḥ sthirā paramārtha-viṣayā yasya matiḥ saḥ sthira-matiḥ | bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ ||BhGS_12.19||
children.translated_text: Moreover, '<s>aniketa</s>' (homeless) — one for whom there is no fixed abode (<s>niketa</s>), no settled dwelling — as per other <s>Smṛtis</s> such as 'not in a village' etc. '<s>Sthira-mati</s>' (of steady mind) — one whose understanding pertaining to the ultimate reality is firm. Full of devotion (<s>bhaktimān</s>) — such a person (<s>nara</s>) is dear to Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.19 //
'Covered by whatever [garment], fed by whatever [food],

children.text: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām [Gītā 12.13] ity ādinākṣaropāsakānāṃ nivṛtta-sarveṣaṇānāṃ saṃnyāsināṃ paramārtha-jñāna-niṣṭhānāṃ dharma-jātaṃ prakrāntam upasaṃhriyate -
children.translated_text: The totality of <s>dharma</s> that has been set forth for the worshippers of the Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), beginning with 'who hates no being' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.13] — [the <s>dharma</s>] of those renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) who have abandoned all desires, who are established in the knowledge of the ultimate reality — is now concluded:

children.text: ye tu dharmyāmṛtam idaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: But those who follow this immortal <s>dharma</s> as declared,

children.text: śraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te 'tīva me priyāḥ ||BhG_12.20||
children.translated_text: with faith, regarding Me as supreme — those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me. // <s>BhG</s> 12.20 //

children.text: ye tu saṃnyāsino dharmyāmṛtaṃ dharmād anapetaṃ dharmyaṃ ca tad amṛtaṃ ca tat, amṛtatva-hetutvāt, idaṃ yathoktam, adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām ity ādinā paryupāsate 'nutiṣṭhanti śraddadhānāḥ santaḥ mat-paramāḥ yathokto 'ham akṣarātmā paramo niratiśayā gatir yeṣāṃ te mat-paramāḥ, mad-bhaktāś cottamāṃ paramārtha-jñāna-lakṣaṇāṃ bhaktim āśritāḥ, te 'tīva me priyāḥ | priyo hi jñānino 'ty artham [Gītā 7.18] iti yat sūcitaṃ tat vyākhyāyehopasaṃhṛtam bhaktās te 'tīva me priyā iti | yasmād dharmyāmṛtam idaṃ yathoktam anutiṣṭhan bhagavato viṣṇoḥ parameśvarasyātīva priyo bhavati, tasmād idaṃ dharmyāmṛtaṃ mumukṣuṇā yatnato 'nuṣṭheyaṃ viṣṇoḥ priyaṃ paraṃ dhāma jigamiṣuṇeti vākyārthaḥ ||BhGS_12.20||
children.translated_text: But those renunciants (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) who follow this '<s>dharmyāmṛta</s>' (immortal <s>dharma</s>) — what is in accordance with <s>dharma</s> is '<s>dharmya</s>'; and it is '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar) because it is the cause of immortality — this, as declared by the passage beginning with 'who hates no being' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.13] etc. — who practice [it], who are endowed with faith (<s>śraddadhāna</s>), who regard Me as supreme (<s>mat-parama</s>) — I, the Self of the Imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), am the supreme, unsurpassed goal of those — they are '<s>mat-parama</s>.' And [they are] My devotees who have resorted to the highest devotion characterized by the knowledge of the ultimate reality. They are exceedingly dear to Me. What was indicated by 'exceedingly dear am I to the <s>jñānin</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.18] has been explained here and concluded with 'those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.' Since one who practices this immortal <s>dharma</s> as declared becomes exceedingly dear to the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Supreme Lord, therefore this immortal <s>dharma</s> should be diligently practiced by one who desires liberation, who wishes to go to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the purport of the passage. // <s>BhGS</s> 12.20 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most exalted wandering monk (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s>),

children.text: dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [this is] the twelfth chapter.

children.text: BhG 13
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 13

children.text:
*NOTE: Numbering of this adhyaya out of tune with standard editions
and probably defective; "13.33" missing!
children.translated_text: *NOTE: Numbering of this chapter is out of tune with standard editions and probably defective; "13.33" missing!

children.text:
atha kṣetra-kṣetrajña-yogo nāma
trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the thirteenth chapter, named the Yoga of the Field and the Knower of the Field (<s>Kṣetra-Kṣetrajña-yoga</s>).

children.text: (śrī-śaṅkarācārya-bhagavat-pāda-kṛta-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavatpāda</s>)

children.text:
saptame 'dhyāye sūcite dve prakṛtī īśvarasya triguṇātmikāṣṭadhā bhinnāparā saṃsāra-hetutvāt, parā cānyā jīva-bhūtā kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇeśvarātmikā | yābhyāṃ prakṛtibhyām īśvaro jagad-utpatti-sthiti-laya-hetutvaṃ pratipadyate | tatra kṣetra-kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇa-prakṛti-dvaya-nirūpaṇa-dvāreṇa tadvata īśvarasya tattva-nirdhāraṇārthaṃ kṣetrādhyāya ārabhyate | atītānantarādhyāye ca adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṃ [Gītā 12.13] ity ādinā yāvad-adhyāya-parisamāptis tāvat tattva-jñānināṃ sannyāsināṃ niṣṭhā yathā te vartanta ity etad uktam | kena punas te tattva-jñānena yuktā yathokta-dharmācaraṇād bhagavataḥ priyā bhavanty evam arthaś cāyam adhyāya ārabhyate | prakṛtiś ca triguṇātmikā sarva-kārya-karaṇa-viṣayākāreṇa pariṇatā puruṣasya bhogāpavargārtha-kartavyatayā
dehendriyādyākāreṇa saṃhanyate | so 'yaṃ saṅghāta idaṃ śarīram | tad etad bhagavān uvāca --
children.translated_text:
In the seventh chapter, the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> (natures) of the Lord were indicated: the lower (<s>aparā</s>), consisting of three <s>guṇas</s>, divided eightfold, being the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>; and the other, the higher (<s>parā</s>), the living entity (<s>jīva-bhūtā</s>), characterized as the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), whose nature is the Lord. Through these two <s>Prakṛtis</s>, the Lord becomes the cause of the origin, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe. Therein, for the purpose of determining the truth of the Lord who possesses [these two natures], through the examination of the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> characterized as the field and the knower of the field — the chapter on the field (<s>kṣetrādhyāya</s>) is begun. And in the preceding chapter, from 'who hates no being' [<s>Gītā</s> 12.13] up to the completion of the chapter, it was stated how those renunciants who know the ultimate truth conduct themselves. With what knowledge of truth are they endowed such that, by practicing the aforementioned <s>dharma</s>, they become dear to the Blessed Lord? — for this purpose too this chapter is begun. <s>Prakṛti</s>, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, having transformed into the form of all effects, instruments, and objects, is assembled
in the form of the body, senses, etc. for the purpose of the <s>Puruṣa's</s> experience and liberation. This aggregate is this body. This the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: This body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, is called the 'field' (<s>kṣetra</s>);

children.text: etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tad-vidaḥ ||BhG_13.1||
children.translated_text: one who knows this — him, the knowers of that call the 'knower of the field' (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 13.1 //

children.text: idam iti sarva-nāmnoktaṃ viśinaṣṭi śariram iti | he kaunteya ! kṣata-trāṇāt kṣayāt kṣaraṇāt, kṣetravad vāsmin karma-phala-niṣpatteḥ kṣetram iti | iti-śabda evaṃ-śabdedārthakaḥ | kṣetram ity evam abhidhīyate kathyate | etac charīraṃ kṣetraṃ yo vetti vijānāti, āpāda-tala-mastakaṃ jñānena viṣayīkaroti, svābhāvikenaupadeśikena vā vedanena viṣayīkaroti vibhāgaśaḥ, taṃ veditāraṃ prāhuḥ kathayanti kṣetrajña iti | iti-śabdaḥ evaṃ-śabda-padārthaka eva pūrvavat | kṣetrajñaḥ ity evam āhuḥ | ke ? tad-vidas tau kṣetra-kṣetrajñau ye vidanti te tad-vidaḥ ||BhGS_13.1||
children.translated_text: The pronoun 'this' (<s>idam</s>) is specified by 'body' (<s>śarīra</s>). O son of <s>Kuntī</s>! Because of protecting from destruction (<s>kṣata-trāṇa</s>), or because of perishing (<s>kṣaya</s>), or because of wasting away (<s>kṣaraṇa</s>); or because the fruits of action ripen in it like [crops] in a field — [therefore it is called] '<s>kṣetra</s>' (field). The word '<s>iti</s>' has the meaning of the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus). It is thus called, spoken of, as '<s>kṣetra</s>' (field). One who knows (<s>vetti</s>) this body, this field — who makes it the object of knowledge, from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, through natural or instructed cognition, by parts — him, the knower, they call the 'knower of the field' (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). The word '<s>iti</s>' again has the meaning of '<s>evam</s>' as before. [They call him] thus '<s>kṣetrajña</s>.' Who [calls]? The knowers of that (<s>tad-vid</s>) — those who know both the field and the knower of the field; they are the '<s>tad-vidaḥ</s>.' // <s>BhGS</s> 13.1 //

children.text: evaṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajñau uktau | kim etāvan-mātreṇa jñānena jñātavyau? iti nety ucyate -
children.translated_text: Thus, the field and the knower of the field have been stated. Is it sufficient to know them to just this extent? No, it is said —

children.text: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata |
children.translated_text: Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O scion of <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor jñānaṃ yat taj jñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||BhG_13.2||
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the field and the knower of the field — that is [true] knowledge, in My view. // <s>BhG</s> 13.2 //

children.text: kṣetrajñaṃ yathokta-lakṣaṇaṃ cāpi māṃ parameśvaram asaṃsāriṇaṃ viddhi jānīhi | sarva-kṣetreṣu yaḥ kṣetrajño brahmādi-stamba-paryantāneka-kṣetropādhi-pravibhaktaḥ | taṃ nirasta-sarvopādhi-bhedaṃ sad-asad-ādi-śabda-pratyayāgocaraṃ viddhīty abhiprāyaḥ | he bhārata ! yasmāt kṣetra-kṣetrajñeśvara-yāthātmya-vyatirekeṇa na jñāna-gocaram anyad avaśiṣṭam asti, tasmāt kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor jñeya-bhūtayor yaj jñānaṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajñau yena jñānena viṣayīkriyete, taj jñānaṃ samyag-jñānam iti matam abhiprāyaḥ mameśvarasya viṣṇoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The knower of the field, of the characteristics described — know him also to be Me, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), who is beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>. In all fields — the knower of the field who is differentiated by the <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts) of the many fields, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass. Know Him — divested of all distinctions of <s>upādhi</s>, beyond the reach of words and cognitions such as 'being' and 'non-being' — this is the purport. O scion of <s>Bharata</s>! Since, apart from the knowledge of the true nature of the field, the knower of the field, and the Lord, there remains no other object of knowledge — therefore, the knowledge of the field and the knower of the field — the knowledge by which the field and the knower of the field, which are the objects of knowledge, are made known — that is [true] knowledge, right knowledge; [this is] the view, the opinion, of Me, the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text:
nanu sarva-kṣetreṣv eka eveśvaraḥ | nānyas tad-vyatirikto bhoktā vidyate cet, tata īśvarasya saṃsāritvaṃ prāptam | īśvara-vyatirekeṇa vā saṃsāriṇo 'nyasyābhāvāt saṃsārābhāva-prasaṅgaḥ | tac cobhayam aniṣṭam, bandha-mokṣa-tad-dhetu-śāstrānarthakya-prasaṅgāt, pratyakṣādi-pramāṇa-virodhāc ca | pratyakṣeṇa tāvat sukha-duḥkha-tad-dhetu-lakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāra upalabhyate | jagad-vaicitryopalabdhe ca dharmādharma-nimittaḥ saṃsāro 'numīyate | sarvam etad anupapannam ātmeśvaraikatve | na | jñānājñānayor anyatvenopapatteḥ | dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā [KaṭhU 1.2.4] tathā tayor vidyāvidyā-viṣayayoḥ phala-bhedo 'pi viruddho nirdiṣṭaḥ - śreyaś ca preyaś ca [KaṭhU 1.2.2] iti | vidyā-viṣayaḥ śreyaḥ, preyas tv avidyā-kāryam iti | tathā ca vyāsaḥ - dvāv
imāv atha panthānau [Mbh 12.241.6] ity ādi, imau dvāv eva panthānāv ity ādi ca | iha ca dve niṣṭhe ukte | avidyā ca saha kāryeṇa vidyayā hātavyeti śruti-smṛti-nyāyebhyo 'vagamyate |
children.translated_text: Objection: If there is only one Lord in all fields, and there is no other experiencer distinct from Him, then <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) would attach to the Lord. Or, in the absence of any other transmigrating entity apart from the Lord, the consequence would be the non-existence of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Both of these are undesirable — because of the consequence that the scriptures dealing with bondage, liberation, and their means would become purposeless, and because of contradiction with the means of valid knowledge such as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) etc. For through perception, <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by pleasure, pain, and their causes is apprehended. And from the diversity observed in the world, <s>saṃsāra</s> caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is inferred. All this would be untenable if the Self and the Lord were one. Reply: No — because it is justified through the otherness of knowledge and ignorance. 'Far apart are these two, diverging: ignorance and what is known as knowledge' [<s>KaṭhU</s> 1.2.4] — thus the two, knowledge and ignorance, are [declared to be different]. And the distinction in the fruits of the two, knowledge and ignorance, has been stated as opposed: 'the good and the pleasant' [<s>KaṭhU</s> 1.2.2]. The good (<s>śreyas</s>) is the domain of knowledge; the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>) is the effect of ignorance. And thus <s>Vyāsa</s> [states]: 'These two paths are...' [<s>MBh</s> 12.241.6] etc., and 'These indeed are the two paths' etc. And here [in the <s>Gītā</s>] too, two distinct paths (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) have been stated. That ignorance together with its effects is to be removed by knowledge — this is understood from <s>Śruti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, and reasoning.

children.text:
śrutayas tāvat - iha ced avedīd atha satyam asti na ced ihāvedīn mahatī vinaṣṭiḥ [KenaU 2.5],
tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati [TaittĀ 3.12], nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya [ŚvetU 3.8] vidvān na bibheti kutaścana [TaittU 2.9] |
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrutis</s> indeed [declare]: 'If one has known [it] here, then there is truth; if one has not known [it] here, great is the destruction' [<s>KenaU</s> 2.5]; 'Knowing Him thus, one becomes immortal here; there is no other path to liberation' [<s>TaittĀ</s> 3.12]; 'There is no other path known for going [to liberation]' [<s>ŚvetU</s> 3.8]; 'The knower does not fear anything' [<s>TaittU</s> 2.9].

children.text: aviduṣas tu - atha tasya bhayaṃ bhavati [TaittU 2.7], avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ [KaṭhU 1.2.5], brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati [MuṇḍU 3.2.9], anyo 'sāv anyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda yathā paśur evaṃ sa devānām [BAU 1.4.10] | ātmavid yaḥ sa idaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati [BAU 1.4.10], yadā carmavat [ŚvetU 6.20] ity ādyāḥ sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But for the ignorant — [there are <s>śruti</s> texts such as:] 'Then fear arises for him' [<s>TaittU</s> 2.7]; 'Those who dwell within ignorance' [<s>KaṭhU</s> 1.2.5]; 'One who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself' [<s>MuṇḍU</s> 3.2.9]; 'One who [thinks] "He is one and I am another" does not know — he is like a domestic animal to the gods' [<s>BAU</s> 1.4.10]; 'One who knows the Self becomes all this' [<s>BAU</s> 1.4.10]; 'When [it rolls up the sky] like a piece of leather' [<s>ŚvetU</s> 6.20] — and thousands of such [texts].

children.text: smṛtayaś ca - ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ [Gītā 5.25], ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ [Gītā 5.19], samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra [Gītā 13.29] ity ādyāḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And <s>smṛti</s> texts [too] — 'Knowledge is covered by ignorance; thereby beings are deluded' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.25]; 'Here itself creation is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.19]; 'For one who sees equally everywhere' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.29] — and such [texts].

children.text:
nyāyataś ca -
sarpān kuśāgrāṇi tathodapānaṃ
jñātvā manuṣyāḥ parivarjayanti |
ajñānatas tatra patanti kecij jñāne
phalaṃ paśya yathā-viśiṣṭam || [Mbh 12.201.17] iti |

children.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And from reasoning too —
'Knowing [the danger from] snakes, sharp grass-tips, and wells,
people avoid them;
but some fall into them through ignorance — see, then, the distinctive fruit of knowledge'

children.text: tathā ca - dehādiṣu ātma-buddhir avidvān rāga-dveṣādi-prayukto dharmādharmānuṣṭhāna-kṛj jāyate mriyate cety avagamyate | dehādi-vyatiriktātma-darśino rāga-dveṣādi-prahāṇāpekṣa-dharmādharma-pravṛtty-upaśamān mucyanta iti na kenacit pratyākhyātuṃ śakyaṃ nyāyataḥ | tatraivaṃ sati, kṣetrajñasyeśvarasyaiva sato 'vidyā-kṛtopādhi-bhedataḥ saṃsāritvam iva bhavati, yathā dehādy-ātmatvam ātmanaḥ | sarva-jantūnāṃ hi prasiddho dehādiṣv anātmasu ātma-bhāvo niścito 'vidyā-kṛtaḥ, yathā sthāṇau puruṣa-niścayaḥ | na caitāvatā puruṣa-dharmaḥ sthāṇor bhavati, sthāṇu-dharmo vā puruṣasya | tathā na caitanya-dharmo dehasya, deha-dharmo vā cetanasya sukha-duḥkha-mohātmakatvādir ātmano na yuktaḥ | avidyā-kṛtatvāviśeṣāt, jarā-mṛtyuvat |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And likewise — it is understood that the ignorant person, who identifies the Self with the body and the like, impelled by desire, aversion, and the rest, performs <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and is born and dies. [And conversely,] that those who see the Self as distinct from body etc., through the cessation of the activities of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> consequent upon the abandonment of desire, aversion, and the rest, are liberated — this cannot be refuted by anyone on rational grounds. This being so, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), being none other than the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), appears to have the nature of a transmigrating being (<s>saṃsārin</s>) due to the distinctions of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), just as the Self [appears to have] the nature of being identical with body etc. For it is well known among all beings that there is a settled conviction, created by <s>avidyā</s>, that the non-self — body etc. — is the Self; just as [there is] the settled conviction that a post is a man. But thereby, the properties of a man do not belong to the post, nor do the properties of the post belong to the man. Similarly, the properties of consciousness do not belong to the body, nor do the properties of the body — such as being constituted of pleasure, pain, and delusion — appropriately belong to the conscious Self. [They are so attributed] because there is no distinction in their being created by <s>avidyā</s>, just like old age, death, etc.

children.text: na, atulyatvāt | iti cet - sthāṇu-puruṣau jñeyāv eva santau jñātrānyonyasminn adhyastāv avidyayā | dehātmanos tu jñeya-jñātror eva itaretarādhyāsaḥ, iti na samo dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] No, because there is a dissimilarity. The post and the man, both being objects of knowledge, are superimposed upon each other through <s>avidyā</s>. But in the case of body and Self, the superimposition is between an object of knowledge and a knower — therefore the analogy is not equivalent.

children.text: ato deha-dharmo jñeyo 'pi jñātur ātmano bhavatīti cet, na | acaitanyādi-prasaṅgāt | yadi hi jñeyasya dehādeḥ kṣetrasya dharmāḥ sukha-duḥkha-mohecchādayo jñātur bhavanti, tarhi, jñeyasya kṣetrasya dharmāḥ kecit ātmano bhavanty avidyādhyāropitāḥ, jarā-maraṇādayas tu na bhavantīti viśeṣa-hetur vaktavyaḥ | na bhavantīty asty anumānam - avidyādhyāropitatvāj jarā-maraṇādivad iti, heyatvāt, upādeyatvāc cety ādi |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, even though the body is an object of knowledge, its properties become [those] of the Self, the knower? No — because then there would be the unwanted consequence of the Self being insentient and the like. For if the properties of the body, the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), which is an object of knowledge — pleasure, pain, delusion, desire, etc. — become [properties] of the knower, then a reason must be given for the distinction: 'Some properties of the field, the object of knowledge, belong to the Self through the superimposition of <s>avidyā</s>, but old age, death, and the like do not.' [In fact,] there is an inference that they do not [belong to the Self]: 'Because they are superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>, like old age, death, etc.' — because they are to be rejected, because they are to be adopted — and so on.

children.text: tatraivaṃ sati, kartṛtva-bhoktṛtva-lakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāro jñeya-stho jñātary avidyayādhyāropita iti, na tena jñātuḥ kiṃcid duṣyati | yathā bālair adhyāropitenākāśasya tala-malinatvādinā |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This being so, <s>saṃsāra</s> — characterized by agency and experiencership — resides in the object of knowledge [i.e., the body-mind complex] and is superimposed upon the knower through <s>avidyā</s>; therefore, nothing of the knower is actually tainted by it. Just as the sky is not [actually tainted] by the surface-impurity etc. superimposed upon it by children.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati, sarva-kṣetreṣv api sato bhagavataḥ kṣetrajñasyeśvarasya saṃsāritva-gandha-mātram api nāśaṅkayam | na hi kvacid api loke 'vidyādhyastena dharmeṇa kasyacid upakāro 'pakāro vā dṛṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And this being so, not even a trace of the nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) should be suspected for the Blessed Lord, the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, who is identical with <s>Īśvara</s>, even though present in all fields (bodies). For nowhere in the world has any benefit or harm ever been observed [to result] from a property superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: yat tūktam - na samo dṛṣṭānta iti, tad asat | katham ? avidyādhyāsa-mātraṃ hi dṛṣṭānta-dārṣṭāntikayoḥ sādharmyaṃ vivakṣitam | tan na vyabhicarati | yat tu jñātari vyabhicaratīti manyase, tasyāpy anaikāntikatvaṃ darśitaṃ jarādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] As for the objection stated — 'the analogy is not equivalent' — that is wrong. How so? The similarity intended between the illustration and the thing illustrated is merely the superimposition through <s>avidyā</s>. That does not deviate [from its purpose]. As for what you think deviates [in the case of] the knower — the non-conclusiveness of that too has been shown by [the examples of] old age, death, etc.

children.text: avidyāvattvāt kṣetrajñasya saṃsāritvam iti cet, na | avidyāyās tāmasatvāt | tāmaso hi pratyayaḥ, āvaraṇātmakatvād avidyā viparīta-grāhakaḥ, saṃśayopasthāpako vā, agrahaṇātmako vā | viveka-prakāśa-bhāve tad-abhāvāt tāmase cāvaraṇātmake timirādi-doṣe saty agrahaṇāder avidyā-trayasya upalabdheḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] The <s>kṣetrajña</s> has the nature of a <s>saṃsārin</s> because it possesses <s>avidyā</s>? No — because <s>avidyā</s> is of the nature of <s>tamas</s> (darkness/inertia). For <s>avidyā</s>, being a cognition of the nature of <s>tamas</s>, being of the nature of concealment, either grasps wrongly (produces erroneous cognition), or presents doubt, or is of the nature of non-apprehension. In the presence of the light of discrimination, it ceases to exist. And when a defect of the nature of <s>tamas</s> and concealment — such as an eye-disease — is present, the threefold <s>avidyā</s> of non-apprehension etc. is observed.

children.text:
atrāha - evaṃ tarhi jñātṛ-dharmo 'vidyā | na | karaṇe cakṣuṣi taimirikatvādi-doṣopalabdheḥ | yat tu manyase - jñātṛ-dharmo 'vidyā, tad eva cāvidyā-dharmavattvaṃ kṣetrajñasya saṃsāritvam | tatra yad uktam īśvara eva kṣetrajñaḥ, na saṃsārīty etad ayuktam iti, tan na | yathā karaṇe cakṣuṣi viparīta-grāhakādi-doṣasya darśanāt | na viparītādi-grahaṇaṃ tan-nimittaṃ vā taimirikatvādi-doṣo grahītuḥ, cakṣuṣaḥ saṃskāreṇa timire 'panīte grahītur adarśanān na grahītur dharmo yathā | tathā sarvatraivāgrahaṇa-viparīta-saṃśaya-pratyayās tan-nimittāḥ karaṇasyaiva kasyacit bhavitum arhanti, na jñātuḥ kṣetrajñasya | saṃvedyatvāc ca teṣāṃ pradīpa-prakāśavan na jñātṛ-dharmatvam | saṃvedyatvād eva svātma-vyatirikta-saṃvedyatvam | sarva-karaṇa-viyoge ca kaivalye sarva-vādibhir
avidyādi-doṣavat-tvānabhyupagamāt | ātmano yadi kṣetrajñasyāgny-uṣṇavat svo dharmaḥ, tato na kadācid api tena viyogaḥ syāt | avikriyasya ca vyomavat sarva-gatasyāmūrtasya ātmanaḥ kenacit saṃyoga-viyogānupapatteḥ, siddhaṃ kṣetrajñasya nityam eveśvaratvam | anāditvān nirguṇatvād [Gītā 13.32] ity ādīśvara-vacanāc ca ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Here one objects: Then <s>avidyā</s> is a property of the knower! No — because the defect of dimness etc. is observed in the instrument, the eye. What you think — that <s>avidyā</s> is a property of the knower, and that very possession of the property of <s>avidyā</s> constitutes the <s>saṃsāra</s>-nature of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>; and therefore what was stated — 'the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is the Lord, not a <s>saṃsārin</s>' — is improper — that is not so. Because defects of erroneous cognition etc. are observed in the instrument, the eye. The erroneous cognition or its cause — the defect of dim-sightedness etc. — does not belong to the perceiver; just as, when the dim-sightedness is removed through treatment of the eye, it is not seen [to belong] to the perceiver — therefore it is not a property of the perceiver. Likewise, everywhere the cognitions of non-apprehension, erroneous cognition, and doubt, and their causes, can only be properties of some instrument, not of the knower, the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. And because they are objects of awareness — like the light of a lamp, they are not properties of the knower. And because they are objects of awareness, they must be objects of awareness distinct from the Self. And in the state of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), when separated from all instruments, all disputants accept that there is no possession of defects such as <s>avidyā</s> etc. If <s>avidyā</s> were an intrinsic property of the Self, the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, like heat of fire, then there could never be separation from it. And since the Self, which is like space — actionless, all-pervading, formless — cannot logically have conjunction or disjunction with anything, it is established that the lordship of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is eternal. And because of the Lord's own statement: 'Because of being beginningless, because of being without qualities' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.32] etc.

children.text: nanv evaṃ sati saṃsāra-saṃsāritvābhāve śāstrānarthakyādi-doṣaḥ syād iti cet, na | sarvair abhyupagatatvāt | sarvair hy ātma-vādibhir abhyupagato doṣo naikena parihartavyo bhavati | katham abhyupagata iti ? muktātmanāṃ hi saṃsāra-saṃsāritva-vyavahārābhāvaḥ sarvair eva ātma-vādibhir iṣyate | na ca teṣāṃ śāstrānarthakyādi-doṣa-prāptir abhyupagatā | tathā naḥ kṣetrajñānām īśvaraikatve sati, śāstrānarthakyaṃ bhavatu | avidyā-viṣaye cārthavattvam - yathā dvaitināṃ sarveṣāṃ bandhāvasthāyām eva śāstrādy-arthavattvam, na muktāvasthāyām, evam ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] If this is so — in the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> and a <s>saṃsārin</s> — there would be the defect of scripture being purposeless and the like? No — because this [defect] is accepted by all. For a defect that is accepted by all proponents of the Self (<s>ātma-vādin</s>) need not be resolved by one alone. How is it accepted [by all]? For it is accepted by all proponents of the Self without exception that the liberated Self has no transactional dealings of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the nature of being a <s>saṃsārin</s>. And the unwanted consequence of scripture being purposeless is not accepted by them [in that state]. Similarly, for us, when the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is identical with the Lord, let scripture be purposeless [in the ultimate state]. But in the domain of <s>avidyā</s>, [scripture] has its purpose — just as for all dualists, scripture etc. has its purpose only in the state of bondage, not in the state of liberation. Similarly [for us].

children.text: nanv ātmano bandha-muktāvasthe paramārthata eva vastu-bhūte dvaitināṃ sarveṣām | ato heyopādeya-tat-sādhana-sad-bhāve śāstrādy-arthavattvaṃ syāt | advaitināṃ punaḥ, dvaitasyāparamārthatvāt, avidyā-kṛtatvād bandhāvasthāyāś cātmano 'paramārthatve nirviṣayatvāt, śāstrādyānarthakyam iti cet, na | ātmano 'vasthā-bhedānupapatteḥ | yadi tāvat ātmano bandha-muktāvasthe, yugapat syātām, krameṇa vā | yugapat tāvat virodhān na saṃbhavataḥ sthiti-gatī ivaikasmin | krama-bhāvitve ca, nirnimittatvaṃ sa-nimittatvaṃ vā ? nirnimittatve 'nirmokṣa-prasaṅgaḥ | sa-nimittatve ca svato 'bhāvāt aparamārthatva-prasaṅgaḥ | tathā ca saty abhyupagama-hāniḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] But for all dualists, the states of bondage and liberation of the Self are ultimately real entities. Therefore, since that which is to be rejected, that which is to be adopted, and the means thereof truly exist, scripture etc. would be purposeful. But for the Advaitins, since duality is not ultimately real, and since the state of bondage is not ultimately real for the Self — being created by <s>avidyā</s> — scripture etc. would be purposeless because [it would be] without an object? No — because there cannot be different states of the Self. If the states of bondage and liberation of the Self were [real], they would exist either simultaneously or sequentially. Simultaneously, they are impossible due to mutual contradiction, like rest and motion in one [entity]. And if they are sequential — is there a cause, or no cause? If without cause, there would be the consequence of never attaining liberation. If with a cause, since [that cause] does not exist by itself, there would be the consequence of its being not ultimately real. And that being so, the [dualist's own] position is undermined.

children.text: kiṃ ca, bandha-muktāvasthayoḥ paurvāparya-nirūpaṇāyāṃ bandhāvasthā pūrvaṃ prakalpyā, anādimaty antavatī ca | tac ca pramāṇa-viruddham | tathā mokṣāvasthādimaty anantā ca pramāṇa-viruddhaivābhyupagamyate | na cāvasthāvato 'vasthāntaraṃ gacchato nityatvam upapādayituṃ śakyam | athānityatva-doṣa-parihārāya bandha-muktāvasthā-bhedo na kalpyate | ato dvaitinām api śāstrānarthakyādi-doṣo 'parihārya eva | iti samānatvān nādvaita-vādinā parihartavyo doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover, in determining the temporal sequence of the states of bondage and liberation, the state of bondage must be posited as prior — beginningless yet having an end. But that contradicts the means of valid knowledge. Likewise, the state of liberation — having a beginning yet endless — is also posited in contradiction to the means of valid knowledge. And for an entity that has states and transitions from one state to another, permanence cannot be established. If, to avoid the defect of impermanence, the distinction of states of bondage and liberation is not posited — then for the dualists too, the defect of scripture being purposeless is unavoidable. Therefore, since the situation is the same [for both], the defect need not be resolved by the Advaitin alone.

children.text:
na ca śāstrānarthakyam, yathā-prasiddhāvidvat-puruṣa-viṣayatvāc chāstrasya | aviduṣāṃ hi phala-hetvor anātmanor ātma-darśanam, na viduṣām | viduṣāṃ hi phala-hetubhyām ātmano 'nyatva-darśane sati, tayor aham ity ātma-darśanānupapatteḥ | na hy atyanta-mūḍha unmattādir api jalāgnyoś chāyā-prakāśayor vaikātmyaṃ paśyati | kim uta vivekī | tasmān na vidhi-pratiṣedha-śāstraṃ tāvat phala-hetubhyām ātmano 'nyatva-darśino bhavati |
na hi "devadatta, tvam idaṃ kuru" iti kasmiṃścit karmaṇi niyukte, "viṣṇumitro 'haṃ niyuktaḥ" iti tatra-stho niyogaṃ sṛṇvann api pratipadyate | viyoga-viṣaya-vivekāgrahaṇāt tūpapadyate pratipattiḥ | tathā phala-hetvor api ||
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Nor is scripture purposeless, because scripture has as its domain the well-known ignorant person. For the ignorant see the non-self — the causes and fruits [of action] — as the Self; the wise do not. For the wise, who see the Self as different from the causes and fruits, the vision of those [causes and fruits] as 'I' — as the Self — is impossible. For not even the extremely deluded or the insane see unity between water and fire, or between shadow and light. How much less so the discriminating person. Therefore, the scripture of injunctions and prohibitions does not apply to one who sees the Self as different from the causes and fruits of action.
For when <s>Devadatta</s> is enjoined to a certain action — 'Devadatta, do this' — <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, standing there, even though hearing the injunction, does not understand [it as addressed to himself] — 'I, <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, have been enjoined.' But understanding does arise from the non-apprehension of the distinction between the subject of separation [i.e., the one enjoined and oneself]. Similarly regarding the causes and fruits [of action].

children.text: nanu prākṛta-saṃbandhāpekṣayā yuktaiva pratipattiḥ śāstrārtha-viṣayā - phala-hetubhyām anyātma-viṣaya-darśane 'pi sati - iṣṭa-phala-hetau pravartito 'smi, aniṣṭa-phala-hetoś ca nivartito 'smīti | yathā pitṛ-putrādīnām itaretarātmānyatva-darśane saty apy anyonya-niyoga-pratiṣedhārtha-pratipattiḥ | na | vyatiriktātma-darśana-pratipatteḥ prāg eva phala-hetvor ātmābhimānasya siddhatvāt | pratipanna-niyoga-pratiṣedhārtho hi phala-hetubhyām ātmano 'nyatvaṃ pratipadyate, na pūrvam | tasmād vidhi-pratiṣedha-śāstram avidvad-viṣayam iti siddham ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] But in view of the natural connection [between Self and body], understanding regarding the subject-matter of scripture is entirely appropriate — even when there is the vision of the Self as different from the causes and fruits — [thinking] 'I have been directed toward the cause of a desired fruit, and turned away from the cause of an undesired fruit.' Just as father and son etc., even while seeing each other as distinct selves, understand each other's injunctions and prohibitions? No — because before [one attains] the understanding of the Self as distinct from the causes and fruits, the identification of the Self with the causes and fruits is already established. For one first understands the content of an injunction or prohibition, and only then understands the Self as different from the causes and fruits — not before. Therefore, it is established that the scripture of injunctions and prohibitions pertains to the ignorant.

children.text: nanu svarga-kāmo yajeta [Ap.Śr.S. 10.2.1] na kalañjaṃ bhakṣayed ity ādāv ātma-vyatireka-darśinām apravṛttau, kevala-dehādy-ātma-dṛṣṭīnāṃ ca | ataḥ kartur abhāvāc chāstrānarthakyam iti cet, na | yathā-prasiddhita eva pravṛtti-nivṛtty-upapatteḥ | īśvara-kṣetrajñaikatva-darśī brahma-vit tāvan na pravartate | tathā nairātmyavādy api nāsti para-loka iti na pravartate | yathā-prasiddhitas tu vidhi-pratiṣedha-śāstra-śravaṇānyathānupapattyānumitātmāstitva ātma-viśeṣānabhijñaḥ karma-phala-saṃjāta-tṛṣṇaḥ śraddadhānatayā ca pravartate | iti sarveṣāṃ na pratyakṣam | ato na śāstrānarthakyam ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] If those who see the Self as distinct do not act [upon scriptural injunctions like] 'One who desires heaven should perform sacrifice' [<s>Āp.Śr.S.</s> 10.2.1], 'One should not eat <s>kalañja</s>' etc., and if those who identify the Self merely with the body etc. [also do not act upon them — due to lack of interest in invisible results] — then, due to the absence of an agent, scripture would be purposeless? No — because engagement and disengagement are possible based on what is well-known [in common experience]. The knower of <s>Brahman</s>, who sees the identity of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> and the Lord, does not engage [in scriptural action]. Likewise, even the <s>Nairātmyavādin</s> (Buddhist), [who thinks] 'There is no other world,' does not engage. But based on common understanding — one who, through the impossibility of otherwise explaining Vedic statements about injunctions and prohibitions, has inferred the existence of the Self, yet does not know the specific nature of the Self, who has craving born of the [desire for the] fruits of action, and who acts with faith — [that one engages]. This is not directly perceived by anyone. Therefore, scripture is not purposeless.
