children.text: vivekinām apravṛtti-darśanāt tad-anugāminām apravṛttau śāstrānarthakyam iti cet, na | kasyacid eva vivekopapatteḥ | anekeṣu hi prāṇiṣu kaścid eva vivekī syāt, yathedānīm | na ca vivekinam anuvartante mūḍhāḥ, rāgādi-doṣa-tantratvāt pravṛtteḥ, abhicaraṇādau ca pravṛtti-darśanāt, svābhāvyāc ca pravṛtteḥ | svabhāvas tu pravartate [Gītā 5.14] iti hi uktam ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] [Objection:] Since the discriminating person is seen not to engage [in action], and since those who follow that person also do not engage, scripture would be purposeless? No — because discrimination arises only for a few. Among the many living beings, only a few may be discriminating, just as [we observe] now. And the deluded do not follow the discriminating person, because engagement [in action] depends on the force of defects such as desire and the like, and because engagement is observed even in sorcery and the like, and because engagement is natural. For it has been said: 'Nature itself impels [one to act]' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.14].

children.text: tasmāt avidyā-mātraṃ saṃsāro yathā-dṛṣṭa-viṣaya eva | na kṣetrajñasya kevalasyāvidyā tat-kāryaṃ ca | na ca mithyā-jñānaṃ paramārtha-vastu dūṣayituṃ samartham | na hy ūṣara-deśaṃ snehena paṅkī-kartuṃ śaknoti marīcy-udakam | tathāvidyā kṣetrajñasya na kiṃcit kartuṃ śaknoti | ataś cedam uktam - kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi | ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānam [Gītā 5.15] iti ca ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is nothing but <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) alone, pertaining only to the domain of perceived [appearances]. For the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) in its pure state, there is neither <s>avidyā</s> nor its effects. Nor is false knowledge capable of vitiating a thing that is ultimately real. For the water [seen in] a mirage cannot make a barren land muddy. Similarly, <s>avidyā</s> cannot do anything whatsoever to the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. And therefore this has been said: 'Know the <s>kṣetrajña</s> to be myself as well' [<s>BhG</s> 13.2]; and 'Knowledge is covered by ignorance' [<s>BhG</s> 5.15].

children.text: atha kim idaṃ saṃsāriṇām ivāham evam mamaivedam iti paṇḍitānām api ? sṛṇu | idaṃ tat pāṇḍityam, yat kṣetra evātma-darśanam | yadi punaḥ kṣetrajñam avikriyaṃ paśyeyus tato na bhogaṃ karma vākāṅkṣeyur mama syād iti | vikriyaiva bhoga-karmaṇī | athaivaṃ sati, phalārthitvād avidvān pravartate | viduṣaḥ punar avikriyātma-darśinaḥ phalārthitvābhāvāt pravṛtty-anupapattau kārya-karaṇa-saṃghāta-vyāpāroparame nivṛttir upacaryate ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, what is this — that even for the learned, as for <s>saṃsārins</s> (transmigrating beings), [there is the notion] 'I am thus, this is mine'? Listen: this is that [so-called] 'learning' — namely, seeing the Self in the <s>kṣetra</s> (field) alone. If, however, they were to see the <s>kṣetrajña</s> as without modification, then they would not desire enjoyment or action [thinking] 'it should be mine.' For enjoyment and action are nothing but modification. And this being so, the ignorant person acts because of desiring results. But for the wise one who sees the Self as without modification, since there is no desire for results and hence no logical possibility of engagement [in action] — when the activity of the aggregate of body and instruments ceases — cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) is figuratively attributed.

children.text: idaṃ cānyat pāṇḍityaṃ kasyacid astu - kṣetrajña īśvara eva | kṣetraṃ cānyat kṣetrajñasyaiva viṣayaḥ | ahaṃ tu saṃsārī sukhī duḥkhī ca | saṃsāroparamaś ca mama kartavyaḥ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-vijñānena, dhyānena ceśvaraṃ kṣetrajñaṃ sākṣāt kṛtvā tat-svarūpāvasthāneneti | yaś caivaṃ budhyate, yaś ca bodhayati, nāsau kṣetrajña iti | evaṃ manvāno yaḥ sa paṇḍitāpaśabdaḥ | saṃsāra-mokṣayoḥ śāstrasya cārthavattvaṃ karomīti | ātmahā svayaṃ mūḍho 'nyāṃ ca vyāmohayati śāstrārtha-saṃpradāya-rahitatvāt, śruta-hānim aśruta-kalpanāṃ ca kurvan | tasmāt asaṃpradāya-vit sarva-śāstra-vid api mūrkhavad eva upekṣaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And let someone else have this other [kind of] 'learning': '<s>Kṣetrajña</s> is indeed the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>); the <s>kṣetra</s> is something other, merely the object of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. But I am a <s>saṃsārin</s>, happy and unhappy. And the cessation of my <s>saṃsāra</s> is to be accomplished through the knowledge of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, and by directly realizing through meditation the <s>kṣetrajña</s> who is the Lord, [and then] abiding in His own nature.' One who understands thus, and one who teaches thus — that person is not the [true] <s>kṣetrajña</s>. One who thinks in this way deserves the pejorative term 'learned' (<s>paṇḍitāpaśabda</s>). [Such a person says:] 'I make <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>mokṣa</s> and the scripture meaningful.' [But in reality] such a one, self-destroying and deluded, deludes others as well, being devoid of the authentic tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>) of scriptural meaning — creating the loss of what has been heard and the fabrication of what has not been heard. Therefore, one who does not know the [authentic] tradition (<s>asaṃpradāya-vit</s>), even if learned in all the scriptures, should be disregarded like a fool.

children.text: yat tūktam īśvarasya kṣetrajñaikatve saṃsāritvaṃ prāpnoti | kṣetrajñānāṃ ceśvaraikatve saṃsāriṇo 'bhāvāt saṃsārābhāva-prasaṅga iti | etau doṣau pratyuktau vidyāvidyayor vailakṣaṇyābhyupagamād iti | katham ? avidyā-parikalpita-doṣeṇa tad-viṣayaṃ vastu pāramārthikaṃ na duṣyatīti | tathā ca dṛṣṭanto darśitaḥ - marīcy-ambhasā ūṣara-deśo na paṅkīkriyata iti | saṃsāriṇo 'bhāvāt saṃsārābhāva-prasaṅga-doṣo 'pi saṃsāra-saṃsāriṇor avidyā-kalpitatvopapattyā pratyuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But it was said: if the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is identical with the Lord, then [the Lord] would have the status of a <s>saṃsārin</s>. And if the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> are identical with the Lord, then since there would be no <s>saṃsārins</s>, there would be the absurd consequence of the non-existence of <s>saṃsāra</s>. These two objections have been answered by the acceptance of the complete distinctness of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). How? The ultimately real entity is not vitiated by a defect superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>. And thus the illustration has been shown — a barren land is not made muddy by the water of a mirage. The objection regarding the absurd consequence of the non-existence of <s>saṃsāra</s> due to the non-existence of <s>saṃsārins</s> has also been answered by the cogent reasoning that both <s>saṃsāra</s> and the <s>saṃsārin</s> are fabricated by <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text:
nanu avidyāvattvam eva kṣetrajñasya saṃsāritva-doṣaḥ | tat-kṛtaṃ ca sukhitva-duḥkhitvādi pratyakṣam upalabhyate iti cet, na | jñeyasya kṣetra-dharmatvāt, jñātuḥ kṣetrajñasya tat-kṛta-doṣānupapatteḥ | yāvat kiṃcit kṣetrajñasya doṣa-jātam avidyamānam āsañjayasi, tasya jñeyatvopapatteḥ kṣetra-dharmatvam eva, na kṣetrajña-dharmatvam | na ca tena kṣetrajño duṣyati, jñeyena jñātuḥ saṃsargānupapatteḥ | yadi hi saṃsargaḥ syāt, jñeyatvam eva nopapadyeta | yady ātmano dharmo 'vidyāvattvaṃ duḥkhitvādi ca kathaṃ bhoḥ pratyakṣam upalabhyate | kathaṃ vā kṣetrajña-dharmaḥ | jñeyaṃ ca sarvaṃ kṣetraṃ jñātaiva kṣetrajña ity avadhārite, avidyā-duḥkhitvādeḥ kṣetrajña-viśeṣaṇatvaṃ kṣetrajña-dharmatvaṃ tasya ca pratyakṣopalabhyatvam iti viruddham ucyate 'vidyā-mātrāvaṣṭambhāt
kevalam ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: the very possession of <s>avidyā</s> by the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is the defect of being a <s>saṃsārin</s>. And the happiness, unhappiness, etc. caused by it are directly perceived. Reply: No — because [happiness, unhappiness, etc.] are properties of the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>), hence properties of the <s>kṣetra</s> (field). Since they are properties of the <s>kṣetra</s>, there is no logical possibility of defects caused by them applying to the knower (<s>jñātṛ</s>), the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. Whatever defects you ascribe to the <s>kṣetrajña</s> — all of which do not [truly] exist — since it is logically established that they are knowable (<s>jñeya</s>), they are properties of the <s>kṣetra</s> alone, not properties of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. Nor is the <s>kṣetrajña</s> vitiated by them, since there is no logical possibility of contact between the knowable and the knower. For if there were contact, it could not even be knowable. If the possession of <s>avidyā</s> and unhappiness etc. were properties of the Self, how then, sir, could they be directly perceived? And how could they be properties of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>? Once it is determined that everything knowable is <s>kṣetra</s> and the knower alone is <s>kṣetrajña</s>, it is contradictory to say that <s>avidyā</s>, unhappiness, etc. are qualifiers of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, are properties of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, and are directly perceived — [one says this] merely out of clinging to nothing but <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: atrāha - sāvidyā kasya ? iti | yasya dṛśyate tasyaiva | kasya dṛśyate ? iti | atrocyate - avidyā kasya dṛśyate iti praśno nirarthakaḥ | katham ? dṛśyate ced avidyā, tadvantam api paśyasi | na ca tadvaty upalabhyamāne sā kasya ? iti praśno yuktaḥ | na hi gomati upalabhyamāne gāvaḥ kasya ? iti praśno 'rthavān bhavati |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Here one objects: to whom does this <s>avidyā</s> belong? [Reply:] To the very one in whom it is seen. [Objection:] In whom is it seen? [Reply:] Here it is said — the question 'To whom does <s>avidyā</s> belong, in whom is it seen?' is meaningless. How so? If <s>avidyā</s> is seen, then you also see the one who possesses it. And when the possessor is perceived, the question 'to whom does it belong?' is inappropriate. For when one who possesses cows is perceived, the question 'to whom do the cows belong?' is not meaningful.

children.text: nanu viṣamo dṛṣṭāntaḥ | gavāṃ tadvataś ca pratyakṣatvāt tat-saṃbandho 'pi pratyakṣa iti praśno nirarthakaḥ | na tathāvidyā tadvāṃś ca pratyakṣau, yataḥ praśno nirarthakaḥ syāt | apratyakṣeṇāvidyāvatāvidyā-saṃbandhe jñāte, kiṃ tava syāt ? avidyāyā anartha-hetutvāt parihartavyā syāt | yasyāvidyā, sa tāṃ parihariṣyati |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: the illustration is not analogous. Since cows and their possessor are both perceptible, their relation too is perceptible — hence the question is meaningless. But <s>avidyā</s> and its possessor are not both perceptible, such that the question would be meaningless. [Reply:] If the possessor of <s>avidyā</s> were known imperceptibly to be related to <s>avidyā</s>, what would that mean for you? [Objection:] Since <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of harm, it should be eliminated. The one who possesses <s>avidyā</s> will eliminate it.

children.text: nanu mamaivāvidyā | jānāsi tarhy avidyāṃ tadvantaṃ ca ātmānam | jānāmi, na tu pratyakṣeṇa | anumānenaś cej jānāsi, kathaṃ saṃbandhagrahaṇam ? na hi tava jñātuḥ jñeya-bhūtayāvidyayā tat-kāle saṃbandho grahītuṃ śakyate, avidyāyā viṣayatvenaiva jñātur upayuktatvāt | na ca jñātur avidyāyā ca saṃbandhasya yo grahītā, jñānaṃ cānyat tad-viṣayaṃ saṃbhavati | anavasthā-prāpteḥ | yadi jñātrāpi jñeya-saṃbandho jñāyate, anyo jñātā kalpyaḥ syāt, tasyāpy anyaḥ, tasyāpy anyaḥ ity anavasthāparihāryā | yadi punar avidyā jñeyā, anyad vā jñeyaṃ jñeyam eva | tathā jñātāpi jñātaiva, na jñeyaṃ bhavati | yadā caivam, avidyā-duḥkhitvādyair na jñātuḥ kṣetrajñasya kiṃcit duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: <s>avidyā</s> belongs to me alone. [Reply:] Then you know <s>avidyā</s> and the self who possesses it. [Objection:] I know it, but not through direct perception. [Reply:] If you know it through inference, how is the relation grasped? For it is not possible for you, the knower, to grasp the relation with <s>avidyā</s>, which is an object to be known (<s>jñeya</s>), at that very time [of knowing] — since <s>avidyā</s> is already utilized by the knower merely as an object of knowledge. Nor is it possible that there be another grasper of the relation between the knower and <s>avidyā</s>, and yet another cognition having that [relation] as its object — because an infinite regress would result. If the relation between the knower and the knowable is [itself] known, another knower would need to be posited, and for that one another, and for that one yet another — an infinite regress that cannot be avoided. But if <s>avidyā</s> is knowable, and everything else knowable is indeed knowable — likewise the knower too is only the knower, it does not become a knowable. And when this is so, the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, the knower, is not in any way vitiated by <s>avidyā</s>, unhappiness, etc.

children.text: nanu ayam eva doṣaḥ, yat doṣavat-kṣetra-vijñātṛtvam | na ca vijñāna-svarūpasyaivāvikriyasya vijñātṛtvopacārāt | yathoṣṇatā-mātreṇāgnes tapti-kriyopacāraḥ, tadvat | yathātra bhagavatā kriyākāraka-phalātmatvābhāva ātmani svata eva darśitaḥ - avidyādhyāropita eva kriyā-kārakādir ātmany upacaryate | tathā tatra tatra ya enaṃ vetti hantāram [Gītā 2.19], prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ [Gītā 3.27], nādatte kasyacit pāpam [Gītā 5.15] ity ādi-prakaraṇeṣu darśitaḥ | tathaiva ca vyākhyātam asmābhiḥ | uttareṣu ca prakaraṇeṣu darśayiṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: this itself is the defect — that it is the cognizer of the defective <s>kṣetra</s>. [Reply:] No — because the status of cognizer is merely figuratively attributed to what is, by nature, pure consciousness and without modification. Just as the mere heat of fire occasions the figurative attribution of the activity of burning, so too [with the <s>kṣetrajña</s>]. Just as in this text the Blessed Lord has shown that the nature of action, agent, and result does not intrinsically belong to the Self — [rather] it is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> and then figuratively attributed to the Self — so too in the various passages: 'He who knows this to be the slayer' [<s>BhG</s> 2.19], 'All actions are performed in every way by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>' [<s>BhG</s> 3.27], 'It does not take upon itself anyone's sin' [<s>BhG</s> 5.15], etc. — it has been shown. And it has been explained thus by us. And in the subsequent passages we shall show [the same].

children.text: hanta ! tarhy ātmani kriyā-kāraka-phalātmatāyāḥ svato 'bhāve, avidyayā cādhyāropitatve, karmāṇy avidvat-kartavyāny eva, na viduṣām iti prāptam | satyam evaṃ prāptam, etad eva ca na hi deha-bhṛtā śakyam ity atra darśayiṣyāmaḥ | sarva-śāstrārthopasaṃhāra-prakaraṇe ca samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā ity atra viśeṣato darśayiṣyāmaḥ | alam iha bahu-prapañcanena, iti upasaṃhriyate ||BhGS_13.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Well then! Since the nature of action, agent, and result does not intrinsically belong to the Self, and since it is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> — it follows that actions are to be performed only by the non-knower, not by the wise. This is indeed the correct conclusion. And we shall show this very point in the passage 'For an embodied being, it is not possible...' [<s>BhG</s> 18.11]. And in the chapter that summarizes the meaning of all scripture, in the passage 'O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the supreme culmination of knowledge' [<s>BhG</s> 18.50], we shall show it specifically. Enough of excessive elaboration here — thus [the discussion] is concluded. ||<s>BhGS</s> 13.2||

children.text: idaṃ śarīram [Gītā 13.2] ity-ādi-ślokopadiṣṭasya kṣetrādhyāyārthasya saṃgraha-śloko 'yam upanyasyate tat kṣetraṃ yac cety ādi, vyācikhyāsitasya hy arthasya saṃgrahopanyāso nyāyya iti -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This summary verse of the chapter on the <s>kṣetra</s>, the meaning taught by the verse beginning 'This body' [<s>BhG</s> 13.2], is now presented — 'That <s>kṣetra</s>, which...' etc. — for it is proper to present a summary of the meaning one wishes to expound:

children.text: tat kṣetraṃ yac ca yādṛk ca yad-vikāri yataś ca yat |
children.translated_text: That <s>kṣetra</s> (field), what it is, of what nature, what its modifications, whence arises what,

children.text: sa ca yo yat-prabhāvaś ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu ||BhG_13.3||
children.translated_text: and who he [the <s>kṣetrajña</s>] is, and what his powers — hear that from me in brief. ||<s>BhG</s> 13.3||

children.text: yan nirdiṣṭam idaṃ śarīram iti tat tac-chabdena parāmṛśati | yac ca idaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ kṣetraṃ tat yādṛk yādṛśaṃ svakīyair dharmaiḥ | ca-śabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ | yad-vikāri yo vikāro yasya tat yad-vikāri, yato yasmāc ca yat, kāryam utpadyate iti vākya-śeṣaḥ | sa ca yaḥ kṣetrajño nirdiṣṭaḥ sa yat-prabhāvo ye prabhāvā upādhi-kṛtāḥ śaktayo yasya sa yat-prabhāvaś ca | tat kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor yāthātmyaṃ yathā-viśeṣitaṃ samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa me mama vākyataḥ śṛṇu | śrutvāvadhāraya ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That which was indicated as 'this body' — that is referred to by the word 'that.' 'And what' — this <s>kṣetra</s> that was indicated — 'of what nature' (<s>yādṛk</s>), i.e., what it is like by virtue of its own properties. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) serves as a conjunction. 'Of what modifications' (<s>yad-vikāri</s>) — what modification belongs to it, that is <s>yad-vikāri</s>. 'Whence arises what' — from what [cause] what [effect] arises — this is the completion of the sentence. 'And who he is' — the <s>kṣetrajña</s> that was indicated — he whose powers, whose capacities conditioned by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>), are such — that is 'of such powers' (<s>yat-prabhāva</s>). That — the true nature of the <s>kṣetra</s> and the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, as specifically characterized — in brief (<s>samāsena</s>), in summary, hear from me, from my words. Having heard, ascertain it — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 13.3||

children.text: tat kṣetra-kṣetrajña-yāthātmyaṃ vivakṣitaṃ stauti śrotṛ-buddhi-prarocanārtham -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The intended teaching about the true nature of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> is praised, in order to engage the listener's intellect:

children.text: ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṃ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak |
children.translated_text: It has been sung by sages in many ways, in diverse <s>Vedic</s> hymns, separately,

children.text: brahma-sūtra-padaiś caiva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ ||BhG_13.4||
children.translated_text: and also in the well-reasoned, definitive passages of the <s>Brahma-sūtras</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 13.4||

children.text: ṛṣibhir vasiṣṭhādibhir bahudhā bahu-prakāraṃ gītaṃ kathitam | chandobhiś chandāṃsi ṛg-ādīni taiś chandobhir vividhair nānā-bhāvair nānā-prakāraiḥ pṛthag vivekato gītam | kiṃ ca, brahma-sūtra-padaiś caiva brahmaṇaḥ sūcakāni vākyāni brahma-sūtrāṇi taiḥ padyate gamyate jñāyata iti tāni padāny ucyante tair eva ca kṣetra-kṣetrajña-yāthātmyam gītam ity anuvartate | ātmety evopāsīta ity evam ādibhir brahma-sūtra-padair ātmā jñāyate | hetumadbhir yukti-yuktair viniścitair niḥsaṃśaya-rūpair niścita-pratyayotpādakair ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'By sages' — by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and others — 'in many ways,' i.e., in many manners, 'it has been sung,' i.e., declared. 'In <s>Vedic</s> hymns' (<s>chandas</s>) — the <s>Ṛg-veda</s> etc. are the <s>chandas</s>; in those <s>Vedic</s> hymns, 'diverse,' i.e., of various kinds, of various forms, 'separately' (<s>pṛthak</s>), i.e., with discrimination — it has been sung. Moreover — 'in the passages of the <s>Brahma-sūtras</s>' — the sentences that indicate <s>Brahman</s> are <s>Brahma-sūtras</s>; those [sūtras] by which [<s>Brahman</s>] is reached, known — hence they are called 'passages' (<s>padāni</s>). By those very [passages] the true nature of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> has been sung — this is supplied [from the context]. [Through passages such as] 'One should meditate: It is the Self' — by such <s>Brahma-sūtra</s> passages, the Self is known. '[These are] well-reasoned' (<s>hetumat</s>) — furnished with logical reasoning; 'definitive' (<s>viniścita</s>) — of an unambiguous nature, producing certain knowledge — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 13.4||

children.text: stutyābhimukhībhūtāyārjunāyāha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] To <s>Arjuna</s>, whose attention has been engaged through the praise, the Blessed Lord says:

children.text: mahā-bhūtāny ahaṃkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca |
children.translated_text: The great elements, ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) as well,

children.text: indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriya-gocarāḥ ||BhG_13.5||
children.translated_text: the ten senses and one [more], and the five objects of the senses — ||<s>BhG</s> 13.5||

children.text:
mahā-bhūtāni mahānti ca tāni sarva-vikāra-vyāpakatvād bhūtāni ca sūkṣmāṇi | sthūlāni tv indriya-gocara-śabdenābhidhāyiṣyante | ahaṃkāro mahā-bhūta-kāraṇam ahaṃ-pratyaya-lakṣaṇaḥ | ahaṃkāra-kāraṇaṃ buddhir adhyavasāya-lakṣaṇā | tat-kāraṇam avyaktam eva ca, na vyaktam avyaktam avyākṛtam īśvara-śaktir mama māyā duratyayā ity uktam | eva-śabdaḥ prakṛty-avadhāraṇārtha etāvaty evāṣṭadhā bhinnā prakṛtiḥ | ca-śabdo bheda-samuccayārthaḥ | indriyāṇi daśa, śrotrādīni pañca buddhy-utpādakatvād buddhīndriyāṇi | vāk-pāṇy-ādīni pañca karma-nirvartakatvāt karmendriyāṇi | tāni daśa | ekaṃ ca | kiṃ tat ? mana ekādaśaṃ saṃkalpādyātmakam | pañca cendriya-gocarāḥ śabdādayo viṣayāḥ | tāny etāni sāṃkhyāś catur-viṃśati-tattvāny ācakṣate
||BhGS_13.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Great elements' (<s>mahā-bhūtāni</s>) — great, because they pervade all modifications, and elements (<s>bhūta</s>) — but subtle [elements]. The gross [elements], however, will be denoted by the term 'objects of the senses.' '<s>Ahaṃkāra</s>' (ego-sense) — the cause of the great elements, characterized by the 'I'-notion. The cause of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is '<s>buddhi</s>' (intellect), characterized by determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). Its cause is the '<s>avyakta</s>' (Unmanifest) as well — what is not manifest is <s>avyakta</s>, the undifferentiated, the power of the Lord — 'My <s>Māyā</s>, difficult to cross' [<s>BhG</s> 7.14] — this has been stated. The word 'eva' (indeed/as well) serves to delimit <s>Prakṛti</s> — <s>Prakṛti</s> is divided eightfold to exactly this extent. The word 'ca' (and) serves to conjoin the divisions. The senses are ten: the five beginning with hearing — producing cognition, hence 'cognitive senses' (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>); and the five beginning with speech and hands — effecting action, hence 'organs of action' (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>). These are ten. 'And one' — what is that? The mind (<s>manas</s>), the eleventh, whose nature is deliberation etc. 'And the five objects of the senses' — the objects beginning with sound. These — the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> enumerate them as the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> (principles). ||<s>BhGS</s> 13.5||

children.text: athedānīṃ ātma-guṇāḥ iti yān ācakṣate vaiśeṣikās te 'pi kṣetra-dharmā eva, na tu kṣetrajñasyety āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, those that the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> call 'qualities of the Self' — they too are properties of the <s>kṣetra</s> alone, not of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> — thus the Blessed Lord says:

children.text: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃghātaś cetanā dhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness, and firmness —

children.text: etat kṣetraṃ samāsena sa-vikāram udāhṛtam ||BhG_13.6||
children.translated_text: this <s>kṣetra</s> (field), together with its modifications, has been briefly described. ||<s>BhG</s> 13.6||

children.text:
icchā yaj-jātīyaṃ sukha-hetum artham upalabdhavān pūrvam, punas taj-jātīyam upalabhamānas tam ādātum icchati sukha-hetur iti | seyaṃ icchāntaḥ-karaṇa-dharmo jñeyatvāt kṣetram | tathā dveṣaḥ, yaj-jātīyam arthaṃ duḥkha-hetutvenānubhūtavān, punas taj-jātīyam artham upalabhamānas taṃ dveṣṭi | so 'yaṃ dveṣo jñeyatvāt kṣetram eva | tathā sukham anukūlaṃ prasanna-sattvātmakaṃ jñeyatvāt kṣetram eva | duḥkhaṃ pratikūlātmakam | jñeyatvāt tad api kṣetram | saṃghāto dehendriyāṇāṃ saṃhatiḥ | tasyām abhivyaktāntaḥkaraṇa-vṛttiḥ, tapta iva loha-piṇḍe 'gniḥ | ātma-caitanyābhāsa-rasa-viddhā cetanā | sā ca kṣetraṃ jñeyatvāt | dhṛtir yayāvasāda-prāptāni dehendriyāṇi dhriyante | sā ca jñeyatvāt kṣetram | sarvāntaḥ-karaṇa-dharmopalakṣaṇārtham icchādi-grahaṇam | yata
uktam upasaṃharati - etad iti | etat kṣetraṃ samāsena sa-vikāraṃ saha vikāreṇa mahad-ādinā udāhṛtam uktam ||BhGS_13.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Desire — when one has previously experienced an object of a certain kind as a cause of pleasure, upon encountering another object of the same kind, one desires to seize it, [thinking] 'it is a cause of pleasure.' This desire is a property of the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>); being an object of knowledge, it is the field (<s>kṣetra</s>). Likewise aversion — when one has experienced an object of a certain kind as a cause of pain, upon encountering another object of the same kind, one hates it. This aversion, being an object of knowledge, is indeed the field. Likewise pleasure — that which is agreeable, whose nature is the clarity of <s>sattva</s> (purity) — being an object of knowledge, it is indeed the field. Pain — that whose nature is disagreeable; being an object of knowledge, it too is the field. The aggregate (<s>saṃghāta</s>) — the combination of body and senses. In that [combination] is manifested the activity of the inner faculty, like fire in a heated ball of iron. Consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>) — imbued with the reflection of the awareness of the Self. And that too is the field, being an object of knowledge. Fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) — that by which the body and senses, when about to sink [into exhaustion], are sustained. And that too, being an object of knowledge, is the field. The mention of desire and the rest is for the purpose of exemplifying all properties of the inner faculty. Since this has been stated, he concludes with 'this' (<s>etat</s>): this field, in brief, together with its modifications — along with the modifications beginning with <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) — has been described, has been stated. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.6 //

children.text: yasya kṣetra-bheda-jātasya saṃhatiḥ idaṃ śarīraṃ kṣetram [Gītā 13.2] ity uktam | tat kṣetraṃ vyākhyātaṃ mahā-bhūtādi-bheda-bhinnaṃ dhṛty-antam | kṣetrajño vakṣyamāṇa-viśeṣaṇaḥ - yasya sa-prabhāvasya kṣetrajñasya parijñānād amṛtatvaṃ bhavati, tam jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmīty ādinā sa-viśeṣaṇaṃ svayam eva vakṣyati bhagavān | adhunā tu taj-jñāna-sādhana-gaṇam amānitvādi-lakṣaṇam, yasmin sati taj-jñeya-vijñāne yogyo 'dhikṛto bhavati, yat-paraḥ saṃnyāsī jñāna-niṣṭha ucyate, tam amānitvādi-gaṇaṃ jñāna-sādhanatvāj jñāna-śabda-vācyaṃ vidadhāti bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The aggregate of the various categories of the field — this body has been called the field in 'this body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, is called the field' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.1]. That field has been explained as differentiated into the categories beginning with the great elements and ending with fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>). The knower of the field, whose characteristics are to be stated — of the knower of the field possessed of powers, through the knowledge of whom immortality results — 'I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality' — the Blessed Lord Himself will describe it with its qualifications. But now, the group of means to that knowledge, characterized by humility and the rest — by possessing which one becomes fit and qualified for the knowledge of that which is to be known, and devoted to which one is called a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) established in knowledge — that group beginning with humility, being called 'knowledge' because it is the means to knowledge, the Blessed Lord sets forth —

children.text: amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṃsā kṣāntir ārjavam |
children.translated_text: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-violence, patience, uprightness,

children.text: ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ ||BhG_13.7||
children.translated_text: service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-restraint — // <s>BhG</s> 13.7 //

children.text: amānitvaṃ mānino bhāvaḥ mānitvam ātmano ślāghanam, tad-abhāvo 'mānitvam | adambhitvaṃ sva-dharma-prakaṭīkaraṇaṃ dambhitvam, tad-abhāvo 'dambhitvam | ahiṃsā hiṃsanaṃ prāṇinām apīḍānam | kṣāntiḥ parāparādha-prāptāv avikriyā | ārjavam ṛju-bhāvo 'vakratvam | ācāryopāsanaṃ mokṣa-sādhanopadeṣṭur ācāryasya śuśrūṣādi-prayogeṇa sevanam | śaucaṃ kāya-malānāṃ mṛj-jalābhyāṃ prakṣālanam | antaś ca manasaḥ pratipakṣa-bhāvanayā rāgādi-malānām apanayanaṃ śaucam | sthairyaṃ sthira-bhāvaḥ, mokṣa-mārga eva kṛtādhyavasāyatvam | ātma-vinigraha ātmano 'pakārakasya ātma-śabda-vācyasya kārya-karaṇa-saṃghātasya vinigrahaḥ svabhāvena sarvataḥ pravṛttasya san-mārga eva nirodha ātma-vinigrahaḥ ||BhGS_13.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Humility (<s>amānitva</s>) — the state of one who shows honor is honor-seeking (<s>mānitva</s>), i.e., self-praise; its absence is humility. Unpretentiousness (<s>adambhitva</s>) — the display of one's own <s>dharma</s> (religious merit) is pretentiousness (<s>dambhitva</s>); its absence is unpretentiousness. Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) — <s>hiṃsā</s> is the causing of pain to living beings; [its absence is non-violence]. Patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) — remaining undisturbed upon encountering another's offense. Uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>) — straightforwardness, non-crookedness. Service to the teacher (<s>ācāryopāsana</s>) — attending upon the teacher who instructs in the means of liberation, through devoted service and the like. Purity (<s>śauca</s>) — the cleansing of bodily impurities with earth and water; and internally, the removal of impurities such as attachment and the rest from the mind through the cultivation of their opposites — that is purity. Steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>) — the state of being firm; having made one's determination solely in the path of liberation. Self-restraint (<s>ātma-vinigraha</s>) — the restraint of the self — meaning the aggregate of body and senses, which is denoted by the word 'self' and which tends by nature to go astray in every direction — its control solely on the right path is self-restraint. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.7 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam anahaṃkāra eva ca |
children.translated_text: Dispassion toward sense-objects, and absence of egoism,

children.text: janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣānudarśanam ||BhG_13.8||
children.translated_text: perception of the evil in birth, death, old age, disease, and suffering — // <s>BhG</s> 13.8 //

children.text:
indriyārtheṣu śabdādiṣu dṛṣṭādṛṣṭeṣu bhogeṣu virāga-bhāvo vairāgyam | anahaṃkāro 'haṃkārābhāva eva ca | janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣānudarśanaṃ janma ca mṛtyuś ca jarā ca vyādhayaś ca duḥkhāni ca teṣu janmādi-duḥkhānteṣu pratyekaṃ doṣānudarśanam | janmani garbha-vāsa-yoni-dvāra-niḥsaraṇaṃ doṣaḥ, tasyānudarśanam ālocanam | tathā mṛtyau doṣānudarśanam | tathā jarāyāṃ prajñā-śakti-tejo-nirodha-doṣānudarśanaṃ paribhūtatā ceti | tathā vyādhiṣu śiro-rogādiṣu doṣānudarśanam | tathā duḥkheṣu adhyātmādhibhūtādhidaiva-nimitteṣu | athavā duḥkhāny eva doṣo duḥkha-doṣas tasya janmādiṣu pūrvavad anudarśanam | duḥkhaṃ janma, duḥkhaṃ mṛtyuḥ, duḥkhaṃ jarā, duḥkhaṃ vyādhayaḥ | duḥkha-nimittatvāj
janmādayo duḥkham, na punaḥ svarūpeṇaiva duḥkham iti | evaṃ janmādiṣu duḥkha-doṣānudarśanād dehendriyādi-viṣaya-bhogeṣu vairāgyam upajāyate | tataḥ pratyag-ātmani pravṛttiḥ karaṇānām ātma-darśanāya | evaṃ jñāna-hetutvāj jñānam ucyate janmādi-duḥkha-doṣānudarśanam ||BhGS_13.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward sense-objects — toward objects such as sound and the rest, toward enjoyments both seen and unseen — the state of being free from attachment is dispassion. Absence of egoism (<s>anahaṃkāra</s>) — the very absence of the ego-sense. Perception of the evil in birth, death, old age, disease, and suffering — birth, death, old age, diseases, and sufferings: in each of these, from birth to suffering, there is perception of evil. In birth, the evil is the suffering of dwelling in the womb and passing through the birth canal; the perception of that is its contemplation. Likewise, the perception of evil in death. Likewise in old age — the perception of the evil of the suppression of intelligence, strength, and vigor, and of being treated with contempt. Likewise the perception of evil in diseases such as headache and the rest. Likewise in sufferings caused by the self (<s>adhyātma</s>), by beings (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and by the gods (<s>adhidaiva</s>). Alternatively, the sufferings themselves are the evil — 'suffering-evil'; the perception of that in birth and the rest is as before. Birth is suffering, death is suffering, old age is suffering, diseases are suffering. Because they are causes of suffering, birth and the rest are suffering — not that they are suffering by their very nature. Thus, from the perception of suffering-evil in birth and the rest, dispassion toward the enjoyment of body, senses, and sense-objects arises. From that, the faculties turn toward the inner Self for the vision of the Self. Thus, because it is a cause of knowledge, the perception of suffering-evil in birth and the rest is called 'knowledge.' // <s>BhGS</s> 13.8 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛhādiṣu |
children.translated_text: Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife, home, and the like,

children.text: nityaṃ ca sama-cittatvam iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu ||BhG_13.9||
children.translated_text: and constant equanimity in the occurrence of the desirable and undesirable — // <s>BhG</s> 13.9 //

children.text: asaktiḥ saktiḥ saṅga-nimitteṣu viṣayeṣu prīti-mātram, tad-abhāvo 'saktiḥ | anabhiṣvaṅgo 'bhiṣvaṅgābhāvaḥ | abhiṣvaṅgo nāma āsakti-viśeṣa evānanyātma-bhāvanā-lakṣaṇaḥ | yathānyasmin sukhini duḥkhini vāham eva sukhī, duḥkhī ca, jīvati mṛte vāham eva jīvāmi mariṣyāmi ceti | kva ? ity āha - putra-dāra-gṛhādiṣu | putreṣu dāreṣu gṛheṣv ādi-grahaṇād anyeṣv apy atyanteṣṭeṣu dāsa-vargādiṣu | tac cobhayaṃ jñānārthatvāj jñānam ucyate | nityaṃ ca sama-cittatvaṃ tulya-cittatā | kva ? iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣv iṣṭānām aniṣṭānāṃ copapattayaḥ saṃprāptayas tāsv iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu nityam eva tulya-cittatā | iṣṭopapattiṣu na hṛṣyati, na kupyati cāniṣṭopapattiṣu | tac caitan nityaṃ sama-cittatvaṃ jñānam ||BhGS_13.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Non-attachment (<s>asakti</s>) — <s>sakti</s> (attachment) is mere affection toward objects that are causes of attachment; its absence is non-attachment. Absence of clinging (<s>anabhiṣvaṅga</s>) — the absence of <s>abhiṣvaṅga</s> (intense clinging). <s>Abhiṣvaṅga</s> is a special form of attachment characterized by identification with another — as when one [thinks] regarding another who is happy or unhappy: 'I myself am happy, I myself am unhappy'; or regarding one who is alive or dead: 'I myself live, I myself shall die.' Toward what? — he says: toward son, wife, home, and the like. Toward sons, toward wives, toward homes; and by the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), toward other extremely dear ones such as the class of servants. And both of these [non-attachment and absence of clinging] are called 'knowledge' because they serve the purpose of knowledge. And constant equanimity — evenness of mind. In what? In the occurrence of the desirable and undesirable — the occurrences, the arrivals, of the desired and the undesired; in those occurrences of the desirable and undesirable, there is constant evenness of mind. One does not rejoice at the occurrence of the desirable, nor is one angered at the occurrence of the undesirable. And this constant equanimity is knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.9 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: mayi cānanya-yogena bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī |
children.translated_text: Unswerving devotion to Me through undivided <s>yoga</s> (discipline),

children.text: vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratir jana-saṃsadi ||BhG_13.10||
children.translated_text: resorting to solitary places, distaste for the company of people — // <s>BhG</s> 13.10 //

children.text: mayi ceśvare 'nanya-yogena apṛthak-samādhinā nānyo bhagavato vāsudevāt paro 'sti, ataḥ sa eva no gatir ity evaṃ niścitāvyabhicāriṇī buddhir ananya-yogaḥ, tena bhajanaṃ bhaktir na vyabhicaraṇa-śīlā avyabhicāriṇī | sā ca jñānam | vivikta-deśa-sevitvam | viviktaḥ svabhāvataḥ saṃskāreṇa vāśucy-ādibhiḥ sarpa-vyāghrādibhiś ca rahito 'raṇya-nadī-pulina-deva-gṛhādibhir vivikto deśaḥ, taṃ sevituṃ śīlam asyeti vivikta-deśa-sevī, tad-bhāvo vivikta-deśa-sevitvam | vivikteṣu hi deśeṣu cittaṃ prasīdati yatas tataḥ ātmādi-bhāvanā vivikta upajāyate | ato vivakta-deśa-sevitvaṃ jñānam ucyate | aratir aramaṇaṃ jana-saṃsadi | janānāṃ prākṛtānāṃ saṃskāra-śūnyānām avinītānāṃ saṃsat samavāyo jana-saṃsat | na saṃskāravatāṃ vinītānāṃ saṃsat | tasyā jñānopakārakatvāt | ataḥ
prākṛta-jana-saṃsady aratir jñānārthatvāj jñānam ||BhGS_13.10||
children.translated_text: distaste in the company of common people is knowledge, because it serves the purpose of knowledge. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.10 //

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And to Me, the Lord, through undivided <s>yoga</s> — through concentration that is not separate [from Me] — 'There is nothing other than the Blessed Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> that is supreme; therefore He alone is our refuge' — with such firm, unswerving conviction, which is undivided <s>yoga</s> — through that, worship (<s>bhajana</s>) is devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — not prone to deviation, [hence] unswerving. And that is knowledge. Resorting to solitary places — a solitary (<s>vivikta</s>) place is one that is naturally or through purificatory rites free from impurities and the like, and from snakes, tigers, and the like — such as a forest, a river sandbank, a temple, and the like. One whose habit is to frequent such [places] is a 'frequenter of solitary places'; the state of being such is 'resorting to solitary places.' For in solitary places the mind becomes clear, and from that, contemplation of the Self and the like arises in solitude. Therefore, resorting to solitary places is called knowledge. Distaste in the company of people — non-enjoyment in the assembly of people. The assembly (<s>saṃsat</s>) of common (<s>prākṛta</s>), uncultured, ill-mannered people is 'the company of people' — not the company of the cultured and well-mannered, because that aids knowledge. Therefore,

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṃ tattva-jñānārtha-darśanam |
children.translated_text: Constancy in the knowledge of the Self, perception of the purpose of the knowledge of truth —

children.text: etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṃ yad ato 'nyathā ||BhG_13.11||
children.translated_text: this is declared to be knowledge; what is contrary to this is ignorance. // <s>BhG</s> 13.11 //

children.text: adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvam ātmādi-viṣayaṃ jñānam adhyātma-jñānam, tasmin nitya-bhāvo nityatvam | amānitvādīnāṃ jñāna-sādhanānāṃ bhāvanā-paripāka-nimittaṃ tattva-jñānam, tasyārtho mokṣaḥ saṃsāroparamaḥ | tasyālocanaṃ tattva-jñānārtha-darśanam | tattva-jñāna-phalālocane hi tat-sādhanānuṣṭhāne pravṛttiḥ syād iti | etad amānitvādi-tattva-jñānārtha-darśanāntam uktaṃ jñānam iti proktaṃ jñānārthatvāt | ajñānaṃ yad ato 'smād yathoktād anyathā viparyayeṇa | mānitvaṃ dambhitvaṃ hiṃsā kṣāntir anārjavam ity ādy ajñānaṃ vijñeyaṃ pariharaṇāya, saṃsāra-pravṛtti-kāraṇatvād iti ||BhGS_13.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Constancy in the knowledge of the Self (<s>adhyātma-jñāna-nityatva</s>) — knowledge pertaining to the Self and the like is '<s>adhyātma-jñāna</s>'; being constant in that, i.e., perpetually [engaged in it], is constancy. The knowledge of truth (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>), which results from the ripening of the cultivation of the means of knowledge beginning with humility — its purpose (<s>artha</s>) is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The contemplation of that is 'perception of the purpose of the knowledge of truth.' For when one contemplates the fruit of the knowledge of truth, one would engage in the practice of its means. This — what has been stated from humility through to 'perception of the purpose of the knowledge of truth' — is declared to be knowledge, because it serves the purpose of knowledge. Ignorance is what is contrary to this — the opposite of what has been described: pride, pretentiousness, violence, impatience, crookedness, and the rest — that should be recognized as ignorance, to be avoided, because it is the cause of the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.11 //

children.text: yathoktena jñānena jñātavyaṃ kim ? ity ākāṅkṣāyām āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What is to be known through the knowledge described above? — in response to this expectation, he says —

children.text: jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute |
children.translated_text: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality;

children.text: anādimat paraṃ brahma na sat tan nāsad ucyate ||BhG_13.12||
children.translated_text: the beginningless supreme <s>Brahman</s> — it is said to be neither being (<s>sat</s>) nor non-being (<s>asat</s>). // <s>BhG</s> 13.12 //

children.text: nanu yamāḥ niyamāś cāmānitvādayaḥ | na tair jñeyaṃ jñāyate | na hy amānitvādi kasyacit vastunaḥ paricchedakaṃ dṛṣṭam | sarvatraiva ca yad-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ tad eva tasya jñeyasya paricchedakaṃ dṛśyate | na hy anya-viṣayeṇa jñānenānyad upalabhyate, yathā ghaṭa-viṣayeṇa jñānenāgniḥ | naiṣa doṣaḥ | jñāna-nimittatvāj jñānam ucyata iti hy avocāma | jñāna-sahakāri-kāraṇatvāc ca | jñeyaṃ jñātavyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi prakarṣeṇa yathāvat vakṣyāmi | kiṃ-phalaṃ tat ? iti prarocanena śrotur abhimukhīkaraṇāyāha - yaj jñeyaṃ jñātvāmṛtam amṛtatvam aśnute, na punar mriyata ity arthaḥ | anādimat ādir asyāstīti ādimat, nādimad anādimat | kiṃ tat ? paraṃ niratiśayaṃ brahma, jñeyam iti prakṛtam |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, humility and the rest are moral and disciplinary observances (<s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>). The knowable is not known through them. For humility and the rest have never been seen to determine any real entity. And in every case, only the knowledge pertaining to an object is seen to determine that knowable object. For one thing is not apprehended through knowledge pertaining to another thing — just as fire is not [apprehended] through knowledge pertaining to a pot. This is not a fault. For we have said that [humility etc.] are called 'knowledge' because they are the cause of knowledge, and because they are cooperative causes of knowledge. The knowable — that which is to be known — I shall declare, I shall properly and fully state. What is the fruit of that? — thus, for the purpose of arousing interest and directing the listener's attention, he says: knowing which knowable, one attains immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) — meaning one does not die again. Beginningless (<s>anādimat</s>) — that which has a beginning is '<s>ādimat</s>'; that which is not '<s>ādimat</s>' is '<s>anādimat</s>.' What is it? The supreme — unsurpassed — <s>Brahman</s>, which is the subject under discussion as 'the knowable.'

children.text: atra kecit anādi mat-param iti padaṃ chindanti, bahu-vrīhiṇokte 'rthe matupa ānarthakyam aniṣṭaṃ syād iti | artha-viśeṣaṃ ca darśayanti - ahaṃ vāsudevākhyā parā śaktir yasya tan mat-param iti | satyam evam apunar-uktaṃ syāt | arthaś cet saṃbhavati | na tv arthaḥ saṃbhavati, brahmaṇaḥ sarva-viśeṣa-pratiṣedhenaiva vijijñāpayiṣitvān na sat tan nāsad ucyate iti | viśiṣṭa-śaktimattva-pradarśanaṃ viśeṣa-pratiṣedhaś ceti vipratiṣiddham | tasmāt matupo bahu-vrīhiṇā samānārthatve 'pi prayogo śloka-pūraṇārthaḥ | amṛtatva-phalaṃ jñeyaṃ mayocyata iti prarocanenābhimukhīkṛtyāha - na sat taj jñeyam ucyate iti nāpy asat tad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, some break the compound as '<s>anādi mat-param</s>' [i.e., 'beginningless, having Me as supreme'], [arguing that] since the meaning is already expressed by the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the possessive suffix <s>matup</s> would be redundant, which is undesirable. And they show a special meaning: 'that whose supreme [nature] is Me, called <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supreme power — that is <s>mat-param</s>.' True, this would avoid redundancy. [But only] if the meaning is tenable. However, the meaning is not tenable, because the intent is to make [<s>Brahman</s>] known solely through the negation of all distinctions — 'it is said to be neither being nor non-being.' Showing that it possesses a distinguished power while negating all distinctions — this is contradictory. Therefore, even though the possessive suffix <s>matup</s> has the same meaning as the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, its use is for completing the meter. Having aroused interest by saying 'the knowable whose fruit is immortality is being stated by Me,' and thereby directing [the listener's] attention, he says: that knowable is said to be not being (<s>sat</s>), nor is it said to be non-being (<s>asat</s>).

children.text: nanu mahatā parikara-bandhena kaṇṭha-raveṇodghuṣya jñeyaṃ pravakṣyāmīti, ananurūpam uktaṃ na sat tan nāsad ucyata iti | na, anurūpam evoktam | katham ? sarvāsu hy upaniṣatsu jñeyaṃ brahma neti neti [BAU 2.3.6] asthūlam anaṇu [BAU 3.8.8] ity ādi-viśeṣa-pratiṣedhenaiva nirdiśyate, nedaṃ tad iti vāco 'gocatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: Having made a great preamble and loudly proclaimed 'I shall declare the knowable,' what has been said — 'it is said to be neither being nor non-being' — is inappropriate. Reply: No, it is entirely appropriate. How? For in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the knowable <s>Brahman</s> is indicated solely through the negation of distinctions — 'not this, not this' [<s>BAU</s> 2.3.6], 'neither gross nor subtle' [<s>BAU</s> 3.8.8] — and so on, because it is beyond the range of speech, [such that one cannot say] 'this is that.'

children.text: nanu na tad asti, yad vastv asti-śabdena nocyate | athāsti-śabdena nocyate, nāsti taj jñeyam | vipratiṣiddhaṃ ca - jñeyaṃ tad asti-śabdena nocyate iti ca | na tāvan nāsti, nāsti-buddhy-aviṣayatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Objection: There exists nothing real that cannot be designated by the word 'being' (<s>asti</s>). If it cannot be designated by the word 'being,' then the knowable does not exist. And it is contradictory [to say] 'the knowable exists' and 'it cannot be designated by the word being.' Reply: It is certainly not non-existent, because it is not an object of the cognition 'non-existence.'

children.text: nanu sarvā buddhayo 'sti-nāsti-buddhy-anugatā eva | tatraivaṃ sati jñeyam apy asti-buddhy-anugata-pratyaya-viṣayaṃ vā syāt, nāsti-buddhy-anugata-pratyaya-viṣayaṃ vā syāt | na, atīndriyatvenobhaya-buddhy-anugata-pratyayāviṣayatvāt | yad dhīndriya-gamyaṃ vastu ghaṭādikam, tad asti-buddhy-anugata-pratyaya-viṣayaṃ vā syāt, nāsti-buddhy-anugata-pratyaya-viṣayaṃ vā syāt | idaṃ tu jñeyam atīndriyatvena śabdaika-pramāṇa-gamyatvān na ghaṭādivad ubhaya-buddhy-anugata-pratyaya-viṣayam ity ato na sat tan nāsad ity ucyate ||

yat tūktam - viruddham ucyate, jñeyaṃ tan na sat tan nāsad ucyata iti | na viruddham, anyad eva tad-viditād atho aviditād adhi [KenaU 1.3] iti śruteḥ | śrutir api viruddhārthā iti cet - yathā yajñāya śālām ārabhya yajñam ko hi tad veda yady amuṣmin loke 'sti vā na veti [TaittS 6.1.1] ity evam iti cet, na | viditāviditābhyām anyatva-śruter avaśya-vijñeyārtha-pratipādana-paratvāt yady amuṣmin ity ādi tu vidhi-śeṣo 'rtha-vādaḥ | upapatteś ca sad-asad-ādi-śabdair brahma nocyata iti |

sarvo hi śabdo 'rtha-prakāśanāya prayuktaḥ śrūyamāṇaś ca śrotṛbhir jāti-kriyā-guṇa-saṃbandha-dvāreṇa saṃketa-grahaṇa-sa-vyapekṣārthaṃ pratyāyayati | nānyathā, adṛṣṭatvāt | tad yathā - gaur aśva iti vā jātitaḥ, pacati paṭhatīti vā kriyātaḥ, śuklaḥ kṛṣṇa iti vā guṇataḥ, dhanī gomān iti vā saṃbandhataḥ | na tu brahma jātimat, ato na sad-ādi-śabda-vācyam | nāpi guṇavat, yena guṇa-śabdenocyeta, nirguṇatvāt | nāpi kriyā-śabda-vācyaṃ niṣkriyatvān niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntam [ŚvetU 6.19] iti śruteḥ | na ca saṃbandhī, ekatvāt | advayatvād aviṣayatvād ātmatvāc ca na kenacit, śabdenocyata iti yuktam | yato vāco nivartante [TaittU 2.9] ity ādi-śrutibhiś ca ||BhGS_13.12||
sac-chabda-pratyayāviṣayatvād asattvāśaṅkāyāṃ jñeyasya sarva-prāṇi-karaṇopādhi-dvāreṇa tad-astitvaṃ pratipādayan tad-āśaṅkā-nivṛtty-artham āha -
sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ tat sarvato 'kṣi-śiro-mukham |
sarvataḥ śrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati ||BhG_13.13||

sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ sarvataḥ pāṇayaḥ pādāś cāsyeti sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ taj jñeyam | sarva-prāṇi-karaṇopādhibhiḥ kṣetrajñasyāstitvaṃ vibhāvyate | kṣetrajñaś ca kṣetropādhita ucyate | kṣetraṃ ca pāṇi-pādādibhir anekadhā bhinnam | kṣetropādhi-bheda-kṛtaṃ viśeṣa-jātaṃ mithyaiva kṣetrajñasya, iti tad-apanayanena jñeyatvam uktam na sat tan nāsad ucyate iti | upādhi-kṛtaṃ mithyā-rūpam apy astitvādhigamāya jñeya-dharmavat parikalpya ucyate sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādam ity ādi | tathā hi saṃpradāya-vidāṃ vacanam - adhyāropāpavādābhyāṃ niṣprapañcaṃ prapañcyate iti | sarvatra sarva-dehāvayavatvena gamyamānāḥ pāṇi-pādādayo jñeya-śakti-sad-bhāva-nimitta-svakāryā iti jñeya-sad-bhāve liṅgāni jñeyasyeti upacārata ucyante | tathā vyākhyeyam anyat | sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ taj
jñeyam | sarvato 'kṣi-śiro-mukhaṃ sarvato 'kṣīṇi śirāṃsi mukhāni ca yasya tat sarvato 'kṣi-śiro-mukham | sarvataḥ śrutimat | śrutiḥ śravaṇendriyam, tat yasya tat śrutimat | loke prāṇi-nikāye | sarvam āvṛtya saṃvyāpya tiṣṭhati sthitiṃ labhate ||BhGS_13.13||
upādhibhūta-pāṇi-pādādīndriyādhyāropaṇāj jñeyasya tadvattāśaṅkā mā bhūd ity evam arthaḥ ślokārambhaḥ -
sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriya-vivarjitam |
asaktaṃ sarva-bhṛc caiva nirguṇaṃ guṇa-bhoktṛ ca ||BhG_13.14||

sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṃ sarvāṇi ca tānīndriyāṇi śrotrādīni buddhīndriya-karmendriyākhyāni, antaḥ-karaṇe ca buddhi-manasī, jñeyopādhitvasya tulyatvāt, sarvendriya-grahaṇena gṛhyante | api ca, antaḥ-karaṇopādhi-dvāreṇaiva śrotrādīnām api upādhitvam ity ato 'ntaḥ-karaṇa-bahiṣkaraṇopādhi-bhūtaiḥ sarvendriya-guṇair adhyavasāya-saṃkalpa-śravaṇa-vacanādibhir avabhāsate iti sarvendriya-guṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriya-vyāpārair vyāpṛtam iva taj jñeyam ity arthaḥ | dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva [BAU 4.3.7] iti śruteḥ |

kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇān na vyāpṛtam eveti gṛhyata ity ataḥ āha - sarvendriya-vivarjitam, sarva-karaṇa-rahitam ity arthaḥ | ato na karaṇa-vyāpāraiḥ vyāpṛtaṃ taj jñeyam | yas tv ayaṃ mantraḥ - apāṇi-pādo javano grahītā paśyaty acakṣuḥ sa sṛṇoty akarṇaḥ [ŚvetU 3.19] ity ādiḥ | sa sarvendriyopādhi-guṇānuguṇya-bhajana-śaktimat taj jñeyam ity evaṃ pradarśanārthaḥ, na tu sākṣād eva javanādi-kriyāvattva-pradarśanārthaḥ | andho maṇim avindad [TaittĀ 1.11] ity ādi-mantrārthavat tasya mantrasyārthaḥ | yasmāt sarva-karaṇa-varjitaṃ jñeyam, tasmād asaktaṃ sarva-saṃśleṣavarjitam | yadyapy evam, tathāpi sarva-bhṛc caiva | sad-āspadaṃ hi sarvaṃ sarvatra sad-buddhy-anugamāt | na hi mṛgatṛṣṇikādayo 'pi nirāspadā bhavanti | ataḥ sarva-bhṛt sarvaṃ bibhartīti | syād idaṃ cānyaj jñeyasya sattvādhigama-dvāram -

nirguṇaṃ sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi guṇās tair varjitaṃ taj jñeyam, tathāpi guṇa-bhoktṛ ca guṇānāṃ sattva-rajas-tamasāṃ śabdādi-dvāreṇa sukha-duḥkha-mohākāra-pariṇatānāṃ bhoktṛ copalabdhṛ ca taj jñeyam ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.14||
kiṃ ca -
bahir antaś ca bhūtānām acaraṃ caram eva ca |
sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṃ dūra-sthaṃ cāntike ca tat ||BhG_13.15||

bahis tvak-paryantaṃ deham ātmatvenāvidyā-kalpitam apekṣya tam evāvavadhiṃ kṛtvā bahir ucyate | tathā pratyag-ātmānam apekṣya deham evāvadhiṃ kṛtvā antar ucyate | bahir antaś cety ukte madhye 'bhāve prāpte, idam ucyate - acaraṃ caram eva ca, yac carācaraṃ dehābhāsam api tad eva jñeyaṃ, yathā rajju-sarpābhāsaḥ |

yady acaraṃ caram eva ca syāt vyavahāra-viṣayaṃ sarvaṃ jñeyam, kim-artham idam iti sarvair na vijñeyam ? ity ucyate - satyaṃ sarvābhāsaṃ tat | tathāpi vyomavat sūkṣmam | ataḥ sūkṣmatvāt svena rūpeṇa taj jñeyam apy avijñeyam aviduṣām | viduṣāṃ tu, ātmaivedaṃ sarvam [BAU 7.25.2] brahmaivedaṃ sarvam [BAU 2.5.1] ity ādi-pramāṇato nityaṃ vijñātam | avijñātatayā dūra-sthaṃ varṣa-sahasra-koṭyāpy aviduṣām aprāpyatvāt | antike ca tat, ātmatvād viduṣām ||BhGS_13.15||
kiṃ ca -
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam |
bhūta-bhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||BhG_13.16||

avibhaktaṃ ca pratidehaṃ vyomavat tad ekam | bhūteṣu sarva-prāṇiṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitaṃ deheṣv eva vibhāvyamānatvāt | bhūta-bhartṛ ca bhūtāni bibharti taj jñeyaṃ bhūta-bhartṛ ca sthiti-kāle | pralaya-kāle grasiṣṇu grasana-śīlam | utpatti-kāle prabhaviṣṇu ca prabhavana-śīlaṃ yathā rajjvādiḥ sarpāder mithyā-kalpitasya ||BhGS_13.16||
kiṃ ca, sarvatra vidyamānam api san nopalabhyate cet, jñeyaṃ tamas tarhi ? na | kiṃ tarhi ? -
jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñāna-gamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||BhG_13.17||

jyotiṣām ādity-ādīnām api taj jñeyaṃ jyotiḥ | ātma-caitanya-jyotiṣeddhāni hy ādity-ādīni jyotīṃṣi dīpyante, yena sūryas tapati tejaseddhaḥ [TaittBr 3.12.9], tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti [ŚvetU 6.14] īty ādi-śrutibhyaḥ | smṛte ca ihaiva - yad āditya-gataṃ tejaḥ [Gītā 15.12] ity ādeḥ | tamaso 'jñānāt param aspṛṣṭam ucyate | jñānāder duḥsaṃpādana-buddhyā prāptāvasādasyottambhanārtham āha - jñānam amānitvādi | jñeyam jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmīty [Gītā 13.13] ādinoktam | jñāna-gamyam jñeyam eva jñātaṃ saj jñāna-phalam iti jñāna-gamyam ucyate | jñāyamānaṃ tu jñeyam | tad etat trayam api hṛdi buddhau sarvasya prāṇi-jātasya viṣṭhitaṃ viśeṣeṇa sthitam | tatraiva hi trayaṃ vibhāvyate ||BhGS_13.17||
yathoktārthopasaṃhārārtho 'yaṃ śloka ārabhyate -
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāyopapadyate ||BhG_13.18||

ity evaṃ kṣetraṃ mahā-bhūtādi-dhṛty-antaṃ, tathā jñānam amānitvādi tattva-jñānārtha-darśana-paryantaṃ, jñeyaṃ ca jñeyaṃ yat tat ity ādi tamasaḥ param ucyate ity evam antam uktaṃ samāsataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ | etāvān sarvo hi vedārtho gītārthaś copasaṃhṛtyoktaḥ | asmin samyag-darśane ko 'dhikriyate ? ity ucyate - mad-bhakto mayīśvare sarvajñe parama-gurau vāsudeve samarpita-sarvātma-bhāvo yat paśyati śṛṇoti spṛśati vā sarvam eva bhagavān vāsudevaḥ ity evaṃ-grahāviṣṭa-buddhir mad-bhaktaḥ sa etad yathoktaṃ samyag darśanaṃ vijñāya, mad-bhāvāya mama bhāvo mad-bhāvaḥ paramātma-bhāvas tasmai mad-bhāvāya upapadyate, mokṣaṃ gacchati ||BhGS_13.18||

tatra saptame īśvarasya dve prakṛtī upanyaste parāpare kṣetra-kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇe | etad-yonīni bhūtāni [Gītā 7.7] iti coktam | kṣetra-kṣetrajña-prakṛti-dvaya-yonitvaṃ kathaṃ bhūtānām ity ayam artho 'dhunocyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In the seventh [chapter], the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> (natures) of the Lord were presented — the higher and the lower — characterized as the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) and the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). And it was stated: 'all beings have these as their source' [<s>Gītā</s> 7.7]. How the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> — the field and the knower of the field — serve as the source of beings — this meaning is now being stated:

children.text: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api |
children.translated_text: Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the person) to be beginningless;

children.text: vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś caiva viddhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān ||BhG_13.19||
children.translated_text: and know the modifications and the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) to be born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 13.19 //

children.text: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva īśvarasya prakṛtī | tau prakṛti-puruṣau ubhāv apy anādi viddhi, na vidyate ādir yayos tau anādī | nityeśvaratvād īśvarasya tat-prakṛtyor api yuktaṃ nityatvena bhavitum | prakṛti-dvayavattvam eva hīśvarasyeśvaratvam | yābhyāṃ prakṛtibhyām īśvaro jagad-utpatti-sthiti-pralaya-hetus te dve 'nādī satyau saṃsārasya kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> indeed — these are the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> of the Lord. Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> to be beginningless (<s>anādi</s>) — that which has no beginning is <s>anādi</s>. Since the Lord is eternally the Lord, it is fitting that His two <s>Prakṛtis</s> also exist eternally. For it is the very possession of the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> that constitutes the Lord's status as Lord. These two <s>Prakṛtis</s>, through which the Lord is the cause of the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe — being beginningless and real, they are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).

children.text: nādī anādī iti tat-puruṣa-samāsaṃ kecit varṇayanti | tena hi kileśvarasya kāraṇatvaṃ sidhyati | yadi punaḥ prakṛti-puruṣāv eva nityau syātāṃ tat-kṛtam eva jagat, neśvarasya jagataḥ kartṛtvam | tad asat | prāk prakṛti-puruṣayor utpatter īśitavyābhāvād īśvarasyānīśvaratva-prasaṅgāt, saṃsārasya nirnimittatve 'nirmokṣa-prasaṅgāt śāstrānarthakya-prasaṅgād bandha-mokṣābhāva-prasaṅgāc ca | nityatve punar īśvarasya prakṛtyoḥ sarvam etad upapannaṃ bhavet | katham ? vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś caiva | vakṣyamāṇān vikārān buddhy-ādi-dehendriyāntān guṇāṃś ca sukha-duḥkha-moha-pratyayākāra-pariṇatān viddhi jānīhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān | prakṛtir īśvarasya vikāra-kāraṇa-śaktis triguṇātmikā māyā | sā saṃbhavo yeṣāṃ vikārāṇāṃ guṇānāṃ ca tān vikārān
guṇāṃś ca viddhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān prakṛti-pariṇāmān ||BhGS_13.19||
children.translated_text: and <s>guṇas</s> to be born of <s>Prakṛti</s> — to be transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.19 //

[Śaṅkara's commentary:] Some explain '<s>nādī anādī</s>' as a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound. For thereby, they claim, the Lord's causality is established. But if <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> alone were eternal, the universe would be produced by them alone, and the Lord would not be the creator of the universe. This is untenable — because, prior to the origination of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there would be no entity to be governed, and hence the undesirable consequence that the Lord would not be the Lord; because, if <s>saṃsāra</s> were without a cause, the undesirable consequence would follow that there is no liberation; because the undesirable consequence that scripture would become purposeless would arise; and because the undesirable consequence of the absence of bondage and liberation would follow. But if the Lord together with His <s>Prakṛtis</s> is eternal, all of this would be justified. How? 'Modifications and <s>guṇas</s> indeed' — the modifications to be described — from the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) down to the body and the senses — and the <s>guṇas</s> — which have transformed into the cognitions of pleasure, pain, and delusion — know these to be born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s> is the Lord's power that is the cause of modifications, the <s>Māyā</s> consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>. That is the source (<s>saṃbhava</s>) from which the modifications and the <s>guṇas</s> arise — know the modifications

children.text: ke punas te vikārāḥ guṇāś ca prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ ? ity āha --
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] What then are those modifications and <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>? He says —

children.text: kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> is said to be the cause in the production of the body and the senses;

children.text: puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate ||BhG_13.20||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain. // <s>BhG</s> 13.20 //

children.text: kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve - kāryaṃ śarīraṃ karaṇāni tat-sthāni trayodaśa | dehasyārambhakāṇi bhūtāni pañca viṣayāś ca prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ vikārāḥ pūrvoktā iha kārya-grahaṇena gṛhyante | guṇāś ca prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ sukha-duḥkha-mohātmakāḥ karaṇāśrayatvāt karaṇa-grahaṇena gṛhyante | teṣāṃ kārya-karaṇānāṃ kartṛtvam utpādakatvaṃ yat tat kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtvaṃ tasmin kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ kāraṇam ārambhakatvena prakṛtir ucyate | evaṃ kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtvena saṃsārasya kāraṇaṃ prakṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] 'In the production of the body and the senses' — the body is the effect (<s>kārya</s>); the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) are the thirteen [senses and faculties] situated in it. The five elements and the five sense-objects that constitute the body — these are the previously mentioned modifications born of <s>Prakṛti</s>, here denoted by the word 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>). And the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s> — of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion — since they depend on the senses, are denoted by the word 'instruments' (<s>karaṇa</s>). The production (<s>kartṛtva</s>) — i.e., the generative capacity — of those effects and instruments: in that production of body and senses, <s>Prakṛti</s> is said to be the cause, as the initiator.

children.text: kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve ity asminn api pāṭhe, kāryaṃ yat yasya pariṇāmas tat tasya kāryaṃ vikāro vikāri kāraṇaṃ tayor vikāra-vikāriṇoḥ kārya-kāraṇayoḥ kartṛtve iti | athavā, ṣoḍāśa vikārāḥ kāryaṃ sapta prakṛti-vikṛtayaḥ kāraṇam tāny eva kārya-kāraṇāny ucyante teṣāṃ kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate, ārambhakatvenaiva |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] In the alternative reading '<s>kāryakāraṇakartṛtve</s>' — the effect (<s>kārya</s>) is that which is the transformation of something; that something is the cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>); in the production of both the effect-thing and the cause-thing. Alternatively, the sixteen modifications are the effect; the seven <s>prakṛtivikṛtis</s> (products-cum-causes) are the cause; these themselves are called 'effect and cause'; in the production of these, <s>Prakṛti</s> is said to be the cause, precisely as the initiator.

children.text:
puruṣaś ca saṃsārasya kāraṇaṃ yathā syāt tad ucyate - puruṣo jīvaḥ kṣetrajño bhoktā iti paryāyaḥ, sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhogyānāṃ bhoktṛtve upalabdhṛtve hetur ucyate | kathaṃ punar anena kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtvena sukha-duḥkha-bhoktṛtvena ca prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ saṃsāra-kāraṇatvam ucyate ? ity atrocyate - kārya-karaṇa-sukha-duḥkha-rūpeṇa hetu-phalātmanā prakṛteḥ pariṇāmābhāve, puruṣasya ca cetanasyāsati tad-upalabdhṛtve, kutaḥ saṃsāraḥ syāt ? yadā punaḥ kārya-karaṇa-sukha-duḥkha-svarūpeṇa hetu-phalātmanā pariṇatayā prakṛtyā bhogyayā puruṣasya tad-viparītasya bhoktṛtvenāvidyā-rūpaḥ saṃyogaḥ syāt, tadā saṃsāraḥ syād iti | ato yat prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ kārya-karaṇa-kartṛtvena sukha-duḥkha-bhoktṛtvena ca saṃsāra-kāraṇatvam uktam, tad
yuktam | kaḥ punar ayaṃ saṃsāro nāma ? sukha-duḥkha-saṃbhogaḥ saṃsāraḥ | puruṣasya ca sukha-duḥkhānāṃ saṃbhoktṛtvaṃ saṃsāritvam iti ||BhGS_13.20||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And how <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> is stated: <s>Puruṣa</s> — the individual self (<s>jīva</s>), the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), the experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>) — these are synonyms. In the experience (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) — i.e., the apprehension — of pleasures and pains that are objects of experience, [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is said to be the cause. But how is the causality of <s>saṃsāra</s> predicated of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> through the production of body-and-senses and the experience of pleasure-and-pain? To this it is replied: if <s>Prakṛti</s> did not transform in the form of body-senses-pleasure-pain as cause and effect, and if <s>Puruṣa</s>, being conscious, did not apprehend that [transformation], how would <s>saṃsāra</s> exist? But when <s>Prakṛti</s>, having transformed in the form of body-senses-pleasure-pain as cause and effect, serves as the object of experience, and <s>Puruṣa</s>, being the opposite [i.e., non-material], becomes the experiencer — [when] there is a conjunction of the nature of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) [between them] — then <s>saṃsāra</s> would exist. Therefore, the statement that <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> through the production of body-and-senses and the experience of pleasure-and-pain is justified. But what is this <s>saṃsāra</s>? The experiencing of pleasures and pains is <s>saṃsāra</s>. And <s>Puruṣa's</s> being an experiencer of pleasures and pains is [its] being a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating entity). // <s>BhGS</s> 13.20 //

children.text: yat puruṣasya sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ saṃsāritvam ity uktaṃ tasya tat kiṃ-nimittam ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] It was stated that <s>Puruṣa's</s> being an experiencer of pleasures and pains constitutes its state of being a <s>saṃsārin</s>. What is the cause of that? It is stated —

children.text: puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijān guṇān |
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>, situated in <s>Prakṛti</s>, experiences the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>;

children.text: kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅgo 'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu ||BhG_13.21||
children.translated_text: attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs. // <s>BhG</s> 13.21 //

children.text:
puruṣo bhoktā prakṛti-sthaḥ | prakṛtāv avidyā-lakṣaṇāyāṃ kārya-karaṇa-rūpeṇa pariṇatāyāṃ sthitaḥ prakṛti-sthaḥ | prakṛtim ātmatvena gataḥ ity etat | hi yasmāt | tasmād bhuṅkte upalabhata ity arthaḥ | prakṛtijān prakṛtito jātān sukha-duḥkha-mohākārābhivyaktān guṇān sukhī, duḥkhī, mūḍhaḥ, paṇḍito 'ham ity evam | satyām apy avidyāyāṃ sukha-duḥkha-moheṣu guṇeṣu bhujyamāneṣu yaḥ saṅga ātma-bhāvaḥ saṃsārasya sa pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ yasya puruṣasya janmanaḥ | sa yathā-kāmo bhavati tat kratur bhavati [BAU 4.4.5] ity ādi śruteḥ | tad etad āha - kāraṇaṃ hetur guṇa-saṅgo guṇeṣu saṅgo 'sya puruṣasya bhoktuḥ sad-asad-yoni-janmasu | satyaś cāsatyaś ca yonayaḥ sad-asad-yonayas tāsu sad-asad-yonuṣu janmāni sad-asad-yoni-janmāni, teṣu sad-asad-yoni-janmaṣu
viṣaya-bhūteṣu kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅgaḥ | athavā, sad-asad-yoni-janmasu asya saṃsārasya kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅga iti saṃsāra-pada-madhyāhāryam | sad-yonayo devādi-yonayaḥ | asad-yonayaḥ paśvādi-yonayaḥ | sāmarthyāt sad-asad-yonayaḥ manuṣya-yonayo 'py aviruddhāḥ draṣṭāvyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] <s>Puruṣa</s>, the experiencer, is situated in <s>Prakṛti</s> — in <s>Prakṛti</s> characterized as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), which has transformed into the form of body and senses — 'situated in <s>Prakṛti</s>' means: having assumed <s>Prakṛti</s> as its own self — this is the meaning. Because — therefore, it experiences, i.e., apprehends, the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s> — born from <s>Prakṛti</s>, manifested in the forms of pleasure, pain, and delusion — [thinking] 'I am happy, I am miserable, I am deluded, I am learned' — thus. Even when ignorance exists, the attachment (<s>saṅga</s>) — the identification with the self — to the <s>guṇas</s> of pleasure, pain, and delusion that are being experienced — that is the primary cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, [the cause] of <s>Puruṣa's</s> birth. [As the <s>Śruti</s> states:] 'As is his desire, so is his will; as is his will, so he acts' [<s>BAU</s> 4.4.5]. This is what he says — the cause, the reason, is attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> — attachment in the <s>guṇas</s> — for this <s>Puruṣa</s>, the experiencer, in births in good and evil wombs. 'Good' (<s>sat</s>) and 'evil' (<s>asat</s>) wombs are <s>sadasadyonis</s>; births in those good and evil wombs are <s>sadasadyonijanmas</s>; in those births in good and evil wombs, which are the domain [of attachment], the cause is attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>. Alternatively, in births in good and evil wombs, of this <s>saṃsāra</s> — the word '<s>saṃsāra</s>' is to be supplied — the cause is attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>. Good wombs are those of gods and the like; evil wombs are those of animals and the like. By implication, human wombs, being both good and evil, are also not excluded.

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati - prakṛti-sthatvākhyāvidyā guṇeṣu ca saṅgaḥ kāmaḥ saṃsārasya kāraṇam iti | tac ca parivarjanāya ucyate | asya ca nivṛtti-kāraṇaṃ jñāna-vairāgye sa-saṃnyāse gītā-śāstre prasiddham | tac ca jñānaṃ purastād upanyastaṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-viṣayam yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute [Gītā 12.13] iti | uktaṃ cānyāpohenātad-dharmādhyāropeṇa ca ||BhGS_13.21||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] What has been stated is this: ignorance, termed 'being situated in <s>Prakṛti</s>,' and attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> — i.e., desire (<s>kāma</s>) — are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And this is stated for the purpose of abandoning [them]. And the cause of their cessation — knowledge and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) together with renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) — is well-established in the <s>Gītā</s> scripture. And that knowledge was previously presented as pertaining to the field and the knower of the field: 'knowing which, one attains immortality' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.12]. And it was stated through the negation of what is other [than the Self] and through the superimposition of non-Self properties. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.21 //

children.text: tasyaiva punaḥ sākṣān nirdeśaḥ kriyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] A direct designation of that very [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is now given —

children.text: upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The witness (<s>upadraṣṭā</s>), the sanctioner (<s>anumantā</s>), the sustainer (<s>bhartā</s>), the experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>), the great Lord (<s>maheśvara</s>),

children.text: paramātmeti cāpy ukto dehe 'smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ ||BhG_13.22||
children.translated_text: and also called the Supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) — this is the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> in this body. // <s>BhG</s> 13.22 //

children.text:
upadraṣṭā samīpa-sthaḥ san draṣṭā svayam avyāpṛtaḥ | yathā ṛtvig-yajamāneṣu yajña-karma-vyāpṛteṣu taṭastho 'nyo 'vyāpṛto yajña-vidyā-kuśalaḥ ṛtvig-yajamāna-vyāpāra-guṇa-doṣāṇām īkṣitā, tadvac ca kārya-karaṇa-vyāpāreṣu sa-vyāpārāṇāṃ sāmīpyena draṣṭā upadraṣṭā | athavā, deha-cakṣur-mano-buddhy-ātmāno draṣṭāraḥ | teṣāṃ bāhyo draṣṭā dehaḥ | tata ārabhyāntaratamaś ca pratyak samīpe ātmā draṣṭā, yataḥ paro 'ntaratamo nāsti draṣṭā | so 'tiśaya-sāmīpyena draṣṭṛtvād upadraṣṭā syāt | yajñopadraṣṭṛavad vā sarva-viṣayī-karaṇād upadraṣṭā | anumantā ca | anumodanam anumananaṃ kurvatsu tat-kriyāsu paritoṣas tat-kartānumantā ca | athavā, anumantā kārya-karaṇa-pravṛttiṣu svayam apravṛtto 'pi pravṛtta
iva tad-anukūlo vibhāvyate, tenānumantā | athavā, pravṛttān sva-vyāpāreṣu tat-sākṣi-bhūtaḥ kadācid api na nivārayatīty anumantā |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The witness (<s>upadraṣṭā</s>) — being in proximity, a seer, while itself remaining uninvolved. Just as in a sacrifice, while the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) and the patron (<s>yajamāna</s>) are engaged in the sacrificial acts, a bystander, another person who is uninvolved, versed in sacrificial lore, observes the merits and defects of the activities of the priests and patron — similarly, one who, through proximity to the activities of the body, senses, and their functions, is the seer, is the witness (<s>upadraṣṭā</s>). Alternatively, body, eye, mind, and intellect are [all] seers. Of these, the outermost seer is the body. Beginning from that, progressively more inward, the innermost is the Self as seer, beyond whom there is no more inward seer. That Self, being a seer through the utmost proximity, would be the witness. Or, like the overseer of a sacrifice, [the Self] is the witness because it cognizes all objects. The sanctioner (<s>anumantā</s>) as well — approval, acquiescence; when one performing those actions shows satisfaction, the one who does that is the sanctioner. Alternatively, though itself not active in the activities of body and senses, it appears as if active, as if conforming to them — therefore it is the sanctioner. Or, being the witness of those engaged in their respective activities, it never restrains [them] — therefore it is the sanctioner.

children.text:
bhartā| bharaṇaṃ nāma dehendriya-mano-buddhīnāṃ saṃhatānāṃ caitanyātma-pārārthyena nimitta-bhūtena caitanyābhāsānāṃ yat svarūpa-dhāraṇam, tac caitanyātma-kṛtam eveti bhartā ātmety ucyate | bhoktā | agny-uṣṇavan nitya-caitanya-svarūpeṇa buddheḥ sukha-duḥkha-mohātmakāḥ pratyayāḥ sarva-viṣaya-viṣayāś caitanyātma-grastā iva jāyamānā vibhaktā vibhāvyante iti bhoktā ātmocyate | maheśvaraḥ | sarvātmatvāt svatantratvāc ca mahān īśvaraś ceti maheśvaraḥ | paramātmā | dehādīnāṃ buddhy-antānāṃ pratyag-ātmatvena kalpitānām avidyayā parama upadraṣṭṛtvādi-lakṣaṇa ātmeti paramātmā | so 'ntaḥ paramātmā ity anena śabdena cāpy uktaḥ kathitaḥ śrutau | kvāsau ? asmin dehe puruṣaḥ paro 'vyaktāt | uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ
[Gītā 13.3] iti yo vakṣyamāṇaḥ kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi [Gītā 13.2] iti upanyasto vyākhyāyopasaṃhṛtaś ca ||BhGS_13.22||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The sustainer (<s>bhartā</s>) — sustaining means the maintenance of the proper form of the body, senses, mind, and intellect assembled together, through the conscious Self as its final purpose — [the body etc.,] being reflections of consciousness, their sustenance of form is accomplished by the conscious Self alone — therefore the Self is called the sustainer. The experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>) — just as fire [has] heat, through its nature as eternal consciousness, the cognitions of the intellect — of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, pertaining to all objects — arising as if consumed by the conscious Self, are experienced as distinct — therefore the Self is called the experiencer. The great Lord (<s>maheśvara</s>) — because it is the Self of all and because it is self-sufficient, it is great and the Lord — hence <s>Maheśvara</s>. The Supreme Self (<s>paramātman</s>) — of the body etc., down to the intellect, which are imagined through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) as inner selves progressively — the supreme, characterized by being a witness and the rest, is the Self — hence <s>Paramātman</s>. This inner <s>Paramātman</s> has been spoken of, declared, in <s>Śruti</s> by this very word. Where [does it dwell]? In this body — the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, higher than the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). 'But the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is other [than these], called the <s>Paramātman</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 15.17] — which will be stated; 'and know Me also as the knower of the field' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.2] — which was introduced, explained, and concluded. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.22 //

children.text: tam etaṃ yathokta-lakṣaṇam ātmānam -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] This Self, of the characteristics described —

children.text: ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha |
children.translated_text: He who thus knows <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> together with its <s>guṇas</s> —

children.text: sarvathā vartamāno 'pi na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate ||BhG_13.23||
children.translated_text: in whatever way he may be living, he is not born again. // <s>BhG</s> 13.23 //

children.text: ya evaṃ yathokta-prakāreṇa vetti puruṣaṃ sākṣād ātma-bhāvena "ayam aham asmi" iti prakṛtiṃ ca yathoktām avidyā-lakṣaṇāṃ guṇaiḥ sva-vikāraiḥ saha nivartitām abhāvam āpāditāṃ vidyayā, sarvathā sarva-prakāreṇa vartamāno 'pi sa bhūyaḥ punaḥ patite 'smin vidvac-charīre dehāntarāya nābhijāyate notpadyate, dehāntaraṃ na gṛhṇātīty arthaḥ | api-śabdāt kim u vaktavyaṃ ? sva-vṛtta-stho na jāyate ity abhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] He who knows thus — in the manner described — <s>Puruṣa</s>, directly, as his own Self — [knowing] 'this I am' — and <s>Prakṛti</s> as described, characterized as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), together with its <s>guṇas</s>, i.e., its own modifications — [knowing it to be] removed, brought to non-existence, through knowledge — in whatever way, in whatever condition he may be living — he is not born again. When this body endowed with knowledge falls, he does not take another body — this is the meaning. From the word 'even' (<s>api</s>), what more need be said? The purport is: one who abides in his proper conduct is certainly not born again. //

children.text:
nanu, yady api jñānotpatty-anantaraṃ punar-janmābhāva uktaḥ, tathāpi prāg jñānotpatteḥ kṛtānāṃ karmaṇām uttara-kāla-bhāvināṃ ca yāni cātikrāntāneka-janma-kṛtāni teṣāṃ ca phalam adattvā nāśo na yukta iti | syus trīṇi janmāni kṛta-vipraṇāśo hi na yukta iti, yathā phale pravṛttānām ārabdha-janmanāṃ karmaṇām | na ca karmaṇāṃ viśeṣo 'vagamyate | tasmāt tri-prakārāṇy api karmāṇi trīṇi janmāny ārabheran | saṃhatāni vā sarvāṇy ekaṃ janmārabheran | anyathā kṛta-vināśe sati sarvatrānāśvāsa-prasaṅgaḥ, śāstrānarthakyaṃ ca syāt | ity ataḥ idam ayuktam uktam na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate iti | na | kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi [MuṇḍU 2.2.8], brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati [MuṇḍU 3.2.9], tasya tāvad eva ciram [ChāU 6.14.2], iṣīkā-tūlavat sarvāṇi karmāṇi pradūyante [ChāU
5.24.3] ity ādi-śruti-śatebhya ukto viduṣaḥ sarva-karma-dāhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, even though it has been stated that after the arising of knowledge there is no rebirth, still, it is not reasonable that the <s>karmas</s> (actions) performed before the arising of knowledge, those to be performed in the future, and those performed in countless past lives should be destroyed without yielding their fruit. There would be three lifetimes [of karma], for the destruction of what has been done is not reasonable — just as with <s>karmas</s> that have begun to bear fruit and have initiated the present birth. And no distinction among <s>karmas</s> is discernible. Therefore, all three types of <s>karmas</s> should initiate three births; or, combined together, all of them should initiate one birth. Otherwise, if what has been done is destroyed, there would be the absurd consequence of unreliability everywhere, and scripture would become purposeless. Hence, it is improper to say "he is not born again." No — [this objection is invalid]. From hundreds of <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) passages such as "And his <s>karmas</s> are destroyed" [<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.2.8], "One who knows <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself" [<s>Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.2.9], "For him the delay is only so long" [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.14.2], "All <s>karmas</s> are burnt up like a tuft of <s>iṣīkā</s> (reed) cotton" [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 5.24.3], the burning of all <s>karmas</s> of the knower has been declared.

children.text: ihāpi cokto yathaidhāṃsi [Gītā 4.37] ity ādinā sarva-karma-dāhaḥ | vakṣyati copapatteś ca | avidyā-kāma-kleśa-bīja-nimittāni hi karmāṇi janmāntarāṅkuram ārabhante | ihāpi ca sāhaṃkārābhisaṃdhīni karmāṇi phalārambhakāṇi, netarāṇīti tatra tatra bhagavatoktam |
children.translated_text: Here too, the burning of all <s>karmas</s> has been stated with "Just as firewood..." [<s>Gītā</s> 4.37] and so forth. And it will be stated further, since it is logically established. For <s>karmas</s> whose seed-cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) initiate the sprout of future births. And here too, the Blessed Lord has stated in various places that only <s>karmas</s> performed with the sense of ego and self-interested intention produce results, not others.

children.text:
bījāny agny-upadagdhāni na rohanti yathā punaḥ |
jñāna-dagdhais tathā kleśair nātmā saṃpadyate punaḥ [Mbh 3.200.10] iti ca |
