astu tāvaj jñānotpatty-uttara-kāla-kṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ jñānena dāhaḥ, jñāna-saha-bhāvitvāt | na tv iha janmani jñānotpatteḥ prāk kṛtānāṃ karmaṇām atīta-janma-kṛtānāṃ ca dāho yuktaḥ | na | sarva-karmāṇīti viśeṣaṇāt | jñānottara-kāla-bhāvinām eva sarva-karmaṇām iti cet, na | saṃkoce kāraṇānupapatteḥ | yat tūktam yathā vartamāna-janmārambhakāṇi karmāṇi na kṣīyante phala-dānāya pravṛttāny eva saty api jñāne, tathānārabdha-phalānām api karmaṇāṃ kṣayo na yukta iti, tad asat | katham ? teṣāṃ mukteṣuvat pravṛtta-phalatvāt | yathā pūrvaṃ lakṣya-vedhāya mukta iṣuḥ dhanuṣo lakṣya-vedhottara-kālam api ārabdha-vega-kṣayāt patanenaiva nivartate, evaṃ śarīrārambhakaṃ karma śarīra-sthiti-prayojane nivṛtte 'pi, ā saṃskāra-vega-kṣayāt pūrvavat vartata
eva | yathā sa eva iṣuḥ pravṛtti-nimittānārabdha-vegas tv amukto dhanuṣi prayukto 'pi upasaṃhriyate, tathānārabdha-phalāni karmāṇi svāśraya-sthāny eva jñānena nirbījī-kriyanta iti | patite 'smin vidvac-charīre na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate iti yuktam evoktam iti siddham ||BhGS_13.23||
children.translated_text: "Just as seeds scorched by fire do not sprout again, so too by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) burnt by knowledge, the Self is not reborn" [<s>Mahābhārata</s> 3.200.10]. Let it be granted that the burning by knowledge of <s>karmas</s> performed after the arising of knowledge is [reasonable], since they coexist with knowledge. But the burning of <s>karmas</s> performed in this life before the arising of knowledge, and those performed in past lives, is not reasonable. No — because of the qualifier "all <s>karmas</s>." If [you say] it refers only to all <s>karmas</s> that will occur after the time of knowledge — no, because there is no valid reason for such restriction. As for the objection that just as <s>karmas</s> that have initiated the present birth are not destroyed, being already engaged in yielding their fruit even when knowledge exists, similarly the destruction of <s>karmas</s> whose fruits have not yet begun is also not reasonable — that is wrong. How so? Because those [present-birth karmas] have their fruit already set in motion, like an arrow that has been released. Just as an arrow previously released to pierce a target, even after the target is pierced, comes to rest only through falling when the momentum of its initial force is exhausted, so too the <s>karma</s> that initiated the body continues as before until the momentum of its impressions is exhausted, even though its purpose of sustaining the body has ceased. Just as that very arrow, whose momentum has not yet begun — though fitted to the bow — can be withdrawn, so too <s>karmas</s> whose fruits have not yet begun, remaining in their substrate, are rendered seedless by knowledge. Therefore, it is rightly stated that when this body of the wise one falls, "he is not born again" — this is established. // BhGS 13.23 //
[Section break]

children.text: atrātma-darśane upāya-vikalpā ime dhyānādaya ucyante -
children.translated_text: Here, these alternatives of means for Self-realization — <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the rest — are stated:

children.text: dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: Some perceive the Self in the self by the self through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);

children.text: anye sāṃkhyena yogena karma-yogena cāpare ||BhG_13.24||
children.translated_text: others through <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), and yet others through <s>Karma-yoga</s> (the yoga of action). // BhG 13.24 //

children.text:
dhyānena | dhyānaṃ nāma śabdādibhyo viṣayebhyaḥ śrotrādīni karaṇāni manasy upasaṃhṛtya, manaś ca pratyak-cetanayitari, ekāgratayā yac cintanaṃ tad dhyānam | tathā, dhyāyatīva bakaḥ, dhyāyatīva pṛthivī, dhyāyantīva parvatāḥ [ChāU 7.6.1] iti upamopādānāt | taila-dhārāvat saṃtato 'vicchinna-pratyayo dhyānam | tena dhyānena ātmani buddhau paśyanty ātmānaṃ pratyak-cetanam ātmanā svenaiva pratyak-cetanena dhyāna-saṃskṛtenāntaḥ-karaṇena kecid yoginaḥ | anye sāṃkhyena yogena | sāṃkhyaṃ nāma ime sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi guṇā mayā dṛśyā ahaṃ tebhyo 'nyas tad-vyāpāra-sākṣi-bhūto nityo guṇa-vilakṣaṇa ātmeti cintanam eṣa sāṃkhyo yogaḥ | tena paśyanti ātmānam ātmanety anuvartate | karma-yogena | karmaiva yogaḥ | īśvarārpaṇa-buddhyānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ ghaṭana-rūpaṃ
yogārthatvād yoga ucyate guṇataḥ | tena sattva-śuddhi-jñānotpatti-dvāreṇa cāpare ||BhGS_13.24||
children.translated_text: "By <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation)" — <s>dhyāna</s> is that contemplation in which one withdraws the sense organs such as hearing from their objects such as sound into the mind, and the mind into the innermost consciousness, with one-pointed concentration. Thus, since similes are employed — "the crane meditates as it were, the earth meditates as it were, the mountains meditate as it were" [<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 7.6.1]. <s>Dhyāna</s> is an unbroken, continuous flow of thought, like a stream of oil. By that <s>dhyāna</s>, some <s>yogins</s> perceive the Self — the innermost consciousness — in the self, that is, in the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), by the self, that is, by one's own innermost consciousness through the inner instrument purified by meditation. "Others through <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>" — <s>Sāṃkhya</s> means the contemplation: "These <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — are perceived by me; I am different from them; I am the witness of their operations, eternal, distinct in nature from the <s>guṇas</s> — this is the Self." This is <s>Sāṃkhya-yoga</s>. By that, they perceive the Self — "by the self" is supplied from the previous clause. "By <s>Karma-yoga</s>" — action itself is the yoga. Action performed with the attitude of offering to the Lord, being of the nature of a means [to union], is called <s>yoga</s> by virtue of its quality. Through that, by the gateway of purification of <s>sattva</s> and the arising of knowledge, yet others [realize the Self]. // BhGS 13.24 //
[Section break]

children.text: anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate |
children.translated_text: But others, not knowing thus, worship having heard from others;

children.text: te 'pi cātitaranty eva mṛtyuṃ śruti-parāyaṇāḥ ||BhG_13.25||
children.translated_text: they too certainly cross beyond death, being devoted to what they have heard. // BhG 13.25 //

children.text: anye tv eṣu vikalpeṣu anyatamenāpy evaṃ yathoktam ātmānam ajānanto 'nyebhyaḥ ācāryebhyaḥ śrutvā "idam eva cintayata" ity uktā upāsate śraddadhānāḥ santaś cintayanti | te 'pi cātitaranty eva atikrāmanty eva mṛtyum mṛtyu-yuktaṃ saṃsāram ity etat | śruti-parāyaṇāḥ śrutiḥ śravaṇaṃ param ayanaṃ gamanaṃ mokṣa-mārga-pravṛttau paraṃ sādhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te śruti-parāyaṇāḥ | kevala-paropadeśa-pramāṇāḥ svayaṃ viveka-rahitā ity abhiprāyaḥ | kim u vaktavyam pramāṇaṃ prati svatantrā vivekino mṛtyum atitarantīty abhiprāyaḥ ||BhGS_13.25||
children.translated_text: But others, not knowing the Self as described above through any one of these alternatives, having heard from others — from teachers — "Contemplate this alone," being instructed thus, they worship — being faithful, they contemplate. They too certainly cross beyond, that is, certainly transcend death — meaning <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) which is characterized by death. "<s>Śruti-parāyaṇāḥ</s>" — <s>śruti</s> means hearing; <s>paraṃ ayanam</s> means the highest path or means; those for whom hearing is the supreme means of proceeding on the path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) are <s>śruti-parāyaṇāḥ</s> (those devoted to hearing). The purport is: they rely solely on the instruction of others as their authority, being themselves devoid of discrimination. How much more, then, need it be said that those who are independent with regard to the means of knowledge — the discriminating ones — transcend death? This is the implied meaning. // BhGS 13.25 //
[Section break]

children.text: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi [Gītā 13.3] iti kṣetrajñeśvarakatva-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ mokṣa-sādhanaṃ, yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute [Gītā 13.13] ity uktam | tat kasmāt hetoḥ ? iti tad-dhetu-pradarśanārthaṃ śloka ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: The knowledge pertaining to the identity of <s>Kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field) with <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) — stated as "Know Me also as the <s>Kṣetrajña</s> in all <s>kṣetras</s>" [<s>Gītā</s> 13.3] — is the means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), as declared in "knowing which, one attains immortality" [<s>Gītā</s> 13.13]. For what reason is this so? To demonstrate that reason, the [next] verse is begun:

children.text: yāvat saṃjāyate kiṃcit sattvaṃ sthāvara-jaṅgamam |
children.translated_text: Whatever being is born, whether stationary or moving,

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha ||BhG_13.26||
children.translated_text: know that to be from the conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> (the field) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>. // BhG 13.26 //

children.text: yāvat yat kiṃcit saṃjāyate samutpadyate sattvaṃ vastu | kim aviśeṣeṇa ? nety āha - sthāvara-jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogāt taj jāyate ity evaṃ viddhi jānīhi bharatarṣabha |
children.translated_text: "Whatever" — whatever being, any entity whatsoever, is born, comes into existence. Is this without distinction? No, he specifies — "stationary and moving" — that which is stationary and that which is moving — it is born from the conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> (the field) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field) — know this thus, understand it, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.

children.text:
kaḥ punar ayaṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ saṃyogo 'bhipretaḥ ? na tāvat rajjveva ghaṭasyāvayava-saṃśleṣa-dvārakaḥ saṃbandha-viśeṣaḥ saṃyogaḥ kṣetreṇa kṣetrajñasya saṃbhavati, ākāśavat niravayavatvāt | nāpi samavāya-lakṣaṇas tantu-paṭayor iva kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor itaretara-kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvānabhyupagamāt | ity ucyate - kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor viṣaya-viṣayiṇor bhinna-svabhāvayor itaretara-tad-dharmādhyāsa-lakṣaṇaḥ saṃyogaḥ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-svarūpa-vivekā-bhāva-nibandhanaḥ, rajju-śuktikādīnāṃ tad-viveka-jñānābhāvād adhyāropita-sarpa-rajatādi-saṃyogavat | so 'yam adhyāsa-svarūpaḥ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogo mithyā-jñāna-lakṣaṇaḥ | yathā-śāstraṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-lakṣaṇa-bheda-parijñāna-pūrvakaṃ prāk darśita-rūpāt kṣetrān muñjād iveṣīkāṃ
yathokta-lakṣaṇaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ pravibhajya na sat tan nāsad ucyate [Gītā 13.13] ity anena nirasta-sarvopādhi-viśeṣaṃ jñeyaṃ brahma-svarūpeṇa yaḥ paśyati, kṣetraṃ ca māyā-nirmita-hasti-svapna-dṛṣṭa-vastuvad gandharva-nagarādivad asad eva sad ivāvabhāsate | ity evaṃ niścita-vijñāno yaḥ, tasya yathokta-samyag-darśana-virodhād apagacchati mithyā-jñānam | tasya janma-hetor apagamād ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha [Gītā 13.25] ity anena vidvān bhūyo nābhijāyate iti yad uktam, tad upapannam uktam ||BhGS_13.26||
children.translated_text: Now what exactly is this conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> that is intended? It is not a conjunction in the form of a particular relation through contact of parts, like a rope with a pot, that is possible between <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, because [<s>kṣetrajña</s>] is without parts, like space. Nor is it of the nature of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), as between threads and cloth, because the mutual cause-effect relationship between <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> is not accepted. Therefore it is said: the conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, which are of different natures as object and subject, is characterized by the mutual superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) of the properties of each upon the other, and is rooted in the absence of discrimination between the true natures of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> — like the conjunction of a snake or silver superimposed upon a rope or oyster shell due to the absence of discriminative knowledge regarding them. This conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, whose nature is superimposition, has the character of false knowledge (<s>mithyā-jñāna</s>). One who, having first ascertained the distinction between the characteristics of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> as taught in scripture, separates the <s>kṣetrajña</s> of the aforementioned nature from <s>kṣetra</s> — as one draws the reed from the <s>muñja</s> grass — and sees the knowable as having the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, with all limiting adjuncts negated, as stated in "It is called neither existent nor non-existent" [<s>Gītā</s> 13.13]; and [sees] <s>kṣetra</s> as non-existent yet appearing as if existent, like a magically created elephant, an object seen in a dream, or a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s> — for one who has such firm conviction, the false knowledge departs, being opposed to right vision as described. Since the cause of birth departs, what was stated — "One who knows <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self) and <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) together with the <s>guṇas</s>" [<s>Gītā</s> 13.25] — "the wise one is not born again" — is rightly and properly stated. // BhGS 13.26 //
[Section break]

children.text: na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate [Gītā 13.24] iti samyag darśana-phalam avidyādi-saṃsāra-bīja-nivṛtti-dvāreṇa janmābhāva uktaḥ | janma-kāraṇaṃ cāvidyā-nimittakaḥ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyoga uktaḥ | atas tasyāḥ avidyāyā nivartakaṃ samyag-darśanam uktam api punaḥ śabdāntareṇocyate -
children.translated_text: "He is not born again" [<s>Gītā</s> 13.24] — the fruit of right vision has been stated as the absence of rebirth through the cessation of the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And the conjunction of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, caused by <s>avidyā</s>, has been stated as the cause of birth. Therefore, right vision, which is the remover of that <s>avidyā</s>, though already stated, is stated again with different words:

children.text: samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram |
children.translated_text: The supreme Lord, abiding equally in all beings,

children.text: vinaśyatsv avinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||BhG_13.27||
children.translated_text: the imperishable within the perishable — he who sees this, truly sees. // BhG 13.27 //

children.text:
samaṃ nirviśeṣaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ sthitiṃ kurvantam | kva ? sarveṣu samasteṣu bhūteṣu brahmādi-sthāvarānteṣu prāṇiṣu | kam ? parameśvaraṃ dehendriya-mano-buddhy-avyaktātmano 'pekṣya parameśvaraḥ, taṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu samaṃ tiṣṭhantam | tāni viśinaṣṭi vinaśyatsv iti | taṃ ca parameśvaram avinaśyantam iti, bhūtānāṃ parameśvarasya cātyanta-vailakṣaṇya-pradarśanārtham | katham ? sarveṣāṃ hi bhāva-vikārāṇāṃ jani-lakṣaṇo bhāva-vikāro mūlam | janmottara-kāla-bhāvino 'nye sarve bhāva-vikārā vināśāntāḥ | vināśāt paro na kaścid asti bhāva-vikāraḥ, bhāvābhāvāt | sati hi dharmiṇi dharmā bhavanti | ato 'ntya-bhāva-vikārābhāvānuvādena pūrva-bhāvinaḥ sarve bhāva-vikārāḥ pratiṣiddhā bhavanti saha kāryaiḥ | tasmāt sarva-bhūtaiḥ vailakṣaṇyam atyantam
eva parameśvarasya siddham, nirviśeṣatvam ekatvaṃ ca | ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ parameśvaraṃ paśyati, sa paśyati |
children.translated_text: "Equally" — abiding without distinction, dwelling. Where? In all, in the totality of beings, in living creatures from <s>Brahmā</s> down to stationary things. Whom? The supreme Lord — He is the supreme Lord in relation to the body, senses, mind, intellect, and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) — Him, abiding equally in all beings. He distinguishes those [beings] with "in the perishable." And that supreme Lord is "imperishable" — this is to show the utter dissimilarity between beings and the supreme Lord. How so? For among all modifications of existence, the modification characterized by birth is the root. All other modifications of existence that occur after birth end in destruction. There is no modification of existence beyond destruction, because existence itself ceases. For properties exist only when a substance exists. Therefore, by stating the absence of the final modification of existence [i.e., destruction], all prior modifications of existence along with their effects are negated. Thus, the utter dissimilarity of the supreme Lord from all beings is established, as well as His being without distinction and His oneness. He who sees the supreme Lord as thus described — he truly sees.

children.text: nanu sarvo 'pi lokaḥ paśyati, kiṃ viśeṣaṇeneti | satyaṃ paśyati | kiṃ tu viparītaṃ paśyati | ato viśinaṣṭi - sa eva paśyatīti | yathā timira-dṛṣṭir anekaṃ candraṃ paśyati, tam apekṣya eka-candra-darśī viśiṣyate - sa eva paśyatīti | tathaivehāpy ekam avibhaktaṃ yathoktaṃ ātmānaṃ yaḥ paśyati, sa vibhaktān ekātma-viparīta-darśibhyo viśiṣyate - sa eva paśyatīti | itare paśyanto 'pi na paśyanti | viparīta-darśitvāt aneka-candra-darśivad ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.27||
children.translated_text: But does not everyone in the world see? What is the point of the qualifier? True, [everyone] sees. But they see wrongly. Therefore he distinguishes — "he alone truly sees." Just as one with a vision defect sees many moons, and in contrast to him, the one who sees a single moon is distinguished — "he alone truly sees" — so too here, one who sees the one, undivided Self as described is distinguished from those who see it as divided and who hold the opposite view of a single Self — "he alone truly sees." The others, though seeing, do not [truly] see, because their vision is distorted, like the one who sees many moons — this is the meaning. // BhGS 13.27 //
[Section break]

children.text: yathoktasya samyag-darśanasya phala-vacanena stutiḥ kartavyā iti śloka ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: A verse is begun to praise [right vision] by stating the fruit of the right vision as described:

children.text: samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram |
children.translated_text: For one who sees equally the Lord established everywhere,

children.text: na hinasty ātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||BhG_13.28||
children.translated_text: does not injure the Self by the self, and thereby attains the supreme goal. // BhG 13.28 //

children.text: samaṃ paśyann upalabhamāno hi yasmāt sarvatra sarva-bhūteṣu samavasthitaṃ tulyatayāvasthitam īśvaram atītānantara-ślokokta-lakṣaṇam ity arthaḥ | samaṃ paśyan kim ? na hinasti hiṃsāṃ na karoti ātmanā svenaiva svam ātmānam | tat-tad-ahiṃsanād yāti parāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatiṃ mokṣākhyām ||
children.translated_text: "Seeing equally" — perceiving, since [he perceives] in all, in all beings, the Lord established equally, that is, abiding in an identical manner — the Lord whose characteristics were described in the immediately preceding verse, this is the meaning. Seeing equally, what [follows]? He does not injure — does not cause harm — to the Self, to his own Self, by the self, by himself. Because of such non-injury [to the Self], he attains the supreme, the most exalted destination called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // BhGS 13.28 //

children.text: nanu naiva kaścit prāṇī svayaṃ svam ātmānaṃ hinasti | katham ucyate 'prāptam na hinastīti ? yathā na pṛthivyām nāntarikṣe na divy agniś cetavyaḥ [TaittS 5.2.7.1] ity ādi | naiṣa doṣaḥ, ajñānām ātma-tiraskaraṇopapatteḥ | sarvo hy ajño 'tyanta-prasiddhaṃ sākṣād aparokṣād ātmānaṃ tiraskṛtyānātmānam ātmatvena parigṛhya, tam api dharmādharmau kṛtvopāttam ātmānaṃ hatvānyam ātmānam upādatte navaṃ, taṃ caivaṃ hatvānyam | evaṃ tam api hatvānyam ity evam upāttam upāttam ātmānaṃ hantīty ātmahā sarvo 'jñaḥ | yas tu paramārthātmāsāv api sarvadāvidyayā hata iva vidyamāna-phalābhāvād iti sarve ātma-hana evāvidvāṃsaḥ | yas tv itaro yathoktātma-darśī, sa ubhayathāpi ātmanātmānaṃ na hinasti na hanti | tato yāti parāṃ gatim yathoktaṃ phalaṃ tasya bhavatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: No living being ever harms its own Self. How then can it be said '[the one who has] attained does not harm'? [This is] like 'fire is not to be sought on the earth, nor in the atmosphere, nor in heaven' [<s>TaittS</s> 5.2.7.1] etc. [Answer:] This is not a defect, because for the ignorant, the concealment of the Self is possible. For every ignorant person, having concealed the Self — which is supremely well-known, directly and immediately present — and having grasped the non-Self as the Self, performs <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [through that non-Self], and then having slain the adopted [non-]Self, takes on another new self; and having slain that one too, [takes on] another; and having slain that one too, [takes on yet] another — thus one slays each successively adopted [non-]Self, and hence every ignorant person is a 'self-slayer.' And as for the Self in the ultimate sense — that too, through <s>avidyā</s>, is always as if slain, since the fruit [of Self-knowledge] that should exist is absent. Thus, all the ignorant are indeed self-slayers. But the other one, who sees the Self as described, in both ways does not harm, does not slay, the Self by the Self. Therefore 'goes to the supreme destination' — the result as described accrues to that one — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.28 //

children.text: sarva-bhūta-stham īśvaraṃ samaṃ paśyan na hinasty ātmanātmānam [Gītā 13.28] ity uktam | tad anupapannaṃ sva-guṇa-karma-vailakṣaṇya-bheda-bhinneṣv ātmasu, ity etad āśaṅkyāha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] It was stated: 'Seeing the Lord equally dwelling in all beings, one does not harm the Self by the Self' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.28]. This is impossible if the selves are differentiated by the distinctions of their own qualities and actions — anticipating this [objection], He says:

children.text: prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: And one who sees that all actions are performed by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) alone in every way,

children.text: yaḥ paśyati tathātmānam akartāraṃ sa paśyati ||BhG_13.29||
children.translated_text: and sees likewise that the Self is the non-agent — that one [truly] sees. // <s>BhG</s> 13.29 //

children.text: prakṛtyā prakṛtir bhagavato māyā triguṇātmikā | māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyād [ŚvetU 4.10] iti mantra-varṇāt | tayā prakṛtyaiva ca nānyena mahad-ādi-kārya-kāraṇākāra-pariṇatayā karmāṇi vāṅ-manaḥ-kāyārabhyāṇi kriyamāṇāni nirvartyamānāni sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakārair yaḥ paśyaty upalabhate, tathātmānaṃ kṣetrajñam akartāraṃ sarvopādhi-vivarjitaṃ sa paśyati, sa paramārtha-darśīty abhiprāyaḥ | nirguṇasyākartur nirviśeṣasyākāśasyeva bhede pramāṇānupapattir ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.29||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'By <s>Prakṛti</s>' — <s>Prakṛti</s> is the <s>māyā</s> of the Blessed Lord, consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>. From the <s>mantra</s>-text: 'Know <s>māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s>' [<s>ŚvetU</s> 4.10]. By that <s>Prakṛti</s> alone and by nothing else — which has transformed into the forms of effects and causes beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) — all actions, whether initiated by speech, mind, or body, are being performed, i.e., accomplished, in every way, i.e., in all manners. One who sees this, who perceives [this], and likewise sees the Self — the <s>kṣetrajña</s> — as the non-agent, free from all limiting adjuncts — that one [truly] sees; the purport is: that one is a seer of ultimate reality. The meaning is: for the Self, which is without qualities, without agency, without distinctions — like space — there is no possibility of a means of valid knowledge [establishing] differentiation. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.29 //

children.text: punar api tad eva samyag darśanaṃ śabdāntareṇa prapañcayati -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Once again, that very right vision is elaborated in different words:

children.text: yadā bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvam ekastham anupaśyati |
children.translated_text: When one perceives the diverse states of beings as resting in the One,

children.text: tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||BhG_13.30||
children.translated_text: and their expansion as from that [One] alone — then one attains <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 13.30 //

children.text: yadā yasmin kāle bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvaṃ bhūtānāṃ pṛthag-bhāvaṃ pṛthaktvam ekasminn ātmani sthitaṃ eka-stham anupaśyati śāstrācāryopadeśam anu ātmānaṃ pratyakṣatvena paśyaty ātmaivedaṃ sarvam [ChāU 7.25.2] iti | tata eva ca tasmād eva ca vistāraṃ utpattiṃ vikāsam ātmataḥ prāṇa ātmata āśā ātmataḥ smara ātmata ākāśa ātmatas teja ātmata āpa ātmata āvirbhāva-tirobhāvāv ātmato 'nnam [ChāU 7.26.1] ity evam ādi-prakārair vistāraṃ yadā paśyati brahma saṃpadyate bhavati tadā tasmin kāla ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.30||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'When' — at whichever time — one perceives the diverse states of beings, the multiplicity of beings, as resting in the one Self, as established in the one — [that is,] following the instruction of scripture and teacher, one sees the Self directly: 'This Self alone is all this' [<s>ChāU</s> 7.25.2]. 'And their expansion from that alone' — their origination, their unfolding from the Self alone — 'From the Self [comes] <s>prāṇa</s>, from the Self hope, from the Self memory, from the Self space, from the Self light, from the Self water, from the Self appearance and disappearance, from the Self food' [<s>ChāU</s> 7.26.1] — in such various ways, when one sees the expansion, one attains <s>Brahman</s>, becomes [<s>Brahman</s>] — at that time — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.30 //

children.text: ekasyātmānaḥ sarva-dehātmatve tad-doṣa-saṃbandhe prāpte, idam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] If the one Self is the Self of all bodies, the consequence of being connected with the faults of those [bodies] would arise; therefore this is said:

children.text: anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Because of being beginningless and without qualities, this Supreme Self is imperishable;

children.text: śarīra-stho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate ||BhG_13.31||
children.translated_text: though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, It neither acts nor is tainted. // <s>BhG</s> 13.31 //

children.text: anāditvāt | anāder bhāvo 'nāditvam, ādiḥ kāraṇam, tad yasya nāsti tad anādi | yad dhy ādimat tat svenātmanā vyeti | ayaṃ tv anāditvān niravayava iti kṛtvā na vyeti | tathā nirguṇatvāt | saguṇo hi guṇa-vyayāt vyeti | ayaṃ tu nirguṇatvāc ca na vyeti | iti paramātmāyam avyayaḥ | nāsya vyayo vidyata ity avyayaḥ | yata evam ataḥ śarīra-stho 'pi, śarīreṣu ātmana upalabdhir bhavatīti śarīra-stha ucyate | tathāpi na karoti | tad-akaraṇād eva tat-phalena na lipyate | yo hi kartā, sa karma-phalena lipyate | ayaṃ tv akartā, ato na phalena lipyate ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Because of being beginningless' — the state of being beginningless (<s>anāditva</s>); 'beginning' means cause; that which has no cause is beginningless. For what has a beginning perishes through its own nature. But this [Self], being beginningless, and therefore without parts, does not perish. Likewise, 'because of being without qualities' — for what possesses qualities perishes through the loss of qualities. But this [Self], being without qualities, does not perish. Therefore this Supreme Self is imperishable — It has no decay. Because this is so, though dwelling in the body — since the Self is perceived in bodies, It is said to dwell in the body — even so, It does not act. And precisely because of not acting, It is not tainted by the fruit [of action]. For one who is an agent is tainted by the fruit of action. But this [Self] is a non-agent; therefore It is not tainted by fruit — this is the meaning.

children.text: kaḥ punar deheṣu karoti lipyate ca ? yadi tāvat anyaḥ paramātmano dehī karoti lipyate ca, tataḥ idam anupapannam uktaṃ kṣetrajñeśvaraikatvam kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi [Gītā 13.2] ity ādi | atha nāsti īśvarād anyo dehī | kaḥ karoti lipyate ca ? iti vācyam | paro vā nāstīti sarvathā durvijñeyaṃ durvācyaṃ ceti bhagavat-proktam aupaniṣadaṃ darśanaṃ parityaktaṃ vaiśeṣikaiḥ sāṃkhyārhata-bauddhaiś ca | tatrāyaṃ parihāro bhagavatā svenaiva uktaḥ svabhāvas tu pravartate [Gītā 5.14] iti | avidyā-mātra-svabhāvo hi karoti lipyate iti vyavahāro bhavati, na tu paramārthata ekasmin paramātmani tad asti | ata evaitasmin paramārtha-sāṃkhya-darśane sthitānāṃ jñāna-niṣṭhānāṃ paramahaṃsa-parivrājakānāṃ tiraskṛtāvidyā-vyavahārāṇāṃ karmādhikāro nāstīti tatra tatra darśitaṃ bhagavatā ||BhGS_13.31||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But who, then, acts in bodies and is tainted? If there is an embodied being other than the Supreme Self who acts and is tainted, then this statement of the identity of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> and the Lord — 'Know the <s>kṣetrajña</s> to be Me also' [<s>Gītā</s> 13.2] etc. — would be untenable. But if there is no embodied being other than the Lord — who acts and is tainted? — this must be stated. Or else, 'there is nothing beyond' — in every way, the teaching of the Blessed Lord, which is the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> vision, is difficult to understand and difficult to express, [though] it has been abandoned by the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Jainas</s>, and <s>Buddhists</s>. The resolution here has been stated by the Blessed Lord Himself: 'Nature itself impels [one to act]' [<s>Gītā</s> 5.14]. For the transactional dealings 'acts' and 'is tainted' arise from a nature that is nothing but <s>avidyā</s>, but do not ultimately exist in the one Supreme Self. For this very reason, the Blessed Lord has shown in various places that there is no qualification for action for those established in this ultimate <s>Sāṃkhya</s> vision, the knowers (<s>jñāna-niṣṭhas</s>), the supreme renunciants (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakas</s>), who have transcended the transactional dealings of <s>avidyā</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.31 //

children.text: kim iva na karoti na lipyate ity atra dṛṣṭāntam āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Like what does It neither act nor become tainted? He gives an illustration:

children.text: yathā sarva-gataṃ saukṣmyād ākāśaṃ nopalipyate |
children.translated_text: Just as the all-pervading space, due to its subtlety, is not tainted,

children.text: sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate ||BhG_13.32||
children.translated_text: so the Self, though situated everywhere in the body, is not tainted. // <s>BhG</s> 13.32 //

children.text: yathā sarva-gataṃ vyāpy api sat saukṣmyāt sūkṣma-bhāvād ākāśaṃ khaṃ nopalipyate na saṃbadhyate, sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate ||BhGS_13.32||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Just as the all-pervading space (<s>ākāśa</s>), though pervasive, due to its subtlety — its subtle nature — is not tainted, is not contaminated; so the Self, though situated everywhere in the body, is not tainted. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.32 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Moreover —

children.text: yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokam imaṃ raviḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the one sun illuminates this entire world,

children.text: kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata ||BhG_13.34||
children.translated_text: so the owner of the field (<s>kṣetrin</s>) illuminates the entire field, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 13.34 //

children.text: yathā prakāśayaty avabhāsayati ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokam imaṃ raviḥ savitā ādityaḥ, tathā tadvat mahā-bhūtādi-dhṛty-antaṃ kṣetram ekaḥ san prakāśayati | kaḥ ? kṣetrī paramātmā ity arthaḥ | ravi-dṛṣṭanto 'tra ātmana ubhayārtho 'pi bhavati | ravivat sarva-kṣetreṣv eka evātmā, alepakaś ceti ||BhGS_13.34||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Just as the one sun, the solar orb, illuminates this entire world, so likewise — the field, from the great elements down to steadfastness — the one [Self], being single, illuminates. Who? The owner of the field — the Supreme Self — this is the meaning. The sun-illustration here serves a dual purpose for the Self: like the sun, the Self is one in all fields, and [like the sun] is also untainted. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.34 //

children.text: samastādhyāyārthopasaṃhārārtho 'yaṃ ślokaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This verse is for summarizing the meaning of the entire chapter:

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor evam antaraṃ jñāna-cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: Those who, with the eye of knowledge, thus know the distinction between the field and the knower of the field,

children.text: bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣaṃ ca ye vidur yānti te param ||BhG_13.35||
children.translated_text: and the liberation of beings from <s>Prakṛti</s> — they go to the Supreme. // <s>BhG</s> 13.35 //

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajñayor yathā-vyākhyātayor evaṃ yathā-pradarśita-prakāreṇāntaram itaretara-vailakṣaṇya-viśeṣaṃ jñāna-cakṣuṣā śāstrācārya-prasādopadeśa-janitam ātma-pratyayikaṃ jñānaṃ cakṣuḥ, tena jñāna-cakṣuṣā, bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣaṃ ca, bhūtānāṃ prakṛtir avidyā-lakṣaṇāvyaktākhyā, tasyā bhūta-prakṛter mokṣaṇam abhāva-gamanaṃ ca ye vidur vijānanti, yānti gacchanti te paraṃ paramātma-tattvaṃ brahma, na punar dehaṃ ādadate ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_13.35||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Between the field and the knower of the field as explained — 'thus,' in the manner as demonstrated — the distinction, the mutual differentiation and specificity — [known] with the eye of knowledge: the knowledge that is the eye, generated by the gracious instruction of scripture and teacher, directed toward the Self's own conviction. With that eye of knowledge — [they also know] the liberation of beings from <s>Prakṛti</s>: the <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) of beings is the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) characterized as <s>avidyā</s>; the liberation from that <s>Prakṛti</s> of beings, i.e., the going into non-existence [of <s>avidyā</s>] — those who know this go to the Supreme, the reality of the Supreme Self, <s>Brahman</s>. They do not take on a body again — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 13.35 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary on the Blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṃkara Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda</s>,

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajña-yogo nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [ends] the thirteenth chapter, called the Yoga of the Field and the Knower of the Field.

children.text: BhG 14
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 14

children.text:
atha guṇa-traya-vibhāga-yogo nāma
caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
(śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavat-pāda-viracitam śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣyam)
sarvam utpadyamānaṃ kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyogād utpadyata ity uktam | tat kathamiti, tat-pradarśanārtham paraṃ bhūya ity ādir adhyāya ārabhyate | athavā, īśvara-paratantrayoḥ kṣetra-kṣetrajñayoḥ jagat-kāraṇatvaṃ na tu sāṃkhyānām iva svatantrayor ity evam artham | prakṛti-sthatvaṃ guṇeṣu ca saṅgaḥ saṃsāra-kāraṇam ity uktam | kasmin guṇe kathaṃ saṅgaḥ ? ke vā guṇāḥ ? kathaṃ vā te badhnantīti ? guṇebhyaś ca mokṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ syāt ? muktasya ca lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam, ity evam arthaṃ ca bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text:
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now [begins] the fourteenth chapter called the Yoga of the Division of the Three <s>Guṇas</s>.
(Commentary composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat-pāda</s>)
It has been stated that everything that is produced arises from the conjunction of the field and the knower of the field. How is that? For the purpose of demonstrating that, the chapter beginning with 'the supreme, once again' is commenced. Or alternatively: [the purpose is to show that] the field and the knower of the field, being dependent on the Lord, are the cause of the world, and not [as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold] independent [entities]. It has been stated that being established in <s>Prakṛti</s> and attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>. To which <s>guṇa</s> is there attachment and how? What are the <s>guṇas</s>? How do they bind? And how does liberation from the <s>guṇas</s> occur? And the characteristics of the liberated one must be stated — with such purposes the Blessed Lord said:

children.text: paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānam uttamam |
children.translated_text: I shall once again declare the supreme knowledge, the best of all forms of knowledge,

children.text: yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ ||BhG_14.1||
children.translated_text: knowing which, all the sages have gone from here to the highest perfection. // <s>BhG</s> 14.1 //

children.text: paraṃ jñānam iti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ | bhūyaḥ punaḥ pūrveṣu sarveṣv adhyāyeṣu asakṛd uktam api pravakṣyāmi | tac ca paraṃ para-vastu-viṣayatvāt | kiṃ tat ? jñānaṃ sarveṣāṃ jñānānām uttamam, uttama-phalatvāt | jñānānām iti nāmānitvādīnām | kiṃ tarhi ? yajñādi-jñeya-vastu-viṣayāṇām iti | tāni na mokṣāya, idaṃ tu mokṣāyeti parottama-śabdābhyāṃ stauti śrotṛ-buddhi-rucy-utpādanārtham | yaj jñātvā yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā prāpya munayaḥ saṃnyāsino manana-śīlāḥ sarve parāṃ siddhiṃ mokṣākhyām ito 'smāt deha-bandhanāt ūrdhvaṃ gatāḥ prāptāḥ ||BhGS_14.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Supreme knowledge' — the connection is with [this word] which is separated [by intervening words]. 'Once again' — although stated repeatedly in all the preceding chapters, I shall declare [it]. And it is 'supreme' because it pertains to the supreme reality. What is it? Knowledge — the best of all forms of knowledge, because it has the best fruit. 'Of all forms of knowledge' does not mean [knowledge] of names etc. But rather, [knowledge] pertaining to the objects to be known such as sacrifice and the like. Those [forms of knowledge] do not lead to liberation, but this one does — thus He praises [it] with the words 'supreme' and 'best' for the purpose of generating interest in the listener's mind. 'Knowing which' — having known, having attained this knowledge — all the sages (<s>muni</s>), the renunciants given to reflection, have gone to the highest perfection, namely liberation, from here, i.e., from this bondage of the body. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.1 //

children.text: asyāś ca siddhair aikāntikatvaṃ darśayati -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And He shows the certainty [of this result] through [the example of] the perfected ones:

children.text: idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having resorted to this knowledge, they have attained identity of nature with Me;

children.text: sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca ||BhG_14.2||
children.translated_text: they are not born [even] at the time of creation, nor do they suffer at the time of dissolution. // <s>BhG</s> 14.2 //

children.text: idaṃ jñānaṃ yathoktam upāśritya, jñāna-sādhanam anuṣṭhāya ity etat, mama parameśvarasya sādharmyaṃ mat-svarūpatām āgatāḥ prāptā ity arthaḥ | na tu samāna-dharmatā sādharmyam, kṣetrajñeśvarayor bhedānabhyupagamād gītā-śāstre | phala-vādaś cāyaṃ stuty-artham ucyate | sarge 'pi sṛṣṭi-kāle 'pi nopajāyante | notpadyante | pralaye brahmaṇo 'pi vināśa-kāle na vyathanti ca vyathāṃ nāpadyante, na cyavantīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_14.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having resorted to this knowledge as described — meaning having practiced the means of knowledge — they have attained identity of nature with Me (<s>sādharmya</s>), i.e., they have attained My own essential nature — the Supreme Lord's — this is the meaning. 'Identity of nature' does not mean sharing similar properties, because the non-difference of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> and the Lord is accepted in the <s>Gītā-śāstra</s>. And this statement about the fruit is said for the purpose of praise. They are not born [even] at the time of creation, and at the time of dissolution — even the dissolution of <s>Brahmā</s> — they do not suffer, i.e., they do not experience distress; they do not fall — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.2 //

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetrajña-saṃyoga īdṛśo bhūta-kāraṇam ity āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This is how the conjunction of the field and the knower of the field is the cause of beings — He says:

children.text: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham |
children.translated_text: My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s> (i.e., <s>Prakṛti</s>); in that I place the seed;

children.text: saṃbhavaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata ||BhG_14.3||
children.translated_text: the birth of all beings arises from that, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 14.3 //

children.text: mama sva-bhūtā madīyā māyā triguṇātmikā prakṛtir yoniḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ kāraṇam | sarva-kāryebhyo mahattvāt kāraṇatvād bṛṃhaṇāc ca [bharaṇāc ca] sva-vikārāṇāṃ mahad brahma iti yonir eva viśiṣyate | tasmin mahati brahmaṇi yonau garbhaṃ hiraṇyagarbhasya janmano bījaṃ sarva-bhūta-janma-kāraṇaṃ bījaṃ dadhāmi nikṣipāmi kṣetra-kṣetrajña-prakṛti-dvaya-śaktimān īśvaro 'ham, avidyā-kāma-karmopādhi-svarūpānuvidhāyinaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ kṣetreṇa saṃyojayāmīty arthaḥ | saṃbhava utpattiḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hiraṇyagarbhotpatti-dvāreṇa tatas tasmād gabrhādhānād bhavati | he bhārata ||BhGS_14.3||
children.translated_text: My own <s>Māyā</s> (illusive power), consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, is <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the womb, the cause of all beings. Because it is greater than all effects, because it is the cause, and because it nourishes [and sustains] its own modifications, it is distinguished as the great <s>Brahman</s> — the womb itself is thus qualified. In that great <s>Brahman</s> which is the womb, I place the seed — the seed that is the cause of the birth of all beings, the seed of the birth of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. I, the Lord, possessed of the twofold power of <s>kṣetra</s> (field) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) as <s>Prakṛti</s>, place it — the meaning is: I conjoin the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), who conforms to the nature of the limiting adjuncts of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s> (action), with the <s>kṣetra</s> (field). The origination, the birth of all beings, comes about through the birth of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, from that placing of the seed. O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||BhGS_14.3||

children.text: sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
children.translated_text: In all wombs, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, whatever forms come into being,

children.text: tāsāṃ brahma mahad yonir ahaṃ bīja-pradaḥ pitā ||BhG_14.4||
children.translated_text: of all of them the great <s>Brahman</s> is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father. ||BhG_14.4||

children.text: deva-pitṛ-manuṣya-paśu-mṛgādi-sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya, mūrtayo deha-saṃsthāna-lakṣaṇā mūrcchitāṅgāvayavā mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ, tāsāṃ mūrtīnāṃ brahma mahat sarvāvasthaṃ yoniḥ kāraṇam aham īśvaro bīja-prado garbhādhānasya kartā pitā ||BhGS_14.4||
children.translated_text: In all wombs — of <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors), humans, cattle, wild animals, and so forth — O <s>Kaunteya</s>, whatever forms come into being — forms characterized by bodily configuration, having solidified limbs and parts — of all those forms, the great <s>Brahman</s>, present in all states, is the womb, the cause; I, the Lord, am the seed-giver, the agent of the placing of the seed, the father. ||BhGS_14.4||

children.text: ke guṇāḥ ? kathaṃ badhnanti ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: What are the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities)? How do they bind? This is stated —

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)

children.text: nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam ||BhG_14.5||
children.translated_text: bind the imperishable embodied Self in the body, O mighty-armed one. ||BhG_14.5||

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama ity evaṃ-nāmāno guṇā iti pāribhāṣikaḥ śabdaḥ | na rūpādivad dravyāśritā guṇāḥ | na ca guṇa-guṇinor anyatvam atra vivakṣitam | tasmād guṇā iva nitya-para-tantrāḥ kṣetrajñaṃ praty avidyātmakatvāt kṣetrajñaṃ nibadhnantīva tam āspadīkṛtyātmānaṃ pratilabhanta iti nibadhnantīty ucyate | te ca prakṛti-saṃbhavā bhagavan-māyā-saṃbhavā nibadhnantīva | he mahābāho | mahāntau samarthatarāv ājānu-pralambau bāhū yasya saḥ mahābāhuḥ he mahābāho | dehe śarīre dehinaṃ dehavantam avyayam, avyayatvaṃ coktam anāditvād [Gītā 13.32] ity ādi ślokena | nanu dehī na lipyate [Gītā 13.32] ity uktam | tat katham iha nibadhnantīty anyathocyate ? parihṛtam asmābhir iva-śabdena nibadhnantīveti ||BhGS_14.5||
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s> — these are names; '<s>guṇas</s>' is a technical term. They are not qualities inhering in a substance like color and so forth. Nor is the difference between quality and the qualified intended here. Therefore, being always dependent like qualities, since they are of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) with respect to the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), they bind the <s>kṣetrajña</s> as it were — it is said they 'bind' because they establish themselves by making him their locus. And they are born of <s>Prakṛti</s>, born of the Lord's <s>Māyā</s>, and they bind as it were. O mighty-armed one — he whose two arms are great, most capable, hanging down to the knees, is <s>Mahābāhu</s> (mighty-armed), O <s>Mahābāhu</s>. In the body, in the physical frame, the embodied one, the possessor of the body, who is imperishable — and the imperishability has been stated in the verse beginning with 'due to beginninglessness' [Gītā 13.32]. But it was said 'the embodied Self is not tainted' [Gītā 13.32]. Then how is it said here differently that they 'bind'? This has been resolved by us through the word 'iva' (as it were) — they bind as it were. ||BhGS_14.5||

children.text: tatra sattvādīnāṃ sattvasyaiva tāval lakṣaṇam ucyate -
children.translated_text: Among these, the characteristic of <s>sattva</s> among <s>sattva</s> and the rest is stated first —

children.text: tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam |
children.translated_text: Among these, <s>sattva</s>, being pure, is illuminating and free from affliction;

children.text: sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena cānagha ||BhG_14.6||
children.translated_text: it binds through attachment to happiness and through attachment to knowledge, O sinless one. ||BhG_14.6||

children.text: nirmalatvāt sphaṭika-maṇir iva prakāśakam anāmayaṃ nirupadravaṃ sattvaṃ tan nibadhnāti | katham ? sukha-saṅgena sukhy aham iti viṣaya-bhūtasya sukhasya viṣayiṇy ātmani saṃśleṣāpādanaṃ mṛṣaiva sukhe sañjanam iti | saiṣāvidyā | na hi viṣaya-dharmo viṣayiṇo bhavati | icchādi ca dhṛty-antaṃ kṣetrasyaiva viṣayasya dharmaḥ ity uktaṃ bhagavatā | ato 'vidyayaiva svakīya-dharma-bhūtayā viṣaya-viṣayy-aviveka-lakṣaṇayāsvātma-bhūte sukhe saṃjayatīva, āsaktam iva karoti, asaṅgaṃ saktam iva karoti, asukhinaṃ sukhinam iva | tathā jñāna-saṅgena ca, jñānam iti sukha-sāhacaryāt kṣetrasyaiva viṣayasyāntaḥ-karaṇasya dharmaḥ, nātmanaḥ | ātma-dharmatve saṅgānupapatteḥ, bandhānupapatteś ca | sukha iva jñānādau saṅgo mantavyaḥ | he anagha avyasana ||BhGS_14.6||
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, being pure like a crystal gem, is illuminating, free from affliction, free from trouble — that <s>sattva</s> binds. How? Through attachment to happiness — the false identification of happiness, which is an object, with the Self who is the subject, thinking 'I am happy,' is the clinging to happiness which is indeed false. This itself is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). For a property of the object does not belong to the subject. And it has been said by the Lord that desire and the rest up to firmness are properties of the <s>kṣetra</s> (field), the object. Therefore, through <s>avidyā</s> alone, which is its own property, characterized by non-discrimination between object and subject, it causes attachment as it were to happiness which is not one's own nature — it makes the unattached appear as if attached, and the one who is not happy appear as if happy. Likewise through attachment to knowledge — knowledge, because of its association with happiness, is a property of the <s>kṣetra</s> (field), the object, the inner instrument, not of the Self. If it were a property of the Self, attachment would be impossible, and bondage would be impossible. The attachment to knowledge and so forth should be understood like the attachment to happiness. O sinless one, O one free from vice! ||BhGS_14.6||

children.text: rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅga-samudbhavam |
children.translated_text: Know <s>rajas</s> to be of the nature of passion, arising from craving and attachment;

children.text: tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena dehinam ||BhG_14.7||
children.translated_text: it binds the embodied Self through attachment to action, O <s>Kaunteya</s>. ||BhG_14.7||

children.text: rajaḥ rāgātmakaṃ rajanād rāgo gairikād iva drāg ātmakaṃ viddhi jānīhi | tṛṣṇāsaṅga-samudbhavaṃ tṛṣṇā aprāptābhilāṣaḥ | āsaṅgaḥ prāpte viṣaye manasaḥ prīti-lakṣaṇaḥ saṃśleṣaḥ | tṛṣṇāsaṅgayoḥ samudbhavaṃ tṛṣṇāsaṅga-samudbhavam | tan nibadhnāti tad rajo nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena, dṛṣṭādṛṣṭārtheṣu karmasu sañjanaṃ tat-paratā karma-saṅgas tena nibadhnāti rajo dehinam ||BhGS_14.7||
children.translated_text: <s>Rajas</s> — know it to be of the nature of passion; from coloring (<s>rajanāt</s>) comes passion (<s>rāga</s>), like red chalk it quickly colors — such is its nature, know this. Arising from craving and attachment — craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is desire for what is not yet obtained; attachment (<s>āsaṅga</s>) is the clinging characterized by delight of the mind in an object already obtained. It arises from craving and attachment, hence 'arising from craving and attachment.' That <s>rajas</s> binds, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, through attachment to action — the clinging to actions directed toward seen and unseen ends, being wholly devoted to them, is attachment to action; through that, <s>rajas</s> binds the embodied Self. ||BhGS_14.7||

children.text: tamas tv ajñāna-jaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarva-dehinām |
children.translated_text: But know <s>tamas</s> to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings;

children.text: pramādālasya-nidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata ||BhG_14.8||
children.translated_text: it binds through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep, O <s>Bhārata</s>. ||BhG_14.8||

children.text: tamas tṛtīyo guṇo 'jñāna-jam ajñānāj jātam ajñāna-jaṃ viddhi | mohanaṃ moha-karam aviveka-karaṃ sarva-dehināṃ sarveṣāṃ dehavatām | pramādālasya-nidrābhiḥ pramādaś cālasyaṃ ca nidrā ca pramādālasya-nidrās tābhiḥ pramādālasya-nidrābhis tat tamo nibadhnāti bhārata ||BhGS_14.8||
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s>, the third <s>guṇa</s>, is born of ignorance — born from <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), know it to be born of ignorance. It is deluding, causing delusion, causing non-discrimination, in all embodied beings, in all possessors of bodies. Through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep — heedlessness, laziness, and sleep are <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness), <s>ālasya</s> (laziness), and <s>nidrā</s> (sleep); through these — through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep — that <s>tamas</s> binds, O <s>Bhārata</s>. ||BhGS_14.8||

children.text: punar guṇānāṃ vyāpāraḥ saṃkṣepata ucyate -
children.translated_text: Again, the operation of the <s>guṇas</s> is stated in brief —

children.text: sattvaṃ sukhe saṃjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> causes attachment to happiness, <s>rajas</s> to action, O <s>Bhārata</s>;

children.text: jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde saṃjayaty uta ||BhG_14.9||
children.translated_text: but <s>tamas</s>, veiling knowledge, causes attachment to heedlessness. ||BhG_14.9||

children.text: sattvaṃ sukhe saṃjayati saṃśleṣayati, rajaḥ karmaṇi he bhārata saṃjayatīty anuvartate | jñānaṃ sattva-kṛtaṃ vivekam āvṛtya ācchādya tu tamaḥ svena āvaraṇātmanā pramāde saṃjayaty uta | pramādo nāma prāpta-kartavyākaraṇam ||BhGS_14.9||
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> causes attachment to happiness, creates a bond with it; <s>rajas</s> to action — O <s>Bhārata</s>, 'causes attachment' is carried over from the previous clause. But <s>tamas</s>, veiling, covering over knowledge — the discrimination produced by <s>sattva</s> — by its own nature of obscuration, causes attachment to heedlessness. <s>Pramāda</s> (heedlessness) means the failure to perform what ought to be done when the occasion has arrived. ||BhGS_14.9||

children.text: uktaṃ kāryaṃ kadā kurvanti guṇāḥ ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: When do the <s>guṇas</s> perform their stated functions? This is stated —

children.text: rajas tamaś cābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> prevails, O <s>Bhārata</s>, having overcome <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>;

children.text: rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaś caiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tathā ||BhG_14.10||
children.translated_text: <s>rajas</s> prevails over <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> over <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> likewise. ||BhG_14.10||

children.text: rajas tamaś ca ubhāv apy abhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati udbhavati vardhate yadā, tadā labdhātmakaṃ sattvaṃ sva-kāryaṃ jñāna-sukhādy ārabhate | he bhārata ! tathā rajo-guṇaḥ sattvaṃ tamaś caiva ubhāv apy abhibhūya vardhate yadā, tadā karma tṛṣṇādi sva-kāryam ārabhate | tama-ākhyo guṇaḥ sattvaṃ rajaś ca ubhāv apy abhibhūya tathaiva vardhate yadā, tadā jñānāvaraṇādi sva-kāryam ārabhate ||BhGS_14.10||
children.translated_text: When <s>sattva</s> prevails, arises, and increases, having overcome both <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, then <s>sattva</s>, having gained strength, commences its own effects such as knowledge and happiness. O <s>Bhārata</s>! Likewise, when the quality of <s>rajas</s> increases, having overcome both <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, then it commences its own effects such as action and craving. When the quality called <s>tamas</s> increases, having overcome both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> in the same way, then it commences its own effects such as the veiling of knowledge. ||BhGS_14.10||

children.text: yadā yo guṇa udbhūto bhavati, tadā tasya kiṃ liṅgam ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: When a particular <s>guṇa</s> has arisen and prevails, what is its sign? This is stated —

children.text: sarva-dvāreṣu dehe 'smin prakāśa upajāyate |
children.translated_text: When at all the gates of this body illumination arises,

children.text: jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛddhaṃ sattvam ity uta ||BhG_14.11||
children.translated_text: which is knowledge, then one should know that <s>sattva</s> has become predominant. ||BhG_14.11||

children.text: sarva-dvāreṣu, ātmana upalabdhi-dvārāṇi śrotrādīni sarvāṇi karaṇāni, teṣu sarva-dvāreṣu antaḥ-karaṇasya buddher vṛttiḥ prakāśo dehe 'smin upajāyate | tad eva jñānam | yadaivaṃ prakāśo jñānākhya upajāyate, tadā jñāna-prakāśena liṅgena vidyād vivṛddham udbhūtaṃ sattvam ity utāpi ||BhGS_14.11||
children.translated_text: At all the gates — the ears and other sense organs, which are all the gates of perception for the Self — at all these gates, illumination, which is the activity of the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), the inner instrument, arises in this body. That itself is knowledge. When such illumination called knowledge arises, then by that sign of the light of knowledge, one should know that <s>sattva</s> has become predominant, has arisen. ||BhGS_14.11||

children.text: rajasa udbhūtasyedaṃ cihnam -
children.translated_text: This is the sign when <s>rajas</s> has arisen —

children.text: lobhaḥ pravṛttir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā |
children.translated_text: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, and craving —

children.text: rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha ||BhG_14.12||
children.translated_text: these arise when <s>rajas</s> has become predominant, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>. ||BhG_14.12||

children.text: lobhaḥ para-dravyāditsā | pravṛttiḥ pravartanam | sāmānya-ceṣṭā ārambhaḥ | kasya ? karmaṇām | aśamo 'nupaśamaḥ harṣa-rāgādi-pravṛttiḥ | spṛhā sarva-sāmānya-vastu-viṣayā tṛṣṇā | rajasi guṇe vivṛddha etāni liṅgāni jāyante | he bharatarṣabha ||BhGS_14.12||
children.translated_text: Greed is the desire to seize others' wealth. Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is engagement in action. General exertion is the undertaking — of what? Of actions. Restlessness (<s>aśama</s>) is the absence of tranquility, the manifestation of excitement, passion, and the like. Craving (<s>spṛhā</s>) is desire directed toward all things in general. When the quality of <s>rajas</s> has become predominant, these signs arise. O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>! ||BhGS_14.12||

children.text: aprakāśo 'pravṛttiś ca pramādo moha eva ca |
children.translated_text: Non-illumination, inactivity, heedlessness, and delusion —

children.text: tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kuru-nandana ||BhG_14.13||
children.translated_text: these arise when <s>tamas</s> has become predominant, O joy of the <s>Kurus</s>. ||BhG_14.13||

children.text: aprakāśo 'vivekaḥ | atyantam apravṛttiś ca pravṛtty-abhāvas tat-kāryaṃ pramādo moha eva ca | aviveko mūḍhatā ity arthaḥ | tamasi guṇe vivṛddha etāni liṅgāni jāyante he kuru-nandana ! ||BhGS_14.13||
children.translated_text: Non-illumination is non-discrimination. Complete inactivity, the absence of engagement — its effects are heedlessness and delusion. Non-discrimination means stupefaction, that is the meaning. When the quality of <s>tamas</s> has become predominant, these signs arise, O joy of the <s>Kurus</s>! ||BhGS_14.13||

children.text: maraṇa-dvāreṇāpi yat phalaṃ prāpyate, tad api saṅga-rāga-hetukaṃ sarvaṃ gauṇam eveti darśayan āha -
children.translated_text: Showing that even the fruit obtained through the gate of death is entirely secondary, caused by attachment and passion, he says —

children.text: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti deha-bhṛt |
children.translated_text: When one who bears a body meets death while <s>sattva</s> is predominant,

children.text: tadottama-vidāṃ lokān amalān pratipadyate ||BhG_14.14||
children.translated_text: then he attains the pure worlds of the knowers of the highest. ||BhG_14.14||

children.text: yadā sattve pravṛddha udbhūte tu pralayaṃ maraṇaṃ yāti pratipadyate deha-bhṛd ātmā, tadottama-vidāṃ mahad-ādi-tattva-vidām ity etat | lokān amalān mala-rahitān pratipadyate prāpnotīty etat ||BhGS_14.14||
children.translated_text: When <s>sattva</s> is predominant, has arisen, and the bearer of the body, the Self, meets death, goes to dissolution — then he attains the worlds of the knowers of the highest, meaning those who know the principles beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) and so forth. The worlds that are pure, free from impurity — he attains, he reaches them. ||BhGS_14.14||

children.text: rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karma-saṅgiṣu jāyate |
children.translated_text: Dying when <s>rajas</s> predominates, one is born among those attached to action;

children.text: tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍha-yoniṣu jāyate ||BhG_14.15||
children.translated_text: likewise, dying when <s>tamas</s> predominates, one is born in the wombs of the deluded. ||BhG_14.15||

children.text: rajasi guṇe vivṛddhe pralayaṃ maraṇaṃ gatvā prāpya karma-saṅgiṣu karmāsakti-yukteṣu manuṣyeṣu jāyate | tathā tadvad eva pralīno mṛtas tamasi vivṛddhe mūḍha-yoniṣu paśv-ādi-yoniṣu jāyate ||BhGS_14.15||
children.translated_text: When the quality of <s>rajas</s> is predominant and one meets death, having gone to dissolution, one is born among those attached to action — among humans possessed of attachment to <s>karma</s> (action). Likewise, in the same way, one who has died when <s>tamas</s> is predominant is born in the wombs of the deluded — in the wombs of animals and the like. ||BhGS_14.15||

children.text: atīta-ślokārthasyaiva saṃkṣepa ucyate -
children.translated_text: A summary of the meaning of the preceding verses is stated —

children.text: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: Of well-performed action, they say the fruit is <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) and untainted;

children.text: rajasas tu phalaṃ duḥkham ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam ||BhG_14.16||
children.translated_text: but the fruit of <s>rajas</s> is suffering, and the fruit of <s>tamas</s> is ignorance. ||BhG_14.16||

children.text: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasya sāttvikasya ity arthaḥ, āhuḥ śiṣṭaḥ sāttvikam eva nirmalaṃ phalam iti | rajasas tu phalaṃ duḥkhaṃ rājasasya karmaṇa ity arthaḥ, karmādhikārāt phalam api duḥkham eva, kāraṇānurūpyāt, rājasam eva | tathā ajñānaṃ tamasas tāmasasya karmaṇo 'dharmasya pūrvavat ||BhGS_14.16||
children.translated_text: Of well-performed action — meaning <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>) action — the learned say the fruit is <s>sāttvika</s>, pure. But the fruit of <s>rajas</s> — meaning of <s>rājasa</s> (of the nature of <s>rajas</s>) action — since the context concerns action, the fruit too is nothing but suffering, because the effect corresponds to the cause, and is itself <s>rājasa</s>. Likewise, ignorance is the fruit of <s>tamas</s> — of <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>) action, of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) — as explained before. ||BhGS_14.16||

children.text: kiṃ ca, guṇebhyo bhavati -
children.translated_text: Moreover, from the <s>guṇas</s> there arises —

children.text: sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca |
children.translated_text: From <s>sattva</s> arises knowledge, and from <s>rajas</s> greed indeed;

children.text: pramāda-mohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca ||BhG_14.17||
children.translated_text: from <s>tamas</s> arise heedlessness and delusion, and indeed ignorance as well. ||BhG_14.17||

children.text: sattvāl labdhātmakāt saṃjāyate samutpadyate jñānam, rajaso lobha eva ca, pramāda-mohau ca ubhau tamaso bhavataḥ, ajñānam eva ca bhavati ||BhGS_14.17||
children.translated_text: From <s>sattva</s>, when it has gained strength, knowledge arises, is produced; from <s>rajas</s>, greed indeed; and heedlessness and delusion, both, arise from <s>tamas</s>; and ignorance as well arises. ||BhGS_14.17||

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those established in <s>sattva</s> go upward; those of <s>rājasa</s> nature stay in the middle;

children.text: jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtta-sthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ ||BhG_14.18||
children.translated_text: those abiding in the ways of the lowest <s>guṇa</s> go downward — the <s>tāmasas</s>. ||BhG_14.18||

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti devalokādiṣūtpadyante sattva-sthāḥ sattva-guṇa-vṛtta-sthāḥ | madhye tiṣṭhanti manuṣyeṣūtpadyante rājasāḥ | jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtta-sthā jaghanyaś cāsau guṇaś ca jaghanya-guṇas tamaḥ, tasya vṛttaṃ nidrālasyādi, tasmin sthitāḥ jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtta-sthāḥ mūḍhāḥ adho gacchanti paśv-ādiṣūtpadyante tāmasāḥ ||BhGS_14.18||
children.translated_text: Those established in <s>sattva</s> go upward — they are born in the worlds of the <s>devas</s> (gods) and the like; those established in the conduct of the <s>sattva</s> quality. Those of <s>rājasa</s> nature stay in the middle — they are born among humans. Those abiding in the ways of the lowest <s>guṇa</s> — the lowest quality is <s>tamas</s>; its ways are sleep, laziness, and the like; those established in these are those abiding in the ways of the lowest <s>guṇa</s>, the deluded — they go downward, they are born among animals and the like, the <s>tāmasas</s>. ||BhGS_14.18||

children.text: puruṣasya prakṛti-sthatva-rūpeṇa mithyā-jñānena yuktasya bhogyeṣu guṇeṣu sukha-duḥkha-mohātmakeṣu sukhī duḥkhī mūḍho 'ham asmīty evaṃ-rūpo yaḥ saṅgas tat-kāraṇaṃ puruṣasya sad-asad-yoni-janma-prāpti-lakṣaṇasya saṃsārasyeti samāsena pūrvādhyāye yad uktam, tad iha sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛti-saṃbhavā ity ārabhya guṇa-svarūpam, guṇa-vṛttam, sva-vṛttena ca guṇānāṃ bandhakatvam, guṇa-vṛtta-nibaddhasya ca purūṣasya yā gatiḥ, ity etat sarvaṃ mithyā-jñāna-mūlaṃ bandha-kāraṇaṃ vistareṇoktvā, adhunā samyag-darśanān mokṣo vaktavya ity ata āha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What was stated in brief in the preceding chapter — that the attachment of the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Self), who is endowed with false knowledge in the form of abiding in <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature), to the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) that are objects of experience, consisting of pleasure, pain, and delusion, in the form 'I am happy, I am unhappy, I am deluded' — that [attachment] is the cause of the <s>Puruṣa's</s> <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) characterized by birth in good and evil wombs — that is here, beginning with '<s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these <s>guṇas</s> are born of <s>Prakṛti</s>,' elaborated in detail: the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>, the activity of the <s>guṇas</s>, the binding nature of the <s>guṇas</s> through their activity, and the destiny of the <s>Puruṣa</s> bound by the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> — all this, which is the cause of bondage rooted in false knowledge, having been stated at length, now, since liberation through right knowledge is to be stated, the Blessed Lord says —

children.text: nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati |
children.translated_text: When the seer perceives no agent other than the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),

children.text: guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti mad-bhāvaṃ so 'dhigacchati ||BhG_14.19||
children.translated_text: and knows that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, he attains My state of being. // <s>BhG</s> 14.19 //

children.text: nānyaṃ kārya-karaṇa-viṣayākāra-pariṇatebhyo guṇebhyaḥ kartāram anyaṃ yadā draṣṭā vidvān san nānupaśyati, guṇā eva sarvāvasthāḥ sarva-karmaṇāṃ kartāra ity evaṃ paśyati, guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ guṇa-vyāpāra-sākṣi-bhūtaṃ vetti, mad-bhāvaṃ mama bhāvaṃ sa draṣṭādhigacchati ||BhGS_14.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] No agent other than the <s>guṇas</s> — [other than] the <s>guṇas</s> that have transformed into the forms of effects, instruments, and objects — when the seer, the wise one, perceives no other agent, [but rather] sees that the <s>guṇas</s> alone in all their states are the agents of all actions — and knows that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, the witness of the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> — he, that seer, attains My state of being (<s>mad-bhāva</s>), My nature. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.19 //

children.text: katham adhigacchati ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: How does he attain [it]? — it is said:

children.text: guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān |
children.translated_text: Having transcended these three <s>guṇas</s>, which are the source of the body, the embodied one,

children.text: janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhair vimukto 'mṛtam aśnute ||BhG_14.20||
children.translated_text: freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, attains immortality. // <s>BhG</s> 14.20 //

children.text: guṇān etān yathoktān atītya jīvann evātikramya māyopādhi-bhūtān trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān dehotpatti-bīja-bhūtān janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhair janma ca mṛtyuś ca jarā ca duḥkhāni ca janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhāni tair jīvann eva vimuktaḥ san vidvān amṛtam aśnute | evaṃ mad-bhāvam adhigacchatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_14.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having transcended these <s>guṇas</s> as described — having gone beyond them even while living, [the <s>guṇas</s>] which serve as the limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of <s>māyā</s> — the three [<s>guṇas</s>], the embodied one, which are the source of the body, the seeds of the body's origination — freed from the sufferings of birth, death, and old age — birth, death, old age, and suffering are 'birth-death-old-age-sufferings' — freed from those even while living, the wise one attains immortality (<s>amṛta</s>). Thus he attains My state of being — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.20 //

children.text: jīvann eva guṇān atītyāmṛtam aśnute iti praśna-bījaṃ pratilabhyārjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having obtained the seed for a question from [the statement] 'having transcended the <s>guṇas</s> even while living, one attains immortality,' <s>Arjuna</s> said —

children.text: kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho |
children.translated_text: By what marks is one who has transcended these three <s>guṇas</s> known, O Lord?

children.text: kim-ācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃs trīn guṇān ativartate ||BhG_14.21||
children.translated_text: What is his conduct, and how does he transcend these three <s>guṇas</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 14.21 //

children.text: kair liṅgaiś cihnais trīn etān vyākhyātān guṇān atīto 'tikrānto bhavati prabho, kim-ācāraḥ ? ko 'sya ācāra iti kim-ācāraḥ | kathaṃ kena ca prakāreṇa etān trīn guṇān ativartate 'tītya vartate ||BhGS_14.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] By what marks (<s>liṅga</s>), what signs, is one who has transcended, gone beyond, these three <s>guṇas</s> as described — [how is he] known, O Lord? What is his conduct? — what is his mode of behavior, [hence] 'what is his conduct?' And how, by what means, does he transcend these three <s>guṇas</s> — go beyond and abide [beyond them]? // <s>BhGS</s> 14.21 //

children.text: guṇātītasya lakṣaṇaṃ guṇātītatvopāyaṃ cārjunena pṛṣṭo 'smin śloke praśna-dvayārthaṃ prativacanaṃ bhagavān uvāca | yat tāvat kair liṅgair yukto guṇātīto bhavatīti tat śṛṇu -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Asked by <s>Arjuna</s> about the marks of one who has transcended the <s>guṇas</s> and the means of transcending them, the Blessed Lord gives the answer to both questions in this verse. First, hear about the marks by which one who has transcended the <s>guṇas</s> is recognized —

children.text: prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca moham eva ca pāṇḍava |
children.translated_text: Light, activity, and delusion, O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati ||BhG_14.22||
children.translated_text: he does not hate when they arise, nor does he long for them when they cease. // <s>BhG</s> 14.22 //

children.text:
prakāśaṃ ca sattvakāryaṃ pravṛttiṃ ca rajaḥkāryaṃ moham eva ca tamaḥkāryam ity etāni na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni samyagviṣayabhāvena udbhūtāni - mama tāmasaḥ pratyayo jātaḥ, tenāhaṃ mūḍhaḥ | tathā rājasī pravṛttir mama utpannā duḥkhātmikā, tenāhaṃ rajasā pravartitaḥ pracalitaḥ svarūpāt | kaṣṭaṃ mama vartate yo 'yaṃ matsvarūpāvasthānāt bhraṃśaḥ | tathā sāttviko guṇaḥ prakāśātmā māṃ vivekitvam āpādayan sukhe ca sajayan badhnātīti tāni dveṣṭy asamyag-darśitvena | tat evaṃ guṇātīto na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni | yathā ca sāttvikādipuruṣaḥ sattvādikāryāṇi ātmānaṃ prati prakāśya nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati, na tathā guṇātīto nivṛttāni kāṅkṣatīty arthaḥ | etat na parapratyakṣaṃ liṅgam | kiṃ tarhi ? svātmapratyakṣatvāt ātmārtham
eva etat lakṣaṇam | na hi svātmaviṣayaṃ dveṣamākāṅkṣāṃ vā paraḥ paśyati ||BhGS_14.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Light (<s>prakāśa</s>) — the effect of <s>sattva</s>; activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) — the effect of <s>rajas</s>; and delusion (<s>moha</s>) — the effect of <s>tamas</s>: these he does not hate when they have fully arisen, when they have manifested as their respective objects — [he does not think] 'A <s>tāmasic</s> cognition has arisen in me, by which I am deluded,' or likewise 'A <s>rājasic</s> [cognition has arisen],' or 'A <s>sāttvic</s> [cognition has arisen]' — he does not hate [them] thus. Nor, when they have ceased, does he long for them — [he does not think] 'When shall these arise in me [again]?' // <s>BhGS</s> 14.22 //

children.text: atha idānīm guṇātītaḥ kim-ācāraḥ ? iti praśnasya prativacanam āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, the answer to the question 'what is the conduct of one who has transcended the <s>guṇas</s>?' is given —

children.text: udāsīnavad āsīno guṇair yo na vicālyate |
children.translated_text: Seated as if indifferent, undisturbed by the <s>guṇas</s>,

children.text: guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate ||BhG_14.23||
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'the <s>guṇas</s> alone operate' — he who stands firm and does not waver — // <s>BhG</s> 14.23 //

children.text: udāsīnavad yathā udāsīno na kasyacit pakṣaṃ bhajate, tathāyaṃ guṇātītatvopāya-mārge 'vasthita āsīna ātmavid guṇair yaḥ saṃnyāsī na vicālyate viveka-darśanāvasthātaḥ | tad etat sphuṭīkaroti - guṇāḥ kārya-karaṇa-viṣayākāra-pariṇatā anyonyasmin vartante iti yo 'vatiṣṭhati | chando-bhaṅga-bhayāt parasmaipada-prayogaḥ | yo 'nutiṣṭhatīti vā pāṭhāntaram | neṅgate na calati, svarūpāvastha eva bhavatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_14.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] As if indifferent — just as an indifferent person takes no one's side, so this knower of the Self, established on the path that is the means of transcending the <s>guṇas</s>, seated [thus] — he who is a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) is not disturbed by the <s>guṇas</s> from his position of discriminative vision. He makes this clear: the <s>guṇas</s>, [in their forms as] effects, instruments, and objects, operate among the <s>guṇas</s> [themselves] — knowing this, he stands firm and does not waver from the knowledge of the truth. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.23 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ svasthaḥ sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Equal in pain and pleasure, self-abiding, regarding a clod, a stone, and gold as equal,

children.text: tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-saṃstutiḥ ||BhG_14.24||
children.translated_text: the same toward the agreeable and disagreeable, wise, equal in blame and praise of himself — // <s>BhG</s> 14.24 //

children.text: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ same duḥkha-sukhe yasya saḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ, svasthaḥ sve ātmani sthitaḥ prasannaḥ sama-loṣṭāśma-kāñcanaḥ loṣṭaṃ cāśmā ca kāñcanaṃ ca loṣṭāśmakāñcanāni samāni yasya saḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ, tulyapriyāpriyaḥ priyaṃ cāpriyaṃ ca priyāpriye tulye same yasya so 'yaṃ tulyapriyāpriyaḥ, dhīro dhīmān, tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ nindā ca ātmasaṃstuti ca nindātmasaṃstutī, tulye nindātmasaṃstutī yasya yateḥ sa tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ ||BhGS_14.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Equal in pain and pleasure — one for whom pain and pleasure are the same; self-abiding (<s>svastha</s>) — established in one's own Self, serene. Regarding a clod, a stone, and gold as equal — a clod, a stone, and gold are 'clod-stone-gold'; one for whom these are equal. The same toward the agreeable and disagreeable; wise (<s>dhīra</s>); equal in blame and praise of himself. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.24 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: mānāpamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāri-pakṣayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward the sides of friend and foe,

children.text: sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate ||BhG_14.25||
children.translated_text: renouncing all undertakings — he is said to have transcended the <s>guṇas</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 14.25 //

children.text: mānāpamānayos tulyaḥ samo nirvikāraḥ | tulyo mitrāri-pakṣayoḥ | yadyapy udāsīnā bhavanti kecit svābhiprāyeṇa, tathāpi parābhiprāyeṇa mitrāri-pakṣayor iva bhavantīti tulyo mitrāri-pakṣayor ity āha | sarvārambha-parityāgī | dṛṣṭādṛṣṭārthāni karmāṇy ārabhyanta ity ārambhāḥ | sarvān ārambhān parityaktuṃ śīlam asyeti sarvārambha-parityāgī | deha-dhāraṇa-mātra-nimitta-vyatirekeṇa sarva-karma-parityāgīty arthaḥ | guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate ||BhGS_14.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Equal in honor and dishonor — the same, unchanged. Equal toward the sides of friend and foe. Even though some may be indifferent of their own accord, still, from others' perspectives, they appear as if on the side of friend or foe — therefore he says 'equal toward the sides of friend and foe.' Renouncing all undertakings — he is said to have transcended the <s>guṇas</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 14.25 //

children.text: udāsīnavad ity ādi guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate ity etad-antam uktaṃ yāvat yatna-sādhyaṃ tāvat saṃnyāsino 'nuṣṭheyaṃ guṇātītatva-sādhanaṃ mumukṣoḥ | sthirī-bhūtaṃ tu sva-saṃvedyaṃ sad guṇātītasya yater lakṣaṇaṃ bhavatīti | adhunā kathaṃ ca trīnguṇān ativartate ? ity asya praśnasya prativacanam āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What was stated from 'seated as if indifferent' up to 'he is said to have transcended the <s>guṇas</s>' — all of that, insofar as it is achievable through effort, is to be practiced by a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>) who desires liberation as the means of transcending the <s>guṇas</s>. But when it has become firmly established, it is self-evident as the mark of one who has transcended the <s>guṇas</s>, a renunciant who is a knower —

children.text: māṃ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa bhakti-yogena sevate |
children.translated_text: And one who serves Me with unswerving <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (the yoga of devotion),

children.text: sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate ||BhG_14.26||
children.translated_text: having fully transcended these <s>guṇas</s>, becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 14.26 //

children.text: māṃ ca īśvaraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ sarva-bhūta-hṛdayāśritaṃ yo yatiḥ karmī vā avyabhicāreṇa na kadācid yo vyabhicarati bhakti-yogena bhajanaṃ bhaktiḥ saiva yogas tena bhakti-yogena sevate, sa guṇān samatītya etān yathoktān | brahma-bhūyāya | bhavanaṃ bhūyaḥ, brahma-bhūyāya brahma-bhavanāya mokṣāya kalpate samartho bhavatīty arthaḥ ||BhGS_14.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And one who serves Me, the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who dwells in the hearts of all beings — the renunciant (<s>yati</s>) or the performer of rites — with unswerving [devotion], never deviating — with <s>bhakti-yoga</s>: worship (<s>bhajana</s>) is devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), and that itself is <s>yoga</s>; with that <s>bhakti-yoga</s> — serves [Me]. He, having fully transcended these <s>guṇas</s> as described, becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-bhūya</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 14.26 //

children.text: kuta etad ? ity ucyate -
children.translated_text: How is this so? — it is said:

children.text: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham amṛtasyāvyayasya ca |
children.translated_text: For I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>, of the immortal and imperishable,

children.text: śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca ||BhG_14.27||
children.translated_text: of the eternal <s>dharma</s>, and of absolute bliss. // <s>BhG</s> 14.27 //

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ paramātmano hi yasmāt pratiṣṭhāhaṃ pratitiṣṭhaty asmin iti pratiṣṭhāhaṃ pratyag-ātmā | kīdṛśasya brahmaṇaḥ ? amṛtasya avināśinaḥ | avyayasya avikāriṇaḥ | śāśvatasya ca nityasya dharmasya dharma-jñānasya jñāna-yoga-dharma-prāpyasya sukhasya ānanda-rūpasya aikāntikasya avyabhicāriṇo 'mṛtādi-svabhāvasya paramānanda-rūpasya paramātmanaḥ pratyag-ātmā pratiṣṭhā |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Of <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self — for (<s>hi</s>), because — I am the foundation: that in which [something] is established is the foundation; I am the inner Self (<s>pratyag-ātmā</s>). Of what kind of <s>Brahman</s>? Of the immortal — the indestructible. Of the imperishable — the unchanging. And of the eternal <s>dharma</s> — of the permanent <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: samyag-jñānena paramātmatayā niścīyate | tad etad brahma-bhūyāya kalpata ity uktam | yayā ceśvara-śaktyā bhaktānugrahādi-prayojanāya brahma pratiṣṭhate pravartate, sā śaktir brahmaivāham | śakti-śaktimator ananyatvād ity abhiprāyaḥ | athavā, brahma-śabda-vācyatvāt sa-vikalpakaṃ brahma | tasya brahmaṇo nirvikalpako 'ham eva nānyaḥ pratiṣṭhāśrayaḥ | kiṃ-viśiṣṭasya ? amṛtasyāmaraṇa-dharmakasyāvyayasya vyaya-rahitasya | kiṃ ca, śāśvatasya ca nityasya dharmasya jñāna-niṣṭhā-lakṣaṇasya sukhasya taj-janitasya aikāntikasya ekānta-niyatasya ca, pratiṣṭhāham iti vartate ||BhGS_14.27||
