children.translated_text: [<s>Brahman</s>] is ascertained as the Supreme Self through right knowledge. This is what is meant by 'becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>.' And the power of the Lord by which <s>Brahman</s> operates for the purpose of bestowing grace upon devotees and the like — that power is <s>Brahman</s> itself, which is I. The power and the possessor of power are non-different.

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
||14||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavān</s>, disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most exalted wandering monk (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s>), [this is] the fourteenth chapter.

children.text: BhG 15
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 15

children.text:
atha puruṣottama-yogo nāma
pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the fifteenth chapter, named the Yoga of the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama-yoga</s>).

children.text: (śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavat-pāda-viracitam śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavatpāda</s>)

children.text: yasmān mad-adhīnaṃ karmiṇāṃ karma-phalaṃ jñānināṃ ca jñāna-phalam, ato bhakti-yogena māṃ ye sevante te mama prasādāj jñāna-prāpti-krameṇa guṇātītā mokṣaṃ gacchanti | kim u vaktavyam ātmanas tattvam eva samyak vijānanta ity ato bhagavān arjunenāpṛṣṭo 'py ātmanas tattvaṃ vivakṣur uvāca ūrdhva-mūlam ity ādinā | tatra tāvad vṛkṣa-rūpaka-kalpanayā vairāgya-hetoḥ saṃsāra-svarūpaṃ varṇayati - viraktasya hi saṃsārāt bhagavat-tattva-jñāne 'dhikāraḥ, nānyasyeti | śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Since the fruit of action for performers of rites and the fruit of knowledge for the wise are both dependent on Me, therefore those who serve Me through <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (the yoga of devotion), by My grace, through the gradual attainment of knowledge, transcend the <s>guṇas</s> and reach liberation. What more need be said — those who know the truth of the Self itself [certainly attain liberation]. For the purpose of knowing the truth of the Lord, through the analysis of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) and [the knowledge of] the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Puruṣottama</s>) who is distinct from both the perishable and the imperishable — this chapter is begun. The Blessed Lord said —

children.text: śrī-bhagavān uvāca
children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śākham aśvatthaṃ prāhur avyayam |
children.translated_text: They speak of the imperishable <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree) with roots above and branches below,

children.text: chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yas taṃ veda sa veda-vit ||BhG_15.1||
children.translated_text: whose leaves are the Vedic hymns (<s>chandas</s>) — one who knows it is a knower of the <s>Vedas</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 15.1 //

children.text: ūrdhva-mūlaṃ kālataḥ sūkṣmatvāt kāraṇatvān nityatvāt mahattvāc cordhvam | ucyate brahmāvyaktaṃ māyā śaktimat, tan mūlam asyeti so 'yaṃ saṃsāra-vṛkṣaḥ ūrdhva-mūlaḥ | śruteś ca - ūrdhva-mūlo 'vāk-śākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ [KaṭhU 2.3.1] iti | purāṇe ca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] With roots above — because, in terms of time, [the root] is subtle, because it is the cause, because it is eternal, and because it is great, [<s>Brahman</s>] is said to be 'above.' The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) <s>Brahman</s>, possessing the power of <s>māyā</s>, is called [the root]; that is its root — thus this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> has its roots above. And from <s>Śruti</s>: 'With roots above and branches below' [<s>KaṭhU</s> 6.1].

children.text: avyakta-mūla-prabhavas tasyaivānugrahotthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Arising from the root of the unmanifest, sprung by its grace,

children.text: buddhi-skandha-mayaś caiva indriyāntara-koṭaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: having intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) as its trunk, with hollows that are the sense-organs,

children.text: mahā-bhūta-viśākhaś ca viṣayaiḥ patravāṃs tathā |
children.translated_text: with the great elements as its main branches, and with sense-objects as its leaves —

children.text: dharmādharma-supuṣpaś ca sukha-duḥkha-phalodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> as its abundant flowers, and the arising of pleasure and pain as its fruits;

children.text: ājīvyaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ brahma-vṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: the eternal tree of <s>Brahman</s>, the sustenance of all beings.

children.text: etad brahma-vanaṃ cāsya brahmācarati sākṣivat ||
children.translated_text: And this is its forest of <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Brahman</s> moves about in it as a witness.

children.text: etac chittvā ca bhittvā ca jñānena paramāsinā |
tataś cātma-gatiṃ prāpya tasmān nāvartate punaḥ || [Mbh 14.35.20-22] ity ādi |
children.translated_text: and then having attained the destination of the Self, one does not return from there again. [<s>Mahābhārata</s> 14.35.20-22] — thus and so forth.
Having cut and split this [tree] with the supreme sword of knowledge,

children.text:
tam ūrdhva-mūlaṃ saṃsāraṃ māyā-mayaṃ vṛkṣam āhuḥ | adhaḥ-śākhaṃ mahad-ahaṃkāra-tanmātrādayaḥ śākhā ivāsyādho bhavantīti so 'yam adhaḥ-śākhaḥ, tam adhaḥ-śākham | na śvo 'pi sthātety aśvatthas taṃ kṣaṇa-pradhvaṃsinam aśvatthaṃ prāhuḥ kathayanty avyayaṃ saṃsāra-māyāyā anādi-kāla-pravṛttatvāt so 'yaṃ saṃsāra-vṛkṣo 'vyayaḥ, anādy-anta-dehādi-saṃtānāśrayo hi suprasiddhaḥ, tam avyayam | tasyaiva saṃsāra-vṛkṣasya idam anyat viśeṣaṇam - chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni, chandāṃsi cchādanād ṛg-yajuḥ-sāma-lakṣaṇāni yasya saṃsāra-vṛkṣasya parṇānīva parṇāni | yathā vṛkṣasya parirakṣaṇārthāni parṇāni, tathā vedāḥ saṃsāra-vṛkṣa-parirakṣaṇārthā dharmādharma-tad-dhetu-phala-prakāśanārthatvāt | yathā-vyākhyātaṃ
saṃsāra-vṛkṣaṃ sa-mūlaṃ yas taṃ veda sa veda-vit, vedārtha-vid ity arthaḥ | na hi sa-mūlāt saṃsāra-vṛkṣād asmāj jñeyo 'nyo 'ṇu-mātro 'py avaśiṣṭo 'stīty ataḥ sarvajñaḥ sarva-vedārtha-vid iti sa-mūla-saṃsāra-vṛkṣa-jñānaṃ stauti ||BhGS_15.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>, rooted above, made of <s>Māyā</s> — they call [thus]. 'With branches below' — <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense), <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), etc. are, as it were, its branches extending downward — thus it has 'branches below.' 'That which will not stand even tomorrow' — hence <s>Aśvattha</s>; they call it the <s>Aśvattha</s>, perishing at every moment. Yet 'imperishable' (<s>avyaya</s>) — because the <s>Māyā</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been operative from beginningless time, this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> is imperishable, for it is well known as resting upon the beginningless and endless continuum of bodies etc. — [they call it] imperishable. This is another characterization of that very tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>: 'whose leaves are the <s>Vedic</s> hymns' (<s>chandāṃsi</s>) — the <s>chandas</s>, so called because they cover (<s>chādana</s>), characterized as <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajuḥ</s>, and <s>Sāma</s>, are like the leaves of this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Just as the leaves serve to protect the tree, so the <s>Vedas</s> serve to protect the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>, since they illuminate <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, their causes and fruits. He who knows the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> as thus explained, together with its root — that one is a knower of the <s>Veda</s> (<s>veda-vit</s>), meaning a knower of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>. For beyond this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> together with its root, there is not even an atom's worth of anything else remaining to be known — therefore [such a one] is omniscient, a knower of the meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s> — thus he praises the knowledge of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> together with its root. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.1||

children.text: tasyaitasya saṃsāra-vṛkṣasyāparāvayava-kalpanocyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The description of the further parts of this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> is stated:

children.text: adhaś cordhvaṃ prasṛtās tasya śākhā
children.translated_text: Below and above its branches spread forth,

children.text: guṇa-pravṛddhā viṣaya-pravālāḥ |
children.translated_text: nourished by the <s>guṇas</s>, with sense-objects as their sprouts;

children.text: adhaś ca mūlāny anusaṃtatāni
children.translated_text: and below, the roots extend continuously,

children.text: karmānubandhīni manuṣya-loke ||BhG_15.2||
children.translated_text: binding to action, in the world of human beings. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.2||

children.text:
adho manuṣyādibhyo yāvat sthāvaram, ata ūrdhvaṃ ca yāvad brahmaṇo viśva-sṛjo dhāma ity etad-antaṃ yathā-karma yathā-śrutaṃ jñāna-karma-phalāni, tasya vṛkṣasya śākhā iva śākhāḥ prasṛtāḥ pragatāḥ | guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ guṇaiḥ sattva-rajas-tamobhiḥ pravṛddhāḥ sthūlīkṛtā upādāna-bhūtaiḥ | viṣaya-pravālā viṣayāḥ śabdādayaḥ pravālā iva dehādi-karma-phalebhyaḥ śākhābhyo 'ṅkurī-bhavantīva, tena viṣaya-pravālāḥ śākhāḥ | saṃsāra-vṛkṣasya parama-mūlaṃ upādāna-kāraṇaṃ pūrvam uktam | athedānīṃ karma-phala-janita-rāga-dveṣādi-vāsanā mūlānīva dharmādharma-pravṛtti-kāraṇāny avāntara-bhāvīni tāny adhaś ca devādy-apekṣayā mūlāny anusantatāny anupraviṣṭani karmānubandhīni karma dharmādharma-lakṣaṇam
anubandhaḥ paścād-bhāvi, yeṣām udbhūtim anu udbhavati, tāni karmānubandhīni manuṣya-loke viśeṣataḥ | atra hi manuṣyāṇāṃ karmādhikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ ||BhGS_15.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Below' — from human beings downward to the immovable [plants]; 'and above' — up to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s> the world-creator — within this range, according to one's <s>karma</s> and according to one's learning, the fruits of knowledge and action — these are the branches of that tree, like branches, spread forth, i.e., extended. 'Nourished by the <s>guṇas</s>' — strengthened, i.e., made gross, by the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — which serve as the material [cause]. 'With sense-objects as their sprouts' — the sense-objects such as sound etc. are like sprouts from the branches that are the bodies, actions, and karmic fruits — sprouting forth, as it were — hence 'with sense-objects as their sprouts.' The supreme root, the material cause, of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been stated earlier. Now the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) of attachment, aversion, etc. produced by the fruits of action — like subsidiary roots, being intermediate causes of the engagement in <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — these extend below (from the perspective of the gods etc.) as roots, continuously extending, binding to action — action characterized as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is the binding factor (<s>anubandha</s>), arising subsequently, from whose emergence [the roots] arise — these are 'binding to action,' particularly in the world of human beings. For here in this world, the qualification for action is well known for human beings. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.2||

children.text: yas tv ayaṃ varṇitaḥ saṃsāra-vṛkṣaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> that has been described —

children.text: na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate
children.translated_text: Its form as described here is not perceived as such,

children.text: nānto na cādir na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |
children.translated_text: nor its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation;

children.text: aśvattham enaṃ su-virūḍha-mūlam
children.translated_text: having cut down this <s>Aśvattha</s> with its well-grown roots

children.text: asaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā ||BhG_15.3||
children.translated_text: with the firm weapon of non-attachment — ||<s>BhG</s> 15.3||

children.text: na rūpam asyeha yathopavarṇitaṃ tathā naiva upalabhyate, svapna-marīcy-udaka-māyā-gandharva-nagara-samatvāt | dṛṣṭa-naṣṭa-svarūpo hi sa ity ata eva nānto na paryanto niṣṭhā parisamāptir vā vidyate | tathā na cādiḥ | "ita ārabhyāyaṃ pravṛttaḥ" iti na kenacid gamyate | na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā sthitir madhyam asya na kenacid upalabhyate | aśvattham enaṃ yathoktaṃ suvirūḍha-mūlaṃ suṣṭhu virūḍhāni virohaṃ gatāni sudṛḍhāni mūlāni yasya tam enaṃ suvirūḍha-mūlam | asaṅga-śastreṇa asaṅgaḥ putra-vitta-lokaiṣaṇābhyo vyutthānaṃ tenāsaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena paramātmābhimukhya-niścaya-dṛḍhīkṛtena punaḥ punar vivekābhyāsāśma-niśitena cchitvā saṃsāra-vṛkṣaṃ sa-bījam uddhṛtya ||BhGS_15.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Its form as described is not perceived as such in this world — because it is like a dream, mirage-water, magic, or a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>. For its nature is to appear and disappear — therefore its end (<s>anta</s>), conclusion, or completion is not found. Likewise, it has no beginning (<s>ādi</s>) — no one can determine 'it commenced from this point.' Nor does it have a foundation (<s>saṃpratiṣṭhā</s>), a stable middle — no one perceives it. This <s>Aśvattha</s> as described, 'with well-grown roots' (<s>su-virūḍha-mūla</s>) — whose roots have grown well, i.e., have become very firm — this <s>Aśvattha</s> with well-grown roots; with the 'weapon of non-attachment' (<s>asaṅga-śastra</s>) — non-attachment is the withdrawal from the desires for sons, wealth, and worlds — with that weapon of non-attachment, firm (<s>dṛḍha</s>), i.e., strengthened by the firm resolve of turning toward the Supreme Self, sharpened on the whetstone of repeated practice of discrimination — having cut the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> together with its seed, having uprooted it — ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.3||

children.text: tataḥ padaṃ tat parimārgitavyaṃ
children.translated_text: Then, that state is to be sought

children.text: yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: from which, having gone, they do not return again;

children.text: tam eva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye
children.translated_text: 'I take refuge in that very primeval Person

children.text: yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī ||BhG_15.4||
children.translated_text: from whom the ancient activity has streamed forth.' ||<s>BhG</s> 15.4||

children.text: tataḥ paścāt yat padaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tat parimārgitavyam, parimārgaṇam anveṣaṇaṃ jñātavyam ity arthaḥ | yasmin pade gatāḥ praviṣṭā na nivartanti nāvartante bhūyaḥ punaḥ saṃsārāya | kathaṃ parimārgitavyam ity āha - tam eva ca yaḥ pada-śabdenokta ādyam ādau bhavam ādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye ity evaṃ parimārgitavyaṃ tac-charaṇatayā ity arthaḥ | ko 'sau puruṣaḥ ? ity ucyate - yato yasmāt puruṣāt saṃsāra-māyā-vṛkṣa-pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā niḥsṛtā aindrajālikād iva māyā | purāṇī ciraṃtanī ||BhGS_15.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Then' — thereafter — that state (<s>pada</s>), the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is to be sought (<s>parimārgitavya</s>) — seeking means investigating, i.e., it is to be known — this is the meaning. The state from which, having gone, having entered, they do not return again for <s>saṃsāra</s>. How is it to be sought? He says: 'I take refuge in' (<s>prapadye</s>) — taking refuge in — that very one who is denoted by the word 'state' (<s>pada</s>) — the primeval (<s>ādya</s>), existing from the beginning, Person (<s>puruṣa</s>) — thus [the state] is to be sought, i.e., through taking refuge in him — this is the meaning. Who is that Person? It is said: from whom — from which Person — the activity of the <s>saṃsāra</s>-<s>Māyā</s>-tree has streamed forth, like magic from a magician. 'Ancient' (<s>purāṇī</s>) — of great antiquity. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.4||

children.text: kathaṃ-bhūtās tat padaṃ gacchantīty ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] What kind of persons attain that state? This is stated:

children.text: nirmāna-mohā jita-saṅga-doṣā
children.translated_text: Free from pride and delusion, with the fault of attachment conquered,

children.text: adhyātma-nityā vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: ever devoted to the Supreme Self, with desires completely turned away,

children.text: dvandvair vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñair
children.translated_text: liberated from the dualities known as pleasure and pain —

children.text: gacchanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṃ tat ||BhG_15.5||
children.translated_text: the undeluded ones attain that imperishable state. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.5||

children.text: nirmāna-mohā mānaś ca mohaś ca māna-mohau, tau nirgatau yebhyas te nirmāna-mohā māna-moha-varjitāḥ | jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ saṅga eva doṣaḥ saṅga-doṣaḥ, jitaḥ saṅga-doṣo yais te jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ | adhyātma-nityāḥ paramātma-svarūpālocana-nityās tat-parāḥ | vinivṛtta-kāmā viśeṣato nirlepena nivṛttāḥ kāmā yeṣāṃ te vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ | yatayaḥ saṃnyāsino dvandvaiḥ priyāpriyādibhir vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñaiḥ parityaktā gacchanty amūḍhā moha-varjitāḥ padam avyayaṃ tad yathoktam ||BhGS_15.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Free from pride and delusion' (<s>nirmāna-moha</s>) — pride and delusion are <s>māna-moha</s>; those from whom these have departed are <s>nirmāna-moha</s>, i.e., devoid of pride and delusion. 'With the fault of attachment conquered' (<s>jita-saṅga-doṣa</s>) — attachment itself is the fault; those who have conquered the fault of attachment are <s>jita-saṅga-doṣa</s>. 'Ever devoted to the Supreme Self' (<s>adhyātma-nitya</s>) — constantly engaged in contemplation of the nature of the Supreme Self, devoted to that. 'With desires completely turned away' (<s>vinivṛtta-kāma</s>) — those whose desires have been completely and stainlessly turned away. Renunciants (<s>yatis</s>, <s>saṃnyāsins</s>), liberated from the dualities — pleasant and unpleasant etc. — known as pleasure and pain, freed from [these] — the undeluded, i.e., devoid of delusion — they attain that imperishable state as described. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.5||

children.text: tad eva padaṃ punar viśeṣyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That very state is further characterized:

children.text: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: That, the sun does not illuminate, nor the moon, nor fire;

children.text: yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama ||BhG_15.6||
children.translated_text: having gone to which, they do not return — that is my supreme abode. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.6||

children.text: tat dhāmeti vyavahitena dhāmnā saṃbadhyate | tad dhāma tejo-rūpaṃ padaṃ na bhāsayate sūrya ādityaḥ sarvāvabhāsana-śaktimattve 'pi sati | tathā na śaśāṅkaś candraḥ, na pāvako nāgnir api | yad dhāma vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ gatvā prāpya na nivartante, yac ca sūryādir na bhāsayate, tad dhāma padaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇor mama padam ||BhGS_15.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'That abode' (<s>dhāma</s>) — this is connected with the [syntactically] separated word 'abode.' That abode, that state of luminous nature, the sun (<s>sūrya</s>), i.e., <s>Āditya</s>, does not illuminate, even though possessing the power to illuminate everything. Likewise, neither the moon (<s>śaśāṅka</s>), nor fire (<s>pāvaka</s>). That abode, the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having gone to which, having reached which, they do not return — and which the sun and the rest do not illuminate — that is my supreme abode, the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which is mine. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.6||

children.text: nanu sarvā hi gatir āgaty-antāḥ | saṃyogāḥ viprayogāntāḥ [Mbh 11.2.3] iti hi prasiddham | katham ucyate tat dhāma gatānāṃ nāsti nivṛttiḥ ? iti | sṛṇu tatra kāraṇam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: all destinations end in return. 'Unions end in separation' [<s>Mahābhārata</s> 11.2.3] — this is well known. How then is it said that those who have gone to that abode do not return? Listen to the reason for this:

children.text: mamaivāṃśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: An eternal portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) of myself alone, having become the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) in the world of living beings,

children.text: manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛti-sthāni karṣati ||BhG_15.7||
children.translated_text: draws to itself the senses, with the mind as the sixth, which abide in <s>Prakṛti</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.7||

children.text: mamaiva param ātmano nārāyaṇasya, aṃśo bhāgo 'vayava eka-deśa ity anarthāntaraṃ jīva-loke jīvānāṃ loke saṃsāre jīva-bhūtaḥ kartā bhokteti prasiddhaḥ sanātanaś cirantanaḥ | yathā jala-sūryakaḥ sūryāṃśo jala-nimittāpāye sūryam eva gatvā na nivartate ca tenaivātmanā gacchati, evam eva | yathā ghaṭādy-upādhi-paricchinno ghaṭādy-ākāśa ākāśāṃśaḥ san ghaṭādi-nimittāpāye ākāśaṃ prāpya na nivartate | ata upapannam uktam yad gatvā na nivartante iti |
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Of myself alone — of the Supreme Self, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — a portion (<s>aṃśa</s>), a part, a segment, a fraction — [these are] synonymous. In the world of <s>jīvas</s>, i.e., in the realm of living beings, in <s>saṃsāra</s> — it has become the <s>jīva</s>, well known as agent and experiencer — eternal (<s>sanātana</s>), i.e., ancient. Just as a reflection of the sun in water, being a portion of the sun, upon the removal of the cause [i.e., the water], goes to the sun itself and does not return — and goes as that very self — just so. And just as the space delimited by the limiting adjunct of a pot etc., being a portion of space, upon the removal of the cause [i.e., the pot], reaches space and does not return. Therefore it is appropriate that it was said 'having gone to which, they do not return.'

children.text: nanu niravayavasya paramātmanaḥ kuto 'vayava eka-deśo 'ṃśaḥ iti ? sāvayavatve ca vināśa-prasaṅgo 'vayava-vibhāgāt | naiṣa doṣaḥ, avidyā-kṛtopādhi-paricchinna eka-deśo 'ṃśa iva kalpito yataḥ | darśitaś cāyam arthaḥ kṣetrādhyāye vistaraśaḥ | sa ca jīvo mad-aṃśatvena kalpitaḥ kathaṃ saṃsaraty utkrāmati ca ? ity ucyate - manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi śrotrādīni prakṛti-sthāni sva-sthāne karṇa-śaṣkuly-ādau prakṛtau sthitāni karṣati ākarṣati ||BhGS_15.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Objection: how can the partless Supreme Self have a part or a portion? And if It had parts, then destruction would follow from the separation of parts. Reply: this is not a fault, because the portion is merely imagined (<s>kalpita</s>), as a single area delimited by a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) created by <s>avidyā</s> — as if a portion. And this meaning has been shown at length in the chapter on the <s>kṣetra</s>. And how does this <s>jīva</s>, imagined as a portion of me, transmigrate and depart [from the body]? It is stated: the senses, with the mind as the sixth, beginning with hearing — abiding in <s>Prakṛti</s>, i.e., situated in their own places such as the cavity of the ear etc. — it draws to itself (<s>karṣati</s>), i.e., attracts. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.7||

children.text: kasmin kāle ? -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] At what time [does it draw them]?

children.text: śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac cāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: When the Lord [of the body] obtains a body, and also when it departs [from one],

children.text: gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt ||BhG_15.8||
children.translated_text: taking these [senses] along, it goes, as the wind [carries] fragrances from their source. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.8||

children.text: yac cāpi yadā cāpi utkrāmatīśvaro dehādi-saṃghāta-svāmī jīvaḥ, tadā karṣati [15.8] iti ślokasya dvitīya-pādo 'rtha-vaśāt prāthamyena saṃbadhyate | yadā ca pūrvasmāt śarīrāt śarīrāntaram avāpnoti tadā gṛhītvaitāni manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi saṃyāti samyak yāti gacchati | kim iva ? ity āha - vāyuḥ pavano gandhān iva āśayāt puṣpādeḥ ||BhGS_15.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'And also when' — and when — it departs (<s>utkrāmati</s>), the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), i.e., the <s>jīva</s> who is master of the aggregate of body etc. — then it draws [the senses] — the second quarter of the verse 'draws' [15.7] is connected with this verse first, as required by the meaning. And when, from the former body, it obtains another body — then, taking these senses with the mind as the sixth, it goes, i.e., proceeds. Like what? He says: as the wind (<s>vāyu</s>) [carries] fragrances from their source (<s>āśaya</s>), i.e., from a flower etc. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.8||

children.text: kāni punas tāni -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And what are those [senses]?

children.text: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell,

children.text: adhiṣṭhāya manaś cāyaṃ viṣayān upasevate ||BhG_15.9||
children.translated_text: and presiding over the mind as well — this one enjoys the sense-objects. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.9||

children.text: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca tvag-indriyaṃ rasanaṃ ghrāṇam eva ca manaś ca ṣaṣṭhaṃ pratyekam indriyeṇa saha, adhiṣṭhāya deha-stho viṣayān śabdādīn upasevate ||BhGS_15.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Hearing, sight, touch — the organ of touch (skin), taste, and smell — and the mind as the sixth — presiding over (<s>adhiṣṭhāya</s>) each sense individually, being situated in the body, it enjoys, i.e., experiences, the sense-objects such as sound etc. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.9||

children.text: evaṃ deha-gataṃ dehāt -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Thus, [the Self] situated in the body, from the body —

children.text: utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam |
children.translated_text: Whether departing, remaining, or experiencing, accompanied by the <s>guṇas</s> —

children.text: vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ ||BhG_15.10||
children.translated_text: the deluded do not perceive [it]; those with the eye of knowledge see [it]. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.10||

children.text: utkrāmantaṃ dehaṃ pūrvopāttaṃ parityajantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi dehe tiṣṭhantaṃ bhuñjānāṃ vā śabdādīṃś copalabhamānaṃ guṇānvitaṃ sukha-duḥkha-mohādyair guṇair anvitam anugataṃ saṃyuktam ity arthaḥ | evaṃ-bhūtam apy enam atyanta-darśana-gocara-prāptaṃ vimūḍhā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭa-viṣaya-bhoga-balākṛṣṭa-cetas tayānekadhā mūḍhā nānupaśyanti | aho kaṣṭaṃ vartate ity anukrośati ca bhagavān | ye tu punaḥ pramāṇa-janita-jñāna-cakṣuṣas ta enaṃ paśyanti jñāna-cakṣuṣo vivikta-dṛṣṭaya ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_15.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Departing' — leaving the previously acquired body; 'or remaining' — abiding in the body; 'or experiencing' — perceiving sounds and other [objects]; 'accompanied by the <s>guṇas</s>' — accompanied, attended, associated with the <s>guṇas</s> such as pleasure, pain, delusion, etc. — this is the meaning. Even though [the Self] of this nature has come within the reach of direct perception, the 'deluded' — those whose minds are drawn in many directions by attachment to the enjoyments of seen and unseen [objects], deluded in many ways — do not perceive [it]. Alas, how grievous this is! — thus the Lord expresses compassion. But those who possess the eye of knowledge born of the valid means of knowledge — those with the eye of knowledge, those of discriminative vision — they see [it] — this is the meaning. ||<s>BhGS</s> 15.10||

children.text: yatanto yoginaś cainaṃ paśyanty ātmany avasthitam |
children.translated_text: Striving <s>yogins</s> also see this [Self] established in the Self;

children.text: yatanto 'py akṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyanty acetasaḥ ||BhG_15.11||
children.translated_text: but those of unprepared selves, though striving, do not see this — the unintelligent ones. ||<s>BhG</s> 15.11||

children.text: yatantaḥ prayatnaṃ kurvanto yoginaś ca samāhita-cittā enaṃ prakṛtam ātmānaṃ paśyanty ayam aham asmīty upalabhanta ātmani svasyāṃ buddhāv avasthitam | yatanto 'pi śāstrādi-pramāṇair akṛtātmāno 'saṃskṛtātmānas tapasā indriya-jayena ca, duścaritād anuparatāḥ, aśānta-darpāḥ prayatnaṃ kurvanto 'pi nainaṃ paśyanty acetaso 'vivekinaḥ ||BhGS_15.11||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Those who strive — making effort — and are <s>yogins</s> with concentrated minds, they see this Self as described, perceiving 'this I am,' established in the self, in their own intellect. But those who strive even through the means of valid knowledge such as scriptures, yet whose selves are unrefined — whose selves are uncultivated — through austerity and conquest of the senses, who have not ceased from evil conduct, whose pride is unquelled, even though making effort, they do not see this [Self], being mindless, lacking discrimination. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.11 //

children.text: yat padaṃ sarvasyāvabhāsakamapy agnyādity ādikaṃ jyotiḥ nāvabhāsayate, yat prāptā ca mumukṣavaḥ punaḥ saṃsārābhimukhāḥ na nivartante, yasya ca padasya upādhi-bhedam anuvidhīyamānāḥ jīvāḥ - ghaṭākāśādayaḥ iva ākāśasya - aṃśāḥ, tasya padasya sarvātmatvaṃ sarvavyavahārāspadatvaṃ ca vivakṣuś caturbhiḥ ślokaiḥ vibhūtisaṃkṣepamāha bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] That state which, though it illumines everything, no light such as fire or the sun illumines; having attained which, seekers of liberation do not turn back again toward <s>saṃsāra</s>; and of which state the <s>jīvas</s> — following the distinctions of limiting adjuncts, like the space in a pot and so forth [are portions] of space — are parts; wishing to express the nature of that state as the Self of all and the ground of all transactions, the Blessed Lord speaks in four verses a summary of [His] glories —

children.text: yad āditya-gataṃ tejo jagad bhāsayate 'khilam |
children.translated_text: That light which, abiding in the sun, illumines the entire world,

children.text: yac candramasi yac cāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam ||BhG_15.12||
children.translated_text: which is in the moon, and which is in fire — know that light to be Mine. // <s>BhG</s> 15.12 //

children.text: yat āditya-gatam ādityāśrayam | kiṃ tat ? tejo dīptiḥ prakāśo jagad bhāsayate prakāśayaty akhilaṃ samastam | yac candramasi śaśabhṛti tejo 'vabhāsakaṃ vartate, yac cāgnau hutavahe, tat tejo viddhi vijānīhi māmakaṃ madīyaṃ mama viṣṇos taj jyotiḥ | athavā, āditya-gataṃ tejaś caitanyātmakaṃ jyotir yac candramasi, yac cāgnau vartate tat tejo viddhi māmakaṃ madīyaṃ mama viṣṇos taj jyotiḥ |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] That which abides in the sun — residing in the sun. What is it? Light — brilliance, radiance — that illumines, illuminates the world, the entirety, the whole. That light which is in the moon — in the bearer of the hare [i.e. the moon] — which is illuminating, and which is in fire — in the oblation-eater — know that light, understand it to be Mine, belonging to Me, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that is [My] radiance. Or alternatively, the light abiding in the sun — the luminosity of the nature of consciousness — that which is in the moon, and which is in fire, know that light to be Mine, belonging to Me, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; that is [My] radiance.

children.text: nanu sthāvareṣu jaṅgameṣu ca tat samānaṃ caitanyātmakaṃ jyotiḥ | tatra katham idaṃ viśeṣaṇam - yad āditya-gatam ity ādi | naiṣa doṣaḥ, sattvādhikyād vistaratvopapatteḥ | ādity-ādiṣu hi sattvam atyanta-prakāśam atyanta-bhāsvaram | atas tatraivāvistaraṃ jyotir iti tad viśiṣyate, na tu tatraiva tad adhikam iti | yathā hi loke tulye 'pi mukha-saṃsthāne na kāṣṭha-kuḍyādau mukham āvirbhavati, ādarśādau tu svacche svacchatare ca tāratamyenāvirbhavati, tadvat ||BhGS_15.12||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Objection: In stationary and moving beings alike, that light of the nature of consciousness is the same. How then is this specification — 'that which abides in the sun' and so forth? This is not a fault, because the expansion [of light] is justified due to the predominance of <s>sattva</s>. In the sun and others, <s>sattva</s> is exceedingly luminous, exceedingly radiant. Therefore, the light is [as if] expanded there alone — thus it is distinguished there, not that there is more of it there. Just as in the world, though the facial form is the same, a face does not appear in wood, a wall, and such, but in a mirror and similar [surfaces] — in what is clear and in what is clearer — it appears in varying degrees; so too is it here. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.12 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā |
children.translated_text: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings by [My] power,

children.text: puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ ||BhG_15.13||
children.translated_text: and I nourish all plants, having become <s>Soma</s>, full of sap. // <s>BhG</s> 15.13 //

children.text: gāṃ pṛthivīm āviśya praviśya dhārayāmi bhūtāni jagad aham ojasā balena | yad balaṃ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam aiśvaraṃ rūpaṃ jagad-vidhāraṇāya pṛthivyām praviṣṭaṃ yena pṛthivī gurvī nādhaḥ patati na vidīryate ca | tathā ca mantra-varṇaḥ - yena dyaur ugrā pṛthivī ca dṛḍhā [TaittS 4.1.8] iti, sa dādhāra pṛthivīm [Ṛk 8.7.3.1] ity ādiś ca | ato gām āviśya ca bhūtāni carācarāṇi dhārayāmīti yuktam uktam | kiṃ ca, pṛthivyāṃ jātā oṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ vrīhi-yavādyāḥ puṣṇāmi puṣṭi-matīḥ rasa-svādumatī ca karomi somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ somaḥ san rasātmakaḥ rasa-svabhāvaḥ | sarva-rasānām ākaraḥ somaḥ | sa hi sarva-rasātmakaḥ sarvāḥ oṣadhīḥ svātma-rasān anupraveśayan puṣṇāti ||BhGS_15.13||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Entering the earth — having entered the earth, I sustain the beings, the world, by power, by strength. That strength which is free from desire and attachment, the sovereign form [of power] that entered the earth for sustaining the world — by which the earth, being heavy, does not fall downward and does not disintegrate. And thus the Vedic text says: 'By whom the formidable heaven and earth are made firm' [<s>TaittS</s> 4.1.8], and 'He upheld the earth' [<s>Ṛk</s> 8.7.3.1], and so forth. Therefore, it is fitting to say 'entering the earth, I sustain beings, both moving and stationary.' And moreover, I nourish all the plants born on the earth — rice, barley, and the rest — making them full of nourishment and sweet with sap, having become <s>Soma</s>, full of sap — being <s>Soma</s>, whose nature is sap. <s>Soma</s> is the source of all flavors. For he, being of the nature of all flavors, nourishes all plants by infusing them with his own sap. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.13 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having become <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire, I dwell in the body of living beings,

children.text: prāṇāpāna-samāyuktaḥ pacāmy annaṃ catur-vidham ||BhG_15.14||
children.translated_text: and, united with <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, I digest the four kinds of food. // <s>BhG</s> 15.14 //

children.text: aham eva vai vaiśvānara udara-stho 'gnir bhūtvā - ayam agnir vaiśvānaro yo 'yam antaḥ puruṣe yenedam annaṃ pacyate yad idam adyate [BAU 5.9.1] ity ādi-śruteḥ | vaiśvānaraḥ san prāṇināṃ prāṇavatāṃ deham āśritaḥ praviṣṭaḥ prāṇāpāna-samāyuktaḥ prāṇāpānābhyāṃ samāyuktaḥ saṃyuktaḥ pacāmi paṅkti karomy annam aśanaṃ caturvidhaṃ catuṣprakāraṃ bhojyaṃ bhakṣyaṃ coṣyaṃ lehyaṃ ca | bhoktā vai vānaro 'gniḥ | agner bhojyam annaṃ somaḥ | tad etad ubhayam agnīṣomau sarvam iti paśyato 'nna-doṣa-lepo na bhavati ||BhGS_15.14||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] I indeed, having become <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the fire dwelling in the stomach — as the <s>śruti</s> says: 'This fire is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which is within a person, by which this food is digested, that which one eats' [<s>BAU</s> 5.9.1], and so forth. Being <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, dwelling in the body of living beings — of those possessing life-breath — united with <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, conjoined with <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, I digest, I cook the food — what is eaten — of four kinds, of four varieties: that which is chewed, that which is swallowed, that which is sucked, and that which is licked. The eater indeed is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire. The food of fire is <s>Soma</s>. These two together — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> — are everything; for one who sees thus, there is no taint from defects in food. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.14 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭo
children.translated_text: And I am seated in the hearts of all;

children.text: mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal.

children.text: vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo
children.translated_text: I alone am that which is to be known by all the <s>Vedas</s>;

children.text: vedānta-kṛd veda-vid eva cāham ||BhG_15.15||
children.translated_text: I am indeed the author of <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 15.15 //

children.text: sarvasya ca prāṇi-jātasyāham ātmā san hṛdi buddhau saṃniviṣṭaḥ | ato matta ātmanaḥ sarva-prāṇināṃ smṛtir jñānaṃ tad-apohanaṃ cāpagamanaṃ ca | yeṣāṃ yathā puṇya-karmaṇāṃ puṇya-karmānurodhena jñāna-smṛtī bhavataḥ, tathā pāpa-karmaṇāṃ pāpa-karmānurūpeṇa smṛti-jñānayor apohanaṃ cāpāyanam apagamanaṃ ca | vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva paramātmā vedyo veditavyaḥ | vedānta-kṛd vedāntārtha-saṃpradāya-kṛd ity arthaḥ, veda-vid vedārtha-vid eva cāham ||BhGS_15.15||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] And of all living beings, I — being the Self — am seated in the heart, in the intellect. Therefore, from Me, the Self, come memory and knowledge for all living beings, as well as their removal — their departure, their going away. For those of meritorious deeds, memory and knowledge arise in accordance with their meritorious actions; similarly, for those of sinful deeds, there is the removal — the taking away, the departure — of memory and knowledge in accordance with their sinful actions. And I alone, the Supreme Self, am to be known by all the <s>Vedas</s> — am to be realized. I am the author of <s>Vedānta</s> — meaning the one who established the tradition of the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>. And I am indeed the knower of the <s>Vedas</s> — the one who knows the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.15 //

children.text: bhagavata īśvarasya nārāyaṇākhyasya vibhūti-saṃkṣepa ukto viśiṣṭopādhi-kṛto yad āditya-gataṃ tejaḥ [Gītā 15.12] ity ādinā | athādhunā tasyaiva kṣarākṣaropādhi-pravibhaktatayā nirupādhikasya kevalasya tattva-svarūpa-nirdidhārayiṣayottara-ślokā ārabhyante | tatra sarvam evātītān āgatān antarādhyāyārtha-jātaṃ tridhā rāśīkṛtya āha -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The summary of the glories of the Blessed Lord, the sovereign <s>Īśvara</s> named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, conditioned by distinguished limiting adjuncts, has been stated beginning with 'that light which abides in the sun' [<s>Gītā</s> 15.12] and so forth. Now, with the desire to ascertain the true nature of that very [Lord] as unconditioned and absolute, by analyzing [Him] as distinct from the two limiting adjuncts of the perishable and the imperishable, the following verses are begun. There, having grouped together the entire subject matter of the preceding and following chapters into three categories, He says —

children.text: dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca |
children.translated_text: There are these two <s>puruṣas</s> (persons) in the world — the perishable and the imperishable;

children.text: kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate ||BhG_15.16||
children.translated_text: the perishable is all beings; the immutable is called the imperishable. // <s>BhG</s> 15.16 //

children.text: dvāv imau pṛthag-rāśī-kṛtau puruṣāv ity ucyete loke saṃsāre - kṣaraś ca kṣaratīti kṣaro vināśī ity eko rāśiḥ | aparaḥ puruṣo 'kṣaras tad-viparītaḥ, bhagavato māyā-śaktiḥ, kṣarākhyasya puruṣasya utpatti-bījam aneka-saṃsāri-jantu-kāma-karmādi-saṃskārāśraya akṣaraḥ puruṣa ucyate | kau tau puruṣau ? ity āha svayam eva bhagavān - kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni, samastaṃ vikāra-jātam ity arthaḥ | kūṭāsthaḥ kūṭāḥ rāśī rāśir iva sthitaḥ | athavā, kūṭā māyā vacanā jihmatā kuṭilatā iti paryāyāḥ | aneka-māyā-vacanādi-prakāreṇa sthitaḥ kūṭāsthaḥ | saṃsāra-bījānantyāt, na kṣaratīty akṣara ucyate ||BhGS_15.16||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] These two, classified into separate groups, are called two <s>puruṣas</s> in the world, in <s>saṃsāra</s> — the perishable, that which perishes, the destructible — this is one group. The other <s>puruṣa</s> is the imperishable, the opposite of that — the <s>māyā</s>-power of the Blessed Lord, the seed of origination of the <s>puruṣa</s> called the perishable, the substratum of the latent impressions of desire, action, and so forth of the many beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is called the imperishable <s>puruṣa</s>. What are these two <s>puruṣas</s>? The Blessed Lord Himself says — the perishable is all beings, meaning the entire collection of modifications. The immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) — standing like a heap upon heap. Or alternatively, <s>kūṭa</s> means <s>māyā</s>, deception, crookedness, and curvedness — these are synonyms. That which abides through many forms of <s>māyā</s>, deception, and so forth is <s>kūṭastha</s>. Because the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s> is inexhaustible, it does not perish — hence it is called the imperishable. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.16 //

children.text: ābhyāṃ kṣarākṣarābhyām anyo vilakṣaṇaḥ kṣarākṣaropādhi-dvaya-doṣeṇāspṛṣṭaḥ nitya-śuddha-buddham ukta-svabhāvaḥ -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Different from these two — the perishable and the imperishable — distinct, untouched by the defects of the two limiting adjuncts of the perishable and the imperishable, whose nature has been described as eternally pure and awakened —

children.text: uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: But the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is another, called the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self),

children.text: yo loka-trayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ ||BhG_15.17||
children.translated_text: who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them — the imperishable Lord. // <s>BhG</s> 15.17 //

children.text: uttama utkṛṣṭatamaḥ puruṣas tv anyo 'tyanta-vilakṣaṇa ābhyāṃ paramātmeti paramaś cāsau dehādy-avidyā-kṛtātmabhyaḥ, ātmaś ca sarva-bhūtānāṃ pratyak-cetanaḥ, ity ataḥ paramātmety udāhṛta ukto vedānteṣu | sa eva viśiṣyate yo loka-trayaṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svar-ākhyaṃ svakīyayā caitanya-bala-śaktyā āviśya praviśya bibharti svarūpa-sad-bhāva-mātreṇa bibharti dhārayati | avyayo nāsya vyayo vidyata ity avyayaḥ | kaḥ ? īśvaraḥ sarvajño nārāyaṇākhya īśana-śīlaḥ ||BhGS_15.17||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The Supreme — the most exalted — <s>Puruṣa</s>, however, is another, utterly distinct from these two. [He is called] <s>Paramātman</s> — supreme among the selves created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) such as the body and so forth, and the Self, the innermost consciousness of all beings — therefore He is called <s>Paramātman</s>, spoken of thus in the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. He alone is distinguished — He who, pervading the three worlds known as <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>svaḥ</s>, by His own power of consciousness and strength, having entered them, sustains — upholds, supports — merely by the existence of His own true nature. Imperishable — there is no diminution of Him, hence imperishable. Who? The Lord — the omniscient one named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose nature is sovereignty. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.17 //

children.text: yathā-vyākhyātasyeśvarasya puruṣottama ity etat nāma prasiddham | tasya nāma-nirvacana-prasiddhayārthavattvaṃ nāmno darśayan niratiśayo 'ham īśvara ity ātmānaṃ darśayati bhagavān -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] The name <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person) is well-known for the Lord as explained above. Showing the meaningfulness of the name through the well-known etymological derivation, the Blessed Lord reveals Himself as the unsurpassed Lord —

children.text: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable,

children.text: ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ||BhG_15.18||
children.translated_text: therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). // <s>BhG</s> 15.18 //

children.text: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'haṃ saṃsāra-māyā-vṛkṣam aśvatthākhyam atikrānto 'ham akṣarād api saṃsāra-māyā-rūpa-vṛkṣa-bīja-bhūtād api cottama utkṛṣṭatamaḥ ūrdhvatamo vā | atas tābhyāṃ kṣarākṣarābhyām uttamatvād asmi loke vede ca prathitaḥ prakhyātaḥ | puruṣottama ity evaṃ māṃ bhakta-janā viduḥ | kavayaḥ kāvyādiṣu cedaṃ nāma nibadhnanti | puruṣottama ity anenābhidhānenābhigṛṇanti ||BhGS_15.18||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Since I transcend the perishable — I have gone beyond the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>māyā</s> called the <s>Aśvattha</s> — and am even higher than the imperishable, which is the seed of the tree in the form of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>māyā</s> — most exalted, or most elevated. Therefore, being superior to these two — the perishable and the imperishable — I am celebrated, renowned, in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s>. Thus do the devotees know Me. And poets employ this name in their poems and other works. They invoke [Me] by this designation <s>Puruṣottama</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.18 //

children.text: athedānīṃ yathā-niruktam ātmānaṃ yo veda, tasyedaṃ phalam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Now, the fruit for one who knows the Self as etymologically explained is stated —

children.text: yo mām evam asaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam |
children.translated_text: He who, undeluded, thus knows Me as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person),

children.text: sa sarva-vid bhajati māṃ sarva-bhāvena bhārata ||BhG_15.19||
children.translated_text: he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 15.19 //

children.text: yo mām īśvaraṃ yathokta-viśeṣaṇam evaṃ yathoktena prakāreṇa asaṃmūḍhaḥ saṃmoha-varjitaḥ san jānāty ayam aham asmīti puruṣottamaṃ, sa sarva-vit sarvātmanā sarvaṃ vettīti sarvajñaḥ sarva-bhūta-sthaṃ bhajati māṃ sarva-bhāvena sarvātmatayā he bhārata ||BhGS_15.19||
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] He who [knows] Me, the Lord, with the characteristics as described, in the manner stated, being undeluded — free from delusion — knows 'this I am' as <s>Puruṣottama</s>, he is the knower of all — knowing everything through knowing the Self of all, he is omniscient — and he worships Me, who abides in all beings, with his whole being — with the sense of being the Self of all, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.19 //

children.text: asmin adhyāye bhagavat-tattva-jñānaṃ mokṣa-phalam uktvā, atha idānīṃ tat stauti -
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] Having stated in this chapter that knowledge of the true nature of the Blessed Lord has liberation as its fruit, now He praises that [knowledge] —

children.text: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstram idam uktaṃ mayānagha |
children.translated_text: Thus this most secret teaching has been declared by Me, O sinless one;

children.text: etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛta-kṛtyaś ca bhārata ||BhG_15.20||
children.translated_text: understanding this, one becomes wise and has fulfilled all duties, O <s>Bhārata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 15.20 //

children.text:
iti etad guhyatamaṃ gopyatamam, atyanta-rahasyaṃ ity etat | kiṃ tat ? śāstram | yady api gītākhyaṃ samastam śāstram ucyate, tathāpy ayam evādhyāya iha śāstram ity ucyate stuty-arthaṃ prakaraṇāt | sarvo hi gītā-śāstrārtho 'smin adhyāye samāsena uktaḥ | na kevalaṃ gītā-śāstrārtha eva, kiṃtu sarvaś ca vedārtha iha parisamāptaḥ | yas taṃ veda sa veda-vit [Gītā 15.1] vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ [Gītā 15.15] iti coktam | idam uktaṃ kathitaṃ mayā he 'nagha apāpa ! etac chāstraṃ yathā-darśitārthaṃ buddhvā buddhimān syāt bhavet nānyathā | kṛta-kṛtyaś ca bhārata kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ kartavyaṃ yena sa kṛta-kṛtyaḥ | viśiṣṭa-janma-prasūtena brāhmaṇena yat kartavyaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhagavat-tattve vidite kṛtaṃ bhaved ity arthaḥ | na cānyathā kartavyaṃ parisamāpyate kasyacid ity abhiprāyaḥ | sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ
pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate [Gītā 4.33] iti coktam |
children.translated_text: [Śaṅkara's commentary:] 'Thus' — this most secret, most to be guarded, the utmost mystery — this is it. What is it? The teaching. Although the entire teaching called the <s>Gītā</s> is referred to as a scripture, nevertheless this chapter alone is here called 'the teaching' for the purpose of praise, due to the context. For the entire meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> scripture has been stated in summary in this chapter. Not only the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> scripture, but indeed the entire meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> is brought to completion here — as it was said: 'He who knows that is the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 15.1] and 'I alone am to be known by all the <s>Vedas</s>' [<s>Gītā</s> 15.15]. 'This has been declared, spoken by Me, O sinless one!' Understanding this teaching according to its demonstrated meaning, one would become wise — not otherwise. 'And one who has fulfilled all duties, O <s>Bhārata</s>' — one whose duty, what is to be done, has been accomplished is <s>kṛta-kṛtya</s>. For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> born of distinguished birth, all that is to be done becomes accomplished when the truth of the Blessed Lord is known — this is the meaning. And no one's duties are brought to completion otherwise — this is the purport. As it was also said: 'All action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge' [<s>Gītā</s> 4.33].

children.text: etad dhi janma-sāmagryaṃ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: For this is the fulfillment of birth, especially for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: prāpyaitat kṛta-kṛtyo hi dvijo bhavati nānyathā || [Manu 12.93]
children.translated_text: having attained this, the twice-born becomes one who has accomplished all duties — not otherwise. // [<s>Manu</s> 12.93] //

children.text: iti ca mānavaṃ vacanam | yataḥ etat paramārthatattvaṃ mattaḥ śrutavān asi, ataḥ kṛtārthas tvaṃ bhārateti ||BhGS_15.20||
children.translated_text: Thus is the statement from <s>Manu</s>. Since you have heard this ultimate truth from Me, therefore you are one who has fulfilled [his] purpose, O scion of <s>Bharata</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 15.20 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bhāṣya</s> on the blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the most exalted wandering monk (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s>),

children.text: pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [this is] the fifteenth chapter.

children.text: BhG 16
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 16

children.text:
atha daivāsura-sampad-vibhāga-yogo nāma
ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now begins the sixteenth chapter, named the Yoga of the Division of Divine and Demoniac Endowments (<s>Daivāsura-sampad-vibhāga-yoga</s>).

children.text: (śrī-śaṅkarācārya-bhagavat-pāda-kṛta-bhāṣyam)
children.translated_text: (Commentary composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkarācārya Bhagavatpāda</s>)

children.text: daivī āsurī rākṣasī ceti prāṇiṇāṃ prakṛtayo navame 'dhyāye sūcitāḥ | tāsāṃ vistareṇa pradarśanāya abhayaṃ sattva-saṃśuddhir ity ādir adhyāyaḥ ārabhyate | tatra saṃsāra-mokṣāya daivī prakṛtiḥ, nibandhāyāsurī rākṣasī ceti daivyā ādānāya pradarśanaṃ kriyate | itarayoḥ parivarjanāya ca śrī-bhagavān uvāca -
children.translated_text: The divine (<s>daivī</s>), demoniac (<s>āsurī</s>), and fiendish (<s>rākṣasī</s>) natures of living beings were indicated in the ninth chapter. For the purpose of displaying them in detail, the chapter beginning with 'fearlessness, purity of <s>sattva</s>' etc. is commenced. Therein, the divine nature is for liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>, while the demoniac and fiendish are for bondage — thus the display is made for the adoption of the divine [nature] and for the rejection of the other two. The Blessed Lord said —

children.text: abhayaṃ sattva-saṃśuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: Fearlessness, purity of <s>sattva</s> (inner being), steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge,

children.text: dānaṃ damaś ca yajñaś ca svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam ||BhG_16.1||
children.translated_text: charity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, uprightness — // <s>BhG</s> 16.1 //

children.text: abhayam abhīrutā | sattva-saṃśuddhiḥ sattvasyāntaḥ-karaṇasya saṃśuddhiḥ | saṃvyavahāreṣu para-vañcanā-māyānṛtādi-parivarjanaṃ śuddha-sattva-bhāvena vyavahāra ity arthaḥ | jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitir jñānaṃ śāstrata ācāryataś ca ātmādi-padārthānām avagamaḥ | avagatānām indriyādy-upasaṃhāreṇaikāgratayā svātma-saṃvedyatāpādanaṃ yogaḥ | tayor jñāna-yogayor vyāvasthitiḥ vyavasthānaṃ tan-niṣṭhatā | eṣā pradhānā daivī sāttvikī socyate | dānaṃ yathā-śakti saṃvibhāgo 'nnādīnām | damaś ca bāhya-karaṇānām upaśamaḥ | antaḥ-karaṇasyopaśamaṃ śāntiṃ vakṣyati | yajñaś ca śrauto 'gnihotrādiḥ | smārtaś ca deva-yajñādiḥ | svādhyāya ṛg-vedādyadhyayanam adṛṣṭārtham | tapo vakṣyamāṇaṃ śārīrādi | ārjavam ṛjutvaṃ sarvadā ||BhGS_16.1||
children.translated_text: Fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>) is absence of fear. Purity of <s>sattva</s> (<s>sattva-saṃśuddhi</s>) is purity of the inner organ (<s>antaḥ-karaṇa</s>). In worldly dealings, the avoidance of deceiving others, of trickery, falsehood, and the like — conducting oneself in a state of pure <s>sattva</s> — this is the meaning. Steadfastness in the yoga of knowledge (<s>jñāna-yoga-vyavasthiti</s>) — knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the comprehension of entities such as the Self etc. from scripture and from a teacher. <s>Yoga</s> is the bringing of these comprehended [truths] to direct self-experience through withdrawal of the senses and one-pointedness. Steadfastness in these two, knowledge and <s>yoga</s>, means being established in them, being devoted to them. This is proclaimed as the primary divine, <s>sāttvic</s> [endowment]. Charity (<s>dāna</s>) is sharing food and the like according to one's ability. Self-restraint (<s>dama</s>) is the quieting of the external sense-organs. The quieting of the internal organ, [i.e.,] tranquility (<s>śānti</s>), will be stated [later]. Sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) includes the Vedic (<s>śrauta</s>) [rites] such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> etc., and the traditional (<s>smārta</s>) [rites] such as worship of the gods etc. Study of scriptures (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is the study of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> and others for the sake of unseen merit. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the bodily and other [austerities] to be described later. Uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>) is straightforwardness at all times. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.1 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ahiṃsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śāntir apaiśunam |
children.translated_text: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, tranquility, absence of calumny,

children.text: dayā bhūteṣv aloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam ||BhG_16.2||
children.translated_text: compassion toward beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness — // <s>BhG</s> 16.2 //

children.text: ahiṃsāhiṃsanaṃ prāṇināṃ pīḍā-varjanam | satyam apriyānṛta-varjitaṃ yathā-bhūtārtha-vacanam | akrodhaḥ parair ākruṣṭasyābhihatasya vā prāptasya krodhasya upaśamanam | tyāgaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ, pūrvaṃ dānasyoktatvāt | śāntir antaḥkaraṇasyopaśamaḥ | apaiśunam apiśunatā | parasmai para-randhra-prakaṭī-karaṇaṃ paiśunam, tad-abhāvo 'paiśunam | dayā kṛpā bhūteṣu duḥkhiteṣu | aloluptvam indriyāṇāṃ viṣaya-saṃnidhāv avikriyā | mārdavaṃ mṛdutākrauryam | hrīr lajjā | acāpalam asati prayojane vāk-pāṇi-pādādīnām avyāpārayitṛtvam ||BhGS_16.2||
children.translated_text: Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is not injuring, [i.e.,] the avoidance of causing pain to living beings. Truthfulness (<s>satya</s>) is speaking of things as they are, free from what is unpleasant and false. Absence of anger (<s>akrodha</s>) is the calming of anger that has arisen when one is abused or struck by others. Renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) is <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (formal renunciation), since charity (<s>dāna</s>) has already been mentioned earlier. Tranquility (<s>śānti</s>) is the quieting of the internal organ. Absence of calumny (<s>apaiśuna</s>) is the absence of malicious gossip; revealing another's faults to a third person is calumny (<s>paiśuna</s>), and its absence is <s>apaiśuna</s>. Compassion (<s>dayā</s>) is pity toward beings who are suffering. Non-covetousness (<s>aloluptva</s>) is the non-disturbance of the senses in the proximity of sense-objects. Gentleness (<s>mārdava</s>) is softness, absence of cruelty. Modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is shame. Absence of fickleness (<s>acāpala</s>) is not engaging the speech, hands, feet, and the like without purpose. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.2 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adroho nātimānitā |
children.translated_text: Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of malice, absence of excessive pride —

children.text: bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijātasya bhārata ||BhG_16.3||
children.translated_text: these belong to one born to the divine endowment, O scion of <s>Bharata</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 16.3 //

children.text:
tejaḥ prāgalbhyaṃ na tvag-gatā dīptiḥ | kṣamā ākruṣṭasya tāḍitasya vāntar-vikriyānutpattiḥ | utpannāyāṃ vikriyāyām praaśamanam akrodha ity avocāma | itthaṃ kṣamāyā akrodhasya ca viśeṣaḥ | dhṛtir dehendriyeṣv avasādaṃ prāpteṣu tasya pratiṣedhako 'ntaḥ-karaṇa-vṛtti-viśeṣaḥ | yenottambhitāni karaṇāni dehaś ca nāvasīdanti | śaucaṃ dvi-vidhaṃ mṛj-jala-kṛtaṃ bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ ca mano-buddhayor nairmalyaṃ māyā-rāgādi-kāluṣyābhāvaḥ | evaṃ dvi-vidhaṃ śaucam | adrohaḥ para-jighāṃsābhāvo 'hiṃsanam | nātimānitā atyarthaṃ māno 'timānaḥ, sa yasya vidyate so 'timānī | tad-bhāvo 'timānitā | tad-abhāvo nātimānitā ātmanaḥ pūjyatātiśaya-bhāvanābhāva ity arthaḥ | bhavanty abhayādīni etad-antāni saṃpadam abhijātasya | kiṃ-viśiṣṭaṃ saṃpadam
? daivīṃ devānāṃ yā saṃpat tām abhilakṣya jātasya deva-vibhūty-arhasya bhāvi-kalyāṇasyety arthaḥ | he bhārata ! ||BhGS_16.3||
children.translated_text: Vigor (<s>tejas</s>) is boldness, not the radiance of the skin. Forgiveness (<s>kṣamā</s>) is the non-arising of inner disturbance when abused or struck. When such disturbance has arisen and is then calmed, that was called 'absence of anger' (<s>akrodha</s>) — we have stated this. Thus is the distinction between forgiveness and absence of anger. Fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) is that particular modification of the inner organ which counteracts the dejection arising in the body and senses, by which the organs and the body, being sustained, do not sink down. Purity (<s>śauca</s>) is of two kinds: external, produced by earth and water; and internal, the cleanliness of mind and intellect, [meaning] the absence of the impurity of <s>māyā</s>, attachment, and the like. Thus purity is twofold. Absence of malice (<s>adroha</s>) is the absence of desire to harm others, [i.e.,] non-violence. Absence of excessive pride (<s>nātimānitā</s>) — excessive self-regard is <s>atimāna</s>; one who possesses it is <s>atimānī</s>; its state is <s>atimānitā</s>; its absence is <s>nātimānitā</s> — meaning the absence of considering oneself supremely worthy of honor. [These qualities] from fearlessness to this — belong to the endowment. Of what kind of endowment? The divine (<s>daivī</s>) — the endowment belonging to the gods; one born in view of that, one who is fit for divine glory and destined for future welfare — this is the meaning. O scion of <s>Bharata</s>! // <s>BhGS</s> 16.3 //

children.text: athedānīṃ āsurī saṃpad ucyate -
children.translated_text: Now the demoniac endowment is stated —

children.text: dambho darpo 'timānaś ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Ostentation, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness,

children.text: ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha saṃpadam āsurīm ||BhG_16.4||
children.translated_text: and ignorance — [these belong to] one born to the demoniac endowment, O <s>Pārtha</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 16.4 //

children.text: dambho dharma-dhvajitvam | darpo vidyā-dhana-svajanādi-nimitta utsekaḥ | atimānaḥ pūrvoktaḥ | krodhaś ca | pāruṣyam eva ca paruṣa-vacanam | yathā kāṇam cakṣuṣmān, virūpaṃ rūpavān, hīnābhijanam uttamābhijana ity ādi | ajñānaṃ cāviveka-jñānaṃ kartavyākartavyādi-viṣaya-mithyā-pratyayaḥ | abhijātasya pārtha | kim-abhijātasyety āha - saṃpadam āsurīm asurāṇāṃ saṃpat āsurī tām abhijātasya ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_16.4||
children.translated_text: Ostentation (<s>dambha</s>) is making a show of righteousness. Arrogance (<s>darpa</s>) is the elation caused by learning, wealth, kinsmen, and the like. Excessive pride (<s>atimāna</s>) is as previously described. And anger (<s>krodha</s>). Harshness (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is rough speech — such as [calling] the one-eyed 'one-eyed' by those who can see, the deformed 'deformed' by the beautiful, and the low-born 'low-born' by those of high birth, and so on. And ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is knowledge devoid of discrimination — false judgment regarding what should and should not be done, etc. [These belong to] one born to, O <s>Pārtha</s> — born to what? — the demoniac endowment; that which belongs to the <s>asuras</s> is <s>āsurī</s>, and [he is] born in view of that — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.4 //

children.text: anayoḥ saṃpadoḥ kāryam ucyate -
children.translated_text: The consequence of these two endowments is stated —

children.text: daivī saṃpad vimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
children.translated_text: The divine endowment is deemed [to lead] to liberation; the demoniac, to bondage.

children.text: mā śucaḥ saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijāto 'si pāṇḍava ||BhG_16.5||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve — you are born to the divine endowment, O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 16.5 //

children.text: daivī saṃpat yā sā vimokṣāya saṃsāra-bandhanāt | nibandhāya niyato bandho nibandhas tad-artham āsurī saṃpat matā abhipretā | tathā rākṣasī ca | tatraivam ukte saty ar junasyāntar-gataṃ bhāvam kim aham āsura-saṃpad-yuktaḥ ? kiṃ vā daiva-saṃpad-yuktaḥ ? ity evam ālocanā-rūpam ālakṣya āha bhagavān - mā śucaḥ śokaṃ mā kārṣīḥ | saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijāto 'sy abhilakṣya jāto 'si | bhāvi-kalyāṇas tvam asīty arthaḥ | he pāṇḍāva ||BhGS_16.5||
children.translated_text: The divine endowment — that is for liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>), [liberation] from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For bondage (<s>nibandha</s>) — a fixed, definite bondage is <s>nibandha</s>; for that purpose is the demoniac endowment, [this is] the opinion. And likewise the fiendish (<s>rākṣasī</s>) [endowment]. Thereupon, having thus spoken, perceiving <s>Arjuna's</s> inner thought — 'Am I endowed with the demoniac disposition? Or am I endowed with the divine disposition?' — an inquiry of this nature — the Blessed Lord said: 'Do not grieve' — do not sorrow. You are born to the divine endowment — you are born in view of it; you are destined for future welfare — this is the meaning. O son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>! // <s>BhGS</s> 16.5 //

children.text: dvau bhūta-sargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca |
children.translated_text: There are two types of created beings in this world — the divine and the demoniac.

children.text: daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu ||BhG_16.6||
children.translated_text: The divine has been declared at length; hear from Me about the demoniac, O <s>Pārtha</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 16.6 //

children.text: dvau dvi-saṃkhyākau bhūta-sargau bhūtānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ sargau sṛṣṭī bhūta-sargau sṛjyeteti sargau bhūtāny eva sṛjyamānāni daivāsura-saṃpad-dvaya-yuktānīti dvau bhūta-sargāv ity ucyate | dvayā ha vai prājāpatyā devāś cāsurā ca [BAU 1.3.1] iti śruteḥ | loke 'smin, saṃsāra ity arthaḥ | sarveṣāṃ dvaividhyopapatteḥ | kau tau bhūta-sargau ? ity ucyate - prakṛtāv eva daiva āsura eva ca | uktayor eva punar anuvāde prayojanam āha - daivo bhūta-sargo 'bhayaṃ sattva-saṃśuddhir ity ādinā vistaraśo vistara-prakāraiḥ proktaḥ kathitaḥ, na tu āsuro vistaraśaḥ | atas tat-parivarjanārtham āsuraṃ pārtha me mama vacanād ucyamānaṃ vistaraśaḥ sṛṇu avadhāraya ||BhGS_16.6||
children.translated_text: Two — twofold in number — types of created beings (<s>bhūta-sarga</s>): the creations of beings, of humans; 'creations' because [beings] are created — beings themselves, being created, endowed with the two types of divine and demoniac endowments — thus 'two types of created beings' is said. As per the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Two indeed are the offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s> — gods and demons' [<s>BAU</s> 1.3.1]. In this world — meaning in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Because the twofold division applies to all [beings]. What are these two types of created beings? — it is said: [they are] the divine and the demoniac, as already described. Having mentioned both again, [<s>Śaṅkara</s>] states the purpose of the repetition: the divine creation has been declared at length, in detail, by the passage beginning with 'fearlessness, purity of <s>sattva</s>' — but not the demoniac at length. Therefore, for the purpose of its avoidance, hear the demoniac [account] at length from Me — from My words being spoken — O <s>Pārtha</s>, comprehend [it]. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.6 //

children.text: ā adhyāya-parisamāpter āsurī saṃpat prāṇi-viśeṣaṇatvena pradarśyate, pratyakṣī-karaṇena ca śakyate tasyāḥ parivarjanaṃ kartum iti -
children.translated_text: Up to the end of the chapter, the demoniac endowment is displayed as characterizing [certain] types of beings, and through direct observation, its avoidance can be accomplished — thus:

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidur āsurāḥ |
children.translated_text: Persons of demoniac nature know neither activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) nor cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>);

children.text: na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate ||BhG_16.7||
children.translated_text: neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truth is found in them. // <s>BhG</s> 16.7 //

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca pravartanaṃ yasmin puruṣārtha-sādhane kartavye pravṛttis tām, nivṛttiṃ ca etad-viparītāṃ yasmāt anartha-hetoḥ nivartitavyaṃ sā nivṛttis tāṃ ca, janā āsurā na vidur na jānanti | na kevalaṃ pravṛtti-nivṛttī eva te na viduḥ, na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate | aśaucā anācārā māyāvino 'nṛta-vādino hy āsurāḥ ||BhGS_16.7||
children.translated_text: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) — engagement in that which is the means for human ends, in what ought to be done; cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) — the opposite of this, that from which, being the cause of harm, one should desist. Persons of demoniac nature do not know these. Not only do they not know activity and cessation — neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truth is found in them. Impure, lacking in proper conduct, deceitful, and speakers of falsehood — such are the demoniac. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.7 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: asatyam apratiṣṭhaṃ te jagad āhur anīśvaram |
children.translated_text: They say the world is unreal, without foundation, without a Lord,

children.text: aparaspara-saṃbhūtaṃ kim anyat kāma-haitukam ||BhG_16.8||
children.translated_text: not produced by mutual causation — what else [could it be] but caused by desire? // <s>BhG</s> 16.8 //

children.text: asatyaṃ yathā vayam anṛta-prāyās tathedaṃ jagat sarvam asatyam | apratiṣṭhaṃ ca nāsya dharmādharmau pratiṣṭhāto 'pratiṣṭhaṃ ceti | te āsurāḥ janāḥ jagad āhur anīśvaram na ca dharmādharma-sa-vyapekṣako 'sya śāsiteśvaro vidyata ity ato 'nīśvaraṃ jagad āhuḥ | kiṃ ca, aparaspara-saṃbhūtaṃ kāma-prayuktayoḥ strī-puruṣayor anyonya-saṃyogāj jagat sarvaṃ saṃbhūtam | kim anyat kāma-haitukam | kāma-hetukam eva kāma-haitukam | kim anyaj jagataḥ kāraṇam ? na kiṃcit adṛṣṭaṃ dharmādharmādi kāraṇāntaraṃ vidyate | jagataḥ kāma eva prāṇināṃ kāraṇam iti lokāyatika-dṛṣṭir iyam ||BhGS_16.8||
children.translated_text: Unreal (<s>asatya</s>) — 'just as we are mostly liars, so too this entire world is unreal.' Without foundation (<s>apratiṣṭha</s>) — 'it has no foundation in <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>,' [hence] it is without foundation — thus those demoniac persons say the world is without a Lord (<s>anīśvara</s>): 'there exists no governing Lord who acts with regard to <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>' — therefore they say the world is without a Lord. Moreover, [they say it is] produced by mutual [causation alone] — from the union of man and woman impelled by desire, the entire world is born. What else is the cause of the world but desire? There is no other unseen cause such as <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>. Desire of living beings alone is the cause of the world — this is the view of the materialists (<s>Lokāyatika</s>). // <s>BhGS</s> 16.8 //

children.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno 'lpa-buddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Holding fast to this view, these lost souls of meager intellect

children.text: prabhavanty ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato 'hitāḥ ||BhG_16.9||
children.translated_text: come forth as enemies of the world, [engaged in] cruel deeds, for [its] destruction. // <s>BhG</s> 16.9 //

children.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya āśritya naṣṭatmāno naṣṭa-svabhāvā vibhraṣṭa-para-loka-sādhanā alpa-buddhayo viṣaya-viṣayālpaiva buddhir yeṣāṃ te 'lpa-buddhayaḥ prabhavanti udbhavanti ugra-karmāṇaḥ krūra-karmāṇo hiṃsātmakāḥ | kṣayāya jagataḥ prabhavantīti saṃbandhaḥ || jagato 'hitāḥ śatravaḥ ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_16.9||
children.translated_text: Holding fast to this view — relying on it — [they are] lost souls (<s>naṣṭātmāna</s>), of destroyed nature, having fallen from the means of attaining the other world; of meager intellect (<s>alpa-buddhi</s>) — those whose intellect is limited to sense-objects alone; they come forth, they arise, [as those] of cruel deeds, of violent actions, of a nature characterized by <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence). For the destruction of the world they come forth — this is the connection. They are enemies (<s>ahita</s>) of the world — this is the meaning. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.9 //

children.text: te ca -
children.translated_text: And they —

children.text: kāmam āśritya duṣpūraṃ dambha-māna-madānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Taking refuge in insatiable desire, possessed of ostentation, conceit, and intoxication,

children.text: mohād gṛhītvāsad-grāhān pravartante 'śucivratāḥ ||BhG_16.10||
children.translated_text: having grasped false notions through delusion, they act with impure vows. // <s>BhG</s> 16.10 //

children.text: kāmam icchā-viśeṣam āśritya avaṣṭabhya duṣpūram aśakya-pūraṇaṃ dambha-māna-madānvitā dambhaś ca mānaś ca madaś ca dambha-māna-madās tair anvitāḥ dambha-māna-madānvitā mohād avivekato gṛhītvā upādāya asad-grāhān aśubha-niścayān pravartante loke aśuci-vratāḥ aśucīni vratāni yeṣāṃ te 'śuci-vratāḥ ||BhGS_16.10||
children.translated_text: Taking refuge in desire (<s>kāma</s>) — clinging to a particular form of craving — which is insatiable (<s>duṣpūra</s>), impossible to fill; possessed of ostentation, conceit, and intoxication — ostentation (<s>dambha</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and intoxication (<s>mada</s>) are 'ostentation-conceit-intoxication,' and they are possessed of these; through delusion (<s>moha</s>) — through lack of discrimination — having grasped false notions (<s>asad-grāha</s>), evil convictions; they act in the world; [they are] of impure vows (<s>aśuci-vrata</s>) — those whose vows are impure. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.10 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: cintām aparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntām upāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Given over to immeasurable anxiety ending only in death,

children.text: kāmopabhoga-paramā etāvad iti niścitāḥ ||BhG_16.11||
children.translated_text: regarding the gratification of desires as the highest [goal], convinced that this is all [there is] — // <s>BhG</s> 16.11 //

children.text: cintām aparimeyāṃ ca, na parimātuṃ śakyate yasyāś cintāyā iyattā sāparimeyā, tām aparimeyām, pralayāntāṃ maraṇāntām upāśritāḥ, sadā cintā-parā ity arthaḥ | kāmopabhoga-paramāḥ, kāmyante iti kāmā viṣayāḥ śabdādayas tad-upabhoga-paramā ayam eva paramaḥ puruṣārtho yaḥ kāmopabhoga ity evaṃ niścitātmānaḥ | etāvat iti niścitāḥ ||BhGS_16.11||
children.translated_text: Given over to immeasurable anxiety — that anxiety whose extent cannot be measured is immeasurable; [they are] given over to such [anxiety], which ends only in death (<s>pralayāntā</s>), [meaning] it lasts until death — they are always absorbed in anxiety, this is the meaning. Regarding the gratification of desires as the highest (<s>kāmopabhoga-paramā</s>) — the objects of desire (<s>kāma</s>) are the sense-objects such as sound etc.; those for whom the enjoyment of these is the highest — [thinking] 'this enjoyment of desires alone is the supreme human goal' — thus having firm conviction; convinced that 'this is all [there is].' // <s>BhGS</s> 16.11 //

children.text: āśā-pāśa-śatair baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Bound by hundreds of fetters of expectation, devoted to desire and anger,

children.text: īhante kāma-bhogārtham anyāyenārtha-saṃcayān ||BhG_16.12||
children.translated_text: they strive to amass wealth by unjust means for the gratification of desires. // <s>BhG</s> 16.12 //

children.text: āśā-pāśa-śatair āśaiva pāśās tac-chatair baddhāḥ niyantritāḥ santaḥ sarvata ākṛṣyamāṇāḥ, kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ kāma-krodhau param ayanam āśrayo yeṣāṃ te kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ | īhante ceṣṭante kāma-bhogārthaṃ kāma-bhoga-prayojanāya na dharmārtham | anyāyena para-svāpaharaṇādinety arthaḥ | kim ? artha-saṃcayān artha-pracayān ||BhGS_16.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Bound by hundreds of fetters of hope' — hopes themselves are the fetters; bound, i.e., restrained by hundreds of those [fetters], being pulled in every direction. 'Given to desire and anger' — those for whom desire and anger are the supreme resort, the refuge — they are 'given to desire and anger.' They strive — exert effort — for the purpose of sensual enjoyment (<s>kāma-bhoga</s>), not for the sake of <s>dharma</s>; by unjust means, such as seizing others' property — this is the meaning. For what? For the accumulation of wealth — amassing of riches. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.12 //

children.text: īdṛśaś ca teṣām abhiprāyaḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And of this kind is their mentality:

children.text: idam adya mayā labdham idaṃ prāpsye manoratham |
children.translated_text: 'This has been gained by me today; this desire I shall obtain;

children.text: idam astīdam api me bhaviṣyati punar dhanam ||BhG_16.13||
children.translated_text: this wealth is [already] mine, and this too shall be mine in the future.' // <s>BhG</s> 16.13 //

children.text: idaṃ dravyam adya idānīṃ mayā labdham | idaṃ cānyat prāpsye manorathaṃ manas-tuṣṭi-karam | idaṃ cāstīdam api me bhaviṣyati āgāmini saṃvatsare punar dhanaṃ tenāhaṃ dhanī vikhyāto bhaviṣyāmīti ||BhGS_16.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'This wealth has been gained by me today, at this time. And this other thing I shall obtain — [something] that gratifies the mind. And this is [already] mine, and this too shall be mine — in the coming year, yet more wealth. By that I shall become renowned as a wealthy person.' // <s>BhGS</s> 16.13 //

children.text: asau mayā hataḥ śatrur haniṣye cāparān api |
children.translated_text: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others too;

children.text: īśvaro 'ham ahaṃ bhogī siddho 'haṃ balavān sukhī ||BhG_16.14||
children.translated_text: I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am accomplished, powerful, and happy.' // <s>BhG</s> 16.14 //

children.text: asau devadattanāmā mayā hato durjayaḥ śatruḥ | haniṣye cāparān anyān varākān api | kim ete kariṣyanti tapasvinaḥ | sarvathāpi nāsti mattulyaḥ | katham ? īśvaro 'ham, ahaṃ bhogī | sarva-prakāreṇaś ca siddho 'haṃ saṃpannaḥ putraiḥ naptṛbhiḥ, na kevalaṃ mānuṣaḥ, balavān sukhī cāham eva | anye tu bhūmibhārāyāvitīrṇāḥ ||BhGS_16.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'That one, named <s>Devadatta</s>, an unconquerable enemy, has been slain by me. And I shall slay others too, those other wretches. What can these miserable ones do? In every way there is none equal to me.' How so? 'I am the lord; I am the enjoyer. In every way I am accomplished — blessed with sons and grandsons. And [I am] not merely human, [but] powerful and happy — I alone.' Others, however, have descended [into this world merely] as a burden to the earth. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.14 //

children.text: āḍhyo 'bhijanavān asmi ko 'nyo 'sti sadṛśo mayā |
children.translated_text: 'I am wealthy and well-born — who else is equal to me?

children.text: yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ity ajñāna-vimohitāḥ ||BhG_16.15||
children.translated_text: I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice' — thus deluded by ignorance. // <s>BhG</s> 16.15 //

children.text: āḍhaḍḥ dhanena, abhijanavān saptapuruṣaṃ śrotriyatvādisaṃpannaḥ - tenāpi na mama tulyo 'sti kaścit | ko 'nyo 'sti sadṛśas tulyaḥ mayā ? kiṃ ca, yakṣye yāgenāpy anyān abhibhaviṣyāmi, dāsyāmi naṭādibhyaḥ, modiṣye harṣaṃ cātiśayaṃ prāpsyāmi, iti evam ajñānavimohitāḥ ajñānena vimohitāḥ vividham avivekabhāvam āpannāḥ ||BhGS_16.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Wealthy' — in riches. 'Well-born' — endowed with a lineage of seven generations of Vedic scholars and the like. 'By that too, no one is equal to me. Who else is equal to, comparable to me? Moreover, I shall perform sacrifice — by sacrifice too I shall surpass others. I shall give — to actors and the like. I shall rejoice — I shall attain excessive delight.' Thus, deluded by ignorance — bewildered by ignorance, having arrived at a manifold state of non-discrimination. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.15 //

children.text: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Bewildered by manifold fancies, enveloped in the net of delusion,

children.text: prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu patanti narake 'śucau ||BhG_16.16||
children.translated_text: addicted to the gratification of desires, they fall into an impure hell. // <s>BhG</s> 16.16 //

children.text: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā ukta-prakārair anekaiś cittaiḥ vividhaṃ bhrāntāḥ aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ, mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ moho 'viveko 'jñānaṃ tad eva jālamiva āvaraṇātmakatvāt, tena samāvṛtāḥ | prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu tatraiva niṣaṇṇāḥ santas tena upacita-kalmaṣāḥ patanti narake 'śucau vaitaraṇyādau ||BhGS_16.16||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Bewildered by manifold fancies' — deluded in various ways by the manifold thoughts of the kinds described; 'enveloped in the net of delusion' — delusion is non-discrimination, ignorance; that itself is like a net, being of the nature of concealment; by that they are enveloped. Addicted to the gratification of desires — devoted entirely to those [gratifications], and thus having accumulated much sin — they fall into an impure hell, such as [the river] <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> and the like. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.16 //

children.text: ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhana-māna-madānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Self-conceited, obstinate, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth,

children.text: yajante nāma-yajñais te dambhenāvidhi-pūrvakam ||BhG_16.17||
children.translated_text: they perform sacrifices that are [mere] names, with ostentation and without proper rites. // <s>BhG</s> 16.17 //
