children.text: ātmasaṃbhāvittāḥ sarvaguṇaviśiṣṭatayā ātmanaiva saṃbhāvitāḥ ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ, na sādhubhiḥ | stabdhāḥ apraṇatātmānaḥ | dhanamānamadānvitāḥ dhananimittaḥ mānaḥ madaś ca, tābhyāṃ dhanamānamadābhyām anvitāḥ | yajante nāmayajñaiḥ nāmamātrair yajñais te dambhena dharmadhvajitayāvidhipūrvakaṃ vidhivihitāṅgetikartavyatārahitam ||BhGS_16.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Self-conceited' — honored by themselves alone as possessing all distinguished qualities, not by the virtuous. 'Obstinate' — having spirits that do not bow. 'Filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth' — the pride and intoxication caused by wealth; possessed of those. They perform sacrifices — with 'name-sacrifices,' sacrifices that are in name only; with ostentation, i.e., under the banner of [false] piety; without proper rites — devoid of the limbs and subsidiary duties prescribed by scripture. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.17 //

children.text: ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Resorting to ego, force, arrogance, desire, and anger,

children.text: mām ātma-para-deheṣu pradviṣanto 'bhyasūyakāḥ ||BhG_16.18||
children.translated_text: these envious ones despise Me in their own and others' bodies. // <s>BhG</s> 16.18 //

children.text: ahaṃkāram ahaṃkaraṇam ahaṃkāraḥ | vidyamānair avidyamānaiś ca guṇair ātmany adhyāropitair viśiṣṭam ātmānam aham iti manyate, so 'haṃkāro 'vidyākhyaḥ kaṣṭatamaḥ sarva-doṣāṇāṃ mūlaṃ sarvānartha-pravṛttīnāṃ ca, tam | tathā balaṃ parābhibhava-nimittaṃ kāma-rāgānvitam | darpaṃ darpo nāma yasya udbhave dharmam atikrāmati so 'yam antaḥkaraṇāśrayo doṣa-viśeṣaḥ | kāmaṃ stry-ādi-viṣayam | krodham aniṣṭa-viṣayam | etān anyāṃś ca mahato doṣān saṃśritāḥ | kiṃ ca te mām īśvaram ātma-para-deheṣu sva-dehe para-deheṣu ca tad-buddhi-karma-sākṣi-bhūtaṃ māṃ pradviṣantaḥ, mac-chāsanātivartitvaṃ pradveṣaḥ, taṃ kurvanto 'bhyasūyakāḥ san-mārga-sthānāṃ guṇeṣu asahamānāḥ ||BhGS_16.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Ego' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) — the act of making 'I'; [it arises when] one considers oneself distinguished by qualities — whether actually possessed or falsely attributed to the self — [thinking] 'I am [this].' This ego, known as <s>avidyā</s>, is the most terrible of all, being the root of all faults and the root of all misfortunes. Likewise, 'force' — [the strength used for] overpowering others, conjoined with desire and attachment. 'Arrogance' (<s>darpa</s>) — arrogance is a particular defect residing in the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), upon whose arising one transgresses <s>dharma</s>. 'Desire' — directed toward women and other objects. 'Anger' — directed toward the undesired. Resorting to these and other great faults. Moreover, they despise Me — the Lord — in their own and others' bodies, [Me who am] the witness of their thoughts and actions. The despising consists in transgressing My commandments. [And they are] envious — unable to bear the good qualities of those established on the path of virtue. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.18 //

children.text: tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
children.translated_text: These hateful, cruel, and lowest of humankind,

children.text: kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu ||BhG_16.19||
children.translated_text: I hurl perpetually, into the cycles of <s>saṃsāra</s>, into demoniac wombs alone. // <s>BhG</s> 16.19 //

children.text: tān ahaṃ sanmārgapratipakṣabhūtān sādhudveṣiṇo dviṣataś ca māṃ krūrān saṃsāreṣu evānekanarakasaṃsaraṇamārgeṣu narādhamān adharmadoṣavattvāt kṣipāmi prakṣipāmy ajasraṃ saṃtatam aśubhān aśubhakarmakāriṇaḥ āsurīṣveva krūra-karma-prāyāsu vyāghraṆsahādiyoniṣu kṣipāmītyanena saṃbandhaḥ ||BhGS_16.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those who are antagonistic to the path of virtue, who hate the righteous and who hate Me — the cruel ones — I hurl them in the cycles of <s>saṃsāra</s>, in the manifold paths of wandering through hells, the lowest of humankind due to their possession of the fault of <s>adharma</s>. I hurl [them] perpetually — continuously — the performers of inauspicious deeds — into demoniac wombs alone, those whose activities are predominantly cruel, such as the wombs of tigers and the like. 'I hurl' is to be connected with this [clause]. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.19 //

children.text: āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
children.translated_text: Entering demoniac wombs, deluded birth after birth,

children.text: mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim ||BhG_16.20||
children.translated_text: without ever attaining Me, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, they go thence to the lowest destination. // <s>BhG</s> 16.20 //

children.text: āsurīṃ yonim āpannāḥ pratipannāḥ mūḍhāḥ avivekino janmani janmani pratijanma tamobahulāsveva yoniṣu jāyamānāḥ adho gacchanto mūḍhāḥ mām īśvaram aprāpyānāsādya eva he kaunteya, tatas tasmādapi yānty adhamāṃ gatiṃ nikṛṣṭatamāṃ gatim | mām aprāpyaiveti na mat-prāptau kācid api āśaṅkāsti, ataḥ macchiṣṭasādhumārgam aprāpya ity arthaḥ ||BhGS_16.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having entered — having obtained — demoniac wombs, the deluded — the undiscriminating — birth after birth, being born in each successive birth in wombs that are predominantly <s>tāmasic</s>, going ever downward, the deluded, without ever attaining Me — the Lord — without ever reaching [Me], O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, from that [state] they go to the lowest destination — the most degraded end. 'Without ever attaining Me' — there is not even the slightest possibility of attaining Me. Therefore, the meaning is: without attaining the righteous path taught by Me. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.20 //

children.text: sarvasyā āsuryāḥ saṃpadaḥ saṃkṣepo 'yam ucyate, yasmin trividhe sarvaḥ āsurīsaṃpadbhedo 'nanto 'py antarbhavati | yatparihāreṇa parihṛtaś ca bhavati, yat mūlaṃ sarvasyānarthasya, tat etad ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This is stated as the summary of the entire demoniac nature, in which the threefold [gate] encompasses all the infinite varieties of the demoniac disposition, and by whose avoidance [the whole demoniac nature] is avoided — the root of all misfortune — this is stated:

children.text: tri-vidhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Threefold is this gate to hell, destructive of the self:

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṃ tyajet ||BhG_16.21||
children.translated_text: desire, anger, and greed — therefore, one should abandon these three. // <s>BhG</s> 16.21 //

children.text: trividhaṃ triprakāraṃ narakasya prāptāv idaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ, yat dvāraṃ praviśanneva naśyati ātmā | kasmaicit puruṣārthāya yogyo na bhavatītyetat, atar ucyate dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ iti | kiṃ tat ? kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhaḥ | tasmāt etat trayaṃ tyajet | yataḥ etat dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanas tasmāt kāmāditrayametat tyajet ||BhGS_16.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Threefold — of three kinds — is this gate to the attainment of hell, destructive of the self; the gate through which the self, upon entering, is destroyed. [This means:] one becomes unfit for any human goal — therefore it is called 'the gate destructive of the self.' What is it? Desire, anger, and greed. Therefore, one should abandon these three. Since these are the gate destructive of the self, therefore the triad of desire and the rest should be abandoned. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.21 //

children.text: tyāga-stutir iyam -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This is the praise of that abandonment:

children.text: etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tribhir naraḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is liberated from these three gates of darkness, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>,

children.text: ācaraty ātmanaḥ śreyas tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||BhG_16.22||
children.translated_text: practices what is good for the self, and then goes to the supreme destination. // <s>BhG</s> 16.22 //

children.text: etaiḥ vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tamaso narakasya duḥkha-mohātmakasya dvārāṇi kāmādayas taiḥ, etais tribhiḥ vimukto nara ācaraty anutiṣṭhati | kim ? ātmanaḥ śreyaḥ | yat-pratibaddhaḥ pūrvaṃ nācacāra, tad-apagamād ācarati | tatas tad-ācaraṇāt yāti parāṃ gatiṃ mokṣam apīti ||BhGS_16.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Liberated from these — the three gates of darkness, of hell — [gates] that are of <s>tamas</s>, of the hell that is of the nature of suffering and delusion; the gates are desire and the rest; from those three, a person who is liberated practices, performs — what? — what is good for the self. That which one was previously unable to practice due to being obstructed [by desire etc.], upon the removal of those [gates], one practices. And from that practice, one goes to the supreme destination — even to liberation. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.22 //

children.text: sarvasya etasya āsurī-saṃpat-parivarjanasya śreya-ācaraṇasya ca śāstraṃ kāraṇam | śāstra-pramāṇād ubhayaṃ śakyaṃ kartum, nānyathā | ataḥ -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Scripture is the cause of all this — the avoidance of the demoniac disposition and the practice of what is good. Through the authority of scripture, both can be accomplished, not otherwise. Therefore:

children.text: yaḥ śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya vartate kāma-kārataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture, acts according to the impulse of desire,

children.text: na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim ||BhG_16.23||
children.translated_text: attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination. // <s>BhG</s> 16.23 //

children.text: yaḥ śāstra-vidhiṃ śāstraṃ vedas tasya vidhiṃ kartavyākartavya-jñāna-kāraṇaṃ vidhi-pratiṣedhākhyam utsṛjya tyaktvā vartate kāma-kārataḥ kāma-prayuktaḥ san, na sa siddhiṃ puruṣārtha-yogyatām avāpnoti, nāpy asmin loke sukhaṃ nāpi parāṃ prakṛṣṭāṃ gatiṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ vā ||BhGS_16.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] One who, casting aside — abandoning — the injunctions of scripture, i.e., the Veda's injunctions that are the means of knowing what should and should not be done — in the form of injunctions and prohibitions — [and instead] acts impelled by desire; that one does not attain perfection, i.e., fitness for any human goal, nor happiness in this world, nor the supreme destination — heaven or liberation. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.23 //

children.text: tasmāc chāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākārya-vyavasthitau |
children.translated_text: Therefore, let scripture be your authority in determining what should and should not be done;

children.text: jñātvā śāstra-vidhānoktaṃ karma kartum ihārhasi ||BhG_16.24||
children.translated_text: having known what is declared by scriptural injunction, you should perform action here. // <s>BhG</s> 16.24 //

children.text: tasmāt śāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ jñāna-sādhanaṃ te tava kāryākārya-vyavasthitau kartavyākartavya-vyavasthāyām | ato jñātvā buddhvā śāstra-vidhānoktaṃ -- vidhir vidhānaṃ śāstram eva vidhānaṃ śāstra-vidhānaṃ kuryān na kuryād ity evaṃ-lakṣaṇam, tena uktaṃ sva-karma yat tat kartum ihārhasi | iheti karmādhikāra-bhūmi-pradarśanārtham iti ||BhGS_16.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, let scripture be the authority — the means of knowledge — for you, in determining what should and should not be done, i.e., in the ascertainment of the obligatory and the prohibited. Therefore, having known, having understood, what is declared by scriptural injunction — 'injunction' means scripture itself as regulation, the scriptural regulation characterized by 'one should do' and 'one should not do' — that which is declared thereby, namely one's own prescribed duty — you should perform [that action] here. 'Here' is for the purpose of indicating the domain of qualification for action. // <s>BhGS</s> 16.24 //

children.text: iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
children.translated_text: Thus, in the commentary on the Blessed <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṃkara Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
children.translated_text: the disciple of the revered <s>Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda</s>,

children.text: ṣoḍāśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [ends] the sixteenth chapter.

children.text: BhG 17
children.translated_text: <s>BhG</s> 17

children.text:
atha śraddhā-traya-vibhāga-yogaḥ
saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Now [begins] the seventeenth chapter, the Yoga of the Division of the Threefold Faith (<s>Śraddhā-traya-vibhāga-yoga</s>).

children.text: tasmāc chāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ ta [Gītā 16.24] iti bhagavad-vākyāl labdha-praśna-bījo 'rjuna uvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having obtained the seed for a question from the Blessed Lord's statement 'therefore, let scripture be your authority' [<s>Gītā</s> 16.24], <s>Arjuna</s> said:

children.text: ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture, worship with faith —

children.text: teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ ||BhG_17.1||
children.translated_text: what is their foundation, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Is it <s>sattva</s>, or <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s>? // <s>BhG</s> 17.1 //

children.text:
ye kecid aviśeṣitāḥ śāstra-vidhiṃ śāstra-vidhānaṃ śruti-smṛti-śāstra-codanām utsṛjya parityajya yajante devādīn pūjayanti śraddhayānvitāḥ śraddhayāstikya-buddhyānvitāḥ saṃyuktāḥ santaḥ | śruti-lakṣaṇaṃ smṛti-lakṣaṇaṃ vā kaṃcit śāstra-vidhim apaśyanto vṛddha-vyavahāra-darśanād eva śraddadhānatayā ye devādīn pūjayanti | te iha ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitā ity evaṃ gṛhyante | ye punaḥ kaṃcit śāstra-vidhiṃ upalabhamānaiva tam utsṛjyāyathā-vidhi devādīn pūjayanti | ta iha ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajanta iti na parigṛhyante | kasmāt ? śraddhayānvitatva-viśeṣaṇāt | devādi-pūjā-vidhi-paraṃ kiṃcit śāstraṃ paśyanta eva tad utsṛjyāśraddadhānatayā tad-vihitāyāṃ devādi-pūjāyāṃ śraddhayānvitāḥ pravartanta iti na śakyaṃ kalpayituṃ
yasmāt, tasmāt pūrvoktaiva ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitā ity atra gṛhyante | teṣām evaṃ-bhūtānāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ, kiṃ sattvaṃ niṣṭhāvasthānam, āho svit rajaḥ, athavā tama iti | etad uktaṃ bhavati - yā teṣāṃ devādi-viṣayā pūjā, sā kiṃ sāttvikī, āho svit rājasī, uta tāmasīti ||BhGS_17.1||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Those unspecified persons who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture — the commands of the <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> scriptures — worship, i.e., honor the gods and others, endowed with faith, i.e., possessed of the conviction of belief. Those who, not seeing any particular injunction of the <s>śruti</s> or <s>smṛti</s> scriptures, worship the gods and others with faith based merely on observing the practice of elders — they are understood here by 'those who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture, worship with faith.' But those who, while being aware of some scriptural injunction, deliberately casting it aside, improperly worship the gods and others — they are not understood here by 'those who cast aside the injunctions of scripture and worship.' Why? Because of the qualification 'endowed with faith.' For it is impossible to suppose that those who see some scripture prescribing the worship of gods and others, yet deliberately cast it aside and faithlessly [engage in that worship], are [at the same time] 'endowed with faith' in the worship of gods prescribed by that scripture. Therefore, only those of the former description are understood here by 'those who, casting aside the injunctions of scripture, worship with faith.' Of such persons, what is the foundation? — O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Is it <s>sattva</s>, or <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s>? — Which is it, <s>sattva</s> as the foundation and abode, or <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s>? The purport is: the worship of gods and the like that they perform — is it <s>sāttvic</s>, or <s>rājasic</s>, or <s>tāmasic</s>? // <s>BhGS</s> 17.1 //

children.text: sāmānya-viṣayo 'yaṃ praśno nāpravibhajrya prativacanam arhatīti śrībhagavānuvāca -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This is a general question, and it does not deserve an answer without proper analysis. The Blessed Lord said —

children.text: tri-vidhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāva-jā |
children.translated_text: Threefold is the faith of the embodied, born of their own nature —

children.text: sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu ||BhG_17.2||
children.translated_text: <s>sāttvic</s>, <s>rājasic</s>, and <s>tāmasic</s> — hear of it. // <s>BhG</s> 17.2 //

children.text: tri-vidhā tri-prakārā bhavati śraddhā | yasyāṃ niṣṭhāyāṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasi | dehināṃ śarīriṇāṃ sā svabhāva-jā | janmāntara-kṛto dharmādi-saṃskāro maraṇa-kāle 'bhivyaktaḥ svabhāva ucyate, tato jātā svabhāva-jā | sāttvikī sattva-nirvṛttā deva-pūjādi-viṣayā | rājasī rajo-nirvṛttā yakṣa-rakṣaḥ-pūjādi-viṣayā | tāmasī tamo-nirvṛttā preta-piśācādi-pūjā-viṣayā | evaṃ tri-vidhāṃ tām ucyamānāṃ śraddhāṃ śṛṇv avadhāraya ||BhGS_17.2||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Threefold — of three kinds — is the faith about which you are asking. Of the embodied — of those possessing bodies — it is born of their own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). The disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) formed by <s>dharma</s> and the like in previous births, which manifests at the time of death, is called one's own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>); born from that is 'born of one's own nature.' <s>Sāttvic</s> — produced from <s>sattva</s> (goodness), having as its object the worship of the gods and the like. <s>Rājasic</s> — produced from <s>rajas</s> (passion), having as its object the worship of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> and the like. <s>Tāmasic</s> — produced from <s>tamas</s> (darkness), having as its object the worship of ghosts, goblins, and the like. Hear — attend to — this faith that is being described as threefold. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.2 //

children.text: sā iyaṃ trividhā bhavati -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This [faith] is of three kinds —

children.text: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: The faith of everyone accords with their inner nature, O scion of <s>Bharata</s>;

children.text: śraddhā-mayo 'yaṃ puruṣo yo yac-chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ ||BhG_17.3||
children.translated_text: this person is made of faith — whatever one's faith is, that indeed is what one is. // <s>BhG</s> 17.3 //

children.text: sattvānurūpā viśiṣṭa-saṃskāropetāntaḥ-karaṇānurūpā sarvasya prāṇi-jātasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata | yady evaṃ tataḥ kiṃ syāt ? ity ucyate - śraddhā-mayo 'yaṃ śraddhā-prāyaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsārī jīvaḥ | katham ? yo yac-chraddho yā śraddhā yasya jīvasya sa yac-chraddhaḥ sa eva tac-chraddhānurūpa eva sa jīvaḥ ||BhGS_17.3||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Accords with one's inner nature (<s>sattvānurūpā</s>) — in accordance with the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) endowed with the particular dispositions — the faith of every living being accords [with it], O scion of <s>Bharata</s>. If so, then what follows? — it is said: this person is made of faith (<s>śraddhā-maya</s>) — predominantly constituted by faith; [this] person means the transmigrating soul (<s>jīva</s>). How? Whatever one's faith is — whatever faith belongs to whatever soul — that person is of that faith, meaning the soul is in accordance with that faith. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.3 //

children.text: tataś ca kāryeṇa liṅgena devādipūjayā sattvādiniṣṭhānumeyā ity āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And therefore, one's establishment in <s>sattva</s> and the rest can be inferred from the observable sign of worshipping the gods and the like — he says:

children.text: yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>sāttvic</s> worship the gods; the <s>rājasic</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>;

children.text: pretān bhūta-gaṇāṃś cānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ ||BhG_17.4||
children.translated_text: and others — the <s>tāmasic</s> people — worship ghosts and hosts of spirits. // <s>BhG</s> 17.4 //

children.text: yajante pūjayanti sāttvikāḥ sattva-niṣṭhā devān, yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ, pretān bhūta-gaṇāṃś ca sapta-mātṛkādīṃś cānye yajante tāmasāḥ janāḥ ||BhGS_17.4||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The <s>sāttvic</s> — those established in <s>sattva</s> — worship the gods. The <s>rājasic</s> [worship] <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. And others — the <s>tāmasic</s> people — worship ghosts and hosts of spirits such as the seven mothers (<s>sapta-mātṛkā</s>) and the like. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.4 //

children.text: evaṃ kāryato nirṇītāḥ sattvādi-niṣṭhāḥ śāstra-vidhy-utsarge | tatra kaścid eva sahasreṣu deva-pūjādi-paraḥ sattva-niṣṭho bhavati, bāhulyena tu rajo-niṣṭhās tamo-niṣṭhāś caiva prāṇino bhavanti | katham ? -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Thus, those established in <s>sattva</s> and the rest have been determined through their effects, in the general context of scriptural injunction. Among them, only a rare one in thousands is established in <s>sattva</s>, devoted to the worship of the gods and the like; but the majority of living beings are established in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. How so? —

children.text: aśāstra-vihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who practice terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture,

children.text: dambhāhaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-balānvitāḥ ||BhG_17.5||
children.translated_text: yoked with ostentation and egoism, endowed with the force of desire and attachment — // <s>BhG</s> 17.5 //

children.text: aśāstra-vihitaṃ na śāstra-vihitam aśāstra-vihitaṃ ghoraṃ pīḍā-karaṃ prāṇinām ātmanaś ca tapas tapyante nirvartayanti ye janās te ca dambhāhaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ | dambhaś cāhaṃkāraś ca dambhāhaṃkārau, tābhyāṃ saṃyuktāḥ dambhāhaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ, kāma-rāga-balānvitāḥ kāmaś ca rāgaś ca kāma-rāgau tat-kṛtaṃ balaṃ kāma-rāga-balaṃ tenānvitāḥ kāma-rāga-balānvitāḥ ||BhGS_17.5||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Not enjoined by scripture — not prescribed by scripture, hence 'not scripturally enjoined'; terrible — causing suffering to living beings and to oneself; [such] austerity is practiced, carried out, by those people who are yoked with ostentation and egoism: ostentation (<s>dambha</s>) and egoism (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) are 'ostentation-egoism'; yoked with those — 'yoked with ostentation and egoism.' Endowed with the force of desire and attachment: desire (<s>kāma</s>) and attachment (<s>rāga</s>) are 'desire-attachment'; the force produced by those is 'the force of desire and attachment'; endowed with that — 'endowed with the force of desire and attachment.' // <s>BhGS</s> 17.5 //

children.text: karśayantaḥ śarīra-sthaṃ bhūta-grāmam acetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Emacating the aggregate of elements dwelling in the body, the senseless ones,

children.text: māṃ caivāntaḥ-śarīra-sthaṃ tān viddhy āsura-niścayān ||BhG_17.6||
children.translated_text: and Me also, dwelling within the body — know them to be of demoniac resolve. // <s>BhG</s> 17.6 //

children.text: karśayantaḥ kṛśī-kurvantaḥ śarīra-sthaṃ bhūta-grāmaṃ karaṇa-samudāyam acetaso 'vivekinaḥ māṃ caiva tat-karma-buddhi-sākṣi-bhūtam antaḥ-śarīra-sthaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ karśayantaḥ, mad-anuśāsanākaraṇam eva mat-karśanam | tān viddhy āsura-niścayān āsuro niścayo yeṣāṃ te āsura-niścayās tān pariharaṇārthaṃ viddhīti upadeśaḥ ||BhGS_17.6||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Emacating — causing to waste away — the aggregate of elements dwelling in the body, the aggregate of sense-organs; the senseless, the undiscriminating; and Me also — <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who dwells within the body as the witness of their actions and thoughts — they emaciate [Me]; the very failure to follow My command is the emaciation of Me. Know them to be of demoniac resolve — those whose resolve is demoniac are 'of demoniac resolve'; know them — this is the instruction — for the purpose of avoidance. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.6 //

children.text: āhārāṇāṃ ca rasya-snigdhādi-varga-traya-rūpeṇa bhinnānāṃ yathā-kramaṃ sāttvika-rājasa-tāmasa-puruṣa-priyatva-darśanam iha kriyate rasya-snigdhādiṣu āhāra-viśeṣeṣv ātmanaḥ prīty-atirekeṇa liṅgena sāttvikatvaṃ rājasatvaṃ tāmasatvaṃ ca buddhvā rajas-tamo-liṅgānām āhārāṇāṃ parivarjanārthaṃ sattva-liṅgānāṃ copādānārtham | tathā yajñādīnām api sattvādi-guṇa-bhedena tri-vidhatva-pratipādanam iha rājasa-tāmasān buddhvā kathaṃ nu nāma parityajet, sāttvikān evānutiṣṭhed ity evam artham āha -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The distinction of foods — which are differentiated into three classes in the form of savory, oily, and the rest — as being preferred by <s>sāttvic</s>, <s>rājasic</s>, and <s>tāmasic</s> persons respectively, is presented here. [This is] so that by recognizing one's own <s>sāttvic</s>, <s>rājasic</s>, or <s>tāmasic</s> nature through the sign of one's particular preference for certain types of food such as the savory and oily, one may avoid foods that are signs of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and adopt those that are signs of <s>sattva</s>. Likewise, the presentation of the threefold division of sacrifice and the rest according to the distinction of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — is for the same purpose: recognizing the <s>rājasic</s> and <s>tāmasic</s> and rejecting them, and practicing only the <s>sāttvic</s> — with this intention he says:

children.text: āhāras tv api sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Food, however, is also of three kinds, dear to everyone;

children.text: yajñas tapas tathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu ||BhG_17.7||
children.translated_text: likewise sacrifice, austerity, and gift — hear this distinction of theirs. // <s>BhG</s> 17.7 //

children.text: āhāras tv api sarvasya bhoktuḥ prāṇinas tri-vidho bhavati priyaḥ iṣṭaḥ | tathā yajñas tathā tapas tathā dānam | teṣām āhārādīnāṃ bhedam imaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ sṛṇu ||BhGS_17.7||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Food, however, is also of three kinds for every eater, every living being — [it is] dear, i.e., preferred. Likewise sacrifice, likewise austerity, likewise gift. Hear this distinction of theirs — of food and the rest — which is about to be stated. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.7 //

children.text: āyuḥ-sattva-balārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Foods that promote longevity, clarity, strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction,

children.text: rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ ||BhG_17.8||
children.translated_text: which are savory, oily, substantial, and agreeable — are dear to the <s>sāttvic</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 17.8 //

children.text: āyuś ca sattvaṃ ca balaṃ ca ārogyaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca prītiś ca āyuḥ-sattva-balārogya-sukha-prītayas tāsāṃ vivardhanāḥ āyuḥ-sattva-balārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ | te ca rasyā rasopetāḥ, snigdhāḥ snehavantaḥ, sthirāś cira-kāla-sthāyino dehe, hṛdyāḥ hṛdaya-priyāḥ, āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ sāttvikasyeṣṭāḥ ||BhGS_17.8||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Longevity, clarity (<s>sattva</s>), strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction — those that promote, increase these — are 'promoters of longevity, clarity, strength, health, happiness, and satisfaction.' And they are savory — endowed with flavor; oily — having unctuousness; substantial — long-lasting in the body; agreeable — pleasing to the heart; [such] foods are dear to the <s>sāttvic</s>, preferred by one established in <s>sattva</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.8 //

children.text: kaṭv-amla-lavaṇātyuṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning

children.text: āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkha-śokāmaya-pradāḥ ||BhG_17.9||
children.translated_text: are preferred by the <s>rājasic</s> — they cause pain, grief, and disease. // <s>BhG</s> 17.9 //

children.text: kaṭv-amla-lavaṇātyuṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhina ity atrāti-śabdaḥ kaṭvādiṣu sarvatra yojyaḥ | atikaṭuḥ atitīkṣṇaḥ ity evam | kaṭuś cāmlaś ca lavaṇaś cātyuṣṇaś ca tīkṣṇaś ca rūkṣaś ca vidāhī ca te āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkha-śokāmaya-pradāḥ duḥkhaṃ ca śokaṃ cāmayaṃ ca prayacchantīti duḥkha-śokāmaya-pradāḥ ||BhGS_17.9||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning — here the prefix 'excessively' (<s>ati</s>) should be applied to all beginning with bitter: 'excessively bitter,' 'excessively pungent,' and so on. Bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning — such foods are preferred by the <s>rājasic</s>; they cause pain, grief, and disease — they give rise to pain, grief, and disease — [hence they are] 'causers of pain, grief, and disease.' // <s>BhGS</s> 17.9 //

children.text: yāta-yāmaṃ gata-rasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover,

children.text: ucchiṣṭam api cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasa-priyam ||BhG_17.10||
children.translated_text: and also the leavings of others and impure — such food is dear to the <s>tāmasic</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 17.10 //

children.text: yāta-yāmaṃ manda-pakvam, nirvīryasya gata-rasa-śabdenoktatvāt | gata-rasaṃ rasa-viyuktam, pūti durgandhi, paryuṣitaṃ ca pakvaṃ sad rātry-antaritaṃ ca yat, ucchiṣṭam api bhukta-śiṣṭam ucchiṣṭam, amedhyam ayajñārhaṃ bhojanam īdṛśaṃ tāmasa-priyam ||BhGS_17.10||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Stale (<s>yāta-yāma</s>) — half-cooked, since the tasteless has already been described by the word 'devoid of flavor.' Devoid of flavor (<s>gata-rasa</s>) — bereft of taste. Putrid (<s>pūti</s>) — foul-smelling. And leftover (<s>paryuṣita</s>) — that which, having been cooked, has been kept overnight. And also the leavings of others (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) — what remains after someone has eaten. Impure (<s>amedhya</s>) — unfit for sacrifice. Such food is dear to the <s>tāmasic</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.10 //

children.text: athedānīṃ yajñas trividha ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, the three kinds of sacrifice are stated —

children.text: aphalākāṅkṣibhir yajño vidhi-dṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
children.translated_text: That sacrifice which is offered in accordance with scriptural injunction, by those who do not desire the fruit,

children.text: yaṣṭavyam eveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||BhG_17.11||
children.translated_text: with the mind focused [thinking] 'this must be offered' — that is <s>sāttvic</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 17.11 //

children.text: aphalākāṅkṣibhir aphalārthibhir yajño vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ śāstra-codanādṛṣṭau yo yajña ijyate nirvartyate, yaṣṭavyam eveti yajña-svarūpa-nirvartanam eva kāryam iti manaḥ samādhāya, nānena puruṣārtho mama kartavya ity evaṃ niścitya, sa sāttviko yajña ucyate ||BhGS_17.11||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] By those who do not desire the fruit — by those who do not seek the fruit; the sacrifice that is prescribed by scriptural injunction (<s>vidhi-dṛṣṭa</s>) — that is, the sacrifice indicated by Vedic command — which is offered, performed, with the mind focused [thinking] 'this sacrifice itself must be performed as a duty' — not [thinking] 'by this, some personal end is to be accomplished by me' — having thus determined, that is called a <s>sāttvic</s> sacrifice. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.11 //

children.text: abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārtham api caiva yat |
children.translated_text: But that which is offered with an eye to the fruit, and also for the sake of display,

children.text: ijyate bharata-śreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam ||BhG_17.12||
children.translated_text: know that sacrifice to be <s>rājasic</s>, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 17.12 //

children.text: abhisandhāya tu uddiśya phalaṃ dambhārtham api caiva yad ijyate bharata-śreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam ||BhGS_17.12||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] But that which is offered having aimed at, targeted, the fruit, and also for the sake of display — that which is offered, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s> — know that sacrifice to be <s>rājasic</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.12 //

children.text: vidhi-hīnam asṛṣṭānnaṃ mantra-hīnam adakṣiṇam |
children.translated_text: Devoid of scriptural injunction, without distribution of food, devoid of <s>mantras</s>, without gifts [to priests],

children.text: śraddhā-virahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate ||BhG_17.13||
children.translated_text: bereft of faith — such a sacrifice they call <s>tāmasic</s>. // <s>BhG</s> 17.13 //

children.text: vidhi-hīnaṃ yathā-codita-viparītam, asṛṣṭānnaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo na sṛṣṭaṃ na dattam, annaṃ yasmin yajñe so 'sṛṣṭānnas tam asṛṣṭānnam | mantra-hīnaṃ mantrataḥ svarato varṇato vā viyuktaṃ mantra-hīnam, adakṣiṇam ukta-dakṣiṇā-rahitam, śraddhā-virahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate tamo-nirvṛttaṃ kathayanti ||BhGS_17.13||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Devoid of scriptural injunction (<s>vidhi-hīna</s>) — contrary to what has been enjoined. Without distribution of food (<s>asṛṣṭānna</s>) — [a sacrifice] in which food has not been distributed, not given, to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; that sacrifice in which food is not distributed is 'without distribution of food.' Devoid of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantra-hīna</s>) — deficient in <s>mantras</s>, either in accent (<s>svara</s>) or in letters (<s>varṇa</s>). Without gifts (<s>adakṣiṇa</s>) — lacking the prescribed ritual fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). Bereft of faith — such a sacrifice they call <s>tāmasic</s>, i.e., produced from <s>tamas</s>. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.13 //

children.text: atha idānīṃ tapas tri-vidham ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now, the three kinds of austerity (<s>tapas</s>) are stated —

children.text: deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanaṃ śaucam ārjavam |
children.translated_text: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity, uprightness,

children.text: brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate ||BhG_17.14||
children.translated_text: <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and non-violence — this is called austerity of the body. // <s>BhG</s> 17.14 //

children.text: devā ca dvijā ca guravaś ca prājñāś ca deva-dvija-guru-prājñās teṣāṃ pūjanaṃ deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanam | śaucam | ārjavam ṛjutvam | brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śarīra-nirvartyaṃ śārīraṃ śarīra-pradhānaiḥ sarvair eva kārya-karaṇaiḥ kartrādibhiḥ sādhyaṃ śārīraṃ tapa ucyate | pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ [Gītā 18.15] iti hi vakṣyati ||BhGS_17.14||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The gods, the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>), teachers, and the wise are 'gods-twice-born-teachers-wise'; their worship is 'the worship of gods, twice-born, teachers, and the wise.' Purity. Uprightness — straightforwardness. <s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) and non-violence — that which is accomplished through the body is bodily (<s>śārīra</s>); [meaning] accomplished through all the factors of action, principally the body, including the agent and the rest — [this] is called bodily austerity. For it will be stated: 'These five are its causes' [<s>Gītā</s> 18.15]. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.14 //

children.text: anudvega-karaṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priya-hitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial,

children.text: svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅ-mayaṃ tapa ucyate ||BhG_17.15||
children.translated_text: and the practice of Vedic study — this is called austerity of speech. // <s>BhG</s> 17.15 //

children.text:
anudvega-karaṃ prāṇinām aduḥkha-karaṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priya-hitaṃ ca yat priya-hite dṛṣṭādṛṣṭārthe | anudvega-karatvādibhir dharmair vākyaṃ viśeṣyate | viśeṣaṇa-dharma-samucayārthaś ca-śabdaḥ | para-pratyayārthaṃ prayuktasya vākyasya satya-priya-hitānudvega-karatvānām anyatamena dvābhyāṃ tribhir vā hīnatā syād yadi, na tad vāṅ-mayaṃ tapaḥ | tathā satya-vākyasya itareṣām anyatamena dvābhyāṃ tribhir vā vihīnatāyāṃ na vāṅ-maya-tapastvam | tathā priya-vākyasyāpītareṣām anyatamena dvābhyāṃ tribhir vā vihīnasya na vāṅ-maya-tapastvam | tathā hita-vākyasyāpītareṣām anyatamena dvābhyāṃ tribhir vā vihīnasya na vāṅ-maya-tapastvam | kiṃ punas tat tapaḥ ? yat satyaṃ vākyam anudvega-karaṃ priyaṃ hitaṃ ca, tat tapo vāṅ-mayam | yathā śānto bhava vatsa, svādhyāyaṃ
yogaṃ cānutiṣṭha, tathā te śreyo bhaviṣyatīti | svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva yathā-vidhi vāṅ-mayaṃ tapa ucyate ||BhGS_17.15||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] That which causes no distress — that which does not cause pain to living beings; such speech that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial — pleasant and beneficial refer to the seen and unseen purposes [respectively]. Speech is qualified by the attributes of causing no distress and the rest. The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) indicates the combination of all qualifying attributes. If speech uttered for the purpose of communicating to another lacks any one, two, or three of the qualities — truth, pleasantness, beneficence, and causing no distress — then it is not austerity of speech. Likewise, if truthful speech lacks any one, two, or three of the other [qualities], it is not austerity of speech. Similarly, if pleasant speech lacks any one, two, or three of the other [qualities], it is not austerity of speech. And if beneficial speech lacks any one, two, or three of the other [qualities], it is not austerity of speech. What then is that austerity? Speech that is truthful, causing no distress, pleasant, and beneficial — that is austerity of speech. For example: 'Be calm, my child, practice Vedic study and <s>yoga</s>, and thus it will be well with you.' And the practice of Vedic study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) according to the prescribed rules — [this too] is called austerity of speech. // <s>BhGS</s> 17.15 //

children.text: manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint,

children.text: bhāva-saṃśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate ||BhG_17.16||
children.translated_text: and purity of being — this is called austerity of the mind. // <s>BhG</s> 17.16 //

children.text: manaḥ-prasādaḥ manasaḥ praśāntiḥ svacchatāpādanaṃ prasādaḥ | saumyatvaṃ yat saumanasyam āhuḥ | mukhādi-prasādādi-kāryonneyāntaḥ-karaṇasya vṛttiḥ | maunaṃ vāṅ-niyamo 'pi manaḥ-saṃyama-pūrvako bhavatīti kāryeṇa kāraṇam ucyate manaḥ-saṃyamo maunam iti | ātma-vinigraho mano-nirodhaḥ sarvataḥ sāmānya-rūpa ātma-vinigrahaḥ | vāg-viṣayasyaiva manasaḥ saṃyamaḥ maunam iti viśeṣaḥ | bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ paraiḥ vyavahāra-kāle 'māyāvitvaṃ bhāva-saṃśuddhiḥ | ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate ||BhGS_17.16||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Serenity of mind' (<s>manaḥ-prasāda</s>) — the tranquility of the mind, the attainment of clarity (<s>svacchatā</s>), is <s>prasāda</s>. 'Gentleness' (<s>saumyatva</s>) — that which is called good-heartedness (<s>saumanasya</s>). The mental state to be inferred from its effects such as cheerfulness of face etc. 'Silence' (<s>mauna</s>) — restraint of speech too is preceded by mental restraint; hence the cause is stated through the effect — mental restraint is silence. 'Self-control' (<s>ātma-vinigraha</s>) — the restraint of the mind in a general, all-encompassing manner. Whereas 'silence' is the restraint of the mind specifically with respect to the domain of speech — this is the distinction. 'Purity of disposition' (<s>bhāva-saṃśuddhi</s>) — non-deceitfulness in one's dealings with others. This is called mental austerity (<s>mānasa tapas</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.16||

children.text: yathoktaṃ kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ mānasaṃ ca tapas taptaṃ naraiḥ sattvādi-guṇa-bhedena kathaṃ tri-vidhaṃ bhavatīti, ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The aforementioned bodily, verbal, and mental austerity, when practiced by persons, becomes threefold according to the distinction of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> etc. How? This is stated:

children.text: śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapas tat trividhaṃ naraiḥ |
children.translated_text: This threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by people

children.text: aphalākāṅkṣibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate ||BhG_17.17||
children.translated_text: who do not desire fruit, who are disciplined — they call it <s>sāttvika</s> (of the nature of <s>sattva</s>). ||<s>BhG</s> 17.17||

children.text: śraddhayā āstikya-buddhyā parayā prakṛṣṭayā taptam anuṣṭhitaṃ tapas tat prakṛtaṃ tri-vidhaṃ tri-prakāraṃ try-adhiṣṭhānaṃ narair anuṣṭhātṛbhir aphalākāṅkṣibhiḥ phalākāṅkṣā-rahitair yuktaiḥ samāhitair yad īdṛśaṃ tapaḥ, tat sāttvikaṃ sattva-nirvṛttaṃ paricakṣate kathayanti śiṣṭāḥ ||BhGS_17.17||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'With faith' (<s>śraddhā</s>) — with the conviction of belief, 'supreme' (<s>parā</s>), i.e., excellent — 'practiced' (<s>tapta</s>), i.e., performed — this threefold, three-fold, three-based austerity under discussion — by persons, i.e., by practitioners, 'who do not desire fruit' (<s>aphalākāṅkṣin</s>), i.e., free from the desire for fruit; 'disciplined' (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., concentrated — austerity of such nature — that is called <s>sāttvika</s>, born of <s>sattva</s> — so declare the learned. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.17||

children.text: satkāra-māna-pūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat |
children.translated_text: Austerity that is performed for the sake of hospitality, honor, and worship,

children.text: kriyate tad iha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calam adhruvam ||BhG_17.18||
children.translated_text: and with ostentation — that is declared here to be <s>rājasa</s> (of the nature of <s>rajas</s>), unstable and impermanent. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.18||

children.text: satkāraḥ sādhu-kāraḥ sādhu ayaṃ tapasvī brāhmaṇa ity evam artham | māno mānanaṃ pratyutthānābhivādanādis tad-artham | pūjā pāda-prakṣālanārcanāśayitṛtvādis tad-arthaṃ ca tapaḥ satkāra-māna-pūjārtham | dambhena caiva yat kriyate tapas tad iha proktaṃ kathitaṃ rājasaṃ calaṃ kādācitka-phalatvena adhruvam ||BhGS_17.18||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'Hospitality' (<s>satkāra</s>) — good treatment, in the sense of 'this is a fine ascetic, a good <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' — for that purpose. 'Honor' (<s>māna</s>) — veneration such as rising up and salutation — for that purpose. 'Worship' (<s>pūjā</s>) — washing of the feet, reverential offerings, providing a place to lie down, etc. — for that purpose too. Austerity [performed] for the sake of hospitality, honor, and worship; 'and with ostentation' (<s>dambha</s>) — whatever [austerity] is performed — that is declared, i.e., called, here [in this text] to be <s>rājasa</s>, 'unstable' (<s>cala</s>), having only occasional fruit, and 'impermanent' (<s>adhruva</s>). ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.18||

children.text: mūḍha-grāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Austerity that is performed with deluded obstinacy, with self-torture,

children.text: parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||BhG_17.19||
children.translated_text: or for the purpose of destroying another — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s> (of the nature of <s>tamas</s>). ||<s>BhG</s> 17.19||

children.text: mūḍha-grāheṇa aviveka-niścayena ātmanaḥ pīḍayā yat kriyate tapaḥ parasya utsādanārthaṃ vināśārthaṃ vā, tat tāmasaṃ tapa udāhṛtam ||BhGS_17.19||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'With deluded obstinacy' (<s>mūḍha-grāha</s>) — with a determination born of lack of discrimination; 'with self-torture' (<s>ātmanaḥ pīḍā</s>) — whatever austerity is performed; 'or for the purpose of destroying another' (<s>parasya utsādanārtham</s>), i.e., for the purpose of ruining [another] — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s> austerity. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.19||

children.text: idānīṃ dāna-traividhyam ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Now the threefold classification of charity (<s>dāna</s>) is stated:

children.text: dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe |
children.translated_text: That gift which is given with the thought 'it ought to be given,' to one who does no service in return,

children.text: deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||BhG_17.20||
children.translated_text: at the proper place and time, and to a worthy recipient — that gift is considered <s>sāttvika</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.20||

children.text: dātavyam iti evaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe pratyupakārāsamarthāya, samarthāyāpi nirapekṣaṃ dīyate | deśe puṇye kurukṣetrādau | kāle saṃkrānty-ādau | pātre ca ṣaḍ-aṅga-vid veda-pāraga ity ādau | tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||BhGS_17.20||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'It ought to be given' (<s>dātavya</s>) — having made up one's mind thus, whatever gift is given to one who renders no service in return (<s>anupakārin</s>), i.e., to one incapable of reciprocating, or even if capable, given without expectation [of return]. At the proper place — at a holy place such as <s>Kurukṣetra</s> etc. At the proper time — at a [special] time such as a solstice (<s>saṃkrānti</s>) etc. And to a worthy recipient — one versed in the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, one who has mastered the <s>Veda</s>, etc. That gift is considered <s>sāttvika</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.20||

children.text: yat tu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: But that which is given with the aim of reciprocation, or again with an eye to the fruit,

children.text: dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ tad dānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam ||BhG_17.21||
children.translated_text: and [which is given] grudgingly — that gift is considered <s>rājasa</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.21||

children.text: yat tu dānaṃ pratyupakārārthaṃ kāle tv ayaṃ māṃ pratyupakariṣyatīty evam artham, phalaṃ vāsya dānasya me bhaviṣyaty adṛṣṭam iti | tad uddiśya punar dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ kheda-saṃyuktam, tad dānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam ||BhGS_17.21||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Whatever gift [is given] with the aim of reciprocation — [thinking] 'in time this person will serve me in return' — for that purpose; or with an eye to the [unseen] fruit — [thinking] 'from this gift an unseen merit will accrue to me.' Given for that purpose; and 'grudgingly' (<s>parikliṣṭam</s>), i.e., accompanied by reluctance — that gift is considered <s>rājasa</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.21||

children.text: adeśa-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaś ca dīyate |
children.translated_text: That gift which is given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy recipients,

children.text: asatkṛtam avajñātaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||BhG_17.22||
children.translated_text: without respect and with contempt — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.22||

children.text: adeśa-kāle 'deśe 'puṇye deśe mlecchāśucy-ādi-saṃkīrṇe | akāle puṇya-hetutvenāprakhyāte saṃkrānty-ādi-viśeṣa-rahite 'pātrebhyaś ca mūrkha-taskarādibhyaḥ | deśādi-saṃpattau vā asatkṛtaṃ priya-vacana-pāda-prakṣālana-pūjādi-rahitam avajñātaṃ pātra-paribhava-yuktaṃ ca yad dānam, tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||BhGS_17.22||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'At the wrong place and time' — in an unholy place, i.e., a place infested with <s>mlecchas</s>, impurities, etc. At the wrong time — a time not renowned as meritorious, devoid of special occasions such as solstices etc. To unworthy recipients — to fools, thieves, etc. Or even when place etc. are proper — 'without respect' (<s>asatkṛtam</s>), i.e., devoid of kind words, washing of feet, worship, etc.; 'with contempt' (<s>avajñātam</s>), i.e., accompanied by disrespect toward the recipient — whatever gift [is thus given], that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.22||

children.text: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-prabhṛtīnāṃ sādguṇya-karaṇāyāyam upadeśa ucyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] This instruction is stated for making sacrifice, charity, austerity, and similar acts endowed with goodness (<s>sāttva</s>):

children.text: oṃ tat sad iti nirdeśo brahmaṇas trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Tat Sat</s>' — this is declared to be the threefold designation of <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: brāhmaṇās tena vedāś ca yajñāś ca vihitāḥ purā ||BhG_17.23||
children.translated_text: by that, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, and sacrifices were ordained of old. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.23||

children.text: oṃ tat sad iti evaṃ nirdeśaḥ, nirdiśyate 'neneti nirdeśaḥ | trividho nāma nirdeśo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaś cintito vedānteṣu brahma-vidbhiḥ | brāhmaṇās tena nirdeśena trividhena vedāś ca yajñāś ca vihitāḥ nirmitāḥ purā pūrvam iti nirdeśa-stuty-artham ucyate ||BhGS_17.23||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] '<s>Oṃ Tat Sat</s>' — thus [constitutes] the designation (<s>nirdeśa</s>); that by which [<s>Brahman</s>] is designated is the designation. The threefold designation of <s>Brahman</s> is declared, i.e., contemplated, in the <s>Vedānta</s> texts by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. By that threefold designation, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and <s>Vedas</s>, and sacrifices were ordained (<s>vihita</s>), i.e., created, of old (<s>purā</s>), in ancient times — this is stated for the purpose of praising the designation. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.23||

children.text: tasmād om ity udāhṛtya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, uttering '<s>Oṃ</s>,' the acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity

children.text: pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahma-vādinām ||BhG_17.24||
children.translated_text: prescribed by the ordinances are always commenced by the expounders of <s>Brahman</s>. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.24||

children.text: tasmāt om ity udāhṛtya uccārya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyā yajñādi-svarūpāḥ kriyāḥ pravartante vidhānoktāḥ śāstra-coditāḥ satataṃ sarvadā brahma-vādināṃ brahma-vadana-śīlānām ||BhGS_17.24||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Therefore, having uttered (<s>udāhṛtya</s>), i.e., having pronounced, '<s>Oṃ</s>' — the acts that are in the nature of sacrifice, charity, and austerity (<s>yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ</s>) are commenced — those prescribed by the ordinances (<s>vidhāna</s>), i.e., enjoined by scripture — always (<s>satatam</s>) — by the expounders of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahma-vādin</s>), i.e., those whose habit is to speak of <s>Brahman</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.24||

children.text: tad ity anabhisaṃdhāya phalaṃ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Uttering '<s>Tat</s>' (That), without aiming at the fruit, the acts of sacrifice and austerity

children.text: dāna-kriyāś ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ ||BhG_17.25||
children.translated_text: and the various acts of charity are performed by seekers of liberation. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.25||

children.text: tad ity anabhisaṃdhāya | tad iti brahmābhidhānam uccāryānabhisaṃdhāyaś ca yajñādi-karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyā yajña-kriyāś ca tapaḥ-kriyāś ca yajña-tapaḥ-kriyā dāna-kriyāś ca vividhāḥ kṣetra-hiraṇya-pradānādi-lakṣaṇāḥ kriyante nirvartyante mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhir mokṣārthibhir mumukṣubhiḥ ||BhGS_17.25||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Having uttered '<s>Tat</s>' — '<s>Tat</s>' is the designation of <s>Brahman</s>, having uttered [it] — and without aiming at (<s>anabhisaṃdhāya</s>) the fruit of sacrificial and other actions — the acts of sacrifice and austerity (<s>yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ</s>) and the various acts of charity (<s>dāna-kriyāḥ</s>) — characterized as gifts of land, gold, etc. — are performed, i.e., accomplished, by seekers of liberation (<s>mokṣa-kāṅkṣin</s>), i.e., by those desirous of liberation, by <s>mumukṣus</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.25||

children.text: oṃ-tac-chabdayor viniyoga uktaḥ | athedānīṃ sac-chabdasya viniyogaḥ kathyate -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] The application of the words '<s>Oṃ</s>' and '<s>Tat</s>' has been stated. Now the application of the word '<s>Sat</s>' is described:

children.text: sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve ca sad ity etat prayujyate |
children.translated_text: In the sense of 'reality' and in the sense of 'goodness,' the word '<s>Sat</s>' is employed;

children.text: praśaste karmaṇi tathā sac-chabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||BhG_17.26||
children.translated_text: likewise, O <s>Pārtha</s>, the word '<s>Sat</s>' is used for a praiseworthy action. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.26||

children.text: sad-bhāve | asataḥ sad-bhāve yathā-vidyamānasya putrasya janmani | tathā sādhu-bhāve cāsad-vṛttasyāsādhoḥ sad-vṛttatā sādhu-bhāvas tasmin sādhu-bhāve ca | sad ity etad abhidhānaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prayujyate 'bhidhīyate | praśaste karmaṇi vivāhādau ca tathā sac-chabdaḥ pārtha yujyate prayujyata ity etat ||BhGS_17.26||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] 'In the sense of reality' (<s>sad-bhāve</s>) — when something non-existent comes into existence, as at the birth of a son who actually exists [as a reality]. Likewise, 'in the sense of goodness' (<s>sādhu-bhāve</s>) — when one of bad conduct becomes one of good conduct, that good state is <s>sādhu-bhāva</s>; in that sense of goodness. The word '<s>Sat</s>' — this designation of <s>Brahman</s> — is employed, i.e., used. For a praiseworthy action — such as a wedding ceremony etc. — likewise the word '<s>Sat</s>' is used, O <s>Pārtha</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.26||

children.text: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ sad iti cocyate |
children.translated_text: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is also called '<s>Sat</s>';

children.text: karma caiva tad-arthīyaṃ sad ity evābhidhīyate ||BhG_17.27||
children.translated_text: and action performed for the sake of that [<s>Brahman</s>] is likewise designated as '<s>Sat</s>.' ||<s>BhG</s> 17.27||

children.text: yajñe yajña-karmaṇi yā sthitiḥ, tapasi ca yā sthitiḥ, dāne ca yā sthitiḥ, sā sad iti cocyate vidvadbhiḥ | karma caiva tad-arthīyaṃ yajña-dāna-tapo 'rthīyam | athavā, yasyābhidhāna-trayaṃ prakṛtaṃ tad-arthīyaṃ yajña-dāna-tapo 'rthīyam īśvarārthīyam ity etat | sad ity evābhidhīyate | tad etad yajña-dāna-tapa-ādi-karmāsāttvikaṃ viguṇam api śraddhā-pūrvakaṃ brahmaṇo 'bhidhāna-traya-prayogeṇa sa-guṇaṃ sāttvikaṃ saṃpāditaṃ bhavati ||BhGS_17.27||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Whatever steadfastness there is in sacrifice — in the act of sacrifice — and whatever steadfastness in austerity, and whatever steadfastness in charity — that is also called '<s>Sat</s>' by the wise. And action that is 'for the sake of that' (<s>tad-arthīya</s>) — for the sake of sacrifice, charity, and austerity. Or alternatively, for the sake of that whose threefold designation is under discussion — i.e., for the sake of the Lord — that is the meaning. [Such action] is likewise designated as '<s>Sat</s>.' Thus, even the action of sacrifice, charity, austerity, etc. that is non-<s>sāttvika</s> or deficient in qualities — when performed with faith and accompanied by the utterance of the threefold designation of <s>Brahman</s> — becomes endowed with qualities, becomes <s>sāttvika</s>. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.27||

children.text: tatra ca sarvatra śraddhā-pradhānatayā sarvaṃ saṃpādyate yasmāt, tasmāt -
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] And since in all cases everything is accomplished primarily through faith — therefore:

children.text: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever is offered in sacrifice, given in charity, or practiced as austerity, or whatever is done

children.text: asad ity ucyate pārtha na ca tat pretya no iha ||BhG_17.28||
children.translated_text: without faith — it is called '<s>asat</s>' (non-existent/unreal), O <s>Pārtha</s>; it avails nothing after death, nor here [in this world]. ||<s>BhG</s> 17.28||

children.text: aśraddhayā hutaṃ havanaṃ kṛtam | aśraddhayā dattaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ | aśraddhayā tapas taptam anuṣṭhitam | tathāśraddhayaiva kṛtaṃ yat stuti-namaskārādi, tat sarvam asad ity ucyate mat-prāpti-sādhana-mārga-bāhyatvāt pārtha | na ca tad bahulāyāsam api pretya phalāya no apīhārtham, sādhubhir ninditatvād iti ||BhGS_17.28||
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary:] Without faith — an oblation offered [without faith]; without faith — given to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; without faith — austerity practiced, i.e., performed. Likewise, without faith — whatever is done, such as praise, obeisance, and the like — all of that is called '<s>asat</s>' (unreal), because it is outside the path of attaining me, O <s>Pārtha</s>. And that, even though accomplished with great effort, is neither for any fruit after death, nor for any purpose here [in this world] — because it is condemned by the wise. ||<s>BhGS</s> 17.28||

children.text:
iti śrīmat-paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācāryasya śrī-govinda-bhagavat-pūjya-pāda-
śiṣyasya śrīmac-chaṃkara-bhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīmad-bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣye
saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the blessed <s>Bhagavad-gītā-bhāṣya</s> composed by the blessed <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, who was a disciple of the blessed <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, who was the foremost among the supreme renunciants and wandering monks.
